# Decision, assumption and risk register

Version 0.3 | 2026-09-04 | Accepted for baseline

## Decision procedure

Every decision record contains ID, question, recommendation, evidence basis, owner, status and date. Entries may be ACCEPTED FOR BASELINE, PROVISIONAL or OPEN. Version 0.3 closes the decisions that version 0.2 left open, on the basis of a structured design interview with the owner rather than measurement. Where a decision rests on preference rather than evidence, this document says so explicitly.

Andrew is the product decision owner, the artistic acceptance reviewer and the sole verifier. No technical or legal reviewer is engaged.

## Closed decisions

D-01 / Platform / ACCEPTED. Windows 11 x64 only for G0 through G1. Declared reference machine: Ryzen 9 9900X, 64 GB RAM, RTX 4070 Ti Super 16 GB. Cross-platform support is not claimed, planned or designed for. Platform-specific code stays behind narrow interfaces so that this remains reversible, not because a port is scheduled.

D-02 / Initial scope / ACCEPTED. Complete the 2D milestone before any 2.5D work. Version 0.3 narrows this further: see D-12.

D-03 / Distribution / ACCEPTED. Open source. This decision was taken early and deliberately in order to remove license review as an ongoing cost, since no legal reviewer is available. All dependency choices must remain compatible with it. Revenue is not a project goal.

D-04 / Capacity / PROVISIONAL. Solo development with Claude Code on a subscription, no API spend, owner as sole reviewer. Weekly hours are deliberately not committed. Consequence: document 13 remains gate-driven with no calendar dates, and no estimate in this pack may be converted into a completion date until this is closed.

D-05 / Reference shot / ACCEPTED. The owner draws it. Specification is in document 22: 1920x1080, 24 fps, 240 frames, one static background, three cel layers on 1s, 2s and 3s with a deliberate five-frame hold and a one-frame accent, mixed soft and hard and semi-transparent edges, one deliberately missing frame and one Japanese filename. Rights-cleared by construction.

D-06 / Stack / ACCEPTED, spike-confirmable. Rust core with rayon for tile parallelism, Tauri with an HTML and CSS interface. Rationale in ADR-003 and ADR-004. Selected against the constraint that the owner cannot read code, which favors a compiler that rejects broken programs and a toolchain with no configuration surface for the owner to repair.

D-07 / Color / ACCEPTED. Linear-light premultiplied float32 working space with explicit PNG interpretation, per document 21.

D-08 / Compatibility / ACCEPTED. Native features only. No AE project import, no binary plugin hosting, no expression translation. Not a research topic during G1.

D-09 / G2 geometry / ACCEPTED. Non-intersecting planes with explicit order, when G2 is reached.

D-10 / Expressions / DEFERRED. G2 concern. The likely answer within a Rust core is an embedded sandboxed scripting runtime or a small custom evaluator, but this is not decided and must not influence G1-core design. **Answered on 2026-09-16 by D-59, accepted by the owner the same day:** a small custom evaluator, not an embedded runtime.

D-11 / Name / DEFERRED. TotallyNotAfterEffects is a working title and repository name only. It is a joke, not a product name, and it references a competitor trademark, which makes it unsuitable for distribution. Choose and screen a public name before any public build. Deferred again by the owner on 2026-09-27 ("3 - unsure still, defer for now", D-167).

## New decisions in version 0.3

D-12 / G1-core narrowing / ACCEPTED. The fifteen-Must G1 list from version 0.2 is split. G1-core is import, exposure timing, layers and transforms, undo, save and recovery, export, color and alpha handling, and offline operation. Masks and mattes, the effect stack, and the bounded preview cache are parked to G1-rest. Rationale: at the available capacity the version 0.2 list was not deliverable, and document 30 identifies exposure-and-layer-first finishing as the only structural gap against existing free tools. Masks and blur are not gaps.

D-12 amended on 2026-09-06: the park on masks and mattes (B-06 / R-04) and on the effect stack (B-07 / R-05) is LIFTED, both together, by the owner. Document 23 words both revisit triggers as things that happen in a real shot - "A real shot cannot be finished without one" for the mask and the alpha matte, "repeated manual effort in real shots" for the effects - and document 23 makes firing them the owner's to do. The owner fired both on being shown what the alternative costs: B-12 / G1 acceptance needs W-01 finished on the reference shot, W-01 needs a matte, a blur and a colour operation, and with the backlog B-01 through B-11 and B-08b complete there is no decision-free work left that reaches G1. Agreed order is B-06, then B-07, then B-12 / G1. What is not lifted: nothing else in G1-rest moves, the narrowing that produced G1-core stands as the reason this project got this far, and B-07 must still address the ADR-011 tile margins that document 15 line 69 names as part of why blur was not in the first milestone. This entry records the decision; the unpark is written into R-04 and R-05 in document 03 in the form R-06b set on 2026-09-05. Of the two lifted, **B-06 was built the same day**: `src/mask.rs`, the mask and matte steps of `src/compose.rs`, and `verification/B-06_mask_table.md`, 45 checks. It settled document 25 line 51 in ADR-016 and raised D-42 and D-43. **B-07 is not started.**

D-13 / Verification model / ACCEPTED. The owner cannot read code. Human source review is removed from the quality system and replaced by fixture-and-artifact verification, specified in document 12. Fixture expected values are read-only to implementation work. This is the primary control of the project and its most important decision.

D-14 / Renderer / ACCEPTED. CPU-only for G1-core, tile-based and multithreaded. No GPU backend is built until a measured stopwatch result on a real shot justifies it. The tile contract in document 21 is designed so a later GPU dispatch is a port rather than a rewrite. Consequence: the dual-path comparison in SP-02 is removed; there is one path.

D-15 / Build versus extend / ACCEPTED ON PREFERENCE. The comparison task in document 30, against Natron, Fusion and OpenToonz, will not be run. The owner wants to build this tool, and the comparison would not change that. This is recorded as a preference-based decision, not an evidence-based one, and document 30 is amended accordingly rather than left implying evidence that does not exist.

D-16 / Pack format / ACCEPTED. Word review copies and the checksum manifest are removed. Markdown is the only source and the repository is under git, which supplies the change record this document previously described by hand.

## New decisions in version 0.4

D-17 / sRGB transfer function / PROVISIONAL. Document 21 requires conversion between sRGB and linear light in both directions but never states which transfer function. B-02 implements IEC 61966-2-1: linear segment `c/12.92` below `c <= 0.04045`, and `((c+0.055)/1.055)^2.4` above, with the matching inverse. Evidence basis: this is the transfer function the sRGB standard defines and the one every tool the owner would compare against uses. Status is PROVISIONAL rather than ACCEPTED because it is an agent's reading of an unstated requirement, not an owner decision. Consequence if changed: every expected value in `verification/B-02_fixture_table.md` moves, and document 25's fixtures move with it.

D-18 / 8-bit quantisation rule / PROVISIONAL. Document 21 says "final integer output conversion clamps only at the declared encoding step" but does not state the rounding rule at that step. B-02 clamps to 0..1 and rounds to nearest with ties away from zero, `floor(c * 255 + 0.5)`. Evidence basis: it is the rule the G0 spikes already used, and it makes all 256 8-bit codes survive a decode and re-encode round trip exactly, which is stronger than the "at most one code value" tolerance document 25 allows. Status PROVISIONAL for the same reason as D-17. Both should be folded into document 21 as specification text rather than left as implementation comments.

## Risks

K-01 / High / Scope expansion. Effect catalogs and conveniences displace core reliability. Trigger: anything from the parked list appearing in a build. Mitigation: the admission rule in document 04, the parked list in document 23, and the agent rule forbidding parked work.

K-02 / High / Pixel errors. Alpha and color mismatch damages edges. Trigger: halos, or preview and export disagreeing. Mitigation: independent fixtures, tagged buffers, render trace.

K-03 / High / Data loss. Partial writes or migrations damage projects. Trigger: failed recovery fixture. Mitigation: atomic replacement, autosave, T-07.

K-04 / High / Unverifiable implementation. The owner cannot detect a wrong implementation that passes its fixtures, or a fixture quietly weakened. Trigger: unexplained fixture changes, or reports lacking artifacts. Mitigation: document 12, the fixture read-only rule, mandatory artifacts, mandatory not-run reporting. This risk is inherent and permanently open.

K-05 / High / Capacity. The project is large and the owner is one person without a coding background. Trigger: milestone stalls, growing unfinished subsystems. Mitigation: the D-12 narrowing, one subsystem at a time, willingness to narrow again.

K-06 / Medium / Preview transport ceiling. WebView2 frame delivery may not sustain full-resolution playback, and browser color management may alter displayed pixels. Trigger: SP-05 or SP-06 failing. Mitigation: both are preview-side only and never affect export; the fallback is a native viewer surface inside the web shell.

K-07 / Medium / Unsafe input. Malformed media exhausts resources. Trigger: unbounded parser. Mitigation: size limits and cancellation.

K-08 / Medium / Dependency drift. WebView2 is a system component updated by Microsoft outside the control of this project. Trigger: a Windows update changing viewer behavior. Mitigation: viewer color and transport fixtures run against each release candidate.

D-19 / Four import diagnostic identifiers / PROVISIONAL. Document 28's catalog defines `MEDIA_SEQUENCE_GAP`, `MEDIA_UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT` and `MEDIA_DECODE_FAILED`, which cover most of B-03. Test T-01 also requires behaviour for mismatched dimensions within one sequence, and the reference shot forces two more cases, and document 28 names none of them. B-03 adds `MEDIA_SEQUENCE_DIMENSION_MISMATCH` (WARNING, the sequence is treated as the majority size and the odd drawings are still imported), `MEDIA_SEQUENCE_DUPLICATE_NUMBER` (ERROR, two selected files claim one drawing number, the first in sort order is kept), `MEDIA_SEQUENCE_UNNUMBERED` (ERROR, a selected file has no number in its name and is excluded) and `MEDIA_SEQUENCE_NAME_VARIANT` (INFO, a file carries a clear number under a name the inferred pattern does not generate, and is imported under its own name). Evidence basis: document 28 requires stable machine IDs and forbids library error strings as user-facing identifiers, so silence was not an option and reusing an unrelated identifier would have been a silent reinterpretation of the catalog. Status PROVISIONAL because the names and severities are an agent's proposal, not the owner's decision. Consequence if changed: the identifiers in `verification/B-03_import_table.md` change, and document 28's catalog gains four entries.

D-20 / Frame numbers come from the file list, not the pattern / PROVISIONAL. Document 19 line 17 requires a sequence asset to store a numeric pattern and a frame-number-to-file map "so missing numbers remain missing rather than being silently compacted", but does not say which of the two decides membership. B-03 makes the map authoritative and the pattern descriptive: a frame number is the last run of ASCII digits in a file's stem, and a file whose name the pattern does not generate is still imported under its own name. Evidence basis: the reference shot requires it. Drawing 13 of layer 2 is `layer2_桜_013.png`, which `layer2_%03d.png` does not generate; a pattern-driven importer reports a false gap and drops a drawing the owner can see in their own folder. Consequence if changed: layer 2 would report a gap it does not have.

D-21 / Three command diagnostic identifiers / PROVISIONAL. Document 26 requires that a command validate intent and that "a rejected command does not change document revision, dirty state, undo stack or caches", and document 28 forbids surfacing a library error string as a user-facing identifier, but document 28's catalog names no identifier for a command that fails validation. B-05 adds `COMMAND_TARGET_MISSING` (ERROR, the command named a composition, layer or keyframe that is not there), `COMMAND_INVALID_VALUE` (ERROR, the command carried a value the model cannot hold: the wrong value kind for the property, a non-finite number, or an index outside the layer stack) and `COMMAND_LAYER_LOCKED` (ERROR, the command would have changed a locked layer). B-05 also raises `MATTE_REFERENCE_MISSING` and `MATTE_CYCLE`, which document 28 does list; it raises them as ERROR from the command that would create the bad reference, where the catalog's WARNING wording describes one found while loading a project. Evidence basis: rejection has to be reportable to be verifiable, and the rows in `verification/B-05_model_table.md` that prove a rejected command changed nothing are keyed on these identifiers. Status PROVISIONAL because the names and severities are an agent's proposal, not the owner's decision. Consequence if changed: those rows change and document 28's catalog gains three entries.

D-22 / Scale is stored as a unit factor, not as a percentage / PROVISIONAL. Document 21 writes the transform chain as `T(position) * R(rotation) * S(scale/100) * T(-anchor)`, which reads the stored scale as a percentage where 100 means unchanged. Document 19 line 25 says scale "is percentage-like in UI but serialized as explicit numeric pairs", and B-05's shipped model already defaults a new layer's scale to `(1, 1)`. B-05a resolves the two in favour of the unit factor: the model and the renderer take 1.0 as identity, and the divide by 100 belongs at the UI boundary, next to the degree sign and the percent sign. Evidence basis: under the other reading every layer created by B-05 renders as a one-percent speck, and the default the owner would see on a new layer would have to be the number 100 in a field document 19 describes as a numeric pair. Status PROVISIONAL because document 21's wording still says `/100` and only the owner can amend it. Consequence if changed: document 21's transform formula and `Affine::from_transform` in `src/render.rs` change together, and every scale value in every saved project changes by a factor of a hundred. B-09 adds evidence the earlier reasoning did not have: every project fixture in `Fixtures/projects/`, all written by hand before any code existed, writes `"scale": { "base": [100, 100] }` for a layer at natural size. The stored form is therefore settled - the file says 100 - and the only live question is where the divide happens. `src/persist.rs` does it at the file boundary and nowhere else, so the model, the renderer and document 21's `S(scale/100)` are all satisfied at once and the fixtures round-trip byte for byte.

D-23 / Trace images are written display-encoded, not in the working space / PROVISIONAL. ADR-012's consequences say "Trace images are written in the working space and tagged with their alpha mode and color space", and the same ADR's rationale says the point of trace mode is that "the owner can see which layer went wrong". Those two pull against each other: the working space is linear light with premultiplied alpha, and a linear-light PNG opened in any ordinary viewer looks wrong, which is the one thing a diagnostic image must not do. B-05b writes trace PNGs through exactly the conversion export uses — unpremultiply in linear light, sRGB transfer function, quantise to 8 bits, straight alpha — and keeps the tagging requirement in full: every file carries `ColorSpace`, `AlphaMode` and a `WorkingSpace` chunk naming what it was converted from, and the manifest repeats it. Evidence basis: an untagged or unviewable trace image fails the ADR's own justification. Status PROVISIONAL because ADR-012's wording still says working space and only the owner can amend an ADR. Consequence if changed: trace images become 32-bit float or 16-bit linear PNGs the owner cannot judge by eye, and the facility would need a second, viewable output beside them.

D-24 / A structurally valid record of a parked feature is reported as `PROJECT_FEATURE_UNSUPPORTED` / PROVISIONAL. Document 28 names `EFFECT_UNSUPPORTED` for an effect this build does not have, and nothing at all for a record of a feature that is not an effect. Masks are the case that exists today: document 23 parks them with R-04, `Schemas/project-v0.schema.json` carries a `mask` field, and B-09 must therefore decide what happens when a valid project arrives with one. Silence is not available - CLAUDE.md and document 28 both forbid a silent fidelity fallback, and rendering the layer as though the mask were not there is exactly that. B-09 raises a WARNING under the proposed identifier `PROJECT_FEATURE_UNSUPPORTED`, preserves the record untouched through save, and excludes it from rendering. Evidence basis: the same reasoning document 28 already applies to `EFFECT_UNSUPPORTED`, applied to the only other parked feature the schema can express. Status PROVISIONAL because only the owner adds an identifier to document 28; `tests/b09_persistence.rs` asserts that this identifier is *not* in the catalogue, so the assertion fails and points at itself on the day it is added. Consequence if changed: the identifier is renamed in `src/diagnostics.rs` and in one test row, or masks become an ERROR that refuses the project, which would make a G1 build unable to open a project a G1-rest build wrote.

D-25 / Repeated frame-level warnings are logged in full three times, then summarised once with a count and frame ranges / PROVISIONAL. Document 28 requires that "repeated frame-level warnings should be rate-limited while retaining counts/ranges" and gives neither a number nor a shape. Two things had to be chosen to write any implementation at all: how many occurrences are logged before suppression begins, and whether the summary replaces them or follows them. B-04b logs the first three in full, suppresses the rest, and appends one summary per group carrying the total, the frame ranges, and the identifier, severity and remediation of the first occurrence. Grouping is by identifier and a caller-supplied subject, never by message text, because a frame-level message names its own frame and so no two are ever equal - grouping on the message would suppress nothing. Evidence basis: the reference shot raises one warning on each of twenty frames, and the rate-limited log of that walk is `verification/B-04b_frame_log_table.md`. Status PROVISIONAL because the number three and the log-then-summarise shape are the loop's choice, not document 28's. Consequence if changed: `FrameLog::new` already takes the limit as an argument, so a different number is a caller's decision and no code changes; ruling that the summary should replace the individual records rather than follow them changes `finish` and the expected strings of about six rows in one test.

D-26 / A render asked for a frame the composition does not have is refused as `COMMAND_INVALID_VALUE` / PROVISIONAL. Document 20 step 1 requires the composition frame to be validated before anything else is evaluated, and document 28's catalog names no identifier for failing that validation: its command identifiers describe a command that edits the document, and a render request edits nothing. B-08a reuses `COMMAND_INVALID_VALUE`, the identifier D-21 introduced for a command carrying a value the model cannot hold, on the reasoning that a frame number outside the composition's range is exactly that kind of value. It refuses rather than clamping: rendering the nearest frame the composition does have would answer a question nobody asked and hide the mistake. Evidence basis: `verification/B-08a_compose_table.md` refuses frame 240 and frame -1 of a 240-frame composition that starts at 0, and renders frame 239. Status PROVISIONAL because reusing a command identifier for a render request is an agent's reading, not the owner's, and document 28 may prefer a distinct name such as `RENDER_FRAME_OUT_OF_RANGE`. Consequence if changed: one identifier in `src/compose.rs`, one entry in `src/diagnostics.rs` and two rows in `verification/B-08a_compose_table.md`.

D-27 / The build item that owns export is B-10, not B-06 / PROVISIONAL, and registered as a conflict rather than settled. Document 15 line 55 names B-10 as the export writer and line 69 names B-06 as masks and mattes, while document 11 line 78 says the export half of T-07 "needs B-06", and `HANDOFF.md` repeated that as its suggested next session. One of the two is wrong, and the wrong one is dangerous rather than merely untidy: masks are PARKED by document 23 under R-04 and `AGENTS.md` forbids implementing a parked feature, so a fresh session reading `HANDOFF.md` would have started building something it is not allowed to build. Nothing about the export work itself depends on the answer, which is why this is a numbering correction and not a design decision: the export writer needs a rendered frame and the colour rules of document 20, neither of which is a mask. `HANDOFF.md`'s suggestion is corrected to name export by its work, not by a number. Evidence basis: the four cited lines, which cannot all be true. Status PROVISIONAL because only the owner renumbers a build item. Consequence if changed: document 11 line 78 and document 15 lines 55 and 69 are edited to agree; no code moves either way.

D-28 / An export whose range contains a frame with no drawing is blocked before anything is written, and writing those frames transparently is an explicit override / PROVISIONAL, and registered as a conflict rather than settled. Document 07 line 39 says the default missing-frame behaviour is a blocked final export, and that a hold-last or transparent override "must be a recorded project choice and appear in export warnings". Document 28 line 38 says the G1 default for an unresolved raster source is "transparent pixels plus persistent warning, not a colored placeholder in final export". Both cannot be the default of the same job. T-08 follows document 07, because it is the document that describes export and because refusing costs the owner a re-export while the other reading costs a delivered shot with a hole in it that nobody was made to look at. The other reading is not discarded: it is `MissingSource::RenderTransparent`, it writes the frames, and every affected frame is still named in the report. A second identifier was needed to say why a job was refused before it started - `EXPORT_BLOCKED_MISSING_MEDIA`, which document 28's catalog does not contain; its `MEDIA_SEQUENCE_GAP` describes a frame, not a refused job. Evidence basis: `verification/T-08_export_table.md` blocks frames 0 to 47 of the reference shot naming "Frames 14 to 15, 38 to 39" with nothing written, and exports the same range's middle six frames under the override with frame 14 empty and warned about. Status PROVISIONAL because which document governs the default is the owner's ruling, not an agent's. Consequence if changed: the default value of one field in `ExportRequest`, one identifier in `src/diagnostics.rs`, and five rows in `verification/T-08_export_table.md`. No pixels move either way.

D-29 / A negative composition frame keeps its minus sign in front of the padded digits in an exported file name / PROVISIONAL. Fixture FX-TIME-004 has a composition that starts at -12 and runs 24 frames, so an export of it has to name a file for frame -12, and no planning document says how. `shot_%04d.png` writes `shot_-0012.png`, which is one character wider than its neighbours and sorts before them in every file browser this build was checked against. The two alternatives were rejected for worse reasons: dropping the sign makes frame -12 and frame 12 the same file, and offsetting the numbering so the first exported frame is 0 makes a file name that cannot be traced back to the frame it came from. Evidence basis: `verification/T-08_export_table.md` exports the FX-TIME-004 shape as 24 files from `neg_-0012.png` to `neg_0011.png`. Status PROVISIONAL because file naming is what the owner hands to other software and only the owner knows what that software will accept. Consequence if changed: one function in `src/export.rs` and two rows in the table.

D-30 / Video export needs a codec, a container and a licence, and none of the three has been chosen / CLOSED on 2026-09-19 by the owner, see the end of this entry. It was OPEN, and deliberately not answered here. R-09 asks for a PNG sequence and T-08 built exactly that. Document 02 line 41 and document 07 speak of an export job without saying what it produces beyond the sequence, and every video encoder this build could reach is either a new dependency, a system binary that has to be found at runtime, or a licence that follows the output rather than the tool. That is a decision about what the owner is allowed to distribute, which is not an agent's to make. Nothing in `src/export.rs` assumes an image sequence beyond its own module: the frames it writes come from `render_frame`, and a video writer would consume the same buffers. Evidence basis: none is possible until a codec is named. Consequence if changed: a new module beside `src/png_out.rs`, a dependency and its licence recorded in the pack, and an output-format field on `ExportRequest`. **On 2026-09-19 the owner asked for MP4 export; D-72 lays out four roads and recommends the encoder Windows carries. D-30 stays open until the owner picks one.** **Later on 2026-09-19 the owner said "proceed with B-21b, B-21c, and B-21d" with that recommendation in front of them. The agent reads this as choosing the recommended road, the Media Foundation encoder Windows carries, with MP4 export Windows only and no codec shipped in the binary. The owner has not said the road's name in their own words, so B-21d confirms it with them before its first commit, and D-30 closes on that confirmation.** **B-21d was built on that road on 2026-09-19 and is held uncommitted.** The owner's next words were "proceed with B-21c, refuse or accept with your recommendation of the app's goals; then proceed with the next items as well", which again does not name the road, and this entry says the choice is not an agent's to make, so the agent did not read a delegation into it. `verification/B-21d_mp4_playtest.md` asks for the one sentence. **CLOSED on 2026-09-19. The owner's words, with the four roads read out to them: "road 1, Media Foundation confirmed". B-21d is committed on that. In the same message the owner asked what is friendly to macOS and Linux users and said "choose what is recommended and proceed with road along with road 1 as well": the agent's recommendation is road 2, a system ffmpeg found at run time, on systems that are not Windows only, because it too ships no encoder. That is B-21e. The MP4 file itself already plays on macOS and Linux; the road is about making one there.**

D-31 / This project's own code is licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0 / CLOSED by the owner on 2026-09-05. Whether to be open source was never open: D-03 and ADR-010 settled it early and deliberately, to remove ongoing licence review from a project with no legal reviewer. This entry was the remaining half - which licence - and the owner answered it: dual MIT or Apache-2.0, the convention almost every crate in this build already follows, and the terms under which a reuser may take either. The gap it named is closed with it: `Cargo.toml` now carries `license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"`, and `LICENSE-MIT` and `LICENSE-APACHE` are in the repository root, so the code is no longer under exclusive copyright and the repository now says what ADR-010 already decided. `publish = false` stays, because it prevents an accidental crates.io publish and has nothing to do with the licence. Two rows of `tests/b11_dependency_record.rs` hold it: the declared licence is the one chosen, and both texts it names exist. One thing is deliberately not settled: the copyright line in `LICENSE-MIT` reads `Copyright (c) 2026 anitastic-pixel`, the GitHub identity that owns the repository, because a legal name on a copyright notice is not an agent's to guess. That line was settled on its own terms as D-34, which keeps it. None of the 28 dependencies constrained the answer; all are permissive and none is copyleft. Evidence basis: `Cargo.toml`, `LICENSE-MIT`, `LICENSE-APACHE`, `verification/B-11_record_table.md`.

D-32 / Playback that cannot keep up drops frames and holds real time / CLOSED by the owner on 2026-09-05. SP-05 measured 24.9 fps at full resolution against a 24 fps target, about four percent of margin, so a viewer that plays a shot has to be told what to sacrifice when it falls behind. The two answers are not interchangeable: dropping frames keeps the timing true and may not show every drawing, while showing every drawing runs the shot slow and makes the timing a lie. The owner chose to hold real time, on the reasoning that judging timing and spacing is what playback is for, and inspecting an individual drawing is what frame stepping is for. Consequence: B-08's playback clock is wall-clock driven rather than frame-driven, it skips the frames it cannot deliver in time, and the viewer must report how many it skipped rather than hiding it - a silently dropped frame is a fidelity fallback and document 28 forbids those. Evidence basis: SP-05's measurement in `spikes/B-01_G0_spike_report.md`.

D-33 / The preview defaults to draft resolution with a visible indicator / CLOSED by the owner on 2026-09-05. SP-05 measured 145 fps at draft against 24.9 at full, so the default decides whether scrubbing is comfortable or marginal. R-06a already requires "a visible indication when preview quality differs from final export", which makes the draft default safe: the owner is never left believing they are looking at final pixels. Full resolution remains selectable, and export never passes through the display path at all, so nothing here can reach a delivered frame. Consequence: B-08 carries a resolution selection with draft as its initial value, an always-visible indicator of which is active, and a preview-versus-export pixel comparison at full resolution as part of its exit artifact. Evidence basis: SP-05, and R-06a's own wording. Qualified but not reopened on 2026-09-05 by `verification/B-08_preview_latency.md`, which measured the production preview path rather than a spike and found draft only slightly faster than full, because three quarters of a frame's cost is decoding cels and a drawing is decoded at its own size whatever the preview extent. Draft remains the faster of the two and remains the default; what the measurement changes is the expectation of what the default buys, and it is what fired the cache's revisit trigger. See D-37.

D-34 / The copyright holder named in `LICENSE-MIT` is `anitastic-pixel` / CLOSED on 2026-09-05, by the owner, who delegated the call to the agent's recommendation. D-31 chose the licence; it did not choose whose name sits on the notice. The answer is that the notice keeps what it already said - `Copyright (c) 2026 anitastic-pixel` - and the placeholder becomes the decision. Three reasons. It is the only identity this project is published under: it owns the repository and authors every commit in it, so the notice matches a record a reader can check rather than a name that appears nowhere else. A copyright notice is valid under a consistently used name and does not require a legal one. And a legal name in a public file is the one edit in this repository that publishes something about a person rather than about a program, which makes it the wrong kind of thing for an agent to write on the owner's behalf even when asked to decide - the cost of guessing wrong is not a broken build. The owner replaces the line the moment they want their legal name on it, and nothing else moves, because no check asserts the name: a name is not a thing a fixture can derive. Consequence if changed: one line in `LICENSE-MIT`. Evidence basis: `LICENSE-MIT`, which this decision leaves byte for byte as it was.

D-35 / The frame shown at rest is the work area's first frame / PROVISIONAL, taken by the agent on 2026-09-05 while building B-08's playback clock. Nothing in the requirements says which frame a viewer displays before playback has begun or after it stops, and a viewer has to display something. The alternatives are the first frame of the work area, the first frame of the composition, and whichever frame was last shown. The first was taken because playback loops within the work area, so any other choice shows a frame that pressing play would immediately leave, and because it makes the state before playback identical to the state at the start of playback. `Playback::at_rest` is that behaviour and `verification/B-08_preview_table.md` holds the row that pins it. Consequence if the owner disagrees: one function and one fixture row. The neighbouring question - what a viewer shows while the owner is dragging the time cursor rather than playing - is not answered here and is not yet needed, because nothing scrubs yet.

D-36 / Frames reach the viewer over a custom URI scheme rather than raw IPC / PROVISIONAL, taken by the agent on 2026-09-05 while starting B-08's window. SP-05 measured both and declined to choose: "Raw IPC and the custom URI scheme are within 4% of each other. There is no measured reason to prefer one on speed." Since speed does not separate them, the decision was made on the two things that do. A custom scheme hands the webview a frame as an ordinary resource with its own content type, so the picture arrives through the same path an image would and nothing has to be re-encoded into a message body; and it leaves the IPC channel carrying commands only, so a frame in flight cannot delay a stop or a scrub. Raw IPC remains the fallback and is a change of one function, because both were measured working on this machine at both resolutions with no wrong-size frames. Consequence if the owner or a later measurement prefers raw IPC: the transport function and its fixture row. Evidence basis: SP-05's table in `spikes/B-01_G0_spike_report.md`.

D-37 / The bounded preview cache is unparked, as a bounded cache of decoded cels / CLOSED on 2026-09-05, by the owner, who delegated the call to the agent's recommendation. Document 23 parks the cache with the trigger "measured preview latency, recorded with numbers", and notes that it "scores value 5 and was a version 0.2 Must, and it is still parked, because it is a performance optimization for a workflow that has never been run. Its trigger is a measurement, not an opinion." The measurement now exists: `verification/B-08_preview_latency.md`, taken on the production preview path against the reference shot, records a median of 81.69 ms per draft frame and 99.90 ms per full frame, which is 12.2 and 10.0 frames per second against a 24 fps target. Of the draft median, 75.15 ms is reading and decoding the four cels the frame needs and 6.53 ms is rendering. Decoding is the same cost at both resolutions, because a drawing is decoded at its own size before anything scales it, so D-33's draft default cannot reach it - the resolution choice buys back rendering time only. Nothing here is broken and no requirement is unmet: D-32 already decided what happens when playback cannot keep up, and it will keep up less often than SP-05's transport numbers suggested. What the cache would change is that a drawing shown twice is decoded once. What it would buy is measured rather than guessed at, in `verification/D-37_decode_cost.md`: a cel of this shot costs six to fifteen milliseconds to decode whatever it weighs on disk, because the cost is in writing 1920x1080 samples and not in inflating the file; the shot's 240 frames make 960 decode requests for 57 distinct drawings; a cache holding one cel avoids nothing at all, because the four layers are asked for in rotation; holding four avoids 54%; and holding all 57, which costs 473 MB of memory, avoids 94%. The single largest saving for the smallest cache is the background, which is the most expensive drawing in the shot and the one that never changes. Those figures come from the exposure sheet by arithmetic, in `verification/derive_d37_reuse.py`, and from a decoding measurement on this build; neither of them is a cache, and no cache was written before this entry was closed.

The answer is to build it, bounded four ways, because a fired trigger is permission to build the thing that was measured and nothing beyond it. **What is built is a cache of decoded source cels, not of finished frames.** Decoding is 75.15 ms of the 81.69 ms draft median and rendering is 6.53 ms, so a frame cache would chase eight percent of the cost while a cel cache can reach ninety; a frame cache stays unbuilt until a measurement asks for one, on the same discipline that produced this entry. The unit held is the cel after document 21's step 1 - decoded, tagged and converted into the working space - rather than the bytes off the disk, because the conversion is inside the time that was measured; its interpretation therefore joins the key, which is what document 27's key material asks for. **It has a memory ceiling and it evicts**, per document 27, because a cache that grows until the machine complains is a worse defect than the latency it removes. The ceiling is counted in bytes actually held, which is not the figure `verification/D-37_decode_cost.md` quotes: that table's 473 MB for 57 drawings counts a cel as 1920x1080x4 bytes, the shape it has on disk and on the wire, while this build holds a decoded cel as f32 samples in the working space - four times that, so the same 57 drawings are about 1.9 GB in memory. The reuse curve in that table is unaffected and is what the budget buys: nothing at one entry, 54% at four, 94% at all 57. **Export neither reads it nor writes it.** A full-resolution preview and an export of the same frame differ in 0 of 8,294,400 samples today and T-08's tables are byte-exact; a cache that can change one exported sample is the only failure here that would matter, and keeping it out of the export path is cheaper than proving it harmless inside one. **Masks (B-06 / R-04) and effects (B-07 / R-05) stay parked**, their own triggers unfired - this moves one row and not the table. B-08b enters G1 with document 27 as its specification, ADR-015 as its record, and T-06 as its exit artifact, which has to be a measurement of the same reference-shot playback before and after, not an assertion that a cache exists. Consequence if the owner reverses it: B-08b returns to G1-rest and the preview path loses a lookup.

D-38 / The dependency and licence record describes the Windows build only / PROVISIONAL, taken by the agent on 2026-09-06 while bringing the shell's dependencies in. `Cargo.lock` is the union of every platform cargo could resolve for, and until the shell arrived that distinction cost nothing: all twenty-eight crates were portable and the union was the build. With Tauri in the graph the lock file lists 435 crates, of which 264 compile on `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`; the other 171 are the GTK, Cocoa and Android windowing stacks. Document 10 asks for a bill of materials "generated from the final build inputs rather than a guessed list", and a record naming 171 crates that never compile here describes a program nobody has - while the licence archive beside it would claim a distribution carries code it does not. So `tools/gen_dependencies.py`, `tools/archive_licenses.py` and `tests/b11_dependency_record.rs` all resolve through `cargo metadata --filter-platform x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, which is the platform ADR-001 supports and the one CI runs. `Cargo.lock` is still read and still checked: every crate the build resolves must appear in it at the same version, so it remains the reproducibility record. It is PROVISIONAL because it is the agent's reading of what "final build inputs" means, and because a second supported platform would reopen it - the answer then is two filtered records or one union with a platform column, not this. Consequence if reversed: three call sites and a larger archive. Evidence basis: the counts above, from `cargo metadata` with and without the filter.

D-39 / The Windows web view contacts the network on its own account, and this project cannot stop it / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28 by the owner (D-175)**, answered by its first choice as D-173 recommends: the one Microsoft connection left after B-113 is accepted and stated in `docs/SUPPORTED_ENVELOPE.md`. Raised by the agent on 2026-09-05 while checking R-11. R-11 says the application works offline and sends nothing anywhere. Read off the build, that holds and is recorded in `verification/B-11_offline_table.md`: there is no HTTP client in this program, no crate that can open a socket is reachable from the code that reads projects and renders frames, the page is confined by its content security policy to two addresses on this machine, and it contains no other address. Watched while running, it does not hold: `verification/B-11_offline_run.md` records the release shell idle on a project for thirty seconds, during which `anime_compositor_app.exe` held no connection at all and `msedgewebview2.exe` — Microsoft's web view, running inside this application's window — held four to two addresses off this machine, both on port 443. One resolves to `cdns1.cox.net`, the machine's own internet provider's DNS service over HTTPS; the other has no reverse name and its low bits differ between runs. Six Chromium switches were set in `app/src/main.rs` to quieten it — no background networking, no component updates, no reporting, no pings, no sync, and an attempt at no DNS-over-HTTPS. The first run before any of them showed five off-machine connections in twenty seconds and every run since has shown four, so the switches are kept as a narrowing and not described as a fix. What this leaves is not a defect in this repository's code and cannot be resolved by editing it, which is why it is registered rather than worked on: a project's frames are drawn inside that process and a project's name and warnings arrive there as text, so nothing here can prove what does or does not travel over those four connections. It is OPEN because the three answers are the owner's. Accept it and say so plainly in the shipped documentation and the supported envelope, which is what this build does today. Or block the process outbound at the Windows firewall as part of installing, which is a per-machine instruction rather than code and which nothing in this repository can verify for someone else's machine. Or stop using the operating system's web view, which is a different architecture, a different program, and not a version 0.1 question. Consequence of the third: ADR-004 and the whole of the shell. Evidence basis: `verification/B-11_offline_run.md`, three runs, and `verification/B-11_offline_table.md`, 9 of 9 checks off the resolved build. The owner asked on 2026-09-27 for it to be tackled in G4 as B-113 (D-167).

D-40 / The preview cache budget that suits playback cannot suit scrubbing, and 128 MB is the one this build chose / ACCEPTED on 2026-09-06: leave the default at 128 MB. Raised by the agent on 2026-09-06 while measuring document 08's performance envelope. The budget is `cache::DEFAULT_BUDGET_BYTES`, 134,217,728 bytes, chosen by `verification/B-08b_cache_budget.md` on the workload that table measured: forty-eight consecutive frames, where 128 MB and 512 MB finished within a fraction of a millisecond of each other because playback asks for a cel again within a few frames or not at all. That reasoning is sound and this entry does not dispute it. What it did not cover is the other thing a person does to a shot, which is scrub. The arithmetic is not in doubt and needs no measurement to state: one cel of this composition costs 1920 x 1080 x 4 channels x 4 bytes = 33,177,600 bytes to hold, every frame of the reference shot needs four of them, and 134,217,728 divided by 33,177,600 is 4.04. **The viewer's default budget holds the frame being shown and nothing else.** Asking for that same frame again is a full hit; jumping anywhere else evicts all four cels and decodes four more, which is a cold render. **Document 08 line 41's "p95 cached seek-to-display at or below 100 ms" is nevertheless met at this budget on this machine, so this entry is a cost, not a failure report.** `verification/T-06_performance_envelope.md` walks all 240 frames of the shot in a scattered order at the default budget and measures 54.20 ms at the median and 67.75 ms at p95, inside the target; the slowest single seek of the 240 was 107.66 ms, which is outside it, and p95 is what document 08 asks about. What the budget costs shows as a comparison rather than as a breach: the same walk with every drawing already in memory is 20.06 ms at the median and 27.86 ms at p95, so scrubbing at the default pays about 2.7 times the median of a scrub that does not re-decode. Two things bound that headroom and both understate the cost: it is one machine, and it is four layers where document 08's own fixture has ten. Holding every distinct drawing in the shot is about 1.9 GB, the figure `src/cache.rs` records and `verification/D-37_decode_cost.md` derives; `verification/T-06_performance_envelope.md` is the measurement of what that buys and what the default costs. It is OPEN because the answer is a trade the owner makes and not one an agent should make for them: a larger default buys a scrub that does not re-decode, and spends memory on a machine whose headroom document 08 line 43 explicitly declines to assume - "Set initial budgets from observed headroom rather than assuming the entire machine is available." The three answers are to leave the default where it is and let scrubbing pay for itself, to raise it to something that holds a working neighbourhood of frames, or to make it a setting with a stated cost, which is the only one of the three that needs interface. Nothing here is a defect: D-32 already decided what happens when the viewer cannot keep up, and the cache is correct at every budget by `verification/B-08b_cache_table.md`. Consequence of raising it: one constant, and the memory line in `docs/SUPPORTED_ENVELOPE.md`. Evidence basis: the arithmetic above, `verification/B-08b_cache_budget.md` and `verification/T-06_performance_envelope.md`. Decided by the owner on 2026-09-06, the first of the three answers: the default stays at 128 MB and scrubbing pays for itself. The reason given back was the one in the entry - the target document 08 line 41 actually asks about is met at this budget on this machine, and document 08 line 43 declines to assume a machine's headroom, so spending memory that has not been measured on machines that have not been seen buys a comfort the specification never asked for. No code changes. This decision was taken on a four-layer shot, which is the floor D-41 describes; if B-06 and B-07 make the reference shot heavy enough that the measured p95 crosses 100 ms, that is a new measurement and reopens this entry rather than contradicting it. **REOPENED and re-decided on 2026-09-08. Default raised from 128 MB to 1 GiB; the reason is written in `src/cache.rs` (`DEFAULT_BUDGET_BYTES`).** The 2026-09-06 decision to stay at 128 MB carried a condition - a measured p95 crossing 100 ms reopens the entry - and it fired: on the ten-layer fixture one frame is 316.4 MiB, so 128 MB could not hold even one frame and a re-ask was never a warm seek. The raise took "ask for the frame just shown" from 371.71 ms to 190.15 ms at the median, the scattered walk from 369.83 ms to 290.92 ms, and the scrub p95 from 391.62 ms to 328.48 ms, every figure from `verification/T-06_declared_fixture.md` and seek-to-buffer rather than seek-to-display. It is a ceiling, not a reservation: about 1.0 GiB steady, 1.4 GiB peak on the heaviest shot, nothing at all during export (ADR-015). Bigger is not better, measured: 4 GiB buys nothing (324.92 ms p95), 6 GiB buys 267.23 ms only because it exceeds the about 5.5 GB the shot's 166 drawings cost, and nothing in between helps - six times the memory for 19% and still 2.7 times off target is not a trade to impose on every machine. What stays open: only whether the budget becomes a setting with a stated cost. What is not D-40's and needs its own entry: no budget reaches 100 ms, because what remains after decoding is compositing ten layers, two mattes and three effects - 268 ms a frame against a 41.7 ms clock. D-32 already says what the person sees meanwhile.

D-41 / The performance fixture document 08 declares cannot be built in this build / CLOSED on 2026-09-12: it was built, and the entry had gone stale. Raised by the agent on 2026-09-06 while measuring the envelope. Document 08 line 41 names the fixture the targets are set against: "1080p, 24 fps, 240 frames, ten raster layers, two alpha mattes and three simple effect instances". The reference shot is 1080p, 24 fps and 240 frames exactly, and there the agreement stops - it has four raster layers, no mattes and no effects, because mattes are B-06 and effects are B-07 and both are PARKED under D-12. There is no way to assemble the declared fixture without unparking one of them, and document 23 makes each park's revisit trigger the owner's to fire. This is registered rather than worked around because the alternative is worse than the gap: substituting the shot for the fixture and reporting the numbers under document 08's heading would state a measured capability the build does not have, and a measurement of four layers is not a measurement of ten. `verification/T-06_performance_envelope.md` therefore measures what exists, says at the top of the file that it is not the declared fixture, and states every figure as a floor rather than an estimate - six more layers cost more, and the two parked features are the two document 08 itself says need bounds expansion and a second evaluation of alpha. The three answers are the owner's: accept the reference shot as the performance fixture and amend line 41 to say so, keep line 41 and accept that the envelope stays unmeasured until a park lifts, or fire a revisit trigger. Consequence of the first: one line of document 08 and a note in this register. Evidence basis: document 08 line 41, document 15 line 69, and `verification/B-08a_project.json`, which has four layers. Resolved on 2026-09-06 as a consequence of the D-12 lift rather than by a choice between the three answers: with B-06 and B-07 unparked, the second answer becomes the live one. Document 08 line 41 is kept as written, and the declared fixture - ten raster layers, two alpha mattes, three effect instances - becomes buildable once B-07 lands. Until then every figure in `verification/T-06_performance_envelope.md` stays stated as a floor and the file keeps saying at the top that it is not the declared fixture. This entry stays OPEN, and what closes it is the re-measurement against the real fixture after B-07, not an edit to line 41. **Closed on 2026-09-12 by the condition this entry set for itself.** B-07 landed, the declared fixture was built, and the re-measurement exists: `verification/T-06_declared_fixture.json` is ten raster layers, two alpha mattes and three effect instances at 1080p, 24 fps, 240 frames, and `verification/T-06_declared_fixture.md` measures it. Line 41 is unedited, which was the point. Nothing was decided here; a condition was met and the register had not caught up, which is why this closes as CLOSED rather than as one of the three answers.

D-42 / A layer used as a matte stops being drawn in its own right because a flag says so, not because it was switched off / CLOSED on 2026-09-06, by the owner, who delegated the call to the agent's recommendation. Document 21 step 5 says the matte layer is "not separately composited into the final stack", and document 19 gives `MatteReference` nothing to say that with: it "stores another layer ID and mode `alpha`" and no more. B-06 needed an answer before it could render a matte at all, because a matte layer that is also drawn is a different picture from one that is not. The first answer written into this build was to read the matte layer's own `enabled: false` that way: a disabled layer is not composited, which is literally what step 5 asks for, and it needed no new field. That answer is now rejected. It makes one field mean two unrelated things, and the cost lands exactly where this project can least afford it - on an owner who verifies by reading project files and looking at pictures. A file showing a layer switched off while that layer visibly shapes the picture reads as a fault to be chased, not as a setting that was chosen, and there is nothing in the file to tell the two apart. Worse, it is not reversible: switching that layer back on to see it would change what the matte does, so the one obvious way to inspect it destroys the thing being inspected. What is built instead is `matte_only`, a boolean on `MatteReference` - on the layer that *uses* the matte, saying the layer it points at is not also drawn. False is the neutral value and the one a project written before this decision gets when it is opened, so no existing file changes what it renders. `Command::SetMatte` carries the flag, so it is undoable like anything else, and `src/persist.rs` writes and reads it, so it survives the file. Evidence: seven rows under "matte-only" in `verification/B-06_mask_table.md`, including that the matte layer is still drawn unless the flag is set, that setting it removes exactly one layer from the plan while the layer that uses the matte stays matted, that undo puts it back, and that saving and reopening keeps it. Consequence if the owner reverses it: one field, one command field, two lines of persistence, and the earlier reading returns along with the ambiguity above.

D-43 / A mask outline this build refuses to draw gets its own diagnostic identifier / CLOSED on 2026-09-06, by the owner, who chose it directly. Document 19 makes a self-intersecting mask "unsupported in G1" and requires it to be "rejected or normalized only through an explicit command", and a polygon of fewer than three vertices encloses nothing. Both were already refused, but under borrowed identifiers: a command was refused with `COMMAND_INVALID_VALUE`, which is document 28's generic "the value was wrong", and a project file already holding one warned with `PROJECT_FEATURE_UNSUPPORTED`, which D-24 had introduced for a record of a *parked* feature. Neither still fits. Masks are not parked as of D-12, so `PROJECT_FEATURE_UNSUPPORTED` on a mask now says something false about why. And a generic identifier cannot be searched for, counted, or given remediation text of its own, which is the whole reason document 28 keeps a catalogue rather than one error. `MASK_INVALID_OUTLINE` is added to document 28: ERROR when a command would create such a mask, refused outright; WARNING when a project on disk already holds one, in which case the outline is preserved exactly, the layer is drawn unmasked, and the exported output reports that its fidelity is incomplete. That last clause is what made this more than a rename. Before it, a mask that could not be drawn was skipped at render time with nothing recorded per frame - a silent fidelity fallback, which CLAUDE.md forbids and which would have let a picture go out with a mask quietly missing from it. `src/compose.rs` now records the diagnostic on every frame it happens, and `src/export.rs` treats either identifier as grounds for the incomplete-fidelity mark. `PROJECT_FEATURE_UNSUPPORTED` stays in the catalogue and nothing produces it today; it is what a future parked-feature record would use. Evidence: two command rows in `verification/B-06_mask_table.md`, three rows in `verification/B-09_persistence_table.md` covering warn-do-not-draw-do-not-lose including a save-and-reopen of the crossed outline, and the fidelity rows of `verification/T-08_export_table.md`, which were re-pointed at a crossed mask because the track matte they used before is a feature this build now draws. Consequence if reversed: one enum variant, four call sites and a catalogue row.

D-44 / The effect stack is not tiled, so the comparison R-05 asked for has nothing to compare / CLOSED on 2026-09-06, by the owner, who delegated the call to the agent's recommendation. Document 21 line 119 requires an operation whose output pixel depends on a neighbourhood to be evaluated with a margin "declared by the operation rather than assumed by the renderer", line 121 names the blur as the first operation to exercise it and calls that "a direct reason R-05 sits in G1-rest", and R-05 was written to match: B-07 was to "show that a tiled render equals the full-frame reference math within tolerance". When B-07 came to write that comparison there was nothing to compare. `effects::apply_stack` runs inside `compose::resolve_layer`, on the layer's own pixels in layer space, at document 21's step 3; what it hands on is a `LayerDraw` whose source is a finished buffer. `render::render` then cuts tiles out of the *composition* and samples each layer's finished source through that layer's transform, so by the time a tile exists every blur in the frame is already a set of pixel values. Effects are never tiled, no effect declares a tile margin, line 119 is satisfied vacuously, and the region-of-interest equivalence R-05 named cannot be demonstrated because there is no region-of-interest optimisation to demonstrate it about. The alternative - evaluating effects per tile, expanding each tile by the radius and cropping - is the right design for a compositor that keeps everything lazy at output resolution, and this build is not that one: it would mean running the same blur once per tile a layer touches and reconciling the overlaps, which buys a new class of bug, the seam, in exchange for nothing this build needs. Document 21's own render order also puts effects at step 3 and the transform at step 4, so whole-layer evaluation is the literal reading. What B-07 proves in place of the named experiment is the property that would have failed had this been got wrong: **the finished frame does not depend on the tile size.** `verification/B-07_effects_table.md` renders one blurred frame at tile sizes 1, 3, 7, 16, 32 and 64, three of which do not divide the frame, and requires six byte-identical results. Line 89's separate requirement, that each effect declare its input bounds expansion, is honoured and checked for all four effect kinds, and the check that it is honoured *correctly* is the alpha centroid of the whole frame, which stays at (15.50, 15.50) when a blur grows the layer buffer by the kernel radius on all four sides. The cost is memory: a layer carrying a blur holds an expanded buffer for the life of the plan, about ten per cent at 1920x1080 with a sigma of 10, bounded by a stored parameter rather than by anything the renderer chooses. ADR-017 is the architecture record. Evidence basis: document 21 lines 89 and 119-121, ADR-011, `src/effects.rs`, `src/compose.rs` and `verification/B-07_effects_table.md`. Consequence if a later stage moves effect evaluation into the tile loop - a GPU path, a lazy graph, preview-resolution effects - this entry and ADR-017 are void, line 119 applies in full, and the tiled-equals-full-frame comparison becomes the check that must be written; the tile-size-invariance rows are the ones that would catch such a change going wrong.

D-45 / Changing an effect's settings is a fourth command that document 24 does not list / PROVISIONAL, decided by the agent on 2026-09-06 while building B-07. Document 24 gives the effect stack three commands - `effect.add`, `effect.delete` and `effect.toggle_bypass` - and no way to change a parameter once an effect exists. Adding an effect and bypassing it are not enough to use one: the whole of R-05 is choosing a sigma, a number of stops and a colour, and a build that could only delete and re-add an effect to change its sigma would lose that instance's identity and its place in the stack every time. The alternative to a command is editing the property directly, which document 26 forbids in effect: undo is defined over commands, so a change made outside one is a change that cannot be undone, and the register would silently stop matching the file. `Command::SetEffectParameters` is therefore built as the fourth, carrying the instance ID and a full replacement of that effect's parameters. It refuses two things rather than coercing them: parameters for a different effect type than the instance holds, and out-of-contract values, both with the identifiers D-46 describes. It is PROVISIONAL rather than CLOSED because it is an agent's reading of a gap rather than the owner's decision, and because document 24 is an interaction map - the command exists and is undoable, but nothing decides yet what gesture in the interface produces it. Evidence basis: document 24 lines 35-37, document 26's definition of undo over commands, and the command rows of `verification/B-07_effects_table.md`, which cover the refusals, that a refusal leaves the stack untouched, and that a parameter change is undoable. Consequence if the owner reverses it: one command variant, one row of document 24, and parameter editing has to be re-answered before the effect stack is usable.

D-46 / An invalid effect parameter is an error in a command and a warning in a file, and the file is never repaired / PROVISIONAL, decided by the agent on 2026-09-06 while building B-07. Document 28 gives `EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID` one severity, ERROR, and one remediation, "reject edit/load as appropriate", which decides nothing for the case that actually matters: a project already on disk holding a negative sigma. Rejecting the load loses the whole project over one number. Repairing the number silently changes what the owner saved without saying so, which is the silent fidelity fallback CLAUDE.md forbids. The answer built is the one D-43 gave `MASK_INVALID_OUTLINE` a day earlier, and it is the same answer for the same reason: ERROR when a command would create the value, refused outright and the stack left exactly as it was; WARNING when a file already holds one, in which case the record is preserved unrepaired, that one effect is bypassed while the rest of the stack still runs, the diagnostic is recorded on every frame it happens rather than once at load, and the exported output reports that its fidelity is incomplete. The per-frame recording is the part that is not bookkeeping: without it a picture could go out with an effect quietly missing from it and nothing in the render saying so. Evidence basis: document 28 line 24 as written, D-43's precedent, `src/persist.rs`, `src/compose.rs`, `src/export.rs`, and the command and persistence rows of `verification/B-07_effects_table.md`. It is PROVISIONAL because it is an agent's reading; reversing it costs the two-severity row in document 28 and one branch in the loader.

D-47 / A ten-layer shot costs about six times the frame budget a 24 fps target allows, and no cache can pay it / ACCEPTED on 2026-09-12: keep the 24 fps target and say in the envelope that a ten-layer shot misses it. **Finding amended on 2026-09-28 by D-174 (D-175):** measured the way the viewer runs, the ten-layer shot plays at about 5 ms a frame when its drawings fit in the memory setting, and misses the deadline only when they do not; the decision to keep the 24 fps target stands. Raised by the agent on 2026-09-09 while closing D-40. D-40 was the cache budget and D-41 was the fixture not existing; neither is the largest number the declared fixture produced, and `verification/T-06_declared_fixture.md` says plainly that the finding belongs in an entry of its own. **Measured, on the fixture document 08 line 41 declares: 264.17 ms a frame at draft against the 41.7 ms a 24 fps clock allows, and 0 of ten warm loops came in under the deadline.** That is a factor of about six, and a factor is not a margin. **This is not a regression and the entry does not report one.** Two and a half times the layers of the four-layer reference shot costs about 3.2 times the frame, which the layer count alone accounts for; `verification/T-06_performance_envelope.md` has the four-layer shot sitting on the deadline and flipping either side of it between runs. The shot document 08 declares is more work than this build does in real time, and the raised cache budget cannot change that: with every cel of a frame already in memory what remains is compositing ten layers, two mattes and three effects, which is not a cache's to save. What the person sees is already decided and this entry does not reopen it: D-32 holds real time and drops the frames it cannot make, so the shot plays at the right speed and shows fewer frames rather than playing slowly. **What is undecided is the target itself, and there are three answers.** Keep 24 fps for a ten-layer shot and accept that draft preview drops frames on it, which costs nothing to choose and makes document 08 line 41 a target this build knowingly misses. Lower the declared target to what the fixture actually reaches, which is honest and changes a specification. Or reach it by doing the work differently, which is `Markdown/32_Performance_Architecture_Investigation.md` and is the only one of the three that is engineering rather than a sentence. D-48 / ADR-015 bound 3 says the export path "gains nothing and must not", and two units in a row could not tell whether that forbids a cache or forbids threads / ACCEPTED on 2026-09-12: amend the wording to name the cache, which is what the bound defends. Raised by the agent on 2026-09-10 while closing the performance batch. P-03(b) drew the boundary and `verification/P-10_encode.md` records it again; a sentence that has been read twice and left open twice is written down rather than guessed at a third time. **What bound 3 protects is real.** A full-resolution preview matching an export in 0 of 8,294,400 samples is a property this build has, and a cache reachable from export is the obvious way to lose it. **What bound 3 says is wider than that, and the build already contradicts the wider reading.** ADR-011 has rendered every frame tiled across the rayon pool since B-05a, and `crate::export` renders through `compose::render_frame` like everything else, so threads have been running on the export path since before there was a cache to keep off it. `verification/D-48_export_threads.md` says so as a check that runs on every build: the same eight export frames in a pool of one thread and in a pool of twenty-four, **8 of 8 identical**, both holding `CelCache::none()`. The guard was made to fail before it was trusted - one byte flipped in the second render and the test reports the fixture, the frame and both pool sizes. **Recommendation: amend the wording rather than widen the bound.** State bound 3 as what it defends - *the export path neither reads nor writes the cel cache or the effect cache* - and the open question dissolves, because a thread count is not a cache. One thing worth knowing before the amendment is written: the parallel decode as built is `CelCache::prewarm`, which returns early when the budget is zero, and its own comment gives the reason - decoding in advance into a cache that cannot store is work thrown away twice. So the amendment does not by itself give export a parallel decode; it removes the reason not to build one, and building one would be a unit of its own with its own byte-equality evidence. Evidence basis: `verification/D-48_export_threads.md`; `tests/p03_byte_equality.rs`, whose manifest P-10 ran 960 of 960 lines identical between a serial encode and one spread over twenty-four threads; `src/render.rs` line 314, which already documents that the result does not depend on the worker count. Consequence if the owner declines: nothing breaks and export keeps decoding serially; the cost is that the same question reopens in every future unit that touches the decode. Owner's to decide; nothing in the build waits on it. **Decided on 2026-09-12: amend, in the words this entry recommended.** ADR-015 bound 3 now reads that the export path neither reads nor writes the cel cache or the effect cache, and the sentence that said it "gains nothing" is kept beside it as the record of what was meant rather than deleted. A thread count is not a cache: `verification/D-48_export_threads.md` checks on every build that the same eight export frames come out identical in a pool of one thread and a pool of twenty-four. This does not give export a parallel decode and is not meant to - `CelCache::prewarm` returns early at a zero budget, and building a parallel export decode would be a unit of its own with its own byte-equality evidence. It removes the reason not to.

D-49 / The supported envelope is measured with a cache no shipped viewer builds / **CLOSED on 2026-09-28 by D-174, accepted by the owner (D-175)**: `verification/B-114_viewer_envelope.md` measures the viewer's own cache and `docs/SUPPORTED_ENVELOPE.md` is restated from it.
