D-50 / Draft-resolution cels would make the preview cheaper and would change what the preview shows / DECLINED on 2026-09-12: a draft preview is the same drawings at a smaller size, not different drawings. Raised by the agent on 2026-09-10. This is the register entry document 15's P-06 says is owed before any of that work could land, and it is written now because the measurement it needed exists: `verification/P-06_draft_cels.md`, with six pictures beside it. **The saving is in bytes, not milliseconds.** Held at full resolution the reference shot's 56 distinct drawings are 1.73 GiB and the declared fixture's 166 are 5.13 GiB, both over the gibibyte D-40 sets; held at a quarter on each side they are 0.11 and 0.32 GiB, both several times inside it. The draft frame time roughly halves - 1.914 ms to 1.007 and 4.141 to 1.944 - but reducing one frame's cels costs 42.3 and 135.5 ms, so a reduced cel pays for itself only after 47 and 62 frames of reuse. It is a cache change wearing a renderer's clothes: what it buys is a cache that fits, and the frame time is the missing that stops. **The pixels move, and a person can see it.** More than half of every draft frame's 129,600 pixels differ once encoded to eight bits, by up to 46 of 255 on the reference shot and 93 on the declared fixture. The amplified difference pictures put it on edges and fine detail with flat areas black: averaging sixteen source pixels is not the same as taking one bilinear sample of them, and the reduced frame is the less aliased of the two. Which is *correct* the measurement cannot say, and neither can this entry. **The question for the owner is not whether it is faster.** It is whether D-33's sentence - the preview defaults to draft and the viewer must say when the preview differs from export - covers a difference of this size, or whether a draft preview is required to be the same picture as the export at a smaller size. **No recommendation is offered**, because the two answers differ on what a draft preview is *for*, and that is not a question measurement reaches. Evidence basis: `verification/P-06_draft_cels.md` and its pictures, measured on the D-01 reference machine in release on 2026-09-10; ADR-015 keeps the export byte-identical either way, checked over eight frames. Consequence if accepted: document 14 gains a pixel-changing entry, D-33's wording is revisited, and P-06 becomes a unit rather than a branch. Consequence if declined: P-06 stays measured and unbuilt, and the 1 GiB budget keeps holding a fraction of either fixture. Owner's to decide; nothing in the build waits on it. **Decided on 2026-09-12: declined, and the answer to the question this entry actually asked is written down rather than left implied.** D-33's sentence does not cover a difference of this size. **A draft preview is the same drawings at a smaller size.** It may be cheaper, it may be coarser, and it is allowed to differ from the export - but what it differs by must be the size it is shown at, not which pixels the drawings are made of. The reason is what this product is: a cel finishing compositor whose whole job is judging a drawing. More than half of every draft frame's pixels moving, by up to 46 of 255 on the reference shot and 93 on the declared fixture, concentrated on edges and fine detail, is a change to the thing being judged. That the reduced frame is the *less* aliased of the two does not help and is part of the objection: a preview that flatters the artwork is worse than one that is merely smaller, because the artist corrects against what they are shown. The saving declined is a cache that fits, not a frame time - the entry says so itself, 1.914 ms to 1.007 - and a cache that fits is not worth the picture. What would reopen this is not a measurement but a control: draft-resolution cels offered as a switch the artist throws, labelled with what it changes, the way OpenToonz and After Effects offer theirs. That is a different entry from this one, which proposed them as the default. P-06 stays measured and unbuilt.

D-51 / GPU or CPU acceleration for the effects / ACCEPTED on 2026-09-12: do not start a GPU path; measure the blur drag first, as P-14. Raised by the owner on 2026-09-11 at the second sitting with the window, finding 9 in `verification/B-12_run_notes.md`, and written here rather than started. **ADR-006 holds as written**: one tile-based multithreaded CPU renderer, and no GPU backend "until a measured result on a real shot on the reference machine shows the CPU path is too slow for the workflow"; ADR-011's tile contract is what makes a GPU path a dispatch port later rather than a rewrite. **What is already there.** The blur is separable, two one-dimensional passes rather than one two-dimensional kernel; a frame is cut into tiles across the machine's threads (P-03); and P-11 caches each effect instance's result keyed by the value of its settings, so a blur whose radius has not changed costs nothing on the next frame. **What the measurement says**, from `verification/P-11_effect_cache.md`, the declared ten-layer fixture on the D-01 machine in release on 2026-09-10: before the cache the blur was 111.749 to 123.073 ms of a frame and the exposure and the tint together under two milliseconds; with it a first playthrough is 46.729 to 50.817 ms a frame in draft. **What the sitting saw was not this.** The effect that "did not show until the layer was toggled" is finding 10: a setting was not sent until its field lost focus, and the toggle is what took the focus. W-07 sends it as it is typed. **What is not measured** is the case the cache cannot help: a blur while its radius is being dragged, where every pixel of drag is a new value and the whole blur runs again per frame. No number is claimed for it here. **Recommendation: do not start a GPU path.** Measure the drag first, as a P-unit - the frame time during a live blur drag on the declared fixture, recorded with machine, build and configuration - and if it is over budget, the CPU answers come before a second renderer: a blur at draft resolution during the drag, since the blur's cost scales with the pixels it touches, and a bounded preview radius. A GPU path is ADR-006's own escape clause and needs the measured result that clause names. Consequence if accepted: a measurement unit joins document 15 and nothing in the renderer changes. Consequence if declined and a GPU path is ordered: ADR-006 is revised, the dispatch port ADR-011 anticipated becomes the unit, and every effect gains a second implementation that document 25's fixtures must hold to the same bytes. Owner's to decide; nothing in the build waits on it. **Decided on 2026-09-12: the recommendation as written. ADR-006 is not reopened, and P-14 joins document 15** - the frame time during a live blur-radius drag on the declared fixture, on the D-01 machine in release, which is the one case the P-11 cache cannot help and the one number ADR-006's escape clause asks for. The reason for not starting a GPU path is not that a GPU would be slower. It is that this project is verified by fixtures read by someone who cannot read code, and a second renderer means every effect fixture held to the same bytes on hardware that is not bit-identical between vendors or driver versions. That is the unverifiable surface area document 01 calls worse than an absent feature, bought with a measurement nobody has taken yet. If P-14 comes back over budget, the CPU answers this entry already names come first - the blur at draft resolution during a drag, and a bounded preview radius - because both are smaller than a second renderer and neither changes an exported pixel. **Measured on 2026-09-12: `verification/P-14_blur_drag.md`, and ADR-006 is left alone with evidence.** A sixty-move drag of the blur's radius from sigma 4.1 to 10.0 source pixels at the page's own 0.1 step, the playhead held on one frame of the declared ten-layer fixture, on the D-01 machine in release: at draft the median frame of the drag is 34.8 ms and the worst single frame 40.0, which is 0.96x the 41.667 ms a 24 fps clock allows; at full the median is 52.8 and the worst frame 59.7, which is 1.43x it. The case this entry said was not measured is now measured, and it behaves as predicted: the blur is evaluated on every one of the sixty frames, so P-11's cache does nothing for the effect being dragged, and the blur is 64.1% of a draft frame and 41.4% of a full one. **The escape clause is not triggered.** ADR-006 opens a GPU path only on "a measured result on a real shot on the reference machine shows the CPU path is too slow for the workflow", and a drag that keeps up with the pointer at draft and runs at about seventeen updates a second at full is not that result. Neither of the two CPU answers this entry names is started either, for the same reason. What the measurement does not say is on its own page and not repeated here: one machine, one run, and a drag that stops at sigma 10, where a blur's cost grows with the pixels it touches.

D-52 / Eased keyframes and motion paths / ACCEPTED IN PART on 2026-09-12: the ease is specified and named here; the motion path stays open. Raised by the owner on 2026-09-11 at the third sitting with the window, finding 5 in `verification/B-12_run_notes.md`, and written here rather than started. The owner's picture: a shape layer whose position is keyframed along a path, easing in and out of parts of it, shown on the timeline as one solid bar beside the exposure-sheet layers whose bars are many blocks. **What R-03 says** is hold and linear interpolation, and document 20 is what the fixtures pin: a keyframe on an integer frame carrying the mode used to the next, a linear segment component-wise linear. **What is already there:** position, anchor, scale, rotation and opacity keyframe with hold and linear in the core, and a keyframed solid renders as the owner describes. The timeline draws no key on any bar yet, so that solid is a bar with nothing on it. **What is not there:** an ease, which is a curve of the value against time between two keys, and a spatial path, which is a curve of the position through its keys rather than straight lines between them. Both change what a frame between two keys looks like, so both are changes to documents 20 and 21 and the file format, with fixture rows of their own, and neither is window work. **Recommendation: two steps, the second not yet.** First, presentation, as W-10: a diamond beside each property to set or remove a key, and a mark on the bar at each keyframe, as After Effects draws its diamonds; moving a key along the bar is W-11, and every fixture holds. Second, when the owner wants an ease, a specification decision that names the curve - After Effects' easy ease is a cubic Bezier of value against time with a tangent at each key, and Premiere's is the same - and the field in the file that carries it, with a fixture that pins one eased segment to exact values before any code is written. A motion path through the keys is a third decision and a different curve, and can wait for the ease. Consequence if accepted: W-10 sets, removes and draws the keys, W-11 drags them; easing waits for its fixture. Consequence if declined: the solid bar stays blank, R-03 stays hold and linear, and the owner animates an ease by placing more keys. Resolved on 2026-09-12, the second step taken and the third still not. **The curve is a cubic Bezier of the value against time**, stored as the two inner control points of a curve whose ends are pinned at (0,0) and (1,1) and written `[x1, y1, x2, y2]` - the four numbers CSS writes as `cubic-bezier()` and After Effects draws as two handles in its value graph. It was chosen over a tangent-and-influence pair, which is how After Effects presents the same curve in its own dialog, because the two describe the same shape and only one of them is a shape a reader can check by hand: handles are points on a graph, while influence and speed are a polar encoding of those points that has to be decoded before anyone can say whether a number is right. The mode is a third value of the existing `interp` field, `ease`, carried by the keyframe the segment starts at exactly as `hold` and `linear` are, so document 20's keyframe model does not change shape and every existing fixture holds unchanged. `x1` and `x2` are refused outside 0 to 1 rather than clamped, because a handle outside its own segment folds the curve back and gives one frame two values, and document 28 says what cannot be understood is diagnosed; `y1` and `y2` are left unbounded on purpose, because a `y` past its end is an overshoot and an animator means it. **The fixture came before the code**, which is what this entry asked for: FX-EASE-001 to 005 in document 25, generated by `tools/ease_reference.py`, which solves the same equation by bisection in another language written from document 20 rather than from the build. FX-EASE-001 is the curve that is exactly linear and FX-EASE-002 is easy ease, whose value is exactly half way at half the segment; FX-EASE-005 exists because the first two have their `x` handles at a third and two thirds, where `x(t) = t` and the solve is free, and a fixture set made only of those would not notice a solver that never worked. Documents 03, 19, 20 and 25 are amended. **What stays open is the motion path**, the third decision this entry named: an eased position still travels a straight line between its keys, faster and slower, and a curve through the keys in space is a different curve with fixtures of its own. Consequence of this part being accepted: R-03 widens by one word, the file format gains one optional array, and an artist gets an ease without placing more keys. Not decided here is whether the ease is edited by a graph or only by a preset, which is window work and follows this: both were built, the preset beside the diamond in the inspector and a graph editor sharing the timeline's panel, and `verification/B-12a_transform_table.md` holds their rows. **The third step is taken on 2026-09-12 and is D-53**, which names the spatial curve and pins it; nothing in this entry is reopened by it, because a path changes where the fraction lands and an ease changes what the fraction is, and the two do not touch.

D-53 / The motion path through the position keys / ACCEPTED on 2026-09-12: the spatial curve is named here and pinned by fixtures before any code. Raised by D-52, which named three decisions, settled two and left this one: "an eased position still travels a straight line between its keys, faster and slower, and a curve through the keys in space is a different curve with fixtures of its own." **What is already there:** position keyframes with hold, linear and eased interpolation, where every segment between two keys is the straight line joining them and an ease changes only how fast the layer travels it. **What is not there:** any way to make a layer arc. The owner's picture in D-52 was a shape layer "keyframed along a path", and a path is the part of that sentence nothing in the build answers yet. **The curve is a cubic Bezier in composition pixels**, four control points per segment: the first key's value, that value plus the key's outgoing handle, the second key's value plus its incoming handle, and the second key's value. The handles are stored as offsets in composition pixels from the key that owns them, because a handle is a thing an artist drags on the canvas and an offset in pixels is what they see when they drag it; an absolute point would say the same thing in a form that moves when the key moves. This is the same curve type as the ease and for the same reason - it is the shape After Effects draws, and it is a shape a reader can check by hand - but it is a different curve doing a different job, and the two are independent: **the ease says when the layer is a given fraction of the way along, and the path says where that fraction is.** **The parameter is the temporal fraction, not arc length.** This is the one real choice in the entry and the one with a cost. Feeding the fraction straight into the Bezier makes a segment a polynomial: exact, hand-checkable, evaluated without a solver, and - the part that decides it - reducing to today's straight line exactly, so no existing fixture moves. Arc-length parameterization is what After Effects does and would keep a layer at a constant speed under linear timing, but it needs a numerical length integral and a root solve on top of it, which means the fixtures would pin the output of a chosen method rather than the answer to an equation, and the ease's own solve would stack on top of it. **The cost of the choice, stated plainly: on a curved segment with uneven handles the layer speeds up and slows down a little even under linear timing.** An artist who does not want that evens the handles, which is a thing they can see. If that turns out to be wrong in the owner's hands, arc length can be added later as a per-segment choice without invalidating one fixture written here, because the straight-line case is identical either way. **A segment with no handles is the straight line, and the handles that make it one are at the thirds** - one third and two thirds of the way to the other key - exactly as `[1/3, 1/3, 2/3, 2/3]` is the ease that is linear. Handles of *zero* are deliberately not the default and are a different segment: they give the straight line at an easy-ease speed. So an absent field and a linear segment are the same segment, and every fixture that exists today holds unchanged. **Validation:** the handles are unbounded, which is the opposite of the ease, and the asymmetry is the point. An `x` handle outside its segment in time folds the curve back and gives one frame two values, which document 19 diagnoses; a handle longer than its segment in space makes the layer loop back on itself, which is a thing an animator means. The field is valid only on `position`; on any other property it is diagnosed rather than ignored, under the `PROJECT_SCHEMA_INVALID` that already covers an out-of-range ease, and document 28 gains no new identifier because nothing here is a feature this build declines to draw. On a `hold` segment it is preserved and has no effect, for the reason D-52 gave about an ease on a last keyframe. **The fixture came before the code**, which is what D-52 asked for: FX-PATH-001 to 004 in document 25, generated by `tools/path_reference.py`, which evaluates the curve by de Casteljau against document 20 while the build expands the polynomial, so an agreement is two answers and not one answer twice. FX-PATH-001 is the straight line written as a path, FX-PATH-003 is a curved segment with an ease on it and exists to show the two curves composing, and FX-PATH-004 is the handle longer than its own segment. Documents 03, 19, 20 and 25 are amended; document 28 is not, and document 21 is not, because a path changes what number `position` holds at a frame and changes nothing about the transform that number feeds. Consequence if accepted: R-03 widens by three words, the file format gains one more optional array on position keyframes, and an artist gets an arc without placing more keys. Consequence if declined: a layer travels in straight lines forever and an arc is approximated by placing keys along it, which is what the owner is doing now. Not decided here is how a handle is dragged on the canvas, which is window work and follows this the way the graph editor followed the ease.

D-57 / Parenting: a layer may ride on another layer's transform / ACCEPTED on 2026-09-15 by the owner ("I accept it"), written by the agent under D-56 with its fixtures first. **What is already there:** every layer is placed on its own, by document 21's transform. **What is not there:** any way to say that a mouth cel moves with its head cel, other than keying both the same. **The field.** A layer gains an optional `parent`: the ID of another layer in the same composition. Absent or null means no parent, and the file carries the field only when it is set, so no existing project changes. **The math.** The parent's whole transform is applied after the child's own, `M_world(child) = M_world(parent) * M(child)`, up the chain to a layer with no parent. A child's position is therefore a point in its parent's layer space. Position, rotation, scale and anchor reach the child through that product; **opacity, effects, masks, mattes, blend mode and exposures do not**, which is After Effects' rule. A parent is read at the same frame as its child, whether or not that frame is inside the parent's in and out points, and whether or not the parent is switched on or drawn at all, so a hidden layer can be a handle that moves others. **Keeping place.** Setting or clearing a parent keeps the child where it is on screen at the playhead, as After Effects does by default: the new position is the old one carried back through the parent's chain, the new rotation is the old one less the chain's rotations, and the new scale is the old one divided by the chain's scales, applied to the base value and to every keyframe. This is exact when every layer in the chain has equal x and y scale, or when nothing involved is rotated. Otherwise the exact answer is a slant no transform here can hold; the anchor still lands exactly where it was, the rest of the layer can shift, and the window says so rather than hiding it. A parent whose scale is zero at the playhead cannot be undone, so setting it is refused. **What would break a reference.** A chain that loops back on itself is refused as a command and diagnosed as `PARENT_CYCLE` on load, exactly as a matte loop is. A parent ID that names no layer is kept in the file and reported as `PARENT_REFERENCE_MISSING`, and the layer is drawn as if it had no parent. Deleting a parent is **the one place parenting does not copy mattes**: a deleted matte leaves its reference behind, but a child left pointing at a deleted parent would jump, so deleting a parent lets go of its children in place, in the same undo. Duplicating, splitting, copying and pasting carry a parent the way they already carry a matte: to the copy if the parent was copied too, to the same layer if it is in this composition, and let go otherwise. **The fixture came before the code.** FX-PARENT-001 to 008 in document 25, generated by `tools/parent_reference.py`, which walks a point through the four steps of document 21 one at a time and never builds a matrix, while the build multiplies matrices. `Fixtures/projects/parenting_project.json` is a three-layer chain with an animated rotation and a fourth layer whose parent is missing. Documents 07, 19, 20, 21, 25, 26 and 28 and the schema are amended, each marked proposed. Consequence if accepted: B-13b builds this, with a parent pick list on the layer row beside the matte's, and R-12's "parent transforms" is specified. Consequence if declined, or changed: the fixtures are rewritten before any code, which is what they are for. Not decided here is the camera, which is the next entry, and whether a layer can be parented without keeping its place, which After Effects offers on a modifier key and nothing in W-04 asks for.

D-58 / The camera and depth: a composition is seen from somewhere, and a layer sits on a plane / ACCEPTED on 2026-09-15 by the owner ("proceed to build b-13c"), written by the agent under D-56 with its fixtures first and built by B-13c the same day. **What is already there:** every layer is drawn flat, at the size it was drawn, in the order the layer stack gives, and D-57 lets one layer ride on another's transform. **What is not there:** any way to say that a background is far away and a foreground cel is close, which is the whole of W-04 and the rest of R-12. **The fields.** A layer gains an optional `depth`, a scalar property in pixels, absent meaning 0, animatable exactly as position and rotation are. A composition gains an optional `camera` with three animatable properties: `position`, a point in composition pixels; `depth`, its own place on the same axis as a layer's; and `zoom`, a length in pixels. Both are written only when set, so no existing project changes. **A composition with no `camera` field is not a composition with no camera.** It has the default one: at the centre of the frame, `zoom` in front of the depth-0 plane, with `zoom` equal to `width * 50 / 36` - a 50 mm lens on a 36 mm film back, which is After Effects' own default, so for 1920 by 1080 that is position (960, 540) with depth and zoom 2666.6666666666665. A layer therefore starts working in depth the moment it is given one, without anybody adding a camera first. **The projection.** Document 21 puts a layer's pixels in composition space and stops. The camera carries them to the screen in two lines: `s = zoom / (world_depth(layer) - camera_depth)`, and `screen = centre + (p_comp - camera_position) * s`, with all three camera numbers read at the frame being drawn. `s` is how big the plane is drawn: 1 on the plane the camera draws at true size, 1/2 on one twice as far, 2 on one half as far, which is the convention D-56 accepted. With the default camera a layer at depth 0 has `s = 1` and lands exactly where document 21 puts it. **The projection is affine, and that is the point of choosing it.** A uniform scale about a point and a shift compose into the single matrix document 21 step 4 already samples through, so a far plane is minified by the bilinear filter G1 already has, in one resampling rather than two. Document 21 line 111 reserved camera projection as a separate contract; this is that contract, and it changes step 4 and the draw order and nothing else. **Identity is exact, not nearly exact.** With the default camera and a layer at depth 0 the two lines are the identity in arithmetic and not in floating point: `960 + (x - 960) * 1.0` is not bitwise `x`. **A build must leave out a projection that is the identity rather than apply one**, so that every fixture written before this entry reproduces exactly instead of within a tolerance. This was found by running the reference generator, not by arguing about it, and FX-CAM-001 is the case that holds it. **Depth is measured from the plane a layer rides on.** A parented layer's depth adds to its parent's, up the chain, exactly as its position is a point in its parent's space, so a mouth cel parented to a head plane is on the head's plane by default and its own `depth` is how far it stands in front of it. D-57 says a parent carries anchor, position, scale and rotation and nothing else; `depth` is a field D-57 never spoke about, and this entry says it is carried, because the alternative leaves every cel parented to a plane floating at depth 0 in front of the plane it belongs to. **Keeping place extends to it**: setting or clearing a parent subtracts or adds the parent's world depth so the layer stays on the plane it was on, and unlike D-57's scale and rotation conversion this one is a subtraction and is always exact. **What is drawn first.** Planes are drawn far to near, and layers at equal depth keep the order the composition gives them. **This overrides the layer stack whenever two layers are at different depths**, which is the one consequence of this entry a person meets without asking for it: bringing a layer to the front of the stack does not bring it in front of something nearer. `layer_order` stays the authority for the list, for ties, and for everything a person drags. This is what W-04 means by occlusion following documented rules. **A matte is a plane too.** Both a layer and its matte are projected at their own depths before the matte's alpha is sampled, so a matte on another plane slides against the layer it shapes as the camera moves. That is correct and it looks like a defect, so it is written down: the window should offer to put a matte on its layer's plane, and this contract does not force it. **What would break a picture.** A layer at or behind the camera's own depth has no size, because `world_depth - camera_depth` is zero or negative: the layer is not drawn, its record is untouched, and `CAMERA_PLANE_BEHIND` says so, which is the shape document 28 already gives `MEDIA_MISSING`. A `zoom` at or below zero is refused as a command and diagnosed as `PROJECT_SCHEMA_INVALID` on load with the camera's record preserved; it is not clamped into a working value. **No shutter**, per D-56: the camera is read once at the frame's own time while a cel holds on its exposure, and motion blur stays where document 21 line 111 put it. **What this takes from After Effects, and what it refuses.** The arithmetic above is already theirs: an After Effects camera scales a plane by its zoom over the distance from the camera to it, and stores that zoom in pixels, which is the first line of this entry. Three things are taken deliberately. The **default lens** is theirs - they name a camera by the focal length of a lens on a 36 mm film back and default to 50 mm, so this entry's default zoom is `width * 50 / 36` rather than the `width` first proposed, and a depth copied out of an After Effects project parallaxes here by the amount it does there (FX-CAM-011). **Depth is animatable** because they keyframe Z constantly and a plane that pushes in is an ordinary shot, not an advanced one (FX-CAM-010). And the window shows the zoom **in millimetres** while the file stores pixels, which is D-22's rule about where a unit is converted, applied to a second number. What is refused is the thing they are named for: **a camera is not a layer here.** In After Effects it is, which buys several cameras in one composition, a camera with in and out points, and a camera parented to a null object - the standard rig. Taking that means a layer kind with no drawing, a parent contract that accepts a camera, and a rule for which camera is live on which frame, and it buys a shot with one camera in it nothing at all. One camera per composition is the multiplane rig this project is for. The cost is named rather than hidden, and a camera layer is a later contract if a playtest asks for one. The other refusal is quieter and worth stating because it is the most confusing thing in their renderer: After Effects applies its camera only to layers whose 3D switch is on, and a 2D layer in the middle of the stack cuts the depth-sorted group in two. Here every layer has a depth and it defaults to 0, so there is no switch to forget, at the price that a layer cannot opt out of the camera to stay pinned in front - which is the one thing the switch is genuinely good for, and is listed below as undecided. **The fixture came before the code.** FX-CAM-001 to 011 in document 25, generated by `tools/camera_reference.py`, which reuses `tools/parent_reference.py` to walk a point through document 21's four steps and then does the two lines above by hand, never building a matrix, while the build multiplies them. `Fixtures/projects/camera_project.json` is FX-CAM-003's three planes and its keyed camera, with a layer order deliberately unlike the draw order. The number the entry exists for is FX-CAM-003's: over 400 pixels of camera travel the near plane moves 400 pixels, the middle 300 and the far 200. FX-CAM-010 is the case the After Effects answer added, where an animated depth changes which plane is in front between one frame and the next. Documents 07, 08, 19, 20, 21, 24, 25 and 28 and the schema are amended, each marked proposed. Document 26 is not: a camera edit is an ordinary command with an ordinary inverse and raises nothing its contract does not already cover. Consequence if accepted: B-13c builds this, W-04 can be walked, and R-12 is fully specified. Consequence if declined, or changed: the fixtures are rewritten before any code exists to argue with, which is what they are for. **Not decided here:** a camera that tilts or turns, which D-56 excluded and which needs a real perspective transform rather than an affine one; a camera as a layer, with the several cameras, in and out points and null-object rig that come with it; whether a layer can opt out of the camera to stay pinned in front of everything, which is what After Effects' 2D switch is good for and which no fixture here needs yet; intersecting planes and depth of field, which document 21 line 111 keeps out; and whether the window puts a matte on its layer's plane by default, which is B-13c's to propose.

D-59 / Expressions: a small language of our own, spelled like After Effects' / ACCEPTED on 2026-09-16 by the owner ("accept d-59"), written by the agent as B-14a with its fixtures first. It answers D-10. **What is already there:** every property is a base and keys (document 20), a composition has a camera (D-58), and a layer is named by an ID that survives a rename. **What is not there:** any way to say "this turns at 90 degrees a second", "this shakes", "this follows that one a quarter of a second late" or "this repeats its keys" without keying every frame by hand, which is R-13. **The choice.** D-10 left two answers open: embed a sandboxed scripting runtime, or write a small evaluator. **This entry chooses the small evaluator**, a language document 09 specifies in full and this project reads and evaluates itself, whose words are After Effects' where After Effects has one - `time`, `value`, `wiggle`, `loopOut`, `valueAtTime`, `posterizeTime`, `linear`, `ease`, `clamp`, `random`, `seedRandom`, `Math`, `thisComp.layer(...)` - so the expressions an animator types most are typed the same way here. **Why not a runtime.** Three of R-13's requirements are hard for a borrowed interpreter and free for an owned one. Seeded randomness must be the same on every machine and every build, so the noise behind `wiggle` is written out to the operation in document 09 and a second implementation reproduces it to the last bit; a runtime brings its own random numbers. Runaway work must stop the same way every time, so evaluation is counted in steps rather than timed, and a language with no loops and no functions has only two ways to run long - a long text and properties reading one another - each with a counted wall. And the sandbox has no door to close, because the language has no word for a file, a network, a process, `eval` or `require`: FX-EXPR-012 is eight attempts, all refused when the text is read. A runtime would also be the largest dependency this project has taken, with a licence and a security record for document 10 to review. **What it costs, named rather than hidden.** It is not JavaScript, and After Effects' language is. An expression copied from a tutorial works here if it uses only the words above and fails with `EXPRESSION_SYNTAX` otherwise, which is visible and never a wrong picture. **There is no `if`, no comparison and no loop in this first version** - many After Effects expressions use `if` - and adding them later is a specification change with fixtures, not a rewrite. **The fields.** A property may carry `"expression": {"text", "enabled"}`, written only when present, on a layer's anchor, position, scale, rotation, opacity and depth and on the camera's position, depth and zoom. A switched-off expression is kept byte for byte and ignored. No existing project changes. **Units** are the file's, except that **opacity is 0 to 100 inside an expression**, because that is what the window shows and what an After Effects user types. Running the reference found a mistake here before any build could make it: the first draft gave an expression reading another layer's opacity 0 to 100 if that opacity had no working expression and 0 to 1 if it had one. FX-EXPR-016 now pins both. **References are by ID**, so a rename never breaks one, where After Effects names a layer by its name or its index. **Failure.** A property whose expression fails is drawn at its keyed value with the identifier shown on that property, a property reading it fails the same way, and **an export whose range meets a failing enabled expression is refused** until it is corrected or switched off, which is document 09's G2 acceptance rule kept. Three identifiers join document 28 beside the two it already had: `EXPRESSION_SYNTAX`, `EXPRESSION_TYPE` and `EXPRESSION_REFERENCE_MISSING`. **Where this departs from After Effects on purpose:** `value + 5` on a position is an error rather than a surprise; an expression reading its own property through `thisLayer` is `EXPRESSION_CYCLE`, where After Effects quietly gives the keyed value; `valueAtTime` reads whole frames only, which is D-58's no-shutter rule; a wiggle here is a wiggle of the same character and not the same numbers as theirs; and `ease` is a stated curve, because theirs is not published. **The fixture came before the code.** FX-EXPR-001 to 016 in document 25 are generated by `tools/expression_reference.py`, a whole reader and evaluator in Python written from document 09 and sharing nothing with the build, and `Fixtures/projects/expression_project.json` is the file both evaluate - nine layers and a wiggling camera. Documents 03, 07, 09, 11, 15, 19, 20, 24, 25 and 28 and the schema are amended, each marked proposed and now accepted. Document 21 is not: an expression changes a property's value and nothing about how a value is drawn. Document 26 is not either: setting an expression is an ordinary command with an ordinary inverse. Document 27 needs no change of rule, but B-14b must show that the effect cache is keyed on the evaluated values rather than on keys, since an expression makes a value change on a frame with no key. **Consequence if accepted:** B-14b builds the evaluator and the file round trip against these fixtures, with the export refusal; B-14c puts an expression box on each property in the window and shows its error there. **Consequence if declined, or changed:** the fixtures are rewritten before any code exists to argue with. **Not decided here:** `if`, comparisons and loops; `toWorld` and other space conversions; text layers and `sourceText`, which need a text layer first; expressions on effect parameters; a pick whip that writes a reference by pointing; and a translator for After Effects projects, which is level C of document 09's ladder and a separate decision.

D-60 / G2 passed, and G3 entered for B-15 and B-16 / ACCEPTED on 2026-09-16 by the owner's decision ("Open G2 and G3"), in answer to the owner's request "B-14C playtest works; b-15, try running that for me please, then we proceed to B-16". **G2.** Document 04 says G2 adds T-11 and T-12 plus W-04 to G1. T-11 passed with B-13, done by the owner's word on 2026-09-16; T-12 passes 184 of 184 in `verification/B-14b_expression_table.md`; W-04, the parallax shot, is what B-13's camera and depth playtests walked. B-14c, the last unit of B-14, is done by the owner's word the same day. The agent did not open the gate: it asked, and the owner opened it. **G3.** Document 04 enters G3 on evidence of repeated manual effort. The evidence here is the owner's own request for B-15 and B-16, and it is written down as that, not as a measurement. **Order.** B-15 (R-14, collect and package) first. Then B-16 (R-15), whose first format is EXR by the owner's choice ("EXR first"), with WAV after it only if a shot needs it. **What this makes required.** T-13 for what B-15 ships and T-14 for each format B-16 ships, as document 11 says. **Not changed:** one subsystem in active development at a time (document 04), and a specification and its fixtures come to the owner before the code, as B-13 and B-14 did.

D-61 / Collect and package: one folder that opens from anywhere, with a manifest of every file / ACCEPTED on 2026-09-16 by the owner ("accept d-61"), written by the agent as B-15a with its fixtures first. It answers R-14. **What is already there:** a project stores each drawing's path relative to the project file (document 07), Save As rewrites those paths for the new folder (B-13e), and a missing drawing is kept and reported as `MEDIA_MISSING`. **What is not there:** a way to hand a shot to someone else without copying the drawings by hand and hoping every path still points somewhere. Document 02's W-05 does that by hand today and names the automatic version as R-14. **The command.** `project.collect`, File > Collect Files..., asks for a folder and writes the package there. It writes from the project as it is in the window, saved or not, and it changes nothing in the window: the open project, its file, its history and its unsaved state stay as they were, as After Effects' Collect Files leaves them. **The folder.** The package is the project file, under its own name (`project.json` if it was never saved), a `media` folder, and `package-manifest.json`. Each asset gets its own folder, `media/<asset ID>/`, holding its drawings under their own file names. Every asset is collected, used or not, because an asset nothing uses today may be the one the recipient needs. Two assets using the same drawing each get a copy, and a drawing one sequence uses for several frame numbers is copied once. **The naming rule,** for a folder and for a file alike, so that every package opens on Windows, macOS and Linux: each of `< > : " / \ | ? *` and every control character becomes `_`; dots and spaces at the end are removed; an empty name becomes `_`; a name whose part before the first dot is a Windows device name (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1 to COM9, LPT1 to LPT9, in any case) gets `_` in front. Other characters, Japanese included, are kept. If two names in the same folder are then the same, ignoring case, the later one in project order (for folders) or in frame order (for files) gets `-2`, then `-3`, before its extension: `x.png`, `x-2.png`, `X-3.png`. **The project in the package** is the open project with every drawing's path rewritten to its place in the package, and nothing else changed; unknown data is kept, as every save keeps it. So the package opens from wherever the folder is moved to. **Media the artist may not pass on.** An asset may carry `"redistribute": false`, written only when false, set by a new undoable command, `asset.set_redistribute`: a "Can be passed on" tick on the asset in the Project panel. Such an asset's drawings are not copied. They are still listed, with their size and hash, and the packaged project still points at where they would be, so a recipient who has their own licensed copy puts it there and the shot opens. Until then that asset is `MEDIA_MISSING` in the recipient's window, as any missing drawing is. Whether a drawing may be passed on is the artist's call and this program cannot know it; the default is yes, because most drawings in a shot are the artist's own. **A missing drawing** does not stop the package. It is listed as missing, with no size and no hash, and the finished message names how many drawings were missing and how many were left out. **The manifest** is JSON, two-space indent, UTF-8, keys in this order: `format` (`anime-compositor-package`), `version` (1), `project` (the project file's name), and `assets` in project order. Each asset has its `id`, `name`, `kind`, `redistribute`, `used_by` (every composition and layer that uses it, in project order) and `files`, in the order of the first frame number that uses each. Each file has `frames` (the frame numbers it stands for, empty for a still), `path` (inside the package), `status` (`copied`, `excluded` or `missing`), `bytes` and `sha256` (lowercase hex; both null when missing). It holds no path from the artist's own disk, so a package does not tell the recipient how the sender's drives are laid out. `Fixtures/packaging/expected_manifest.json` is the exact file a build must write for the fixture shot. **The hash is SHA-256**, which document 27 already prefers for packages. **The build writes its own SHA-256 rather than taking a library for it:** about eighty lines, checked against the published test messages of FIPS 180-4 and against every hash in the fixture, which Python's hashlib made. No new dependency means nothing new for document 10 to review and nothing new in `docs/DEPENDENCIES.md`. If the owner would rather take the `sha2` library, that is a dependency record instead and the fixtures do not change. **Failure.** A folder that is not empty is refused and nothing is written (`PACKAGE_DESTINATION_NOT_EMPTY`). The package is written into `<folder>.partial` beside it and renamed only when every file is written; if anything fails, the partial folder is removed and the reason is shown (`PACKAGE_WRITE_FAILED`), so a half-written package never looks like a whole one. If `<folder>.partial` already exists, that is refused the same way as a folder that is not empty, rather than deleted. **Checking a package.** `package.check`, File > Check Package, reads `package-manifest.json` beside the open project and answers for each listed file: `ok` when it is there with the listed size and hash; `changed` when it is there and differs (`PACKAGE_FILE_CHANGED`, ERROR); `missing` when it is not there and was not left out on purpose (`MEDIA_MISSING`); `excluded` when it was left out on purpose and has not been supplied (`PACKAGE_MEDIA_EXCLUDED`, INFO); and `unverified` when a drawing missing at packing time has since been put in place, since there is no hash to check it against (`PACKAGE_FILE_UNVERIFIED`, INFO). A missing or unreadable manifest is `PACKAGE_MANIFEST_INVALID`. Checking is a command rather than something done on every open, because hashing a long sequence takes seconds and opening a shot should not. **The fixture came before the code.** `tools/package_reference.py`, written from this entry in Python and sharing nothing with the build, writes the shot in `Fixtures/packaging/source/` and the expected manifest, places and check answers. FX-PACK-001 to 006 in document 25 are its tables. Documents 03, 07, 11, 15, 19, 24, 25 and 28 and the schema are amended. Document 21 is not: a package changes where a drawing is, not how it is drawn. Document 26 needs no new rule: `asset.set_redistribute` is an ordinary command, and collecting and checking make no history item, as saving makes none. **Consequence if accepted:** B-15b builds collecting, the manifest, the hash and checking against these fixtures, with a generated table that also moves the package to a second folder, opens it there and compares its frames with the source's. B-15c puts the two File menu items and the tick in the window, with a playtest sheet. **Consequence if declined, or changed:** the fixtures are rewritten before any code exists to argue with. **Not decided here:** a zip file rather than a folder; leaving out drawings no frame uses ("reduce project"); packaging the fonts and effects a shot needs, which this program does not yet have; checking automatically on open; and a record of each drawing's licence, which the tick stands in for.

D-62 / EXR in and out: the OpenEXR file read into the working buffer as it is, and written from it as it is / ACCEPTED on 2026-09-17 by the owner ("accept d-62"), written by the agent as B-16a with its fixtures first. It answers the first format of R-15, which D-60 made EXR by the owner's choice. **What is already there:** the working buffer is RGBA float32, linear light, premultiplied (document 21), and may hold colour below 0 and above 1. PNG stills and sequences come in and go out, and a drawing that cannot be read is kept and reported (`MEDIA_UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT`, `MEDIA_DECODE_FAILED`). **What is not there:** a way to take a render from a 3D or compositing program, or give one back, without squeezing it into eight or sixteen bits and losing everything above white. OpenEXR is that format, and its own convention - linear light, premultiplied - is the working buffer's, so no colour conversion is needed in either direction. **Coming in.** `media.import` and `media.relink` accept `.exr` beside `.png`; the extension decides which reader is used, and stills and numbered sequences work exactly as they do for PNG, gaps included. An EXR drawing's interpretation is `linear-srgb`, premultiplied, and is never guessed from the file. **The picture is the display window**: the drawing's size is the display window's, its top-left pixel is the display window's top-left corner, and wherever the data window does not cover it the drawing is transparent black. Samples outside the display window are cut off. **Channels,** matched exactly, capitals included: if the file has any of `R`, `G`, `B`, those are the colour, and a missing one is 0. Otherwise, if it has `RY` or `BY`, it is refused, because colour-difference files need a conversion this entry does not specify. Otherwise, if it has `Y`, then R, G and B are all `Y`. Otherwise it is refused. `A` is the alpha, and 1 where there is no `A`. Every other channel - depth, a render layer such as `diffuse.R`, a `Y` beside RGB - is not used, and is reported. Half and float samples are used as they are; whole-number samples become the float of the same number. **Values** below 0 and above 1 in colour are kept. A sample that is not a number or is infinite becomes 0, and then an alpha below 0 or above 1 is clamped into 0 to 1, because document 21 defines alpha as coverage. **Reported, not refused:** a new WARNING, `MEDIA_EXR_ADJUSTED`, says that a file was drawn but not exactly as stored, with one reason for each thing done: `channels_ignored` (naming them in the file's order), `outside_display_window` (how many pixels were cut off), `non_finite` (how many samples became 0), `alpha_clamped` (how many), `pixel_aspect` (a pixel aspect ratio other than 1: drawn with square pixels) and `primaries` (a `chromaticities` attribute that is not Rec. 709: drawn with its numbers unchanged, which is right only if the composition's other drawings share those primaries). A file with none of these is drawn with no report. **Refused** with `MEDIA_UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT`, the asset kept, and the reason named: more than one part (`multipart`), deep data (`deep`), HTJ2K compression (`htj2k`), channels stored at less than full resolution (`subsampled`), colour difference (`luminance_chroma`) and no colour channel at all (`no_colour_channels`). A file that is not EXR, is empty or is cut short is `MEDIA_DECODE_FAILED` (`unreadable`). The refusals are decided from the header before any pixel is decoded. **Going out.** `export.sequence` gains a format choice, PNG or EXR, and for EXR a sample choice, half (the default) or float. Each frame is `<name>_<frame>.exr`: one part, scanlines, top to bottom, channels `A`, `B`, `G`, `R`, ZIP compression, data window and display window both the composition's size at the origin, pixel aspect ratio 1, screen window centre (0, 0) and width 1, Rec. 709 `chromaticities`, and `framesPerSecond` as the composition's rate, a fraction. Nothing else but the `chunkCount` the format itself may add: no dates, no program name, no paths, so the same frame written twice is the same file. **The samples are the working buffer's, unchanged and premultiplied**, so the straight-alpha choice is not offered for EXR. Float is exact. Half is the working value clamped to -65504 to 65504, half's range, then rounded to the nearest half, ties to even: that is the declared encoding step of document 21 and has no diagnostic, as PNG's rounding has none. The missing-drawing choice is the same as PNG's. **The library.** OpenEXR's compressions are many - ZIP, PIZ, PXR24, B44, DWA - and each is a codec of its own. **This entry recommends the `exr` crate, version 1.74.2, with its default features off**, which reads all ten compressions in the fixtures and writes ZIP. It is BSD-3-Clause and brings 14 packages this build does not have yet, all MIT, Apache-2.0 or BSD-3-Clause (B-16b counted 15: `bytemuck` also came, under Zlib, Apache-2.0 or MIT, and two of the 15 ship no licence text, as `Licenses/` records); B-16b records them in `docs/DEPENDENCIES.md` and archives their licences, as every dependency is, and ADR-007's "revisit when EXR handoff arrives" is answered by this entry. It was measured before this entry was written, in a scratch program outside the build: it reads every fixture file whose windows match to the last bit of the reference, DWA and B44 included, so **no tolerance is proposed**; files it wrote passed the export check, 60 of 60; and it does not decode HTJ2K itself, which is one more reason that refusal is made from the header. **The alternative,** if the owner would rather not take the dependency: the build writes its own reader and writer for the uncompressed, RLE and ZIP kinds, using the ZIP code it already has, and refuses PIZ, PXR24, B44 and DWA with `MEDIA_UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT`. Those four are common in renders from other programs, so that would refuse many real files. The fixtures do not change either way; only which ones a build must draw. **The fixture came before the code.** `tools/exr_reference.py` writes every test file with OpenEXR's own library, reads each back with it and applies this entry's rules in Python, sharing nothing with the build; it also checks files the build exports, with the same library. FX-EXR-001 to 010 in document 25 are its tables, and `Fixtures/exr/expected_exr.json` holds every expected pixel. Documents 03, 07, 11, 15, 18, 21, 24, 25 and 28 are amended, each marked proposed. Document 19 and the schema are not: an EXR asset is an asset with a different file, and its interpretation values already exist. Document 26 is not: import and export are ordinary commands. **Consequence if accepted:** B-16b adds the dependency, the reader and the writer, with a generated table walking FX-EXR-001 to 010, which is T-14 for EXR, the export half quoting `tools/exr_reference.py check`. B-16c adds `.exr` to the file dialogs and the format and sample choices to the export dialog, with a playtest sheet that opens an exported frame in another program. **Consequence if declined, or changed:** the fixtures are rewritten before any code exists to argue with. **Not decided here:** choosing a part or a render layer from a multi-layer file; deep data; colour-difference and subsampled files; turning primaries or pixel aspect into a conversion rather than a report; writing other compressions, tiles, or several layers at once; timecode and other metadata; and WAV, which D-60 leaves until a shot needs it.

The exposure list stays as document 20 has it, a new sequence layer included, until that overhaul. D-65 / G3 continues with adjustment layers, precompositions and the graph editor / ACCEPTED on 2026-09-17 by the owner ("Let's mess with precompositions and adjustment layers along with curve and graph editor"). **Order,** chosen by the agent because document 04 allows one subsystem at a time and the owner named none: B-17 adjustment layers first, because it reuses the effect stack that exists and adds one new kind of layer; B-18 precompositions second, the largest of the three (value, complexity and risk all 5 in document 23), which changes what a layer's picture can be; B-19 the graph editor third. **The graph editor is mostly there already:** D-52 and the W-series built a Graph tab that draws one transform property's value or speed, with ease handles, chosen keys and dragging along time (documents 05 and 24). B-19 is therefore the gaps the owner names when it comes up, not a new panel. **Evidence** is the owner's request, written down as that, as D-60's was. **Not changed:** a specification and its fixtures come to the owner before the code.

D-66 / Adjustment layers: a layer whose effects apply to everything drawn beneath it / ACCEPTED on 2026-09-17 by the owner ("proceed"); proposed the same day by the agent as B-17a, with its fixtures first. B-17b built it in the core on 2026-09-17: `verification/B-17b_adjust_table.md`, 46 of 46. **What is already there:** each layer carries an ordered effect stack - exposure, Gaussian blur, tint - that runs on that layer's own drawing, in its own space, before it is moved into place (document 21, ADR-017). **What is not there:** a way to grade or blur several layers at once without repeating the same effects on each. **The layer.** A new layer kind, `adjustment`, with no drawing: no `asset_id`, no exposures and no source offset. Everything else a layer has it has, and it means the same: name, switch, lock, in and out frames, transform, opacity, mask, matte, parent, depth, label, shy, and its effect stack. **Its shape** is an opaque rectangle the size of the composition, in its own layer space, which is cut by its mask (step 2 of document 21), carried by its transform, parent and camera (step 4), and cut by its matte (step 5). A new adjustment layer has its anchor and position at the centre of the composition, so it covers the frame exactly, as After Effects' does. **What it does.** Where it comes in the drawing order, the frame drawn so far - everything beneath it - is one picture the size of the frame, `B`. Its enabled effects run on `B` in order, exactly as document 21 defines them, giving `E(B)`. Samples outside the frame are transparent black, and a blur's growth past the frame is cut off: the result is the frame's own size. Then, at every pixel, with `c` its coverage there times its opacity: `out = B + c * (E(B) - B)`, all four channels, premultiplied. Layers drawn after it are not adjusted. **Order** is document 21's: far to near, the layer stack breaking ties, so an adjustment layer behind everything in depth is drawn first, onto nothing, and changes nothing (FX-ADJ-012). **Nothing to do:** an adjustment layer with no enabled effects, outside its in and out frames, switched off, or with coverage 0 leaves the frame exactly as it was. An unsupported effect in its stack is bypassed and reported, as on any layer (`EFFECT_UNSUPPORTED`). **Blend mode** is normal only. The blend list is not offered for an adjustment layer, `layer.set_blend_mode` refuses one with `COMMAND_INVALID_VALUE`, and a file whose adjustment layer has another mode is `PROJECT_SCHEMA_INVALID`, as a file with an asset on one is; no build writes either. **As a matte** for another layer, an adjustment layer gives its shape's alpha. **The preview at draft size** runs the effects on the quarter-size frame with the blur's sigma a quarter as large; the export always runs at full size (D-33 already marks the draft as differing from the export). **Tiling.** The effect stack runs on the whole frame, as a layer's stack already runs on the whole layer (ADR-017); the mix back in is per pixel and tiled. A frame is drawn in segments: the layers up to the first adjustment layer, the adjustment, the layers up to the next, and so on. **In the window** (B-17c, built on 2026-09-17): a **New adjustment layer** button and Ctrl+Alt+Y, After Effects' shortcut, as `layer.add_adjustment`; the layer shows in the list and on the timeline with its own mark and no drawings; its effects are edited as any layer's. **Not proposed:** After Effects' switch that turns any drawn layer into an adjustment layer shaped by its drawing - it can come later as a field on a raster layer without changing anything here; blend modes on adjustment layers; and effects beyond the three there are (D-64). **The fixture came first:** `tools/adjust_reference.py` renders thirteen six-by-two frames pixel by pixel and blurs with the two-dimensional kernel summed directly, where the build runs two passes; document 25's FX-ADJ-001 to 013 are its output, with their projects and drawings in `Fixtures/adjust/`.

D-67 / Precompositions: a layer whose drawing is another composition / ACCEPTED on 2026-09-18 by the owner ("proceed"); proposed the same day by the agent as B-18a, with its fixtures first. B-18b built it in the core on 2026-09-18: `verification/B-18b_precomp_table.md`, 70 of 70. B-18c put it in the window the same day: `verification/B-18c_panel_table.md`, 14 of 14. **What is already there:** a project holds several compositions, each with its own size, rate, start, length, layers and camera; the window shows one at a time from the Project panel, and copies and deletes them (W-26). **What is not there:** a way to put one composition inside another, so a group of layers can be moved, faded, blurred, masked or matted as one picture, or drawn once and used twice. **The layer.** A new layer kind, `composition`, whose drawing is another composition of the same project, named by `composition_id`: no `asset_id`, no exposures. Everything else a raster layer has it has, and it means the same: name, switch, lock, in and out frames, source offset, transform, opacity, mask, matte, blend mode, parent, depth, label, shy, and its effect stack. **Its picture** at a frame is the inner composition rendered at that layer's local frame, `comp_frame - in_frame + source_offset_frames`, by the same render path, at the inner composition's own size, with the inner composition's own camera, in linear premultiplied. Outside the inner composition's own start and length the picture is transparent. Frame numbers pass between the two, not seconds: the two rates are not compared. That picture then goes through document 21's steps as a decoded drawing would: its mask and effects in the inner composition's pixel space, its transform, parent and camera, its matte, its opacity and its blend mode. A new composition layer has its anchor at the centre of the inner composition and its position at the centre of the outer one, so a composition of the same size covers the frame exactly and a smaller one lands centred, as After Effects' does. **Nesting** has no fixed depth. An adjustment layer inside the inner composition adjusts what is beneath it there and nothing outside (FX-PRE-009); an adjustment layer above a composition layer adjusts it like any layer (FX-PRE-010). The same composition may be used by any number of layers, in any number of compositions. **A cycle** - a composition that holds, at any depth, a layer of itself - is refused: a file with one is `COMPOSITION_CYCLE` and is not opened; `layer.add_composition`, when it would make one, is refused with `COMPOSITION_CYCLE`, as `MATTE_CYCLE` and `PARENT_CYCLE` are. **A composition that is not in the project** is kept in the file and reported once as `COMPOSITION_REFERENCE_MISSING`, a warning, and the layer draws nothing, as `PARENT_REFERENCE_MISSING` keeps its reference (FX-PRE-014). `composition.delete` is refused, with a sentence naming the composition that uses it, while any composition layer names it. **The preview at draft size** renders the inner composition at the draft divisor too, so a nested picture is drawn once at the size it is shown; the export always runs at full size. **Caches** (document 27): a composition layer's source is the inner composition's frame, keyed as that frame is, so an edit inside a composition invalidates the frames of every composition holding a layer of it, at any depth. **Commands** (document 24): `layer.add_composition` adds a layer of a named composition above the chosen layer, or else at the front, from a button on each composition's row in the Project panel; `layer.precompose`, Ctrl+Shift+C as After Effects', moves the chosen layers into a new composition of the same size, rate, start and length, named "Precomp 1", "Precomp 2" and so on, keeping their order and every setting, and puts one composition layer in the place of the frontmost of them, as one entry to undo; it is refused with `COMMAND_INVALID_VALUE` when a chosen layer's parent or matte is not chosen, or an unchosen layer's parent or matte is. Double-clicking a composition layer's row opens its composition; the layer's row is marked "composition" and its bar on the timeline shows the inner composition's name. **Not proposed:** time remapping and speed changes of a nested composition, which After Effects does with Time Remap; collapsing transformations, which draws the inner layers straight into the outer composition without a picture between; a different frame rate inside meaning anything; and rendering the inner composition at a size other than its own. Each can come later without changing anything here. **The fixture came first:** `tools/precomp_reference.py` renders fourteen six-by-two frames pixel by pixel, nesting by plain recursion, and reuses `tools/adjust_reference.py` for the drawings and effects; document 25's FX-PRE-001 to 015 are its output, with their projects and drawings in `Fixtures/precomp/`.

D-68 / Keyframed effect settings: an effect's setting animated as a layer's position is / PROPOSED on 2026-09-18 by the agent as B-19b, with its fixtures first. **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-18 by the owner ("proceed").** The owner asked for it on 2026-09-18 with B-19's scope ("along with adding animation/keyframing stopwatches to effects as well"). **What is already there:** each effect has settings that are plain numbers, the same on every frame: exposure's `stops`, the blur's `sigma_px`, the tint's `color` and `amount`. A layer's transform, its depth and the camera are properties with keys, hold, linear and ease (D-52). **What is not there:** a setting that changes over time, such as a blur that comes on or a tint that fades. **In the file** a setting inside an effect's `parameters` is either what it is today, a plain number, or for a colour three, which is constant; or a property record, `{"base", "keyframes"}`, exactly as document 19 writes a transform property, each key with its `frame`, `value`, `interp` and, when eased, `ease`. A setting with no keys is written plain, so every file made before this reads and saves byte for byte as it did, and the schema version does not change. A colour's `base` and each key's `value` are three numbers. `spatial` on a setting's key is invalid, as it is on any property but position. **Its value at a frame** is document 20's and nothing new: keys sit on composition frames, the first key's value holds before it and the last key's after it, and between two keys it is hold, linear, or the eased fraction of the way. A colour's three numbers all go the same fraction, in linear light, which is the space the tint already works in. **Range.** `sigma_px` is 0 or more and `amount` is within 0 and 1. A `base` or a key's `value` outside its range is treated as a plain number outside it is today (D-46): the file is read, the effect is kept exactly as written and bypassed on every frame with the warning `EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID` (FX-FXK-009), and a command that would set one is refused. **Corrected on 2026-09-18 before anything was built:** as first written this said the file is refused with `PROJECT_SCHEMA_INVALID`, which misread today's rule and would have lost a whole project over one number. An ease may overshoot between two keys that are both in range, so the value worked out for a frame is then held inside the range: a blur of less than nothing is no blur (FX-FXK-007) and a tint amount past 1 is 1 (FX-FXK-005). `stops` and `color` have no range. **Rendering** (document 21) is unchanged: each effect runs with its settings' values at the composition frame, on a drawing's layer, an adjustment layer or a composition layer alike. The blur's bounds grow by the radius of that frame's sigma. **Moving the layer in time** (`layer.shift`) moves its effects' keys with it, as it moves its transform's keys; copying a layer or an effect copies its keys. **Caches** (document 27): an effect stage is keyed by its settings' values at the frame, not by the keys, so frames where an animated setting has the same value share a result and an edit to one key invalidates only the frames whose value changed. **Commands** (document 24), to be built in B-19c: `effect.set_parameters` on a setting with keys sets or makes the key at the playhead, as `property.set_base` does; `keyframe.add_remove`, `keyframe.move`, `keyframe.set_interp` and the key clipboard take a setting named by its effect's instance id and the setting's name, where they take a transform property today. Each is one entry to undo. **The window**, B-19d: a stopwatch beside each effect setting in the inspector, the setting's keys as a row on the timeline under its layer, and the setting in the graph editor as any property is. **An effect this build does not know** keeps its `parameters` exactly as written, keyed or not, and still renders as unsupported with its warning. **Not proposed:** expressions on effect settings; keying an effect's on and off switch; a colour interpolated in any space but linear light; a curve through colours as position has through space (D-53). Each can come later without changing anything here. **The fixture came first:** `tools/fxkey_reference.py` renders eight cases of six-by-two frames pixel by pixel, reusing `tools/adjust_reference.py` for the drawings and effects and `tools/ease_reference.py`'s bisection for the ease; document 25's FX-FXK-001 to 009 are its output, with their projects and drawings in `Fixtures/fxkey/`.

D-69 / Separate X and Y for position, and auto, continuous and roving keys / PROPOSED on 2026-09-18 by the agent as B-19e, with its fixtures first. **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-18 by the owner ("proceed").** They are items 7 and 10 of the scope the owner gave B-19 on 2026-09-18 ("all 10 please"). **What is already there:** a key carries one ease for the segment that starts at it (D-52), and a position key may carry path handles (D-53). Both of a position's numbers take the same ease. Every key is what After Effects calls a plain bezier key: its two sides are set apart, and nothing keeps them smooth when a neighbour moves. **Separate dimensions.** A layer's position may be written `{"x": property, "y": property}` in place of `{"base", "keyframes"}`: two properties of one number each, with their own keys, eases, kinds and expressions. The position at a frame is `[x at the frame, y at the frame]` (FX-SEP-001, 002), and everything that uses a position, the transform, parenting, the camera's view of it, takes that pair as before. A separated position has no path handles, which is After Effects' rule as well: a path is one curve through pairs, and X and Y apart are two curves against time. `property.separate` on a position turns each of its keys into a key of X and a key of Y on the same frame with the same ease and kind, and drops the path handles and roving (FX-SEP-003); it is refused while the position has an expression. Used again it joins them: a key wherever either had one, holding the position at that frame, with X's ease where X had a key and else Y's (FX-SEP-004), which keeps the keys and can lose the shape between them when X and Y were eased apart; Undo brings it back. Commands name the two as `position_x` and `position_y`. **A key's kind.** A key gains `"kind"`: absent, which is today's key; `"continuous"`; or `"auto"`. **Neither changes how a frame is worked out.** The file always holds the eases that are rendered, and the kind says what an edit must keep true of them. The measure is the speed the Keyframe Velocity box has shown since W-25: out of a key, `y1 / x1 * L / frames`, and into it, `(1 - y2) / (1 - x2) * L / frames`, where L is how far the value goes over that segment: the difference for a number, signed; for a pair the straight distance, or three times the path handle's length at that end. **Continuous:** the speed in equals the speed out. Making a key continuous, or moving it or a neighbour, sets both sides to the mean of the two speeds, each handle keeping its length (FX-KIND-005); pulling one side by hand makes the other follow it (FX-KIND-006). **Auto:** both handles are a third long and both speeds are `(L_in + L_out) / (next frame - previous frame)`, the slope between the neighbours (FX-KIND-001, 003), worked out again whenever the key or a neighbour changes (FX-KIND-004); the first and last keys leave and arrive as a straight line (FX-KIND-002). Pulling an auto key's handle by hand makes it continuous, as After Effects does. A side that is a hold, or whose value goes nowhere, has no speed to set and is left alone (FX-KIND-007): this build's ease is a fraction of the way between two values, so a segment between equal values stays flat, where After Effects' value graph could bulge it. Making a key auto or continuous turns a linear segment beside it into the ease that is the same line, `[1/3, 1/3, 2/3, 2/3]`, so there is a curve to set. **Roving.** A position key that is not the first or last, and not separated, may carry `"roving": true`. Its frame is then worked out: across a run of roving keys between two keys that are not, each sits where it would fall if the run's path were travelled at one speed, `first frame + frames * (length so far / whole length)`, rounded to the nearest frame, halves up, and then moved so no two keys share a frame and none leaves the run (FX-ROVE-001, 002). A straight segment's length is the distance; a curved one's is measured along 64 straight pieces at equal steps of D-53's parameter (FX-ROVE-004). The frames are worked out again when a value, a path handle or either end key of the run changes; an edit that leaves a run fewer frames than it has roving keys is refused with `COMMAND_INVALID_VALUE` (FX-ROVE-003). Roving places the key and leaves every ease alone. Dragging a roving key in time by hand stops it roving, as After Effects does. The file holds the frame that resulted, so a reader never works it out. **On reading a file** nothing is recomputed: `kind` on any key and `roving` on a position key are kept, `roving` anywhere else or on a first or last key is `PROJECT_SCHEMA_INVALID`, and so are path handles or a pair's keys inside a separated position. **Commands** (document 24), to be built in B-19f: `property.separate`; `keyframe.set_kind` with `kind=bezier|continuous|auto`; `keyframe.set_roving`; each over every chosen key as one entry to undo. **The window**, B-19g: the three kinds and Rove Across Time in the key menu, with After Effects' key shapes on the timeline; Separate Dimensions on the position's menu, after which the inspector, the timeline and the graph show X Position and Y Position as properties of their own, which is what gives X and Y separate handles in the graph. **Not proposed:** separating the camera's place, the anchor or the scale; a handle that bulges a flat segment; roving at an exact arc length or at a speed the end keys' eases shape across the run; roving on anything but position. **The fixture came first:** `tools/keykind_reference.py` works every case from the formulas above and checks each against a value worked by hand; document 25's FX-SEP-001 to 004, FX-KIND-001 to 007 and FX-ROVE-001 to 004 are its output, with the two separated projects in `Fixtures/keykind/`.

D-70 / Three stale headers and the licence review, delegated / CLOSED on 2026-09-18. The owner's words: "from earlier execute to your recommendation; license reviwer, look over and if it checks out, confirm". The agent's recommendations, carried out: B-12a is ACCEPTED, because B-12 was built on it and accepted on 2026-09-15; P-08 stays CUT, as P-02 measured; P-14 is DONE with ADR-006 left alone, because the draft blur is inside the 24 fps budget (`verification/P-14_blur_drag.md`). D-71 / Reference audio: an audio layer, WAV read exactly, other formats played by the window / ACCEPTED by the owner on 2026-09-19 ("Proceed"), and built in the core as B-20b the same day; proposed that day by the agent as B-20a, with its fixtures first, in answer to the owner ("let's do the WAV reference audio, and allow other audio files as well, have a different preview style layer bar compared to the other layers, maybe do the same with camera and adjustment layer as well, what do you recommend?"). It takes up what D-63 deferred. ADR-018 holds the two engineering choices. **The asset.** `kind: "audio"`, with `id`, `name` and `path`, and no `interpretation`, because there is no colour to interpret. **The layer.** `kind: "audio"`, with `id`, `name`, `asset_id`, `enabled` (heard or not), `locked`, `in_frame`, `out_frame`, `source_offset_frames`, `gain_db`, and the label and shy every layer has. `gain_db` is one number from -96 to +12, 0 when absent. It has no transform, opacity, mask, matte, blend mode, effects, parent or depth, and a file that gives it one is `PROJECT_SCHEMA_INVALID` (FX-AUD-030 to 035), as D-66 did for an adjustment layer's asset. It cannot be a matte or a parent. **It draws nothing.** Every frame is the picture it would be without the layer (FX-AUD-020), an adjustment layer above it does nothing to it, and an exported sequence is unchanged. **Time.** The local frame is document 20's, `composition_frame - in_frame + source_offset_frames`, and frame `n` of the file begins at sample `floor(n * rate * denominator / numerator)` (FX-AUD-001 to 004). Outside the layer, before the file's first sample and after its last there is silence (FX-AUD-005 to 008). A layer may be longer than its file. **WAV.** The core reads the header: PCM of 8, 16, 24 and 32 bits, float of 32 and 64, any number of channels, plain or extensible, chunks in any order with their pad bytes. A `data` chunk that promises more than the file holds is read as far as it goes with the warning `MEDIA_AUDIO_CUT_SHORT`. A file that is not RIFF WAVE, has no format or no data, or is RF64, is `MEDIA_AUDIO_UNREADABLE`, and the layer is kept and silent, as a missing picture is kept. A WAV in another encoding, ADPCM for one, is treated as the other formats are (FX-AUD-010). **Other formats.** `.flac`, `.mp3`, `.m4a`, `.aac`, `.ogg` and `.opus` are taken as audio assets by their extension. The core does not open them; the window's decoder plays them and reports their length. FLAC is exact to the sample; MP3 and AAC can start up to about a frame late, and the import says so. **Editing.** Import makes the asset and the layer, as it does for a picture. Moving, trimming, sliding, renaming, switching, locking, duplicating, reordering and deleting are the commands there are. One new command, `SET_AUDIO_GAIN`, one entry to undo. Commands that set what the layer does not have are refused with a sentence. Relink and collect (D-61) treat the file as any asset. **The window (B-20c).** Play plays the sound in step with the frames, from the audio clock so the two cannot drift; stepping one frame plays that frame's samples; the layer has a speaker where others have an eye, and a level in the inspector. **Layer bars, the agent's recommendation.** Yes, and by pattern as well as colour, so that it does not depend on telling hues apart: a picture layer keeps its blue blocks; an audio layer's bar is green with its waveform drawn in it; an adjustment layer keeps the hatching B-17c gave it; a composition layer keeps its name on the bar and takes a violet of its own; the camera, which is not a layer and has no in or out, gets a thin amber strip the length of the composition so its row reads as a track, and it does not drag. The layer's name row carries the same small mark, so the list and the bars agree. No file changes for any of this. **Known ceilings.** The level is not keyframed. Sound inside a composition layer is not heard through it; open the inner composition to hear it. No sound in any export. No waveform or length for a non-WAV file until the window has decoded it once. The fixtures are FX-AUD-001 to 035 in document 25 and `Fixtures/audio/`, from `tools/audio_reference.py`. The core is built and `verification/B-20b_audio_table.md` walks every case, 46 of 46; the window is B-20c.

D-72 / More drawing formats in; GIF, animated PNG and MP4 out / PROPOSED on 2026-09-19 by the agent as B-21a, with its fixtures first, in answer to the owner ("let's expand the formats of images we could use and formats to export. Like mp4, gif, etc."). **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-19 by the owner ("I accept D-72, proceed with B-21b, B-21c, and B-21d").** It was written that nothing is built against it until the owner accepts it, and that the MP4 part also needs the owner's answer to D-30; see D-30 for how the same sentence is read there. **In.** BMP, TGA, TIFF, WebP and JPEG become drawings beside PNG and EXR.
