FX-VIBRANCE-001 to 018 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-83. **It adds one effect and changes no existing fixture.** **What it does.** It makes a drawing's colours richer or duller, as a colourist wakes up a flat shot without burning the colours that are already strong: vibrance moves the dull colours most and leaves the already vivid ones nearly alone, and saturation moves every colour alike. Each colour is pushed away from its own grey, or towards it, so a grey, black or white pixel never changes. It is `core.vibrance`, named Vibrance in the Effects panel. It touches only the pixels that show, and keeps each one's covering, so a soft line edge stays soft. **Settings:** `vibrance` and `saturation`, each -100 to 100, both starting at 0. Each can be keyed (D-68) and is held inside its range at each frame. **The rule.** Each pixel that shows reads its colour as it is written (encoded values, 0 to 1), its grey from them (the brightness, the standard weights 0.2126, 0.7152 and 0.0722) and its spread, its largest channel less its smallest: 0 for a grey, 1 for a pure red. The colour is then pushed 1 + saturation / 100 + vibrance / 100 times (1 - spread) times as far from its grey as it was: 2 doubles its colour, 1 keeps it, 0 makes it grey. So vibrance 100 moves a dull tan 1.84 times and the vivid blue 1.38 times and leaves pure red as it is, and saturation -100 makes every colour its own grey. Each channel is held between 0 and 1 and goes back to linear light at the pixel's own covering. Both at 0 change nothing. **The method** is this program's own, modelled on After Effects' Vibrance; nothing is ported. The name is After Effects' own effect name, flagged with the rest of the third batch for document 10's pre-launch naming review. **Where it runs.** On a drawing's own pixels before its transform (ADR-017). It does not grow the layer, and a draft preview changes nothing, as nothing in it is a distance. **Known limits:** it does not protect skin tones as After Effects' Vibrance does, so a dull skin is lifted as much as any dull colour; the grey it pushes from is the brightness of the colour as written, not a perceptual lightness, so a strong push can shift how bright a colour looks; and a channel pushed past 0 or 1 is held there, so a push on an already bright colour flattens its top (the skin's red at vibrance 100, FX-VIBRANCE-002). **Out of range.** A command with vibrance or saturation outside -100 to 100 is refused with a sentence; a file that holds one keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, as D-46 does (FX-VIBRANCE-014 to 018).

D-141 / Leave Color / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-26** by the owner's message of 2026-09-26, "afterwards, work on 30 more recommended effects for either AE or/and anime/animation related.", the eighth of the third batch of thirty effects the agent chose and recommended (D-134 to D-163). One picture in `verification/B-84a proposal/`. FX-LEAVE-001 to 022 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-84. **It adds one effect and changes no existing fixture.** **What it does.** It turns a picture grey except for one chosen colour, as a film keeps a single red coat in a black-and-white scene, or an anime flashback is drained of everything but a heroine's ribbon. Each other colour turns the grey of its own brightness, so the rest reads as a black-and-white print. It is `core.leave_color`, named Leave Color in the Effects panel. The name is After Effects' own effect name: it is flagged, with the third batch's other After Effects names, for document 10's pre-launch naming review, as D-127's and D-128's are. It touches only the pixels that show, and keeps each one's covering, so a soft line edge stays soft and is kept or drained as its colour is. **Settings:** `color`, `#rrggbb` as D-87's, starting at `#ff0000`, the colour to keep; `tolerance`, 0 to 100, starting at 15, how far round the colour wheel from that colour a hue is still kept whole, 100 being the far side of the wheel (180 degrees), so 15 is 27 degrees each way; `softness`, 0 to 100, starting at 10, a band past the tolerance, on the same scale, over which the keeping fades out; and `amount`, 0 to 100, starting at 100, how far the other colours are turned grey. The three numbers can be keyed (D-68) and are held inside their ranges at each frame; the colour cannot. **The rule.** Each pixel that shows finds its hue, the angle of its colour round the wheel, as the colours are written (encoded values), the way a paint program's HSV hue is found; a grey has none. Its distance from the chosen colour's hue is the shorter way round the wheel, 0 for the same hue and 1 for the opposite one, and 1 when either is a grey. Within the tolerance the pixel is kept whole; past the tolerance plus the softness it is not kept at all; between, it is kept in proportion. The part not kept, times the amount, moves the pixel's colour toward its own grey: the weighted sum of its encoded red, green and blue (0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722). **The method** is this program's own, modelled on After Effects' Leave Color; nothing is ported. **Where it runs.** On a drawing's own pixels before its transform (ADR-017). It does not grow the layer, and a draft preview changes nothing, as it has no distances. **Known limits:** hue alone decides, so a pale, dull or dark colour of the kept hue is kept as a vivid one is, and the brown of a skin's shadow is kept with a red (FX-LEAVE-001); a grey is never kept, so a `color` that is a grey keeps nothing (FX-LEAVE-009); one colour only, where a scene needing two kept colours needs the effect twice on copies; the grey is the encoded brightness, not a perceptual lightness; and at softness 0 the edge of the tolerance is a hard yes or no, so a gradient across it steps. **Out of range.** A command with a tolerance, softness or amount outside 0 to 100, or a colour not written `#` and six hexadecimal digits, is refused with a sentence; a file that holds one keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, as D-46 does (FX-LEAVE-017 to 022).

D-142 / Solarize / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-26** by the owner's message of 2026-09-26, "afterwards, work on 30 more recommended effects for either AE or/and anime/animation related.", the ninth of the third batch of thirty effects the agent chose and recommended (D-134 to D-163). One picture in `verification/B-85a proposal/`. FX-SOLAR-001 to 016 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-85. **It adds one effect and changes no existing fixture.** **What it does.** It turns the bright part of each colour channel over, as a photograph briefly flashed with light while it develops: a channel at or above the threshold is inverted and one below it is kept, so the lights go dark and strange while the darks stay as they are, the look of a dream or a flashback. It is `core.solarize`, named Solarize in the Effects panel. The name is After Effects' own effect name (and an old darkroom word): it is flagged for document 10's pre-launch naming review. It touches only the pixels that show, and keeps each one's covering, so a soft line edge stays soft. **Settings:** `threshold`, 0 to 255, starting at 128, on the 8-bit scale of the colour as it is written. It can be keyed (D-68) and is held inside its range at each frame. **The rule.** Each pixel that shows reads its colour as it is written (encoded values, 0 to 1). Each channel is decided on its own: when 255 times it is at or above the threshold it becomes 1 minus itself, otherwise it is kept; the colour goes back to linear light at the pixel's own covering. A tiny 0.0001 is added before comparing, so an 8-bit value sitting exactly on the threshold is always inverted, by the build as by the reference. Because each channel is decided on its own, a colour with one channel above the threshold and another below changes hue: skin #f6d6be at 200 turns #0929be (FX-SOLAR-007). At 0 every channel is inverted, as Invert does; at 255 only a channel already at full is, so white turns black and nothing else changes. **The method** is this program's own, modelled on After Effects' Solarize; nothing is ported. **Where it runs.** On a drawing's own pixels before its transform (ADR-017). It does not grow the layer, and a draft preview changes nothing, as nothing in it is a distance. **Known limits:** the choice is a hard step with no softening, so a smooth gradient that crosses the threshold shows a sharp seam, and a keyed threshold moves that seam in whole 8-bit steps; the colour is turned per channel, not by brightness, so a threshold can change a hue as well as a tone; and no setting leaves every drawing untouched, since even 255 turns a full white black. **Out of range.** A command with the threshold outside 0 to 255 is refused with a sentence; a file that holds one keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, as D-46 does (FX-SOLAR-013 to 016).

D-143 / Halftone / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-26** by the owner's message of 2026-09-26, "afterwards, work on 30 more recommended effects for either AE or/and anime/animation related.", the tenth of the third batch of thirty effects the agent chose and recommended (D-134 to D-163). One picture in `verification/B-86a proposal/`. FX-HALFTONE-001 to 025 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-86. **It adds one effect and changes no existing fixture.** **What it does.** It turns a picture into manga screentone: its lightness drawn as round dots of ink on paper, small dots in the lights, large ones in the darks, running together into solid ink in the blacks. It is `core.halftone`, named Halftone in the Effects panel. **The name** is the printing term; the effect is modelled in spirit on After Effects' Color Halftone, not claimed to match it, and is flagged, with the rest of the third batch, for document 10's pre-launch naming review. It touches only the pixels that show and keeps each one's covering, so a soft edge stays soft and the dots never spill past the drawing. **Settings:** `size`, 2 to 200 pixels, starting at 8, the width of one dot's square cell; `angle`, -3600 to 3600 degrees, starting at 45, how far the rows of dots are turned, clockwise on the screen; `ink`, `#rrggbb` as D-87's, starting at `#000000`; `paper`, `#rrggbb`, starting at `#ffffff`; and `amount`, 0 to 100, starting at 100, how strongly the ink and paper are laid over the picture. The numbers can be keyed (D-68) and are held inside their ranges at each frame; the colours cannot. **The rule.** A screen of square cells `size` pixels wide, turned by the angle, is fixed to the drawing's own top left corner. Each pixel that shows finds how far its centre lies from the middle of its cell, in cells, and how dark its own colour is: one less its encoded brightness, 0 for white and 1 for black. Its dot is a circle whose area is that darkness times the cell's, until the dots touch at a darkness of pi / 4; past that the dot keeps widening, straight on to a radius of 0.71 cells at black, beyond the cell's corner, so black is ink everywhere and white is paper everywhere. The pixel is ink when it lies inside its dot and paper when not, with a hard edge and no smoothing, and its colour is moved toward the ink or the paper by the amount: Gradient's blend mix, normal. Each pixel's own lightness sets its own dot, so the dots follow the picture; ink or paper is a cliff, and the fixtures keep every pixel they decide at least 1e-5 from a dot's edge. **The method** is this program's own, modelled on After Effects' Color Halftone and on the screentone of manga; nothing is ported. **Where it runs.** On a drawing's own pixels before its transform (ADR-017), with the screen fixed to the drawing's own corner even after an effect above it has grown the layer, as FX-HALFTONE-016 shows, so the dots move with the drawing (FX-HALFTONE-015). It does not grow the layer. A draft preview scales the size, as it does other distances. On an adjustment layer it screens the picture below. **Known limits:** one screen of one ink, not the four turned screens of a colour print; the dots' edges are hard, one pixel either ink or paper, so at small sizes a dot is a few pixels and its roundness is lost; the dot sizes follow each pixel's own lightness rather than a cell's average, so a cell that crosses an edge is partly one dot and partly another; and the dots are round only, with no lines or squares. **Out of range.** A command with a size outside 2 to 200, an angle outside -3600 to 3600, an amount outside 0 to 100, or an ink or paper not written `#` and six hexadecimal digits is refused with a sentence; a file that holds one keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, as D-46 does (FX-HALFTONE-018 to 025).

D-144 / Mosaic / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-26** by the owner's message of 2026-09-26, "afterwards, work on 30 more recommended effects for either AE or/and anime/animation related.", the eleventh of the third batch of thirty effects the agent chose and recommended (D-134 to D-163). One picture in `verification/B-87a proposal/`. FX-MOSAIC-001 to 020 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-87. **It adds one effect and changes no existing fixture.** **What it does.** It breaks a picture into square blocks and paints each block one flat colour, the average of what was in it: the pixelated look of a censored face, a sign kept unreadable, or an old game's picture. It is `core.mosaic`, named Mosaic in the Effects panel. **The name** is After Effects' own effect name; the effect is modelled on it in spirit, not claimed to match it, and is flagged, with the rest of the third batch, for document 10's pre-launch naming review. **Settings:** `size`, 1 to 1000 pixels, starting at 10, the width and height of one block. It can be keyed (D-68) and is held inside its range at each frame, and it need not be a whole number: at 2.5 the blocks are three and two pixels wide by turns. **The rule.** The blocks are laid from the drawing's own top left corner, `size` pixels apart both ways; a block that runs past the layer's right or bottom edge is cut short and takes only the pixels it has. Every pixel of a block becomes the average of all the block's pixels, colour and covering alike, in linear light with the colour carried by its covering, so empty pixels count as empty and a block the drawing only partly covers comes out partly covered, its colour the drawing's own mix. Size 1 makes one-pixel blocks and changes nothing. Which block a pixel falls in is a choice made from a number, and the fixtures keep every pixel either exactly on a block's edge, with a size single precision holds exactly, or at least 1e-5 from one. **The method** is this program's own, modelled on After Effects' Mosaic; nothing is ported. **Where it runs.** On a drawing's own pixels before its transform (ADR-017), with the blocks fixed to the drawing's own corner even after an effect above it has grown the layer, as FX-MOSAIC-013 shows, so the blocks move with the drawing (FX-MOSAIC-012) and turn and scale with it. It does not grow the layer. A draft preview scales the size, as it does other distances; a size below 1 after that scaling makes one-pixel blocks, and the picture is untouched. On an adjustment layer it breaks up the picture below. **Known limits:** the blocks are square only, with no separate counts across and down as After Effects offers; each block is its average, with no choice of its middle pixel's sharper colour; the average is taken in linear light, so a block mixing black and white comes out lighter than a paint program's average of the written values would; the blocks start at the drawing's corner, not its middle, so a size that does not divide the drawing leaves a narrow row and column of blocks at its right and bottom edges; and the blocks follow the drawing, not the screen, so a layer turned by its transform shows turned blocks. **Out of range.** A command with a size outside 1 to 1000 is refused with a sentence; a file that holds one keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, as D-46 does (FX-MOSAIC-015 to 020).

D-145 / Emboss / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-26** by the owner's message of 2026-09-26, "afterwards, work on 30 more recommended effects for either AE or/and anime/animation related.", the twelfth of the third batch of thirty effects the agent chose and recommended (D-134 to D-163). One picture in `verification/B-88a proposal/`. FX-EMBOSS-001 to 026 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-88. **It adds one effect and changes no existing fixture.** **What it does.** It makes a drawing look pressed into metal or paper: the flat parts go a middle grey and every edge stands up as a raised or sunken ridge, lit from one side. Each pixel looks a little way ahead and the same way behind along one direction; where the picture ahead is brighter it turns lighter, where darker it turns darker, and where both are alike it stays the middle grey. So a drawing brighter than the emptiness around it stands up, and a dark shape inside it sinks in. It is `core.emboss`, named Emboss in the Effects panel. It touches only the pixels that show, and keeps each one's covering, so a soft line edge stays soft. **Settings:** `direction`, in degrees clockwise from up, -3600 to 3600, starting at 135 (the look ahead goes down and to the right); `relief`, 0 to 100, starting at 1, how many pixels ahead and behind it looks; `contrast`, 0 to 1000, starting at 100, how strongly a difference shows; and `mode`, "grey" or "color", starting at grey. The three numbers can be keyed (D-68) and are held inside their ranges at each frame; the mode is a word and is not keyed. **The rule.** Each pixel that shows takes the picture's brightness a relief ahead and a relief behind, each the smooth sample between the four nearest pixels, a look past the layer's edge held at its edge pixels; the brightness is of the colour over black, so a drawing's own outline against emptiness is an edge. Its grey, as written, is 0.5 plus the difference times contrast / 100. In grey mode all three channels become that grey; in color mode each channel as written is moved by the grey less 0.5, so the flat parts keep their colours and the edges are lit or shaded. Each channel is held between 0 and 1 and goes back to linear light at the pixel's own covering. Relief 0 or contrast 0 gives flat grey in grey mode and the drawing unchanged in color mode. **The method** is this program's own, modelled on After Effects' Emboss (grey) and Color Emboss (color) in spirit and not claimed to match them; nothing is ported. The name is After Effects' own effect name, flagged with the rest of the third batch for document 10's pre-launch naming review. **Where it runs.** On a drawing's own pixels before its transform (ADR-017). It does not grow the layer. The relief is a distance, so a draft preview scales it. **Known limits:** it looks at brightness only, so two colours of the same brightness side by side make no ridge; a relief that is not a whole number of pixels along a level or upright direction, or any relief along a slanting one, reads between pixels, so its ridges are softer and a pixel can sit in two ridges at once (FX-EMBOSS-001, 011); a look past the layer's edge reads the edge pixel, so a drawing that touches its layer's edge shows no ridge there (FX-EMBOSS-006); and a large contrast holds most edges at black or white (FX-EMBOSS-010). **Out of range.** A command with a direction outside -3600 to 3600, a relief outside 0 to 100 or a contrast outside 0 to 1000, or a mode other than the two words, is refused with a sentence; a file that holds one keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, as D-46 does (FX-EMBOSS-019 to 026).

D-146 / Find Edges / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-26** by the owner's message of 2026-09-26, "afterwards, work on 30 more recommended effects for either AE or/and anime/animation related.", the thirteenth of the third batch of thirty effects the agent chose and recommended (D-134 to D-163). One picture in `verification/B-89a proposal/`. FX-FINDEDGES-001 to 019 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-89. **It adds one effect and changes no existing fixture.** **What it does.** It turns a drawing into a sketch of its own edges, as a line test pulls the lines out of a painted cel: where the picture is flat it goes white, and where it changes sharply from one pixel to the next it goes dark, so every boundary between two colours, and the drawing's own outline against transparency, comes out as a dark line on white. Switched to invert it gives light lines on black, a neon or chalk look. It is `core.find_edges`, named Find Edges in the Effects panel. The name is After Effects' own effect name: it is flagged for document 10's pre-launch naming review. Its fixture prefix is FX-FINDEDGES, because FX-EDGES already belongs to D-109's Repeat Edge Pixels. **Settings:** `invert`, exactly `off` or `on`, starting at `off`, not keyable; and `amount`, 0 to 100, starting at 100, how far each pixel goes from its own colour to the sketch: 100 all the way, 50 half way, 0 not at all. The amount can be keyed (D-68) and is held inside its range at each frame. **The rule.** Each pixel's lightness is read as the picture shows over black, so an empty pixel counts as black. At each pixel the lightness of the three pixels to its right is compared with the three to its left, and the three below with the three above, the middle one of each three counting twice (a Sobel filter); past the drawing's border the border pixel repeats. The strength of the change, held at 1, is the edge: the sketch is 1 minus it (dark lines on white), or the edge itself with invert on. Each pixel that shows moves its colour, as it is written, the amount's share of the way to that grey, at its own covering; an empty pixel stays empty. Amount 0 changes nothing. **The method** is this program's own, modelled on After Effects' Find Edges; nothing is ported. **Where it runs.** On a drawing's own pixels before its transform (ADR-017). It does not grow the layer, and a draft preview scales nothing, as nothing in it is a distance. Because the border repeats, a picture that fills the frame has no line round its border (FX-FINDEDGES-011), while a character, whose own edges are empty, gets its outline. **Known limits:** the rule looks at a pixel's neighbours, not the pixel itself, so a line one pixel wide comes out as two dark lines, one either side, with its own middle pale where the colours either side of it match, as FX-FINDEDGES-001 and the picture's second panel show; a draft preview works on the smaller picture, where a line is a pixel of that smaller picture, so its lines look thicker than the full frame's; edges are found from lightness alone, so two colours of the same lightness (a red and a green of equal brightness) meet with no line; the sketch is always grey, one edge for all three colour channels, never coloured; and the edge strength is held at 1, so every strong edge is equally black. **Out of range.** A command with an amount outside 0 to 100, or an invert that is not `off` or `on` exactly as written (capitals are not the word), is refused with a sentence; a file that holds one keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, as D-46 does (FX-FINDEDGES-015 to 019).

D-147 / Sharpen / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-26** by the owner's message of 2026-09-26, "afterwards, work on 30 more recommended effects for either AE or/and anime/animation related.", the fourteenth of the third batch of thirty effects the agent chose and recommended (D-134 to D-163). One picture in `verification/B-90a proposal/`. FX-SHARPEN-001 to 018 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-90. **It adds one effect and changes no existing fixture.** **What it does.** It crisps a drawing's edges, as an unsharp mask crisps a soft scan or a slightly blurred render: each colour is pushed away from the blurred colour around it, so along an edge the light side grows lighter and the dark side darker, and a flat area stays as it is. It is `core.sharpen`, named Sharpen in the Effects panel. It touches only the pixels that show, and keeps each one's covering, so a soft line edge stays soft; a drawing's outline against transparency is not an edge to it, so a flat colour alone on an empty layer is left as it is. **Settings:** `amount`, 0 to 500 per cent, starting at 100: how far each colour is pushed; `radius`, 0 to 100 pixels, starting at 1: the width of the blur it is compared with, so how wide the halo along an edge is. Each can be keyed (D-68) and is held inside its range at each frame. **The rule.** Amount 0 or radius 0 change nothing. Otherwise the layer is blurred with the program's Gaussian blur at the radius, read back at the layer's own pixels; each pixel that shows reads its colour as it is written (encoded values, 0 to 1) and the blurred colour the same way, the blur's colour divided by its own covering, so the empty pixels around a drawing do not darken it. The colour is then pushed from the blurred colour by amount / 100 times the difference: at 100 a channel 0.1 darker than its blur ends 0.2 darker than it. Each channel is held between 0 and 1 and goes back to linear light at the pixel's own covering. So at the start settings a dark line beside skin goes to black and the skin beside it grows lighter (FX-SHARPEN-001), and at 500 the halos burn to white and pure colour (FX-SHARPEN-005). **The method** is this program's own, modelled on After Effects' Sharpen and Unsharp Mask, the darkroom's unsharp mask; nothing is ported. The name is After Effects' own effect name, flagged with the rest of the third batch for document 10's pre-launch naming review. **Where it runs.** On a drawing's own pixels before its transform (ADR-017). It does not grow the layer: what the blur spreads past the layer's edge is cut off. A draft preview scales the radius, as it is a distance. **Known limits:** it has no threshold, so it sharpens film grain and noise as readily as edges; it sharpens each channel of the colour as written, not its brightness alone, so an edge between two colours can shift their hues (the skin beside the blue band loses blue, FX-SHARPEN-001); a channel pushed past 0 or 1 is held there, so a strong amount flattens the halos to black, white or pure colour; and the blur is summed over three times the radius each way, so a large radius on a large layer is slow until the build's blur is used. **Out of range.** A command with amount outside 0 to 500 or radius outside 0 to 100 is refused with a sentence; a file that holds one keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, as D-46 does (FX-SHARPEN-013 to 018).

D-148 / Diffusion / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-26** by the owner's message of 2026-09-26, "afterwards, work on 30 more recommended effects for either AE or/and anime/animation related.", the fifteenth of the third batch of thirty effects the agent chose and recommended (D-134 to D-163). One picture in `verification/B-91a proposal/`. FX-DIFFUSE-001 to 018 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-91. **It adds one effect and changes no existing fixture.** **What it does.** It is anime compositing's diffusion: a soft glow of the picture laid over itself, so the lights bloom gently into the darks beside them and the whole cel takes on a hazy, filmic softness while its lines stay where they are. It is `core.diffusion`, named Diffusion in the Effects panel. It touches only the pixels that show and keeps each one's covering, so a soft line edge stays soft and the glow never spills onto an empty pixel. **Settings:** `radius`, 0 to 500, starting at 10, how far the glow spreads, a distance; `amount`, 0 to 100, starting at 50, per cent, how much of the glow is laid on; and `blend`, exactly "screen", "lighten" or "normal", starting at screen, how it is laid on. The radius and the amount can be keyed (D-68) and are held inside their ranges at each frame; the blend is a word and is not keyed. **The rule.** The glow is the drawing through the Gaussian blur at sigma radius / 3, read at the drawing's own pixels, and divided by its own covering, so the emptiness round a drawing does not darken the glow at its edge. Each pixel that shows takes its straight colour and the glow's colour there and lays the glow on: screen lightens the colour by the glow as two slides projected together do, lighten takes the larger of the two in each channel, and normal takes the glow's colour. The amount then moves the colour that far, per cent, from its own towards the result, and it goes back at its own covering; nothing is clamped. So at amount 50 the result is exactly halfway between the drawing and amount 100 (FX-DIFFUSE-001 and 002), screen and lighten never darken a pixel, lighten leaves the brightest colours as they are (FX-DIFFUSE-007), and normal at 100 is the drawing blurred inside its own outline (FX-DIFFUSE-008). Amount 0 or radius 0 changes nothing. **The method** is this program's own, modelled in spirit on the diffusion filter of anime compositing (the picture blurred and screened over itself) and on After Effects' soft-glow recipes; nothing is ported. Diffusion is not an After Effects effect name, but the name is flagged with the rest of the third batch for document 10's pre-launch naming review. **Where it runs.** On a drawing's own pixels before its transform (ADR-017). It does not grow the layer: the glow is cut at the layer's edge. The radius is a distance, so a draft preview scales it. **Known limits:** the glow is of the whole picture, not only its lights, so at a large amount a dark line is lifted as much as a shadow (the line and band in the picture's third panel) and the cel's contrast drops; the glow stays inside the layer's own pixels, so it never haloes out past a drawing's outline onto what is behind, as a light-wrap or a glow does; and a wide radius on a small drawing reads mostly the drawing's own average colour, as FX-DIFFUSE-006 shows. **Out of range.** A command with a radius outside 0 to 500, an amount outside 0 to 100 or a blend other than the three words is refused with a sentence; a file that holds one keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, as D-46 does (FX-DIFFUSE-013 to 018).

D-149 / Wave Warp / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-26** by the owner's message of 2026-09-26, "afterwards, work on 30 more recommended effects for either AE or/and anime/animation related.", the sixteenth of the third batch of thirty effects the agent chose and recommended (D-134 to D-163). One picture in `verification/B-92a proposal/`. FX-WAVE-001 to 024 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-92. **It adds one effect and changes no existing fixture.** **What it does.** It runs a regular wave across a drawing: a flag in the wind, a reflection in water, a wobbling title, a dream sequence's sway. The wave runs along a direction and pushes each pixel across it, to one side and then the other, so straight lines across the wave become waves; with a speed the wave travels from frame to frame. It is `core.wave_warp`, named Wave Warp in the Effects panel. **The name** is After Effects' own effect name; the effect is modelled on it in spirit, not claimed to match it, and is flagged, with the rest of the third batch, for document 10's pre-launch naming review. **Settings:** `shape`, the word `sine` or `triangle`, starting at `sine`, a smooth wave or a zigzag of straight sides; `height`, 0 to 1000, starting at 10, how many pixels a push reaches at most; `width`, 1 to 10000, starting at 40, how many pixels one whole wave spans; `direction`, -3600 to 3600 degrees, starting at 90, the way the wave runs, 0 up and 90 to the right, clockwise on the screen; `speed`, -360 to 360 degrees a frame, starting at 0; `phase`, -100000 to 100000 degrees, starting at 0, how far along the wave is slid; and `edges`, the word `transparent` or `repeat`, starting at `transparent`. Every number can be keyed (D-68) and is held inside its range at each frame; the words cannot. **The rule.** Each pixel finds how far along the wave's direction its centre lies in the drawing's own space, and from that its place on the wave, the phase and the speed times the frame added in degrees; the wave's value there, between -1 and 1, times the height is how far the pixel is pushed, a quarter turn clockwise from the direction. The pixel then takes the smooth sample between the four nearest pixels at the point that far back, so the picture moves by the push. With direction 90 the wave runs to the right and pushes pixels down and up; with direction 0 it runs up and pushes them right and left. With `transparent` the layer first grows by the height, rounded up, on every side, so a picture pushed past its edge is kept, and a push that reaches past the picture reads emptiness; with `repeat` it does not grow and a push past the edge reads the nearest edge pixel. Height 0 changes nothing. **The method** is this program's own, modelled on After Effects' Wave Warp in spirit; nothing is ported. The wave is fixed to the drawing, so a layer that moves carries its wave with it. **Where it runs.** On a drawing's own pixels before its transform (ADR-017), in the drawing's own space even after an effect above it has grown the layer. With `transparent` it grows the layer by the height rounded up; with `repeat` it does not. The frame it uses is the composition frame, a hidden value filled in as Noise's is, never saved, and the effect cache keys on it. The height and the width are distances, so a draft preview scales both. **Known limits:** two shapes only, with none of After Effects' square, sawtooth, circle, semicircle or noise waves; no pinning of the layer's edges, so a whole drawing sways, its border included; the push is one straight line across the wave, so the wave never folds over or curls; and on a small drawing the start settings' height is large, so most of the drawing is pushed out of the frame (FX-WAVE-001), which is the right look on a full frame. **Out of range.** A command with a number outside its range, or a shape or edges word other than its two, is refused with a sentence; a file that holds one keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, as D-46 does (FX-WAVE-017 to 024).

D-150 / Ripple / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-26** by the owner's message of 2026-09-26, "afterwards, work on 30 more recommended effects for either AE or/and anime/animation related.", the seventeenth of the third batch of thirty effects the agent chose and recommended (D-134 to D-163). One picture in `verification/B-93a proposal/`. FX-RIPPLE-001 to 026 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-93. **It adds one effect and changes no existing fixture.** **What it does.** It sends rings out from a point across a picture, as on a pond after a stone falls in: each pixel shows the picture from a little way along its line through the centre, further out and nearer in by turns, so straight lines bend into rings about the centre, and with a speed the rings travel outward from frame to frame on their own, with no keys. It is `core.ripple`, named Ripple in the Effects panel. **The name** is modelled in spirit on After Effects' Ripple, not claimed to match it, and is flagged, with the rest of the third batch, for document 10's pre-launch naming review. **Settings:** `center`, two numbers, per cent of the drawing, each -1000 to 1000, starting at 50, 50, the middle; `amplitude`, 0 to 1000 pixels, starting at 5, the farthest a pixel reads from; `wavelength`, 1 to 10000 pixels, starting at 30, how far apart the rings are; `speed`, -360 to 360 degrees a frame, starting at 20, how fast the rings travel, outward above 0 and inward below, a full turn of 360 moving them one wavelength; `phase`, -100000 to 100000 degrees, starting at 0, where the rings stand at frame 0; and `fade`, 0 to 100000 pixels, starting at 0, off, the distance from the centre at which the ripple has died away to nothing. All of them can be keyed (D-68) and are held inside their ranges at each frame. **The rule.** With amplitude 0 the picture is unchanged. Otherwise each pixel measures its distance d from the centre. The pixel at the centre itself, if a pixel's middle lands there exactly, is kept as it is. Every other pixel takes a wave height w, the sine of 2 pi d over the wavelength less the phase plus the speed times the frame, turned to radians, between -1 and 1; with a fade, w is scaled down in a straight line to 0 at the fade distance and stays 0 beyond it. The pixel shows the picture at the point amplitude times w pixels further out along its line from the centre (nearer in when w is below 0), read with document 21's bilinear sample, and empty where that point lies off the picture. The frame is the composition frame, filled in by the build as Noise's is and never saved. A pixel whose w is 0, on a still ring or past the fade, is kept exactly. **The method** is this program's own, modelled on After Effects' Ripple; nothing is ported. **Where it runs.** On a drawing's own pixels before its transform (ADR-017), with the centre fixed to the drawing, so the rings move with it (FX-RIPPLE-015). It does not grow the layer, so a picture drawn in toward the centre leaves empty pixels at its edges rather than reaching past them. A draft preview scales the amplitude, the wavelength and the fade, as it does other distances. On an adjustment layer it ripples the picture below. **Known limits:** one centre only, with no second source to interfere; the rings are perfect circles, with no ellipse for a surface seen at an angle; a pixel reads from a single point, so a large amplitude with a short wavelength breaks the picture up rather than blurring it (FX-RIPPLE-016); there is no light or shading on the crests, only the bending; and the layer does not grow, so a ripple that would push the picture past its edge is cut there. **Out of range.** A command with a centre number outside -1000 to 1000, an amplitude outside 0 to 1000, a wavelength outside 1 to 10000, a speed outside -360 to 360, a phase outside -100000 to 100000 or a fade outside 0 to 100000 is refused with a sentence; a file that holds one keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, as D-46 does (FX-RIPPLE-019 to 026).

D-151 / Twirl / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-26** by the owner's message of 2026-09-26, "afterwards, work on 30 more recommended effects for either AE or/and anime/animation related.", the eighteenth of the third batch of thirty effects the agent chose and recommended (D-134 to D-163). One picture in `verification/B-94a proposal/`. FX-TWIRL-001 to 021 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-94. **It adds one effect and changes no existing fixture.** **What it does.** It turns a drawing about a centre, most at the centre and less and less further out, so straight lines bend into a spiral: a whirlpool, a spell being cast, a character's dizzy spell, a transition that swirls the picture away. Inside a circle about the centre each pixel takes the picture from a point turned back about it; on and past the circle nothing moves. A positive angle turns the picture clockwise on the screen. It is `core.twirl`, named Twirl in the Effects panel. The name is After Effects' own effect name: it is flagged for document 10's pre-launch naming review. **Settings:** `angle`, -3600 to 3600 degrees, starting at 90, how far the picture is turned at the centre itself, a negative angle turning it the other way; `radius`, 0 to 10000, starting at 50, how many pixels from the centre the twirl reaches; and `center`, two numbers, per cent of the drawing's width and height as Radial Blur's centre is, starting at 50, 50, its middle, allowed from -1000 to 1000 so the centre may sit off the drawing. All three can be keyed (D-68) and are held inside their ranges at each frame. **The rule.** At each pixel, with d its distance from the centre: at d equal to the radius or more the pixel is kept exactly; nearer, it takes the smooth sample between the four nearest pixels at the point the angle times (1 - d / radius) squared back round the centre, at its own distance from it, and a sample off the layer reads transparent. The turn is the whole angle at the centre, a quarter of it half way out, and falls smoothly to none at the circle's edge, so the picture stays joined up across the edge. Angle 0 or radius 0 changes nothing. **The method** is this program's own, modelled on After Effects' Twirl; nothing is ported. **Where it runs.** On a drawing's own pixels before its transform (ADR-017), with the centre in the drawing's own size even after an effect above it has grown the layer, as FX-TWIRL-015 shows. It does not grow the layer: a picture turned past the layer's edge is cut, and a pixel whose point lies past the edge reads emptiness, so a twirl that reaches the corners of a drawing that fills its layer pulls emptiness in there, as FX-TWIRL-001 shows along its right side. The radius is a distance, so a draft preview scales it; the angle and the centre are not. **Known limits:** each pixel is one sample, so a large angle near the centre, where the picture is wound tightly, breaks into loose pixels rather than a smooth smear (FX-TWIRL-007, and the picture's fourth panel); the circle is round, not the drawing's shape, so on a wide drawing a radius that reaches its sides also reaches past its top and bottom; and the twirl does not grow the layer, so to swirl a picture out past its own edge it needs room drawn around it first. **Out of range.** A command with an angle outside -3600 to 3600, a radius outside 0 to 10000 or a centre number outside -1000 to 1000 is refused with a sentence; a file that holds one, as a constant or at any key, keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, as D-46 does (FX-TWIRL-016 to 021).

D-152 / Bulge / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-26** by the owner's message of 2026-09-26, "afterwards, work on 30 more recommended effects for either AE or/and anime/animation related.", the nineteenth of the third batch of thirty effects the agent chose and recommended (D-134 to D-163). One picture in `verification/B-95a proposal/`. FX-BULGE-001 to 023 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-95. **It adds one effect and changes no existing fixture.** **What it does.** It swells a round part of the picture outward, as if seen through a lens or pushed from behind, or with a negative height pinches it in: a cheek puffed out, a punch landing, a magnifying glass, a comic wobble. It is `core.bulge`, named Bulge in the Effects panel. **The name** is After Effects' Bulge's; the effect is modelled on it in spirit, not claimed to match it, and is flagged, with the rest of the third batch, for document 10's pre-launch naming review. **Settings:** `center`, a point given in per cent of the drawing's own width and height, each -1000 to 1000, starting at 50, 50, the middle; `radius`, 0 to 10000 pixels, starting at 50, the size of the circle that is warped; and `height`, -4 to 4, starting at 1, how strongly the middle is swelled (positive) or pinched (negative). All three can be keyed (D-68) and are held inside their ranges at each frame. **The rule.** Inside the circle, each pixel takes the picture from a point on the line to the centre, pulled in by an amount that is greatest at the centre and falls smoothly to nothing at the circle's edge, so the middle is magnified and the ring round it squeezed; with a negative height the point is pushed out instead and the middle shrinks. At height 1 the centre is magnified twice; from height 2 up, a small disc about the centre all reads the centre point itself, one flat colour. The picture is read between pixels by document 21's bilinear sample, and past the drawing it reads emptiness. Every pixel outside the circle is kept exactly, and at the circle's edge the pull is nothing, so there is no seam. Height 0 or radius 0 leave the picture as it is. **The method** is this program's own, modelled on After Effects' Bulge; nothing is ported. **Where it runs.** On a drawing's own pixels before its transform (ADR-017), the centre fixed to the drawing, so the swell moves with it (FX-BULGE-015). It does not grow the layer: a swell that would carry the picture past the drawing's edge is cut there, and a pinch near the edge reads emptiness from beyond it. A warp moves covering as well as colour, so a soft edge moves with the picture and an empty pixel inside the circle can take covering from its neighbour (FX-BULGE-016). A draft preview scales the radius, as it does other distances. On an adjustment layer it warps the picture below. **Known limits:** the circle is round only, with no separate width and height; the warp's profile is one fixed curve, with no taper setting; the sample is bilinear, so a strong swell softens the picture it magnifies; and a swell can only show what is inside the drawing, never what is past its edge. **Out of range.** A command with a centre outside -1000 to 1000 on either axis, a radius outside 0 to 10000 or a height outside -4 to 4 is refused with a sentence; a file that holds one keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, as D-46 does (FX-BULGE-018 to 023).

D-153 / Mirror / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-26** by the owner's message of 2026-09-26, "afterwards, work on 30 more recommended effects for either AE or/and anime/animation related.", the twentieth of the third batch of thirty effects the agent chose and recommended (D-134 to D-163). One picture in `verification/B-96a proposal/`. FX-MIRROR-001 to 024 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-96. **It adds one effect and changes no existing fixture.** **What it does.** It reflects a drawing across a straight line, as if a looking-glass stood on it: the picture on one side of the line is kept exactly, and the other side shows its reflection, so half a face becomes a whole symmetric one, a figure meets its own double, or a background is made to match itself left and right. It is `core.mirror`, named Mirror in the Effects panel. The name is After Effects' own effect name: it is flagged for document 10's pre-launch naming review. **Settings:** `center`, two numbers, per cent of the drawing's width and height, starting at 50, 50, the drawing's middle, each allowed from -1000 to 1000, a point the line runs through; and `angle`, in degrees, -3600 to 3600, starting at 0, which turns the line: at 0 it runs straight up and down, the right side is kept and the left side shows the right's reflection; at 90 the line lies across, the bottom is kept and shown on top; at 180 the left is kept, and at 270 the top. Both can be keyed (D-68), the centre one key holding both numbers, and are held inside their ranges at each frame. **The rule.** Each pixel on the kept side of the line, or on the line itself, is kept exactly. Each pixel on the other side takes the picture from its mirror point, the point as far past the line on the kept side, as the smooth sample between the four nearest pixels that document 21's bilinear sample takes; a mirror point past the drawing's edge reads emptiness. At whole quarter turns, with the line on a pixel edge or through a pixel's middle, every reflected pixel is an exact copy; otherwise the reflected side's colours are blends of neighbours. On the line the reflection is the point itself, so the two sides meet without a seam. A line at or past the drawing's edge with the whole drawing on its kept side changes nothing; one with the whole drawing on its other side leaves it empty, its reflection lying past the edge. **The method** is this program's own, modelled on After Effects' Mirror in spirit and not claimed to match it; nothing is ported. **Where it runs.** On a drawing's own pixels before its transform (ADR-017). It does not grow the layer, and the centre is per cent of the drawing's own size, placed in the drawing's own space even after an effect above it has grown the layer, so the reflected side can read the pixels that effect grew. A draft preview changes nothing, as nothing in it is a distance. **Known limits:** it reflects within the layer only, so a line near an edge reflects emptiness onto part of the other side, as FX-MIRROR-011 and 013 show, and the composition around the layer is never drawn on; it has one line, not the several of a kaleidoscope; and a line at an angle that is not a whole quarter turn, or through a point between pixel edges and middles, softens the reflected side a little, as FX-MIRROR-008 and 010 show. **Out of range.** A command with a centre number outside -1000 to 1000 or an angle outside -3600 to 3600 is refused with a sentence; a file that holds one, as a constant or at any key, keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, as D-46 does (FX-MIRROR-019 to 024).

D-154 / Motion Tile / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-26** by the owner's message of 2026-09-26, "afterwards, work on 30 more recommended effects for either AE or/and anime/animation related.", the twenty-first of the third batch of thirty effects the agent chose and recommended (D-134 to D-163). One picture in `verification/B-97a proposal/`. FX-TILE-001 to 023 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-97. **It adds one effect and changes no existing fixture.** **What it does.** It repeats a layer's picture around itself, tile against tile, so a small patch of pattern fills a larger area: a repeating background or wallpaper, a floor, a sky of clouds slid with Offset, or a picture that must still cover the frame after it is moved, scaled down or shaken. With mirror on, every other tile is turned over, so the tiles meet edge to matching edge with no seam. It is `core.motion_tile`, named Motion Tile in the Effects panel. **The name** is After Effects' own effect name; the effect is modelled on it in spirit, not claimed to match it, and is flagged, with the rest of the third batch, for document 10's pre-launch naming review. **Settings:** `output_width`, 100 to 1000 per cent, starting at 100, how wide the tiled layer is against the picture; `output_height`, 100 to 1000 per cent, starting at 100, how tall; and `mirror`, the word `off` or `on`, starting at `off`. Both numbers can be keyed (D-68) and are held inside their range at each frame; the word cannot. **The rule.** The layer grows on the left and the right by the extra width, half each side, rounded up to a whole pixel, and above and below by the extra height likewise, so the picture stays where it was, in the middle. Every new pixel copies the pixel of the picture a whole number of picture widths and heights away, exactly, with no mixing, so the tiles repeat outward from the picture; with mirror on, every other tile across is turned over left to right and every other tile down top to bottom, so the pixel beside each edge is that edge's own. Both at 100 change nothing. Because the growth is rounded up to whole pixels, an output of 150 per cent on a picture six pixels wide is ten pixels wide, not nine (FX-TILE-010). **The method** is this program's own, modelled on After Effects' Motion Tile in spirit; nothing is ported. **Where it runs.** On a drawing's own pixels before its transform (ADR-017), on the input as it reaches the effect, the pixels an earlier effect grew included, as Offset's does (D-131), so a drop shadow ahead of it is tiled with the picture (FX-TILE-016). It grows the layer by the rounded-up halves of the extra width and height. The percentages are not distances, so a draft preview does not scale them. **Known limits:** no tile centre or tile width and height of its own, as After Effects has, so the tile is always the whole layer as it reaches the effect; no phase or horizontal phase shift, so rows of tiles never stagger like bricks (Offset ahead of it slides the pattern instead); a layer grown by an earlier effect is tiled with its growth, its empty margin included, which puts gaps between the tiles; and at 1000 per cent a large layer grows to a hundred times its area, which costs memory and time as any growth does. **Out of range.** A command with a number outside its range, or a mirror word other than its two, is refused with a sentence; a file that holds one keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, as D-46 does (FX-TILE-017 to 023).

D-155 / Linear Wipe / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-26** by the owner's message of 2026-09-26, "afterwards, work on 30 more recommended effects for either AE or/and anime/animation related.", the twenty-second of the third batch of thirty effects the agent chose and recommended (D-134 to D-163). One picture in `verification/B-98a proposal/`. FX-LWIPE-001 to 032 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-98. **It adds one effect and changes no existing fixture.** **What it does.** It wipes a layer away behind a straight edge that sweeps across it, the plainest transition between two shots: keyed from 0 to 100, the layer is cleared off one side to the other and whatever is under it shows through. It is `core.linear_wipe`, named Linear Wipe in the Effects panel. **Settings:** `completion`, 0 to 100 per cent, starting at 0, how far the edge has gone; `angle`, in degrees, -3600 to 3600, starting at 90, the way the edge moves, 0 up and 90 right on the screen, so at the start the layer is wiped from the left, the edge moving right; and `feather`, 0 to 10000 pixels, starting at 0, how soft the edge is. All three can be keyed (D-68) and are held inside their ranges at each frame. **The rule.** At completion 0 the layer is untouched, and at 100 it is gone, every pixel transparent. Between, the edge is a straight line across the drawing at right angles to the angle's direction; completion 0 puts it just behind the drawing's first corner in that direction, feather included, and 100 just past its last, so the edge crosses the whole drawing, whatever the angle. A pixel whose centre is ahead of the edge stays whole and one behind it is gone; with a feather, pixels within half the feather either side keep a part growing evenly from none to all. Each pixel keeps that part of all four channels, colour and covering alike. The corners and the pixel centres are the drawing's own, so the wipe moves with the layer. **The method** is this program's own, modelled on After Effects' Linear Wipe; nothing is ported. **The name** is After Effects' own effect name: it is flagged, with the rest of the third batch, for document 10's pre-launch naming review, as D-127's and D-128's are. **Where it runs.** On a drawing's own pixels before its transform (ADR-017). It does not grow the layer. Pixels an earlier effect grew beyond the drawing, a drop shadow's, follow the same edge, which is measured on the drawing alone, so near the ends of a wipe they can outlast the drawing or go before it; completion 0 and 100 hold for them too (FX-LWIPE-021 to 024). A draft preview scales the feather, a distance. **Known limits:** with feather 0 the edge is a cliff, a pixel either side of it whole or gone, so a slowly keyed wipe steps a whole pixel at a time and the edge on a diagonal is a staircase (FX-LWIPE-009); only a straight edge (Radial Wipe, Venetian Blinds and Iris Wipe give the others); the edge crosses the drawing's box, not the grown pixels, so a shadow beyond the drawing is not wiped in step with it; and a pixel within a hair of a hard edge could in principle be decided differently by the build's single precision, which the fixtures avoid by design. **Out of range.** A command with a completion outside 0 to 100, an angle outside -3600 to 3600 or a feather outside 0 to 10000, or any of them not a number, is refused with a sentence; a file that holds one keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, as D-46 does (FX-LWIPE-025 to 032).

D-156 / Radial Wipe / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-26** by the owner's message of 2026-09-26, "afterwards, work on 30 more recommended effects for either AE or/and anime/animation related.", the twenty-third of the third batch of thirty effects the agent chose and recommended (D-134 to D-163). One picture in `verification/B-99a proposal/`. FX-RWIPE-001 to 029 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-99. **It adds one effect and changes no existing fixture.** **What it does.** It wipes a drawing away like the hand of a clock sweeping round a centre: a transition that clears a card off the screen or, on a layer above, reveals the picture below it, a countdown or a cooldown circle, a title card sweeping away between scenes. From a start line the sweep goes clockwise, counter-clockwise, or both ways at once, and the completion says how much of the whole turn has been swept away; a feather softens the sweeping edge. It is `core.radial_wipe`, named Radial Wipe in the Effects panel. The name is After Effects' own effect name: it is flagged for document 10's pre-launch naming review. **Settings:** `completion`, 0 to 100, starting at 0, how much of the turn is swept away, 0 nothing and 100 everything; `start_angle`, -3600 to 3600 degrees, starting at 0, the line the sweep starts from, 0 straight up and 90 to the right; `center`, two numbers, per cent of the drawing's width and height as Radial Blur's centre is, starting at 50, 50, its middle, allowed from -1000 to 1000 so the centre may sit off the drawing; `wipe`, "clockwise", "counterclockwise" or "both", starting at clockwise; and `feather`, 0 to 360 degrees, starting at 0, how wide the fade at the sweeping edge is. The four numbers can be keyed (D-68) and are held inside their ranges at each frame; the word cannot. **The rule.** At completion 0 the drawing is untouched, and at completion 100 every pixel is transparent. Between, each pixel's angle round the centre is measured from the start line, clockwise; counterclockwise measures it the other way round, and both measures the shorter way either side of the start line, doubled, so the wipe opens like a fan both ways at once. The sweeping edge sits at the completion's share of the turn; a pixel the edge has passed is gone, one it has not reached is kept exactly, and with a feather the pixels within half the feather of the edge keep a part of themselves, fading smoothly across it. The part is laid on colour and covering alike, so a soft edge stays soft. The feather is spread so that completion 0 still keeps everything and 100 still clears everything. **The method** is this program's own, modelled on After Effects' Radial Wipe; nothing is ported. **Where it runs.** On a drawing's own pixels before its transform (ADR-017), with the centre in the drawing's own size even after an effect above it has grown the layer; grown pixels are wiped by the same rule, as FX-RWIPE-021 shows. It does not grow the layer. The feather is in degrees, not a distance, so nothing is scaled for a draft preview. **Known limits:** each pixel is decided at its centre, one sample, so a hard edge (feather 0) is stair-stepped along a slant, as FX-RWIPE-009 and the picture's second panel show; a small feather smooths it. The start line is always hard, except for "both", since a pixel just before it has the whole turn to go and one just after it none: a feather softens only the sweeping edge, as FX-RWIPE-010 and 012 show. The wipe takes pixels away and never draws anything; to reveal a picture, the picture goes on a layer below. **Out of range.** A command with a completion outside 0 to 100, a start angle outside -3600 to 3600, a centre number outside -1000 to 1000, a feather outside 0 to 360, or a wipe that is not one of the three words, written exactly, is refused with a sentence; a file that holds one, as a constant or at any key, keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, as D-46 does (FX-RWIPE-022 to 029).

D-157 / Venetian Blinds / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-26** by the owner's message of 2026-09-26, "afterwards, work on 30 more recommended effects for either AE or/and anime/animation related.", the twenty-fourth of the third batch of thirty effects the agent chose and recommended (D-134 to D-163). One picture in `verification/B-100a proposal/`. FX-BLINDS-001 to 026 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-100. **It adds one effect and changes no existing fixture.** **What it does.** It is a transition that wipes a layer away in stripes, as a set of window blinds closing does: the layer is cut into parallel slats, and as the completion goes from 0 to 100 each slat is cleared from one of its edges, the same part of every slat at once, until nothing is left. Keyed from 100 down to 0 it brings a layer in the same way. It is `core.venetian_blinds`, named Venetian Blinds in the Effects panel. The name is After Effects' own effect name: it is flagged, with the rest of the third batch, for document 10's pre-launch naming review, as D-127's and D-128's are. **Settings:** `completion`, 0 to 100, starting at 0, how much of each slat is cleared; `angle`, in degrees, -3600 to 3600, starting at 0, which turns the slats: at 0 they lie level and each is cleared from its bottom edge upward, at 90 they stand upright and each is cleared from its left edge rightward, at 180 from the top down and at 270 from the right; `width`, 1 to 10000 pixels, starting at 20, each slat's width; and `feather`, 0 to 10000 pixels, starting at 0, how far the moving edge is softened. All four can be keyed (D-68) and are held inside their ranges at each frame. **The rule.** The slats are laid across the drawing's own space from its top left corner, in the direction the angle gives. Each pixel's centre is placed across its slat, from 0 at the slat's starting edge up to the width at its far edge. The moving edge sits at the completion's share of the width plus the feather, less half the feather, so it starts just before the slat and ends just past it. Without a feather, a pixel before the edge is cleared and a pixel at or past it is kept exactly; with one, the pixel is kept by a share that rises evenly from 0 to 1 across the feather, centred on the edge. The share multiplies all four channels alike, so the colour is kept and only the covering falls, and an empty pixel stays empty. At completion 0 the layer is untouched and at 100 every pixel is empty, feathered or not. **The method** is this program's own, modelled on After Effects' Venetian Blinds in spirit and not claimed to match it; nothing is ported. **Where it runs.** On a drawing's own pixels before its transform (ADR-017), so the slats move, turn and scale with the layer. It does not grow the layer. The width and the feather are distances, so a draft preview scales them. **Known limits:** without a feather each pixel is either kept or cleared, so the slats' edges are hard and, at angles that are not whole quarter turns, stepped, as FX-BLINDS-008 shows; a feather softens only the moving edge, and each slat's fixed edge stays hard, the covering jumping back to full at the next slat, as FX-BLINDS-012 shows; the slats start at the drawing's top left corner and cannot be slid; the slats are straight, never curved or staggered; and a pixel within a hair of an edge could in principle be decided differently by the build's single precision, which the fixtures avoid by design. **Out of range.** A command with a completion outside 0 to 100, an angle outside -3600 to 3600, a width outside 1 to 10000 or a feather outside 0 to 10000, or one not a number, is refused with a sentence; a file that holds one, as a constant or at any key, keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, as D-46 does (FX-BLINDS-019 to 026).

D-158 / Iris Wipe / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-26** by the owner's message of 2026-09-26, "afterwards, work on 30 more recommended effects for either AE or/and anime/animation related.", the twenty-fifth of the third batch of thirty effects the agent chose and recommended (D-134 to D-163). Inside the circle the picture is kept exactly and outside it the layer is transparent, so whatever lies below shows through. It is `core.iris_wipe`, named Iris Wipe in the Effects panel. The name is After Effects' own effect name: it is flagged for document 10's pre-launch naming review. **Settings:** `completion`, 0 to 100, starting at 0, how far the wipe has gone; `center`, two numbers, per cent of the drawing's width and height as Radial Blur's centre is, starting at 50, 50, the drawing's middle, each allowed from -1000 to 1000, the point the circle closes on; `feather`, 0 to 10000 pixels, starting at 0, the width over which the circle's edge is softened; and `invert`, "off" or "on", starting at off, which opens a hole instead of closing a circle. The three numbers can be keyed (D-68), the centre one key holding both numbers, and are held inside their ranges at each frame; the word cannot be keyed. **The rule.** At completion 0 the drawing is kept exactly and at 100 every pixel is transparent, whatever the other settings. Between, the circle's full size is the distance from the centre to the drawing's farthest corner, so at completion 0 it just covers the drawing; it shrinks in step with the completion, to nothing at 100. A pixel whose centre lies inside the circle, or on it, is kept exactly and one outside it is transparent, all four channels together. Inverted, the hole grows from the centre in step with the completion in the same way, the inside gone and the outside kept, so a wipe inverted at completion c is the exact opposite of one not inverted at 100 - c. **The method** is this program's own, modelled on After Effects' Iris Wipe in spirit and not claimed to match it; nothing is ported. **Where it runs.** On a drawing's own pixels before its transform (ADR-017). It does not grow the layer; the centre is per cent of the drawing's own size and the full size is measured to the corners of the drawing's own box, even after an effect above it has grown the layer. The feather is a distance, so a draft preview scales it. **Known limits:** the shape is a circle only, not a star, a diamond or an ellipse fitted to the frame; it is measured on the layer's own drawing, not on the composition, so on a layer smaller than the frame it closes on that layer, and to close the whole picture it goes on an adjustment layer or a covering solid; with no feather the edge is hard and follows the pixel grid, so a small circle is a blocky shape, as FX-IRIS-006's four by four square shows; and a feather wider than the drawing is a gentle fade of the whole picture rather than a circle, as FX-IRIS-010 shows. **Out of range.** A command with a completion outside 0 to 100, a centre number outside -1000 to 1000, a feather outside 0 to 10000 or an invert other than "off" or "on" is refused with a sentence; a file that holds one, as a constant or at any key, keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, as D-46 does (FX-IRIS-020 to 027).

D-159 / Simple Choker / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-26** by the owner's message of 2026-09-26, "afterwards, work on 30 more recommended effects for either AE or/and anime/animation related.", the twenty-sixth of the third batch of thirty effects the agent chose and recommended (D-134 to D-163). One picture in `verification/B-102a proposal/`. FX-CHOKE-001 to 017 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-102. **It adds one effect and changes no existing fixture.** **What it does.** It tightens or loosens a drawing's edge, as a compositor chokes a matte after keying: a positive choke shrinks the covering by that many pixels, taking away specks, thin lines and fringes and opening holes wider; a negative choke spreads it, filling pinholes and small gaps and fattening a thin line. It never mixes a colour where there was covering: a shrunk pixel keeps its own colour at less covering, and a spread pixel that was empty takes the average colour of the covered pixels within reach. It is `core.simple_choker`, named Simple Choker in the Effects panel. **The name** is After Effects' own effect name; the effect is modelled on it in spirit, not claimed to match it, and is flagged, with the rest of the third batch, for document 10's pre-launch naming review. **Settings:** `choke`, -100 to 100 pixels, starting at 0, positive to shrink and negative to spread. It can be keyed (D-68) and is held inside its range at each frame. **The rule.** The reach is the choke without its sign, counted on whole-pixel steps as Outline's width is: a step counts when its length is no more than the reach, so a reach of 1 is the four pixels beside a pixel, 1.5 adds the four corners, and anything under 1 is the pixel alone, which changes nothing. Shrinking, each pixel takes the least covering within reach, a pixel outside the drawing counting as empty, and keeps its own colour at that covering; an empty pixel stays empty and the layer does not grow. Spreading, the layer first grows by the reach, rounded down, on every side; each pixel takes the greatest covering within reach, in its own colour where it had covering, and where it had none in the covering-weighted average colour of the pixels within reach. Choke 0 changes nothing. **The method** is this program's own, modelled on After Effects' Simple Choker in spirit; nothing is ported. **Where it runs.** On a drawing's own pixels before its transform (ADR-017), in the drawing's own space even after an effect above it has grown the layer. A negative choke grows the layer by the reach, rounded down, so the spread edge is kept when the drawing is moved (FX-CHOKE-013); a positive one grows nothing. The choke is a distance, so a draft preview scales it (D-66). **Known limits:** the reach is counted on whole steps, so a large choke's corners are rounded in whole-pixel stairs rather than smoothly; a shrink or spread is hard-edged, with none of After Effects' Matte Choker softness; a shrink treats the drawing's own edge as empty, so a drawing that fills its layer loses its outer pixels, as FX-CHOKE-002's blue block does; and the work grows with the square of the choke, so a large choke on a large drawing is slow. **Out of range.** A command with a choke outside -100 to 100 is refused with a sentence; a file that holds one, written or at a key, keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, as D-46 does (FX-CHOKE-014 to 017).

D-160 / Speed Lines / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-26** by the owner's message of 2026-09-26, "afterwards, work on 30 more recommended effects for either AE or/and anime/animation related.", the twenty-seventh of the third batch of thirty effects the agent chose and recommended (D-134 to D-163). One picture in `verification/B-103a proposal/`. FX-SPEED-001 to 029 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-103. **It adds one effect and changes no existing fixture.** **What it does.** It draws manga focus lines: thin wedges rushing in from the edges toward a point, leaving the middle clear, the lines redrawn every few frames as hand-drawn focus lines are redrawn on twos. It is a generator, best laid on a solid covering the frame, but it works on any drawing, drawing only inside the pixels that show and keeping each one's covering. It is `core.speed_lines`, named Speed Lines in the Effects panel. **The name** is the animator's term; the effect is modelled on the focus lines (shuchusen) of manga and anime, not on any one After Effects effect, and is flagged, with the rest of the third batch, for document 10's pre-launch naming review. **Settings:** `center`, two numbers, per cent of the drawing's width and height, each -1000 to 1000, starting at 50, 50, the point the lines rush toward; `color`, `#rrggbb` as D-87's, starting at `#000000`; `count`, 4 to 1000, starting at 120, how many lines, a whole number (a fraction is dropped); `thickness`, 0 to 30 degrees, starting at 1.5, how wide a line is at its widest; `inner`, 0 to 100000 pixels, starting at 150, how far from the centre the lines stop; `inner_jitter`, 0 to 100, starting at 40, how much each line's stopping point varies, per cent of `inner`; `angle_jitter`, 0 to 100, starting at 50, how far each line is nudged off its even place, per cent of half a spacing; `seed`, 0 to 100000, starting at 0, a whole number, which set of lines; `hold`, 1 to 100 frames, starting at 2, a whole number, how many frames a set of lines lasts; and `opacity`, 0 to 100, starting at 100. The numbers can be keyed (D-68) and are held inside their ranges at each frame; the colour cannot. **The rule.** The lines are spread evenly round the centre, the first straight up, and each is nudged off its place, made thinner or wider by up to half, and made to stop nearer or further, by Noise's hash (D-119) of the seed, the line's number and the frame divided by `hold`, so the same file always draws the same lines and they change every `hold` frames. Each line is a wedge: at a pixel, how far the pixel's direction from the centre lies inside the line's half-width, turned into pixels at that distance, gives the line's strength there, with its edges softened by half a pixel across, and the line fades in over one pixel at its stopping point. A pixel takes its strongest line and is moved toward the colour by that strength times the opacity: Gradient's blend mix, normal (D-114). There is no cliff; the fixtures are all worked to 2e-5. **The method** is this program's own, modelled on manga focus lines; nothing is ported. **Where it runs.** On a drawing's own pixels before its transform (ADR-017), with the centre fixed to the drawing's own width and height, so the lines move with the drawing (FX-SPEED-020). It does not grow the layer. A draft preview scales `inner`, as it does other distances. On an adjustment layer it draws the lines over the picture below. **Known limits:** at its starting `inner` of 150 the lines start further out than a small drawing reaches, so on a small layer nothing shows until `inner` is lowered (FX-SPEED-001); the softened edge is half a pixel either side of the wedge's edge, so a line thinner than a pixel still shows at up to half strength, and `thickness` 0 draws faint hairlines rather than nothing (FX-SPEED-008); a wedge's width is an angle, so lines widen outward and, near the centre, the softened edges of every line meet and grey the few pixels about it when `inner` is 0 (FX-SPEED-009); the lines are straight wedges only, with no taper at their tips, no curve and no brush texture; and every line is worked at every pixel, so a build may skip lines that cannot reach a pixel but must draw the same. **Out of range.** A command with a centre outside -1000 to 1000, a count outside 4 to 1000, a thickness outside 0 to 30, an inner outside 0 to 100000, an inner jitter, angle jitter or opacity outside 0 to 100, a seed outside 0 to 100000, a hold outside 1 to 100, or a colour not written `#` and six hexadecimal digits is refused with a sentence; a file that holds one keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, as D-46 does (FX-SPEED-022 to 029).

D-161 / Cross Glare / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-26** by the owner's message of 2026-09-26, "afterwards, work on 30 more recommended effects for either AE or/and anime/animation related.", the twenty-eighth of the third batch of thirty effects the agent chose and recommended (D-134 to D-163). One picture in `verification/B-104a proposal/`. FX-GLARE-001 to 029 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-104. **It adds one effect and changes no existing fixture.** **What it does.** It turns the bright points of a drawing into star glints, the sparkle anime compositing puts on a blade's edge, an eye's highlight, a jewel or a star in the sky: each bright pixel is streaked outward in a cross or a star of evenly spread arms that fade as they go, and the streaks are added on top of the drawing, tinted by a colour. It is `core.cross_glare`, named Cross Glare in the Effects panel. **The name** is a compositing term, not an After Effects effect name; the effect is modelled on the cross filter of anime compositing and on star-glint effects such as Trapcode Starglow in spirit, not claimed to match any, and is flagged, with the rest of the third batch, for document 10's pre-launch naming review. **Settings:** `threshold`, 0 to 100, starting at 80, how bright a pixel must be to glint; `length`, 0 to 1000, starting at 40, how many pixels each arm reaches, taken down to a whole number; `points`, 1 to 8, starting at 4, how many arms, taken down to a whole number; `angle`, -3600 to 3600 degrees, starting at 45, the way the first arm points, 0 up and 90 to the right, clockwise on the screen; `intensity`, 0 to 10, starting at 1, how strongly the streaks are added; and `color`, `#rrggbb` as D-87's, starting at `#ffffff`, the streaks' tint. The five numbers can be keyed (D-68) and are held inside their ranges at each frame; the colour cannot. **The rule.** (1) The light: each pixel that shows and whose brightest channel, in 8-bit steps, is at least the threshold's share of 255, exactly Light Rays' light and Glow's and Bloom's bright test (D-124, D-89); every other pixel gives nothing. (2) The arms: `points` directions evenly spread round the circle, the first at `angle`, so 4 arms at 45 make an X and 4 arms at 0 a plus. Along each arm each bright pixel's light is laid down 1, 2, and so on up to `length` pixels out, fading with the square of the distance's share of the length plus one, the fading weights of all the steps together adding to one, so every arm carries the pixel's light once, spread along its length; a pixel never lights itself along an arm that lands on whole pixels, and an arm that runs between pixel centres, as a diagonal does, is spread smoothly onto the pixels either side of its line. (3) The streaks times the colour and the intensity are added to the drawing's colour, and their covering times the intensity to its covering, which stops at full; the colour is not cut off at white. Intensity 0 or a length under 1 changes nothing. **The method** is this program's own, built from Light Rays' light and document 21's bilinear sample; nothing is ported. **Where it runs.** On a drawing's own pixels before its transform (ADR-017). Unless it changes nothing, it grows the layer by the length, taken down to a whole number, on every side, so the arms are kept past the drawing's edge, as FX-GLARE-021 shows. The length is a distance, so a draft preview scales it. **Known limits:** the arms are straight, even and sharp-ended, with none of a real lens's diffraction colours, rotation over time or per-arm lengths; every bright pixel glints, so a large bright area gives a smeared cross the size of the area rather than one star, and the threshold is the way to keep glints to the brightest points; the arms add covering as well as colour, so a black colour lays a dark cross rather than nothing, as FX-GLARE-017 shows; the bright test reads each pixel's own colour; a half-covering edge of a bright colour glints at its own covering; and the work grows with the length times the points, so a long eight-armed glare on a large drawing is slow. **Out of range.** A command with a number outside its range or a colour that is not `#rrggbb` is refused with a sentence; a file that holds one keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, as D-46 does (FX-GLARE-022 to 029).
