D-162 / Camera Shake / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-26** by the owner's message of 2026-09-26, "afterwards, work on 30 more recommended effects for either AE or/and anime/animation related.", the twenty-ninth of the third batch of thirty effects the agent chose and recommended (D-134 to D-163). One picture in `verification/B-105a proposal/`. FX-SHAKE-001 to 021 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-105. **It adds one effect and changes no existing fixture.** **What it does.** It shakes a drawing as if the camera were bumped: each frame the whole drawing jolts to a new place and, if asked, tips a little about its centre, the staple of an anime hit, an explosion, a stomp or a hand-held shot. The jolts are picked by a seeded hash from the frame, so the same settings give the same shake every time, and a hold keeps each jolt for more than one frame, a shake on twos or threes as anime animates. It is `core.camera_shake`, named Camera Shake in the Effects panel. **The name** is the common word for the look, not an After Effects effect's name (After Effects builds it from its Wiggle expression or its Wiggler); it is flagged, with the rest of the third batch, for document 10's pre-launch naming review. **Settings:** `amount`, 0 to 1000, starting at 10, how many pixels a jolt moves the drawing at most, each way across and each way up and down; `rotation`, 0 to 45 degrees, starting at 0, how far a jolt may tip it at most, either way; `hold`, 1 to 100, starting at 1, how many frames each jolt is kept, taken down to a whole number; and `seed`, 0 to 100000, starting at 0, which shake, taken down to a whole number. Every number can be keyed (D-68) and is held inside its range at each frame. **The rule.** The frame is divided by the hold and taken down to a whole number, which numbers the jolt. From that number and the seed, Noise's hash gives three numbers between -1 and 1: the first two times the amount are the move across and down, and the third times the rotation is the tip in degrees, clockwise on the screen when above 0. The drawing is moved by the move and turned by the tip about its own centre: each pixel takes the smooth sample between the four nearest pixels at the point that lands on it. The layer first grows on every side by the amount times the square root of 2 plus the most a corner can swing, rounded up, so nothing moved or turned is cut off. Amount 0 and rotation 0 change nothing and grow nothing. **The method** is this program's own, modelled on the shakes After Effects users build with Wiggle in spirit; nothing is ported. The shake is worked in the drawing's own space, so a layer that moves carries its shake with it. **Where it runs.** On a drawing's own pixels before its transform (ADR-017), turning about the drawing's centre in the drawing's own space even after an effect above it has grown the layer. It grows the layer by the amount and the swing as above. The frame it uses is the composition frame, a hidden value filled in as Noise's is, never saved, and the effect cache keys on it. The amount is a distance, so a draft preview scales it. **Known limits:** each jolt jumps straight to its new place with no easing and no motion blur between jolts, so a smooth, drifting hand-held sway is out of reach; the jolts are independent of each other, with no setting for how often they come other than the hold; it shakes the layer it is on, not the whole composition; the turn is about the drawing's centre only; and on a small drawing the start settings' amount is large, so a jolt can carry the whole drawing out of the frame (FX-SHAKE-001's frame 1), which is the right look on a full frame. **Out of range.** A command with a number outside its range is refused with a sentence; a file that holds one keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, as D-46 does (FX-SHAKE-015 to 021).

D-163 / Rain / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-26** by the owner's message of 2026-09-26, "afterwards, work on 30 more recommended effects for either AE or/and anime/animation related.", the last of the third batch of thirty effects the agent chose and recommended (D-134 to D-163). One picture in `verification/B-106a proposal/`. FX-RAIN-001 to 027 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-106. **It adds one effect and changes no existing fixture.** **What it does.** It draws falling rain: thin pale streaks, scattered at random, sliding down across the picture from frame to frame, the rainy night of an anime scene or a wet street. It is a generator, drawn inside the layer's covering: laid on a solid that covers the frame it rains over the whole frame, and on a drawing it rains only where the drawing shows. It is `core.rain`, named Rain in the Effects panel. **The name** is a plain word, not an After Effects effect name; the effect is modelled in spirit on After Effects' CC Rainfall and the rain of anime compositing, not claimed to match either, and is flagged, with the rest of the third batch, for document 10's pre-launch naming review. **Settings:** `color`, a colour `#rrggbb`, starting at `#c8d8ff`, a pale blue; `density`, 0 to 100, starting at 30, the per cent of the field's cells that hold a drop; `spacing`, 2 to 1000, starting at 24, how many pixels wide each cell is, so how far apart the drops fall; `length`, 0 to 1000, starting at 20, how many pixels long each streak is; `width`, 0 to 20, starting at 1, how many pixels thick; `direction`, -3600 to 3600 degrees, starting at 170, the way the rain falls, 180 straight down, 0 up and 90 to the right, clockwise on the screen, so 170 drifts a little right as it falls; `speed`, 0 to 1000, starting at 30, how many pixels the rain falls each frame; `seed`, 0 to 100000, starting at 0, counted as a whole number, which picks the drops; and `opacity`, 0 to 100, starting at 60. Every number can be keyed (D-68) and is held inside its range at each frame; the colour cannot. **The rule.** The drawing's own space is laid with a field of square cells `spacing` pixels wide, turned so that its columns run along the fall. Each cell holds a drop or not, by the seed and the density, through Noise's hash (D-119); a drop sits at its own place in its cell, is a straight streak `length` pixels long lying along the fall, and has its own strength between a half and the whole. The field slides `speed` pixels a frame along the fall. At each pixel that shows, the strongest drop reaching it sets how much of the rain's colour is mixed in: its strength where the pixel lies within the streak's half width, fading to nothing over the half pixel beyond, times the opacity. The mix is Gradient's normal (D-114), in straight linear colour at the pixel's own covering, so every pixel keeps its covering and a pixel that does not show stays as it is. Density 0 or opacity 0 changes nothing. **The method** is this program's own, modelled on After Effects' CC Rainfall in spirit; nothing is ported. The field is fixed to the drawing, so a layer that moves carries its rain with it. **Where it runs.** On a drawing's own pixels before its transform (ADR-017), in the drawing's own space even after an effect above it has grown the layer; it does not grow the layer. The frame it uses is the composition frame, a hidden value filled in as Noise's is, never saved, and the effect cache keys on it. The spacing, length, width and speed are distances, so a draft preview scales them. **Known limits:** straight streaks of one length and one width, all at one depth, with no splashes, no drops hitting the drawing, no wind gusts and no blur of their own beyond their length; drops that overlap show the stronger one, not the two added; it rains only inside the covering, so on an empty part of a drawing nothing shows, and a whole-frame rain needs a solid under it; and a frame smaller than one cell of the field sees few drops and can go several frames with none, as the start settings do on the fixtures' 16 by 10 frame (FX-RAIN-001), which is the right look on a full frame. **Out of range.** A command with a number outside its range, or a colour not written `#rrggbb`, is refused with a sentence; a file that holds one keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, as D-46 does (FX-RAIN-020 to 027).

D-165 / The third batch of thirty on the card, each held to 1 level of 255 / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-27 by the owner ("2 - accept them all"), with every other decision then proposed (D-167).** It was **PROPOSED on 2026-09-27 by the agent**, the card half of the owner's request of 2026-09-27, "now let's do a full performance audit like we did with these new effects, like gpu-acceleration, etc.", as D-133 was for the second ten. D-100 has each effect declare and measure its own tolerance when it moves to the card, and show it in pictures before it is accepted. **The proposal:** Invert, Brightness & Contrast, Black & White, Posterize, Threshold, Channel Mixer, Vibrance, Leave Color, Solarize, Halftone, Mosaic, Emboss, Find Edges, Sharpen, Diffusion, Wave Warp, Ripple, Twirl, Bulge, Mirror, Linear Wipe, Radial Wipe, Venetian Blinds, Iris Wipe, Simple Choker, Speed Lines, Cross Glare, Camera Shake and Rain each keep compositing's tolerance when they are the last effect of a drawn layer: no channel of any pixel more than 1 level of 255 from the CPU's picture. **Motion Tile stays on the CPU:** it can grow a drawing by different amounts across and down, where the card's path grows a drawing alike on every side, and it is a copy that costs nothing to speak of (P-22: 0.0 ms). **How the card does it:** the same rule as the CPU, pixel for pixel, in double precision where the CPU works in double, with the drawing sent in full precision as for D-122. The seeded effects, Speed Lines, Camera Shake and Rain, use the CPU's own 64-bit hash worked in pairs of 32-bit words as Noise's is, so the lines, jolts and streaks are the same. The card has no double-precision sine: a sine or cosine of a pixel's own angle (Wave Warp, Ripple, Twirl) is worked in double precision by taking whole quarter turns off and summing the series for what is left, the angle round a centre (Radial Wipe, Speed Lines) is a single-precision first guess made exact to double by two Newton steps, with the straight and diagonal directions exact, and Wave Warp's triangle is folded from the angle rather than taken through an arcsine. A setting's own sine, such as Halftone's screen angle, is worked once on the processor. Camera Shake's growth depends on the size of the drawing that reaches it, so the plan works it out as the CPU does. Sharpen, Diffusion and Cross Glare use the card's blur and arm passes with the CPU's weights. **Hard edges.** Threshold, Posterize, Solarize, Halftone, Mirror, Leave Color and the four wipes without feather put a pixel wholly one way or the other. The CPU's rules add a margin where the fixtures sit on an edge, and the card works the same sums in the same precision; the measurement says whether any pixel flips, and if one does, that effect at those settings stays on the CPU, as D-122 keeps a threshold Levels there, and the table says so. B-107 measured none flipping, once the card was kept from fusing a multiply into the add after it, which rounds once where the CPU rounds twice (`verification/B-107_gpu_fx.md`). It needs `SHADER_F64`, as B-65 does; a card without it has such frames drawn by the CPU with an Info message. An effect that changes nothing is not sent. **The measurement** is B-107's, over every fixture frame of the thirty and the reference shot with each, at Full and Draft. **What it does not change:** exports and fixtures stay on the CPU, byte-exact, and a frame the card cannot draw is drawn by the CPU exactly as before. **If refused:** the thirty go back to the CPU, and nothing else moves.

D-166 / Presets and favourites kept in the window, and pasted effects read by the file's rules / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-27 by the owner ("2 - accept them all"), with every other decision then proposed (D-167).** It was **PROPOSED on 2026-09-27 by the agent**, for W-30, the owner's request of 2026-09-27: "1 through 6 sounds great! maybe for 6, it can work like fx console from video copilot". **Where they are kept.** Favourite effects and effect presets are kept in the window's own storage, as the Recently used list and saved workspaces are, and never in the project. A project opened on another machine does not bring its maker's presets with it, and a preset is not shared between machines yet; a preset file to export and import is the recommended next step if the owner wants that. **What a preset is.** A named list of effects with their settings and keys, each written exactly as a layer's `effects` list is written in the project file (document 19). Applying a preset and pasting copied effects are the same new command, `effect.paste`: one undo step per layer, the effects added at the end of that layer's stack with new instance ids, their keys at the same frames they had. **No silent loss (document 28).** The effects are read by the same rules the project file is read by, one function for both. An effect this build does not have, or a setting it does not understand and could not keep, refuses the whole paste with a message naming it; nothing is dropped and nothing is half added. The page also refuses to save a preset holding an effect it cannot name. **Ctrl+Space** opens the search in the middle of the window, as FX Console does in After Effects. Some East Asian keyboard setups use Ctrl+Space to switch the input language; there the owner may prefer another key.

D-167 / G3 is passed; the next stage, G4, is the smaller gaps and then the redesign; release work waits / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-27 by the owner**, in answer to the agent's five questions before the redesign: "1 - yes; 2 - accept them all; 3 - unsure still, defer for now; 4 - so far we have hit the foundational level/feel unless we are missing anything; 5 - very true; fix stale docs; include the keyboard shortcuts editor; release work, for now, just only interested in using it for myself only; smaller gaps should be tackled." **G3 is passed** by the owner's word that the foundation is reached, as G0 was passed by the owner's decision; document 11 gave G3 no exit criterion, and this entry is it. **Every decision then proposed is accepted:** D-99, D-101 to D-104, D-106 to D-110, D-121, D-122, D-133, D-164, D-165 and D-166. **Every built item then awaiting a playtest is accepted without a separate run**, among them B-24l, P-19, B-44, B-47, B-49 to B-51, W-27, B-54 to B-106 and W-30, and D-99's pictures. A defect found later in any of them is a new item, not a reopening. **The name, D-11, stays deferred.** **Release work waits: the tool is for the owner's own use.** An installer, signing, the licence texts beside the build (Q-04's second half), a clean-machine test, a release manifest and the release-candidate re-run of the viewer fixtures (document 13) are set aside, and Q-01, which is about a release candidate, stays open with them. This reopens if the owner wants to share the tool; nothing is to be distributed meanwhile. **G4 is, in order:** (1) the smaller gaps the roadmap audit of 2026-09-27 found, B-108 to B-114 in document 15: shape layers' gradients, trim paths, animated fill colour, stroke colour and stroke width, and line joins and caps (the rest of what document 04 kept out at D-78); a camera that is a layer (document 24, D-58); reference audio in formats other than WAV (R-15); the web view's own network traffic (D-39); and the viewer memory envelope measured with the cache the viewer really builds (D-49, T-06). Each is written fixtures first and proposed before it is built, as before. (2) **The redesign**, W-31 onward, under the rules the owner confirmed ("5 - very true"): every control still sends document 24's commands, or document 24 changes first; everything stays reachable by keyboard and works at 100 to 200 per cent scaling; the empty project, missing media, an export running and failed, unsaved changes and recovery are each designed on purpose (document 05); one screen at a time, starting with the timeline; and it includes the exposure list overhaul D-64 deferred to it ("1 - yes") and a keyboard shortcut editor with an in-app list of shortcuts, which document 05 promised after the baseline. **G4 passes** when the owner accepts the last redesigned screen's playtest and has used the redesigned tool on a real shot (A-02).

D-168 / Gradient fills and strokes on shape layers / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28 by the owner ("accept them all; begin the redesign"), with every other decision then proposed (D-175).** It was **PROPOSED on 2026-09-27 by the agent** as B-108a, the first of G4's gaps (D-167). **The proposal.** A shape's `fill` or `stroke` may carry an optional `gradient`: `{"type": "linear" or "radial", "start", "end", "stops"}`. `start` and `end` are points in the layer's space, which for a shape layer is its composition's, each written as any property is (document 19), so each may be keyed with hold, linear or eased keys. `stops` holds 2 to 64 stops, each `{"offset", "color", "opacity"}`: an offset from 0 to 1, a colour of three numbers from 0 to 1 in the working space, an opacity from 0 to 1. The fill's or stroke's own `color` stays in the file and is what it goes back to if the gradient is taken off; its `opacity` still multiplies the result. **The rule.** At each pixel's centre, t is the distance along the line from start to end as a share of its length (linear), or the distance from the start as a share of the start-to-end length (radial); it is held within 0 and 1, so the end colours carry on past the ends, and it is 1 where the two points are the same. The stops are taken in the order of their offsets, two at one offset keeping the order they were written in, which makes a hard step. Between two stops the colours are mixed as sRGB-encoded values, as the Gradient effect (D-114) and After Effects mix them, and the opacities as they are. The coverage is D-78's, unchanged. A stroke's gradient lies across the frame by position, as After Effects draws it, not along the line. **Refused whole** as `PROJECT_SCHEMA_INVALID`: fewer than 2 or more than 64 stops, an offset, colour or opacity out of range, a type other than linear or radial, a point that is not two numbers, an expression on a point, or motion-path handles on a point's key. No new identifier in document 28. **Not covered:** the colour is worked once per pixel, so a hard step inside a gradient has a stepped edge rather than a smoothed one; a radial gradient has no highlight length or angle; the ends carry on rather than repeat or reflect; a stop's colour and opacity move together, where After Effects keeps separate opacity stops; and a point moves in a straight line between keys. Each is a later item if wanted. **The evidence.** FX-SHP-040 to 051 and the refusals FX-SHP-060 to 069 in document 25, worked by `tools/shape_gradient_reference.py` into `Fixtures/shape_gradients/`, and drawn in `verification/B-108a proposal/`. **If refused,** nothing is built and shapes stay flat colours.

D-169 / Trim paths on shape layers / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28 by the owner ("accept them all; begin the redesign"), with every other decision then proposed (D-175).** It was **PROPOSED on 2026-09-27 by the agent** as B-109a, the second of G4's gaps (D-167). **The proposal.** A shape may carry an optional `trim` of three numbers, each written as any property is (document 19), so each may be keyed with hold, linear or eased keys: `start` and `end`, 0 to 100, the percent of the way along the path, and `offset`, in degrees, 360 of them once along, any number. The stroke is drawn along only that stretch of the path, which is After Effects' Trim Paths and the usual way a line is drawn on. The fill is not trimmed. **The rule.** The path's length is measured on D-77's flattened outline, a closed path's closing side counted last. Start and end are taken low then high, so 75 to 25 is 25 to 75. If they are 100 apart the whole stroke is drawn; if they are equal none of it is. Otherwise the stretch begins at the start moved on by the offset, wrapped once round, and is as long as end less start; a stretch that runs past the path's end carries on from its beginning, on an open path as on a closed one, as After Effects does. The stretch is stroked by D-78's coverage, unchanged, so its cut ends are round like every other end. **Refused whole** as `PROJECT_SCHEMA_INVALID`: a start or end, or any of their keys, below 0 or above 100; any of the three not one number; an expression on any of them; a trim missing any of them. No new identifier in document 28. **Not covered:** After Effects' choice of trimming several shapes one after another rather than each alone; the fill trimmed with the stroke; cut ends that are square rather than round, which waits on B-110's line caps; the length measured on the true curve rather than the flattened outline, which differs by a fraction of a pixel on a curve. Each is a later item if wanted. **The evidence.** FX-SHP-070 to 083 and the refusals FX-SHP-090 to 095 in document 25, worked by `tools/shape_trim_reference.py` into `Fixtures/shape_trims/`, and drawn in `verification/B-109a proposal/`. **If refused,** nothing is built and a stroke is always the whole path.

D-170 / Shape styles over time, and line joins and caps / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28 by the owner ("accept them all; begin the redesign"), with every other decision then proposed (D-175).** It was **PROPOSED on 2026-09-27 by the agent** as B-110a, the third of G4's gaps (D-167). **The proposal, keyed styles.** A fill's `color` and `opacity`, and a stroke's `color`, `opacity` and `width_px`, may each be written either as the plain value, as now, or as a property's record, `{"base", "keyframes"}`, as a keyed effect setting is written (D-68), so each can be keyed with hold, linear or eased keys. A colour's keys hold three numbers that move together, as an effect's colour's do. Each is resolved to the frame by document 20 and then drawn exactly as D-78 draws a plain value. D-78's ranges hold at the base and at every key. **The proposal, joins and caps.** A stroke may carry `join`, one of `miter`, `round` or `bevel`; `miter_limit`, 1 to 100, After Effects' default of 4 when not written; and `cap`, one of `butt`, `round` or `square`. Not written, they are round and round, which is D-78's stroke unchanged, so every file already made draws as it did. A mitre whose point would be more than the limit in half-widths from the corner is bevelled instead, as in After Effects; a mitre on a line that turns straight back is never drawn. The joins are made at every point of D-77's flattened outline, and on a closed path at its first point too. A line with no length is drawn as its cap: a disc, a square lined up with the frame, or nothing for butt. A trimmed stroke (D-169) takes the caps at its cut ends, which answers D-169's round-only cut ends; where a closed path's stretch runs through its first point it is one joined line rather than two cut ones, which is the same pixels as D-169's rule when joins and caps are round, so D-169's fixtures stand. **Refused whole** as `PROJECT_SCHEMA_INVALID`: a join or cap that is not one of its three words; a mitre limit below 1 or above 100; any key outside D-78's ranges (a colour 0 to 1, an opacity 0 to 1, a width above 0 and at most 8192); a colour key of other than three numbers; an expression on any of them. No new identifier in document 28. **A choice for the owner:** the window keeps D-78's round joins and caps for a new stroke; After Effects starts a new stroke mitred with butt caps. Either is one line to change. **Not covered:** dashes; a mitre or bevel at the points a curve is flattened into, which differs from the true curve by far less than a pixel; tapering along the line. Each is a later item if wanted. **The evidence.** FX-SHP-100 to 117 and the refusals FX-SHP-120 to 127 in document 25, worked by `tools/shape_style_reference.py` into `Fixtures/shape_styles/`, drawn in `verification/B-110a proposal/`, whose `joins_and_caps_enlarged.png` shows the three joins across and the three caps down, large enough to judge by eye. **If refused,** nothing is built, a shape's colours and width stay fixed and every join and cap stays round.

D-171 / A camera that rides a layer / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28 by the owner ("accept them all; begin the redesign"), with every other decision then proposed (D-175).** It was **PROPOSED on 2026-09-27 by the agent** as B-111a, the fourth of G4's gaps (D-167). **The proposal.** A composition's `camera` (D-58) may name a `parent`, a layer of the same composition, as a layer names one (D-57). The camera's `position` is then a point in the parent's space: it is carried to the composition through the parent's whole chain, anchor, scale, rotation and position of every layer up it, at the frame being drawn, exactly as D-57 carries a point of a child. The camera's depth is its own depth plus the parent's world depth. Its zoom stays its own, and the view is never turned or scaled by the parent, because D-58's camera does not turn (D-56): a parent's rotation and scale move where the camera stands and nothing else. This is the After Effects rig of a camera parented to a null, which is what B-111 asked a camera layer for: dolly, truck and crane by keying the null, and a camera that follows a moving layer. With no `parent` every file draws as it did. A parent that is not in the composition is `PARENT_REFERENCE_MISSING`, the warning a layer already gives: the reference is kept and the camera stands as if it had none. In the window the camera's inspector gets the parent chooser a layer has, which by default keeps the camera where it is on the current frame, as parenting a layer does (D-57); deleting the parent unparents the camera the same way. **Refused whole** as `PROJECT_SCHEMA_INVALID`: a parent that is not a layer's identifier; a parent that is an audio layer, which has no place (D-71). A camera cannot be in a parent loop, because nothing can name the camera as its parent. No new identifier in document 28. **A choice for the owner:** this makes the existing camera ride a layer; it does not make the camera a layer. After Effects' camera is a layer, so a composition can hold several and cut between them by their in and out points, and the timeline shows it as a bar. That is a larger change to the file and the timeline, and the parent rig covers the common use; say if the full camera layer is wanted and it becomes a later item. **Not covered:** several cameras in one composition; a camera with in and out points; a camera that turns, tilts or looks at a point of interest, which needs D-58's projection to become a perspective one; depth of field. Each is a later item if wanted. **The evidence.** FX-RIG-001 to 031 in document 25, worked by `tools/camera_rig_reference.py` into `Fixtures/camera_rig/`, drawn in `verification/B-111a proposal/rig_cases.png`. **If refused,** nothing is built and the camera is keyed only by its own position, depth and zoom.

D-172 / Sound in other formats: measured, and no decoder in the core / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28 by the owner ("accept them all; begin the redesign"), with every other decision then proposed (D-175).** It was **PROPOSED on 2026-09-27 by the agent** as B-112, the fifth of G4's gaps (D-167). **What B-112 asked.** That MP3, FLAC, Ogg Vorbis and AAC be read by the core as the same samples a WAV gives. **What was found first.** D-71 already keeps these files as audio assets, and the window's own decoder plays them. The window already says when it cannot play one: its layer is silent and the status line gives the reason. The core measures a WAV's header and decodes no samples of any format, a WAV included. Nothing in the core would use decoded samples, because no export carries sound. The one real doubt was D-71's warning that MP3 and AAC "can start up to about a frame late". For lip sync that would matter, so it was measured before anything was built. **The measurement.** `tools/audio_sync_probe.py` writes a WAV with a click on the first sample of frames 2 and 12. It encodes it with ffmpeg 8.1 to FLAC, MP3, Ogg Vorbis, AAC in M4A and Opus, and decodes each with ffmpeg and with Chrome 153's own decoder, which is the Chromium decoder the window's web view uses. In every format, in both decoders, both clicks land on exactly the WAV's samples. The only differences are at the files' ends, at most 128 samples in the silence after the last sound. The exception is an MP3 written without its gapless header: it starts 1105 samples late, a little over half a frame at 24, in both decoders alike. The delay is in the file, and no decoder can know to remove it. `verification/B-112_audio_sync.md` holds the tables and a check to make in the window. **The proposal.** B-112 closes on this evidence without code. The core gains no decoder, and so no new third-party licences and no AAC patent question. D-71's "can start up to about a frame late" is corrected to what was measured: sample-exact, except an MP3 without its gapless header, which starts about half a frame late everywhere. **What would reopen it.** Sound in an export, which D-71 keeps out. That is when the core would need samples, and then a decoder (the pure-Rust `symphonia`, MPL-2.0 as five crates under Tauri already are, for FLAC, MP3 and Vorbis), fixtures against ffmpeg's decode, and the AAC question would come with it. **For the owner:** accept closing B-112 so, or ask for the core decoder anyway.

D-173 / The web view's own traffic: narrowed to one Microsoft connection that no switch reaches / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28 by the owner ("accept them all; begin the redesign"), with every other decision then proposed (D-175).** It was **PROPOSED on 2026-09-27 by the agent** as B-113, the sixth of G4's gaps (D-167). **What B-113 asked.** Switch off what Microsoft's web view fetches on its own account, and watch the window again, so that R-11's "sends nothing anywhere" holds for the whole window. **What was done.** Two more Chromium switches are set before the window is created, making eight. `--host-resolver-rules="MAP * ~NOTFOUND , EXCLUDE *.localhost"` makes every name except `*.localhost` unresolvable; the page only ever asks for `frame.localhost` and `project.localhost`, which the web view answers inside the process. `--proxy-server=127.0.0.1:9` sends every other web request to a closed port on this machine. **What was measured.** `tools/offline_check.ps1`, release build, idle on a project for thirty seconds, three runs: off-machine connections fell from B-11's four to two in every run. The DNS-over-HTTPS pair is gone. The pair left goes to Microsoft's `2603:1036::` addresses on port 443, with the low bits changing between runs as B-11 saw. The program's own process still holds nothing. That pair connected directly while every request through Chromium's network code was going to the dead proxy, so it is made outside that code and no Chromium switch can reach it. A photograph of the window with the switches on shows the page drawing and talking to the program as before. Evidence: `verification/B-113_offline_run.md` and `verification/B-113_window_with_switches.png`; `docs/SUPPORTED_ENVELOPE.md`'s network section is restated to match. **The proposal.** B-113 closes as narrowed, not solved. D-39's three answers stay the owner's, now about one connection instead of two: accept it and say so, as the envelope does; block `msedgewebview2.exe` at the firewall, which also blocks every other program on the machine using WebView2, because they run the same file; or leave the operating system's web view, which is a different program. **Recommendation: accept it as stated in the envelope for this version**, and keep the firewall line there for anyone for whom it matters. **For the owner:** accept this, and answer D-39.

D-174 / The envelope measured the way the viewer runs, which settles D-49 and changes D-47's finding / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28 by the owner ("accept them all; begin the redesign"), with every other decision then proposed (D-175).** It was **PROPOSED on 2026-09-27 by the agent** as B-114, the last of G4's gaps (D-167). **What B-114 asked.** D-49: the T-06 pages measure `CelCache::with_budget(DEFAULT_BUDGET_BYTES)`, 1 GiB of drawings with no room for effect results, composited on the processor. Since then P-11 split the cache, D-105 sized it to a quarter of the machine's memory, and B-44 moved compositing to the card, so the published envelope described a configuration the window no longer has. **What was done.** `tests/b114_viewer_envelope.rs` is the harness for the window's own viewer. It builds the cache as the window does, `CelCache::viewer_sized`, at the Automatic size on this machine and at 1 GiB, the least Automatic gives. It draws each frame on the card through `preview::preview_frame_srgb8` when there is one, as the window does with **Draw on: Auto**, and on the processor otherwise. It measures both shots: the four-layer reference shot and document 08's ten-layer fixture. The T-06 pages are left as the record of the old configuration. **Measured** on the Ryzen 9 9900X with 64 GB and an RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, release, draft, two runs (`verification/B-114_viewer_envelope.md` holds the second). At Automatic (15.4 GiB), both shots' drawings fit: the reference shot plays at 0.5 ms a frame and seeks at 1.3 ms p95, and the ten-layer shot at about 5 ms and 7.2 to 7.4 ms, with no frame over 41.7 ms. At 1 GiB, the reference shot still plays at 14 ms, but the ten-layer shot takes 36 ms a frame and 48 to 63 of 240 frames miss the deadline each time round. Both assertions held in both runs: neither half of the cache went over its budget, and the working set grew by less than one cel from the second loop to the tenth. **What it changes.** D-49 is settled: the envelope now rests on the configuration the window runs. D-47's finding, 264.17 ms a frame and "no cache can pay it", no longer holds for a machine whose memory setting holds a shot's drawings; the envelope's paragraph is restated to say speed depends on whether a shot's drawings fit, with the two rows and what the default holds on 16 and 32 GB machines. D-47's decision, to keep the 24 fps target, stands and is now met on this machine. **Not covered.** The window's read-ahead, which decodes coming frames on other threads during playback, is not in the harness, so playback figures are a ceiling. Every figure stops at a finished picture, not the screen. Card memory is not measured. The rest of `docs/SUPPORTED_ENVELOPE.md`'s feature lists predate most of G2 and G3 and are out of date; restating them is release work (D-167 defers release). **For the owner:** accept this, which closes D-49 and amends D-47's finding.


D-176 / The redesign's order, and the timeline drawn first / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28 by the owner ("ok, let's accept")**, proposed by the agent the same day (W-31a). **The screens are redesigned in this order**, each as pictures first, then the build, then a playtest: W-31 the timeline; W-32 the Sheet and the exposure list, D-64's overhaul; W-33 the viewer and its controls; W-34 effect controls; W-35 the Project and Effects panels; W-36 the strip along the top and the status strip, with document 05's states (an empty project, an export running and failed, unsaved changes, recovery); W-37 the keyboard shortcut list and its editor, which replaces the row of shortcuts along the bottom of the window. **The timeline is drawn in `design/W-31_timeline.html`** and photographed in `verification/W-31 pictures/`, against the window as it is in `verification/W-31_before_timeline.png`. `verification/W-31a_timeline_proposal.md` lists its twelve changes: one header row; one New layer menu in place of five buttons; Delete, Forward and Back leaving the header for the layer menu, their shortcuts and the command finder; headings over the columns; one set of switch icons; a timing tag (on 1s, on 2s, irregular, held) read off the exposures; alternating drawing shades with numbers where they fit, a held drawing as one green bar and keys on the bar's lower edge; a missing drawing striped red with a Relink button on its row; seconds on the ruler and the frame on the playhead; mode and parent as quiet text, a mode other than Normal in orange; an empty composition that says so and offers Import drawings and New layer; the layer columns at most 45 per cent of the panel. **No command, shortcut, menu or drag changes**, so document 24 is unchanged. Accepting this lets W-31b build it in `app/ui/index.html`, re-pin the page-text checks in `app/src/main.rs`, and photograph it at 100, 150 and 200 per cent with a keyboard-reach check.
D-175 / G4's gaps are closed; the redesign begins / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28 by the owner**: "accept them all; begin the redesign". **Every decision then proposed is accepted:** D-168 to D-174. **Every item then awaiting a playtest or check is accepted without a separate run:** the B-108 to B-111 playtest sheets, B-112's window check and B-113's run. A defect found later in any of them is a new item, not a reopening. **The owner's choices are settled as the entries proposed them.** A new stroke keeps D-78's round joins and caps rather than After Effects' mitred joins and butt caps (D-170). A camera rides a layer through D-171's camera parent; a full camera layer is not built. D-39 is answered by its first choice, as D-173 recommends: the one Microsoft connection the web view holds is accepted and stated in `docs/SUPPORTED_ENVELOPE.md`. D-49 is closed by D-174, and D-47's finding is amended by it. **All seven of G4's gaps, B-108 to B-114, are done.** **The redesign begins** as W-31 onward, under D-167's rules: one screen at a time, starting with the timeline; every control still sends document 24's commands, or document 24 changes first; keyboard reach and 100 to 200 per cent scaling kept; document 05's states designed on purpose; D-64's exposure-list overhaul and a keyboard shortcut editor with an in-app list of shortcuts included. G4 passes when the owner accepts the last redesigned screen's playtest and has used the tool on a real shot (A-02).

D-177 / The timeline's direction kept, and the owner's answers for W-32 and W-36 / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28 by the owner** ("so far so good though, accept the general direction of timeline, but let's further work on it"; "1 - yes"; "2 - yes"; "3 - middle of the window"). **W-31b's general direction is accepted, and the timeline keeps being refined**: a W-31c follows from the new design round. The owner's first note is that the top of the ruler is cramped; W-31c starts by giving its labels room. **The exposure list leaves Effect controls and becomes the Sheet panel's second view** (W-32, D-64's overhaul); each row shows the last frame its drawing is on. The Sheet and exposure list panel shows by default only in the Timing workspace, and the owner can switch it onto any workspace. **The top strip is compressed** (W-36): Recent, Collect Files, Check Package, Preferences and the Session log go into a File menu, the other buttons and lists fold into the groups the W-36 drawing recommends, and Open, Save and Export stay as buttons. **The recovery offer is a card in the middle of the window** (W-36), not a list in the top strip. **The next design round** covers the timeline, effect controls, the Effects panel, the Project panel and the composition and precomposition windows, drawn after After Effects, DaVinci Resolve and Clip Studio Paint, and shown on a design canvas the owner opens in the browser. No command, shortcut or menu changes by this decision, so document 24 is unchanged.

D-178 / Motion Tile on the graphics card, held to 1 level of 255 / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28** by the owner's messages of 2026-09-28, "1, 2,3,5,6,7,8,9" and then "include 4 as well, just 1 thru 9", accepting items 1 to 9 of the agent's list of the effects and presets left to build; the first of the nine. D-165 left Motion Tile on the CPU because it can grow a drawing by different amounts across and down, where the card's path grew a drawing alike on every side. **What changes.** The card's plan now carries an effect's growth across and down separately, so Motion Tile is done by the card when it is the last effect of a drawn layer, as the other twenty-nine of the third batch are. Every other effect grows alike on every side, as before. **How the card does it.** The same rule as `layer_fx::motion_tile`: each pixel of the grown layer is a copy of one pixel of the drawing, so there is no sum to round and the card's copy is the CPU's exactly. A tile that grows nothing is not sent. **A driver finding.** This card's driver takes the remainder of a negative whole number as if it had no sign, which put the tiles left of the drawing two columns out; the card now moves the count on by an even number of repeats first, which keeps it positive and keeps which repeats are turned over. **The measurement** is B-115's, every fixture frame of Motion Tile and the reference shot with it, at Full and Draft, within 1 level of 255. **What it does not change:** exports and fixtures stay on the CPU, byte-exact; a frame the card cannot draw is drawn by the CPU as before. **If refused:** Motion Tile goes back to the CPU, and nothing else moves.

D-179 / Five big projects on the roadmap, parked / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28 by the owner**: "take everything; list ... onto the roadmap". The owner took every effect of the agent's After Effects list into the build queue, and asked that five larger things be recorded rather than built: particles; Shatter, Card Dance, Caustics and Wave World; a professional key with spill suppression; stabilizing and retiming by motion; liquify and mesh warp. They are L-01 to L-05 in document 15, PARKED, and in document 04 as later, each its own project. Each is too big for a batch unit, for the reason its entry gives, and each waits for the owner to ask for it by name. Recording them changes no exclusion in document 04. Frame blending stays skipped.

D-180 / Effect presets in a file, to take them to another machine or keep them safe / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28** by the owner's messages of 2026-09-28, "1, 2,3,5,6,7,8,9" and then "include 4 as well, just 1 thru 9", accepting items 1 to 9 of the agent's list of the effects and presets left to build; the second of the nine, the step D-166 recommended. The proposal is in `verification/B-116a proposal/`; FX-PRE in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-116. **It changes no existing fixture and nothing in the project file.** **What it does.** The Effects panel gains two commands. *Export presets* writes the window's presets to a file the owner names, ending `.fxpreset`; a preset's own right-click menu exports that one alone. *Import presets* reads such a file and adds its presets to the Presets folder. **The file** is JSON: `preset_file_version` 0 and `presets`, a list of named effect stacks, each effect written exactly as a layer's `effects` are written in the project file, keys and all (document 19). **Read whole or refused whole (document 28).** The effects are read by the rules pasted effects are read by (`persist::read_effects`, D-166), so an effect this build does not have, or a setting it would not keep, refuses the file; so do a file that is not JSON, a project file chosen by mistake, a newer version, anything the rule does not name, an empty or repeated name and a preset with no effects. Nothing is half imported: the window's presets are left exactly as they were, and the message names what was wrong, as the new `PRESET_FILE_INVALID` or as `EFFECT_UNSUPPORTED`. A setting outside its range is read and kept, as a project file's is (D-46). **A name already taken** is not replaced: the imported preset is added as the same name with " 2" (or the next free number) after it, and the message says so, since an import cannot be undone. **Writing.** The build checks what it is about to write by reading it back first, and writes nothing it would refuse. **Where it runs:** the window; the file is chosen in the operating system's own dialog, opened from Rust, as a project is. **If refused:** presets stay in the window only.

D-181 / Starter presets the program comes with / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28** by the owner's messages of 2026-09-28, "1, 2,3,5,6,7,8,9" and then "include 4 as well, just 1 thru 9", accepting items 1 to 9 of the agent's list of the effects and presets left to build; the third of the nine. The proposal is in `verification/B-117a proposal/`, with a sheet of how each looks; FX-STARTER in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-117. **It changes no existing fixture and nothing in the project file.** **What it does.** Nine presets are listed first in the Effects panel's Presets folder on every window: Soft bloom, Night, Sunset, Cel shadow, Rim light, Old film, Impact, Dream haze and Speed lines, each marked *built in*, each with a sentence saying what it does and where it works best. They apply as the owner's presets apply (D-166). **They cannot be removed**; the panel says why when asked to. **They can be copied**: *Copy to my presets…* asks for a name and the copy is an ordinary preset. **Their names are kept for them**: saving under one is refused; an import gives the next free number (D-180); a preset the window kept from before whose name a starter preset now has is given the next free number once, and the status line says so. *Export presets* writes the owner's presets only; a starter preset can be exported alone. **Where they are written:** `Fixtures/starter_presets/starter.fxpreset`, a preset file of D-180's format written by `tools/starter_presets_reference.py`, which the build carries inside itself and reads as an import would. Changing one is a specification decision made there. **Where it runs:** the window; nothing is stored.

D-182 / Color Lookup, a .cube colour lookup file on any layer / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28** by the owner's messages of 2026-09-28, "1, 2,3,5,6,7,8,9" and then "include 4 as well, just 1 thru 9", accepting items 1 to 9 of the agent's list of the effects and presets left to build; the fourth of the nine. The proposal is in `verification/B-118a proposal/`, with a picture; FX-LUT-001 to 013 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-118. **It adds to the project file** the asset kind `lut` (document 19), which an older build refuses to open, as it refuses any asset kind it does not know; no existing fixture changes. **What it does.** Color Lookup (`core.color_lookup`) recolours a layer through a colour lookup file in the .cube format grading programs export: a 3D table mixed trilinearly, a 1D table channel by channel, its domain or input range honoured. Its one setting, `lut`, is the id of a lookup asset of the project, or empty. The card has one row: the file's name and *Choose .cube file…*; choosing a file reads it first and refuses it with the reason, then adds it to the project as a lookup asset (the same file again is the same asset) and sets the effect to it, two steps of undo. **The file stays where it is**, as a drawing does: Collect Files copies it and lists it in the manifest as used by the layers whose effects name it; a missing one is MEDIA_MISSING on opening and at every frame, the layer drawn without the look, and kept to be relinked, Relink taking one .cube file; one the reading rule refuses is MEDIA_DECODE_FAILED at every frame, with the reason; a `lut` naming no lookup asset is EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, and a command that sets one is refused. No layer shows a lookup asset. **Known limits:** the lookup is of the encoded sRGB colour, which suits a creative look and not a camera's log lookup; a file with both a 1D and a 3D table is refused; an asset cannot yet be removed from a project. **Where it runs:** the processor; the graphics card in item 9.

D-183 / Line Blur, softening lines along their own length / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28** by the owner's messages of 2026-09-28, "1, 2,3,5,6,7,8,9" and then "include 4 as well, just 1 thru 9", accepting items 1 to 9 of the agent's list of the effects and presets left to build; the fifth of the nine. **Inspired by OpenToonz's Line Blur, not a port**: OpenToonz traces the lines into curves first, which is far too big for this item, and this is a lighter rule of our own on the pixels, as the coordinator directed on 2026-09-28. Nothing is copied, so document 10 has nothing to record. The proposal is in `verification/B-119a proposal/`, with a picture worked by the reference rule; FX-LBLUR-001 to 016 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-119. **What it does.** Line Blur (`core.line_blur`) finds which way the line through each pixel runs from the smoothed structure tensor of the layer's covering and of its ink (covering less light), and blurs along that way only, with a one-dimensional Gaussian sampled bilinearly, each side stopping where the line ends. Jagged steps soften into slopes; a line keeps its thickness and its ends; a clean straight line stays as it is. **Settings:** `length`, 0 to 50 pixels, 4 when added, scaled for a draft; `strength`, 0 to 100 percent, 100 when added; `lines_only`, the word "off" or "on" as Motion Tile's mirror is, "off" when added, which scales each pixel's change by its own ink so fills and colour edges are left alone. Both numbers can be keyed. No existing line mask fits Lines only (Line Width's is a chosen colour), so it is the pixel's ink. Length 0 or strength 0 is the drawing exactly. It grows the layer by 3 pixels whatever the length. **Known limits:** it follows the straight tangent, not the curve, so a long length thins a tight curve a little; a white line on white paper has no ink to find. **Where it runs:** the processor; the graphics card in item 9.

D-184 / HSV Key, taking out a colour by hue, saturation and value / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28** by the owner's messages of 2026-09-28, "1, 2,3,5,6,7,8,9" and then "include 4 as well, just 1 thru 9", accepting items 1 to 9 of the agent's list of the effects and presets left to build; the sixth of the nine. The proposal is in `verification/B-120a proposal/`, with a picture worked by the reference rule; FX-HSV-001 to 016 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-120. **What it does.** HSV Key (`core.hsv_key`) makes fully transparent each pixel whose hue, saturation and value all fall inside chosen windows, or, with `invert` on, each pixel that shows and does not. **Settings,** in OpenToonz's order: `hue`, 0 to 360 degrees, 120 when added; `saturation`, 0 to 100 percent, 60; `value`, 0 to 100 percent, 60; `hue_range`, 0 to 180 degrees, 40; `saturation_range` and `value_range`, 0 to 100 percent, 40 each; `invert`, the word "off" or "on", "off" when added. The six numbers can be keyed; none is a distance, so a draft keeps them. It grows nothing. **Where it comes from.** It is OpenToonz's HSV Key, `toonz/sources/stdfx/hsvkeyfx.cpp` with the colour conversion `OLDRGB2HSV` from `toonz/sources/toonzlib/hsvutil.cpp`, commit 6571328019e3a6a99c13f408ee6f4755c9cddf73, under OpenToonz's BSD 3-Clause licence, copyright DWANGO Co., Ltd. and the respective contributors, 2016 to 2026, as D-86's line smoothing is: the licence text is already kept whole in `docs/third_party/OpenToonz-LICENSE.txt` and ships with the build, and the notice heads the reference tool `tools/hsv_key_reference.py` and the build's port. **Four changes from OpenToonz,** each pinned by a fixture: the colour is the pixel's straight colour, where OpenToonz reads premultiplied values, so a half-covered screen edge goes with the screen (001); the hue window wraps round the circle, where OpenToonz cuts it at 0 and 360, and so `hue_range` stops at 180 (005, 007); saturation and value are in percent, where OpenToonz's are 0 to 1; and it is added as a green key, where OpenToonz starts at 0 everywhere (001, and 008 is OpenToonz's start). **Known limits:** a hard key, as OpenToonz's is; a grey counts as hue 0. **Where it runs:** the processor; the graphics card in item 9.

D-185 / Paraffin, a soft wash of colour over a figure from one side / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28** by the owner's messages of 2026-09-28, "1, 2,3,5,6,7,8,9" and then "include 4 as well, just 1 thru 9", accepting items 1 to 9 of the agent's list of the effects and presets left to build; the seventh of the nine. The proposal is in `verification/B-121a proposal/`, with a picture worked by the reference rule; FX-PARA-001 to 023 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-121. **What it does.** Paraffin (`core.paraffin`) lays a colour over the figure, the pixels at least half covered, from one side, strongest at the figure's near edge and fading on a smoothstep curve to nothing a chosen share of the way across; each pixel keeps its covering. **Settings:** `color`, "#rrggbb", #6450a0 when added; `direction`, 0 to 360 degrees clockwise from up, the way the wash comes from, 180 (from below); `spread`, 0 to 100 percent of the figure's extent, 70; `opacity`, 0 to 100, 50; `blend`, "normal", "multiply", "screen", "add", "overlay" or "soft_light", "multiply" when added. Direction, spread and opacity can be keyed; none is a distance, so a draft keeps them. It grows nothing. **Where it comes from.** It is this program's own effect, after the paraffin of anime finishing; nothing is ported. The overlay and soft-light blends are the W3C compositing specification's formulas, worked on the sRGB-encoded values as the shared colour rule of D-111's batch does; the four other effects with a blend keep their four words. **How it differs** from Gradient (D-114), which runs between two points on the frame, and from Distance Gradation (D-123) and Rim Light (D-117), which shade by distance from the edge: it is fitted to the figure and runs one way across it. **Known limits:** the figure is the whole layer; the wash is straight across. **Where it runs:** the processor; the graphics card in item 9.

D-186 / Kira-kira, twinkling stars on a drawing's highlights / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28** by the owner's messages of 2026-09-28, "1, 2,3,5,6,7,8,9" and then "include 4 as well, just 1 thru 9", accepting items 1 to 9 of the agent's list of the effects and presets left to build; the eighth of the nine. The proposal is in `verification/B-122a proposal/`, with a picture worked by the reference rule; FX-KIRA-001 to 029 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-122. **What it does.** Kira-kira (`core.kira_kira`) finds the near-white pixels, cuts the drawing into square cells, sets a star at the middle of the highlights of a share of the cells chosen by a seed, and makes each star grow and fade on its own beat; the stars are added as light and paint the clear pixels, so the layer grows. **Settings:** `threshold`, 0 to 100, 95 when added; `spacing`, 2 to 1000 pixels, 64; `density`, 0 to 100, 60; `size`, 0 to 1000 pixels, 40; `shape`, "cross" or "star", "star"; `angle`, -3600 to 3600 degrees, 0; `twinkle`, 0 to 100, 100; `period`, 1 to 1000 frames, 24; `seed`, 0 to 100000, floored, 0; `opacity`, 0 to 100, 100; `color`, "#rrggbb", #ffffff. Every number can be keyed; spacing and size are distances a draft scales. **Where it comes from.** It is this program's own effect, after the kira-kira of anime finishing; nothing is ported. Its cells and seed are Rain's (D-163) and Noise's hash (D-119); its twinkle follows the composition frame, as Rain's fall does. **A highlight is near white**: its smallest channel at least the threshold, where Glow's and Cross Glare's bright test (D-89) takes the largest channel; with that test a pale skin sparkled all over in the proposal's first picture, so the rule was changed before the fixtures were written. **How it differs** from Cross Glare (D-161), which streaks every bright pixel the same on every frame. **Known limits:** a large pure-white area is all highlight; two glints in one cell share a star. **Where it runs:** the processor; the graphics card in item 9.

D-187 / The batch's five new effects on the graphics card, held to 1 level of 255 / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28** by the owner's messages of 2026-09-28, "1, 2,3,5,6,7,8,9" and then "include 4 as well, just 1 thru 9", accepting items 1 to 9 of the agent's list of the effects and presets left to build; the ninth of the nine. The proposal is `verification/B-123a proposal/card_unit.md`. **What changes.** Color Lookup (D-182), Line Blur (D-183), HSV Key (D-184), Paraffin (D-185) and Kira-kira (D-186) are done by the card when one is the last effect of a drawn layer, as the effects of D-165 and D-178 are. **How the card does them.** Color Lookup, HSV Key and Paraffin in the colour-effects pass: the lookup's table rides with the settings; HSV Key reads the same 8-bit steps as the processor; Paraffin's near and far side come from one scan on the processor. Line Blur in one pass that works the direction and the blur along it at each pixel. Kira-kira's highlights and stars are found by the processor, as its rule does; the card lights each star's patch, keeping the strongest light at each pixel, and lays it on. **The measurement** is B-123's: every fixture frame of the five and the reference shot with each, at Full and Draft, within 1 level of 255, with the same warnings. **What it does not change:** no setting, file or default; exports and fixtures stay on the processor, byte-exact; a frame the card cannot draw is drawn by the processor as before. **If refused:** the five go back to the processor, and nothing else moves.

D-188 / Motion blur: the layer drawn at moments inside the shutter and averaged, drawings holding / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28 by the owner** ("I approve of motion blur plan"), with ADR-019; proposed by the agent the same day. Item 10 of the agent's list of what is left to build; the owner's messages of 2026-09-28 ("1, 2,3,5,6,7,8,9", then "include 4 as well, just 1 thru 9") accepted items 1 to 9, and item 10 was to be written up to an ADR and stop before code, as document 20 requires. The proposal is `verification/B-124a proposal/motion_blur.md`, with a picture worked by the rule; the ADR is ADR-019, `docs/adr/0019-motion-blur-averages-moments-inside-the-shutter.md`; FX-MB-001 to 050 in document 25 are its fixtures. **What it is.** A composition's `motion_blur` has a switch, a shutter angle (0 to 720, 180 when added), a shutter phase (-360 to 360, -90) and samples (2 to 64, 16); each drawn layer has its own switch; a layer is blurred when both are on. **The rule.** Frame n is drawn at `t_k = n + phase/360 + (angle/360)(k + 1/2)/N`; at each moment only where the layer is - its transform, its parents', its depth and the camera - is read, by document 20's key rules at a fraction of a frame; the drawing, masks, effects, shapes, a composition layer's picture, opacity and draw order are read once at n, so **drawings hold** and a cel on twos is never smeared into the next. The N placements of the one post-effect picture are averaged in linear premultiplied light, then matte, opacity and blend once; a layer that does not move is drawn once, bit for bit as with its switch off. **Where it runs:** the processor; until a card unit, the viewer draws such a frame on the processor and says so (D-101). **Questions for the owner:** a held key that jumps inside the shutter shows the layer twice at half strength, as After Effects does - keep it?; expression motion holds across the shutter (D-59) - acceptable for now?; should Draft use fewer samples? The owner accepted the plan as written, so the proposal's answers stand: a held jump shows twice at half strength, expression motion holds, and Draft uses the same samples as Full. **Build:** B-124b, on the processor; a card version is a later unit of its own.

D-189 / A layer of this composition as an effect's setting, read before it is placed / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28** by the owner's "take everything" (2026-09-28T23:23:06), which took in the After Effects picks A1 to A12. Three of them, Compound Blur (A2), Displacement Map (A3) and Gradient Wipe (A4), read another layer's picture, and the coordinator asked for that setting to be built once, first, as its own unit, with document 28's diagnostics for a missing or deleted layer and D-67's rules for a composition layer. The proposal is `verification/B-125a proposal/layer_map.md`, with a picture of the three fits; FX-LMAP-001 to 042 in document 25 are its fixtures, every number from `tools/effect_layer_reference.py` into `Fixtures/layer_map/`. **It adds to the project file** a kind of effect setting: a word naming a layer of the same composition as the layer the effect is on, or "" for none, never keyed, with a fit word beside it, `center`, `stretch` or `tile` (document 19). **The rule** (document 21): the map is the named layer's own picture at the same frame by its own timing, after its masks and its own effects and cut back to its own size, before it is placed; its transform, parent, the camera, its matte, opacity, blend mode, its switch, a matte-only role and motion blur make no difference, as After Effects reads a map layer "with its masks and effects". The layer the effect is on gives only its drawing and masks; an adjustment layer gives white through its masks; a null, a layer outside its in and out, a composition layer outside its inner composition, a missing composition or a missing drawing give an empty map, the last two with their own warnings. The map is fitted to the holder's own picture, centred, tiled or stretched, and at Draft it is made at the size the holder's effects run at. A name that is no layer of the composition is kept as written and the effect skipped, with `EFFECT_LAYER_MISSING` every frame, so Undo of a delete brings everything back; effects whose layer settings lead round in a circle are refused with `EFFECT_LAYER_CYCLE` (document 28), built and checked with A2, the first effect that can make one. **Known limits:** no card version; the drop-down, and what happens to the setting when a layer is duplicated or saved in a preset, come with A2 to A4. **Build:** B-125b, on the processor: the map is made and checked through the program before any effect uses it. **Built on 2026-09-28**: FX-LMAP-001 to 042 pass, 37 of 37, in `verification/B-125b_layer_map_table.md`.

D-190 / Lightning Bolt, a forking bolt of light / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28** by the owner's "take everything" (2026-09-28T23:23:06), which took in the After Effects picks A1 to A12; this is A1. The proposal is in `verification/B-126a proposal/`, with a picture worked by the reference rule; FX-BOLT-001 to 032 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-126. **What it does.** Lightning Bolt (`core.lightning_bolt`) draws a jagged bolt of light between two points of the layer, a core in a glow, with forks that thin to nothing, and draws a new bolt every `hold` frames; the light is added and paints the clear pixels; the layer does not grow. **Settings:** `start` and `end`, points in per cent of the drawing's own size, each coordinate -1000 to 1000, (40, 0) and (60, 100) when added; `jagged`, 0 to 100, 40; `detail`, 1 to 8, floored, 6; `branches`, 0 to 100, 30; `width`, 0 to 100 pixels, 3; `glow`, 0 to 500 pixels, 24; `opacity`, 0 to 100, 100; `hold`, 1 to 100 frames, floored, 2; `seed`, 0 to 100000, floored, 0; `color`, "#rrggbb", #ffffff; `glow_color`, "#rrggbb", #6e8cff. Every number can be keyed; width and glow are distances a draft scales. **Where it comes from.** After Effects' Lightning and Advanced Lightning in purpose; the rule is this program's own, nothing ported: the line is halved `detail` times, each middle pushed aside by a number from Noise's hash (D-119), each piece named by a key so that more detail or more branches never move what is already drawn. Its core is the share of each pixel a line of the width covers, exact on whole pixels, and its glow falls off as a square, as Kira-kira's arms do (D-186). **Clipped to the layer**, as After Effects' is, rather than growing it: a bolt reaches wherever its points are put, so a grown layer would have no bound; a solid or an adjustment layer the size of the frame holds a bolt across it. **Known limits:** a bolt appears whole, with no growing strike; the cost grows with glow and detail. **Where it runs:** the processor; the graphics card in a later card unit.

D-191 / Compound Blur, blurred where another layer is bright / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28** by the owner's "take everything" (2026-09-28T23:23:06), which took in the After Effects picks A1 to A12; this is A2, the first effect with D-189's layer setting. The proposal is in `verification/B-127a proposal/`, with a picture worked by the rule; FX-CBLUR-001 to 026 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-127. **What it does.** Compound Blur (`core.compound_blur`) blurs its layer by the picture luma of D-189's map: not at all where the map is black or clear, `max_blur` where it is white. **Settings:** `layer`, D-189's word, `""` when added; `fit`, `stretch` when added (After Effects' Stretch Map to Fit is on when added), `center` or `tile`; `max_blur`, 0 to 500 pixels, 20, keyable, a distance a draft scales; `invert`, `off` or `on`; `edges`, `transparent` or `repeat`, as Lens Blur's (D-116). **Where it comes from.** After Effects' Compound Blur in purpose; the rule is this program's own: the layer is blurred by document 21's Gaussian at five sigmas, the largest `max_blur / 3` and each next a half of it, and each pixel mixes the two nearest its own blur, linearly in sigma. Five levels a factor two apart keep the mix within a sixteenth of the largest blur at worst while costing about two Gaussian Blurs of the largest size; a Gaussian of each pixel's own sigma would cost that per pixel. **Layer settings in copies** (document 19): duplicating a layer renames a layer setting naming the layer itself to the copy; duplicating a composition renames each to the named layer's copy; a pasted effect keeps its setting; a saved preset keeps none. **Circles** (`EFFECT_LAYER_CYCLE`, built with it): every effect counts, switched on or off, so the switch never closes one; a command that would close one is refused and a file holding one is refused on opening, as a circle of mattes is. **Known limits:** the mix between levels can show a faint double at a sharp bright edge; about twice a Gaussian Blur's cost. **Where it runs:** the processor; the graphics card in a later card unit.

D-192 / FX-CBLUR-019's adjustment layer is written beneath the holder / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-29 by the owner** ("D-192 option 1; to your recommendation, like AE"): option 1, the reference corrected and `fx_cblur_019.json` written again, its expected pixels unchanged; done as B-127c. Proposed on 2026-09-29 by the agent, found while building B-127. FX-CBLUR-019 says its Compound Blur is on an adjustment layer above the holder, and expects the holder blurred as FX-CBLUR-002 blurs it. Its file lists the adjustment layer first in `layer_order`, and a composition's layers are drawn in that order, first to last, so the adjustment layer is beneath the holder with nothing under it to work on: `tools/compound_blur_reference.py` writes `[adjust] + layers` where it meant the holder first. The build draws the file as written, the holder unblurred, the same to the byte as FX-CBLUR-001's frame. **The proposal:** correct the reference to write the adjustment layer after the holder, and write `Fixtures/compound_blur/fx_cblur_019.json` again. Its expected pixels do not change: with the order corrected, the build gives them to within 2e-5, which B-127's table checks. Until this is decided the table shows FX-CBLUR-019 as a row in dispute, and the fixture is not changed. **If refused** (the case to stay as written): its expected pixels become FX-CBLUR-001's, the unblurred holder, and its description says the adjustment layer is beneath.

D-193 / Displacement Map, a layer moved by another layer's colours / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28** by the owner's "take everything" (2026-09-28T23:23:06), which took in the After Effects picks A1 to A12; this is A3, the second effect with D-189's layer setting. The proposal is in `verification/B-128a proposal/`, with a picture worked by the rule; FX-DMAP-001 to 031 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-128. **What it does.** Displacement Map (`core.displacement_map`) moves each pixel of its layer across and up or down by a chosen channel of D-189's map there: white by the maximum one way, black the other, mid grey and a clear map not at all. **Settings:** `layer`, D-189's word, `""` when added; `fit`, `stretch` when added, `center` or `tile`; `horizontal`, `red` when added, and `vertical`, `green`, each one of `red`, `green`, `blue`, `alpha`, `luminance`, `hue`, `lightness`, `saturation`, `full` or `off`; `max_horizontal` and `max_vertical`, -1000 to 1000 pixels, 5 when added, keyable, distances a draft scales; `wrap`, `off` or `on`. **Where it comes from.** After Effects' Displacement Map: its channel choices, maxima, map behaviours and Wrap Pixels Around. Its Half is left out, since it moves nothing, as Off does; so is its Expand Output, since this program's effects that move pixels keep the layer's bounds, as Twirl and Bulge do. The rule is this program's own: a pixel reads the picture at its own centre moved by `2v - 1` times each maximum, by document 21's bilinear read, and a map's colours are laid over mid grey by their covering, so a clear part of the map moves nothing. **Circles and copies** as D-191; a circle may run through a Displacement Map and a Compound Blur together. **Known limits:** bounds never grow, so what moves in from beyond the layer's edge is clear unless `wrap` is `on`; a map with hard steps tears the picture at them. **Where it runs:** the processor; the graphics card in a later card unit.

D-194 / Gradient Wipe, a layer wiped away in the order of another layer's brightness / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28** by the owner's "take everything" (2026-09-28T23:23:06), which took in the After Effects picks A1 to A12; this is A4, the third effect with D-189's layer setting. The proposal is in `verification/B-129a proposal/`, with a picture worked by the rule; FX-GWIPE-001 to 028 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-129. **What it does.** Gradient Wipe (`core.gradient_wipe`) makes its layer transparent where D-189's map is darker than a level that rises with the completion, the darkest parts first, with a soft edge over a band of the map's greys as wide as the softness. **Settings:** `completion`, 0 to 100, 0 when added, keyable; `softness`, 0 to 100, 0 when added, keyable; `layer`, D-189's word, `""` when added; `fit`, `stretch` when added, `center` or `tile`; `invert`, `off` or `on`. **Where it comes from.** After Effects' Gradient Wipe: its Transition Completion, Transition Softness, Gradient Layer, Gradient Placement and Invert Gradient, all kept. The rule is this program's own: the map's brightness is Compound Blur's picture luma, so a clear map reads as black, and the level runs so that completion 0 keeps every pixel and 100 none at any softness, as Linear Wipe's edge does (D-155). With no layer named or a missing one the effect does nothing, as D-189's other effects do. **Circles and copies** as D-191; a circle may run through any effects that read layers. **Known limits:** a map with few greys wipes in steps. **Where it runs:** the processor; the graphics card in a later card unit.

D-195 / Echo, copies of a layer from other frames laid over it as trails / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28** by the owner's "take everything" (2026-09-28T23:23:06), which took in the After Effects picks A1 to A12; this is A5, the first effect that reads its layer at other frames. The proposal is in `verification/B-130a proposal/`, with a picture worked by the rule; FX-ECHO-001 to 030 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-130. **What it does.** Echo (`core.echo`) replaces its layer's picture with copies of the layer's own drawing, through its masks, at frames `echo_time` apart, each `decay` of the one before, the present at `intensity`, put together by the operator. **Settings:** `echo_time`, -120 to 120 frames, -1 when added, floored; `echoes`, 0 to 30, 1 when added, floored; `intensity` and `decay`, 0 to 1, 1 when added; all four keyable; `operator`, `add` when added, `maximum`, `minimum`, `screen`, `composite_in_back`, `composite_in_front` or `blend`. **Where it comes from.** After Effects' Echo: its Echo Time, Number Of Echoes, Starting Intensity, Decay and Echo Operator, all kept, and its reading of the layer's own picture rather than what earlier effects made of it. The echo time is in frames, not seconds, as this program's timing is; the operators are this program's own sums on premultiplied numbers, Add and Screen held at 1. The copies are D-189's picture of a layer read by itself, steps 1 and 2, at the other frames, so a layer's movement leaves no trail, as in After Effects. On an adjustment layer it changes nothing, as Light Wrap (D-132). **Known limits:** thirty echoes draw the layer thirty-one times. **Where it runs:** the processor; the graphics card in a later card unit.

D-196 / Posterize Time, a layer held for several frames at a time / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28** by the owner's "take everything" (2026-09-28T23:23:06), which took in the After Effects picks A1 to A12; this is A6. The proposal is in `verification/B-131a proposal/`, with a filmstrip worked by the rule; FX-PTIME-001 to 020 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-131. **What it does.** Posterize Time (`core.posterize_time`) makes its layer show what it showed at an earlier frame `h`, stepped to its `frame_rate` from the composition's first frame: the layer's content (drawing, solid, shapes, composition, masks, and every effect of its stack with its settings, maps and echoes) is taken at `h`; whether the layer is shown, and its transform, opacity, motion blur and depth, stay at the frame drawn. **Settings:** `frame_rate`, 0.1 to 99 frames a second, 12 when added, keyable. **Where it comes from.** After Effects' Posterize Time: its Frame Rate kept, and its holding of the layer's content and effects but not its transform. The steps are counted from the composition's start so layers at one rate change together, and a hold never reaches before the layer's in point. Several in one stack hold in turn. On an adjustment layer it changes nothing, as Echo (D-195). **Known limits:** a movement is not held; the adjustment layer holds nothing beneath it. **Where it runs:** where the layer's content is resolved, before the processor or the graphics card is asked for anything, so both hold alike.

D-197 / Change to Color, one colour turned into another with its shades / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28** by the owner's "take everything" (2026-09-28T23:23:06), which took in the After Effects picks A1 to A12; this is A7. The proposal is in `verification/B-132a proposal/`, with a picture worked by the rule; FX-CTC-001 to 027 in document 25 are its fixtures; built as B-132. **What it does.** Change to Color (`core.change_to_color`) compares each colour with `from` by hue, lightness and saturation (HLS), and turns those near it toward `to`, fully within the tolerances and fading out over a softness band past them. **Settings:** `from`, `#rrggbb`, #ff0000 when added; `to`, `#rrggbb`, #0080ff; `change`, `hue` when added, `hue_lightness`, `hue_saturation` or `hue_lightness_saturation`; `change_by`, `setting` when added or `transforming`; `hue_tolerance` 5, `lightness_tolerance` 50, `saturation_tolerance` 50 and `softness` 50, each 0 to 100 and keyable; `view_matte`, `off` when added or `on`. **Where it comes from.** After Effects' Change to Color: its From, To, Change, Change By, three tolerances, Softness and View Correction Matte kept. The comparison and the change are this program's own sums: a hue tolerance of 100 is the whole wheel, as Leave Color's (D-141); the softness band of each part is that part's tolerance times the softness; the three parts' amounts are taken at their least; and the change is laid on the encoded colour by that amount. A colour with no hue matches no hue short of tolerance 100, and is read as hue 0 where one is needed. **Known limits:** a grey `to` gives red's hue unless saturation is changed. **Where it runs:** the processor; the graphics card in a later card unit.

D-198 / Corner Pin, a drawing pinned by its four corners / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-28** by the owner's "take everything" (2026-09-28T23:23:06), which took in the After Effects picks A1 to A12; this is A8. Each pixel keeps its block's covering whole or not at all, or with a feather the share of a square the feather across, centred on it, that lies in kept blocks.
