A draft scales the block sizes, never below 1, and the feather. **Where it comes from.** After Effects' Block Dissolve (Transition): its purpose and the names Transition Completion, Block Width, Block Height and Feather. The order of the blocks and the feather's square are this program's own. **Known limits:** After Effects' Soft Edges switch is left out; there is no seed, so every Block Dissolve with the same block sizes goes in the same order. **Where it runs:** the processor; the graphics card in a later card unit.

D-215 / FX-EXTRACT-027, a number written as a word again / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-29 by the owner ("yes", to the coordinator's recommendations); done in B-147c**: the case now expects the file refused with `PROJECT_SCHEMA_INVALID`, as D-164, regenerated by `tools/extract_reference.py`, and `verification/B-147_extract_table.md` checks it with no row in dispute. Proposed by the agent the same day, found while building B-147. FX-EXTRACT-027, written by the agent in B-147a the same day, writes Extract's black point as a word (`"black_point": "60"`) and expects the file to open, the effect kept as written and left out of every frame with `EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID`. That is the mistake D-164 settled for the third batch: a number written as a word is a fault in the file's shape, and every effect refuses the file on opening with `PROJECT_SCHEMA_INVALID`, which is what the build does. **The proposal:** the same answer as D-164, the case expecting the file refused; `tools/extract_reference.py` and the fixture are changed only once this is accepted. Until then `verification/B-147_extract_table.md` shows FX-EXTRACT-027 as a row "in dispute" that checks the file is refused, and the other 26 cases pass. **If refused:** a number written as a word would open with the effect skipped, for every effect, as D-164 says.

D-216 / Time stretch, Frame Mix frame blending and the drawing dissolve / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-29 by the owner ("yes", to the coordinator's recommendations), with keys stretching with the layer; written B-150a, changed B-150a2, built B-150b.** Proposed by the agent the same day. Item 5 of the fourth batch; on 2026-09-29 the owner answered "both": a layer time stretch with After Effects' Frame Mix, a layer switch and a composition switch, no Pixel Motion, and a dissolve from one drawing to the next. Time between frames needs an ADR first, as document 20 requires, so this stops before code. The proposal is `verification/B-150a proposal/frame_blending.md`, with a film and a contact sheet worked by the rule; the ADR is ADR-020, `docs/adr/0020-time-stretch-mixes-the-two-frames-either-side.md`; FX-FBLEND-001 to 067 in document 25 are its fixtures. **What it is.** A raster or composition layer's `time_stretch`, 1 to 10000 per cent, 100 when absent; a layer's `frame_blend: "frame_mix"` and a composition's `frame_blending: true`; a raster layer's `drawing_dissolve`, 0 to 100 frames. **The rule.** The source time is `t = (n - in) * 100 / stretch + offset`, `f = floor(t)`, `w = t - f`; the layer shows `P(f)`, and with both switches on and `w > 0` it shows `P(f) + w (P(f + 1) - P(f))` in linear premultiplied light, `P(f)` alone at the end of the source; a gap or a missing drawing mixes in as transparent, the latter reported, never substituted. The dissolve: on the last `d = min(D, hold - 1)` frames of a drawing followed at once by another, `A + (k / (d + 1)) (B - A)`. Masks, effects, transform and motion blur run once on the mixed picture, and the keys stretch with the layer, read at `u = in + (n - in) * 100 / stretch`; a stretched layer's in point trims by whole source frames only, its keys moving with it. The Time Stretch command keeps the in point and scales the out point. **Where it runs:** the processor; until a card unit, the viewer draws such a frame on the processor and says so (D-101). **The owner's answers, 2026-09-29:** (1) keys stretch with the layer, like After Effects, which changed the proposal: B-150a2 rewrote FX-FBLEND-023 and added 025 to 028 (pictures), 045 to 049 (where keys play and where a key set at the playhead is stored) and 064 to 067 (trimming the in point), with the times cases giving the key time `u`; (2) the dissolve works whatever the composition switch says: kept; (3) sped up, only the two nearest frames are mixed: kept; (4) the composition switch stays off until the user turns it on: kept.

D-217 / Ten of the fourth batch on the card, each held to 1 level of 255 / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-29 under the owner's delegation ("sounds great! let's do 1 through 7 to your discretion."), every check within 1 level; built B-151.** Proposed by the agent the same day for eleven; Kaleidoscope failed the check and stays on the processor (D-240, proposed). It is the card half of the owner's request of 2026-09-29, "sweet! it works! motion blur, and let's do a performance audit along with gpu-acceleration please.", as D-165 was for the third batch. D-100 has each effect declare and measure its own tolerance when it moves to the card, and show it in pictures before it is accepted. **The proposal:** Median, Smart Blur, Roughen Edges, Radial Shadow, Bevel Alpha, Snowfall, Cell Pattern, Polar Coordinates, Optics Compensation and Corner Pin, ten of the eleven of the fourth batch P-23 found costing most, keep compositing's tolerance when they are the last effect of a drawn layer: no channel of any pixel more than 1 level of 255 from the CPU's picture. **What stays on the processor, and why.** 4-Color Gradient raises a double-precision number to a power, which the card cannot do exactly. Compound Blur, Displacement Map and Gradient Wipe read another layer, which the card's plan does not carry to an effect. Echo and Posterize Time choose which frames are drawn, before any effect runs. Motion blur and Frame Mix are a separate study. Light Sweep, Lightning Bolt, Change to Color, Radio Waves, Beam, Extract, Bevel Edges and Block Dissolve cost 5 ms or less a frame (P-23), too little to be worth a card pass each. The five of D-187 are there already. An effect at a Mix below 100% stays on the CPU, as before. **How the card does it:** the same rule as the CPU, pixel for pixel, in double precision where the CPU works in double, with the drawing sent in full precision as for D-122. Median finds the middle of each pixel's neighbours by counting bits rather than sorting, which gives the same neighbour exactly; Smart Blur adds its neighbours in the CPU's order. Radial Shadow and Bevel Alpha use the card's blur with the CPU's weights. Snowfall and Cell Pattern use the CPU's own 64-bit hash, and Cell Pattern's points are placed by the processor. Corner Pin's matrix is worked once by the processor. **The measurement** is B-123's, over every fixture frame of the eleven and the reference shot with each, at Full and Draft, with one rule added: each reference shot row must have the effect in fact on the card. `verification/B-151_gpu_fx_table.md`: **2170 of 2170 checks pass**, the worst the reference shot with Median at frame 0, Full, 3,814 pixels 1 level apart; its pictures are in `verification/B-151 pictures/`. **What it does not change:** exports and fixtures stay on the CPU, byte-exact, and a frame the card cannot draw is drawn by the CPU exactly as before. **If refused:** the ten go back to the CPU, and nothing else moves.

D-218 / A motion-blurred, frame-mixed or dissolved layer no longer sends the whole frame to the CPU (G1) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-29 under the owner's delegation ("sounds great! let's do 1 through 7 to your discretion."), every check within 1 level; built B-152.** Until now the viewer's graphics card handed a frame to the CPU whole when any layer in it was motion-blurred (D-188) or frame-mixed or dissolved (D-216), every other layer and card effect included. **What changed.** The CPU still builds that one layer's picture exactly as before, averaging the moments or mixing the drawings, and the card now lays it with the rest of the frame, sent in half precision like any finished drawing. A frame with an adjustment layer is still the CPU's (B-44), for G5. Export and Draft's CPU pictures are untouched. **The check:** `verification/B-152_card_whole_frame_table.md`, **882 of 882 pass**: every frame of every motion blur and frame blending fixture and the reference shot with motion blur on every layer and with frame mix and a dissolve, at Full and Draft, the card drawing the frame itself, within 1 level, with the same warnings; the largest difference is 1 level. **Timing** (`verification/B-152_card_whole_frame_timing_table.md`, no other cargo process running): on its own B-152 is faster only where the card has an effect of its own beside the blur, the reference shot with motion blur and a Roughen Edges at Full going from 86.9 to 72.8 ms a frame; a frame whose only unusual layers are blurred or mixed is slower, motion blur at Full 50.9 to 57.9 ms and frame mix at Draft 50.1 to 63.1 ms, because the CPU's new full-size picture for each such layer is sent to the card every frame, each time through a new transfer buffer. G2 (B-153), next, removes that sending cost; if after it these frames are still slower than before, the card will hand such a frame back to the CPU whenever it has no effect of its own to draw. Putting the blur and the mix themselves on the card is not part of this; they were excluded from the unit. **If refused:** the two refusals go back in `Gpu::refuse`.

D-219 / The card keeps its memory from frame to frame (G2) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-29 under the owner's delegation ("sounds great! let's do 1 through 7 to your discretion."), the pictures byte-identical; built B-153.** Until now the viewer's graphics card made new memory for each frame: a new transfer buffer for each picture the CPU sent it, a new texture for each drawing it held and a new working texture for each step of its effects, letting the old ones go. **What changed.** The card keeps one transfer buffer, grown to the largest frame's needs, and fills it at a different place for each picture; a drawing nothing can ask for again leaves its texture for the next drawing of the same size, within the memory budget (B-48), which counts the kept textures; and a working texture used in the last two frames is cleared and used again. Nothing else changes: the same passes, in the same order, on the same numbers. **Not built, with reasons:** a pipeline cache on disk (opening the card takes a third of a second once a session, and the driver keeps its own shader cache); keeping each pass's settings buffer (under a millisecond a frame); a non-blocking error check (it answers at once on this system); reading the frame back one frame late, and planning the next frame while the card draws (the app's viewer already shows the card's frame without reading it back or waiting). **The check:** `verification/B-153_kept_memory_table.md`, **12 of 12 pass**: the reference shot with motion blur, with frame mix and a dissolve, and with motion blur and a Roughen Edges, played twice at Draft and Full, every 48th frame byte for byte a freshly opened card's, and no new memory the second time through (before it, 180 pieces the second time through the motion blur shot at Full, `verification/B-153_kept_memory_before.md`). Every other card table is unchanged. **Timing** (`verification/B-153_card_timing_table.md`, three builds turn about, four rounds): every shot is at or below B-152's; the motion blur with a Roughen Edges at Full is 57.5 ms a frame, against 90.3 before B-152 and 77.2 after; motion blur at Draft is back to 15.6 against 15.9. A frame whose only unusual layers are blurred or mixed is still slower than when the CPU drew it whole (motion blur at Full 62.2 against 51.2, frame mix at Draft 56.7 against 48.8): the card's own copy of each new full-size picture remains. While it was measured the card sat mostly in its low-power state, its link at PCIe generation 2 with 8 lanes, an observation of the driver's power management, which this program does not set. As D-218 said, such a frame now goes back to the CPU whole when no layer has an effect the card draws: B-153b. **If refused:** each picture, drawing and working texture gets new memory again, as before.

D-220 / A blurred or mixed frame with nothing for the card goes back to the CPU (G1 follow-up) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-29 under the owner's delegation ("sounds great! let's do 1 through 7 to your discretion."), the pictures those of the CPU exactly; built B-153b.** D-218 said that if, after G2, a frame whose only unusual layers are motion-blurred, frame-mixed or dissolved were still slower on the card than drawn whole by the CPU, the card would hand it back whenever no layer has an effect of its own to draw; D-219 measured it still slower. **What changed.** The card refuses such a frame, with the message "The CPU drew this frame: it has motion blur or frame blending and no effect for the GPU, which the CPU draws faster."; the CPU draws it as before B-152. A frame that also has an effect the card draws, a Light Wrap included, stays on the card. And the sending memory D-219 keeps is now capped at an eighth of the card's memory budget rather than four times the frame's size in 32-bit floats: at Draft the frame is half the size of the drawings sent, so a frame mix with a card effect sent more than the cap every frame and made new memory each time. **The check:** `verification/B-152_card_whole_frame_table.md`, **893 of 893 pass**, of which 292 blurred or mixed frames with nothing for the card are the CPU's picture exactly with only the card's message extra (292 failing before, 66ce857, `verification/B-153b_card_whole_frame_before.md`), and the motion blur shot with a Roughen Edges stays on the card within 1 level; `verification/B-153_kept_memory_table.md`, 12 of 12, its frame mix shot given the same Roughen Edges so that it stays on the card (40 new pieces of memory the second time through at Draft without the cap change; the checks-first commit's message said this check passed, which was not so). Every other card table is unchanged. **Timing** (`verification/B-153b_timing_table.md`, before B-152, B-153 and B-153b turn about, four rounds, no other cargo process): motion blur at Full 47.6 ms a frame against 47.5 before B-152 and 58.5 on B-153; frame mix at Draft 44.5 against 40.8 and 59.0, at Full 56.5 against 53.2 and 61.2, the same code as before B-152, its rounds spreading from below to above the earlier ones; motion blur with a Roughen Edges at Full 54.6, against 86.5 and 54.3. **Quiet re-measure** (2026-09-30, `verification/B-153b_timing_table.md`, before B-152, B-153b and the build after the GPU plan turn about, three rounds, no other cargo process or build running, driver 610.88): frame mix at Draft 41.1 against 40.6 before B-152, inside the spread of the rounds, so no real difference is left; motion blur with a Roughen Edges at Draft 22.8 against 18.5, slower on this build in every round, and 9.5 after the GPU plan; after the plan frame mix takes 28.5 ms at Draft and motion blur 13.5 at Full. **If refused:** the card draws such frames itself again, slower, as B-153 left it.

D-221 / How B-164 works big blurs small, where D-235's text did not work / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-29 under the owner's delegation ("sounds great! let's do 1 through 7 to your discretion."), every checked pixel within 1 level; built B-164.** D-235 as written, a plain f by f block average blurred at sqrt(s^2 - (f^2 - 1) / 12 - f^2 / 6) / f, left 2 to 3 levels on dark pixels at the edge of Gaussian Blur 50 and 100 on the card, although D-235's experiment had passed: the exact blur stops at three sigmas (document 21's kernel radius), and a small blur that does not stop where the big one does is off in proportion to f / s. **What was built instead.** (1) The shrink is a tent-weighted mean over 2f by 2f pixels, so its own blur is (2f^2 + 1) / 12 and the small sigma sqrt(s^2 - (2f^2 + 1) / 12 - f^2 / 6) / f. (2) The small blur stops where the big one does, (r + 0.5) / f small pixels out for the big kernel's radius r, its last taps cut by the fraction inside, and is scaled to sum to 1. (3) Enlarging is bilinear from pixel centres, outside the layer transparent, as D-235 said. The safety rule is D-235's: f = 8, halved down to 1 (exact) until the small sigma is at least 6. A Gaussian Blur with Repeat Edge Pixels stays exact. Export and every render to file never take this shortcut: only the viewer's card does. **The check:** `verification/B-164_downsampled_blurs_table.md`, **24 of 24 pass**: Gaussian Blur, Glow and Bloom at 20, 50, 100 and 200, Full and Draft, the reference shot at frame 100 with the effect on three layers; the card worked small exactly the blurs the rule says, and no pixel is more than 1 level from the CPU's exact frame (the furthest, Gaussian Blur 50 at Full, 1 level on 112566 pixels; pictures in `verification/B-164 pictures/`). The checks came first (95ad517, 20 of 24 failing; since then the Draft rows expect the rule at Draft's quartered distances, as the card works them). The blur, glow and bloom fixtures' tables (B-47 288 of 288, B-50 24 of 24, B-51 338 of 338) are unchanged: their frames are too small for the rule to shrink anything. **Timing** (`verification/B-164_timing_table.md`): every Full row faster, Gaussian Blur 200 from 90.9 to 14.6 ms a frame, Glow 200 43.8 to 25.6, Bloom 200 59.4 to 31.6; Gaussian Blur 50 and Glow 200 at Draft under a millisecond slower.

D-222 / Lens Blur by the fast Fourier transform on the card, not built (G14's second half) / **DECIDED on 2026-09-30 by the owner ("accept your recommendation on D-222, decline D-229"): option 1, Lens Blur stays exact and as it is; no FFT is built.** Proposed on 2026-09-29. The plan said: build an FFT Lens Blur for large radii only if it stays within 1 level on the fixtures, else defer. The card's Lens Blur today adds each row of the iris from running totals in double precision, the CPU's own sums, so it is exact, and its cost grows with the radius: the reference shot with a Lens Blur on three layers takes 52.8 ms a frame at Full at radius 25, 118.3 at 100 and 251.9 at 200 (Draft 8.6 to 15.0; `verification/B-164_timing_table.md`). An FFT's cost would not grow with the radius, but the card's FFT works in single precision. **What was measured** (`tools/d222_fft_lens_experiment.py`, scipy's single-precision FFT against the exact blur, on a 1024 by 640 layer, an opaque shape with bright highlights on transparency, a disc iris at radius 25, 100 and 200): the error is tiny, 3 to 5 millionths, and wherever the result shows any alpha at all (1 of 255 or more) it is within 1 level. But it is spread over every pixel, and in the nearly transparent haze at the blur's edge (alpha under 1 of 255) the straight colour, which is the premultiplied colour divided by that tiny alpha, comes out up to 255 levels wrong, on 267 000 to 441 000 pixels. Treating alpha under 1 in 100 000 as empty cures radius 25 but leaves radius 200 with 352 pixels off by up to 255. These pixels are invisible as the viewer shows the frame, but the card's checks compare every channel of every pixel, and counting only visible ones would be widening the tolerance to pass. The fixture frames (16 by 10, radius at most 12) are too small to show it. **Pictures:** `verification/B-164 pictures/`, `lens 200 hidden colour exact.png` and `... single-precision FFT.png` (the straight colour with alpha set aside: the FFT's is streaked noise around the shape), and `lens 200 as seen over grey exact.png` and `... single-precision FFT.png` (the same frames as seen: no visible difference). **For the owner:** (1) leave Lens Blur exact and as it is (recommended; big radii at Full stay slow, Draft stays fast); (2) build the FFT for radii above 50 in the viewer only, and change the card's checks to ignore the colour of pixels whose alpha is 0 of 255; (3) build it with the exact sums redoing the pixels whose alpha is under 1 of 255, a larger build whose speed is unknown. No speed is claimed for an FFT: it was not built.

D-223 / RAM preview: finished frames kept in memory and made ahead while playing (GPU plan G3) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-30 under the owner's delegation of 2026-09-29 ("sounds great! let's do 1 through 7 to your discretion."): every frame from memory is byte for byte the frame made fresh, with the same messages; exports untouched; built B-154.** The viewer made every frame again each time it was shown, even the tenth time round a loop. **What was built.** (1) `FrameCache` in `src/cache.rs` keeps each finished frame the window receives, 8-bit sRGB straight, with its size, whether the card fell back and its warnings, under a key of everything it is made from: the project as shown compared by value (so an edit, undo or solo is a different key, and undo finds its frame again), the composition, the drawings' folder, the quality and which processor at what card budget, and the frame number. Every file the render looked at is recorded with its size and modified time (`cache::looked_at`, now used by the cel key, the missing-media check and the colour tables) and looked at again before a kept frame is sent. Document 27 has the scope entry, under Memory policy. (2) While the shot plays, a worker makes the frames after the one on screen, in playback order, into the same memory, and stops when playback stops or the memory is full. (3) The Preferences memory setting is shared: the finished frames may hold up to half, never leaving the cels under 1 GiB; the cels have the rest, fitted each time they are locked to make a frame. A fixed half for the cels was tried first and starved a heavy shot's first pass (document 08's ten layers at Full dropped 85 of 240 frames against 24). Exports and renders to file never read these frames (ADR-015). **The check:** `verification/B-154_ram_preview_table.md`, **37 of 37 pass** (19 of 36 before the build, d7cb950; the 37th, added with it, checks that the cels give way). **Timing** (`verification/B-154_timing_before.md`, three runs of each build turn about; `verification/B-154_timing_table.md`): the second pass of a 240-frame loop at Full is 0.9 to 1.1 ms a frame, from 15.0 (reference shot, CPU), 27.6 (ten layers, CPU) and 2.3 to 3.6 (card), none late; the first pass drops the same frames as before (24 against 25 for the ten layers on the CPU at Full, 11 against 11 on the card) and costs up to 1.3 ms more a frame at Full on the card, the copy of the kept frame sent to the window; the loop is made ahead in 0.5 to 7.2 s, faster than its 10 s of playing. The playtest sheet is `verification/B-154_playtest.md`.

D-224 / A layer's whole run of card effects drawn on the card (GPU plan G4) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-30 under the owner's delegation of 2026-09-29 ("sounds great! let's do 1 through 7 to your discretion."): every checked picture within 1 level of 255 of the processor's, the tolerance already accepted for the card; exports untouched; built B-155.** The card drew only the last effect of a layer's stack; every effect above it ran on the processor and the picture was sent. **What was built.** `LayerDraw.on_card` is now a list: `compose::resolve_layer` walks back from the end of the stack and leaves the card every effect from the last one it cannot draw to the end, in stack order, each with the buffer size the ones before it grew. The card (`Gpu::applied`) runs them one after another on the same picture, and keeps its picture after each: when only a later effect changes from one frame to the next, it starts again from the kept picture before it. The processor, when the card refuses a frame, runs the same list in the same order (`render`). Two kinds only begin a run: Bloom, Glow, Paraffin and Kira-kira look at the drawing they are given before the card is asked; and an HSV Key, whose hue of a nearly grey pixel swings with the smallest change, keyed pixels the processor kept, 255 levels apart, when it was handed the card's picture after two other effects, in the check's first run after the build. Kaleidoscope stays on the processor (D-240), so a stack with it is split there. **The check:** `verification/B-155_gpu_chain_table.md`, each of the 69 card effects first before two others and last after two, on the reference shot's first three layers, at Draft and Full, frames 0 and 100, and a stack split by Kaleidoscope: **834 of 834 pass** (564 of 834 before, 76394c2); largest difference 1 level (worst, Halftone first: 138,934 pixels 1 level apart; pictures in `verification/B-155 pictures/`); the plan made for the card drawn by the processor is the processor's own frame byte for byte in 278 of 278. `b155_kept_run_is_fresh` checks that a run started from a kept picture gives the fresh card's bytes exactly. The earlier card tables (B-46, B-49, B-50, B-65, B-76) are rewritten with the effects now drawn as runs and still pass. **Timing** (`verification/B-155_timing_before.md`, three runs of each build turn about; `verification/B-155_timing_table.md`): with a Noise that changes every frame at the start of two stacks, Full 96.4 to 24.7 ms a frame; still stacks about the same (10.5 to 10.1 Draft, 10.6 to 9.7 Full), since the effect cache already kept the processor's part; a moving Noise at the end about the same (13.8 to 12.2 Draft, 13.8 to 14.9 Full); and a moving Noise at the start at Draft 10.6 to 14.2 ms slower, the small draft picture being quick on the processor already. A quiet re-measure on 2026-09-30 (before, B-155 and the build after the GPU plan turn about, three rounds, no other cargo process or build running, driver 610.88) confirms that slowdown as real: 10.5 to 13.7 ms, every B-155 round above every round before, and 13.2 ms after the GPU plan, so G13 did not remove it; at Full 97.0 to 24.9 (22.0 after the plan). The playtest sheet is `verification/B-155_playtest.md`.

D-225 / Adjustment layers drawn on the card (GPU plan G5, first part) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-30 under the owner's delegation of 2026-09-29 ("sounds great! let's do 1 through 7 to your discretion."): every checked picture within 1 level of 255 of the processor's, the tolerance already accepted for the card; exports untouched; built B-156.** Any frame with an adjustment layer went to the processor whole (B-44). **What was built.** The card takes the frame it has laid so far (`take`), runs the adjustment layer's stack on it as it runs a layer's (D-224; `compose::adjust_run` gives the run, `Gpu::run` draws it), and mixes the result back by the layer's cover, `B + c*(E(B) - B)` (`render::adjust_frame`, D-66): the cover sampled in double precision as the processor's is, the product rounded once as the processor's is, and at full cover the effected pixel exactly (D-90). An adjustment layer stays the processor's when its stack has an effect the card does not draw, a Bloom, Glow, Paraffin, Kira-kira or HSV Key (which only begin a run, D-224), or a Kaleidoscope (D-240), or when the card has no double precision. **One finding.** In the check's first run after the build, Posterize, Threshold, Halftone, Cross Glare, Line Blur, Smart Blur, Light Rays, Lens Blur and the wipes were up to 255 levels apart: the card keeps drawings in half precision, and a threshold turned that small difference in the frame beneath into a large one; where a wipe cut an opaque pixel under a cover just below one, the colour of the nearly transparent pixel left behind is decided by the last bit of the frame beneath. Under an adjustment layer every drawing is now kept at full precision, as a Light Wrap's already was, and all of them came within 1 level; the tolerance was not changed. It costs twice the card memory for those drawings. **The check:** `verification/B-156_gpu_adjust_table.md`, each of the 64 card effects alone on an adjustment layer over the reference shot, runs of three over the whole frame, over part of it and between two layers, at Draft and Full, frames 0 and 100: **308 of 308 pass** (32 of 308 before, 6a24bc5); largest difference 1 level (worst, Hue/Saturation alone, frame 100, Full: 78,242 pixels 1 level apart; pictures in `verification/B-156 pictures/`); the 32 frames kept on the processor are its own byte for byte. The B-76 and B-123 tables now expect their adjustment-layer fixtures (fx_wrap_015, fx_lut_012) on the card, and they pass there with no difference. **Timing** (`verification/B-156_timing_before.md`, `verification/B-156_timing_table.md`, the median of three runs each): Levels, Gaussian Blur and Hue/Saturation over the whole frame at Full 61.4 to 23.2 ms a frame, over part of it 62.1 to 23.2, after a moving Noise 75.5 to 23.6; at Draft 18.1 to 13.8, 20.3 to 15.0 and 19.1 to 15.5. **Not in this part:** masks drawn by the card, the Draft downscale on the card, the lit scan and motion blur / Frame Mix summed on the card, the rest of G5. The playtest sheet is `verification/B-156_playtest.md`.

D-226 / Motion blur added up on the card (GPU plan G5, second part) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-30 under the owner's delegation of 2026-09-29 ("sounds great! let's do 1 through 7 to your discretion."): every checked picture within 1 level of 255 of the processor's, the tolerance already accepted for the card; exports untouched; built B-156b.** Since B-152 the card drew a motion-blurred frame, but the processor added up each blurred layer's moments (`settle`) and sent the average over. **What was built.** In a plan made for the card, a drawn layer that is not an adjustment layer keeps its moments (`LayerDraw.moments`), its transform the identity at Full and the Draft scaling at Draft, as `settle` would leave it. The card adds each moment into a zeroed frame-sized sum at one over their number (`moment` in the card's shader, `Gpu::averaged`), takes the sum into a texture and lays it as the processor lays the average. The processor's own sum moved out of `settle` unchanged into `render::average`, which the processor path of a card plan also uses, so its bytes are the same. A motion-blurred matte is still settled on the processor, so a frame with one is still the processor's (B-153b). **The check:** `verification/B-156b_gpu_motion_blur_table.md`, every frame of every motion blur fixture and the reference shot with motion blur on every layer, at Draft and Full: **175 of 175 pass** (44 of 175 before, e6d5f7d); largest difference 1 level (worst, the reference shot with motion blur frame 150, Draft: 14,368 pixels 1 level apart; pictures in `verification/B-156b pictures/`); the blurred-matte fixture fx_mb_025 is the processor's picture byte for byte. `tests/b152_card_whole_frame.rs` and `tests/b124_motion_blur.rs` now expect such a layer's moments left for the card instead of an averaged picture (893 of 893 and 75 of 75). The B-153 kept-memory table now counts the card memory the sum takes the first time through (34 pieces at Draft, 29 at Full), and none the second. **Timing** (`verification/B-156b_timing_before.md`, `verification/B-156b_timing_table.md`, the median of three runs each): the reference shot with motion blur at Full 47.4 to 15.2 ms a frame, at Draft 15.4 to 8.6; with a Roughen Edges at Full 53.2 to 16.3, at Draft 25.8 to 12.5; the plain and frame-mix shots unchanged. **Not in this part:** Frame Mix and drawing dissolve (still mixed on the processor), masks drawn by the card, the Draft downscale on the card and the lit scan. The playtest sheet is `verification/B-156b_playtest.md`.

D-227 / Frame mix and drawing dissolve made quicker on the processor, not moved to the card (GPU plan G5, last part) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-30 under the owner's delegation of 2026-09-29 ("sounds great! let's do 1 through 7 to your discretion."): bit-exact, exports untouched; built B-156c.** Measured first (`b152_card_whole_frame_timing`, 32237bc): the reference shot with frame mix and dissolve took 46.0 ms a frame at Draft and 61.8 at Full, against 7.2 and 9.4 for the plain shot; a scratch count put about 15 ms of each card plan in making the mixed pictures. **What was built.** D-216's `mix` shares its pixels among the processor's threads; each number is the same `a + w (b - a)` in double precision, so the bytes are the same. A drawing that is only read on its way into a mix is no longer copied first. **Not built: mixing on the card.** The mixed picture is what the layer's mask, effects and Draft downscale start from on the processor, and it skips the cel cache, so a card mix would have to carry two drawings through each of those; that is more than this part is worth while the processor's mix is now a small share of the frame. **No checks-first commit:** nothing a check can see changes. The check is that nothing moved: every one of the 240 exported frames of the reference shot with frame mix and dissolve hashes the same on 32237bc and on this build, and `verification/B-150_frame_blending_table.md`, `verification/B-152_card_whole_frame_table.md` and `verification/B-153_kept_memory_table.md` came out unchanged. **Timing** (`verification/B-156c_timing_table.md`, the median of three runs each): the reference shot with frame mix and dissolve at Draft 46.0 to 31.3 ms a frame, at Full 61.8 to 44.8; the other shots unchanged. **Still not built in G5:** masks drawn by the card, the Draft downscale on the card and the lit scan. The playtest sheet is `verification/B-156c_playtest.md`.

D-228 / Five effects' heaviest sums on the graphics card in single precision (GPU plan G6, the double-precision audit) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-30 under the owner's delegation of 2026-09-29 ("sounds great! let's do 1 through 7 to your discretion."): every checked picture within 1 level of 255 of the processor's, the tolerance already accepted for the card; exports untouched; built B-157.** **The audit.** `tests/b157_f64_audit.rs` times every effect the card draws on the reference shot's first three layers, with the card made to run every pass each frame (`verification/B-157_audit_table.md`). This machine's card does double-precision sums at 1/64 the rate of single, and the audit found five effects whose cost was mostly that: Cross Glare (185 ms a frame over the plain shot at Full), Bloom (119), Directional Blur (53), Line Blur (48) and Turbulent Displace (23). **What moved to single precision.** Cross Glare's samples along its arms, and Bloom's and Directional Blur's running totals along their streaks (one pass, shared). Line Blur's slopes and taps, with one guard: a tap whose covering is within 0.0001 of the 1/256 that ends a line is worked again in double precision, because in single precision alone a few such taps landed on the other side and the reference shot came out up to 12 levels off at 3 pictures; with the guard it is within 1. Turbulent Displace's noise, which only moves where a pixel is read from. The last step of each, where the sum meets the drawing, stays in double precision. **The pictures.** Every table these effects are in still passes at 1 level: `verification/B-107_gpu_fx_table.md` (Cross Glare), `B-47_gpu_bloom_table.md`, `B-49_gpu_directional_table.md`, `B-123_gpu_fx_table.md` (Line Blur), `B-76_gpu_fx_table.md` (Turbulent Displace), and the chain and adjustment-layer tables of B-155 and B-156. The fixture rows are unchanged; on the reference shot a few more pixels differ by 1 level (Cross Glare frame 0 at Full 2,093 to 2,201 of 2,073,600; Bloom 2,640 to 2,643; Line Blur 1,096 to 1,154; the most, B-155's Bloom after Levels and a Gaussian Blur, frame 0 at Full, 455 to 987), none by 2. D-104's warning (half precision moved pixels across Bloom's threshold) does not apply: the threshold pass is untouched, only the totals after it moved. **Timing** (`verification/B-157_timing_table.md`, the median of three runs, whole frame at Full): Cross Glare 207.4 to 36.7 ms, Bloom 139.5 to 57.1, Directional Blur 72.4 to 31.6, Line Blur 66.8 to 25.9, Turbulent Displace 40.9 to 28.4. **Kept in double precision, not tried:** Lens Blur's and Simple Choker's running totals (one buffer; the Choker divides by a covering that can be very small), Roughen Edges' noise (it feeds a cut-off, where Line Blur showed single precision can tip a pixel across), Distance Gradation's distance passes, and the rest, which cost the card about 12 ms a frame or less at Full. Median (146 ms) is already single precision; its cost is its sorting. **Double precision is still needed** by the passes kept, so a card without it still sends those frames to the processor, as before. **No checks-first commit:** nothing a check can see is meant to change; the check is that every card table above still passes at 1 level. The playtest sheet is `verification/B-157_playtest.md`.

D-229 / Only the part of the picture on screen made and sent (GPU plan G8, the part at 100% or more) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-30 under the owner's delegation of 2026-09-29 ("sounds great! let's do 1 through 7 to your discretion."; G8 added to the queue "to your discretion"): every part byte for byte the whole frame's pixels; exports untouched; built B-158.** The viewer made and sent the whole frame however far in it was zoomed. **What was built.** A still frame asked for by number carries `v=left,top,right,bottom`, the fractions of the picture that show, cut to the window and everything that scrolls or hides the canvas, with a tenth more on every side so a small scroll needs no new frame. The window makes only the pixels those fractions touch and one more on every side (`preview::part_in`), answers with `x-part: x,y,width,height` beside the whole frame's `x-width` and `x-height`, and the page draws the part where it lies. On the processor only that part is laid (`render::render_part`): each pixel is sampled at its own place in the frame and the arithmetic per pixel does not depend on the tiles (B-07), so drawing fewer tiles changes nothing but the clock; a frame with an adjustment layer or a Light Wrap, which read the whole frame drawn so far, is drawn whole and cut, as is every frame the card draws or the frame memory (B-154) holds. A part made alone is never kept as a frame. Playback, and the card painting the window (B-45), send the whole frame as before. The page asks again when a scroll or a zoom shows something outside the part it holds. **The check** (`verification/B-158_part_table.md`, `part_on_screen` in `app/src/main.rs`): five parts (the left half, a box in the middle, the bottom right corner, a single point, the middle quarter) of the reference shot's frames 0, 100 and 239 and of every fixture with an adjustment layer, a Light Wrap, motion blur, frame blending, Bloom, Directional Blur or Glow, at Full and Draft, on the processor and on the card, each compared with the same pixels of the whole frame from a viewer that remembers nothing: **6548 of 6548 pass** (1902 before, ffa59f6, those being parts that with their spare pixel are the whole of a small fixture), byte for byte; plus the frame memory, playback, an unreadable part and export not naming `render_part`. **Timing** (`verification/B-158_timing_table.md`, the median of three runs, the middle quarter a 200% zoom shows): on the processor at Full 21.6 to 11.3 ms a frame on the reference shot and 40.8 to 21.4 on the declared ten-layer fixture, at Draft 9.5 to 7.3 and 19.5 to 17.0; the whole frame unchanged; on the card no saving, since the card still draws the whole frame. **Not built; DECLINED by the owner on 2026-09-30 ("accept your recommendation on D-222, decline D-229"):** below 100%, drawing the picture at the size it is shown rather than at Full and shrinking it on the page. That changes the pixels on screen against Full (it is a new, smaller picture, as Draft is), so under the rule of 2026-09-29 it would be a PROPOSED entry with pictures and a new viewer choice, off by default; it is left unbuilt, as the coordinator directed ("below-100% zoom stays a default-off proposal"), and the owner declined it, so the viewer keeps drawing at Full (or Draft) and shrinking on the page. The checks-first commit, ffa59f6, failed as it should. The page's part of it (asking again after a scroll or a zoom) is not covered by these checks and is what the playtest is for. The playtest sheet is `verification/B-158_playtest.md`.

D-230 / Hardware video encoding: the graphics card encodes an MP4 / **REJECTED on 2026-09-29 by the owner ("trust your recommendation to reject it"); the box, the note and the card encoder are removed in B-160b.** It changes an MP4's bytes, so it is off unless chosen. **What it does.** Preferences gains a box under a new Export heading, **Hardware video encoding**, not ticked. When it is ticked, an MP4 export asks Windows Media Foundation for a hardware encoder. The profile is Baseline, so the film has no reordered frames, the same as the software film's layout. Every MP4 written with the box ticked carries an `EXPORT_VIDEO_ENCODER` note in its report and in the status line: INFO naming the card's encoder, or WARNING when the software encoder wrote the film instead. That happens when Windows picked a software encoder anyway, when the card's encoder could not be started, or on a system that is not Windows. The change is never silent. With the box off, nothing changes and no note is written. **Measured on the D-01 machine (RTX 4070 Ti Super), whole reference shot, Standard quality.** The encoder used was "NVIDIA H.264 Encoder MFT". The file sizes were 8.1 MB for software and 12.3 MB for the card. Decoded by ffmpeg, card film against software film: PSNR 42.91 dB, and the worst single-channel difference was 53 levels of 255. Against the frames they were made from (over black), software scored 40.58 dB with a worst of 117, and the card 42.27 dB with a worst of 116. The card's film is slightly closer to the source, and larger. **Speed (PROVISIONAL, median of 7):** 15931 ms with the card against 13467 ms for software, so it was not faster here. Handing each frame to the encoder, one at a time, costs the same either way, and other builds were running. A 64x64 film with the box ticked was written by the software encoder, with the WARNING, which is the fallback seen for real. The proposed document 28 row, `EXPORT_VIDEO_ENCODER`, is not added.

D-231 / An export draws several frames at once / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-29, within the discretion the owner gave** ("sounds great! let's do 1 through 7 to your discretion."), because it is bit-exact: every file and every report is unchanged. **What it does.** An export used to draw one frame, write it and move on to the next. Now it draws a batch side by side across the machine's threads, then writes the batch strictly in frame order. The number of frames drawn at once is capped by memory: whatever fits in 2 GiB of 16-byte pixels, four buffers per frame, and never more than the drawing threads. That is 15 at 1920x1080 and 3 at 3840x2160 on the D-01 machine. PNG and EXR files are compressed inside the batch too. Each frame keeps its own notes, and they are replayed into the export's report in frame order, so the report says exactly what it said before. A stop is noticed before each frame is written, so a stopped export still holds only whole frames, numbered from the start with no gap. The pre-export block check runs in batches the same way. **Evidence.** `tests/b160_faster_export.rs` hashed every file and every report written by the reference shot (PNG 8-bit, PNG 16-bit, EXR half and float, GIF, animated PNG, MP4) and by all 2296 fixture projects (PNG and EXR half, every composition). It did this with the build before B-160 and with this one: 0 of 28684 changed. The MP4 is compared with its creation and modification dates set aside, because Windows stamps those into every MP4 it writes, so the old build's own MP4 differs from run to run. The same table shows 5 at once and the automatic number giving the same bytes as one at a time, for every format. **Speed (median of 7, D-01 machine, release build; measured again on 2026-09-30 with no other build running, turn about, three rounds, the median of the rounds).** For the whole reference shot, 240 frames at 1920x1080: PNG 8-bit went from 78341 ms to 11713 ms, about 6.7 times as fast, and MP4 from 19152 ms to 13285 ms. The MP4 is held back by its encoder, which takes frames one at a time. The new build told to draw one frame at a time took 78442 ms, the same as the old build; the 97411 ms first measured, beside other builds, was those builds, not a cost of batching.


D-232 / Decoded drawings kept on disk for the viewer (G15) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-29 under the owner's delegation ("let's add all of these as well into queue, but defer if not to our standard/to your discretion."), bit-exact; built B-161.** The first time the viewer decodes a PNG or other 8-bit drawing, the decoder's own bytes (8-bit sRGB straight RGBA, before any arithmetic) are also written to disk; a later miss for the same key, in this session or after a restart, reads them back instead of decoding the file and then runs the same colour conversion a decode runs. **Bit-exact:** `verification/B-161_decode_cache_table.md`, 23 of 23: 402 of 402 decodable fixture images, 56 of 56 reference-shot drawings, and 33,177,600 of 33,177,600 samples of four full reference frames in a first and a second session. **Scope:** preview only; `CelCache::none`, which export uses, never has a disk; EXR is not kept, as it decodes straight to floats. **Key:** document 27's, path, size, modified time, interpretation and a decoder version, hashed into the file name. **Location and cap:** from Preferences, by default a "decoded drawings" folder in the app's local data folder and 5 GB; 0 GB turns it off; least recently used copies go first. **Damage:** a copy failing its length, header or checksum is deleted, the drawing decoded fresh, and a line written to the session log. **Why 8-bit bytes, not the working floats:** the first build kept the floats, 16 bytes a pixel, and measured slower than decoding (49.0 ms against 44.5 ms a frame); flat anime PNGs unpack in about 2.3 ms, and reading 33 MB back took 7.5 ms. The 8-bit copy is a quarter of the size and skips only the unpacking. **Measured:** 24.3 ms against 35.4 ms a frame on the reference shot (69%), release build, 7 interleaved runs, median; measured again on 2026-09-30 at c9bf93e, median of three runs, no other cargo process or build running, driver 610.88 (the first, provisional figures, 32.3 against 45.0, were taken while other builds ran). Copies were read from Windows' file cache, and a cold read after a restart was not measured. **The owner's to change:** the 5 GB default and on-by-default.

D-233 / Serve only the newest viewer request (G16) and refine when idle (G9) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-29 under the owner's delegation ("let's add all of these as well into queue, but defer if not to our standard/to your discretion."), built B-162 and B-163.** Both are bit-exact: every final frame is byte for byte the frame the same request made before, Draft pixels are unchanged (D-99) and export is not touched. **G16.** The viewer keeps one frame request out and only the newest waiting behind it, as P-04 built. The frame in flight is always finished: the window answers frame requests one after another on its own thread and the renderer has no point at which to stop, so cancelling part way is not done. New: a Full picture that comes back while the hand is moving, with a newer frame already waiting, is not drawn; every other answer is drawn, a Draft one included, so the picture keeps up during a drag. **G9, "Refine when idle".** A viewer choice beside the Full/Draft button, kept with the window's preferences, on by default, doing nothing at Draft. At Full, a frame asked for by number within 200 ms of a seek, a drag of a layer or mask, or a live change of a value goes out at Draft; 200 ms after the hand stops the same frame is asked for at Full and replaces the stand-in, which shows "sharpening…" while on screen. Playback is not changed; layer outlines are asked for at the quality of the picture they are drawn over. **Evidence:** `verification/B-162_latest_request_table.md`, 17 of 17, and `verification/B-163_refine_on_stop_table.md`, 21 of 21, from `latest_request_and_refine` in `app/src/main.rs`, which runs the page's own decision lines under Node on a pretend clock and asks the real request handler for the requests that came out. **Not done:** cancelling a render part way, which would need the frame address answered off the window's thread and stopping points in the renderer.

D-234 / One 3D colour table for a stack of colour effects, preview only / **DECLINED on 2026-09-29 by the owner ("decline 234, accept 235")**: nothing is built and no pixel changes; G13's same-answer fusion goes ahead. Proposed by the agent the same day, as the deferred half of G13 (the owner's "defer if not to our standard/to your discretion", 2026-09-29). **The proposal.** A drawing's run of per-pixel colour effects (Curves, Levels, Hue/Saturation, Brightness/Contrast, Tint and the like) is one function of the pixel's encoded straight colour, because the linear round trip between two of them is the identity on a held value. The viewer would sample that function on an N by N by N grid of encoded colours and read each pixel back by `core.color_lookup`'s trilinear rule (D-182's `.cube` rule), rebuilding the table when a setting changes; export would keep the exact chain. **What was measured.** `tools/d234_lut_collapse_experiment.py`, its vectorised effects checked against the curves, levels, hue_saturation, brightness_contrast and cube_lut reference tools first (Tint from `src/effects.rs`), on the reference frame `verification/B-05a_reference_frame.png` and on all 16,777,216 8-bit colours, as the viewer shows them in 8-bit sRGB. A mild five-effect grade: grid 17 worst 9 levels on the frame (11 over all colours), 21.8% of pixels off by more than 1, PSNR 48.8 dB; grid 33 worst 5 (6), 2.8%, 56.1 dB; grid 65 worst 3 (3), 0.18%, 60.4 dB. A hard grade: 17 worst 27 (38), 27.3%, 42.0 dB; 33 worst 14 (18), 10.6%, 49.0 dB; 65 worst 8 (12), 1.6%, 58.6 dB. Each effect alone over all colours: Curves, Levels and Tint within 1 level at 33 and 65, Brightness/Contrast at 65 only, Hue/Saturation up to 5 (mild) and 21 (hard) levels even at 65; the hard grade without Hue/Saturation is still 2 levels off at 65. **No grid meets the accepted 1 level.** **Speed, an estimate by operation counts, not a timing:** about 700 operations a pixel for the five-effect chain against about 170 for the table, some 4 times; but G13's fusion of the same maths into one pass, which changes no pixels, already removes most of the repeated sRGB round trips, leaving the table about 2 times ahead of it. The table costs 35,937 chain evaluations to build at 33 (about 2% of a 1920 by 1080 frame) and 274,625 at 65 (about 13%). **Recommendation: decline for now**, build G13 and measure; reopen only if a colour stack is still slow after it. **For the owner:** (1) decline for now (recommended); (2) a table used only where a check over every colour finds it within 1 level, preview only, off by default, at about 8 frames' work per setting change; (3) the 65 table as it is, preview only, off by default, accepting up to about 12 levels off in the viewer on hard grades. **The evidence.** `verification/D-234 proposal/` (`proposal.md`, the side-by-side pictures exact / table / difference x32 for both grades at 17, 33 and 65, `experiment_output.txt`). **If declined,** nothing is built and no pixel changes.

D-235 / Large Gaussian Blur, Glow and Bloom worked at a reduced size and enlarged, preview only / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-29 by the owner ("decline 234, accept 235")**, the recommended option (1): the safety rule, on in the viewer, exports exact; **built as B-164 on 2026-09-29 with the changes D-221 records, every check within 1 level**; left off until the blur, glow and bloom fixtures and the reference frame pass within 1 level on the card. Proposed by the agent the same day, as the deferred half of G14 (the owner's "defer if not to our standard/to your discretion", 2026-09-29). **The proposal.** In the viewer, a Gaussian blur of sigma s (Gaussian Blur's own blur, Glow's at radius / 3, each of Bloom's four) may be worked by averaging f by f blocks (f = 2, 4 or 8), blurring the small picture at sqrt(s^2 - (f^2 - 1) / 12 - f^2 / 6) / f, which takes out the blur the shrinking and enlarging add, and enlarging it back bilinearly from pixel centres, outside the layer transparent as document 21 has it. **The safety rule:** f is halved, down to 1 (exact), until the small sigma is at least 6. Export keeps document 21's exact blur. **What was measured.** `tools/d235_downsample_blur_experiment.py`, its exact blur checked against `tools/adjust_reference.py`'s first, on `verification/B-05a_reference_frame.png` at 1920 by 1080, Glow and Bloom at their default thresholds and intensity 1, Bloom's streaks off, as the viewer shows the frame over black in 8-bit sRGB; sizes 20, 50, 100, 200 (Gaussian Blur's sigma, Glow's and Bloom's radius), factors 2, 4, 8. The plain shortcut, always at the factor asked, breaks 1 level at small sizes: Gaussian Blur 20 at factor 8, 3 levels; Glow 20 at 2, 4, 8: 3, 7, 18 levels (12.7% of pixels, 50.4 dB at 8); Glow 50 at 4 and 8: 2 and 4; Glow 100 at 8: 2; Bloom 20 at 2, 4, 8: 8, 30, 60 levels (28.2%, 35.0 dB at 8); Bloom 50: 3, 9, 22; Bloom 100 at 4 and 8: 2 and 10; Bloom 200 at 8: 3. Every other case is within 1 level with 0% of pixels off by more, PSNR 59.4 to 76.8 dB. So "above radius 50, factor 2" alone is not safe (Bloom 50 at factor 2 is 3 levels). **With the safety rule** every case measured is within 1 level with no pixel off by more: Gaussian Blur 50, 100, 200 at factor 8, 61.6 to 68.7 dB; Glow 50 at 2, 100 at 4, 200 at 8; Bloom 200 at 8/4/2/1 across its four blurs, 69.9 dB; Glow and Bloom at 20 stay exact. Guards of 2 and 4 each left cases 2 to 3 levels off. **Speed, an estimate by counts of multiply-adds per pixel, not a timing:** with the rule and factor up to 8, Gaussian Blur about 7x at 20, 97x at 50, 162x at 100, 247x at 200; Glow 1x, 6.6x, 35x, 122x; Bloom 1x, 1.8x, 3.8x, 10x. Real gains will be smaller where memory rather than arithmetic sets the pace, as on the card. **Recommendation: accept with the safety rule, viewer only, exports exact,** built with the blur, glow and bloom fixtures and this frame as its checks and left off until they pass on the card; one frame was tested, and a picture with harder bright edges may find a case it did not. **For the owner:** (1) accept with the safety rule, on in the viewer (recommended); (2) the same behind a viewer switch off by default; (3) only while playing or scrubbing, the exact frame replacing it on stop (with G9); (4) decline. **The evidence.** `verification/D-235 proposal/` (`proposal.md`, side-by-side pictures exact / shortcut / difference x16 for each effect at 20 factor 8, 50 factor 2, 100 factor 4 and 200 factor 8 plain, and 200 factor 8 with the rule, `experiment_output.txt`). **If declined,** nothing is built and big blurs stay exact and as slow as today.

D-240 / Kaleidoscope on the card, whose only differences are in pixels no one can see / **DECIDED on 2026-09-30 by the owner ("proceed with your recommended actions based on this"): option 1, Kaleidoscope stays on the processor.** Proposed on 2026-09-29 by the agent, from B-151 (D-217). **What was found.** Kaleidoscope was built on the card with the other ten of D-217 and failed its check on four fixtures: FX-KALEIDO 002, 003, 005 and 010 have one to four pixels a frame up to 246 levels of 255 apart. Every one is a pixel on an exact mirror line whose see-through value is below half a level: the card's sine and cosine differ from the processor's in the last binary place, the sample then lands a hair from the fully clear pixel beside it, and the pixel's coverage becomes about a millionth rather than none. The page's eight-bit picture carries straight colour, so the hidden colour of a pixel that is 0 of 255 visible is compared too, and there it is anything. Laid over anything, such a pixel moves the picture by less than half a level. It cannot be made bit-exact: the card has no sine that matches the processor's. D-217's rule is never to widen a tolerance to make a table pass, so Kaleidoscope stays on the processor, as today. **For the owner:** (1) keep Kaleidoscope on the processor (current; recommended until the viewer is slow on it); (2) change the card check so that a pixel both sides show as 0 of 255 visible compares as equal whatever its hidden colour, and put Kaleidoscope on the card; (3) have the page conversion write black for a pixel 0 of 255 visible, on both paths, then put it on the card; this changes the page's bytes for clear pixels but nothing seen. **The code** is saved outside the repository and is not added. Nothing changes; options 2 and 3 can be revisited if the viewer is ever slow on Kaleidoscope.

D-241 / The layers below an edit kept by the viewer (GPU plan G10, change-aware re-render) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-30 under the owner's delegation of 2026-09-29 ("sounds great! let's do 1 through 7 to your discretion."; G10 added to the queue "to your discretion"): every picture byte for byte what a viewer that keeps nothing draws; exports untouched; built B-159.** The processor drew every layer of a frame again after any edit, however high the layer edited. **What was built.** The viewer's cache (`CelCache::below`, the viewer's only, as it is the only one with an effect budget) holds `render::Below`: the plan it last drew for one frame, and one picture, the frame as it stood below one layer. `render::render_below` compares the new plan's layers with the last, bottom first: the same drawing (the very buffer, which is held, so it cannot have been written on or its memory used again), the same map, opacity, matte and motion-blur moments to the bit, and the same blend mode, adjustment effects, Light Wrap and card effects. When the picture kept lies below a layer and every layer under it is still the same, the frame starts from a copy of it and only the layers above are drawn; each layer is laid on what is beneath it, pixel by pixel, in order, so where the drawing starts changes nothing but the clock (the same fact D-66 and B-158 rest on). The picture kept for next time is the one below the lowest layer that differs; when nothing is kept and the bottom layer differs, as when one edit is taken back and another layer is edited, the one below the next layer up that differs. It is forgotten when another frame or composition is drawn, and not used for a frame of another size, tile or part. A layer whose drawing is made afresh for every plan (an adjustment layer's white, a motion-blur average made on the processor) never compares the same, so an edit above one starts no higher than it: correct, and a smaller saving. Document 27 has the entry. **The check** (`verification/B-159_below_table.md`, `tests/b159_below.rs`): each layer of the reference shot, as it is and with an adjustment layer, a Light Wrap, motion blur and effects, edited in turn three ways (opacity 80%, 60%, moved), at Full and Draft, frames 0 and 100, whole and the middle quarter (B-158), compared bit for bit with a viewer that keeps nothing, and the next frame after must not start from anything kept: **544 of 544 pass** (288 before, c916d8a, every picture the same and none started from anything kept). **Timing** (`verification/B-159_timing_table.md`, frame 10, one layer's opacity 80% and 60% by turns, the median of three runs, on the processor): at Full, the reference shot's top layer 11.2 to 7.2 ms a frame and the declared ten-layer fixture's top layer 24.5 to 7.6, its middle layer 23.8 to 14.9, its second from the bottom 24.0 to 22.4; at Draft, 7.9 to 4.1 for the ten-layer top layer. The card draws as before. The checks-first commit, c916d8a, failed as it should. The playtest sheet is `verification/B-159_playtest.md`.

D-242 / A held masked drawing kept by the viewer (GPU plan G11, the card-side result across holds) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-30 under the owner's delegation of 2026-09-29 ("sounds great! let's do 1 through 7 to your discretion."; G11 added to the queue "to your discretion"): every picture byte for byte what a viewer that keeps nothing draws; exports untouched; built B-170.** G11 asked for each layer's finished card result to be kept across holds. Most of that already existed: the card keeps a drawing it was sent while the drawing is held (B-46), and the results of its effects while their settings are unchanged (B-153, B-155), and G11's probe found no drawing sent again on a held frame of an unmasked layer, with or without effects. The gap was the mask. A masked layer's drawing was masked again on the processor on every frame, into a new copy, and the card, finding a drawing it had not seen, was sent it again: a held frame of the reference shot with one masked layer took 20.5 to 2.3 ms at Full on the card. **What was built.** In `compose::resolve_rest` the effect cache (P-11), which is keyed on the drawing, the masks drawn (their shape at the frame), the effects the processor runs and the draft divisor, is now asked before the mask is drawn rather than after, and is asked for a masked drawing whose effects are all the card's or which has none. A hit is the masked drawing itself, the same buffer each held frame, so no mask is drawn and the card finds the drawing it already holds. The key is unchanged, so what it hands back is what the mask and stack would have made; only the viewer's cache has an effect budget, so an export never uses it. Document 27 has the note. **The check** (`verification/B-170_held_table.md`, `tests/b170_held.rs`): the reference shot held on twos with its second layer masked, alone, with a Gaussian Blur and with an Exposure, Full and Draft, frames 0 to 11 through one viewer on the card: every frame bit for bit a viewer that keeps nothing, and on every held frame no mask drawn and no drawing sent: **72 of 72 pass** (36 before, f1e02d3, every held frame masking again, even where the effect cache then threw that work away, and the mask alone at either quality or with a blur at Full sending the drawing again). **Timing** (`verification/B-170_timing_table.md`, the median of three runs, on the card): a held frame with the mask alone 20.5 to 2.3 ms at Full and 18.4 to 0.7 at Draft; with a blur 21.4 to 2.3 at Full; with an Exposure 21.9 to 2.2 at Full. A frame with a new drawing costs what it did. A shape or text layer, drawn afresh each frame, is still sent each frame: not in scope here. The checks-first commit, f1e02d3, failed as it should. The playtest sheet is `verification/B-170_playtest.md`.

D-243 / A composition inside another kept by the viewer, in memory and on disk (GPU plan G12) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-30 under the owner's delegation of 2026-09-29 ("sounds great! let's do 1 through 7 to your discretion."; G12 added to the queue "to your discretion"): every picture byte for byte the export's; exports untouched; built B-171.** G12 asked for an automatic disk cache of heavy precomps that survives restarts, keyed per document 27, with a Preferences size and location, bit-exact for the preview only. Before it, `compose.rs` drew a composition layer's inner frame every time it was asked for (its own ponytail note named this cache as the upgrade): on every outer frame, after every outer edit, and again after a restart, with only the drawings and their effect results kept. **What was built.** The viewer's `CelCache` keeps each inner frame it draws (`inner_frame`, `store_inner`), under a key of everything the frame is drawn from other than files, compared whole as text: this build of the program (its file's path, length and time), the drawings' folder, the quality, the inner frame number, every composition the inner one can reach, and every asset, as they stand. The files it read (drawings, colour tables, the missing-media checks) are recorded with their length and time as it is drawn, as B-154's finished frames are, and looked at again before a kept frame is used; any change draws it again. A frame that said anything (a warning or error inside) is not kept, so a kept frame says nothing, as the frame it replaces said nothing; a composition that reaches one it is drawn inside is not kept. **Memory:** under the viewer's effect budget, beside the effect results, both let go least recently used first. **Disk:** the same folder and cap as B-161's decoded drawings (Preferences, now "Drawings and compositions on disk"; no new setting), a `.frame` file named by the key's SHA-256 and holding the whole key, the file list and the working-space floats, each checked by checksum, written whole or not at all, and deleted when it fails a check (session log `FRAME_CACHE_DISCARDED`). A frame goes to disk only when drawing it took longer than reading it back would (2 GB a second: 16.6 ms at Full, 4.1 ms at Draft), so light compositions are kept in memory only. Export holds no effect budget and never reads or writes either (ADR-015). **Pre-render:** the existing render-ahead during playback (B-154) fills it; a pre-render while the window is idle is not built. **The check** (`verification/B-171_precomp_table.md`, `tests/b171_precomp.rs`): the reference shot with two blurs inside an outer composition, Full and Draft, frames 0, 1 and 100: drawn again, drawn by a new viewer with the same folder, and with the outer layer edited, the inner composition is not drawn; with an inner layer edited or its drawing files dated anew, it is; every frame bit for bit the export's: **42 of 42 pass** (18 before, e145371). **Timing** (`verification/B-171_timing_table.md`, median of three runs, on the card, Automatic memory): at Full, played again 16.1 to 2.0 ms a frame, outer layer edited 15.8 to 1.9, program opened again 31.8 to 13.5; at Draft 5.0 to 0.3, 5.4 to 0.3 and 15.2 to 1.6. The first play at Full costs the disk writes, 40.5 to 46.7 ms (writes are in the frame; moving them to a worker is the upgrade if it matters). Document 27 has the entry. The playtest sheet is `verification/B-171_playtest.md`.
D-244 / Runs of colour effects drawn in one card pass (GPU plan G13) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-30 under the owner's delegation of 2026-09-29 ("sounds great! let's do 1 through 7 to your discretion."; G13 added to the queue "to your discretion", its table half declined in D-234): every picture byte for byte what it was; exports untouched; built B-172.** G13 asked for adjacent per-pixel colour effects fused into one card pass, the same maths in the same order, built only if the fixtures stay within today's 1 level. Before it, each of the card's 23 colour effects that reads only its own pixel (Curves, Levels, Hue/Saturation, Gradient, Noise, Exposure Flicker, Color Balance, Gradient Map, Vignette, Fractal Noise, Invert, Brightness & Contrast, Black & White, Posterize, Threshold, Channel Mixer, Vibrance, Leave Color, Solarize, Halftone, Color Lookup, HSV Key, Paraffin) was a pass of its own, writing the whole drawing to a texture and the next reading it back. **What was built.** `src/gpu.rs`: a `chain` pass made from the `grade` and `tone` shaders' own text at start-up (`chain_shader`), each shader's body turned into a function of the pixel with its settings read at an offset, and one entry point that walks a table of the run's effects in order. `Gpu::run` gathers each run of two or more such effects next to each other on a layer (`one_pixel`), prepares each exactly as before (`Gpu::fx`, which now only notes the settings for a run) and draws the run in one pass. A pixel goes from one effect to the next as a 32-bit float, as the texture between them held it, so nothing is rounded differently. The card keeps no picture inside a run; when a setting inside a run changes, the run is cut there, the part before it kept, so the next change draws only the rest. **The check** (`verification/B-172_fused_table.md`, `tests/b172_fused.rs`): three shots with every one of the 23 in runs, broken by blurs, an Offset and a Drop Shadow, and begun by Paraffin and HSV Key, at Full and Draft, five frames each drawn from nothing, plus a setting in the middle of a run changed four times through one viewer: **38 of 38 frames byte for byte the same as one pass each, all 38 in fewer passes** (30 of 30 the same and 0 fewer before, 4c35018). **Timing** (`verification/B-172_timing_table.md`, median of three runs, on the card): a Noise then eight colour effects on three layers at Full 43.1 to 33.6 ms a frame (31 card passes to 7), at Draft 14.5 to 12.9; a slider on the fifth of the eight dragged, Full 14.1 to 13.1, Draft 5.8 to 4.9. The first build drew a whole run again for a change inside it (22.6 ms at Full); cutting the run at the change removed that. The playtest sheet is `verification/B-172_playtest.md`.
D-245 / Composition frames written to disk by a worker (GPU plan G12, follow-up) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-30 under the owner's delegation of 2026-09-29 ("sounds great! let's do 1 through 7 to your discretion."; G12 added to the queue "to your discretion"): every copy on disk byte for byte what B-171 wrote and every picture byte for byte the export's; exports untouched; built B-171b.** B-171 (D-243) wrote each kept composition frame's `.frame` copy inside the frame, so the first play of the heavy precomp at Full measured 55.1 ms a frame against 34.8 before B-171 on the same day (40.5 in B-171's own table), a known regression. **What was built.** `src/cache.rs`: one worker thread for the process (`writer`) takes each copy from `store_inner` and writes it with B-161's unchanged `store_frame` (its checksums in a one-thread pool of its own, which gives the same sums); the frame goes on at once. At most eight copies wait (265 MB at Full); a frame kept while eight wait is kept in memory only, rather than the frame waiting for the disk. A viewer asking for a frame whose copy is still on its way waits for that copy (`written`), and `disk_writes_done` waits for all of them. A copy the worker cannot write is noted FRAME_CACHE_NOT_WRITTEN in the viewer's session log as before, on a later frame. A copy still queued when the program closes is not written; one half written is left as a `.part`, never read, and deleted after an hour as before. **The check** (`verification/B-171b_background_table.md`, `tests/b171b_background.rs`): a full-size composition frame kept, keeping returns before its copy is on disk, a new viewer asking at once gets it back bit for bit, and the one copy is laid out byte for byte as B-171 wrote it: **3 of 3 pass** (2 of 3 before, 6d8f042); B-171's table, waiting for the writes before counting copies, still 42 of 42. **Timing** (`verification/B-171b_timing_table.md`, median of three runs, on the card, B-171's method): first play at Full 34.8 ms before B-171, 55.1 with B-171, **27.5** now; at Draft 18.1, 19.5, 17.0; played again, outer layer edited and program opened again as B-171 made them (Full 2.0, 1.9, 13.0). The playtest sheet is `verification/B-171b_playtest.md`.

D-246 / The card keeps the picture of each run it has drawn (GPU plan follow-up, B-173) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-09-30 under the owner's delegation of 2026-09-29 ("sounds great! let's do 1 through 7 to your discretion."; B-173 asked for as "fix the confirmed slowdowns rather than just recording them"): a frame asked for again gets byte for byte the picture the card drew for it the first time, every picture within 1 level of 255 of the processor's, the tolerance already accepted for the card; exports untouched; Draft pixels unchanged; built B-173.** The quiet re-measure of 2026-09-30 (898e398) confirmed slowdowns in the viewer against the build before their unit. At Draft, a layer whose first effect moves was slower with B-155, 12.2 ms a frame before it against 12.9. With B-151, Snowfall and Roughen Edges played again were slower (12.2 to 13.4 and 12.1 to 12.7), and Optics Compensation at Draft and Bevel Alpha at Full slightly so. **The cause.** The card kept only the last run drawn on each layer, with its settings. A layer whose effects move has different settings on every frame, so playing the shot again drew every run afresh, while the processor's frame cache (B-151 left those effects to the card) had given such frames back without drawing. **What was built.** `src/gpu.rs`: each layer kept on the card also keeps the last picture of earlier runs, each under the full list of effects and settings that made it (`Stored::before`). A frame asked for again with the very same settings gets that picture back and runs no effect pass. The kept pictures are limited to a quarter of the card memory the program allows itself (half the card's), the least recently used going first, and a picture let go returns to the working textures. **Rejected on measurement: sending moving effects at Draft to the processor.** This was the directive's first suggestion, and its check was committed first (ac27796). It made first plays much slower, Turbulent Displace 12.7 to 29.5 ms and a keyed Bloom 19.4 to 76.1, so the guard ("make the rule narrower") ruled it out. The check was revised to the present rule before the code (484969d). **The check** (`verification/B-173_draft_moving_table.md`, `tests/b173_draft_moving.rs`): each of the twelve effects the card draws that move by themselves, three keyed ones and B-155's moving Noise first, on the reference shot's first three layers, at Draft and Full. Frame 0 asked for again after frame 100 must run no effect pass and give back every byte of its first picture. **34 of 34 pass** (2 of 34 before, 484969d). Every frame drawn is within 1 level of the processor's, 68 of 68. B-172's table: 38 of 38, a changed setting drawn a third time now takes 4 passes where it took 7. B-153's table: the second time through still makes no new memory, while the first time through makes about twice as many pieces (48 against 20), since kept pictures leave the working textures. **Timing** (`verification/B-173_timing_table.md`, median of six or nine alternating rounds against the build before each unit, with nothing else running, same method). The directive's rows: moving Noise first at Draft 12.2 before B-155, 11.9 now; Snowfall at Draft played again 12.2 before B-151, 12.0 now; Roughen Edges 12.1 and 12.2, inside the runs' spread of 11.7 to 12.9; Optics Compensation 12.1 and 12.1; Bevel Alpha at Full 11.3 and 10.9. Every moving shot played again at Draft now takes 11.6 to 12.3 ms, where before B-173 it took up to 18.3, and the processor takes 12.2 to 13.0. The first time through costs about 0.3 to 0.5 ms a frame more, measured inside one build with keeping switched on and off. **The guard.** None of these rows became slower: B-164's big blurs at Draft (within 0.2 ms or faster over nine rounds), B-156's adjustment layers, B-152's motion blur (with Roughen Edges at Full 17.6 to 12.3) and B-172. B-157's and B-164's timing tests clear the card before every frame, so no picture is kept there (a count found 0), and their scattered Full and single-effect differences in both directions are the machine's. **Noted, not B-173's:** B-151's processor rows at Full measured 1.0 to 1.6 ms slower than before B-151, but equal against 898e398, so the change lies between those builds and has not been looked for. The playtest sheet is `verification/B-173_playtest.md`.

D-249 / The ready frames: a green line under the ruler and a count beside the time / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-02 by the owner** ("I accept"). The answer is the frames of the composition on screen that the frame memory (B-154, D-223) holds for exactly what is on screen now: the project as shown (with solo), the quality, and the processor a frame asked for now would be made with; with the bytes the memory holds and the Preferences memory setting. A ready frame is one the viewer would send from memory at once. The timeline draws them as a green line under the ruler, in runs, and writes "N of M ready" beside the time, N counting the ready frames inside the work area and M the work area's length, as the Sandbox has it (`design/W-38_sandbox/`). Hovering the count says the memory used of the setting. The page asks again, at most four times a second, while frames arrive, and after a stop or an edit. **Its limits, stated:** (1) any edit empties the line and undo brings it back, because the memory keeps frames by the whole project (B-154); the Sandbox's tip "an edit clears the frames it changes" is therefore not what this build does, and the tip will say "an edit clears the line" instead. Keeping the frames an edit cannot change would be its own decision. (2) Ready does not look at the disk, so a drawing replaced outside the app leaves its frames green until each is shown, when it is made again (the picture is never stale, B-154's check). (4) Part-frames made zoomed in (B-158) are not kept, so they are not ready. **The check, first:** `verification/W-40c_ready_frames_table.md`, written by `w40c_ready_frames_are_the_ones_memory_would_send`, against a stub that says nothing is ready: 16 rows, 5 pass before the build. **No command, shortcut, fixture, project file or exported picture changes by this decision**; document 24 gains the line and the count when it is built.

This replaces B-19d's ceiling "the grey lines share the edited property's scale" and changes only the page. **(4) A running render is watched in the Render workspace**, reached from the top bar's export task, as W-45 built it; no popup or own window. **(5) No text tool.** Ctrl+T stays the free-transform box (D-81, D-248) unless the owner asks for text layers.
