D-348 / Pass Extract and Depth Key, the depth and normals a render saves in an EXR file, after After Effects' 3D Channel Extract and Depth Matte (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md` P0-5) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-08 under the owner's /loop request ("Take the first non-done row ... using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar. Add one regression test ... and one perf measurement"): within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-228.** P0-5 had no way to read anything but colour and alpha from an EXR. **What was built.** `exr_io::read_pass` reads one pass, the depth or the normals, from the file a layer is drawn from, by the naming rules of document 21's Pass Extract paragraph (depth: `Z`, `depth.Z`, `zdepth.Z`, `depth`, `zdepth`, case ignored; normals: layer `N`, `normal` or `normals` with parts x/y/z or R/G/B); it lies as the colour does (D-62); not-a-number reads as 0 and an infinity as the largest single-precision number, said every frame as `MEDIA_EXR_ADJUSTED`. `CelCache::pass` keeps it beside the cel, uncounted. `compose::fill_passes` hands it to the two effects each frame, stretched to the drawing at Draft; it is never saved (persist writes the settings only). `core.pass_extract` (Pass Extract): pass depth or normals, Black Point, White Point (-1,000,000..1,000,000, keyable), Invert, Clamp; starting at depth, 0, 1, off, on. `core.depth_key` (Depth Key): Depth, Feather (0..1,000,000, same units), Invert; starting at 0, 0, off. Both on the card (`passx`, `dkey` in `src/gpu.rs`, the pass through `map_texture`); the app's new **3D Channel** group. A layer with no pass (not an EXR, no such channels, a solid, shape, text, composition or adjustment layer, mixed frames) draws without the effect, its settings kept, and says the new `EFFECT_CHANNEL_MISSING` (document 28) every frame. **Evidence.** Fixtures first (0119346, FX-DEPTH-001 to 036, `tools/depth_channel_reference.py`, OpenEXR's own library); `verification/D-348_depth_channels_table.md` 343 of 343 checks; the card within 1 level of the processor on 204 frames (every valid fixture and the sample render with 8 settings, Full and Draft); timing `verification/B-228_depth_channels_timing_table.md`: one 1920 by 1080 EXR layer then a moving Noise, 2.1 ms a frame without, 2.1 with Pass Extract (depth or normals), 2.4 with Depth Key. **Deviations from After Effects.** Black and White start at 0 and 1, not 5000 and 0 (those are for After Effects' own 3D layers); only the depth and normals are read. **Gaps from the tutorials, logged, not worked round:** depth from a nested composition's own 3D layers; Depth Matte's Antialias; the Info panel's depth readout; RLA and RPF files; object ID, material ID, UV, coverage, background and unclamped passes (3D Channel Extract's other choices); EXR files with no plain R, G, B (Blender multilayer) are still refused on import; on import the footage still lists Z and N.* among the channels it ignores for the colour.

D-349 / ID Key, object and material ids, named channels and Blender's multilayer EXR files, after After Effects' ID Matte and EXtractoR (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md` P0-5, part 2) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-08 under the owner's /loop request ("Take the first non-done row ... using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar. Add one regression test ... and one perf measurement"): within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-229.** D-348 left P0-5 partial: no ids, no other named channel, Blender's files refused, and the import note calling the depth and normals ignored. **What was built**, through D-348's one route (`exr_io::read_pass`, `CelCache::pass`, `compose::fill_passes`), whose pass is now `exr_io::Pass` (depth, normals, object id, material id, or a channel named): a layer is matched by its last dotted word, so `ViewLayer.Depth.Z` is a depth; the object id is a channel whose layer (or name) is `IndexOB`, `ObjectID`, `objid`, `ObjectIndex` or `VRayObjectID`, the material id `IndexMA`, `MaterialID`, `matid`, `mtlid`, `MaterialIndex` or `VRayMtlID` (case, `_`, `-` and spaces ignored); a named pass is one name or three, exact. Pass Extract's `pass` gains `object_id`, `material_id` and `named` with a word `channel` (left out of the file while empty). `core.id_key` (ID Key): Aux. Channel (object or material), ID Selection (0..1,000,000, keyable), Feather (0..100 px, keyable), Invert; starting at object, 0, 0, off; m = 1 where |id - v| < 1/2, feathered by Gaussian Blur's kernel with its edges held, the drawing times m; on the card (`idkey` in `src/gpu.rs`, the feather through the bloom passes); a draft reads the ids nearest-neighbour. **Blender's files**: with no R, G, B or Y channel, the colour is `Composite.Combined` if present, else the first `<layer>.Combined` in the file's order; the others are listed as ignored. **The import note** (`MEDIA_EXR_ADJUSTED`, `channels_ignored`) no longer lists the depth, normals or ids an effect reads; this changes one expected value written before it, FX-EXR-003's `channels/extra.exr` (Z dropped from its list), a specification change made here at the owner's request (item 4 of the unit) and re-pinned by `tools/exr_reference.py` in the fixtures commit. **Evidence.** Fixtures first (b62d004, FX-DEPTH-037 to 064, three FX-EXR-003 files); `verification/D-349_id_key_table.md` 245 of 245 checks; the card within 1 level of the processor on 132 frames (every valid fixture and the Blender-style sample with 9 settings, Full and Draft; all 0 levels); timing `verification/B-229_id_key_timing_table.md`: one 1920 by 1080 Blender-style EXR layer then a moving Noise, 2.1 ms a frame without, 1.9 with ID Key, 1.9 with ID Key feathered 3, 2.1 with Pass Extract of the object ids. **Deviations from After Effects.** ID Matte's feather is not documented; ours is a Gaussian of sigma Feather pixels. **The Blender layer rule is ours** (Composite, else the first): the owner may prefer a setting; it is recorded here, not proposed, because it changes no picture that was drawn before (such files were refused). **Gaps from the tutorials, logged, not worked round:** Cryptomatte's hashed ids (P0-5 is done except that decoding); IDentifier; ID Matte's Use Coverage (RLA/RPF only) and clicking the picture to pick an id; RLA and RPF files; EXtractoR's alpha channel and UnMult; choosing another Blender view layer; multiview (stereo) EXR files.

D-350 / Text Animator, after After Effects' text animators and Range Selector (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md` P0-7, part 1) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-08 under the owner's /loop request ("Take the first non-done row ... using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar. Add one regression test ... and one perf measurement"): every number held to the reference within 1e-6 and every outline box within 0.25 pixel, D-263's own tolerance; the card within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-230.** D-263..D-266 drew words, styles, a box and a shadow, but no letter could move on its own. **What was built**: `core.text_animator` (Text Animator, in a new Text group), an effect on a text layer: Position (two numbers, pixels), Scale (two, per cent), Rotation (degrees, clockwise, about the letter's foot), Opacity, Fill Color (Off or On, linear RGB) and Tracking Amount (thousandths of the size); its Range Selector, Start and End (0..100), Offset (-100..100), Amount (-100..100), Based On (Characters, Characters Excluding Spaces, Words), Shape (Square, Ramp Up, Ramp Down, Triangle, Round, Smooth), Smoothness (Square only) and Ease High and Low (0..100, through document 20's ease curve); starting at rest, the whole line picked, Square, so a changed property acts on every letter until Start or End moves. Each letter's amount is its picked share times Amount; several animators add up, top first. Every number is keyable (D-68) and the one-number settings take expressions (D-291). The animator acts while the letters are laid out (`text::animated`), so it has no picture to mix: its Mix is a plain 100, as Posterize Time's (D-202); an invalid one is kept and left out with `EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID`, the words drawn as without it; on a layer that is not text, `TEXT_ANIMATOR_NO_TEXT` (new in document 28) every frame. With no animator the words are drawn byte for byte as before (d263 and d264's pinned pictures). A keyed `start` or `end` is read as one number: before this, a keyed setting of that name was always read as Gradient's two-number point, and a text animator's keyed Start would have been refused on opening (`persist::effect_tracks`, guarded by the record's own `base`). **Card and processor.** The letters stay outlines filled on the processor, as D-263's are; there is no per-pixel work in the animator to move, and the effects after it run on the card as before (b155 rerun, no `GPU_PREVIEW_ON_CPU`). **Evidence.** Fixtures first (ff6daa7, FX-TXA-001 to 013 per character and FX-TXA-020 to 023 as projects, `tools/text_animator_reference.py`, which reads the font with fontTools and draws its stored outline points); `verification/D-350_text_animator_table.md` 61 of 61 checks (worst box 0.120 pixel, worst number 1.2e-12), the card at 0 levels from the processor on six frames; timing `verification/B-230_text_animator_timing_table.md`: FX-TXA-011's 30-character line with two animators (a wave and a fade by character, Offsets keyed so every frame is new) in a 1920 by 1080 composition, medians of three rounds on a quiet machine: the processor's drawing of the line 0.8 ms a frame without animators and 4.1 with the two; the viewer's whole frame with the two, Full, Draw on: GPU, 16.7 first and 18.3 played again. **Deviations from After Effects.** Each letter turns and scales about its foot halfway across its advance (After Effects' Anchor Point Grouping by character, its default, with no Grouping Alignment); Ease High and Low do not go below 0; one Range Selector per animator, in per cent. **Gaps from the tutorials, logged, not worked round:** the Wiggly and Expression selectors; more than one selector on an animator and a selector's Mode; Randomize Order; Units by index and Based On Lines; Ease below 0; per-character 3D and per-character motion blur; Anchor Point Grouping and Grouping Alignment; expressions on Position, Scale and Fill Color (two- and three-number settings take none, D-291); Source Text expressions. Shaping of joined scripts is the rest of P0-7.

D-351 / Whole-picture statistics, and Stretch Levels, Stretch Contrast, Stretch Color and Spread Tones, after After Effects' Auto Levels, Auto Contrast, Auto Color and Equalize (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md` P0-15) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-08 under the owner's /loop request ("Take the first non-done row ... using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar. Add one regression test ... and one perf measurement"): every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; drawn on the processor, so no card tolerance applies; no new tolerance; built B-231.** P0-15 had no reduction over a picture at all. **What was built.** `src/frame_stats.rs`: red, green, blue and brightness histograms (256 bins, on the sRGB-encoded straight colour, each pixel weighted by its covering) of the layer's whole picture at the effect's place in its stack, each brightness bin's colour and the average colour, summed in fixed 64-row blocks in order, so neither threads, tiles (B-07) nor the viewer's part (B-158) change it. Four effects read it, in the Color Correction group: `core.stretch_levels` (each channel to its own clipped darkest and lightest), `core.stretch_contrast` (one stretch from the three channels' histogram together), `core.stretch_color` (the colours of the brightness histogram's clipped ends to black and white; Snap Neutral Midtones takes the average colour to grey by a power on each channel), with Temporal Smoothing (0..10 seconds), Scene Detect, Black Clip and White Clip (0..10 per cent, 0.1 when added), every number keyable; and `core.spread_tones` (Equalize: RGB, Brightness or Photoshop Style; Amount to Equalize 0..100). Blend With Original is the Mix every effect already has (D-202), 100 less it. **Temporal smoothing** reuses Echo's route (D-195): `compose::fill_stats` resolves the layer at each frame around with the effects before this one, counts each, stops a side at a scene change when Scene Detect is on (half the brightness histogram's difference, fixed), and adds them, each over its own total; the sum is handed to the effect and never saved, and the effect cache sees it. On an adjustment layer the frames beneath at other times are not to hand, so smoothing there is not drawn: each frame is stretched alone and the new `TEMPORAL_SMOOTHING_SKIPPED` (document 28) is said every frame. The rule is document 21's whole-picture statistics paragraph. **Evidence.** Fixtures first (b1e517a, FX-AUTO-001 to 032, `tools/auto_tone_reference.py`, numpy, never the build's code); `verification/D-351_auto_tone_table.md` 146 of 146 checks (all 32 cases, largest difference 4.1e-7; files saved as read; tiles of 1 and 64 byte-identical; the middle quarter drawn alone byte-identical to the whole frame's); timing `verification/B-231_auto_tone_timing_table.md`, the reference shot with the effect on three layers then a moving Noise, Full, Draw on: GPU, median of three rounds: 16.1 ms first and 12.3 played again without, Stretch Levels 18.0 / 13.0, Stretch Color with snap 16.9 / 12.4, Spread Tones 17.0 / 12.4, and Stretch Levels with Temporal Smoothing 0.1 s and Scene Detect 113.4 / 128.0, above the budget, because each frame re-reads its neighbours every time it is asked (the way to fix it, keeping each frame's counts, is marked in `fill_stats`, not done). **Draft against Full, recorded, not equalised.** A draft counts its own quarter-size picture, so where small bright or dark details average away its stretch differs from Full's: on B-231's test street the black points agree and a white point differs by up to 20 levels. Export is always Full. **Deviations from After Effects.** Adobe does not publish how its four work, so every rule is ours; Equalize's default (RGB) and its Photoshop Style rule (one histogram of the three channels) are ours; Scene Detect's threshold is fixed. **Left for later:** Color Link and Color Stabilizer (they read these statistics now), a card reduction pass. **Gaps from the tutorials, logged, not worked round:** the common deflicker of an Auto Levels or Auto Color with Temporal Smoothing on an adjustment layer over a time-lapse is not drawn (diagnosed; put the effect on the footage layer or precompose); the old-film flicker made by Auto Color with a short Temporal Smoothing on the layer itself is reproducible.

D-352 / The guided filter, and Matte Choker, Refine Hard Matte and Refine Soft Matte, after After Effects' effects of those names (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md` P0-20) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-08 under the owner's /loop request ("Take the first non-done row ... using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar. Add one regression test ... and one perf measurement"): every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; Matte Choker on the card within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); Refine Hard Matte and Refine Soft Matte drawn on the processor, so no card tolerance applies; no new tolerance; built B-232.** P0-20 had Simple Choker and mask feather, and no edge-aware filter. **What was built.** `src/matte_refine.rs`: running-total box sums and the guided filter of He, Sun and Tang (Algorithm 2, colour guide, epsilon 1e-4), kept once for the keying effects to come. Three effects in Lines & Mattes: `core.matte_choker` (two stages of Geometric Softness 0..100, Choke -127..127 and Gray Level Softness 0..100, Iterations 1..10; each stage the disc average of the covering through a ramp, the colour the pixel's own or the disc's; the layer never grows); `core.refine_hard_matte` and `core.refine_soft_matte` (Feather 0..100 by the guided filter on a guide whose colour runs on past the edge, Contrast, Shift Edge, Decontaminate Edge Colors with Amount, Extend Where Decontaminated and View Decontamination Map, by Germer and others' 2020 foreground estimate at one level; Soft's own Edge Radius, the guided filter fitting the covering to the colours in a band about the edge, and View Edge Region). Every number keyable; the distances scale with a draft. The rule is document 21's matte refinement paragraph. **Card and processor.** Matte Choker has a card pass (`mchoke` in `src/gpu.rs`, per-row running totals in double precision through `prefix`); a stage with Gray Level Softness 0 is a hard step and stays on the processor for D-122's reason. The Refine effects stay on the processor, as D-351's statistics did, with what follows them on the card; a card pass would need many thirteen-channel double-precision box sums and is left for later (b155 rerun 846 of 846, no `GPU_PREVIEW_ON_CPU`). No new diagnostic: an invalid setting is kept and left out with `EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID`. **Evidence.** Fixtures first (be02298, FX-MREF-001 to 035, `tools/matte_refine_reference.py`, numpy, never the build's code); `verification/D-352_matte_refine_table.md` 195 of 195 checks (all 35 cases, largest difference 1.2e-6; files saved as read; tiles of 1 and 64 byte-identical; the card at 0 levels on the fixtures and at most 1 on the reference shot with three settings, Full and Draft; pictures of the test street keyed off its sky: specks and holes gone, the sky-tinted band 28.6 levels from the houses' colour before and 15.2 after decontamination); timing `verification/B-232_matte_refine_timing_table.md`, the reference shot with a moving Noise then the effect on three layers, Full, Draw on: GPU, median of three rounds: 16.9 ms first and 12.6 played again without, Matte Choker 42.0 / 39.7 (about 9 ms a layer, above Target P2), Refine Hard Matte 671.6 / 655.8, with decontamination 917.9 / 844.7, Refine Soft Matte 928.1 / 910.2 (far above Target P3). **Deviations from After Effects.** Adobe does not publish how its three work, so every rule is ours; the radii count whole pixels, so a keyed Feather steps; Shift Edge moves the edge only within the softened band; Refine Soft Matte's Edge Radius stands for After Effects' automatic edge detection; Iterations runs 1..10; Matte Choker never grows the layer; defaults After Effects does not document are ours. **Left for later:** a card pass for the Refine effects (or the processor's box sums adding columns in parallel), a faster Matte Choker pass, Reduce Chatter and Extend Where Smoothed (they read nearby frames), Use Motion Blur, Motion Blur Samples, Shutter Angle and Higher Quality (P0-4), Calculate Edge Details, Invert. **Gaps from the tutorials, logged, not worked round:** the usual Keylight then Refine Soft Matte on hair waits for our keyer (L-03, parked by D-179); after one of our keys, Refine Soft Matte sees only the colours the layer still has, so a pixel keyed out entirely is black to it and dark parts beside such holes come out part see-through (`verification/D-352 pictures/refine_soft_matte.png`); a Refine with motion blur on a moving matte is not available (P0-4).

D-353 / The shared soft-glow engine and pick #1 Soft Physical Glow, a new "physical" falloff of Glow (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md` P0-21; `docs/effects/PLUGINS.md` 2.3 and 5) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-08 under the owner's /loop request ("Take the first non-done row ... using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar. Add one regression test ... and one perf measurement"): every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; drawn on the card within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-233.** Glow and Bloom each had their own single blur; there was no glow with a physical falloff. **What was built.** `src/soft_glow.rs`, kept as functions the later glows (picks #6, #10, #11, #13, #14) can call: the light (premultiplied colour; Threshold Mode Chroma, each channel, or Luminance, Rec. 709; Threshold and Threshold Smooth; Saturation Bias towards the saturation or away from it); Gaussian levels of size Radius/3 halving each time, faded in as clamp(2 sigma - 1, 0, 1) and weighted to sum to one, so the number of levels follows Radius (11 at 2,000) and none jumps in; each level worked on cells of d by d pixels (d the largest power of two with 8 d <= sigma) and spread by two one-way passes, the second along a slanted line, which also make Aspect Ratio and Aspect Angle; the finish (Exposure; Screen as add and hold at 1.0, PLUGINS.md's Screen, or Add; Unmult; the untouched layer back on top at Source Opacity). The layer grows by the largest reach, so no glow is cut off and light off the frame still lights it (no silent crop). Pick #1 is Glow (`core.glow`) with the new setting `falloff` written "physical"; a Glow with no falloff, or "classic", is D-89's, untouched, and every Glow and Bloom fixture passes unchanged. In the window it is its own entry, Soft Physical Glow, in Light & Glow (500 radius, Screen, Unmult on when added). No quality preset and no half-precision switch, as PLUGINS.md 5 settled: one fixed method whose sizes are part of the reference. The rule is document 21's soft glow paragraph. **Card and processor.** Five card passes in `src/gpu.rs` (`sglight`, `sgcells` with double-precision cell sums, `sgpass`, `sgadd`, `sgfinish`); a Threshold above 0 with Smooth 0 is a hard step and stays on the processor for D-122's reason (b155 rerun passes, no `GPU_PREVIEW_ON_CPU`). No new diagnostic: an invalid setting is kept and left out with `EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID`. **Evidence.** Fixtures first (110f2b8, FX-SGLOW-001 to 045, `tools/soft_glow_reference.py`, numpy, never the build's code); `verification/D-353_soft_glow_table.md` 238 of 238 checks (all 45 cases, largest difference 5.3e-7; files saved as read; tiles of 1 and 64 byte-identical; the card against the processor 50 of 50 within 1 level: 32 fixtures at Full and Draft, 25 of them on the card, and the reference shot with three settings, Full and Draft; pictures of the town: the old Glow's short halo against the new long tail, the haze as added, the stretched streak); timing `verification/B-233_soft_glow_timing_table.md`, the reference shot with a moving Noise then the effect on three layers, Full, Draw on: GPU, median of three rounds: 15.6 ms first and 12.1 played again without; as added (radius 500) 61.7 / 59.8; radius 60 with threshold 40 and smooth 50 52.8 / 49.0; radius 2,000 139.1 / 136.5; radius 60 with a hard threshold (processor) 368.3 / 357.5; above Target P3. **Deviations from the plugin.** Its kernel is not published, so ours is our own; no quality preset; a strongly stretched glow is softer than a true oval at its largest levels; a level moving to coarser cells as Radius is keyed steps by at most about 0.00036 in linear light (invisible at 8 bits); Unmult off makes the whole grown area opaque black. **Left for later:** input mask, inner/outer tint (pick #6), per-channel radius (pick #10), tone mapping, lens dirt, Lens Iris, the Gamma Correction amount, the level spacing as a setting, speed (adding the levels only over the part in frame, the grown layer being about 540 pixels on each side at radius 500 and 2,200 at 2,000). **Gaps from the tutorials, logged, not worked round:** the usual tinted Deep Glow on text (Tint on, two colours) waits for pick #6; the chromatic-aberration fringe waits for pick #10; a glow from a masked part of the layer (the input mask) is not available.

D-356 / Effects that draw along paths, and Path Stroke, after After Effects' Stroke (Generate) (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md` P0-22) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-08 under the owner's /loop request ("Take the first non-done row ... using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar. Add one regression test ... and one perf measurement"): every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; drawn on the card within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-235.** The drawing along a path existed only inside shape layers. **What was built.** `src/along.rs`, kept as functions the later path effects can call: `runs` measures closed paths along their length, trims them to Start and End (taken smaller first; with Stroke Sequentially the paths are one length end to end), and lays dabs a step apart from each path's first point, so they stay put as Start moves; `distance` finds a run's nearest dab; `path_stroke` draws a round brush with a smoothstep edge. Path Stroke (`core.stroke`, our name; After Effects' controls): Path (mask n), All Masks, Stroke Sequentially, Color, Brush Size (2 when added), Brush Hardness, Opacity, Start, End, Spacing (0 continuous), Paint Style (On Original Image, On Transparent, Reveal Original Image). The paths are the layer's masks at the frame, flattened and closed as document 19 does; a mask is a path when enabled with two points or more, whatever its mode. With none the layer is left as it is and `EFFECT_PATH_MISSING` (document 28, new) is said every frame. Bounds never grow. On the card (`stroke`), handed the runs and, per band of 16 rows, the runs that reach it. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-STROKE-001 to 046 (`tools/stroke_reference.py`, 024b678) in document 25. **Left over:** masks are always closed (After Effects strokes open masks); text outlines wait on the held text change (src/text.rs); shape-layer paths are not a source yet; on an adjustment layer it finds no path; a crossing mask of mode None still warns MASK_INVALID_OUTLINE; dabs do not build up (Adobe's model is unpublished); Stroke Sequentially shares the time by length.
D-357 / Path Stroke along a shape layer's paths, open or closed (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md` P0-22, second part) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-08 under the owner's /loop request: every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-236.** **What was built.** Path Stroke gains Path From (`source`): Masks, the default and not written, so every earlier file and fixture is unchanged, or Shape Paths. **Deviation:** After Effects' Stroke takes masks only; Path From is this program's own, chosen as the smallest familiar way to pick shapes (one menu at the top, Path and All Masks then counting shapes). With Shape Paths the paths are the layer's own shapes at the frame, enabled with two points or more, whatever their fill and stroke, flattened as document 19 flattens a shape's outline (its own Trim Paths not applied), open or closed as each says; `src/along.rs` `runs` and `stroke_runs` now take an open/closed flag per path, and an open path has no closing leg. A layer with no shapes says `EFFECT_PATH_MISSING`; any other `source` word is refused (`EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID`). Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-STROKE-047 to 061 (`tools/stroke_reference.py`, bb25da1) in document 25; `verification/D-357_stroke_shapes_table.md` 103 of 103. **Open masks not built:** document 19 defines a mask as closed, and an open flag would reach the schema, validator, coverage, commands, undo and the pen tool, which is not a small change; logged as a gap. **Left over:** an effect on a shape layer is drawn by the processor even with Draw on: GPU (B-46's rule that the card takes effects only on drawing layers, unchanged); only the layer's own shapes, not another layer's; no star tool (stars are drawn with the pen); text outlines still wait on the held text change (src/text.rs).

D-358 / Bilateral Blur, after After Effects' Bilateral Blur (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Blur & Sharpen) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-08 under the owner's /loop request ("Implement it with GPU support where it makes sense, using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar"): every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-237.** **What was built.** `core.bilateral_blur`, named Bilateral Blur, in Blur & Sharpen: Radius (0 to 50 pixels, 5 when added), Threshold (0 to 255 levels, 20) and Colorize (On, Off; On). Each pixel becomes the mean of the pixels within a disc of Radius, each weighed by its covering, by a bell on its distance (width Radius / 2) and by a bell on how far its level, 255 times the sRGB curve of its straight colour, is from the pixel's own (width Threshold); Colorize on does this for red, green and blue each with its own likeness, Colorize off on luminance, so the layer comes out grey. The pixel keeps its own covering; Radius below 1 or Threshold 0 leaves the layer as it is (with Colorize off, grey). `src/median.rs` `bilateral_blur`, beside Smart Blur. **Deviation:** Adobe does not publish its method, so the rule is this program's own (document 21); the defaults and ranges are our own pick, as Adobe's help pages could not be read. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-BILAT-001 to 017 (`tools/bilateral_blur_reference.py`, f88a996) in document 25; `verification/D-358_bilateral_blur_table.md` 123 of 123. **On the card** (`bilat` in `src/gpu.rs`, two passes: the levels, then the disc), its taps summed in single precision, every picture within 1 level of the processor; a first pass with double sums was about ten times slower (`verification/B-237_bilateral_blur_timing_table.md`). **Left over:** the processor, which draws exports, is slow at a large radius (about 220 ms a 1080p layer at Radius 10); tutorial gaps logged in EFFECTS.md.

D-359 / Lens Blur's blur map, after After Effects' Camera Lens Blur Blur Map group (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Blur & Sharpen, Camera Lens Blur and pick #12, Shaped Bokeh with blur map) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-08 under the owner's /loop request ("Implement it with GPU support where it makes sense, using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar"): every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); FX-LENS-001 to 044 unchanged; no new tolerance; built B-238.** **What was built.** Inside `core.lens_blur`, not a new effect, as `docs/effects/PLUGINS.md` settled for pick #12: Blur Map Layer (any layer of the composition, D-189, None when added), Blur Map Channel (Luminance, Alpha), Blur Map Placement (Centre, Stretch Map to Fit), Blur Focal Distance (0 to 255, 0, keyable) and Invert Blur Map (Off, On). Where the map's value equals the focal distance the picture stays sharp; the iris widens straight with the distance from it, to the full radius 255 levels away, each pixel mixed between the two nearest whole-pixel iris sizes so the blur grows smoothly. With no layer named the picture is exactly as before; a named layer that cannot be read leaves the layer without the effect, said as `EFFECT_LAYER_MISSING` (document 28). `src/layer_fx.rs` `lens_blur_map`. **Deviations:** Adobe's exact rule is not published, so ours is our own (document 21); there is no Depth channel choice: a depth pass is put on a layer of its own through Pass Extract (D-348) and that layer is the map; no focus point to click (the Bokeh plugin's). Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-LENS-045 to 069 (`tools/lens_blur_map_reference.py`, 0ce104b) in document 25; `verification/D-359_lens_blur_map_table.md` 148 of 148. **On the card** in Lens Blur's own pass (`lmgather` in `src/gpu.rs`, the map through `map_texture`), every picture within 1 level of the processor. **Left over:** on the card the map adds about 5 ms a 1080p layer at radius 10 (`verification/B-238_lens_blur_map_timing_table.md`), above Target P3 as Lens Blur already was; depth from a 3D camera or the composition's 3D layers is off-charter (D-309, D-355).

D-360 / Cross Blur, after CycoreFX's CC Cross Blur (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Blur & Sharpen, CC Cross Blur) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-08 under the owner's /loop request ("Implement it with GPU support where it makes sense, using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar"): every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-239.** **What was built.** A new effect, `core.cross_blur`, Cross Blur under our own name: Radius X and Radius Y (0 to 500 pixels, 10 each, keyable), Transfer Mode (Blend, Add, Screen, Multiply, Lighten, Darken; Blend) and Edges (Transparent, Repeat Edge Pixels). The layer is blurred across by one pass of Fast Box Blur's box (D-327) and, separately, down by another, and the two are laid together: Blend is their mean, the others document 21's blend rule. With transparent edges the layer grows by the larger reach. `src/blurs.rs` `cross_blur`. **Deviations:** the manual does not say how the two are laid together, so Blend as the mean is our reading; Add is held at 1 even in Float, as Solid Composite's; the defaults are our own. D-361 / Spin & Zoom Blur, after CycoreFX's CC Radial Blur (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Blur & Sharpen, CC Radial Blur) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-08 under the owner's /loop request ("Implement it with GPU support where it makes sense, using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar"): every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-240.** **What was built.** A new effect, `core.spin_zoom_blur`, Spin & Zoom Blur under our own name: Type (Straight Zoom, Fading Zoom, Centered Zoom, Rotate, Scratch, Rotate Fading; Straight Zoom), Amount (-360 to 360, 10), Quality (1 to 100, 50) and Centre (50, 50), the numbers keyable. It is Radial Blur's path (D-95) with where the samples start, how they are weighed (evenly or fading) and how many a pixel of path (Quality / 50), through `radial_blur`'s new `Sweep` in `src/blurs.rs`; Radial Blur's own pictures are unchanged. **Deviations:** Cycore does not publish its sampling, so the rule is ours; a zoom over 100 reads through the centre; Rotate reads transparent corners in from outside the layer; the defaults are our own. D-362 / Fast Zoom Blur, after CycoreFX's CC Radial Fast Blur (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Blur & Sharpen, CC Radial Fast Blur) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-08 under the owner's /loop request ("Implement it with GPU support where it makes sense, using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar"): every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-241.** **What was built.** A new effect, `core.fast_zoom_blur`, Fast Zoom Blur under our own name: Amount (0 to 100, 50), Centre (50, 50), both keyable, and Zoom (Standard, Brightest, Darkest; Standard). Each pixel reads back toward the centre, the nearer samples weighed more; Brightest keeps the pixel lit further by any brighter sample, Darkest darkened by any darker one, so Brightest never darkens and Darkest never lightens. Through the same `Sweep` as D-361. **Deviations:** Cycore does not publish its method, so the rule is ours; the defaults are our own; it is not faster than Spin & Zoom Blur here, both being one card pass. D-363 / Channel Blur and Unsharp Mask checked against fixtures (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Blur & Sharpen, Channel Blur and Unsharp Mask) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-08 under the owner's /loop request ("Add one regression test (reference frame or numeric check)"): every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; no code changed; built B-242.** **What was done.** Both rows were partial for thin evidence, not a missing control: After Effects' Channel Blur has Red, Green, Blue and Alpha Blurriness, Repeat Edge Pixels and Blur Dimensions, all in `core.channel_blur` since D-313; its Unsharp Mask has Amount, Radius and Threshold, all in `core.sharpen` since D-147 and D-317. New fixtures from independent references, e22c6c1: FX-CHBLUR-001 to 014 (`tools/channel_blur_reference.py`) and FX-SHARPEN-019 to 030 (`tools/unsharp_threshold_reference.py`, in a new expected file beside FX-SHARPEN-001 to 018's, which are untouched). The build matched both on the first run, so nothing was changed. `verification/D-363_channel_blur_unsharp_table.md` 109 of 109. D-364 / Diffusion's second pass, the owner's pick #2 (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Blur & Sharpen, Pick #2: Diffusion soft-light pass; `docs/effects/PLUGINS.md` top 20, #2, settled there as a merge into `core.diffusion`) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-08 under the owner's /loop request ("for plugin-inspired rows, the notes in docs/effects/PLUGINS.md plus tutorials, aiming for the quality edge that row describes"): every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-243.** **What was built.** `core.diffusion` gains Second Amount (0 to 100, keyable, 0 = off) and Second Blend (Soft Light or Overlay, Soft Light): the same blur laid on again over the first pass's result, with the layer modes' own overlay and soft light on encoded colours (D-301, `grade::mixer`). At 0 the effect is D-148's exactly, and a file without the two settings is saved without them, so every older project opens and draws identically. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-DIFFUSE-019 to 032 (`tools/diffusion_second_reference.py`, 72a26a5) in document 25; code 4ea3ae2; `verification/D-364_diffusion_second_table.md` 71 of 71; the card's Diffusion pass gains the second pass, every picture within 1 level (`verification/B-107_gpu_fx_table.md` 7062 of 7062). **One blur, shared.** No source gives the second copy a blur of its own: tomoex (note.com) lays two blurred adjustment layers, Lighten 50% under Soft Light 50%, sizes not given; taka2composite calls Lighten essential for diffusion and says nothing of a second layer. So both passes share Radius. **Deviations:** (1) tomoex's second layer is an adjustment layer, so its blur reads the picture with the lighten layer already on; ours lays the same blur of the original, the difference small at the usual 30 to 50%. (2) The RETAS Studio lesson that PLUGINS.md cites has a second layer that is the sharp original in Normal at 30%, to bring the lines back, not an overlay; the first pass's Amount below 100 already does that, so nothing was added for it. **Timing** (`verification/B-243_diffusion_second_timing_table.md`, quiet machine): the second pass adds about 1 ms a 1080p layer on the card, about 5 on the processor.

D-365 / Broadcast Safe, after After Effects' Broadcast Colors (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Color Correction, Broadcast Colors) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-08 under the owner's /loop request ("Implement it with GPU support where it makes sense, using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar"): every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-244.** **What was built.** A new effect, `core.broadcast_safe`, Broadcast Safe under our own name: Locale (NTSC, PAL; NTSC), How to Make Colour Safe (Reduce Luminance, Reduce Saturation, Key Out Unsafe, Key Out Safe; Reduce Luminance) and Maximum Signal (90 to 120 IRE, 110, keyable). A pixel whose signal top, from its brightness and colour together, passes the limit is darkened or greyed until it sits on it, or keyed out, or only such pixels are kept. **Deviations:** Adobe does not publish its method, so the rule is ours; the signal is measured on the sRGB-encoded colour as if it were video's, not on linear light nor on Rec. 601 or 709 levels; only the top of the signal is checked, not a dip below black; float values above 1 are held to 1 first. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-BCAST-001 to 015 (`tools/broadcast_safe_reference.py`, 9f10265) in document 25; code ff3cba2; `verification/D-365_broadcast_safe_table.md` 125 of 125. **On the card** in the colour pass, fused in a colour run (B-222/D-341), every picture within 1 level of the processor, the fused run of Color Neutralizer, Levels, Color Offset and Broadcast Safe 9 of 9 on the card; B-155 shows no fall-back to the processor; under 1 ms a 1080p layer on the card, about 4 on the processor, within Target P1 (`verification/B-244_colour_timing_table.md`, quiet machine).

D-366 / Color Neutralizer, after CycoreFX's CC Color Neutralizer (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Color Correction, CC Color Neutralizer) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-08 under the owner's /loop request ("Implement it with GPU support where it makes sense, using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar"): every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-245.** **What was built.** A new effect, `core.color_neutralizer`, Color Neutralizer under our own name: Shadows, Midtones and Highlights Unbalance colours (black, mid grey, white), a red, green, blue triple of levels for each (-255 to 255, 0), Pinning (0 to 100, 0), Black Point and White Point (0 and 255), every number keyable. Each unbalance colour is pulled to its own grey and the numbers add; the three corrections are spread over the picture's brightness between the two points, and Pinning holds black and white in place. **Deviations:** CycoreFX's manual gives no formula, so the rule is ours; worked on the sRGB-encoded colour, where CycoreFX works on stored values; the colours and the numbers add, where CycoreFX's picking a colour sets the numbers; no averaging eyedropper and no View Correction graph; Blend w. Original is the Mix every effect has. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-NEUTRAL-001 to 018 (`tools/color_neutralizer_reference.py`, 9f10265) in document 25; code ff3cba2; `verification/D-366_color_neutralizer_table.md` 123 of 123. **On the card** in the colour pass, fused in a colour run (B-222/D-341), every picture within 1 level of the processor, the fused run of Color Neutralizer, Levels, Color Offset and Broadcast Safe 9 of 9 on the card; B-155 shows no fall-back to the processor; under 1 ms a 1080p layer on the card, about 4 on the processor, within Target P1 (`verification/B-244_colour_timing_table.md`, quiet machine).

D-367 / Color Offset, after CycoreFX's CC Color Offset (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Color Correction, CC Color Offset) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-08 under the owner's /loop request ("Implement it with GPU support where it makes sense, using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar"): every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-246.** **What was built.** A new effect, `core.color_offset`, Color Offset under our own name: Red, Green and Blue Phase (-3600 to 3600 degrees, 0, keyable) and Overflow (Wrap, Solarize, Polarize; Wrap). Each channel is turned round by its phase, a whole turn the full range; Wrap brings what passes white back from black, Solarize folds it back down, Polarize folds it smoothly, both giving the negative at one turn and the picture back at two. **Deviations:** CycoreFX's manual names the overflows without formulas, so the rule is ours; the phases turn the sRGB-encoded colour, where CycoreFX turns its stored 0 to 255 values; with Wrap a whole turn leaves the values between as they were but turns pure black to white and pure white to black, black and white being one point on the circle. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-COFFSET-001 to 016 (`tools/color_offset_reference.py`, 9f10265) in document 25; code ff3cba2; `verification/D-367_color_offset_table.md` 114 of 114. **On the card** in the colour pass, fused in a colour run (B-222/D-341), every picture within 1 level of the processor, the fused run of Color Neutralizer, Levels, Color Offset and Broadcast Safe 9 of 9 on the card; B-155 shows no fall-back to the processor; under 1 ms a 1080p layer on the card, about 4 on the processor, within Target P1 (`verification/B-244_colour_timing_table.md`, quiet machine).

D-368 / Kernel, after CycoreFX's CC Kernel (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Color Correction, CC Kernel) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-09 under the owner's /loop request ("Implement it with GPU support where it makes sense, using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar"): every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-247.** **What was built.** A new effect, `core.kernel`, Kernel under our own name: Line 1, Line 2 and Line 3 (three numbers each, -1000 to 1000; 0 0 0, 0 1 0, 0 0 0), Divider (0.01 to 1000, 1), every number keyable, and Absolute Values (Off, On; Off). Each pixel is rebuilt from itself and its eight neighbours weighed by the grid, divided, made positive if asked and held between black and white; the border pixel repeats past the layer's edge; as added the layer is left exactly as it is. **Deviations:** CycoreFX's manual gives no formula, so the rule is ours; worked on the sRGB-encoded colour, where CycoreFX works on stored values; the result is held inside 0 to 1, so a negative sum is black; Blend w. Original is the Mix every effect has (D-202); no Offset or Alpha control, the manual (HD 1.8.9) having none for CC Kernel. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-KERNEL-001 to 018 (`tools/kernel_reference.py`, 1a36828) in document 25; code 03cd7c1; `verification/D-368_kernel_table.md` 135 of 135. **On the card** in its own pass, the neighbour pass of Emboss and Find Edges, every picture within 1 level of the processor (42 of 42); B-155 shows no fall-back to the processor; about 4.3 to 5.5 ms a 1080p layer on the card, a little above Target P2's 4 ms, about 10.5 on the processor (`verification/B-247_colour_timing_table.md`, quiet machine).

D-369 / Toner, after CycoreFX's CC Toner (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Color Correction, CC Toner) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-09 under the owner's /loop request ("Implement it with GPU support where it makes sense, using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar"): every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-248.** **What was built.** A new effect, `core.toner`, Toner under our own name, sharing Gradient Map's lightness (D-129) but its own effect: Tones (Duotone, Tritone, Pentone; Tritone) and five colours, Highlights, Brights, Midtones, Darktones and Shadows (white, #e0cfb0, #8c7355, #46382a, black, a warm sepia of our own). Each pixel's lightness picks its colour off an evenly spaced ramp of two, three or five of them, shadows to highlights; tones the choice leaves out are kept. **Deviations:** CycoreFX's manual gives no formula and its starting colours are not published, so the rule and the defaults are ours; Blend w. Original is the Mix every effect has (D-202); no eyedroppers. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-TONER-001 to 013 (`tools/toner_reference.py`, 1a36828) in document 25; code 03cd7c1; `verification/D-369_toner_table.md` 105 of 105. **On the card** in the colour pass, fused in a colour run (B-222/D-341), every picture within 1 level of the processor (37 of 37), the fused run of Toner, Levels and Change Color 6 of 6 on the card; B-155 shows no fall-back to the processor; about 1 ms a 1080p layer on the card, about 3 on the processor, within Target P1 (`verification/B-247_colour_timing_table.md`, quiet machine).

D-370 / Change Color, after After Effects' Change Color (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Color Correction, Change Color) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-09 under the owner's /loop request ("Implement it with GPU support where it makes sense, using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar"): every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-249.** **What was built.** A new effect, `core.change_color`, Change Color, sharing Change to Color's HLS (D-197) but its own effect, as After Effects has both: View (Corrected Layer, Color Correction Mask), Hue Transform (-3600 to 3600 degrees, 0), Lightness and Saturation Transform (-100 to 100, 0), Color To Change (red), Matching Tolerance and Softness (0 to 100, 15 and 0), every number keyable, Match Colors (RGB, Hue, Chroma; Hue) and Invert Color Correction Mask (Off). The colours near the picked one, fully within the tolerance and fading out over the softness, are turned round the wheel and made lighter or darker, stronger or greyer; the mask can be shown or turned over; with every transform 0 the layer is left exactly as it is. **Deviations:** Adobe does not publish its method, so the rule is ours; worked on the sRGB-encoded colour; a grey has no hue, so under hue matching it is never near a colour; the chroma distance is the plain HD colour-difference distance, not scaled to 0 to 1, and Softness is an absolute distance beyond the tolerance, not a share of it as in Change to Color; no eyedropper. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-CHCOLOR-001 to 024 (`tools/change_color_reference.py`, 1a36828) in document 25; code 03cd7c1; `verification/D-370_change_color_table.md` 163 of 163. **On the card** in the colour pass, fused in a colour run (B-222/D-341), every picture within 1 level of the processor (48 of 48), the fused run of Toner, Levels and Change Color 6 of 6 on the card; B-155 shows no fall-back to the processor; under 1 ms a 1080p layer on the card, about 2.5 on the processor, within Target P1 (`verification/B-247_colour_timing_table.md`, quiet machine).

D-371 / Text shaping (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md` P0-7, part 2), by D-354's `rustybuzz` / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-09 under the owner's /loop request ("Implement it with GPU support where it makes sense, using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar"): every glyph exactly as HarfBuzz shapes it; every anchor within 1e-6 and every outline box within 0.25 pixel, D-350's own tolerances; ligatures on by the owner's choice of 2026-10-09 ("ligatures on by default"); no new tolerance; built B-250.** **What was built.** A text layer's words are shaped before they are laid out (`src/text.rs`, `text::shaped`, `rustybuzz` 0.20.1 on `ttf-parser` 0.25.1): Arabic letters join and read right to left, Devanagari builds its conjuncts and draws the i-matra before its consonant, a combining mark sits on its letter, and the font's standard ligatures (fi, fl, ff, ffi in the bundled font) are drawn. Each paragraph is cut into runs of one script and one direction; each glyph belongs to a cluster drawn at the cluster's first character typed, which holds the anchor, the box and the Text Animator pick (D-350), the other characters in it drawing nothing. Kerning, when on, is now the font's own as HarfBuzz applies it. Text without joins or ligature pairs draws exactly as before: d263_text, d264_text_styles and D-350's pictures unchanged. Fonts for the checks: Noto Sans Arabic 2.013 and Noto Sans Devanagari 2.007 (SIL Open Font License 1.1, `docs/third_party/`). **Deviations:** no bidirectional algorithm (UAX #9) yet; four gaps, in document 21: a sign between a left-to-right and a right-to-left run takes the earlier run's side; figures starting a right-to-left paragraph are drawn reversed; a right-to-left run that figures split inside a left-to-right paragraph is drawn as two runs, not one embedding; a line broken by a text box is not shaped again at the break. No switch to turn ligatures off. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-SHAPE-001 to 012 and 020 to 023 (`tools/text_shaping_reference.py` with `uharfbuzz` 0.53.3, 889e280) in document 25; code cb2b749; `verification/D-371_text_shaping_table.md` 16 of 16; FX-SHAPE-020 was in dispute until D-372 (a), built B-251, and now passes outright. Six crates added, licences in `Licenses/`, recorded in `docs/DEPENDENCIES.md` (b11). **On the processor**, as D-263's letters are: outlines filled, no per-pixel work to move; B-155 shows no fall-back. Laying out a 30-character Latin line 0.240 ms before, 0.256 after; a 31-character Arabic line 0.298 and 0.334; drawn at 1920 by 1080 1.607 and 1.607, 1.685 and 1.817 (`verification/B-250_text_shaping_timing_table.md`, quiet machine).

D-372 / TrueType side-bearing slide, raised by D-371's FX-SHAPE-020 / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-09 by the owner ("go with your recommendation on D-372"), option (a); built B-251.** Proposed the same day by B-250: it either changes every text picture slightly or changes a fixture. FreeType, HarfBuzz and fontTools slide a TrueType outline sideways by the font's hmtx left side bearing less the xMin in the glyph's own header before drawing it; D-263 draws the points as the font stores them, as D-350's reference does. In the bundled font the two differ for 4134 of its 8546 drawn glyphs, by up to 7 font units in plain Latin (0.7 pixel at size 100: A, V, W, X, Y, v, w, x, y and others) and up to 29 in a few Japanese brackets. D-371's reference drew its boxes through fontTools' glyph set, with the slide, so FX-SHAPE-020's "y" differs by 0.4 pixel; with the slide taken out every box agrees within 0.023 pixel. Choose: **(a)** the build adopts the slide, matching FreeType and Windows; existing text pictures move by up to 0.7 pixel at size 100 and their checks are re-recorded; or **(b)** the build keeps the stored points and FX-SHAPE-020's expected boxes are regenerated without the slide, as D-350's are: a fixture change, the owner's call. **What was built (B-251).** `src/text.rs` slides each glyph of a font with a glyf table by its hmtx left side bearing less its glyf header's xMin, where outlines are read, so drawing, boxes and every later use of the outlines take it; CFF fonts are drawn as stored. D-373 / Text outlines as a path source for Path Stroke (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md` P0-22, part 3) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-09 under the owner's /loop request ("Implement it with GPU support where it makes sense, using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar"); built B-252 on D-372's slide.** After Effects reaches this through Layer > Create > Create Masks from Text, which puts one mask per character outline on a new solid and turns the text layer's video off; Stroke with All Masks, Stroke Sequentially and End keyed 0 to 100 then writes the word on. Ours is a third Path From choice on Path Stroke, **Text Outlines** (`source` "text"): the text layer itself is the source and stays live. Its contours at the frame, laid out exactly as the text is drawn (shaping, the side-bearing slide, Text Animators), glyph by glyph in reading order and each glyph's contours in the font's order, every one closed, starting where ttf-parser starts it, quadratics raised to cubics, flattened as document 19 flattens a mask (document 21, Drawing along paths). Path N counts contours, so an "e" is two steps (the bundled font stores its eye first); no outline (not a text layer, spaces only, Path past the last) draws nothing with EFFECT_PATH_MISSING every frame. A text layer has no cel, so the processor draws the stroke with Draw on: GPU too (B-46's rule), within 1 level of 255. **What was built (B-252).** Fixtures first (dc693ec: FX-STROKE-062 to 069 by `tools/stroke_text_reference.py`, HarfBuzz and fontTools, with the slide); code 7b230fa (`src/text.rs` `outlines`, the same lay-out that draws the text; `src/compose.rs`; the choice in the effect controls). `verification/D-373_stroke_text_table.md` 64 of 64: fixture frames within 3.0e-8, outline lengths within 7.1e-15. **Timing** (`verification/B-252_stroke_text_timing_table.md`, quiet machine): on a 1080p text layer the stroke adds about 10 ms a frame with Draw on: GPU (12.6 to 22.3 ms played again) and about 5 by the processor (47.6 to 52.8), over Target P2, because a stroked text layer is redrawn and, on the card path, sent to the card every frame instead of kept (`verification/B-252_stroke_text_timing_table.md`, quiet machine); keeping a stroked text layer's picture between frames is a separate change. **Gaps against After Effects:** no command that makes editable masks or shape layers from text (ours is a live source instead); no choosing characters by hand (Path N per contour); the outlines' order is fixed (reading order); open masks remain document 19's gap; Energy Stroke's extras are not built. Picture: `verification/D-373 pictures/write_strip.png` (End 0, 50, 100); playtest `verification/B-252_playtest.md`.

D-375 / Color Link, after After Effects' Color Link (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Color Correction, Color Link) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-09 under the owner's /loop request ("Implement it with GPU support where it makes sense, using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar"): every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-254.** **What was built.** A new effect, `core.color_link`, Color Link: Source Layer (a layer of the composition, or none for the layer itself as the effects before this one left it), Sample (Average, Median, Brightest, Darkest, Max RGB, Min RGB; Average), Clip (0 to 49 per cent, 5), Stencil (Off, On; Off), Opacity (0 to 100, 100) and Blending Mode (Normal, Multiply, Screen, Add, Overlay, Soft Light; Normal), Clip and Opacity keyable. A name that is no layer of the composition is EFFECT_LAYER_MISSING, on opening and at each frame, as D-189 says for every layer setting, and the layer is left as it is. **Deviations:** Adobe does not publish its method, so the rule is ours; no alpha samples (Average Alpha and the like); six blending modes, Paraffin's (D-185), not After Effects' full list; the clip range is ours; the named layer is read with its masks and effects. D-376 / Color Stabilizer, after After Effects' Color Stabilizer (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Color Correction, Color Stabilizer) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-09 under the owner's /loop request ("Implement it with GPU support where it makes sense, using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar"): every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-255.** **What was built.** A new effect, `core.color_stabilizer`, Color Stabilizer: Stabilize (Brightness, Levels, Curves; Brightness), Reference Frame (the composition frame whose colours are kept, 0), Black, Mid and White Point (per cent of the layer, (25, 50), (50, 50), (75, 50)) and Sample Size (0 to 100 pixels, 5), the points and size keyable. Each point's sample is the covering-weighted mean colour within the radius; the reference samples are taken from the layer at the reference frame with the effects before this one, and each frame is mapped so its samples come back to them: Brightness moves every channel by the black sample's change in brightness, Levels maps each channel by the line through the black and white pairs, Curves through all three. A missing sample or a reference frame outside the layer leaves the frame as it is. On an adjustment layer there is no reference, so the frame is left as it is with TEMPORAL_SMOOTHING_SKIPPED each frame (D-351's warning, document 28 extended). **Deviations:** Adobe does not publish its method, so the rule is ours; a number for the reference frame where After Effects has a Set Frame button; Curves joins the samples with straight lines. Sources read: the After Effects CS3 manual (manualsdir, pp. 397 to 398) and Adobe community posts; written in our own words. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-CSTAB-001 to 016 (`tools/color_stabilizer_reference.py`, 496fe16) in document 25; code 42e982c; `verification/D-376_color_stabilizer_table.md` 111 of 111. **On the processor**, since the reference frame is read there, as the request allowed ("CPU first"); the card draws the rest of the frame round it, every picture within 1 level of the processor and none refused; B-155 shows no fall-back; timing (`verification/B-253_colour_timing_table.md`) measured on a quiet machine (no other cargo or rustc running) on 2026-10-09, the reference shot, 3 layers after a moving Noise, Full, played again, card / processor: Noise alone 11.5 / 41.3 ms a frame, 58.5 / 52.5 with Levels to frame 0 (a second card round 58.6): about 3.7 ms a layer on the processor, within Target P4; with the card the frame is slower than the processor alone, each layer leaving the card at the stabilizer, logged as a gap.

D-377 / Bend It, after CycoreFX's CC Bend It (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Distort, CC Bend It) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-09 under the owner's /loop request ("Implement it with GPU support where it makes sense, using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar"): every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-256.** **What was built.** A new effect, `core.bend_it`, Bend It under our own name: Bend (-360 to 360 degrees, 45), Start and End (per cent of the layer, -1000 to 1000; 50, 100 and 50, 0: a bar standing up the middle), every number keyable, Render Prestart (None, Static, Bend, Mirror; None) and Distort (Legal, Extended; Legal). The strip of the layer along the bar is bent into an arc of a circle that turns Bend degrees over the bar's length, so at 360 its ends meet; where the bend lays the layer over itself the part farther along the bar is on top; Render Prestart says what is drawn before the Start, Distort whether the layer runs on straight past the End; the layer does not grow. **Deviations:** CycoreFX's manual gives no formula, so the rule is ours: the bend is a true arc, not a slant, and the meaning of each Render Prestart choice is our reading of its sentence. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-BENDIT-001 to 023 (`tools/bend_it_reference.py`, d5f59f0) in document 25; code 053957e; `verification/D-377_bend_it_table.md` 161 of 161. **On the card** in the warp pass (mode 12), every picture within 1 level of the processor; B-155 shows no fall-back to the processor; about 2.7 to 3.1 ms a 1080p layer on the card, within Target P2, about 10.3 on the processor (`verification/B-256_distort_timing_table.md`, PROVISIONAL, measured while another agent's tests ran).

D-378 / Bender, after CycoreFX's CC Bender (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Distort, CC Bender) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-09 under the owner's /loop request ("Implement it with GPU support where it makes sense, using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar"): every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-257.** **What was built.** A new effect, `core.bender`, Bender under our own name: Amount (-1000 to 1000, 20), Style (Bend, Marilyn, Sharp, Boxer; Bend), Adjust To Distance (Off, On; Off), Top and Base (per cent of the layer, -1000 to 1000; 50, 0 and 50, 100: an axis standing up the middle), every number keyable. Each pixel is pushed across the axis by an amount that depends on how far along the axis from Base to Top it is: a curve that runs on straight past the Top (Bend), a swell in the middle (Marilyn), a kink half way (Sharp) or a smooth step that shifts everything past the Top whole (Boxer); Amount is pixels, or with Adjust To Distance on per cent of the axis; the layer does not grow. **Deviations:** CycoreFX's manual gives no formula, so the four shapes are ours; Blend w. Original is the Mix every effect has (D-202). Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-BENDER-001 to 023 (`tools/bender_reference.py`, d5f59f0) in document 25; code 053957e; `verification/D-378_bender_table.md` 160 of 160. **On the card** in the warp pass (mode 13), every picture within 1 level of the processor; B-155 shows no fall-back to the processor; about 0.7 to 0.9 ms a 1080p layer on the card, within Target P2, about 6.6 on the processor (`verification/B-256_distort_timing_table.md`, PROVISIONAL, measured while another agent's tests ran).

D-384 / Photo Filter, after After Effects' Photo Filter (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Color Correction, Photo Filter) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-09 under the owner's /loop request ("Implement it with GPU support where it makes sense, using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar"): every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-263.** **What was built.** `core.photo_filter`, a new effect: Filter (Warming Filter (85), Warming Filter (81), Cooling Filter (80), Cooling Filter (82), Sepia, Underwater or Custom; Warming Filter (85) when added), Color (used only for Custom, #ec8a00 when added), Density (0 to 100, 25 when added, keyable) and Preserve Luminosity (on when added), After Effects' own starting settings. The filter's colour laid over each pixel by multiplying at its density; with Preserve Luminosity on, the result scaled back to the pixel's own brightness. **Research.** After Effects' and Photoshop's Photo Filter share the controls and defaults; fmwconcepts' colorfilter script, written to simulate Photoshop's Photo Filter, gives the six preset colours, and Aspose's documentation agrees on Warming (85) as (236, 138, 0); helpx.adobe.com refused automated reading (HTTP 403). **Deviations:** Adobe does not publish the method, so the rule is ours (document 21): the multiply at density, and brightness as Rec. 709 luma on the encoded values. Photoshop's other presets (Warming LBA, Cooling LBB, Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Cyan, Blue, Violet, Magenta, Deep Red, Deep Blue, Deep Emerald, Deep Yellow) have no published colour we found and are left out; Custom covers them. D-381 / Colorama's remaining controls, after After Effects' Colorama (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Color Correction, Colorama) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-09 under the owner's /loop request ("Implement it with GPU support where it makes sense, using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar"): every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; Add Phase From (the same words, as Get Phase From when left out) and Add Mode (Wrap, Clamp, Average, Screen; Wrap) for the Add Phase layer; Interpolate Palette (On); Opacity 1 to 5 (0 to 100, 100); Modify (All Channels, Hue, Lightness, Saturation, Red, Green, Blue, None; All Channels); Modify Alpha and Change Empty Pixels (Off); Matching Mode (Off, RGB, Hue, Chroma; Off), Matching Colour (white), Matching Tolerance (15) and Softness (0), Change Color's distance and nearness (D-370); Mask Layer, a second layer setting (D-189), with Masking Mode (Luminance, Inverted Luminance, Alpha, Inverted Alpha; Luminance); Composite Over Layer (On); the numbers keyable. `Effect::layer_settings` now lists every layer an effect reads, so the cycle check, the missing-layer warning, copying and precomposing treat the mask layer as the Add Phase layer. **Old projects:** with every new setting at its start the processor and the card work D-316's own sum, so a project saved before draws to the bit what it drew (FX-COLORAMA-002 and 028, files without the new keys, against 001; D-385 / Flow Motion, after CycoreFX's CC Flo Motion (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Distort, CC Flo Motion) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-09 under the owner's /loop request ("Implement it with GPU support where it makes sense, using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar"): every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-264.** **What was built.** A new effect, `core.flow_motion`, Flow Motion under our own name: Knot 1 and Knot 2 (per cent of the layer, -1000 to 1000; 25, 50 and 75, 50), Amount 1 and Amount 2 (-1000 to 1000; 10 and -10), Falloff (0 to 10, 5), every number keyable, Tile Edges (Off, On; On), Finer Controls (Off, On; Off) and Antialiasing (Low, Medium, High; Low). Each knot scales the picture about itself, most strongly at the knot and fading with distance by Falloff: a positive amount draws the picture in towards the knot, a negative one blows it out like a lens; Tile Edges fills what is drawn in from past the edges with a mirrored copy, otherwise it is clear; Finer Controls divides the amounts by 20; Antialiasing averages 1, 2 or 4 points a side in each pixel; the layer does not grow. **Deviations:** CycoreFX's manual gives no formula, so the pull, Falloff's reach and the amounts' scale are ours; Tile Edges mirrors the whole buffer the effect is given. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-FLOW-001 to 024 (`tools/flow_motion_reference.py`, cb8b4f4) in document 25; code b9d1b6d, the card's version made faster at 668d623 with the same pictures; `verification/D-385_flow_motion_table.md` 171 of 171. **On the card** in the warp pass (mode 14), every picture within 1 level of the processor (48 of 48); B-155 shows no fall-back to the processor; about 1.8 ms a 1080p layer on the card at Low, within Target P2, about 19 at High (sixteen points a pixel, over P2, the user's choice), about 16 and 78 on the processor (`verification/B-264_distort_timing_table.md`, PROVISIONAL, the machine was busy). The chosen corner is turned over onto Fold Position, the page rolling round a cylinder of the radius, its back the back page (or the paper colour) laid over the page's own picture and cut to its shape, shaded where it curls; Render shows both sides, only the front or only the back. The layer does not grow; a draft halves the radius. **Deviations:** CycoreFX's manual gives no formula, so the cylinder and the shading are ours; the back page is fixed to the paper, so a turned page shows it mirrored; with a corner the corner lands exactly on Fold Position only once the page is unrolled. D-389 / Power Pin, after CycoreFX's CC Power Pin (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Distort, CC Power Pin) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-09 under the owner's /loop request ("Implement it with GPU support where it makes sense, using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar"): every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-268.** **What was built.** A new effect, `core.power_pin`, Power Pin under our own name, built on Corner Pin's (D-198): Top Left, Top Right, Bottom Left and Bottom Right (per cent of the layer, its corners to start), Perspective (0 to 100, 100), Unstretch (off) and Expansion Top, Left, Right and Bottom (-40 to 100 per cent, 0), every number keyable. The layer is pinned to the four points, with true perspective at 100 and an even squeeze at 0; the expansions push each side of the pinned square out (or in) by its share, carried by the same map; Unstretch fills the layer's own frame with the pinned shape instead of growing the layer. A ring that is not convex, or a corner carried past its horizon, leaves the output clear. A draft changes nothing. **Deviations:** CycoreFX's manual gives no formula, so the blend between perspective and the even squeeze and the reading of the expansions are ours; there are no pin handles on the viewer yet. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-POWERPIN-001 to 025 (`tools/power_pin_reference.py`, f1a1403) in document 25; code 4a7f327; `verification/D-389_power_pin_table.md` 171 of 171. **On the card** in the warp pass (mode 17), every picture within 1 level of the processor; B-155 shows no fall-back to the processor; about 1.5 ms a 1080p layer on the card, within Target P2, about 6.6 on the processor (`verification/B-267_distort_timing_table.md`, PROVISIONAL, the machine was busy). D-390 / Ripple Pulse, after CycoreFX's CC Ripple Pulse (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Distort, CC Ripple Pulse) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-09 under the owner's /loop request ("Implement it with GPU support where it makes sense, using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar"): every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-269.** **What was built.** A new effect, `core.ripple_pulse`, Ripple Pulse under our own name: Center (per cent of the layer, 50, 50), Pulse Level (-1000 to 1000, 0), Time Span (0 to 10 seconds, 1), Amplitude (0 to 1000, 10) and Render Bump Map (off), every number keyable. Each change of Pulse Level sends a ring out from Center that reaches the layer's corners after the time span: a rise pushes the picture outward, a fall draws it in; a level that holds still for the whole time span leaves the layer as it is. The layer does not grow; a draft halves the amplitude. **Deviations:** CycoreFX's manual gives no formula, so the rings' shape and the amplitude's scale are ours; the level's history is read frame by frame, so a ring keyed between frames moves in whole-frame steps. D-395 / Arbitrary Map, after After Effects' PS Arbitrary Map (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Color Correction, PS Arbitrary Map) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-09 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-274.** **What was built.** `core.arbitrary_map` recolours a layer through a Photoshop arbitrary map (.amp), read by Adobe's file format specification as a lookup file of the project, as Color Lookup reads a .cube (D-182): kept where it is, copied by Collect Files, and a missing, unreadable or refused file reported with its reason on the card and in the status line and kept, never dropped. One table is the master, three red, green and blue, four the master then the three, five add alpha. Phase (-255 to 255 levels, keyable) cycles every table; Apply Phase Map To Alpha takes the covering through the fifth table as Curves' alpha curve (D-302). **Deviations:** Adobe does not publish Phase's range, so -255 to 255 levels is ours; a file of more than five tables (CMYK or multichannel) is refused rather than guessed. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-AMAP-001 to 022 (`tools/arbitrary_map_reference.py`, a943159a) in document 25; code 1949635f; `verification/D-395_arbitrary_map_table.md` 161 of 161. **On the card** in the tone pass (mode 11), every fixture picture identical to the processor's and every reference-shot picture within 1 level; with Apply Phase Map To Alpha on over a file with an alpha table the layer is drawn by the processor, as Curves' alpha curve is; B-155 shows no fall-back to the processor; about 1.1 ms a 1080p layer on the card, within Target P1, and about 4.9 to 5.1 ms on the processor (`verification/B-274_arbitrary_map_timing_table.md`, PROVISIONAL, the other lane's tests running). D-396 / Selective Color, after After Effects' Selective Color (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Color Correction, Selective Color) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-09 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-275.** **What was built.** `core.selective_color` turns the cyan, magenta, yellow and black up or down in one family of colours at a time: Method (relative, as Photoshop starts, or absolute) and nine families (reds, yellows, greens, cyans, blues, magentas, whites, neutrals, blacks), each four per cents, -100 to 100, keyable. Adobe does not publish the method; the rule is Clement Boesch's reverse-engineering of Photoshop's, published with FFmpeg's selectivecolor filter, and the reference reproduces his nine Photoshop measurements on (180, 100, 50) within 1 level and Adobe's 50% magenta example; the build reproduces the nine measurements too. A family of the wrong count or a method that is not one of the two words is kept and reported in words. **Deviations:** worked in fractions where FFmpeg rounds to whole levels; relative to start, as Photoshop, where FFmpeg starts absolute; After Effects' Colors menu (which family's sliders are shown) is not a setting. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-SELC-001 to 023 (`tools/selective_color_reference.py`, 2079f07b) in document 25; code ee2a7d55; `verification/D-396_selective_color_table.md` 159 of 159. **On the card** in the tone pass (mode 60), one pixel, every fixture picture within 1 level of the processor's (identical but for the keyed case) and every reference-shot picture within 1 level; B-155 shows no fall-back to the processor; about 1.0 to 1.3 ms a 1080p layer on the card, within Target P1, and about 4.3 to 5.4 ms on the processor (`verification/B-275_selective_color_timing_table.md`, PROVISIONAL, the other lane's tests running). D-397 / Color Grade, first unit, after Premiere Pro's and After Effects' Lumetri Color (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Color Correction, Lumetri Color) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-09 under the owner's /loop request ("Implement it with GPU support where it makes sense, using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar"): every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-276.** **What was built.** A new effect, `core.color_grade`, Lumetri Color under our own name, its first three sections: Basic Correction (Temperature, Tint, Exposure, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites, Blacks, Saturation), Creative (Look, a lut asset of the project picked as Color Lookup's file is; Look Intensity, Faded Film, Vibrance, Creative Saturation, Shadow Tint and Highlight Tint as a hue and an amount each, Tint Balance) and Vignette (Amount, Midpoint, Roundness, Feather), Lumetri's starting values so the effect as added changes nothing, every number keyable. The steps run in Lumetri's order, each that changes anything its own step. **Research.** Lumetri's sections, controls, ranges and order from ProVideo Coalition's "A closer look at the Lumetri Color panel", the Evergreen help wiki's "Lumetri Color - Premiere Pro" and Storyblocks' Lumetri guide; helpx.adobe.com refused automated reading (HTTP 403). None gives the maths. **Deviations:** Adobe publishes no formula, so every rule is ours (document 21), and each section says whose rule it follows: white balance as gains in linear light that keep white's brightness, and the tone sliders as smooth terms on the encoded values, are ours; Saturation, Vibrance and Creative Saturation are Vibrance's rule (D-140); the look is Color Lookup's reading (D-182) mixed by its intensity; Faded Film's shape is ours; the tints are Color balance's rule (D-130) with each hue's pure colour, its brightness taken out; the vignette is Vignette's rule (D-126) at |amount| × 20 per cent, black or white. Ranges are ours where the sources disagree (Exposure ±5 stops; the vignette's Amount ±5). On the card the grade is a chain of its own, not fused into a colour run, so a Mix (B-221) mixes the whole grade, as on the processor. D-398 / Color Grade, second unit, after Lumetri Color's Curves, Color Wheels and HSL Secondary (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Color Correction, Lumetri Color) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-09 under the owner's /loop request ("Implement it with GPU support where it makes sense, using our own effect names, with controls and defaults that feel familiar"): every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-277.** **What was built.** `core.color_grade` (D-397) gains four sections, run after the tints and before the vignette, each only when it changes anything: Curves (Master, Red, Green and Blue, each Curves' list of 2 to 16 points, and Hue vs Saturation, up to 16 points of a hue and its saturation); Color Wheels (Shadows, Midtones and Highlights, each a hue, an amount and a lightness, standing in for Lumetri's wheel and its slider); HSL Secondary (a key by hue with its range and softness, saturation and lightness each from a low to a high with one softness, Invert Key, and Show Key's mask view; then the keyed pixels corrected by their own Temperature, Tint, Contrast, Saturation and a wheel with its lightness).
