Lumetri's wheels are dragged as a point on a disc; ours are a hue and an amount. Below a hue range of 180 a grey, which has no hue, is not keyed. The key holds a pixel's HSL saturation at 1 at most, on the processor and the card alike: the arithmetic can carry a pure colour a rounding step past 1, which would leave it outside a band that ends at 100. With the mask view the vignette is not drawn. On the card each section is a stage of the grade's own chain: Curves' grade pass (mode 0), Color Balance's (mode 6), and two new tone modes, 42 (hue versus saturation) and 43 (the secondary). D-407 / Detail-preserving Upscale, after After Effects' Detail-preserving Upscale (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Distort, Detail-preserving Upscale) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-10 by the owner's choices of 2026-10-10: Fit to Comp Width / Height "One-time buttons (Recommended)" and the scale's range "1000%, like AE (Recommended)"; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-286.** **What was built.** `core.detail_upscale`, in Distort as **Detail-preserving Upscale**: Scale (100 to 1000 per cent, 100), Reduce Noise (0 to 100, 0) and Detail (0 to 100, 20), all keyable, and the Fit to Comp Width and Fit to Comp Height buttons (`effect.fit_scale`, document 24: Scale worked out once from the layer as it reaches the Upscale on the frame shown, written as any value is, a key when Scale has keys, Ctrl+Z takes it back). **Research.** Adobe's Detail-preserving Upscale help page (helpx.adobe.com, several localised copies of the same English text) for the controls: Scale's minimum of 100%, Reduce Noise applied before scaling, high Detail sharpening edges with possible ringing or halos, the Alpha choice (Bicubic by default, for speed) and the kinship with Photoshop's Preserve Details; an aejuice.com article on upscaling in After Effects and an Adobe community thread on taking a composition from HD to 4K (td-p/11696693), both on when to use it, neither with a formula or numbers to match. **Rule** in document 21: Gaussian softening, Lanczos-3 enlarging about the layer's middle, an unsharp mask of Detail / 50 at sigma Scale / 200, the hold. **Deviations:** Adobe's page names the controls and says what they do but gives no formula (the effect is related to Photoshop's Preserve Details resampling, which Adobe does not publish either), so the rule is ours: a Gaussian softening, Lanczos-3 resampling, an unsharp mask; it will not match After Effects pixel for pixel. Detail's starting value of 20 is ours (Adobe's page gives none); Scale starts at 100 and Reduce Noise at 0. After Effects' Alpha choice (the alpha channel enlarged by a cheaper filter, Bicubic by default, for speed) is left out: alpha goes through the same filter as colour. Fit to Comp Width / Height are one-time buttons, as the owner chose: they set Scale from the layer as it reaches the Upscale on the frame shown and are not remembered; on a hidden layer they are refused in words (the layer is not drawn, so there is no size to fit). A layer grown past 30000 pixels, After Effects' largest, or one whose memory cannot be had, is drawn without the Upscale and EFFECT_LAYER_TOO_LARGE (WARNING) says so; a memory failure inside the card's own fall-back to the processor is not reported separately, and an Upscale on an adjustment layer enlarges what is under it as any adjustment effect does. A draft scales Reduce Noise's sigma but not Detail's, which follows Scale (s / 2 pixels of the picture as drawn). **New diagnostic** EFFECT_LAYER_TOO_LARGE (WARNING, document 28), as the owner asked ("diagnose an out-of-memory case"); `tests/b12b_diagnostic_catalogue.rs` now lists it and EFFECT_PATH_MISSING (in document 28 since D-373 but missing from the test's built list, so that test failed on main before this), 64 identifiers. **On the card** warp mode 29 and sharp mode 2; the card's plan refuses a too-large Upscale with the same warning; every picture within 1 level of the processor (fixtures: 18 at 0 and 2 at 1 of 255; the reference shot under four settings at Full and Draft: 24 at 1); B-155 shows no fall-back. Fixtures FX-UPSCALE-001 to 020 (`tools/detail_upscale_reference.py`, e93e6d3c) in document 25; code 1462b70a; `verification/D-407_detail_upscale_table.md` 155 of 155 checks; app test `keyed_settings::fit_to_comp_sets_the_upscale_scale_once`. **Timing** (`verification/B-286_detail_upscale_timing_table.md`, a quiet machine, two rounds on the card): as added about 1.3 to 1.5 ms a 1080p layer on the card and 24 ms on the processor; scale 200 (each layer grown to 3840 by 2160) about 3.0 to 3.1 ms and 76 ms; inside Target P3 on the card. Gaps: After Effects' Alpha choice not offered; no viewer handles. Gaps (tutorial): no After Effects tutorial with Detail-preserving Upscale numbers was found (an SD-to-HD search gave none).

D-403 / Aerial Haze, PLUGINS.md's pick #8 (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Color Correction, Pick #8: Aerial Haze) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-09 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-282.** **What was built.** `core.aerial_haze` takes Haze Color (`#rrggbb`, #b4c8dc when added, a pale sky blue of our own; read in small letters, not keyable), Amount (0 to 100, 30 when added, keyable), a matte layer (D-189's layer setting, "" when added: even haze) and its fit (stretch when added, center, tile). Each pixel moves toward the haze colour in linear light at its own covering by amount / 100, times the picture luma of the fitted matte under it when one is named, as Gradient Wipe reads its map; a clear matte, or outside it, reads black and leaves no haze. It is the atmospheric model `I = J t + A (1 - t)` with `t = 1 - k`. A matte layer not in the composition leaves the layer as it is with EFFECT_LAYER_MISSING; one that names a circle is refused with EFFECT_LAYER_CYCLE. **Whose rule:** ours; taka2 gives the recipe but no numbers. **Sources read:** taka2's note on aerial perspective (note.com/taka2composite, 「空気遠近」を使いこなす, 2025-05-25): raise the black level rather than brighten, lower the saturation and shift bluish toward the colour of the air, made with Levels or Tone Curve; `docs/effects/PLUGINS.md` (the aerial perspective recipe row and pick #8, "Contrast-down plus blue-shift"). **Deviations:** the note says nothing about whites, and the one mix moves them toward the haze too (a white haze at 50 halves the distance to white; a pale haze darkens pure white a little); one colour does the black lift and the blue shift together, where the note uses Levels then a tint; the colour is not keyable. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-HAZE-001 to 025 and `cycle_two.json` (`tools/aerial_haze_reference.py`, 3ca29674) in document 25; code e88e2646; `verification/D-403_aerial_haze_table.md` 162 of 162. **On the card:** a new haze pass, the matte through `map_texture`; every fixture picture within 1 level (27 at 0, 16 at 1 of 255, the reference shot included); B-155 shows no fall-back to the processor. D-408 / Transform, after After Effects' Transform effect (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Distort, Transform) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-09 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-287.** **What was built.** `core.transform` takes Anchor Point and Position (x then y, per cent of the drawing's own width and height, -1000 to 1000, [50, 50] when added), Uniform Scale (on/off, on), Scale Height and Scale Width (-10000 to 10000 per cent, 100; with Uniform Scale on the scale both ways is Scale Height, as Skottie reads it), Skew (-85 to 85 degrees, After Effects' limit as Skottie holds it), Skew Axis and Rotation (-3600 to 3600 degrees), Opacity (0 to 100), Use Composition's Shutter Angle (on/off, on), Shutter Angle (0 to 360, 0) and Sampling (bilinear/bicubic, bilinear). The numbers are keyable, the words not. The drawing's point goes to T(P) R(rotation) K(skew, axis) S(width, height) T(-A); the output keeps the input's size (the layer never grows, what moves off it is cut off), sampled at the inverse, clear when the matrix cannot be undone (a scale of 0), times opacity / 100. Bicubic is Keys' cubic with a = -0.5, each number held at 0 or above and the covering at 1 or below. **The name.** No effect was called Transform; the layer's own Transform group sits apart from the Effects group in the timeline, so the effect keeps After Effects' name. **Motion blur, by the machinery we have (D-188).** Only with the layer's motion blur switch on and the composition's blur enabled (Adobe's page): the composition's moments, or with Use Composition's Shutter Angle off the effect's own angle centred on the frame with the composition's samples; the settings are read at each moment (keys at that moment, as D-188 reads a layer's), the pictures summed and divided once. No new machinery was needed. **Sources read:** Adobe's Distort effects page (helpx, through web.archive.org's 2023 copy), for the controls, "relative to the input layer" and the shutter's condition; Skia's Skottie `modules/skottie/src/Transform.cpp` (the matrix, skew held to 85) and `modules/skottie/src/effects/TransformEffect.cpp` (uniform reads Scale Height; opacity a multiplier), read, not ported. **Deviations:** Adobe does not say how it samples bicubic, or whether its skew shears the way Skottie's does; ours are Keys' a = -0.5 and Skottie's. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-XFORM-001 to 032 (`tools/transform_reference.py`, 06275bb0) in document 25; code bf642e8f; `verification/D-408_transform_table.md` 184 of 184. **On the card:** warp mode 22, the map and the bicubic in f64; every fixture picture within 1 level (16 at 0, 34 at 1 of 255, the reference shot included); B-155 shows no fall-back to the processor. D-409 / Lens Chromatic Aberration, PLUGINS.md's pick #3 with its RGB Separation row as a mode (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Distort, Pick #3) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-10 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-288.** **What was built.** PLUGINS.md says to extend `core.chromatic_aberration` rather than add an effect, so it gains a new form: a file whose effect carries `mode` is the new form; one without it is D-120's form, read, saved and drawn by D-120's code unchanged (FX-CHROMA-001 to 016 keep pinning it, as D-383 and D-401 kept older files). The new form takes Mode (radial or offset, not keyable), Amount (0 to 100 pixels, 3), Centre (radial, per cent, [50, 50]), Angle (offset, -3600 to 3600 degrees, 90; 0 up, 90 right), Falloff (radial, 0 to 100, 0), Red, Green and Blue Scale (-200 to 200 per cent, 100, 0 and -100) and Fringe Blur (0 to 100 per cent of each channel's own shift, 0). At the starting values the picture is D-120's, bit for bit on the processor, so a Chromatic Aberration added from the panel now starts in the new form. Radial: each channel moves along the line from the centre by its scale times amount times rho^(2 falloff / 100), rho the distance over the half-diagonal, so the corner's shift is the amount at any falloff. Offset: the same shift everywhere, along the angle. Fringe blur takes ceil(amount |scale| blur) + 1 samples evenly along the shift, centred on it, and averages them. The covering is the largest of the three channels'. **Sources read:** `docs/effects/PLUGINS.md` (the pick's rows: Lens Chromatic Aberration's falloff, per-channel scale and fringe blur, and RGB Separation's straight offset, "extend `core.chromatic_aberration`"); D-120's rule in document 21. **Deviations:** the plugins' own curves are not published; the falloff's power and the even fringe samples are ours. D-416 / Fractal, After Effects' Fractal (Generate) (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Generate) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-10 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-295.** **What was built.** `core.fractal`, with After Effects' controls: Set Choice (Mandelbrot when added, Mandelbrot Inverse, Mandelbrot Over Julia, Mandelbrot Inverse Over Julia, Julia, Julia Inverse), Equation (z^2 + c when added, up to z^6), Mandelbrot Center and Julia Center (-10 to 10, keyable, (-0.75, 0) and (0, 0)), the two Magnifications (-10 to 40, keyable, 0), the two Escape Limits (1 to 10000, keyable, 100), Overlay, Transparency and Edge Highlight (off when added), Palette (Lightness Gradient when added, Hue Wheel, Black And White, Solid Color), Hue (degrees, keyable, 0), Cycle Steps (1 to 1000, 10) and Cycle Offset (0 to 1000, 0), Oversample Method (Edge Detect when added, Brute Force) and Oversample Factor (1 to 8, 2). The set is drawn in place of the layer; the layer never grows. A draft halves the drawing, so the view is the same, and turns the oversampling off. **Sources read:** Adobe's help page on the Generate effects: Fractal "renders the Mandelbrot or Julia set, creating colorful textures ... the set is the area that is colored black. Any pixel outside the set is colorized, depending on how close it is to the set", and "if the path leads out of the bounded rectangle (-2, -2, 2, 2), it has gone into infinity ... the starting-point color is based on how many line segments it takes to reach infinity. D-420 / Audio Spectrum, After Effects' Audio Spectrum (Generate) (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Generate) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-10 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-299.** **What was built.** `core.audio_spectrum`, with After Effects' controls: Audio Layer (a sound layer of the composition, none when added), Start Point and End Point (per cent, -1000 to 1000, keyable, 10 50 and 90 50), Path (a mask number, 0 none), Use Polar Path (off), Start Frequency and End Frequency (1 to 20000 Hz, keyable, 20 and 2000), Frequency Bands (1 to 4096, keyable, 64), Maximum Height (0 to 10000 pixels, keyable, 200, a distance), Audio Duration (1 to 30000 ms, keyable, 90), Audio Offset (-30000 to 30000 ms, keyable, 0), Thickness (0 to 10000 pixels, keyable, 3, a distance), Softness (0 to 100, keyable, 50), Inside Color (white), Outside Color (#3c8cff), Blend Overlapping Colors, Hue Interpolation (-3600 to 3600 degrees, keyable, 0), Dynamic Hue Phase, Color Symmetry, Display Options (Digital, Analog Lines, Analog Dots), Side Options (Side A, Side B, Side A & B), Duration Averaging and Composite On Original (off). A WAV's samples are read (8, 16, 24 and 32-bit whole numbers, 32 and 64-bit floating point) and kept while the file stays the same; each frame's levels are worked out before the effect is drawn, so frames with different sound are told apart. The layer never grows. **Sources read:** Adobe's After Effects user manual, pages 509 to 510 of the copy on manualsdir.com (Audio Spectrum): it "display[s] the audio spectrum of a layer that contains audio", the controls and what each does; no formula, no window, no scale for a level, so the rule is ours, nothing ported. **Interpretations (ours):** a Hann window over Audio Duration; one Fourier sum per band (no transform size, so no rounding to a power of two); the bands spaced evenly in hertz from Start to End Frequency; each band's level 2 |sum x_k w_k e^(-2 pi i f k / rate)| / sum w_k, so a sine of amplitude A reads A, and its bar Maximum Height times the level held to 1; Use Polar Path round Start Point from straight up, clockwise; Side A along the line's left-hand normal (up for a line drawn left to right); Duration Averaging the mean of three windows half a window apart; the marks drawn as Beam's line (D-207). **Deviation:** Adobe says the effect "uses the audio source footage without time-remapping, effects, stretch, or levels"; we apply the sound layer's gain (FX-ASPEC-028). **Gaps:** only WAV files are read (another format draws silence and says MEDIA_AUDIO_UNREADABLE); no viewer handles for Start Point and End Point; Path takes closed masks only (Adobe allows an open mask path); the After Effects look is not matched pixel for pixel. **New diagnostic** EFFECT_SOUND_MISSING (WARNING, document 28) for an Audio Layer naming a layer with no sound; EFFECT_PATH_MISSING and EFFECT_LAYER_MISSING reused for a missing mask and a missing layer; each is said on opening and on the frame, the effect kept as written and drawing nothing; `tests/b12b_diagnostic_catalogue.rs` lists 65 identifiers. **Fixture project correction** (5a1a70d8): the sound layer in FX-ASPEC-001 to 053's projects no longer carries "transform": {} (document 19, D-71, gives an audio layer no transform); every expected value unchanged. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-ASPEC-001 to 053 (`tools/audio_spectrum_reference.py`, 11954d02) in document 25; code 102dd908; `verification/D-420_audio_spectrum_table.md` 328 of 328. **On the card:** its own "marks" pass (the levels worked out on the processor); every drawn fixture on the card at Full and Draft with difference 0, the reference shot with a sound layer within 1 level in seven settings; B-155 shows no fall-back to the processor. Three layers after a moving Noise, card / processor: as added 49.8 / 56.5 ms a frame against 27.9 / 54.7 for the Noise alone, Analog Dots round the middle 75.7 / 66.7: the card is not quicker for this effect at these settings (`verification/B-299_audio_spectrum_timing_table.md`, quiet). D-421 / Audio Waveform, After Effects' Audio Waveform (Generate) (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Generate) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-10 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-300.** **What was built.** `core.audio_waveform`, with After Effects' controls: Audio Layer (a sound layer of the composition, none when added), Start Point and End Point (per cent, -1000 to 1000, keyable, 10 50 and 90 50), Path (a mask number, 0 to 1000, 0 none), Displayed Samples (1 to 4096, keyable, 32), Maximum Height (0 to 10000 pixels, keyable, 300, a distance), Audio Duration (1 to 30000 ms, keyable, 90), Audio Offset (-30000 to 30000 ms, keyable, 0), Thickness (0 to 10000 pixels, keyable, 2, a distance), Softness (0 to 100, keyable, 50), Random Seed (Analog) (0 to 100000, keyable, its whole part counted, 1), Inside Color (white), Outside Color (#3c8cff), Waveform Options (Mono, Left, Right), Display Options (Digital, Analog Lines, Analog Dots; Analog Lines) and Composite On Original (off). The sound is read as Audio Spectrum's (D-420): a WAV's samples kept while the file stays the same, each frame's least and greatest worked out before the effect is drawn. The layer never grows. **Sources read:** Adobe's After Effects user manual, the copy on manualsdir.com read for D-420, its Audio Waveform section: Digital "displays each sample as a single vertical line connecting the minimum and maximum source sample"; "Nonstereo audio layers play as Mono"; Composite On Original composites the waveform with the layer "using the Add blending mode". No formula: how a displayed sample is taken, how tall it stands and how the seed picks are not said, so the rule is ours, nothing ported. **Interpretations (ours):** displayed sample j of D covers the window's source samples from floor(j N / D) up to floor((j + 1) N / D), at least one, and takes their least and greatest, held to -1..1; Mono the channels' mean, Left channel 0, Right channel 1 (channel 0 of a one-channel file); a level stands Maximum Height times the level along the line's left-hand normal (up for a line drawn left to right), at (j + 1/2) / D along the line or round the mask; Digital a stroke from least to greatest; Analog Lines and Analog Dots take the greatest where the top bit of mix(mix(seed) xor j) is set (SplitMix64's finaliser, `grade::mix`), else the least; the marks drawn as Audio Spectrum's (Beam's line, D-207); Composite On Original off, the waveform stands alone. **Deviation:** as D-420, the sound layer's gain is applied. **Behaviour changes in this code:** the path-missing and sound-missing warnings now name the effect ("Layer X's Audio Waveform ..."; Audio Spectrum's now ends "without the Audio Spectrum"); an effect whose settings are refused is no longer also checked for a missing path or sound on opening (FX-AWAVE-042 says only EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID). The D-420 fixtures still pass unchanged. **Shared drawing:** `layer_fx::sound_feet`, `Marks` and `draw_marks`, Audio Spectrum's, now with two call sites. **Gaps:** only WAV files are read (another format draws silence and says MEDIA_AUDIO_UNREADABLE); no viewer handles for Start Point and End Point; Path takes closed masks only (Adobe allows an open mask path); the After Effects look is not matched pixel for pixel. D-417 / Grid, After Effects' Grid (Generate) (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Generate) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-10 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-296.** **What was built.** `core.grid`, with After Effects' controls: Anchor and Corner (per cent of the drawing, -1000 to 1000, keyable, (50, 50) and (60, 60)), Size From (Corner Point when added, Width Slider, Width & Height Sliders, the cell exactly as Checkerboard's, D-413), Width and Height (1 to 10000 pixels, keyable, 64), Border (0 to 10000 pixels, keyable, 2), Feather Width and Height (0 to 10000 pixels, keyable, 0), Invert Grid (off when added), Color (white), Opacity (0 to 100, keyable, 100) and Blending Mode (Checkerboard's eight: None when added, Normal, Add, Multiply, Screen, Overlay, Soft Light, Stencil Alpha). Lines run along the cells' edges through the anchor; each pixel is covered by the share of a box max(feather, 1) wide that falls inside a line Border thick, the two directions joined as gx + gy - gx gy, Invert 1 minus that; the result is laid as Checkerboard's pattern is (`lay_pattern`). The layer never grows; a draft halves the distances. **Sources read:** Adobe's help page on the Generate effects, through its search snippets (the page refused automated reading): Grid "creates a customizable grid", which "you can render ... in a solid color or as a mask in the alpha channel of the source layer"; Border is "the thickness of the grid lines" and "a value of 0 makes the grid disappear"; Invert Grid "inverts the transparent and opaque areas of the grid". No formula and no starting values were found, so the rule is ours and nothing is ported. **Interpretations (ours):** the cell and Size From exactly as Checkerboard's (After Effects shares the controls); the anchor on a crossing; the feather as a box blur of the line, at least 1 pixel, so an unfeathered line is antialiased by exact coverage; upright and level lines joined as a screen, so crossings are not doubled; Stencil Alpha as the mask in the alpha channel Adobe describes; the starting values. **Gaps:** no viewer handles for Anchor or Corner. D-450 / Noise Alpha, After Effects' Noise Alpha (Noise & Grain) (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Noise & Grain) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-10 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-330.** **What was built.** `core.noise_alpha`, with every one of After Effects' controls: Noise (Uniform Random when added, Squared Random, Uniform Animation, Squared Animation), Amount (0 to 100 per cent, 20), Original Alpha (Clamp when added, Add, Scale, Edges), Overflow (Clip when added, Wrap Back, Wrap), Random Seed (0 to 100000, 0, its whole part), Noise Phase (-100000 to 100000 degrees, 0), Cycle Noise (off) and Cycle (1 to 1000, 1, its whole part); the numbers keyable. D-446 / Curl Noise, After Effects' Curl Noise (Noise & Grain, new in 26.3) (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Noise & Grain) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-10 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-326.** **What was built.** `core.curl_noise` with After Effects' controls: Source (Internal; This Layer and Other Layer kept and refused), Speed and Direction, the Transform's Size and Offset, Evolution, Turbulence Speed, Swirl, Density, Smoothness, Vertical Bias, Sample Count, Sample Radius, Flow Softness, Edge Definition, Flow Falloff, View (Final Render, Input Noise, Curl Generation), Contrast, Brightness, Clip HDR Results and Channel (RGB, Red, Green, Blue, Alpha), every number keyable. D-445 / Turbulent Noise, after After Effects' Turbulent Noise (Noise & Grain) (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Noise & Grain) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-10 under the owner's /loop request, by D-383's "Both names, one engine" and D-394's "Second name, one engine"; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-325.** **What was built.** `core.turbulent_noise` takes After Effects' Fractal Type (Basic when added, Turbulent), Noise Type (Smooth when added, Block), Invert (off), Contrast (0 to 1000, 100), Brightness (-1000 to 1000, 0), the size of a cloud (1 to 1000 pixels, 100) with Scale Width and Scale Height (1 to 10000 per cent of it, 100), Offset Turbulence (pixels, x then y, 0, 0), Complexity (1 to 20, 6), Evolution (degrees, 0), Random Seed (0 to 100000, 0), Opacity (0 to 100, 100) and Blending Mode (Normal when added, Multiply, Screen, Add); every number keyable. It has no speed, no colours and no Cycle Evolution, as After Effects' has none. It is a second name over Fractal Noise's engine (D-128, D-299): Fractal Noise with no speed, black to white, never cycling (`effects::turbulent_fractal`), on the processor and on the card's Fractal Noise pass (grade mode 9), timed as Fractal Noise's stage, so no new stage. Fractal Noise is unchanged: FX-FRACTAL-001 to 028 rerun in the table (022 and 024 superseded by D-318, as b71 has them), and Turbulent Noise matches Fractal Noise with the same settings, speed 0, black to white and cycle 0 byte for byte on four street pictures. **Whose rule:** Adobe publishes no formula for either noise; ours is Fractal Noise's, nothing ported. **Sources read:** Lester Banks, "Exploring the differences between Fractal and Turbulent Noise in After Effects" (lesterbanks.com/?p=23867), for Turbulent Noise as the faster Fractal Noise with fewer controls; the Adobe community thread "Cycle Evolution option missing in Turbulent Noise" (community.adobe.com/t5/after-effects-discussions/cycle-evolution-option-missing-in-turbulent-noise/m-p/12157825), that it has no Cycle Evolution; the Adobe community thread "Fractal Noise vs Turbulent Noise render speed comparison" (community.adobe.com/t5/after-effects-discussions/fractal-noise-vs-turbulent-noise-render-speed-comparison/td-p/15602346), for its speed; our Fractal Noise (D-128, D-299, D-318, D-319, D-326, document 21) for the rule. **Deviations from After Effects' Turbulent Noise:** Fractal Type only Basic and Turbulent (After Effects has a dozen or more, Dynamic, Max, Rocky and the rest); Noise Type only Smooth and Block (After Effects has Block, Linear, Soft Linear and Spline); no Overflow (clipped in a Display composition, past white kept in Float, as Fractal Noise's D-319); no Transform Rotation, Uniform Scaling or Perspective Offset; no Sub Settings (each octave fixed at half the strength and twice the detail); Complexity 1 to 20, its whole part; Blending Mode only Normal, Multiply, Screen and Add; the noise is P0-19's value noise, not Adobe's, so the picture is not matched pixel for pixel; D-461 / Hex Tile, After Effects' CC HexTile (Stylize) (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Stylize) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-11 under the owner's /loop request (and the owner's 2026-10-11 go-ahead to proceed with my recommendations); every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-341.** **What was built.** `core.hex_tile` with every one of After Effects' controls: Render (Tile, Fold Aligned, Fold Seamlessly; Tile), Radius (1 to 4000 pixels, 50, scaled with a draft), Center (per cent of the picture, 50, 50), Lock Center Tile (off), Rotate (-3600 to 3600 degrees, 0) and Smearing (0 to 100 per cent, 0); the numbers keyable. Each pixel finds its hexagon (flat top and bottom) and reads the picture round the centre at its place in that tile, turned by Rotate; the folds fill each tile from one of its six triangles, Fold Seamlessly mirroring every other one so neighbours meet with no seam; Smearing moves each tile's read towards its own place, so at 100 under Tile the picture is as it was; reads past the edges are mirrored back, as Kaleidoscope's (D-205) are, so nothing goes clear. **Sources read:** the CycoreFX HD 1.8.1 manual's CC HexTile page (Render: Tile, Fold Aligned, Fold Seamlessly; Radius; Center; Lock Center Tile, off at first; Rotate; Smearing) and Adobe's page listing the Cycore effects. No formula was published, so the rule beyond what they show is ours, nothing ported. **Gaps:** no formula was published, so the honeycomb's orientation (flat top and bottom), the rounding to the nearest tile, what the two folds do inside a tile (six triangles turned from the first, every other one mirrored under Fold Seamlessly) and the mirroring at the picture's edges are our own reading of the manual's words; After Effects' defaults and ranges are not published, so ours are our own (Tile, radius 50, centre in the middle, unlocked, no turn, no smearing); at Draft a radius under 4 falls below 1 and Hex Tile is left out with a warning, as Rain's spacing is (B-107), on the processor and the card alike; After Effects' look is not matched pixel for pixel. D-583 / Curl Noise, Source This Layer and Other Layer, after After Effects' Curl Noise (Noise & Grain, 26.3) Source menu (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Noise & Grain) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-12 under the owner's /loop request (and the owner's 2026-10-11 go-ahead to proceed with my recommendations); every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-461.** **What was built.** `core.curl_noise` takes `source` `this_layer` or `other_layer`, `source_layer` (D-189's layer word), `softness` 0 to 100, `source_mapping` `fill` or `center` and `mirror_at_edge`, written only when not as added (D-304). The noise is the picture's lightness plane (luminance times covering, blurred by Softness, sigma Softness / 10 pixels), read between pixels at the slid point; its slope steers the flow lines, under 1e-5 nought; This Layer reads the layer as it reaches the effect, Other Layer D-189's map fitted by Source Mapping; Other Layer naming no layer is refused, a missing layer drops the effect with EFFECT_LAYER_MISSING. Under D-566, FX-CURL-033 (This Layer, refused while not built) was regenerated as a working This Layer case and FX-CURL-034 stays refused, reworded to Other Layer naming no layer, its frames unchanged; FX-CURL-001 to 032 and 035 to 044 hold. FX-CURL-033 was first written (0ba12eef) with the settings as they start (flow lines 30 long, 12 samples) and the build missed it at one pixel, (6, 7), by 9.9e-5 against document 25's 2e-5. The cause, traced: the build decodes the drawing's pixels in single precision, the reference in double, so a few lightness values differ in the last bit, and 30-pixel flow lines crossing the card's sharp edges magnify that about 1000 times. By the coordinator's ruling of 2026-10-12, before any code was committed against it, a second fixtures commit (175346ea) gave 033 the small cells and lines the other D-583 cases use; the settings as they start are compared card against processor on the reference shot instead (B-461's "This Layer as added" rows, within 1 level). **Sources read:** Adobe's community announcement "New in Beta: Curl Noise, swirling animated 2D noise" (community.adobe.com/announcements-532/new-in-beta-curl-noise-swirling-animated-2d-noise-26-3x46-1557745), for the Source menu (Internal, This Layer, Other Layer) with Source Layer, Softness, Source Mapping and Mirror at Edge; the Starry Night tutorial below; Bridson, Hourihan and Nordenstam (SIGGRAPH 2007), as D-446. No formula published. **Gaps:** Adobe publishes no formula, so the picture's lightness as the noise, its slope as the flow, the luminance (Rec. 709) and the Softness scale (sigma Softness / 10 pixels) are ours; Size and Density do not scale the picture, only the seed's blocks; no Transform Rotation, Scale or Perspective, as before; known deviation: with long flow lines over a picture with sharp edges, the build and the reference program can differ by up to about 1e-4 at a few pixels (single against double precision in the drawing's decode, magnified along the lines), which is why FX-CURL-033 uses small lines; FX-CURL-033 was first written (0ba12eef) with the settings as they start (flow lines 30 long, 12 samples) and the build missed it at one pixel, (6, 7), by 9.9e-5 against document 25's 2e-5. The cause, traced: the build decodes the drawing's pixels in single precision, the reference in double, so a few lightness values differ in the last bit, and 30-pixel flow lines crossing the card's sharp edges magnify that about 1000 times. By the coordinator's ruling of 2026-10-12, before any code was committed against it, a second fixtures commit (175346ea) gave 033 the small cells and lines the other D-583 cases use; the settings as they start are compared card against processor on the reference shot instead (B-461's "This Layer as added" rows, within 1 level). Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-CURL-045 to 060 (`tools/curl_noise_reference.py`, 0ba12eef and 175346ea) in document 25; code dea24e0a; `verification/D-583_curl_sources_table.md` 138 of 138. **On the card:** the picture's lightness plane is made on the card, bit-identical to the processor's; Softness is a new pass `curlsoft` that sums the blur exactly as the processor does (each product rounded to single precision on its own, through double, so the card cannot fuse it into the add); `curlfield` reads the plane; and `curlflow`'s walk reads the field the same exact way (`curl_sample`), which Internal also uses now. Without these the card fused the sums and long flow lines through a rough picture magnified the last-bit difference to 9 to 128 levels; with them every comparison is within 1 level. D-454 / Match Grain, After Effects' Match Grain (Noise & Grain) (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Noise & Grain) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-10 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-334.** **What was built.** `core.match_grain`: Noise Source Layer (none when added; a layer of the composition) and every setting of Add Grain (D-443) with its range and value when added, the numbers keyable; the intensities are multiples of the grain measured. The noise source's whole picture is read with its effects, its grain measured in red, green and blue, and Add Grain lays grain that spread in each channel. No noise source, a flat one or intensity 0 changes nothing; a noise source that is no layer leaves the layer as it is and says EFFECT_LAYER_MISSING. **Sources read:** Adobe's After Effects user guide, Match Grain effect (manualsdir.com/manuals/753844/adobe-after-effects.html?page=605 and 606) and the Noise & Grain help page (helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/using/noise-grain-effects.html, through search excerpts): it "matches the noise between two images" from a Noise Source Layer, measured in sample boxes, with Add Grain's Tweaking, Color and Application groups and Compensate for Existing Noise; no formula. The measure is J. Immerkaer, "Fast Noise Variance Estimation", Computer Vision and Image Understanding 64(2):300-302, 1996, doi:10.1006/cviu.1996.0060. Nothing is ported. **Interpretations (ours):** Adobe publishes no formula, ranges or values when added for this effect, so these are ours: the grain is measured over the whole noise source layer as drawn with its own effects (as Color Link's, D-375), in each channel of its straight colour through the sRGB curve, by Immerkaer's fast noise estimate, sigma = sqrt(pi/2) / (6 N) times the sum of |[[1,-2,1],[-2,4,-2],[1,-2,1]] * I| over the N 3 by 3 windows whose nine pixels all show (0 when there are none); each channel's Add Grain intensity is multiplied by sigma times 10 sqrt(3), because Add Grain's blocky grain at intensity 1 spreads 0.1 / sqrt(3); every other setting, range and value when added is Add Grain's (D-443); the noise source none when added. **Gaps:** the sample boxes and the whole Sampling group (After Effects measures only where its boxes are put; ours measures the whole noise source), Compensate for Existing Noise, View Mode and Preview Region (always the final result over the whole layer), the Tweaking group's per-channel size and Channel Balance, Tint, Application's Mask/Matte Layer, and the noise source's own time controls are not offered; Blend with Original is the effect's own Mix (D-202); Size, Softness and Aspect Ratio are not measured but set by hand, as Add Grain's; Film lays the measured grain fully only in a channel's middle (Add matches it everywhere); Softness above 0 lays softer and so weaker grain than measured; a draft measures its own smaller picture. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-MATCHGRAIN-001 to 023 (`tools/match_grain_reference.py`, 23039cb6) in document 25; code 28fd0d4c and c540033e; `verification/D-454_match_grain_table.md` 152 of 152. **On the card:** the measure on the processor (one sum over the noise source), then Add Grain's grade pass, mode 10. All 23 fixture projects at Full and Draft and the reference shot (three layers, three settings, three frames, Full and Draft) within 1 level, 41 of 41; B-155 shows no fall-back to the processor. Left on the processor: the measure (a card reduction would serve it, Match Grain and Remove Grain alike). **Timing** (`verification/B-334_match_grain_timing_table.md`), card / processor, again, PROVISIONAL (the graphics card was 97% busy with other work while no cargo, rustc or test process was running): Noise alone 16.8 / 42.4 ms a frame, as added (no noise source) 16.8 / 43.2, reading layer2 111.8 / 115.8, reading layer2, size 3, softness 0.5, monochromatic 106.1 / 110.4; within Target P4 (100 ms or less on the processor): about 23 to 24 ms a layer on the processor, measuring included; on the card about 30 to 32 ms a layer, the measure being on the processor; to be measured again on a quiet machine. D-455 / Remove Grain, After Effects' Remove Grain (Noise & Grain) (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Noise & Grain) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-10 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-335.** **What was built.** `core.remove_grain`: Noise Reduction, Passes and Mode (Noise Reduction Settings) and the Unsharp Mask's Amount, Radius and Threshold, the numbers keyable. The layer's grain is measured in red, green and blue, then smoothed by passes of an edge-keeping (bilateral) filter as strong as the grain measured, then sharpened. Noise Reduction 0 or a layer with no grain changes nothing. **Sources read:** Adobe's After Effects user guide, Remove Grain effect (manualsdir.com/manuals/753844/adobe-after-effects.html?page=609 and 610): it "differentiates fine image detail from grain and noise"; Noise Reduction sets how much is removed, Passes "control the maximum noise radius that can be detected", Multichannel "degrains all channels of a color image together" and Single Channel "degrains each channel independently", and the Unsharp Mask can "return subtle edge detail that the degraining removed"; no formula. The pieces are J. Immerkaer, "Fast Noise Variance Estimation", CVIU 64(2):300-302, 1996; C. Tomasi and R. Manduchi, "Bilateral Filtering for Gray and Color Images", ICCV 1998; M. Zhang and B. Gunturk, "Multiresolution bilateral filtering for image denoising", IEEE TIP 17(12):2324-2333, 2008 (the 2-sigma range spread). Nothing is ported. **Interpretations (ours):** Adobe publishes no formula, ranges or values when added for this effect, so these are ours: the layer's grain as it reaches the effect is measured as Match Grain measures its source (D-454, Immerkaer 1996); pass k of Passes (1 to 4, the whole part) is a bilateral filter on the encoded straight colour over the taps within 2k pixels, spatial spread k, weighed by covering, whose colour spread is h_c = 2 n sigma_c (Multichannel: one weight, h = 2 n sqrt(mean sigma_c^2); Single Channel: one per channel, a channel with h_c = 0 kept), n Noise Reduction 0 to 3 (1); each pass works on the last; the Unsharp Mask is D-147/D-317's Sharpen, amount 0 to 500 (0), radius 0 to 100 (1), threshold 0 to 255 (0); Mode Multichannel when added. **Gaps:** View Mode and Preview Region (always the final output over the whole layer), Channel Noise Reduction, the Fine Tuning group (Chroma Suppression, Texture, Noise Size Bias, Clean Solid Areas), Temporal Filtering, and the Sampling group with its sample boxes are not offered (ours measures the whole layer as it reaches the effect); Blend with Original is the effect's own Mix (D-202); a draft measures and denoises its own smaller picture with the same discs (the Unsharp Mask's radius is scaled, as Sharpen's); high Noise Reduction on heavy grain softens edges as any bilateral filter does, since its colour spread grows past the edges' steps (`4_strong.png`); an Unsharp Mask with a threshold is drawn on the processor (as D-317's Sharpen). Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-REMOVEGRAIN-001 to 021 (`tools/remove_grain_reference.py`, ac80b2a8) in document 25; code 3badaee1; `verification/D-455_remove_grain_table.md` 137 of 137. **On the card:** compose measures the layer before the frame (it draws the layer up to the effect on the processor and sums it, as the card cannot read back mid-chain), then a new degrain pass (encode, one bilateral pass each, decode) and Sharpen's pass. All 21 fixture projects at Full and Draft and the reference shot (three layers after a moving Noise, three settings, three frames, Full and Draft) within 1 level, 39 of 39; B-155 shows no fall-back to the processor. Left on the processor: the measure (a card reduction would serve it, Match Grain and Remove Grain alike) and an Unsharp Mask with a threshold (D-317). **Timing** (`verification/B-335_remove_grain_timing_table.md`), card / processor, again, PROVISIONAL (the card was at 96 to 100 per cent with other work and lane A's b327 test was running): Noise alone 40.1 / 52.0 ms a frame, as added 196.0 / 183.9, Noise Reduction 2, three passes, single channel 325.8 / 480.8, as added with Unsharp Mask 150 436.9 / 217.9; over Target P3 (8 ms or less added on the card): about 52 to 132 ms a layer on the card, the measure (the layer drawn again up to the effect, then summed) on the processor included; on the processor about 44 to 143 ms a layer; to be measured again on a quiet machine. D-456 / Deband, our own effect after CelFX's Deband (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Noise & Grain, `PLUGINS.md` pick #18) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-10 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-336.** **What was built.** `core.deband`, named Deband, with CelFX's control list: View, Edge Threshold, Edge Softness, Blur Amount, Edge Blur Reduction, Diffusion Amount, Edge Diffusion Reduction, Diffusion Reseed Interval, Noise Amount, Edge Noise Reduction and Noise Reseed Interval, the numbers keyable. Flat areas are found by how much each pixel steps from its neighbours; there the steps of a banded gradient are blurred away, never through an edge, then a fine diffusion and dither keep them from coming back; near edges all three are pulled back. Blur, diffusion and noise all 0 change nothing. **Sources read:** P SOFTHOUSE's CelFX reference, P_Deband (docs.psoft.co.jp/cfx100w/en/latest/reference/CFX_Deband.html): it "complements color bands that occur in subtle gradients by applying smoothing" and names the controls (View: Normal, Edge Only, Selected Edge; Edge Threshold; Edge Softness; Blur Amount; Edge Blur Reduction; Diffusion Amount; Edge Diffusion Reduction; Diffusion Reseed Interval; Noise Amount; Edge Noise Reduction; Noise Reseed Interval, "0: never changes, 1: changes every frame"); no formula, ranges or starting values. The pieces are E. Gastal and M. Oliveira, "Domain Transform for Edge-Aware Image and Video Processing", SIGGRAPH 2011; S. Lipshitz, R. Wannamaker and J. Vanderkooy, "Quantization and Dither: A Theoretical Survey", JAES 40(5), 1992. Nothing is ported. **Interpretations (ours):** CelFX's page names the controls and gives nothing else, so these are ours: the edge weight E from the largest step to the four neighbours, 0 at or below Edge Threshold (0 to 255, 4), 1 at or above it plus Edge Softness (0 to 255, 2); an edge-stopping normalised Gaussian blur, across then down, sigma Blur Amount / 3 (0 to 100, 8), each tap weighed a (1 - E) and stopped by the edges between (in the spirit of Gastal and Oliveira's domain transform, SIGGRAPH 2011), pulled back on edges by Edge Blur Reduction (0 to 100, 100); the diffusion reads a tap up to Diffusion Amount (0 to 20, 1) pixels away (D-119's hash); the noise is triangular dither (Lipshitz, Wannamaker and Vanderkooy, JAES 1992) of Noise Amount levels (0 to 32, 1); each reduced near edges by its reduction (0 to 100, 100) and reseeded every whole Reseed Interval frames (0 to 100, 1; 0 never), P0-23's held step. **Gaps:** CelFX publishes no formula, ranges or starting values, so our pictures are not CelFX's; the dither is one number for the three channels; edges are found on the layer's straight colour through the sRGB curve, in levels of 255, against its four neighbours; a draft scales Blur Amount and Diffusion Amount, the thresholds (levels) not. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-DEBAND-001 to 024 (`tools/deband_reference.py`, 69230f1f) in document 25; code fc729350; `verification/D-456_deband_table.md` 157 of 157. **On the card:** a new deband pass (mode 0 the encoded colour and 1 - E, modes 2 and 3 the blur across and down, mode 5 the diffusion, dither and views). Tiny blur weights can decide a ratio, so 1 - E is kept rather than E in single precision, the sums across go through a double-precision buffer, and mode 5 works E again in double precision where it moves a diffusion offset. All 24 fixture projects at Full and Draft and the reference shot (three settings, three frames, Full and Draft) within 1 level, 42 of 42; B-155 shows no fall-back to the processor. Left on the processor: nothing. **Over the target:** the blur in double precision is the cost (this card runs double precision far slower than single); a single-precision blur would be several times faster but strays past 1 level where tiny weights decide the ratio, so it is left as a proposal for the owner, not built. **Timing** (`verification/B-336_deband_timing_table.md`), card / processor, again: the shot alone 11.4 / 20.3 ms a frame, as added 52.4 / 234.7, blur 30, diffusion 4, noise 4 75.1 / 306.3; over Target P2 (4 ms or less added on the card): about 13.7 to 21.2 ms a layer on the card; on the processor about 71 to 95 ms a layer. Gaps (tutorial): none found.

D-457 / Advanced Spill Suppressor, after After Effects' Advanced Spill Suppressor (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Keying) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-10 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-337.** **What was built.** `core.advanced_spill_suppressor`, named Advanced Spill Suppressor, with After Effects' controls: Method (Standard, Ultra), Suppression, and for Ultra Key Color, Tolerance, Desaturate, Spill Range, Spill Color Correction and Luma Correction, the numbers keyable. It takes the green or blue a screen throws onto a keyed subject back out. Suppression 0, or Ultra at Tolerance 0, changes nothing. **Overlap checked:** no despill existed (Color Key, HSV Key and Extract make transparency only); the Obsolete Spill Suppressor row stays skipped, this one covers it; the planned screen keyer's despill can reuse this rule. **Sources read:** Adobe's After Effects help, keying effects (via a search snippet; the page itself was unreadable here): Advanced Spill Suppressor removes the key colour from a keyed subject; Standard "is simpler, automatically detects the dominant key color, and requires less user input"; Ultra "is based on the spill suppression in the Ultra Key effect in Premiere"; Adobe, "Fix green screen footage" (adobe.com/learn/after-effects/web/fix-green-screen-footage); Pro Video Coalition, "Advanced Keying with After Effects, part 4" (provideocoalition.com/advanced-keying-with-after-effects-part-4); Vindral Composer, "Spill suppression" (composer.docs.vindral.com/docs/spill-suppression), limiting the screen channel to the other two. It keys out every colour inside the box the six ends make, and fuzziness fades the colours just outside it. **Overlap checked:** Color Key (`core.color_key`) keys by distance from one colour with a tolerance and feather, not a box in a chosen space; HSV Key keys by hue, saturation and value; Color Difference Key (D-459) builds two partial mattes; Extract keys by brightness alone; EFFECTS.md lists this row as its own effect (Depends on: Color Key, meaning the keying family, nothing reused). **Sources read:** Adobe, After Effects keying effects (helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/using/keying-effects.html, read through search excerpts, the page refusing direct reads): Color Range "creates transparency by keying out a specified range of colors in the Lab, YUV, or RGB color space", for screens "that consist of more than one color" or "unevenly lit"; the Key Color, plus and minus eyedroppers used in the matte thumbnail; Fuzziness "to soften the edges between transparent and opaque regions"; the Min and Max sliders "fine-tune the beginning" and "the end of the color range"; the L, Y, R sliders the first component, a, U, G the second, b, V, B the third; ITU-R BT.601 for the luma and colour-difference weights (full range, as JPEG uses them); our own Lab from Shadow/Highlight (document 21). D-502 / Inner/Outer Key, after After Effects' Inner/Outer Key (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Keying) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-10 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-382.** **What was built.** `core.inner_outer_key`, named Inner/Outer Key, with After Effects' settings but the Additional masks and Cleanup brushes: Foreground (Inside) and Background (Outside), the layer's masks by number as Fill chooses its one (D-418), Single Mask Highlight Radius, Edge Thin, Edge Feather, Edge Threshold, Invert Extraction and Blend With Original, the numbers keyable. It keys a subject out of its background by a mask just inside its edge and one just outside, working the soft edge between them out again without the background's colour. **Overlap checked:** Color Key, Color Range, Color Difference Key and Keylight key by colour, not by masks; Difference Matte keys by a plate; Fill and Path Stroke read the layer's masks but do not key; Refine Soft Matte refines a matte already there; EFFECTS.md lists this row as its own effect (Depends on: P0-8 and P0-20; it uses the masks as Fill does and its own edge estimate). **Sources read:** Adobe, After Effects keying effects (helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/using/keying-effects.html, read through search excerpts, the page refusing direct reads): Inner/Outer Key isolates a foreground object from its background by masks, one just inside the object's edge and one just outside it, for objects with fine edges such as hair, and lists the controls named here; DV Info Net, "Problems with masking in AE" (dvinfo.net/forum/archive/index.php/t-102066.html): trace the inside edge of the object with a mask and tell the effect to use it, then a mask outside the edge, "colors that cross pixels the inner bezier are kept, colors that cross the outer bezier are discarded"; Foundry, Keylight inside and outside masks (learn.foundry.com/nuke/11.3/content/comp_environment/keying_with_keylight/inside_outside_masks.html), the same two-mask idea for another keyer; document 21's Gaussian; ADR-016's covering; Simple Choker's disc; Fill's mask choice (D-418). outside the background mask's half covering is gone; between them unknown; with one mask, the pixels whose centres lie within the highlight radius of its outline are unknown, the rest kept inside and gone outside; Invert Extraction swaps kept and gone; each unknown pixel's kept colour F and gone colour B are the alpha-weighted means of the kept and gone pixels in the square reaching the nearest of each (Chebyshev distance); the matte is its colour's place between B and F, clamped, or the share of the distances when F and B match; its colour is (C - (1 - matte) B) / matte, clamped; then Edge Thin (a disc's minimum, or maximum when negative), Edge Feather (a Gaussian of sigma feather / 2), Edge Threshold ((m - q) / (1 - q)), and Blend With Original. **Gaps:** Adobe publishes no formula, so the rule is ours: the kept and gone colours are the mean of the nearest kept and gone pixels (the square reaching the nearest of each), the pixel made see-through by its place on the line between them, and the gone colour taken back out; not proven equal to After Effects'; the ranges and the settings when added are ours (no foreground, no background, radius 10, no thin, feather or threshold, not inverted, no blend); After Effects' starting values were not found; Additional Foreground, Additional Background and the Cleanup Foreground and Cleanup Background brushes are not built (masks by number only, as Fill's); the masks are read whatever their mode, inversion, feather, expansion or opacity, as Fill reads them (D-418); on the processor only (card pass later, as Refine Hard and Soft Matte, D-352); the card draws what follows it. D-505 / Unmult, after After Effects' Unmult (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Keying, new in After Effects 26.0; `docs/effects/PLUGINS.md` pick #7) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-10 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-385.** **What was built.** `core.unmult`, named Unmult, with After Effects' settings: Background Color (Black, White), Black Level, White Level, Softness, Remove Color Matting and Clip HDR Results, the three numbers keyable. It turns a black or white background into see-through, so fire, flares or smoke shot on black or white lay over other layers without a box. **Overlap checked:** Soft Physical Glow (D-353) has an unmult option, but it acts inside that glow only; PLUGINS.md says to build the Unmult row separately (it helps every flare and fire element) and that Deep Glow reuses its maths later; Adobe ships it as its own Keying effect, so it is its own effect. As added it gives the same covering as Soft Physical Glow's unmult. **Sources read:** Adobe community, "New in Beta: Unmult effect" (community.adobe.com/announcements-532/new-in-beta-unmult-effect-about-time-right-314503): Keying category, the controls named, 8, 16 and 32 bits, processor and card; Adobe bug reports on it: banding with transparency (fixed in 26.2) and alpha left behind (fixed in 26.5); CG Channel's After Effects 26.0 article (the release with Unmult); ProVideo Coalition, "Unmult with and without a plug-in" (Channel Combiner Max RGB into alpha, then Remove Color Matting); Maxon Red Giant's Unmult documentation; elephorm's Unmult tutorial. No source gives a formula or the settings when added. Nothing is ported. **Interpretations (ours):** Adobe says Unmult removes a black or white background by making the pixels transparent in proportion to how close they are to it, with Background Color, Black Level or White Level, Softness, Remove Color Matting and Clip HDR Results, at 8, 16 and 32 bits, but publishes no formula, so the rule is ours ("rule ours" precedent), after the long-standing recipe of the brightest channel as the covering with colour matting removed (Channel Combiner's Max RGB into alpha, then Remove Color Matting): on the premultiplied linear colour c and covering a, the distance m is the brightest channel held inside 0 to a (black) or a less the darkest channel, held inside 0 to a (white); the share kept is (m - level) / softness held inside 0 to 1, a step at softness 0 (kept where m is above the level); the new covering is m times the share; Remove Color Matting on divides out the background, the straight colour c / m over black or (c - a + m) / m over white, held inside 0 to 1 when Clip HDR Results is on; off, the pixel keeps its own straight colour c / a. **Gaps:** Adobe publishes no formula, so the rule is ours (the covering becomes how far the pixel is from the background, its brightest channel over black or its darkest channel's distance below white, less the level, over the softness; Remove Color Matting restores the colour from before the background); not proven equal to After Effects'; the settings when added are ours (black, black level 0, white level 100, softness 0, Remove Color Matting on, Clip HDR Results off), Adobe publishing none we found; it works in linear light, where After Effects' default project is 8-bit and gamma-encoded, so the same footage keeps a different amount of covering there (in linear light a mid grey keeps about a fifth); After Effects shows one level control whose name follows the background; we keep Black Level and White Level both, since the panel cannot hide a number, and each is used only with its background; Clip HDR Results changes only colours past 1, which come from footage or effects brighter than white. It shines a spotlight cone down onto the layer from a lamp above it: the light alone, the light added to the layer (or to the transparent parts too), or the layer left lit inside the cone and darkened outside it. **Overlap checked:** no effect of ours lights a cone (Light Sweep is a band of light across the layer, Radial Shadow a shadow cast from a point); no plug-in in PLUGINS.md replaces it. **Sources read:** the CycoreFX HD 1.8.1 manual's CC Spotlight page (the controls and what each does, as quoted in `tools/cc_spotlight_reference.py`); EFFECTS.md row 341 and PLUGINS.md (no plug-in replaces it). No source gives a formula or the settings when added. Nothing is ported. **Interpretations (ours):** the CycoreFX manual names From and To (the light's place and its target on the layer), Height (the light's distance above the target), Cone Angle (the opening), Edge Softness (lower is sharper), Color, Intensity (higher is brighter), Render (Light Only, Light Add, Light Add+, Light Shadow and four Gel renders) and Gel Layer, but publishes no formula and no settings when added, so the rule is ours ("rule ours" precedent): From and To in per cent of the drawing (as Radial Shadow's light), Height in per cent of its width; the lamp F = (from W, from H, -height W) / 100 aimed at T = (to W, to H, 0) / 100; at a pixel's centre the angle off the axis theta = atan2(|A x D|, A . D); the half opening o = cone / 2 and the inner angle n = o (1 - softness / 100); the share f is 1 to n, 0 from o, smoothstep between, and 0 everywhere with no axis or no opening; with k = f intensity / 100 and C the colour in linear light, on the premultiplied pixel: Light Only (C k, min(k, 1)); Light Add (c + C k a, a); Light Add+ (c + C k, a + (1 - a) min(k, 1)); Light Shadow c ((1 - f)(1 - min(i, 1)) + f C), so outside the cone darkened by the intensity and inside tinted by the colour. **Gaps:** the CycoreFX 1.8.1 manual only describes the controls, so the rule and the settings when added are ours (a lamp at From, Height above the drawing, aimed at To; full light inside the inner angle, none outside half the Cone Angle, smoothstep between); not proven equal to CycoreFX's; no fall-off with distance: the light is as strong far from the lamp as near it; the light is computed in linear light, where After Effects' default project is 8-bit and gamma-encoded, so the edge's fade and the colour's mix look different there; the four Gel renders (Gel Only, Gel Add, Gel Add+, Gel Shadow) and Gel Layer are not built: a Gel render is refused by name (EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID), the effect kept as written and left out of every frame. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-SPOT-001 to 027 (`tools/cc_spotlight_reference.py`, c089f730) in document 25; code dce14dce; `verification/D-507_cc_spotlight_table.md` 167 of 167. **On the card:** one new pass, `spotlight`, sharing `layer_fx::spotlight_numbers` with the processor, its pixel read and written one channel at a time (B-222); not fused, no tone mode. All 27 fixture projects at Full and Draft and the reference shot (four settings, three frames, Full and Draft) within 1 level, 51 of 51; B-155 shows no fall-back to the processor. **Timing** (`verification/B-387_cc_spotlight_timing_table.md`), card / processor, again: the shot after a moving Noise 11.8 / 45.9 ms a frame, light shadow as added 14.7 / 56.6, light add orange at intensity 250 14.5 / 56.0, light add plus low and wide 14.5 / 54.0; about 0.9 to 1.0 ms a 1080p layer on the card, at the row's Target P1 (1 ms), and about 2.7 to 3.6 on the processor. **For the owner:** whether the settings when added and the edge's fade suit your footage, and whether the Gel renders are wanted next.

D-520 / CC Wide Time, after CycoreFX's CC Wide Time (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Time, row 292) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-11 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; drawn by the processor only, as Echo is, so no card comparison; no new tolerance; built B-400.** **What was built.** `core.cc_wide_time`, named CC Wide Time, in the Time group, with CycoreFX's settings: Forward Steps and Backward Steps (0 to 100 whole frames, both keyable) and Native Motion Blur (Off, On). It averages the layer over a span of frames before and after the present one: a smearing blur for anything moving over a still background. **Overlap checked:** Echo's Blend operator averages frames on one side only, at a fixed spacing; frame blending (D-216) mixes only the two neighbouring source frames; layer motion blur blurs the transform, not the drawing's own change. No plug-in in PLUGINS.md replaces it. **Sources read:** the CycoreFX HD 1.8.1 manual's CC Wide Time page (Time menu, page 132); reiwan's note on CycoreFX time effects (https://note.com/0to1_reiwan/n/n4e766d130657: Native Motion Blur off by default); Preston Kanak, "Remove the staccato effect in timelapse footage" (http://www.prestonkanak.com/blog/2016/10/10/remove-staccato-effect-timelapse-footage: Wide Time to smooth timelapse, with Pixel Motion Blur); Larry Jordan's trail-effects article (https://larryjordan.com/articles/technique-creating-trail-effects/, Motion's equivalent only); EFFECTS.md row 292. Nothing is ported. **Interpretations (ours):** the CycoreFX manual says Forward Steps and Backward Steps set the range of frames that make the temporal blur, behind and ahead of the present frame, that layers with effects must be pre-composed first, and that Native Motion Blur Off disables motion blur in nested compositions while On keeps it where enabled; it publishes no formula and no defaults, so the rule is ours ("rule ours" precedent): at frame n, F = floor(forward_steps) and B = floor(backward_steps); P_m is the holder's drawing through its masks at frame m, its effects not run (as Echo's copies and as the manual's pre-compose note implies), empty outside the layer; R = (sum of P_m for m = n - B to n + F) / (B + F + 1), all four numbers, laid on the drawing; Off draws the compositions inside with their blur switched off; 3 and 3 and Off when added (the reiwan guide notes Native Motion Blur is off by default). **Gaps:** the CycoreFX 1.8.1 manual only describes the controls, so the rule and the settings when added are ours (every frame of the span weighted the same, a frame outside the layer counted empty, whole frames only, no frames made between them); not proven equal to CycoreFX's; a fast-moving drawing shows separate faint copies, not a continuous streak, since no in-between frames are made; Native Motion Blur On draws the compositions inside as they are, where CycoreFX says it adjusts their blur: their shutter is not lengthened to the span; Preston Kanak's timelapse tutorial pairs CC Wide Time with Pixel Motion Blur, which needs P0-13 (motion vectors, parked): that step cannot be reproduced; speed above the row's Target P4 (PROVISIONAL timing). Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-WIDE-001 to 019 (`tools/cc_wide_time_reference.py`, 8df0cc90) in document 25; code 938a6872; `verification/D-520_cc_wide_time_table.md` 94 of 94. **On the card:** no pass; the layer's effect is drawn by the processor (compose's `fill_wide_time`, Echo's blend fold), as every multi-frame effect is; B-155 shows no fall-back warning. No tone mode. **Timing** (`verification/B-400_cc_wide_time_timing_table.md`), PROVISIONAL (the machine was not quiet: another lane's test started during the run), Draw on: GPU, milliseconds a frame first / again: Noise alone 18.3 / 14.5, CC Wide Time as added (7 frames) then Noise 297.4 / 474.0, CC Wide Time 10 and 10 (21 frames) then Noise 1153.0 / 1194.2; about 150 ms a 1080p layer as added, above the row's Target P4 (100 ms a frame), each frame of the span drawn afresh. **For the owner:** whether 3 and 3 suits as the starting span, and whether the speed matters enough to keep the frames drawn for one frame for the next.

D-509 / Glass Melt, after the purpose of CycoreFX's CC Glass Wipe (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md` Transition, row 271) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-11 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-389.** **What was built.** `core.glass_melt`, named Glass Melt (a name of our own), in Transition: the layer melts away like bending glass into the Layer to Reveal, the darkest parts of the Gradient Layer first (the layer itself when none is chosen), with Completion, Layer to Reveal, Gradient Layer (D-189's layer settings), Softness and Displacement Amount; the three numbers keyable. **Overlap checked:** Gradient Wipe (D-194) wipes in the same order with no bend; CC Glass (D-317) bends with no wipe; Displacement Map bends by another layer with no wipe. **Sources read:** the CycoreFX HD 1.8.1 manual's CC Glass Wipe page (the controls and what each does); for the parts reused, this project's own CC Glass (D-317) and Gradient Wipe (D-194). D-521 / Time Difference, after After Effects' Time Difference (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Time, row 296) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-11 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; drawn by the processor only, as Echo and CC Wide Time are, so no card comparison; no new tolerance; built B-401.** **What was built.** `core.time_difference`, named Time Difference, in the Time group, with After Effects' settings: Target (a layer, or none for the layer itself), Time Offset (-60 to 60 seconds, keyable), Contrast (0 to 100, keyable), Absolute Difference (On, Off) and Alpha Channel (Original, Target, Blend, Max, Full On, Lightness Of Result, Max Of Result, Alpha Difference, Alpha Difference Only). It shows how the layer differs from a target, often itself a frame earlier: what moved lights up and what stood still goes black (or grey), for motion mattes, clean-plate comparisons and trails. **Overlap checked:** the Difference blending mode compares two layers at the same time with no time offset and no covering choices; Difference Matte (D-189 family) keys out what matches rather than showing the difference; Echo and CC Wide Time mix frames, they do not subtract them. No plug-in in PLUGINS.md replaces it. **Sources read:** Adobe's After Effects help page on Time effects, Time Difference section (archived at web.archive.org/web/2024/https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/using/time-effects.html); a creativecow.net forum thread (https://creativecow.net/?p=258756: Time Difference against the layer one frame back for motion detection, then Gaussian Blur and Levels); reiwan's note on After Effects time effects (https://note.com/0to1_reiwan/n/n4e766d130657: the nine Alpha Channel choices); EFFECTS.md row 296. Nothing is ported. **Interpretations (ours):** Adobe's help says Time Difference shows the colour difference between the layer and a target layer, that the target's video switch need not be on, that Time Offset is in seconds with 0 meaning now, that Contrast adjusts the result, that Absolute Difference shows no difference as black and any difference as brighter (grey for no difference when off), and lists the nine Alpha Channel choices; it publishes no formula and no defaults, so the rule is ours ("rule ours" precedent): the shift k = floor(time_offset x rate + 1e-6) whole frames; the target is the holder's own picture at frame n + k (its effects not run) when no layer is named, or D-189's centred map of the named layer at n + k; both pixels to straight sRGB colour; d = S - M; gain g = 1 + contrast / 10; absolute e = clamp(g|d|), otherwise e = clamp(0.5 + g d / 2); the covering by the nine choices; the output linear(e) x covering; empty, layer "", offset 0, Contrast 0, Absolute Difference on, Alpha Channel Original when added. **Gaps:** Adobe's help names the controls and what they are for but publishes no formula and no defaults, so the rule and the settings when added are ours; not proven equal to After Effects' pixels; Adobe says the effect works in 8 bits a channel, ours works in floating point on straight sRGB colour, so differences finer than one 8-bit level show where After Effects' would not; the Time Offset is read relative to now (the target at now plus the offset), and only whole frames, so an offset between frames takes the frame before; Adobe's note pairs it with Particle Playground to shed particles only from moving parts, which needs P0-6 (particles, parked): that step cannot be reproduced; the creativecow motion-detection recipe (Time Difference then Gaussian Blur then Levels) is reproducible with our Gaussian Blur and Levels; its expression-driven offset (`source.frameDuration`) is not, as expressions are not supported, so the offset is typed as -1/24 instead. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-TDIFF-001 to 031 and `cycle_two.json` (`tools/time_difference_reference.py`, 64e014ad) in document 25; code 5016e2b4; `verification/D-521_time_difference_table.md` 140 of 140. **On the card:** no pass; the target frame is drawn by the processor (compose's `fill_time_difference`) and the difference is a processor fold (`layer_fx::time_difference`); B-155 shows no fall-back warning. No tone mode. **Timing** (`verification/B-401_time_difference_timing_table.md`), PROVISIONAL (the machine was not quiet), Draw on: GPU, milliseconds a frame first / again: Noise alone 18.3 / 14.3, Time Difference as added (itself, now) then Noise 41.8 / 67.6, Time Difference one frame back then Noise 98.4 / 85.4; Time Difference is a processor fold on three 1920 by 1080 layers, so it costs tens of milliseconds a frame, more one frame back, where the target frame is drawn as well. **For the owner:** whether the starting values suit (the layer against itself now, which shows nothing until Time Offset is set; one frame back, -0.042 seconds at 24 a second, is the usual motion setting).

D-510 / Tile Wipe, after the purpose of CycoreFX's CC Grid Wipe (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md` Transition, row 272) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-11 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-390.** **What was built.** `core.tile_wipe`, named Tile Wipe (a name of our own), in Transition: the layer is cut into square tiles that shrink away, the tiles nearest the Center first, with Completion, Center, Rotation, Border, Tiles, Shape (Doors, Radial, Rectangle) and Reverse Transition; the five numbers keyable. **Overlap checked:** Iris Wipe (B-107) opens one round hole; Venetian Blinds shrinks strips, not squares; Block Dissolve (D-214) removes blocks in a random order with no shrinking; Mosaic makes blocks without wiping. **Sources read:** the CycoreFX HD 1.8.1 manual's CC Grid Wipe page (what the effect does and the controls); for the parts reused, this project's own wipe pass (B-107's Linear, Radial, Venetian Blinds and Iris Wipe). D-540 / Screen Key, this program's own green and blue screen keyer in Keylight's place (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Keying, row 312, and its plan "Our own keyer"; roadmap item L-03) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-11 under the owner's /loop request and the owner's word of 2026-10-11, "for keylight, build our own, proceed with your recommendations, even if we may need to rewrite/change things."; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-420. It closes roadmap item L-03, parked on 2026-09-28 by D-179 and un-parked by that word.** **What was built.** `core.screen_key`, named Screen Key, in Lines & Mattes beside the other keyers, with our own setting names: View (Final Result, Screen Matte, Status), Screen Colour, Screen Gain, Screen Balance, Clip Black, Clip White, Despill Bias, Despill, Shrink/Grow, Softness and Edge Refine, every number keyable. It makes a pixel see-through by how far its screen channel stands above its other two against how far the screen colour's does, firms the matte with clip levels, holds the screen channel down to take the spill out, and finishes the edge with Simple Choker's disc, document 21's Gaussian and Key Cleaner's guided fit. **Overlap checked:** Color Difference Key (D-459) builds its matte from Ihringer's hue windows, Linear Color Key (D-504) from a distance to one colour, Color Key (D-97) and HSV Key from a colour box, and Advanced Spill Suppressor (D-457) only despills; none is a screen keyer with clip levels, despill and edge finishing in one, and EFFECTS.md plans this one as its own row, so it is its own effect. Its despill is the plain limit, not Advanced Spill Suppressor's Ultra (whose hue window, give-back, desaturation and brightness restore a keyer's despill does not need); Advanced Spill Suppressor can still follow it. **Sources read:** The Foundry, Keylight 1.2 user guide for After Effects (comp.nus.edu.sg/~cs4340/lab/Keylight_1.2v12_AE.pdf): the order of work (pick the screen colour, view the screen matte, clip black and white, then despill and soften), its saturation "comparing the intensity of the primary component against a weighted average of the two other components" with the balance taking the smaller at 100%, the larger at 0% and their average at 50%, about 50% suiting green screens and 95% blue, and its Status view of three colours; the openfx/Natron Despill node's documentation after Steve Wright, "Digital Compositing for Film and Video" section 4.5 (the screen channel limited to a mix of the other two); a LinkedIn Learning Keylight course outline (the same order of work); He, Sun and Tang 2010, the guided filter (through Refine Soft Matte, D-352). No Keylight code, text or names are used; only the openly published colour difference idea and the order of work are shared. **Interpretations (ours):** the rule is ours ("rule ours" precedent), stated in document 21: the screen channel is the screen colour's largest (ties green, then blue, then red); on the straight colour through the sRGB curve, D(c) = c_s - weigh(c, balance), weigh being the larger of the other two at 1 - t plus the smaller at t; the matte is 1 - gain D(e) / D(k) held inside 0 to 1, a grey screen colour keying nothing; clip levels stretch it, a step where white <= black; shrink or grow takes the least or greatest over Simple Choker's disc and softness document 21's Gaussian, both with the picture's edge held so the frame's own edge is never eaten; despill holds the screen channel no higher than weigh(e, bias), by the despill share; Final Result is the despilled colour at covering a m, then Key Cleaner at radius floor(edge refine), contrast 0, strength 100 when edge refine is 1 or more; Screen Matte shows m as grey; Status shows white at m >= 0.999, black at m <= 0.001 and the encoded grey 0.5 between. The settings when added are ours: pure green, gain 100, balance 50, clip 0 to 100, despill bias 50 at 100, no shrink, softness or edge refine. **Gaps:** no light wrap (put Light Wrap after it, as the row's plan says); Keylight's Screen Pre-blur, Clip Rollback, Screen Despot, inside and outside masks, Alpha Bias, Replace Method and Colour, and edge colour correction are not built; the despill bias is a number between the other two channels, not a picked colour; no eyedropper (the screen colour is typed or picked from the colour box); Status shows no warning colours, only black, white and one grey; Screen Matte and Status show the matte before Edge Refine; Edge Refine is Key Cleaner's fit and can give a little covering back to see-through pixels just outside an edge; Keylight's screen subtraction (the screen colour taken out of the kept colour) is not built, so edges keep the despilled colour rather than the screen removed; the rule is ours, not proven equal to Keylight's, so the same footage keys differently. Gaps (tutorial): every step of Keylight's user guide's order of work has its setting; the light wrap and the steps on the settings above are not reproduced.
