D-541 / Linear Color Key's tolerance 0 and Key Operation's Keep Colors (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Keying, row 313; D-504) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-11 under the owner's /loop request and the owner's word of 2026-10-11, "for keylight, build our own, proceed with your recommendations, even if we may need to rewrite/change things."; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-421. It changes accepted D-504 fixtures, as an owner-authorised change, listed below.** **What was built.** (a) Matching Tolerance 0 keys nothing, the whole image opaque, as Adobe documents ("A value of 0 makes the entire image opaque"), whatever the softness; before, it keyed the key colour itself. (b) Key Operation (Key Colors, Keep Colors), the setting D-504 left out, saved as `key_operation` "key" (when added, and when a file written before D-541 has none) or "keep". A Keep Colors instance brings back colours that the keys above it took out, as Adobe and Creative COW's second-instance workflow use it. **The rule (ours).** The run above a Keep Colors is the Linear Color Keys directly above it, one after another; switched-off, refused and unsupported instances draw nothing and are passed over, any other effect ends the run. The run's input P is the pixels before its first instance (the Keep instance's own input when nothing above it is a Linear Color Key). Where P has covering a0 > 0, the keep share kk = 1 - m, m the share D-504's rule keeps of P's straight colour by the Keep instance's own key colour, matching, tolerance and softness. Final Output: where a0 kk is above the pixel's covering, the pixel becomes P times kk, colour and covering (the covering is the larger of the two, the colour brought back from before the run); Matte Only: the grey max(covering, a0 kk) / a0 at covering a0; Source Only: the layer. Tolerance 0 brings nothing back. P is kept, one copy of the layer, only when the stack holds a valid Keep Colors, so stacks without one cost nothing more; that copy answers D-504's gap (the colour under fully keyed pixels, which the premultiplied frame no longer has). A Keep Colors is drawn by the processor with the keys above it (the card's plan leaves it off the card); a Key Colors stays on the card as mode 72, now with the tolerance 0 rule. **Fixtures changed (owner-authorised, written by `tools/linear_color_key_reference.py` in their own commit before the code).** FX-LCKEY-007 (tolerance 0, softness 20): was "only pure blue's top row, the key colour itself, is gone; its next two rows keep a share d / 20"; now "nothing is keyed, the layer as it was". FX-LCKEY-011 frame 0 (tolerance keyed 0 to 40 on the blue screen): was the blue screen's top row keyed at tolerance 0; now nothing keyed at frame 0; frames 2 and 4 unchanged. FX-LCKEY-001 to 018's projects gain `key_operation` "key", the value when added, no picture changing. Every other old case's frames are byte for byte the same. New: FX-LCKEY-019 to 023 (Keep Colors after a hue key, alone, after a run of two keys, as the matte, at tolerance 0) and the refused FX-LCKEY-024 ("Keep", a capital). **Gaps.** Adobe publishes no formula for Keep Colors, so the rule above is ours, not proven equal to After Effects'; the run counts Linear Color Key instances only (Adobe documents Keep Colors with Linear Color Key; whether After Effects' run also passes over other keyers, Color Key or Color Range, is not documented), a choice for the owner; a Keep Colors whose run is ended by another effect has nothing to bring back; the views of a key instance above a Keep (matte, source) are taken as that instance drew them. **For the owner:** whether other keyers above a Keep Colors should count in its run; the build's word is Linear Color Key only.

D-522 / Cryptomatte, after After Effects' Cryptomatte (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, 3D Channel, row 375) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-11 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; the card within 1 level of the processor on every fixture and the sample, at Full and Draft; no new tolerance; no new card pass and no tone mode; built B-402.** **What was built.** `core.cryptomatte`, named Cryptomatte, in the 3D Channel group: Layer (the Cryptomatte layer's name, empty for the first), Selection (the names of the objects or materials picked, a comma between) and Output (Colors, Matte, Keyed). It reads the Cryptomatte a 3D render saved in the layer's EXR file and picks objects by name, with soft edges where an object is antialiased, blurred or see-through, which ID Key's single id cannot give. **Overlap checked:** ID Key (D-349) keeps one integer id with no coverage, so its edges are hard; Pass Extract shows a channel, not a pick; neither decodes Cryptomatte's hashed ranks (EFFECTS.md P0-5 left this to this row). No plug-in in PLUGINS.md replaces it. **Sources read:** Psyop's Cryptomatte specification 1.2.0 (the PDF in github.com/Psyop/Cryptomatte, specification folder): the channel layout, the hash and the test value torus = 4053562365; fnord's ProEXR 2 manual (fnordware.com/ProEXR, the Cryptomatte section: a colour display of the ids at first, objects picked by clicking with the effect selected, Shift to add, Alt to remove, Import As Composition for the metadata); Adobe's After Effects help page on 3D Channel effects (helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/using/3d-channel-effects.html, last updated 2024-04-14), which documents no Cryptomatte settings; lesterbanks.com, "Working With Cryptomattes in After Effects" (2018-11-26, Helge Maus's ProEXR 2 tutorial: Cryptomatte mattes made automatically from render-time names); an Adobe community thread on scripting access to Cryptomatte; EFFECTS.md row 375. Nothing is ported. **Interpretations (ours):** Adobe's 3D Channel help documents no Cryptomatte settings (the effect is fnord's, bundled with After Effects; its manual says it shows every id in colour and objects are picked by clicking), so the three settings and the colour rule are ours: layer (text, "" the first, matched whole or by the last dotted word, case ignored), selection (names, commas between, trimmed), output colors / matte / keyed; the file read by Psyop's specification 1.2.0: levels T00, T01, ... red id with green coverage, blue id with alpha coverage; ids by MurmurHash3_x86_32 seed 0 with bit 23 flipped where the exponent is all 0 or all 1; m = clamp(sum of the picked ids' coverage, 0, 1); colours: each id coloured by its low bits ((b & 255) / 255, (b >> 8 & 255) / 255, (b >> 16 & 127) / 127), the picked white, mixed by coverage, opaque; matte (m, m, m, 1); keyed the picture times m; a coverage not finite read as D-62 reads one, an id not finite read as no object, said as MEDIA_EXR_ADJUSTED; when added: the first layer, nothing picked, colors. **Gaps:** objects are picked by typing their names, not by clicking in the viewer as in fnord's effect (click, Shift-click to add, Alt-click to remove): the tutorial's picking steps cannot be reproduced, and need a viewer pick tool (a later decision); the manifest (the names a file lists in its metadata) is not read, so there is no list of names to choose from and a name is hashed as typed; a name containing a comma cannot be picked, and an id cannot be typed as a raw number; fnord's tutorial step "Import As Composition so the metadata comes along" has no counterpart, since the file is read directly each frame; the old preview channels (T.r, T.g, T.b) are not read; RLA/RPF files, another Blender view layer, multiview files and nested compositions are not read (as P0-5); the colours of the Colors output are ours (the id's low bits), not fnord's or Nuke's, so a Colors view will not match those programs' colours; not proven equal to After Effects' pixels, as Adobe publishes no settings or rule for the effect. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-CRYPTO-001 to 023 (`tools/cryptomatte_reference.py`, 0b341e6a) in document 25; code 0fd4faf1; `verification/D-522_cryptomatte_table.md` 228 of 228. **On the card:** the colours or the matte are worked out on the processor as the file is read (`exr_io::read_cryptomatte`, through D-348's route and cache, keyed now by the whole pass so the names and output are part of the key), then laid on by the existing passes: Pass Extract's (`passx`) for Colors and Matte, ID Key's (`idkey`, multiply) for Keyed. No new pass, no tone mode; B-155 shows no fall-back warning. **Timing** (`verification/B-402_cryptomatte_timing_table.md`), PROVISIONAL (the machine was not quiet), Draw on: GPU, a 1920 by 1080 EXR with a two-level CryptoObject layer, milliseconds a frame first / again: Noise alone 10.5 / 3.3, Colors then Noise 8.8 / 3.3, Matte of two objects then Noise 8.3 / 3.7, Keyed on two objects then Noise 6.0 / 3.9; Cryptomatte costs well under a millisecond a frame once the file's passes are read and kept (3.3 to 3.9 again against 3.3 for Noise alone). **For the owner:** whether typed names suit until a viewer pick tool exists (a later, separate decision), and whether the starting Colors view suits.

D-523 / Depth of Field, after After Effects' Depth of Field (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, 3D Channel, row 377) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-11 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; the card within 1 level of the processor on every fixture and the sample, at Full and Draft; no new tolerance; no new card pass and no tone mode; built B-403.** **What was built.** `core.depth_of_field`, named Depth of Field, in the 3D Channel group: Focal Plane, Maximum Radius, Focal Plane Thickness and Focal Bias, all keyable. It blurs a 3D render more the further each pixel lies from the distance in focus, reading the depth saved in the layer's EXR file (D-348's route). **Overlap checked:** Lens Blur (D-359) with a blur map already blurs by a map's brightness, but a depth is not a brightness from 0 to 1, so this effect turns the depth into the fraction out of focus and then draws exactly that Lens Blur; Depth Key cuts by depth and does not blur. No plug-in in PLUGINS.md replaces it. **Sources read:** Adobe's After Effects help page on 3D Channel effects (helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/using/3d-channel-effects.html, last updated 2024-04-14), its Depth Of Field section (the four settings and their meaning) and its 3D Channel Extract section; EFFECTS.md row 377. Nothing is ported. **Interpretations (ours):** Adobe's page names four settings and no formula, so the rule is ours: beyond = max(0, |z - Focal Plane| - Focal Plane Thickness / 2); k = Focal Bias / 50; the fraction out of focus f = 0 where beyond or k is 0, 1 where k beyond >= |z|, else k beyond / |z| (a thin lens's blur circle at bias 50, the same in any depth unit and for a depth written negative); the blur D-359's Lens Blur with a blur map: radius Maximum Radius, a circle iris, no highlights, edges repeated so the layer does not grow, the map f read by its alpha with focal distance 0 (f = 0 sharp, f = 1 the full radius, between the two nearest levels mixed); when added: Focal Plane 0, Maximum Radius 10, Thickness 0, Bias 50; all keyable; the radius scaled with a draft, the distances not. **Gaps:** the rule from depth to blur is ours (Adobe gives none), so the amount of blur at a depth is not proven equal to After Effects'; the tutorial step of finding the depth to focus on by reading it in the Info panel or clicking the picture cannot be reproduced: the depth is typed (a viewer depth pick is a later decision); the blur is Lens Blur's mixed levels, so a sharp object in front of a blurred one keeps a hard edge and a blurred one in front does not spread over a sharp one behind (no layered depth sorting, as After Effects' Depth of Field also blurs a single layer); no depth from a nested composition's 3D layers; RLA/RPF files, another Blender view layer and multiview files are not read (as P0-5). Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-DOF-001 to 027 (`tools/depth_of_field_reference.py`, 58be00a8) in document 25; code 0141dbee; `verification/D-523_depth_of_field_table.md` 221 of 221. **On the card:** the fractions are worked out on the processor as the depth is read (`compose::fill_passes`), then the effect is drawn as its Lens Blur (`effects::depth_lens`) by Lens Blur's existing map passes (`prefix`, `lmgather`). No new pass, no tone mode, no new perf stage (timed as Lens Blur); B-155 shows no fall-back warning. **Timing** (`verification/B-403_depth_of_field_timing_table.md`), PROVISIONAL (the machine was not quiet), Draw on: GPU, a 1920 by 1080 EXR with a depth pass, milliseconds a frame first / again: Noise alone 23.0 / 5.1, Depth of Field radius 10 then Noise 134.7 / 107.1, radius 30 112.7 / 102.8, radius 60 100.7 / 105.1; about 100 milliseconds a frame more than Noise alone at every radius, far above the row's Target P3 (8 ms added), measured while four other test runs used the card. **For the owner:** whether the blur's growth away from focus looks right (Focal Bias 50 is a thin lens's), and whether typing the focal depth suits until a viewer depth pick exists.

D-524 / Fog 3D, after After Effects' Fog 3D (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, 3D Channel, row 379) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-11 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; the card within 1 level of the processor on every fixture and the sample, at Full and Draft; no new tolerance; one new card pass (`fog`), no tone mode; built B-404.** **What was built.** `core.fog_3d`, named Fog 3D, in the 3D Channel group: Fog Color, Fog Start Depth, Fog End Depth, Fog Opacity, Scattering Density, Foggy Background, Gradient Layer and Layer Contribution. It lays fog over a 3D render that thickens with distance, reading the depth saved in the layer's EXR file (D-348's route). **Overlap checked:** Aerial Haze moves a picture toward a colour by a matte's brightness, but a depth is not a brightness from 0 to 1 and it has no fog behind the layer; Depth Matte cuts by depth. No plug-in in PLUGINS.md replaces it. **Sources read:** Adobe's After Effects help page on 3D Channel effects (helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/using/3d-channel-effects.html, last updated 2024-04-14), its About 3D Channel effects and Fog 3D sections; EFFECTS.md row 379. Nothing is ported. **Interpretations (ours):** Adobe's page names the settings and no formula, so the rule is ours: t = clamp((z - Fog Start Depth) / (Fog End Depth - Fog Start Depth), 0, 1) (with the two equal, 1 at or beyond the start); with d = Scattering Density / 10, the fog share f = t at d = 0, else (1 - e^(-d t)) / (1 - e^(-d)); a gradient layer's picture luma L scales it by 1 - c + c L with c = Layer Contribution / 100; the pixel moves toward the fog colour by f times Fog Opacity, and with Foggy Background on the fog shows through where the layer does not cover; when added: white, 0 to 10, opacity 100, density 50, Foggy Background on, no gradient layer, contribution 100; the numbers keyable; nothing in pixels, so a draft changes nothing. **Gaps:** the rule from depth to fog is ours (Adobe gives none), so how fast the fog thickens at a density is not proven equal to After Effects'; the gradient layer is read as D-189 reads an effect layer (centred on the drawing, at its own size), not stretched to the scene's size; reading the start and end depths off the picture by clicking is not built: they are typed (a viewer depth pick is a later decision); no depth from a nested composition's 3D layers; RLA/RPF files, another Blender view layer and multiview files are not read (as P0-5). Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-FOG-001 to 030 (`tools/fog_3d_reference.py`, c5dd2f61) in document 25; code 55706a33; `verification/D-524_fog_3d_table.md` 237 of 237. **On the card:** the shares are worked out on the processor as the depth is read, then one new pass `fog` lays the colour; no tone mode; perf stage `effect: fog 3d` (Stage::ALL 206); B-155 shows no fall-back warning. **Timing** (`verification/B-404_fog_3d_timing_table.md`), PROVISIONAL (the machine was not quiet), Draw on: GPU, a 1920 by 1080 EXR with a depth pass, milliseconds a frame first / again: Noise alone 24.3 / 6.5, Fog 3D as added then Noise 20.1 / 5.7, Fog 3D from 4 to 20 at density 0 then Noise 19.9 / 6.2; Fog 3D adds no measurable time over Noise alone (5.7 to 6.2 again against 6.5), within the run's noise. **For the owner:** whether the fog's thickening at density 50 looks right, and whether typing the depths suits until a viewer depth pick exists.

D-525 / IDentifier, after After Effects' IDentifier (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, 3D Channel, row 381) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-11 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; the card within 1 level of the processor on every fixture and the sample, at Full and Draft; no new tolerance; no new card pass and no tone mode; built B-405.** **What was built.** `core.identifier`, named IDentifier, in the 3D Channel group: Channel (Object ID, Material ID), ID (keyable) and Output (Colors, Luma Matte, Alpha Matte, Raw). It shows the object or material ids saved in a render's EXR file: every id as its own colour, a black and white matte of one id, the picture cut to one id, or the ids as greys. **Overlap checked:** ID Key (D-349, after ID Matte) already keeps one id with a feather; IDentifier adds the colour and raw views and the luma matte, and reads the ids by the same route. No plug-in in PLUGINS.md replaces it. **Sources read:** fnord software's ProEXR manual, version 2.6.6 (2 February 2026), its EXtractoR, IDentifier and Cryptomatte sections; Adobe's After Effects help page on 3D Channel effects (helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/using/3d-channel-effects.html, last updated 2024-04-14), its IDentifier and ID Matte sections; an OTOY forum thread (render.otoy.com, viewtopic p=316850) where IDentifier refused an Octane object id pass stored as colour; EFFECTS.md row 381. Nothing is ported. **Interpretations (ours):** fnord's manual gives the four outputs' purposes and no colours or formula, so the rule is ours: Colors gives each nearest whole id k the hue (k times 0.618033988749895) mod 1 at saturation 0.7 and value 0.9, opaque; Luma Matte white where the id is within a half of ID, black elsewhere; Alpha Matte the picture kept where it is, transparent elsewhere (ID Key with no feather); Raw the id over 255 as an sRGB grey, so the 8-bit picture reads the id; when added: Object ID, ID 0, Colors; ID keyable; nothing in pixels. **Gaps:** fnord's IDentifier lists only integer channels (it says "No suitable integer channels available" for ids stored as floats, as Blender and Octane store them); ours reads the object or material id channel by name, float or whole, as D-349 does, so a file fnord refuses shows here; fnord's colour palette is not published, so the colours are ours (the golden ratio's turn of hue per id) and will not match After Effects' picture; there is no menu of every integer channel in the file: only the object and material ids D-349 finds by name; Cryptomatte's hashed ids are the Cryptomatte effect's (D-522); RLA/RPF files, another Blender view layer and multiview files are not read (as P0-5); choosing the id by clicking an object in the picture is not built: the id is typed (a viewer pick is a later decision, as ID Key's). Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-IDENT-001 to 023 (`tools/identifier_reference.py`, 6fb0fad1) in document 25; code 875dbb03; `verification/D-525_identifier_table.md` 192 of 192. **On the card:** the picture is worked out on the processor as the ids are read (`layer_fx::identifier`), then laid by ID Key's and Pass Extract's existing passes (`idkey`, `passx`). No new pass, no tone mode; perf stage `effect: identifier` (Stage::ALL 207); B-155 shows no fall-back warning. **Timing** (`verification/B-405_identifier_timing_table.md`), PROVISIONAL (the machine was not quiet), Draw on: GPU, a 1920 by 1080 EXR with an object id pass, milliseconds a frame first / again: Noise alone 21.9 / 3.9, IDentifier as added (colours) then Noise 9.9 / 4.0, alpha matte of 3 then Noise 6.6 / 3.5; IDentifier adds no measurable time over Noise alone (3.5 to 4.0 again against 3.9), within the run's noise. **For the owner:** whether the colours are distinct enough, and whether typing the id suits until a viewer pick exists.

D-526 / Numbers, after After Effects' Numbers (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Text, row 387) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-11 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; the card within 1 level of the processor on every fixture and four samples, at Full and Draft; no new tolerance; one new card pass (over), no tone mode; built B-406.** **What was built.** `core.numbers`, named Numbers, in the Text group: Type (Number, Number [Leading Zeros], Timecode [30], [25], [24], Time, Numerical Date, Short Date, Long Date, Hexadecimal), Random Values, Value/Offset/Random Max (keyable), Decimal Places, Position, Display Options, Fill Color, Stroke Color, Stroke Width, Size, Tracking, Proportional Spacing, Composite On Original, Font and Alignment. It draws a number, a counter, the layer's timecode, a time, a date or a hexadecimal number on the layer, filled, stroked or both, or a random number each frame. A font this computer does not have is said each frame (TEXT_FONT_MISSING) and nothing is drawn. **Overlap checked:** a text layer (D-263) with an expression can show a number, but Numbers keeps every digit in an even cell so a count does not jitter, and needs no expression. No plug-in in PLUGINS.md replaces it. **Sources read:** Adobe's After Effects help page on Text effects (helpx.adobe.com, via the web.archive.org copy), its Numbers section; a Creative COW forum thread (creativecow.net, p=1856527) on counting past 30,000 and Numbers' even spacing; an Adobe community thread ("Number effect random timecode 30") on random timecode changing every frame; Noble Desktop's "Number Counter" tutorial (blog.nobledesktop.com), a slider keyed from 0 to 10 driving a text layer; EFFECTS.md row 387. Nothing is ported. **Interpretations (ours):** Adobe's page names the settings and what each type shows and gives no layout or formula, so the rule is ours: a number correctly rounded to its places (a minus dropped when every digit is 0), leading zeros to five whole digits, timecode hh:mm:ss:ff of the layer's time plus the value in seconds, the time a 24-hour HH:MM of the value in hours, the dates the value's days after 1 January 1995, hexadecimal the value times 65,536; random values r times the value (30,000 when it is 0), a new r each frame; monospaced cells as wide as the font's widest digit; the stroke D-264's, outside the letters; when added a white 0 of 64 pixels in the middle, over the layer. **Gaps:** Current Time/Date (the computer's clock when the frame is drawn) is not built, since a frame must be the same on every render (document 21); the font is a font file's name typed as a text layer's (D-263), with no family and style menu; the random numbers are D-119's hash, so they will not be After Effects' numbers, only as random; the three timecodes are non-drop only, counted from the layer's in point plus the value in seconds (Timecode, D-527, has drop frame and the composition's time); kerning is off with proportional spacing on; After Effects runs Numbers at 8 bits a channel only, ours at every depth; the colours and size when added are ours; counting past 30,000 (the Creative COW thread) needs an expression on a text layer and is not built; Noble Desktop's slider driving a text layer is not reproduced: Numbers' Value, keyed, counts the same way. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-NUM-001 to 045 (`tools/numbers_reference.py`, cc4c2b21 (layer order corrected in dcce662d): the first fixtures listed each same/ project's layers top first, against document 19, found when the code's frames were first compared and corrected before the code was committed) in document 25; code 3f16fc4f; `verification/D-526_numbers_table.md` 252 of 252. **On the card:** the words are drawn on the processor (`layer_fx::numbers_picture`, D-263's text), then laid on by one new pass, `over`, over the layer or alone; no tone mode; perf stage `effect: numbers` (Stage::ALL 208); B-155 shows no fall-back warning. **Timing** (`verification/B-406_numbers_timing_table.md`), PROVISIONAL (the machine was not quiet), Draw on: GPU, a 1920 by 1080 still, milliseconds a frame first / again: Noise alone 6.2 / 2.5, Numbers timecode 30 at size 200 then Noise 27.3 / 2.7, monospaced long date, stroke over fill, size 120, then Noise 797.5 / 3.7; a frame Numbers has not drawn before costs about 21 milliseconds more for the timecode and about 790 more for the stroked long date at size 120, far above the row's Target P2 (4 ms added); a frame drawn before is kept and costs well under a millisecond. **For the owner:** whether a typed font file name suits until a font menu exists, and whether Current Time/Date is wanted despite frames then differing between renders.

D-527 / Timecode, after After Effects' Timecode (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Text, row 388) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-11 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; the card within 1 level of the processor on every fixture and four samples, at Full and Draft; no new tolerance; no new card pass (Numbers' over), no tone mode; built B-407.** **What was built.** `core.timecode`, named Timecode, in the Text group: Display Format (SMPTE, Frames, Feet + Frames 35mm, Feet + Frames 16mm), Time Source (Layer Source, Composition, Custom), Time Units, Drop Frame, Starting Frame, Text Position, Text Size, Text Color, Show Box, Box Color, Box Opacity and Composite On Original. It burns a time onto the picture on a box: SMPTE (drop frame at 29.97 and its multiples, with a semicolon), a frame number or feet and frames of film. Drop frame at time units that are not a multiple of 30 is refused in a sentence. **Overlap checked:** Numbers' Timecode types (D-526) show the layer's time non-drop at 24, 25 or 30 with no box; Timecode adds the composition's frame, drop frame, film feet, a custom count and the box, as After Effects keeps both. No plug-in in PLUGINS.md replaces it. **Sources read:** Adobe's After Effects help page on Text effects (helpx.adobe.com, via the web.archive.org copy), its Timecode section; AEJuice's "How to add timecode in After Effects" (aejuice.com, 2025); the ae-expressions documentation's time conversion page (timeToTimecode, timeToNTSCTimecode, timeToFrames, timeToFeetAndFrames); Chris Meyers' expressions article on ProVideo Coalition (p=4062), a composition's first frame being time 0; the film trade's 16 frames a foot (35mm) and 40 (16mm); EFFECTS.md row 388. Nothing is ported. **Interpretations (ours):** Adobe's page names the settings and what each does and gives no layout or formula, so the rule is ours: the layer source counts the layer's source frame (through its stretch and source offset), the composition source the composition's frame number, the custom source starting frame plus the layer's time in time units; drop frame is automatic at an NTSC rate (29.97 and its multiples; 23.976 counts non-drop at 24) and a setting for the custom source; every character in a cell as wide as the bundled font's widest digit, centred on Text Position; the box reaches a fifth of the size past the words and from the top of a "0" to the baseline, edges to whole pixels; when added SMPTE of the layer's source in white 36-pixel characters on a black box low in the middle, over the layer. **Gaps:** a timecode written in the file (a QuickTime timecode track, a DPX header) is not read: every source counts from its first frame, 0, and a layer with a file says so each frame as information, which also marks an export's fidelity incomplete; After Effects runs Timecode at 8 bits a channel only, ours at every depth; the semicolon before a drop-frame label's frames, the zeros in front (five digits for frames, four for feet) and the box's padding and height are ours; Text Position is in per cent of the picture, not pixels; the font is the bundled one only; AEJuice's slider-and-expression timecode on a text layer is not reproduced as such: Timecode's Custom source counts the same way without an expression. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-TC-001 to 027 and 040 to 046 (`tools/timecode_reference.py`, 471c0f53) in document 25; code 516fd328; `verification/D-527_timecode_table.md` 220 of 220. **On the card:** the box and words are drawn on the processor (`layer_fx::timecode_picture`, through Numbers' words), laid on by Numbers' pass `over`; no new pass, no tone mode; perf stage `effect: timecode` (Stage::ALL 209); B-155 shows no fall-back warning. **Timing** (`verification/B-407_timecode_timing_table.md`), PROVISIONAL (the machine was not quiet), Draw on: GPU, a 1920 by 1080 still, milliseconds a frame first / again: Noise alone 12.0 / 3.9, Timecode of the composition at size 200 then Noise 290.0 / 3.9, custom drop frame at size 120 on a half-opacity box, composite off, then Noise 229.0 / 6.1; a frame Timecode has not drawn before costs about 220 to 280 milliseconds more, far above the row's Target P2 (4 ms added); a frame drawn before is kept and costs at most about 2 more. **For the owner:** reading a file's own starting timecode needs a reader for the files' timecode tracks and headers, which we do not have; until then every source counts from 0 and says so. Is that acceptable, or should a file's timecode reader be its own project?

D-516 / Stretch Wipe, after the purpose of CycoreFX's CC Scale Wipe (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md` Transition, row 278) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-11 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-396.** **What was built.** `core.stretch_wipe`, named Stretch Wipe (a name of our own), in Transition: everything past a line through the Center stretched along the Direction, with Scale, Center and Direction, all keyable. **Overlap checked:** Linear Wipe (B-107) cuts along a straight edge without stretching; Transform scales the whole layer; Push Iris (D-515) pushes the picture out round a hole. **Sources read:** the CycoreFX HD 1.8.1 manual's CC Scale Wipe page (what the effect does and the controls); for the parts reused, this project's own wipe pass (B-107, D-510). No source gives a formula or the settings when added. Nothing is ported. **Interpretations (ours):** the manual says the effect stretches a layer off the screen (or onto it) by moving the scale center, and names Scale (the scale factor), Center (the point of origin for the wipe) and Direction (the angle in which the layer is scaled), but publishes no formula, so the rule is ours, in `tools/stretch_wipe_reference.py` and document 21: everything past a line through the Center, across the Direction, stretched Scale times along the Direction, so the line's own colours draw out in streaks and moving the Center across the layer stretches it off the drawing. **Gaps:** CycoreFX publishes no formula and no settings when added, so the rule and those settings are ours; not proven equal to CC Scale Wipe's look; there is no Completion, as in CycoreFX's own controls: the wipe is made by keying the Center or the Scale; the side behind the line is left as it is; the layer never grows. D-547 / The card's maths audit (B-427; D-100, ADR-006) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-11 under the owner's /loop request; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; pictures change only where the card disagreed with the processor.** **Finding.** This machine's card (NVIDIA RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, Vulkan, driver 610.88) takes a signed whole number's `%` as unsigned when the left side is negative: -1 % 12 gave 3, -7 % 6 gave 3, and the wrap ((-2 % 7) + 7) % 7 gave 2, not 5. Signed `/` is right, and a divisor that is a power of two comes out right by luck. **Shown wrong first.** A negative Noise Phase (Noise Alpha) or Evolution (Fractal Noise) with a cycle of 3, 5 or 7 drew a different noise on the card: 24 of 56 checks failed before the fix, up to 180 levels apart (`verification/D-547_card_remainder_before_table.md`, pictures `noise_alpha_card_before.png`). **Fixed** in `cell_noise_look` as `rem_euclid` with `%` kept off negatives: for z < 0, z mod p = p - 1 - ((-1 - z) mod p). After: 56 of 56 checks. Every `%` in `src/gpu.rs`'s card code was read: the noise's period in `cell_noise_look` (Noise Alpha's Cycle Noise, Fractal Noise's Cycle Evolution) was the only one that could meet a negative number with a divisor that is not a power of two, and the only one fixed. The others hold: `from_hsl`'s sextant (the hue always comes from `rem` or `hsl`, 0 to 360, so its floor is never negative); `around` (Offset; the shift is brought inside the drawing first, so the position is never negative); `turns` (divisor 4: for a power of two the unsigned remainder of a negative number's bits is already the wrapped answer); Fractal's bands (the escape count is never negative there, inside returns first, and Cycle Offset is 0 to 1000); Fractal's Hue Wheel band (`b % s` after `b < 0` returns); Lens Dirt's mirror (already kept off negatives, B-425); the `% 2` parity tests in Bend It's bars and 3D Glasses' interlace (a negative number's parity is the same either way); and every `u32` remainder. **The f64 vector cast (lane A's finding, B-346).** In the warp pass's Strobe Light case, `vec4<f32>(vec4<f64>(p) * b)` with p a texel just read drew 255 on every pixel. Measured in that pass: widening the texel channel by channel, or scaling in single precision, or widening only its three colours, each drew right; widening the whole four-channel texel and then multiplying in double precision drew wrong whether it was narrowed whole or channel by channel, so the narrowing cast is not the fault. In a small shader of its own on this card, every shape gave the right answer, including the exact shapes at Noise Alpha's alpha scale, Kira-kira's sum, the adjustment mix-back and the chain's stage mix. **So the cast is proven bad only in that one context**, which lane A already fixed channel by channel. The other places that widen a whole four-channel value to double precision (Lens Blur and Simple Choker's sums, Offset, Kira-kira, Simple Wire Removal, 3D Glasses, Glass Melt, the adjustment mix-back, an effect's Mix and the chain's stage mix) each sit in a pass of their own, and their card tests pass again within 1 level on this build: b338, b386, b389, b137, b221, b123, b156, b115, b151, b172, b107 and b155 (b157's audit is a measurement, not run). No cast was changed. Evidence: `tests/b427_card_remainder.rs`, `verification/D-547_card_remainder_table.md`, pictures `verification/D-547 pictures/`; speed `verification/B-427_card_remainder_timing_table.md`.

D-531 / CC Environment, after CycoreFX's CC Environment (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Perspective, row 339) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-11 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; the card within 1 level of the processor on every fixture and picture; no new tolerance; one new card pass (`environment`), no tone mode; built B-411.** **What was built.** `core.cc_environment`, named CC Environment, under Camera & Lens: Environment (a layer of the composition, D-189's way), Mapping (Spherical, Probe, Vertical Cross), Horizontal Pan, Tilt, Roll, Field of View and Filter Environment. It shows an environment picture round the viewer, as a 3D program's sky does, filling the layer's shape, with its own fake 3D, as the P0-12 row allows a self-contained effect to. **Overlap checked:** CC Cylinder (D-530) wraps the layer's own picture on a shape; Displacement Map and Time Difference read another layer but draw no view. D-563 / Shadow/Highlight's Midtone Contrast and Black/White Clip (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md` Color Correction, row 125) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-11 under the owner's /loop request (the partial-rows pass); every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-443.** **What was built.** Three of the settings D-400 left as gaps, after After Effects' Shadow/Highlight: Midtone Contrast (-100 to 100), Black Clip and White Clip (0 to 50 per cent), each keyable. After D-400's lift, Midtone Contrast is Color Grade's contrast curve (D-397) on the lightness, l' = l + m l (1 - l) (2 l - 1); the clips count the layer's lightness in 256 bins as Stretch Levels does (D-351, `frame_stats::clip_points`) and stretch it so the clipped share reaches, and passes, the layer's own darkest and lightest bins in use; the chroma follows each change toward black or white. What the three controls do is taken from the panel's wording as recalled. D-580 / Card Wipe, after After Effects' Card Wipe (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Transition, row 270) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-11 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; the card within 1 level of the processor on every fixture and picture; no new tolerance; one new card pass (`cardwipe`), no tone mode; built B-460.** **What was built.** `core.card_wipe`, named Card Wipe, under Transition: Transition Completion, Transition Width, Back Layer, Rows & Columns, Rows, Columns, Card Scale, Flip Axis, Flip Direction, Flip Order, Gradient Layer, Timing Randomness, Random Seed; the camera (X, Y and Z Rotation, X, Y Position, Z Position, Focal Length); the light (Light Type, Light Intensity, Light Color, Light Position, Light Depth, Ambient Light); the material (Diffuse Reflection, Specular Reflection, Highlight Sharpness). It cuts the layer into cards that flip over to show the Back Layer, drawn with its own fake 3D, as the P0-12 row allows a self-contained effect to, the same way CC Cylinder and CC Sphere are. The Back Layer and Gradient Layer are D-189's layer settings, fitted as `stretch`. **Overlap checked:** Card Dance (row 271, missing) moves cards by a layer's values rather than flipping them as a transition; Block Dissolve and Venetian Blinds cut the layer flat with no turn, back or light; Gradient Wipe uses a gradient layer for a flat reveal. No plug-in in PLUGINS.md replaces it. **Sources read:** Adobe's Transition effects page (helpx, Card Wipe's section: the controls and a sentence on each, as named in `tools/card_wipe_reference.py`); a Creative COW thread on Card Wipe's gradient order; EFFECTS.md row 270 and its P0-12 row, and PLUGINS.md. Adobe's page on the lighting and material controls Card Wipe shares with Card Dance answered 403. No source gives a formula or the settings when added. Nothing is ported. **Interpretations (ours):** a card turns about its own middle by half a turn as the sweep passes it, its order a share 0 to 1 by Flip Order (the gradient's brightness for Gradient), mixed towards a random share by Timing Randomness, its progress clamp((c (1 + w) - o) / w, 0, 1) over Transition Width; Random flips each card's axis and direction by Noise's hash; the camera looks from X, Y Position at Z Position focal lengths in front with Focal Length on a 36 mm frame, turned X then Y then Z about the drawing's middle, so as added the picture is unchanged; the nearest card a pixel's ray meets is drawn, its front the picture and its back the Back Layer upright (clear when none); the light (distant or point, at Light Position and Light Depth drawing widths in front) gives ambient, diffuse and a Blinn-Phong highlight; when added: completion 0, width 50, 8 by 8 independent, scale 1, axis X, positive, left to right, no layers, randomness 0, seed 0, no turn, position [50, 50], Z 1, 50 mm, a distant white light of intensity 1 at [50, 50] and depth 1, ambient 0.25, diffuse 0.75, specular 0, sharpness 5; every number keyable, the words exact; the layer never grows; a draft changes nothing. **Gaps:** the composition's camera and lights are not used: the cards are seen by the effect's own camera and lit by its own light (P0-12, D-355), so Camera System's Corner Pins and Comp Camera and the First Comp Light are not built; Transform Order is fixed (rotate X, then Y, then Z, about the drawing's middle); Position Jitter and Rotation Jitter are not built; Adobe gives no formula and no settings when added, so when each card turns, the camera, the light model and the settings when added are ours and not proven equal to Card Wipe's; the nearest card a ray meets wins even where that card's picture is clear; one ray a pixel, so the cards' edges are not smoothed; the menu words (Columns Follows Rows, the eight Flip Order directions, Distant Source and Point Source) are written from Adobe's control names without a source listing every word; the shared lighting and material help page answered 403 and was not read. D-581 / CC Force Motion Blur as an effect (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Time, row 291) / **PROPOSED on 2026-10-11** under the owner's /loop request; **ACCEPTED (a) on 2026-10-12, the owner saying "go with your recommendations on all six"; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; no new tolerance; no card pass, no tone mode; built B-470.** **What CycoreFX says** (CycoreFX HD 1.7.1 manual, the CC Force Motion Blur section, read in full): it blends several in-between moments of the layer's own contents into each frame, and is meant for an adjustment layer or a precomposed layer; its controls are Motion Blur Samples, Override Native Shutter, Shutter Angle (used only with the override) and Native Motion Blur (on or off, for the nested composition's own motion blur); it ignores the shutter phase. An Adobe community thread ("difference between CC Force Motion Blur and Pixel Motion Blur") adds that it slices each frame into sub-frames and that 8 samples is usual. **Why it does not map cleanly onto our motion blur:** D-188's layer motion blur samples only the layer's transform at moments inside the shutter; drawings, effects and a composition layer's picture are read once, at the frame itself ("drawings hold"), and P0-4 takes whole frames for other times. CC Force Motion Blur's whole point is to blur what moves inside a nested composition, which needs that composition drawn at fractional moments, a thing no part of the app does today. **The choice:** (a) build `core.force_motion_blur` for composition layers only: the nested composition drawn at N moments inside the shutter (its keys, transforms and effect settings read at each moment; drawings still hold at their frame) and averaged in linear premultiplied light; Motion Blur Samples is N, Native Motion Blur switches the nested composition's own D-188 blur on or off, Override Native Shutter with Shutter Angle replaces the composition's shutter angle, the phase ignored as CycoreFX does; processor first, the card later; costs N nested draws a frame. (b) as (a), and also on adjustment layers, which would redraw every layer under it at each moment. (c) leave row 291 partial: D-188's layer motion blur stays the way to blur movement. **Recommended: (a)**, with drawings holding, as the smallest form that does what the effect is for; (b) can follow if a tutorial needs it. **What was built (B-470).** `core.force_motion_blur`, named CC Force Motion Blur, under Time: Motion Blur Samples (1 to 64, 8 when added), Override Native Shutter (off when added), Shutter Angle (0 to 720, 180) and Native Motion Blur (on when added); the two numbers keyable. On a composition layer without a Time Remap, the composition inside is drawn at N moments across the shutter (`model::at_moment` moves every key time inside by the moment; `cache::cels_only` keeps the later moments out of the effect cache) and averaged in linear premultiplied light, the average laid as CC Wide Time's is; Native Motion Blur off draws a copy of the project with the motion blur inside switched off. **Sources read:** the CycoreFX HD 1.7.1 manual's CC Force Motion Blur section and the Adobe community thread named above; nothing is ported. **Gaps:** only composition layers: an adjustment layer (D-581 (b)), a holder with a Time Remap, and any other layer keep their picture and record EFFECT_UNSUPPORTED on each frame; drawings, in and out points, text, shapes and expressions inside hold at the whole frame; a composition inside with its own time stretch takes its moments unstretched by it; processor only, no card pass for the moments or the average; CycoreFX gives no formula and no settings when added beyond its manual's words, so the moments' spacing (the shutter opening on the frame) and 8, off, 180, on when added are ours. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-FMB-001 to 030 (`tools/force_motion_blur_reference.py`, 92cb0d59) in document 25; code 1cac5bad; `verification/D-581_force_motion_blur_table.md` 126 of 126; perf stage `effect: force motion blur` (Stage::ALL 214 on lane-b). **Timing** (`verification/B-470_force_motion_blur_timing_table.md`): PROVISIONAL, measured while other lanes built (4 cargo or rustc processes before and after): on the reference shot precomposed, once warm, 8 samples at 180 degrees cost about 349 ms a frame over the shot alone (448.8 against 100.0 ms) and 16 at 360 degrees about 310 ms (409.8); played in order a second time through the viewer's cache, 31.5 against 28.6 ms.

D-582 / CC Rainfall as its own effect (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Simulation, row 359) / **PROPOSED on 2026-10-11** under the owner's /loop request; **ACCEPTED (b) on 2026-10-12, the owner saying "go with your recommendations on all six"; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; no new tolerance; no card pass, no tone mode; built B-471.** **What CycoreFX says** (CycoreFX HD 1.8.1 manual, the CC Rainfall section, read in full): Drops, Size, Scene Depth (pixels), Speed, Wind, Variation % (Wind), Spread, Color, Opacity; Background Reflection (Influence %, Spread Width, Spread Height); Transfer Mode (Composite or Lighten); Composite With Original; Extras (Appearance: Refracting or Soft Solid, Offset, Ground Level %, Embed Depth %, Random Seed). Adobe's tutorial "Add rain to video" gives some values (Drops 5000 when added, Speed 4000 in its example). **Why a second name over `core.rain` (D-163) does not fit:** core.rain is a flat field of streaks (colour, density as a share of cells, spacing, length, width, direction, speed in pixels a frame, seed, opacity). Of CC Rainfall's 19 controls only Color, Opacity, Random Seed and Speed (in our pixels a frame) map cleanly; Drops is a count where ours is a share, and Size, Scene Depth, Wind with Variation, Spread, the background reflection, both transfer modes, Composite With Original, Appearance, Ground Level and Embed Depth have nothing under them. D-383 and D-394 allow a second name only where every control maps (Split 2 mapped all of its own), so 4 of 19 is not a second name. **The choice:** (a) a second name `core.cc_rainfall` anyway, carrying those 4 controls under CycoreFX's names and core.rain's other 5 under ours, and logging the other 15 as gaps; (b) a new self-contained fake-3D rain, drawn by the effect itself as Card Wipe and CC Sphere are: drops placed in a volume Scene Depth deep, smaller and slower with distance, Wind with Variation tilting them, Spread, Ground Level and Embed Depth where they stop, Soft Solid drops (Refracting, which bends the picture behind each drop, and Background Reflection as a second step), Composite or Lighten, Composite With Original; every rule ours, fixtures first; (c) leave row 359 partial, core.rain standing in. **Recommended: (b)**, since rain with depth is what CC Rainfall is used for, with Refracting and Background Reflection logged as gaps in its first build if they do not fit. **What was built (B-471).** `core.cc_rainfall`, named CC Rainfall, under Generate beside Rain: Drops, Size, Scene Depth, Speed, Wind, Variation % (Wind), Spread, Color, Opacity, Transfer Mode (Composite or Lighten), Composite With Original and, from Extras, Ground Level and Random Seed; every number keyable. Drops are placed in a volume Scene Depth deep behind the picture, scaled F / (F + depth) with F the drawing's width, so the far ones are smaller, slower and fainter; each tilts within Spread and has its own wind; each falls from wholly above the picture to Ground Level and round again by the composition's clock, a streak of half a frame's travel; they are laid far to near in Color and the rain laid over the layer, or alone. `core.rain` (D-163) and its fixtures are unchanged. **Sources read:** the CycoreFX HD 1.8.1 manual's CC Rainfall section and Adobe's tutorial "Add rain to video" (Drops 5000 when added), as named above; nothing is ported. **Gaps:** Background Reflection (Influence, Spread Width, Spread Height), the Refracting appearance (every drop is drawn as a soft solid streak), Offset and Embed Depth are not built; CycoreFX gives no formula, so the volume, the perspective (focal length the drawing's width), the streak of half a frame's travel, the fall from above the picture to the ground and round again, the ranges and every setting when added but Drops are ours; processor only, no card pass; every row tries every drop. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-RAIN3D-001 to 037 (`tools/cc_rainfall_reference.py`, 25739042) in document 25; code 92369655; `verification/D-582_cc_rainfall_table.md` 166 of 166; perf stage `effect: cc rainfall` (Stage::ALL 215 on lane-b). **Timing** (`verification/B-471_cc_rainfall_timing_table.md`): PROVISIONAL (2 cargo or rustc processes from other lanes counted): over two runs, once warm, the reference shot with an animated Noise measured 126.2 and 72.5 ms a frame without CC Rainfall and 38.5 to 62.5 ms with it (5000 drops as added, 20000 drops at size 4, or 5000 near drops at size 6), so the effect's own cost could not be told apart from the run-to-run spread on a busy machine; a quiet re-measure would settle it.

D-566 / The owner's fixture rule: when a pinned case may be regenerated / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-12 by the owner: "go with your recommendations on all six".** Fixtures stay read-only to implementation work (`CLAUDE.md`, document 25), with two exceptions, each done the same way. (1) A fixture case that only records that a setting is refused because it is not built yet (its expected frame is the drawing without it, plus the refusal) may be regenerated by its own reference script when that setting is built. (2) A fix to a case's description only, with every expected value unchanged, is allowed. Either is done in its own fixtures commit, before the code, written by the reference script and not by hand, and every changed case is listed by name in the decision's records, with what changed in it. Fixtures whose values come from working behaviour stay read-only: a feature that would change them must be off for older files, D-304's way (written to the file only if moved, keyed or already there, and read as the old behaviour when absent), or go back to the owner. First use: FX-TURBNOISE-029 and 030 (D-567), which pin Turbulent Noise's then-unbuilt `dynamic` fractal type and `spline` noise type as refused.

D-600 / The owner's plan for the parked groups (P0-6, P0-13, P0-17, P0-18) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-12 by the owner, from the owner's answers of that day.** It replaces the 2026-10-08 order (D-355, `EFFECTS.md` build order) that put all four last together. **Order:** mesh and brush warping (P0-18) first, then particles (P0-6), then 3D surfaces (P0-17), then motion from footage (P0-13). **Particles,** in the owner's words: "however the real particle effects/3rd party plugins for AE works. if it's real 3d, 2d, or fake, go full all out with recreating them." So they are full 3D particle simulations, drawn inside the effect through the composition's camera, the self-contained way Card Wipe and CC Sphere draw theirs. That is not true 3D layers, so D-309 and D-355 stand for layers (P0-12 stays skipped). **Motion from footage:** "Blur + retiming only". This program's own motion estimate between frames, for Pixel Motion Blur and Timewarp, then Warp Stabilizer if the estimate holds up. 3D Camera Tracker, Object Matte, mocha shape and Camera-Shake Deblur are skipped by the owner's choice. Rolling Shutter Repair stays missing, after Warp Stabilizer. **3D surfaces,** in the owner's words: "how AE treats them/are done." Wave World is a flat height-field simulation whose output is a map; Caustics renders light through that surface; Card Dance and Shatter are 3D inside the effect, through the composition's camera and with lights. `docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`: the P0-6, P0-13, P0-17 and P0-18 rows, the build order, the two particle picks and the four skipped rows (three of them counted among Adobe's rows, so 3 fewer missing; Object Matte is a tool, not counted). First work: P0-18, D-601 onward.

D-571 / Color Grade, third unit, the last of Lumetri Color's gaps (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Color Correction, row 121, Lumetri Color; D-397, D-398) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-12 under the owner's /loop request; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-450.** **What was built.** `core.color_grade` gains, each starting where it changes nothing and every number keyable: four curves after Hue vs Saturation, typed as points like it, in Lumetri's order: Hue vs Hue (a hue and a turn of -180 to 180 degrees), Hue vs Luma (a hue and a lift of -100 to 100), Luma vs Saturation and Saturation vs Saturation (a brightness or a saturation, 0 to 100, and a saturation, 100 as it was); the HSL Secondary's Secondary Wheels (One or Three), with a Shadow and a Highlight wheel (each a hue, an amount and a lightness) beside the old wheel, which becomes the midtones'; and the key's Denoise and Blur (0 to 100), which tidy the key before it is used and show in Show Key's mask view. Draft halves Denoise and Blur. Saved by D-121's rule, so a D-398 file opens, draws and saves exactly as before. **Our choices (deviations).** Adobe publishes no maths, so every rule is ours (document 21): Hue vs Hue turns the HLS hue by the curve eased round the circle and keeps lightness and saturation, greys untouched; Hue vs Luma lifts each channel by the curve times the colour's chroma over 200; the two saturation curves are Vibrance's rule (D-140) at the curve's value of the luma or the HLS saturation, flat past the end points and eased between them; the three wheels are Color Balance's weights (D-130) on the keyed pixel's luma; Denoise is Median's disc (D-203) of radius denoise / 10 and Blur Gaussian Blur's kernel of sigma blur / 10, edges repeated, in that order. On the card the curves are four new tone modes, 120 to 123, and mode 43 takes the three wheels; a grade with Denoise or Blur above 0 is drawn by the processor (the key's median and blur read round each pixel), the same picture, slower. **Not built.** Highlight recovery past white: the grade works on encoded colours held between 0 and 1 (D-397), so nothing lies past white to recover, and any rule would be invented; logged in document 21. Also still not built: the eyedropper, dragged curve points and wheels, Adobe's bundled looks, Lumetri's Sharpen and a squarer vignette, so row 121 stays partial. Evidence: FX-GRADE3-001 to 034 (`tools/color_grade_3_reference.py`, fixtures 50f640ae), code 3aec1083, `tests/b450_color_grade_3.rs`, `verification/D-571_color_grade_3_table.md` 195 of 195 checks (fixtures within 6.5e-7, every card picture within 1 level), FX-GRADE-001 to 034 and FX-GRADE2-001 to 040 unchanged; B-155 shows no fall-back; speed `verification/B-450_color_grade_3_timing_table.md` (PROVISIONAL, the machine busy with other lanes' tests, two on the same card: the curves and three wheels about 10 ms a 1080p layer on the card and about 50 on the processor; a refined key, drawn by the processor, came out slower with the card on than off (737 against 349 ms a frame, three layers), to be measured again on a quiet machine). **Later:** Lumetri's Sharpen and the squarer vignette were built by D-637 (B-517); **the owner's answer of 2026-10-13** (relayed by the coordinator): dragged curves and wheels and the key eyedropper stay gaps, so row 121 stays partial.

D-614 / Particle Playground's property mappers, after After Effects' Persistent and Ephemeral Property Mappers (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md` row 364; P0-6, D-600, D-613) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-12 under the owner's /loop request and D-600, as the second step of the coordinator's Particle Playground unit ("and the property mappers, as far as they fit the no-carried-state rule"); every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5, every particle's numbers within 1e-7; no new tolerance; built B-494.** **What was built.** Two mappers on `core.particle_playground`, each reading a layer's red, green and blue under every particle into the particle's colour, opacity, scale, angle, place, speed or force, between a Min and a Max per channel, with D-613's Affects. The Persistent one sets the property at every step and keeps it; the Ephemeral one works it through an operator (set, add, difference, subtract, multiply, min, max) for one step (speed and force) or for the drawing only (colour, opacity, scale, angle, place). 16 numbers, 9 words and 4 layers added, all keyable, each as added when a file leaves it out, so a file written before D-614 is the effect it was and is saved as it was. Nothing is carried from frame to frame: a property is part of the particle, worked out along its own steps from its birth. **Sources read:** Adobe's Particle Playground help, for what each mapper control is for. Nothing is copied or ported. **Interpretations (ours; Adobe publishes no formula and no settings when added):** the whole rule is in `tools/particle_mapper_reference.py` and document 21: the map's channel sRGB-coded, read at the pixel under the particle, and put back on the 8-bit level it lies within 1e-4 of (maps are held in single precision, which moves an 8-bit level by up to about 1e-7; a finer value is kept as it is); the Persistent values set after the Particle Exploder is asked and before each step; the Ephemeral speed and force taken back after the step; children born with their parent's properties; scale and opacity at 0 or below not drawn. **Gaps logged:** the Mass, Kinetic and Static Friction, Angular Velocity, Torque, Gradient Velocity, separate X and Y Scale and Lifespan properties (nothing in this playground has mass, friction or spin, or dies, so they would change nothing yet); Character and Font Size (no text particles); the maps read as they stand at the frame drawn, not as they moved. D-611 / Particle Space's textured particles, after CycoreFX's CC Particle World textured types (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md` Simulation, row 357; P0-6, D-600, D-610) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-12 under the owner's /loop request and D-600, as D-610 plans it (textured particles are D-611/B-491); every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-491.** **What was built.** Three more Particle Types on `core.particle_space`: Textured Square, Textured Disc and Textured Faded Disc, each showing a layer of the composition (Texture Layer, D-189's layer setting, read whole at its own size at the frame drawn) and turning (Rotation Speed, -3600 to 3600 degrees a second, and Initial Rotation, 0 to 360 degrees, a random share of it per particle; both keyable, both read at the particle's birth, 0 when added). The texture is taken down through its own smaller copies (each half the size, the mean of the pixels under it) as the particle shrinks, two copies mixed, so a far particle shows the texture's average and does not shimmer. With no Texture Layer, the textured kinds draw in the Color Map's colour, so Textured Disc and Textured Faded Disc are D-610's Disc and Faded Sphere unlit. 46 numbers now (44 + 2); a file written before D-611 reads as added and is saved as before (59 settings, no new keys) until one of the three is changed. **Overlap checked:** nothing of ours draws a layer as a particle; Particle Playground's layer map and Particle Emitter's sprites (EFFECTS.md rows 364 and 367) are to reuse this. **Sources read:** the D-610 sources' descriptions of CC Particle World's Textured Square, Textured Disc, Textured Faded Disc, Texture Layer and rotation controls for what they are for; for the parts reused, this project's D-189 layer setting and document 21's bilinear. Nothing is copied or ported. **Interpretations (ours; CycoreFX publishes no formula and no settings when added):** the rule is in `tools/particle_texture_reference.py` and document 21: the turn and coverings, the copies' levels and how one is picked (log2 of the texture's longer side over the particle's width), never lit, Depth Cue Fog mixing the texture towards the fog colour, the Color Map not used when there is a texture; a texture layer with no picture at the frame (before its in point) draws no textured particles; a named layer not in the composition leaves the effect out with the warning EFFECT_LAYER_MISSING every frame (D-189's rule 4); CC Particle World's Texture Time and its texture's own time-shift choices are not built (no source says what they do beyond the name), so the layer is read at the frame drawn. **Fixture correction (D-566).** The five refused files FX-PTEX-026 to 030 first held a texture layer `late` starting after their six frames ended, which the project format refuses, so they did not open; the tool now leaves that layer out of them and they were regenerated alone in 3956d225 (cases 001 to 025 and every expected value unchanged). **On the card:** the one `particles` pass draws the textured kinds too, the texture's copies packed into one picture the pass reads; no card mode taken, 160 to 179 stay free. A driver fault found and worked around: on this card (RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, Vulkan) widening a whole texture read to double precision in one step (`vec4<f64>(textureLoad(...))`) gave wrong values, while widening each part on its own was right; `src/gpu.rs` does the latter with a B-491 comment, and other passes that widen a texture read that way may carry the same fault. **Ceiling logged:** a keyed setting makes every frame sample the settings once a frame from the in point (D-610), so a keyed Particle Space costs more the later the frame: FX-PSPACE-050 measured 2.6, 51.6, 135.4 and 247.6 ms at frames 30, 1440, 4800 and 9999 (about 25 ms a thousand frames, about 355 ms at 10 minutes at 24 a second); unkeyed it stays flat (about 1 ms at frames 30 to 9999), as only births inside the longest life are worked out. Upgrade path: sample only Birth Rate from the in point and the rest over the last Longevity plus a second. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-PTEX-001 to 030 (`tools/particle_texture_reference.py`, 26d238cb, corrected under D-566 in 3956d225) in document 25; code 77875949; `verification/D-611_particle_texture_table.md` 164 of 164. **Timing** (`verification/B-491_particle_texture_timing_table.md`), PROVISIONAL (machine not quiet): with a 1920 by 1080 texture on the reference shot, about 14 ms a layer on the card with 1000 particles alive and 65 with 6000, about 92 to 95 on the processor; untextured about 12 and 5; a quiet re-measure is owed. **For the owner:** whether the rotation settings' ranges and their share-per-particle reading suit you, and how far particles soften the texture.

D-610 / The particle engine (P0-6) and its first effect, Particle Space, after CycoreFX's CC Particle World (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md` Simulation, row 357; D-600) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-12 under the owner's /loop request and D-600 ("however the real particle effects/3rd party plugins for AE works. if it's real 3d, 2d, or fake, go full all out with recreating them"); the design approved as written by the coordinator on 2026-10-12; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every particle within 1e-7; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-490.** **What was built.** `src/particles.rs`, the engine, and `core.particle_space`, named Particle Space, in Generate (the panel has no Simulation group), with CC Particle World's controls in its order: Birth Rate, Longevity, the Producer's place and radius, the eleven Animations (Explosive, Direction Axis, Cone Axis, Viscous, Twirl, Twirly, Vortex, Fire, Jet Sideways, Fractal Omni, Fractal Uni), Velocity, Inherit Velocity, Gravity, Resistance, Direction Axis, Extra, Extra Angle, Gravity Vector, the Floor (None, Ice, Glue, Bounce) with its bounces, five Particle Types (Line, Faded Sphere, Shaded Sphere, Disc, Bubble), sizes, Max Opacity, the five Color Maps with Birth, Death and five custom colours, Volume Shade, Transfer Mode (Composite, Screen, Add), the effect's own camera, Depth Cue (None, Fade, Fog), the light, Composite on Original and Random Seed; plus an Air group of ours (Wind and Turbulence: CC Particle World has none, Trapcode Particular does), whose zeros as added leave the rest alone. 44 numbers, all keyable, 7 choices and 8 colours. Particles are drawn in real 3D inside the effect: through the composition camera when the file has one, nearer ones larger, in front, and moving more when the camera moves; through the effect's own orbiting camera when not. **The engine's rule: no state is carried from frame to frame** (document 20): a particle at a frame is a pure function of the seed, its number and the settings sampled once a frame from the in point, stepped on one grid of 4 steps a frame with gravity and resistance in closed form, so any frame drawn alone, on any tile, in any order, equals the same frame played from the start. **Overlap checked:** CC Rainfall (`core.rain`), Glue Gun and Write-on draw strokes, not a particle system; nothing of ours throws, pulls and floors particles in 3D; PLUGINS.md 2.1-2.2 asks for exactly this engine. **Sources read:** public descriptions of CC Particle World (good-elephant.co.jp, riotproducts.co.jp, ae.blender-osamu.com, makeuseof.com's tutorial and a bucknell.edu course blog; Adobe's help and motionarray refused, 403) for what each control is for, its order, and the sourced Birth Rate 2, Longevity 1 second and Inherit Velocity's range; for the parts reused, this project's D-58 camera and `grade::unit` noise (D-119, document 21). Nothing is copied or ported. **Interpretations and deviations (ours; CycoreFX publishes no formula and no settings when added):** the rule is in `tools/particle_space_reference.py` and document 21. Against the design text as approved, the build and its fixtures differ in these ways, each stated in the tool: the world's unit is the layer's width (not the composition's), its origin the layer's centre; Birth Rate's unit is 100 particles a second, our unit (CC's count is unpublished); the random draws are D-119's `grade::unit` hash, not splitmix64; every setting is sampled once a frame from the in point whenever any is keyed (not only Birth Rate); Viscous adds 3 to the resistance (not times 10); Wind is a pull like gravity; the light's z part is -sin of its height; Shaded Sphere and Bubble are always lit and Volume Shade lights only Disc and Faded Sphere; Origin is the input's colour under the spawn point; the five custom colours start from Birth to Death; the composition camera is used whenever `comp.camera` is set, at the frame drawn; there is no particle limit and so no `PARTICLE_LIMIT` diagnostic (the cost is the alive particles times their steps, measured below); the card draws from one new entry point, `particles`, with the particles placed, ordered and binned in 16 by 16 tiles on the processor, so no card mode was taken and modes 160 to 179 stay free. One new timing stage, `EffectParticleSpace` (238 to 239), as every effect has its own. **Gaps:** CycoreFX publishes no formula, so not proven equal to CC Particle World's look; Black Matte, Hold Particle Release and Grid & Guides are left out, as no source read says what they do; the composition camera cannot turn (D-58, D-309, D-355 stand), so through it the particles get pan, dolly and zoom only, and only the effect's own camera orbits; textured particles (Textured Square, Disc and Faded Disc, Texture Time, rotation) are D-611/B-491; solid 3D shapes (Star, Polygons, Cube and the rest) and the Lens types are later (D-612) and only if sourced; no motion blur of particles; no comp lights. Rule in document 21 and document 20; fixtures FX-PSPACE-001 to 071 (`tools/particle_space_reference.py`, 445393cf) in document 25; code f93a492f; `verification/D-610_particle_space_table.md` 383 of 383. **On the card:** one new pass, `particles` (each pixel draws its tile's particles in depth order with the processor's formulas in double precision); every fixture project at Full and Draft and the reference shot (three settings, frames 0, 100 and 239) within 1 level; B-155 shows no fall-back. **Timing** (`verification/B-490_particle_space_timing_table.md`), three layers on the reference shot, PROVISIONAL (machine not quiet: other lanes' cargo and rustc processes were running), card 62.6, 68.1 and 61.2 ms a frame (as added; 1000 a second, shaded spheres, over the drawing; 2000 a second living 3 s, vortex, faded spheres, added) against 22.6 for the Noise alone, about 13 to 15 ms added a 1080p layer; processor 79.1, 81.1 and 117.2 against 57.7; a quiet re-measure is owed. **For the owner:** whether the settings when added, Birth Rate's unit, the light and the shaded kinds' look, and the Air group suit you; the name Particle Space is ours.

D-601 / P0-18's shared part: a forward mesh and a backward field (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md` P0-18) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-12 under the coordinator's queue (the owner's D-600 order); no new tolerance; built B-480 (0a8631b7).** Two ways to bend a drawing, for P0-18's six effects: a forward mesh (where each grid corner lands, drawn triangle by triangle, a fold's later triangle on top, card warp mode 150) for Bezier Warp, Mesh Warp and Warp; and a backward field (a grid of steps blended bilinearly, each output pixel read back from its place plus the step, card warp mode 151) for Liquify, Reshape and Smear. This program's own rule (document 21); `tools/mesh_reference.py` works it a second way and checks itself; `src/mesh.rs` carries it, with 4 of 4 library tests. Nothing is ported. No effect of its own, so no fixture of its own: each effect's fixtures pin it.

D-650 / Our own motion estimate (P0-13) and its first effect, Pixel Motion Blur, after After Effects' Pixel Motion Blur (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Time, row 294; P0-13, row 44) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-12 under the owner's /loop request, within the owner's D-600 ("Blur + retiming only"); every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; drawn by the processor only, as Echo and CC Wide Time are, so no card comparison; no new tolerance; ADR-022; built B-530.** **What was built.** (1) The motion estimate (`src/flow.rs`): for two pictures of the same size, how far each pixel moved from one to the other, found by dense pyramidal Lucas-Kanade with a ridge term in double precision, on a weighted brightness and on alpha, with a fixed count of steps and no choice made on the data, so the same two pictures always give the same field. (2) `core.pixel_motion_blur`, named Pixel Motion Blur, in the Time group, with After Effects' settings: Shutter Control (Automatic, Manual), Shutter Angle (0 to 720 degrees), Shutter Samples (2 to 64) and Vector Detail (0 to 100), the three numbers keyable. It smears the layer along its own movement between the frame before and the frame after, as a camera's open shutter would: motion blur for footage and for drawings that move by being redrawn, where layer motion blur (D-188) only blurs a layer's transform. **Overlap checked:** layer motion blur (D-188) and CC Force Motion Blur (D-581) blur only what a transform or a composition inside moves; CC Wide Time (D-520) and Echo average whole frames and show separate copies; frame blending (D-216) mixes two source frames and refuses Pixel Motion (ADR-020), which stays refused; no plug-in in PLUGINS.md replaces it (after-the-fact motion blur is a parked pick there, 2.8). **Sources read:** Adobe's Time effects page, Distort effects page and Rolling Shutter Repair page (through web.archive.org, helpx refusing automated reading); ProVideo Coalition's two articles on Pixel Motion Blur; Adobe Learn's Pixel Motion Blur and Stabilize Footage videos; the UT Austin wiki on Timewarp; Foundry's Nuke OFlow page (for the weighting and block size only, as background). No text or code was copied; nothing is ported. **Interpretations (ours):** Adobe's page names the four controls, says Automatic takes the composition's motion blur settings and that Vector Detail 100 is one vector for every pixel, and lists where the effect fails (fast objects over a sharp still background, pixels appearing or disappearing); it publishes no formula and no settings when added, so the estimate and the rule are ours ("rule ours" precedent), in document 21: Automatic takes the composition's angle and samples whatever its switch says; the frames either side are the holder with the effects before, by the layer's own timing, a frame outside the layer standing in as the present one; two fields, back and ahead; the shutter centred on the frame, each sample reading the present frame along the motion at that pixel; 180 degrees, 16 samples and Vector Detail 20 when added. **Deviations and gaps:** not proven equal to After Effects, whose vectors are closed; the alpha channel is part of the estimate (our addition, so a drawing over nothing moves by its edges; opaque footage is unchanged by it); the shutter is centred on the frame (the composition's default phase), not set by the composition's phase; the smear is a gather, so a moving shape smears inward and only as far outward as the estimate spreads past its edge, which matches Adobe's own failure list and is not worked around; the frames either side are cut to the present drawing's rectangle, so motion from beyond its margins is not seen; on an adjustment layer nothing changes and TEMPORAL_SMOOTHING_SKIPPED says why; processor only (D-651). **Timing** PROVISIONAL (`verification/B-530_pixel_motion_blur_timing_table.md`): the reference shot's rows mostly time the viewer's cache, since its held drawings repeat; a frame whose drawings change costs far above the row's Target P4. Pictures in `verification/D-650 pictures/`, playtest `verification/B-530_playtest.md`, **awaiting the owner's playtest**.

D-651 / A card version of Pixel Motion Blur and the motion estimate (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Time, row 294) / **PROPOSED on 2026-10-12, not built.** Pixel Motion Blur (D-650) runs on the processor, as Echo, CC Wide Time and CC Force Motion Blur do, and a layer holding it is drawn by the processor with no diagnostic. A card version would add one card pass, `pixel_motion`, with modes 200 to 209 (grey pack, halve, tensor, residual, box across, box down, solve, enlarge, local smoothing, the gather), the frames either side sent to the card through `map_texture` (B-223), the fields kept in 32-bit float textures and the maths in f64 converted channel by channel (B-222). The present frame and its neighbours must meet on one side, which is why it is not done now; the card must agree with the processor within 1 level on every row before it is used, or it stays proposed. A faster processor estimate (its full-size steps run one after another) may come first, since the estimate is most of the cost. The owner may accept, change or refuse it.

D-652 / Timewarp, after After Effects' Timewarp (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Time, row 298; P0-13, row 44) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-12 under the owner's /loop request, within the owner's D-600 ("Blur + retiming only"); every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; drawn by the processor only, as Pixel Motion Blur (D-650) is, so no card comparison; no new tolerance; built B-531.** **What was built.** `core.timewarp`, named Timewarp, in the Time group, with After Effects' settings for D-600's list: Method (Whole Frames, Frame Mix, Pixel Motion), Adjust Time By (Speed, Source Frame), Speed (-1000 to 1000 per cent), Source Frame, the Tuning group (Vector Detail, Global Smoothness, Local Smoothness, Smoothing Iterations, Build From One Image, Correct Luminance Changes, Filtering Normal or Extreme, Error Threshold, Block Size, Red, Green and Blue Weight) and the Motion Blur group (Enable Motion Blur, Shutter Control Automatic or Manual, Shutter Angle, Shutter Samples), the numbers keyable. It reads the layer, with the effects before it, at a source time of its own, and makes the frames between the drawings by repeating them, by fading the two either side together, or by moving both along the motion D-650's estimate finds between them and mixing the two moved pictures. **Overlap checked:** frame blending (D-216) mixes a stretched layer's two source frames and refuses Pixel Motion (ADR-020), which stays refused, since Timewarp is the way to it; time remapping and time stretch change the layer's own time and come first, under Timewarp; Pixel Motion Blur (D-650) blurs without retiming; CC Wide Time and Echo average whole frames. **Sources read:** Adobe's Time effects page (through web.archive.org, helpx refusing automated reading), Adobe Learn, ProVideo Coalition and the UT Austin wiki on Timewarp. No text or code was copied; nothing is ported. **Interpretations (ours):** Adobe's page names the controls and says what each is for, and publishes no formula, so the rule is ours, in document 21: the source time sums Speed frame by frame from the in point, centred on each frame, so a constant 50 lands a quarter and three quarters between drawings, and Source Frame counts from the in point; the time is held inside the layer; the in-between moves the two drawings toward each other along a second-order path through both estimates; Extreme filtering reads with Keys' cubic (Catmull-Rom), as Transform's bicubic; the motion blur's moments are spread across the shutter in source time by the rate of change; the settings when added (Pixel Motion, Speed 50, Vector Detail 20, Smoothing Iterations 4, Error Threshold 1, Block Size 6, weights 0.3, 0.6 and 0.1, Shutter Samples 5) are ours where Adobe's are not stated. **Deviations and gaps:** not proven equal to After Effects, whose vectors are closed; Error Threshold is a smooth mix toward Frame Mix by how far the two moved pictures disagree, not a hard switch; the alpha channel is part of the estimate (our addition, as D-650); Matte Layer, Matte Channel, Warp Layer, Show (the vectors or the matte) and Source Crops are not built (outside D-600's list); Automatic takes the composition's angle and samples whatever its switch says, and the shutter is centred on the frame; on an adjustment layer nothing changes and TEMPORAL_SMOOTHING_SKIPPED says why; processor only. **Timing** PROVISIONAL, measured on a busy machine: inside Timewarp, Whole Frames and Frame Mix take about 110 to 120 ms a frame at Full, and Pixel Motion (as added) about 2 s at Full and 250 ms at Half when its estimate runs; above Target P4 and far from real time; no speed claim, to be re-measured on a quiet machine. (`verification/B-531_timewarp_timing_table.md`). Pictures in `verification/D-652 pictures/`, playtest `verification/B-531_playtest.md`, **awaiting the owner's playtest**.
