Code, test and table 33ea89bc; `verification/D-607_mask_smear_table.md` 144 of 144. **On the card:** warp mode 151; every fixture project at Full and Draft and the reference shot within 1 level, 36 of 36. **Timing** (`verification/B-486_mask_smear_timing_table.md`), PROVISIONAL, the machine busy with other lanes (5.3 GB of the card's memory in use by other programs): on the card 52.9 ms a frame for the square carried 200 right and 36.7 for the same turned, scaled and within a boundary at Liquid, 60 per cent, against 15.4 for the Noise alone; the processor 91.1 and 85.1 against 50.2. **For the owner:** nothing to decide; the playtest awaits.

D-653 / Warp Stabilizer, after After Effects' Warp Stabilizer (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Distort, row 170; P0-13, row 44) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-13 under the owner's /loop request, within the owner's D-600 ("Blur + retiming only", Warp Stabilizer "if the estimate holds up": it did, the fits recovering the fixtures' known shake); every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; drawn by the processor only, as Pixel Motion Blur (D-650) is, so no card comparison; no new tolerance; built B-532.** **What was built.** `core.warp_stabilizer`, named Warp Stabilizer, in the Distort group, with After Effects' settings except the gaps below: Result (Smooth Motion, No Motion), Smoothness (0 to 1000 per cent), Method (Position; Position, Scale, Rotation; Perspective), Preserve Scale, Framing (Stabilize Only; Stabilize, Crop; Stabilize, Crop, Auto-scale), Maximum Scale, Action-Safe Margin, Additional Scale and Detailed Analysis, the numbers keyable. For each pair of neighbouring frames it fits the camera's move to D-650's estimate, weighted by alpha and refitted twice with far points counting less; it chains the moves, smooths them over a window of frames about the present one (or holds them to the layer's first frame), and moves the picture back by the difference, then crops and scales so the edges the shake uncovers stay hidden. Nothing is analysed ahead or kept: every frame is worked from the drawings around it, so there is no Analyze button and nothing goes stale. **Overlap checked:** the motion tracker is left out by the charter (D-309) and stays so; Transform and the layer's own transform move a layer by hand; Timewarp (D-652) and Pixel Motion Blur (D-650) retime and blur on the same estimate; no plug-in in PLUGINS.md replaces it. **Sources read:** Adobe's Distort effects page, its stabilizing page and Premiere's Warp Stabilizer settings page (through web.archive.org, helpx refusing automated reading), Adobe Learn's Stabilize Footage video, and the articles by whoismatt.com, Larry Jordan, MediaStorm and Pond5. Adobe says Stabilize, Crop is Auto-scale with Maximum Scale at 100%, which ours keeps. No text or code was copied; nothing is ported. **Interpretations (ours):** Adobe's pages name the controls and say what each is for, and publish no formula, so the rule is ours, in document 21: the pair fit (a move; a move, scale and turn; or a full perspective), Vector Detail 50 for the estimate, 100 with Detailed Analysis; Smoothness turned into a Gaussian window of floor(fps Smoothness / 200 + 0.5) frames each side, narrowed near the layer's ends so it stays even; the crop the largest middle rectangle the steadied frame still covers, found per frame; Auto-scale fills it, held to Maximum Scale and the margin. **Deviations and gaps:** not proven equal to After Effects, whose analysis is closed; Method Subspace Warp (After Effects' default) is not built, so Position, Scale, Rotation is the default here, and a file asking for Subspace Warp keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame, with a warning; Framing Stabilize, Synthesize Edges, Crop Less Smooth More, Rolling Shutter Ripple, Show Track Points, the Objects (track points) group and the Analyze banner are not built (outside D-600's list, or having no meaning without an analysis pass); the crop is found per frame, so on a hard shake it can breathe in and out; the alpha channel weighs each pixel's vote (our addition, so a drawing over nothing is steadied by its own pixels); on an adjustment layer nothing changes and TEMPORAL_SMOOTHING_SKIPPED says why; processor only. **Timing** PROVISIONAL, measured on a partly busy machine while Rolling Shutter Repair's timing ran for part of it: inside the effect, as added about 6 s a frame at Full and 1.1 s at Half, Detailed Analysis about 13 s at Full; each frame works D-650's estimate for 12 neighbouring pairs a layer at Smoothness 50 (none kept between frames); far above Target P4; no speed claim, to be re-measured on a quiet machine. (`verification/B-532_warp_stabilizer_timing_table.md`). Pictures in `verification/D-653 pictures/`, playtest `verification/B-532_playtest.md`, **awaiting the owner's playtest**.

D-654 / Rolling Shutter Repair, after After Effects' Rolling Shutter Repair (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Distort, row 163; P0-13, row 44) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-13 under the owner's /loop request, within the owner's D-600 ("Blur + retiming only", Rolling Shutter Repair "then try": tried, and it takes most of the fixtures' known lean out); every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; drawn by the processor only, as Pixel Motion Blur (D-650) and Warp Stabilizer (D-653) are, so no card comparison; no new tolerance; built B-533.** **What was built.** `core.rolling_shutter_repair`, named Rolling Shutter Repair, in the Distort group, with After Effects' settings: Rolling Shutter Rate (0 to 100 per cent of a frame), Scan Direction (Top to Bottom, Bottom to Top, Left to Right, Right to Left), Method (Warp, Pixel Motion), Detailed Analysis and Pixel Motion Detail, the numbers keyable. Each row (or column) is taken to have been seen Rate x (its place - one half) of a frame after the frame's middle moment, and is read back along the motion toward the next frame (rows after the middle) or the frame before (rows before it): with Warp the whole frame's move, fitted as Warp Stabilizer's Position, Scale, Rotation model to D-650's estimate; with Pixel Motion the estimate itself at Pixel Motion Detail. A held drawing, or the layer's first or last frame, takes the motion on its other side turned round. Nothing is analysed ahead or kept. **Overlap checked:** Warp Stabilizer (D-653) steadies the whole frame but leaves the lean, and its Rolling Shutter Ripple is not built; Transform and Corner Pin skew by hand, the same for every frame; no plug-in in PLUGINS.md replaces it. **Sources read:** Adobe's Distort effects page and Rolling Shutter Repair page (through web.archive.org, helpx refusing automated reading) and Premiumbeat's rolling-shutter article. Adobe gives a DSLR about 50 to 70 per cent and a phone near 100; Premiumbeat gives Warp and Pixel Motion Detail 20 as the settings when added. No text or code was copied; nothing is ported. **Interpretations (ours):** Adobe's pages name the controls and say what each is for, and publish no formula, so the rule is ours, in document 21: the scan's timing (a pixel at place u, from 0 to 1 along the scan, seen r (u - 0.5) frames after the middle), each side's motion taken as straight over the frame, Warp as one whole-frame fit (Vector Detail 50, or 100 with Detailed Analysis), and the picture read back bilinearly. **Deviations and gaps:** not proven equal to After Effects, whose analysis is closed; the Rate when added is not confirmed by any source read (50 is the value tutorials report, used here), nor the Scan Direction when added (Top to Bottom, as Adobe says most cameras scan); After Effects' Warp tracks points and bends a mesh, so it can follow parts moving differently, where ours fits one move, scale and turn to the whole frame (Pixel Motion follows each part); motion is taken as straight between neighbouring frames, so a whip pan that changes speed within a frame is only partly mended; the edges a row moves in from outside are clear; the alpha channel weighs each pixel in the estimate (D-650's addition); on an adjustment layer nothing changes and TEMPORAL_SMOOTHING_SKIPPED says why; processor only. **Timing** PROVISIONAL, measured on a busy machine while Warp Stabilizer's timing ran: inside the effect, Pixel Motion takes about 1 s a frame at Full, and Warp (as added) about 7 s at Full and 390 ms at Half, which is not explained; above Target P4 and far from real time; no speed claim, to be re-measured alone on a quiet machine. (`verification/B-533_rolling_shutter_repair_timing_table.md`). Pictures in `verification/D-654 pictures/`, playtest `verification/B-533_playtest.md`, **awaiting the owner's playtest**.

D-631 / Caustics, after After Effects' Caustics (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Simulation, row 350; P0-17, L-02) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-12 by the coordinator** under the owner's /loop request and D-600's plan for P0-17 (the owner: "how AE treats them/are done"): "The D-630 design is approved; go ahead." D-671 / Bubbles, after CycoreFX's CC Bubbles (Simulation) (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, row 352) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-12 under the owner's /loop request (D-600: "however the real particle effects/3rd party plugins for AE works ... go full all out with recreating them"), lane C's design D-670 approved by the coordinator; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-550.** **What was built.** `core.bubbles`, in Generate beside Particle Space: Bubble Amount, Bubble Speed, Wobble Amplitude, Wobble Frequency, Bubble Size, Random Seed, Reflection Type (Inverse, World) and Shading Type (None, Lighten, Darken, Fade Inwards, Fade Outwards). Each bubble has its own place, size, pace and wobble from the seed; it rises (falls for a negative speed) from wholly below the layer to wholly above it and comes round again, swinging side to side, and shows the picture through itself: Inverse reads it turned over and spread, as a glass ball shows it; World reads the picture round it upright. The layer becomes the bubbles alone, laid in order onto clear. Nothing is carried from frame to frame (document 20, D-610): every frame works each bubble out from the in point, the keyed speed and wobble frequency summed from the in point (a `ponytail:` ceiling, O(frames) a frame when either is keyed, as Particle Space's). Draw code in the new `src/simulate.rs`; binning reuses `particles::tile_lists`, nothing in `src/particles.rs` changed. **Sources read:** the CycoreFX HD 1.8.1 manual's CC Bubbles page (the controls and what each is for, the five shadings, Inverse "self-contained, like refraction"); ProVideo Coalition's "After Effects A-Z: CC Bubbles". **Gaps:** CycoreFX publishes no formula, so the rule, the units (speed 1 lifts a bubble a quarter of the layer's height a second, size 1 a radius of about a fortieth of its height, wobble 10 a swing of one radius), the ranges and the settings when added are ours; the manual says Reflection Type World "reflects the source layer" without saying how, so World reads the picture round the bubble upright, ours; no tutorial page could be read in full (web.archive.org and motionarray refused automated reading), so the cases follow the CycoreFX manual and ProVideo Coalition's "After Effects A-Z: CC Bubbles" summary. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-BUBBLE-001 to 034 (`tools/bubbles_reference.py`, 8b07655b) in document 25; code e073f346; `verification/D-671_bubbles_table.md` 201 of 201. **On the card:** a new pass `bubbles`, in double precision, the bubbles placed and binned into the card's 16 by 16 tiles on the processor as the particles are; every fixture at Full and Draft and the reference shot at frames 0, 100 and 239 within 1 level (52 of 52 comparisons). One new measured stage, `effect: bubbles`.

D-647 / Turbulent Noise, Overflow, Transform and Sub Settings, after After Effects' Turbulent Noise (Noise & Grain) (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, row 224) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-13 under the owner's /loop request (the coordinator's lane B queue); every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; no existing Fractal Noise, Turbulent Noise or type expected value changed (FX-TURBNOISE-001 to 032, FX-TURBTYPE-001 to 025 and FX-FRACTAL rerun unchanged); built B-526.** **What was built.** `core.turbulent_noise` takes `overflow` (`allow_hdr` when added, `clip`, `soft_clamp` or `wrap_back`), `rotation` (-100000 to 100000 degrees, 0), `uniform_scaling` (`off`, or `on`: Scale Width and Height are left out), `perspective_offset` (`off`, or `on`: octave o slides 0.5^o of Offset), `sub_influence` (0 to 100 per cent, 50), `sub_scaling` (10 to 100 per cent, 50), `sub_rotation` (-100000 to 100000 degrees, 0), `sub_offset` (x then y in pixels, (0, 0)) and `center_subscale` (`off`, or `on`); every number can be keyed; Blending Mode adds `soft_light`, `hard_light`, `darken`, `lighten` and `difference`. A file without them reads them as added, and they are written only when moved, keyed or already in the file (D-304). Every setting as added takes the old path exactly, so every earlier file draws as before. Fractal Noise shares the engine and keeps its own settings as before. On the card Fractal Noise's pass takes the same rule as grade mode 112 when anything is moved. **App.** Rotation and Sub Rotation (dials), Sub Influence, Sub Scaling and Sub Offset on Turbulent Noise's card; Overflow, Uniform Scaling, Perspective Offset and Center Subscale among its choices, and the five new blending modes; a window from before sends none and they read as added. **Gaps.** Overlay is not built: FX-TURBNOISE-032 (D-445, a built effect, so D-566 does not cover it) pins Overlay as refused, and adding Overlay needs the owner's fixture decision; nor are Hue, Saturation, Color, Luminosity, None or the stencil and silhouette modes. Adobe publishes no formula, so the Transform, the Sub Settings and the Overflow rules are ours (Soft Clamp a tanh, Wrap Back a fold at black and white); After Effects' own defaults (Sub Influence 70, Sub Scaling 56) are not the as-added values, because 50 and 50 keep every earlier file drawing as before. Rotation turns round the drawing's middle. On the card Soft Clamp uses single precision's tanh (within a level); in a Float composition Allow HDR Results keeps D-319's behaviour (only black held). **Timing.** PROVISIONAL (a busy machine), `verification/B-526_turbulent_more_timing_table.md`: on the reference shot with three layers, Turbulent Noise as added 60.9 ms a frame on the card (58.5 for the Noise alone) and with every D-647 setting moved 78.0; on the processor 186.1 and 200.3 (111.8 alone); the moved settings add about 17 ms on the card and 14 on the processor, the settings as added nothing. **Evidence.** Fixtures first (01fd9691, `tools/turbulent_more_reference.py`, FX-TURBNOISE-033 to 060); code 0b39e8b8; `tests/b526_turbulent_more.rs`, `verification/D-647_turbulent_more_table.md` 305 of 305 checks; pictures in `verification/D-647 pictures/`; timing `verification/B-526_turbulent_more_timing_table.md`; playtest `verification/B-526_playtest.md`, awaiting the owner.

D-730 / Turbulent Noise, Saturation, Color, Luminosity, None, Stencil Alpha and Stencil Luma, after After Effects' Turbulent Noise (Noise & Grain) (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, row 224) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-13 under the owner's /loop request (the coordinator's lane B queue, option (a) on FX-TURBNOISE-060); every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; no existing expected value changed (FX-TURBNOISE-001 to 060 and FX-TURBTYPE-001 to 025 rerun unchanged); built B-600.** **What was built.** `core.turbulent_noise`'s Blending Mode adds `saturation`, `color`, `luminosity`, `none`, `stencil_alpha` and `stencil_luma`, on the processor (`grade::fractal_noise`) and the card (grade blend codes 10 to 15). Saturation, Color and Luminosity mix by Opacity as the other modes do. None draws the noise at Opacity in place of the layer, so None at Opacity 0 leaves the layer clear and is not skipped as a do-nothing; the stencils keep the layer by the noise's alpha or lightness at Opacity, and are not skipped at Opacity 0 either. The app's Blending Mode list gains the six. **Sources.** Adobe's After Effects help on Noise & Grain (Fractal Noise, whose modes Turbulent Noise shares) says its blending modes are the same as the Timeline's Modes column, except that None draws the fractal noise only and does not composite it on the layer. So None replaces the layer with the noise at Opacity (as D-413's lay_pattern None), and Stencil Alpha and Stencil Luma follow the Timeline's own stencils (D-301, `composite::blend_pixel`). Adobe publishes no formula for Saturation, Color or Luminosity: ours are the W3C Compositing and Blending Level 1 non-separable modes (Lum = 0.3 R + 0.59 G + 0.11 B, SetLum with ClipColor, SetSat). That is our basis, not a match to After Effects. No text or code was copied. **Gaps.** Silhouette Alpha and Silhouette Luma are not built and are refused (FX-TURBNOISE-073, 074): the program has no Timeline rule for them to follow, and we did not guess one. Hue stays refused as FX-TURBNOISE-060 pins it, and Overlay as FX-TURBNOISE-032 pins it; adding either is the owner's fixture decision. Turbulent Noise's colour is a grey, so Saturation and Color draw the same picture (the layer's lightness in the noise's grey). **Timing.** Three layers after a moving Noise, card / processor, ms a frame, again (PROVISIONAL, the machine was busy, `verification/B-600_turbulent_blends_timing_table.md`): Noise alone 45.2 / 107.3, Turbulent Noise as added 50.1 / 221.3, Luminosity 57.0 / 103.2, None at opacity 60 69.0 / 204.0, Stencil Luma 53.8 / 198.4; a busy machine cannot rank the modes. **Evidence.** Fixtures first (625bce69, `tools/turbulent_blends_reference.py`, FX-TURBNOISE-061 to 074); code 3a08badf; `tests/b600_turbulent_blends.rs`, `verification/D-730_turbulent_blends_table.md` 309 of 309 checks, card comparisons 38 of 38 within 1 level; pictures in `verification/D-730 pictures/`; timing `verification/B-600_turbulent_blends_timing_table.md`; playtest `verification/B-600_playtest.md`, awaiting the owner.

D-731 / Turbulent Noise, Overlay and Hue, after After Effects' Turbulent Noise (Noise & Grain) (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, row 224) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-13 as the owner's specification decision, asked directly by the coordinator and answered in session (not a /loop acceptance): FX-TURBNOISE-032 (Overlay) and FX-TURBNOISE-060 (Hue) may be regenerated so that both modes can be built. They were regenerated in their own commit (b4261ea0); no other expected value changed; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-601.** **What was built.** `core.turbulent_noise`'s Blending Mode adds `overlay` and `hue`, on the processor (`grade::fractal_noise`) and the card (Overlay is grade blend code 4, Hue is 16); the app's list gains both. **Sources.** Overlay is the Timeline's own Overlay formula (D-301, `grade::mixer`: 2 b g where the layer b is up to one half, else 1 - 2 (1 - b)(1 - g)); it is taken on the straight linear colour, as every other mode of this effect is, while the Timeline takes it on the encoded colour, so the two differ in the midtones. Hue is the W3C Compositing and Blending Level 1 Hue, SetLum(SetSat(noise, Sat(layer)), Lum(layer)), the basis D-730 chose for Saturation, Color and Luminosity: ours, not a match to After Effects, whose rule is unpublished. No text or code was copied. **Gaps.** The noise is a grey, so Hue draws the same picture as Saturation and Color. Silhouette Alpha and Silhouette Luma stay refused (D-730). D-445's table now reads 263 of 263 (was 265), D-647's 305 of 305 (was 309) and D-730's 309 of 309 (was 314): only the rows that expected 032 and 060 to be refused left them; every other row is unchanged. **Timing.** Three layers after a moving Noise, card / processor, ms a frame, again (PROVISIONAL, the machine was busy, `verification/B-601_turbulent_overlay_hue_timing_table.md`): Noise alone 43.3 / 115.0, Turbulent Noise as added 55.0 / 220.9, Overlay 53.4 / 111.4, Hue 48.0 / 157.6; a busy machine cannot rank the modes. **Evidence.** Fixtures first (b4261ea0, `tools/turbulent_noise_reference.py`, `tools/turbulent_more_reference.py`); code 740217e3; `tests/b601_turbulent_overlay_hue.rs`, `verification/D-731_turbulent_overlay_hue_table.md` 48 of 48 checks, card comparisons 26 of 26 within 1 level; pictures in `verification/D-731 pictures/`; timing `verification/B-601_turbulent_overlay_hue_timing_table.md`; playtest `verification/B-601_playtest.md`, awaiting the owner.

D-732 / Increment and Save (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+S), after After Effects' File > Increment and Save / **BUILT on 2026-10-14 from the 2026-10-14 audit's ideas list, which the owner approved; built B-602; the playtest awaits the owner.** **What was built.** File > Increment and save, the command palette line of that name and Ctrl+Alt+Shift+S save the open project under its own name with the next version number and the window carries on with the new file: `shot_v002.json` becomes `shot_v003.json`, a name with no `_v` number gains `_v002` (`shot.json` becomes `shot_v002.json`), and a number a file in the folder already has is skipped, so an older version is never written over. It is Save As to a name the window picks (the route `save-increment`, `increment_and_save` in `app/src/main.rs`), so what Save As promises holds: media paths rewritten for the folder, unknown data kept, the file it came from left exactly as it was, the new file on the recent list. A project with no file yet asks where to save, as Save does. Document 24 gains `project.save_increment` with Ctrl+Alt+Shift+S; no other shortcut changed. **Checks:** `verification/D-732_increment_save_table.md` 14 of 14 (the names, the skip of taken numbers, a project saved twice from `scene.json` to `scene_v002.json` and `scene_v003.json` with the first file unchanged); the command map, page, routes and keyboard tables (B-12b, B-12c) pass with the new rows. **Gaps:** none known. D-734 / Replace layer source (Ctrl+Alt+/), after After Effects / **BUILT on 2026-10-14 from the 2026-10-14 audit's ideas list, which the owner approved; built B-604; the playtest awaits the owner.** **What was built.** With a layer selected and a picture, sequence or sound picked in the Project panel, Ctrl+Alt+/ (Layer > Replace layer source, or the command palette line) makes the layer show the picked item. It is the new core command `SetLayerSource` (`SET_LAYER_SOURCE`), sent as `layer.replace_source?layer=&asset=`: only the layer's source changes, and its name, keys, effects, masks, transform, timing, exposures and every switch stay; it is one entry to undo, named "Replace the layer's source with <item>". A drawing layer takes a still or a sequence and a sound layer a sound file; a missing item, the item already shown, a kind that does not fit, a layer that shows no imported item (solid, shape, text, null, adjustment, composition) and a locked layer are refused with a sentence and change nothing. Relinking (`persist::relink_candidate`) is unchanged: it repairs a missing file, this swaps one item for another. **Keys.** Ctrl+Alt+/ is After Effects' own and was free; document 24 gains `layer.replace_source` with it. **Checks:** `verification/D-734_replace_source_table.md` 12 of 12 (the page's key arm and request pinned; the swap, the whole layer compared before and after apart from its source, one undo entry, undo restoring it exactly, and each refusal's sentence); B-12b command map table passes with the new row. **Gaps:** a composition layer's composition is not swapped by this; a drawing number the Sheet uses that the new sequence lacks is not refused and shows as a missing drawing, as it would anywhere else. It lists every command finder line in twelve areas (Project, Edit, New layers, Layers, Time, Keys, Properties, Timeline, Viewer, Tools, Finding, Sheet) with its keys; it searches by words, or by pressing a key (A key). If Split layers at the playhead takes it, Duplicate layers (Layers) will have no shortcut until you give it one.") with Replace, Cancel and Reset to its default; a key the window does not change (the arrows, A S R T M, the Alt+Shift keys that set a key, Alt+Left/Right, the Sheet's keys) is refused with a sentence. D-736 / Mask shortcuts F, MM and TT, and the pen's path drawn open until it is closed, as After Effects has them / **BUILT on 2026-10-15 at the owner's request ("include mask shortcuts like AE like feather for F, m for mask; and have it so that the mask shape/outline doesn't connect end to end, until I actually click the end point like in AE"); the playtest awaits the owner.** **What was built.** With layers selected on the timeline, F shows each mask with its Mask feather, M pressed twice within half a second shows each mask with all its settings (feather, opacity, expansion), and T pressed twice shows each mask with its Mask opacity; M once still shows only the masks and T once the layer's opacity. Shift with any of them adds to or takes away from what is shown, keeping the mask's own row. The command finder and the Keyboard shortcuts window list the three as Show mask feather (F), Show every mask setting (MM) and Show mask opacity (TT); F can be changed there, MM and TT cannot. While the pen draws a mask or a shape, the path is drawn open: the last point is no longer joined back to the first. Once there are three points the first point turns yellow, and clicking it closes the path. Enter still closes a mask from the keyboard and leaves a shape open; Escape still abandons it. No command, file format or picture changed. **Checks:** B-12c keyboard table (F is now a key the window answers), D-735 table (129 command finder lines, 91 with keys), 104 app tests; driven in a private copy of the app with pictures. **Gaps:** a mask is still always closed once made (D-77); open masks, AE's shape-layer tools and animation presets are proposed separately.

D-737 / Open masks, as After Effects allows them (reopens D-77) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-21 as recommended ("proceed with the next recommended builds on the roadmap"); built as B-611.** **As accepted.** A mask may be open: it has no piece from its last point back to its first, needs two points where a closed mask needs three, and may cross itself. An open mask encloses nothing, so its mode is None and it cuts nothing; Path Stroke, Vegas, Energy Stroke, Audio Spectrum and Audio Waveform take it open, as they take an open shape. The pen leaves a mask open with Enter, as it leaves a shape open, and closes it by a click on its first point; Effect Controls gives each mask a Closed switch, and closing or opening one is one step to undo. A file writes `"closed": false` only for an open mask (document 19). **Differences from the proposal, for the owner to see.** An older build is not shown a message about the switch: it keeps the field and writes it back, as document 28 keeps any field it does not know, and because an open mask's mode is written as None it cuts nothing there either; it draws a Path Stroke along it closed, and says a two-point mask cannot be drawn. The effects that fill a mask's area (Fill, the two Keys, Reshape, Liquify, Mask Smear, Scribble and the particle wall) take an open mask closed, as they took a two-point mask before. Opening a mask sets its mode to None and closing it sets None back to Add; a mode other than None is refused on an open mask. Fixtures FX-MSKO in document 25. **As proposed.** D-77 made every mask closed. After Effects lets a mask stay open: it then cuts nothing out of the layer and is used as a path for effects (Stroke, Audio Spectrum, Vegas, Trim) and for Text on a path. **Proposal.** A mask gains a Closed switch, saved only when it is off, so every saved project reads as before. The pen leaves a mask open with Enter, as it already leaves a shape open; an open mask is drawn as a line, cuts nothing, and is listed by effects that take a path. Fixtures first: an open mask leaves every pixel of its layer as it was; closing and opening it is one step to undo; a file with the switch off reloads with it off; an older reader is told of the switch per document 28. **Recommendation:** after D-738 (a), because the effects that would use an open mask already take shape paths.

D-738 / Shape layers as After Effects draws them / **Step (a) ACCEPTED on 2026-10-21 as recommended ("rebuild and go with your recommendation, start D-738a"); built as B-609. Step (b) ACCEPTED on 2026-10-21 ("proceed with the next recommended builds on the roadmap"); built as B-610. Step (c) ACCEPTED on 2026-10-21 under the same words; built as B-612. Step (d) ACCEPTED on 2026-10-21 under the same words: Round Corners, Pucker & Bloat, Twist, Zig Zag, Wiggle Paths and Offset Paths built as B-613; Merge Paths built as B-614.** **(d) as accepted.** A shape group may carry up to eight path operations, applied in order to every path drawn in the group, its inner groups' paths included, in the group's own space before its repeater and transform place them, as After Effects applies the operations at the foot of a group's contents: Round Corners (radius), Pucker & Bloat (amount), Twist (angle, center), Zig Zag (size, ridges per segment, corner or smooth points), Wiggle Paths (size, detail, wiggles per second, correlation, random seed) and Offset Paths (amount, miter, round or bevel join, miter limit), each number keyed as any number is (document 19). Effect Controls lists a group's operations under its transform, with an Add operation list and a Remove button for each. Trim applies after the operations; effects that take a shape layer's paths, and the viewer's handles, take each shape without them. Merge Paths (mode: add, merge, subtract, intersect or exclude intersections; a new one adds, as After Effects' does) makes every path drawn in the group so far, its inner groups' paths and repeated copies included, one shape of several outlines, drawn where the first of them was and painted as the first is; the operations after it change each of its outlines. **Differences from After Effects, for the owner to see.** Merge Paths' boolean modes work on each shape's outline flattened to corners, so a merged curve has no handles, only many short sides, and an open path is closed by a straight line; each shape's area and the merged shape's fill take the even-odd rule, as every shape here does, where After Effects fills by the non-zero rule, so where one path crosses itself or the merge mode keeps overlapping outlines the overlap is left unfilled. The merged shape takes the paint of the first path drawn (After Effects' bottom one). A merge over more than 20000 sides in all leaves the paths as they are. An operation belongs to a group and changes the whole group: to change part of a group, group that part. Offset Paths works on the outline flattened to corners, so its result has no curves, only many short sides; where an inward offset folds a path over itself the fold is filled by the even-odd rule. Wiggle Paths' points move smoothly at random from a seed, not as After Effects' own random numbers move them, and its smooth-or-corner points and its temporal and spatial phase are left out. Zig Zag's ridges split every segment, as After Effects' Ridges per segment does. Fixtures FX-SHPO and FX-SHPM in document 25. **(c) as accepted.** A shape group may carry a repeater, as After Effects' Repeater at the foot of a group's contents: copies (0 to 1000), offset (-1000 to 1000), composite below or above, and a transform per copy of anchor, position, scale and rotation with a start and an end opacity, each number keyed as any number is. Everything in the group, the groups inside it included, is drawn again for each copy, each copy turned about the anchor, scaled about it and moved from where the one before it was, so rotation and position together lay copies along an arc; the opacity runs from the start's on the first copy to the end's on the last (**D-778 changed** this on 2026-10-24: the last copy stops one step short of the end, i / copies, as After Effects' does). A fraction of an offset slides the copies part of a step; a fraction of a copy draws the last one at that fraction of its opacity. Below draws each copy under the one before, so the first is on top; above, over it. Effects that take a shape layer's paths take each shape once, not its copies, and the viewer's handles show the first copy where an offset of 0 puts it. **Differences from After Effects, for the owner to see.** A repeater belongs to a group and repeats the whole group: to repeat part of a group, group that part. A fraction of a copy fading the last copy is this build's reading. Fixtures FX-SHPR in document 25. **(b) as accepted.** A shape layer may hold groups, each with a name and a transform of anchor, position, scale, rotation, opacity, skew and skew axis, each keyed as any number is; a group may sit in another group; a shape may be in one group. A group's transform places its shapes as After Effects places a group's contents, and a group in a group is placed by both (document 19). Effect Controls shows each group's transform and stopwatches beside the shapes in it; Group puts the chosen shapes in a new group, Ungroup takes a group's shapes out of it. **Differences from the proposal, for the owner to see.** A stroke under a scale that is not even is drawn the same width all round, scaled by the size of the scale, where After Effects stretches it. Ungroup drops the group's transform, so its shapes move back to where their paths are; After Effects does the same. The timeline lists a group's keyed numbers by name ("Body position") among the layer's other keyed rows, not as a folded Contents tree; the tree is left for the redesign's timeline. Fixtures FX-SHPG in document 25. **(a) as accepted.** A shape may be a parametric rectangle, ellipse, polygon or star whose settings are keyed as any number is; its outline is worked from them at each frame as After Effects draws it, and the file keeps its outline too so that an older build still draws it (document 19). Q cycles rectangle, rounded rectangle, ellipse, polygon and star; a drag draws one on the chosen shape layer, or as a mask on any other chosen layer, and with no layer chosen makes a new shape layer for it, as After Effects does. **Differences from the proposal, for the owner to see.** A new rounded rectangle starts with a roundness of 16 pixels, a polygon and a star with 5 points and a star's inner radius half its outer one. Its points cannot be pulled one by one: Convert to Bezier Path in the shape's settings makes it a plain path at its settings' bases, its setting keys dropped, as After Effects' command does. After Effects' path direction switch is left out. Fixtures FX-SHPP in document 25. **As proposed on 2026-10-15** from the owner's request of 2026-10-15 ("expand in the shape tool/shape layer functionality like in AE. keyframing and animating along with presets just like in AE"). Today a shape layer holds paths with fill, stroke, gradient and trim, all keyable (D-75, B-25); Q draws a rectangle or ellipse as plain points. **Proposal, in four steps, each with its fixtures committed before its code:** (a) Parametric Rectangle (size, position, roundness), Ellipse (size, position) and Polystar (star or polygon; points, rotation, inner and outer radius and roundness), each keyable; Q cycles rectangle, rounded rectangle, ellipse, polygon, star; drawing with a shape tool with nothing selected makes a new shape layer, as After Effects does. (b) Groups, each with its own transform (anchor, position, scale, rotation, opacity, skew), nesting, and the timeline's Contents showing them. (c) Repeater (copies, offset, transform per copy, start and end opacity). (d) Path operations: Merge Paths, Offset Paths, Round Corners, Zig Zag, Wiggle Paths, Pucker & Bloat, Twist. D-75 left repeaters and merge paths out; (c) and (d) reopen that. **Recommendation:** (a), then (b), then (c), then (d); (a) alone covers most anime title and effect work.

D-739 / Animation presets, as After Effects saves them / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-21 as recommended ("go with your recommendation, start D-739"); built as B-608.** **As accepted.** An animation preset is a preset of D-180's file marked `"kind": "animation"`, holding any of a layer's transform properties, masks, a shape's trim, and effects, each written as a project writes them (document 19, "Animation presets"). Applied at the playhead, every key moves by the playhead less the preset's earliest key; numbers are never scaled to the layer; a transform property marked `added` is added to the layer's own value, which is how Slide in and Spin in end where the layer already is. The layer's own keys at other frames stay. Applying one preset to one layer is one undo step. A trim needs a shape layer, and is refused whole on any other. Twelve starter animation presets come in `Fixtures/starter_presets/animation.fxpreset`, apart from D-181's six to ten. **Differences from the proposal, for the owner to see.** Wipe reveal keys a Linear Wipe rather than a mask, because a mask's path is in pixels and would not fit a layer of another size, where the wipe's completion does. Save as animation preset… offers the layer's moving parts as ticks (each keyed or expressed transform property, its masks, its shapes' trim, its effects), not a choice of single properties on the timeline. A shape's colours and widths are not in presets yet, only its trim; they come with D-738. Fixtures FX-ANP in document 25. **As proposed on 2026-10-15** from the owner's request of 2026-10-15 ("expand in the shape tool/shape layer functionality like in AE. keyframing and animating along with presets just like in AE"). Presets today carry effects and their settings and keys (D-166, D-180, D-181), with keys kept at the frames they were saved at. **Proposal.** Save as animation preset… takes the chosen properties of a layer (transform, masks, shape contents, effects) with their keys; applying one lays it on the selected layers starting at the playhead, keys kept relative to their first key; the Effects & Presets list shows them beside the effect presets. A starter set: Fade in, Fade out, Pop in (scale overshoot), Slide in from each side, Spin in, Wiggle shake, Typewriter (text), Write-on (trim paths), Wipe reveal (mask). Fixtures first: a preset applied at frame 10 puts its first key at frame 10; applied to a layer with a different size it keeps its numbers; an unknown property in a preset file is reported per document 28, never dropped silently. **Recommendation:** first of the three, because it needs no new drawing and makes D-738's shapes reusable.

D-740 / Every key travels with its layer when the layer is moved / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-22 by the owner ("go"), built as B-615.** The owner's decision of 2026-09-13 is that a layer's keys move with its bar, as in After Effects. `Command::ShiftLayer` moves the transform's keys, depth, Time Remap and every effect setting, and nothing else. A check over every project in `Fixtures/`, moving each keyed layer 10 frames later, found 22 kinds of key left where they were: a mask's path, feather and expansion; a shape's path, fill and stroke colour and opacity, stroke width, gradient start and end, parametric position and size, and trim; a shape group's position and rotation, its repeater's numbers and its operations' numbers; a sound layer's level and pan. So dragging a shape or sound layer along the timeline, or pressing [ or ] on it, plays its animation at the old frames, out of step with its own bar. `Command::TrimLayer` moves keys only on a stretched layer (D-216), and only raster and composition layers stretch, which hold none of those kinds but masks, which it already moves; so a trim, and a split, which uses it, leave nothing behind today. **Accepted:** one walk over every key a layer holds, used by both commands, so a key kind added later is moved by adding it in one place. `tools/layer_shift_reference.py` writes `Fixtures/layer_shift/`: 18 cases, each a keyed layer of a fixture project moved, every key of 26 kinds listed at its frame after the move; `host.json` keys depth, the anchor, scale, rotation and opacity, and a stroke's gradient, which no other fixture keys. A stretched layer trimmed stays covered by FX-FBLEND-064 to 067. Nothing saved changes form. Fixtures FX-LSHIFT in document 25.

D-741 / Chosen keys of a mask's, a shape's and a group's numbers moved, deleted and reversed together / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-22 under the owner's instruction to build what the architecture review recommends ("proceed to tackle what you recommend"), built as B-616.** The timeline sends a person's chosen keys, each named `layer|property|frame`, to three requests: `keyframe.move` (a drag, the arrow keys), `keyframe.add_remove` with keys named (Delete) and `keyframe.reverse` (Time-Reverse Keyframes). Each answers a layer's transform, the camera's, an effect setting's and, since B-24f, a mask's or shape's path, and nothing else: a chosen key of a mask's feather, opacity or expansion (D-298), a shape's trim, style, gradient point or parametric setting (B-108b to D-738 (a)), or a group's transform, repeater or operation number (D-738 (b) to (d)) is refused, "A key is layer|property|frame", or "has no" it, though the same key alone can be moved, eased and taken off. Two paths' keys moved together on one layer lose the first path's move, each built from the layer as it was. **Accepted:** the three requests answer every property name the single-key requests answer to. A layer's chosen masks, shapes and groups are edited in one copy and sent back as one command each, so keys of several paths and numbers on one layer move together. A moved key keeps its value and its ease; a reversed one follows D-314's rule; the last key of a number taken out leaves the number at the value the first chosen key of it held, as a path's does (B-24f); a key put onto one not chosen is refused and nothing moves. A value sent with such a key is not read, as with a path's: the graph draws no curve for them. `tools/key_requests_reference.py` writes `Fixtures/key_requests/`: 16 cases of trims, two keyed masks on one layer (`host.json`), group transforms, repeaters, operations and a parametric size, each listing every key the layer holds afterwards. Nothing saved changes form. Fixtures FX-KREQ in document 25.

D-742 / The boxes of a stretched layer show the value the picture is drawn from / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-22 under the owner's instruction to build what the architecture review recommends ("proceed to tackle what you recommend"), built as B-617.** A layer stretched to other than 100 percent (D-216) plays its keys at its key time, `in + (frame - in) * 100 / stretch`, and the picture of each frame is drawn from its transform, depth, effect settings and mask paths read there. The inspector's boxes read the same keys at the frame itself, so on a stretched layer they show a value from another moment of the animation: a layer stretched to 200 percent, starting at 4, shows at frame 14 the rotation it reaches at frame 24. A mask's feather, opacity and expansion and the Time Remap were already read at the key time (D-298, D-323). **Accepted:** every box reads its keys at the layer's key time, as the picture does: the five transform numbers and the depth through the expression reader at that time, each effect setting, and each mask's path. Shapes and their groups cannot be stretched (only raster and composition layers can), so their boxes do not change. Nothing saved changes form. `tools/stretched_values_reference.py` writes `Fixtures/stretched_values/`: one stretched composition layer with linear keys on its position, rotation, depth, one mask's path and feather and one Fractal Noise's Brightness and Offset, and what each box shows on six frames. Fixtures FX-SVAL in document 25.

D-743 / Fractal Noise shows its Rotation, Sub Settings and Overflow (audit of 2026-10-22, row 16) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-23 under the owner's words of that day: "Proceed, if an effect is more like a inspiration/modified version of a AE effect, only improve it. But it is to be a 1 to 1 match, then go for it. Proceed down all the waves." Fractal Noise is a 1 to 1 effect (D-128, D-299: modelled on After Effects' Fractal Noise). Built as B-622.** Since D-647 Fractal Noise's engine draws Overflow, Rotation, Perspective Offset and the Sub Settings (Sub Influence, Sub Scaling, Sub Rotation, Sub Offset, Center Subscale), because Turbulent Noise is drawn by it (D-445), but Fractal Noise's file never held them: loading and saving always put them back at their start, so a person could not reach them. Wave 1's evidence (lane A, Fractal Noise, seven tutorials): four tutorials show these controls in After Effects' panel, and Cinecom's tutorial moves the Sub Settings (Sub Influence 77.5 with Sub Scaling 49.0, then 77.5 with 59.7) and After Effects' picture changes with them. **Accepted:** the panel shows Rotation (a dial), Perspective Offset, Sub Influence (0 to 100), Sub Scaling (10 to 100), Sub Rotation (a dial), Sub Offset (x and y), Center Subscale and Overflow (Allow HDR Results, Clip, Soft Clamp, Wrap Back), each keyable and typed like any other setting, and the file holds them. **What changes in a saved project:** a Fractal Noise saved from now on writes a setting only when it is moved, keyed or already in the file (D-304); one added from now on writes `"sub_influence": 70, "sub_scaling": 56`. A file without them, every project before D-743, reads Allow HDR Results, Rotation 0, Perspective Offset off, Sub Influence 50, Sub Scaling 50, Sub Rotation 0, Sub Offset (0, 0) and Center Subscale off, exactly what it always drew, and saves back without them. **After Effects' values and ours:** a Fractal Noise added from now on starts at After Effects' own Sub Influence 70 and Sub Scaling 56 (read in Wave 1 from the tutorials' panels at the effect's start). Rotation 0, Sub Rotation 0, Sub Offset (0, 0), Center Subscale off, Perspective Offset off and Overflow Allow HDR Results are After Effects' starts and ours alike (one older source shows Clip as the start; we keep Allow HDR Results, the start since D-647). The 50 and 50 a file without the settings reads are ours, kept so older projects draw as before; they are not After Effects'. How each sub layer is scaled, turned and added is the engine's of D-647, ours. **Fixtures:** none added or changed. Turbulent Noise's reference, `tools/turbulent_more_reference.py` (FX-TURBNOISE-033 to 058), already holds the pixels for these settings on the shared engine; B-622's test draws each case as a Fractal Noise and holds it to the same 2e-5, and FX-FRACTAL-001 to 038 rerun unchanged. **Gaps:** Uniform Scaling is not shown for Fractal Noise, which has Scale Width and Height instead and whose drawing does not use it. Audit row 16's other items stay open: fractional Complexity, and the None, Hue and Saturation blend choices for Fractal Noise; Wave 1 also found our basic noise cell about 1.5 times After Effects' (6 of 7 tutorials, short of the 7 a stored-check change needs) and our Terrain type unlike After Effects', both untouched here. **If refused:** the panel rows and the file keys go, and Fractal Noise draws at the fixed 50 and 50 as before; a project saved meanwhile with the settings keeps them in the file, which an older build keeps as unknown data (ADR-008).

D-748 / A layer takes eight more of After Effects' blend modes: Darken, Lighten, Hard Light, Difference, Hue, Saturation, Color and Luminosity / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-23** under the owner's words of that day: "Proceed, if an effect is more like a inspiration/modified version of a AE effect, only improve it. But it is to be a 1 to 1 match, then go for it. Proceed down all the waves." Audit row 18 (https://claude.ai/artifact/A63KdY44N4HfUHzUnLQhTp). A layer's blend modes are a 1:1 match to After Effects' Modes column, so the missing ones are added. Built as B-627. Reopens D-301, which left "After Effects' other modes (Color Dodge, Linear Light, Difference, Hue and the rest)" out until a tutorial needed one. **Evidence (Wave 1, lane D, task replay of 7 tutorials from 7 creators, `S/wave1/d/blend/SOURCES.md`):** Hard Light is picked on screen in 4 of the 7 (ActionVFX, Gareth David Studio, Adam Chraibi, AITEE; AITEE names it 5 times), Difference in 4 (School of Motion, Kenneth Moore, Adam Chraibi, AITEE; AITEE 9 times), Darken in 1 (Adam Chraibi), Lighten in 1 (Kenneth Moore), Hue, Saturation, Color and Luminosity in 1 (Adam Chraibi; Kenneth Moore shows a colour-group mode). The textbook formula on 8-bit encoded values against After Effects' own frame: Hard Light at 80 percent (Gareth David Studio, CC 2018) median 3.0 / 90th percentile 8.7 levels, Lighten (Kenneth Moore, 8 bpc) 4.0 / 12.0, Difference (Kenneth Moore) 6.0 / 18.0, all within the recipe's reading error, so After Effects works these modes on the encoded colours at 8 bpc, as D-301 found for Overlay. **The rule** (document 21): each mode is document 21's blend equation with `B` worked on the encoded colours held to 0 to 1 and decoded again, as D-301's Overlay. Per channel, with b beneath and s the layer: Hard Light `2bs` where `s <= 0.5`, else `1 - 2(1-b)(1-s)`; Darken `min(b, s)`; Lighten `max(b, s)`; Difference `|b - s|`. On the whole colour, the W3C Compositing and Blending Level 1 non-separable modes (Lum 0.3, 0.59, 0.11, ClipColor, SetLum, SetSat): Hue, Saturation, Color, Luminosity. Hard Light, Darken, Lighten and Difference are Adobe's published formulas; the four colour modes are our basis, since Adobe publishes none for them. The program already had all eight formulas, for Turbulent Noise (D-647, D-730, D-731), and the layer reuses them. Multiply, Screen and Add do not change: whether they too should mix on encoded colours is still only Likely (Wave 1) and waits for more evidence. **In a saved project:** a layer's `blend_mode` may now also be `darken`, `lighten`, `hard_light`, `difference`, `hue`, `saturation`, `color` or `luminosity`. Nothing else is written differently, so every older file opens and draws exactly as before. A file naming a mode the program does not know (After Effects' Color Dodge, say, or a mode from a newer build) is still refused with the reason, which now lists the sixteen modes in After Effects' order (document 28: no mode is drawn as another). An older build refuses a file that uses one of the eight new modes, with the same kind of reason. The Mode list in the timeline, the layer's right-click menu, the command bar and the `layer.set_blend_mode` command take all sixteen, in After Effects' order. The graphics card does not draw the eight; a frame with one is drawn on the CPU and says so (`GPU_PREVIEW_ON_CPU`), as for D-301's four, so the viewer and the export give the same picture. An adjustment layer takes them as it takes every mode (D-297). **Fixtures:** new, nothing old changes. `tools/layer_blend_modes_reference.py` writes `Fixtures/layer_blend_modes/`, FX-LBLEND-001 to 008, one per mode, a 10 by 8 frame of four backdrop strips under four strips in the mode (the last at 50 percent, two columns over nothing), every pixel, tolerance 2e-5; and FX-LBLEND-009, a layer in `color_dodge`, refused with the reason. No existing fixture value moves. `tests/b186_blend_modes.rs`'s check of the refusal reason now reads the sixteen modes. **Gaps:** After Effects' other modes (Dissolve, Dancing Dissolve, Color Burn, Classic Color Burn, Linear Burn, Darker Color, Classic Color Dodge, Color Dodge, Linear Dodge (After Effects' Add), Lighter Color, Linear Light, Vivid Light, Pin Light, Hard Mix, Exclusion, Subtract, Divide, Silhouette Alpha and Luma, Alpha Add, Luminescent Premul) are not added; their formulas are not in the program yet. In Float depth the eight are held to 0 to 1 like Overlay; After Effects at 32 bpc works them unheld on linear values. After Effects at 8 bpc rounds each step to 8 bits, which we do not. Only three Wave 1 cases show one of the eight with clean frames (Hard Light, Lighten, Difference); the colour modes rest on a transcript, so their formula is our basis, not a measured match. **If refused:** the eight are taken out of the list again; a file saved with one is then refused on opening, with the reason.

D-744 / Twirl turns as After Effects' does: a smoother falloff and a radius in per cent of the layer (audit row 10) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-23** under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-23: "Proceed, if an effect is more like a inspiration/modified version of a AE effect, only improve it. But it is to be a 1 to 1 match, then go for it. Proceed down all the waves." D-151 says Twirl is "modelled on After Effects' Twirl", so it is a 1:1 effect and is brought to After Effects as far as the tutorial evidence allows; built as B-623. **Why.** Row 10 of the effects audit of 2026-10-22 found two differences, and Wave 1 (lane B, 2026-10-23) confirmed both on six tutorials. (1) The falloff: each tutorial's untwirled frame was twirled again by a script under each candidate law and compared with After Effects' twirled frame (grey RMS, lower is closer). Smoothstep, the turn = Angle x s(1 - d/R) with s(t) = t^2 (3 - 2t), beats our t^2 in every fit: eskchat (Angle 1165, Radius 30) 11.8 against 92, Ervin (100, 30) 21.6 against 35.4, KuroCutt (70, 30) 6.65 against 18.4, Ilija Kostic (-55, 30) 2.84 against 10.0, Ag Motion Designs (69, 30) 24.6 against 42.9, Dope Motions (58, 30) 11.5 against 23.6 and (211, 25) 16.6 against 35.0; at 385 px on KuroCutt's Radius 100 the turn is 0.906 of the angle, smoothstep says 0.896 and t^2 0.64. (2) The radius: After Effects' Twirl Radius is a per cent of the layer's larger side, not pixels. In 1920-wide comps the best-fitting reach was 589 to 630 px at Radius 30 (predicted 576), 500 at 25 (480), about 2000 at 100 (1920). The direction (a positive angle turns clockwise on the screen) and the centre's start (the layer's middle) already match: every fit above uses our direction. **Accepted.** (a) The turn falls off as smoothstep: angle x t^2 (3 - 2t) with t = 1 - d / reach, on the CPU and the card alike; it is still the whole angle at the centre and none at the edge, but a pixel half way out turns by half the angle, not a quarter. (b) A new setting `twirl_radius`, named Twirl Radius, per cent of the drawing's own larger side, 0 to 100 (After Effects' range), starting at 30 (After Effects' start), keyable, held inside its range at each frame. (c) `radius`, pixels, stays, so a file from before D-744 keeps its reach: where `radius` is above 0 it is the reach, as before; only where it is 0 is the reach twirl_radius / 100 x max(drawing width, drawing height). A Twirl added from now on starts at angle 90, radius 0 and twirl radius 30. The larger side is the drawing's own, not a layer grown by an earlier effect (FX-TWIRL-025), so a draft, which halves the drawing, halves the reach without scaling the per cent. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing in its form for an old file: `radius` is read as before, and `twirl_radius` is written only when it is not 0, is keyed or was already in the file, so a file from before D-744 is saved again byte for byte. **How an old project looks afterwards:** the same reach in pixels, with the new falloff, so the swirl is stronger away from the centre: at half the reach a pixel turns by half the angle where it turned by a quarter, and at 83 per cent of the reach by 8 per cent where it turned by 3. The middle and the edge of the circle are where they were. Nothing is silently replaced: radius 0 with no twirl radius still changes nothing, as before. A twirl radius outside 0 to 100 in a command is refused with a sentence, and in a file, as a constant or at any key, keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID (D-46). **Fixtures.** `tools/twirl_reference.py` now works the smoothstep falloff and the reach rule. The project files of FX-TWIRL-001 to 021 are unchanged; the expected frames of 001, 002, 005 to 015 move, and their first values are retired: 113 pixels of 001 by at most 1.000 (a move of 1 is a pixel that now takes line where it took skin), 114 of 002, 144 of 006, 148 of 007 by at most 1.000, 50 of 005 by at most 0.452, 104 of 008 by at most 0.010, 22 of 009 by at most 0.864, the keyed 010 to 013 and the moved 014 as their plain cases, and 87 of 015 by at most 1.000; document 25 lists every case. 003, 004 and the invalid 016 to 021 do not move. New: FX-TWIRL-022 (the new start, twirl radius 30: a circle of 4.8 pixels), 023 (radius above 0 wins over twirl radius), 024 (twirl radius keyed), 025 (after a directional blur, the drawing's own larger side), and 026 and 027 (twirl radius 101 and -1, refused). **Gaps.** The tutorials never show a fresh Twirl, so the angle's start stays 90 (so the effect shows at once) and is not claimed to be After Effects'. Cosine bell fits almost as well as smoothstep in three of the fits (Ilija 2.98 against 2.84, KuroCutt 8.1 against 6.65, Dope 9.85 against 11.5); smoothstep wins the sum and is the simpler rule. The reach fits ran 2 to 9 per cent past the per-cent prediction (589 to 630 against 576), within the fits' own spread, so no correction is made. After Effects' own edge smoothing of the samples is not matched; we keep document 21's bilinear sample. **If refused:** the falloff stays t^2 and the radius stays pixels only; the fixtures go back to their first values and FX-TWIRL-022 to 027 are removed; a project saved with a twirl radius in the meantime keeps that key as written (the save merges the file's own settings), but the earlier build does not read it, so such a Twirl, at radius 0, changes nothing until its radius is set in pixels.

D-745 / Wave Warp gains After Effects' Circle and Pinning, and Width says what it means (audit row 9) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-23** under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-23: "Proceed, if an effect is more like a inspiration/modified version of a AE effect, only improve it. But it is to be a 1 to 1 match, then go for it. Proceed down all the waves." D-149 says Wave Warp is "modelled on After Effects' Wave Warp in spirit and not claimed to match it", so it is an inspired effect and is only improved: nothing it draws today changes. Built as B-624. **Why.** Row 9 of the effects audit of 2026-10-22 found that our Width is one whole wave while After Effects' Wave Width is half of one, and that two of After Effects' choices are missing. Wave 1 (lane B, 2026-10-23) measured After Effects' wave length on twelve stills from seven tutorials (FLOWTUTS, MotionXP, HOOP Studios, Creative Dojo, neon motions, Motion Academy, MS Motions): about twice Wave Width every time (1.94 to 2.03 where the scale was on screen), and our picture at twice the Width matched the four it was set beside. It saw Pinning in four tutorials (FLOWTUTS 1:36 All Edges, HOOP Studios Left Edge from 1:10, Creative Dojo 4:26 to 5:38, Motion Academy 5:30 All Edges) and Wave Type Circle in one (Motion Academy 2:00). On Motion Academy's All Edges the wave grows from nothing at the left edge to its whole height about a quarter of the layer's width in: read on its grid lines, 24, 44 and 64 per cent of the height in the first three half-wave windows, against 21, 42 and 62.5 for a straight ramp over a quarter of the width. **Accepted.** (a) Width keeps its meaning, one wave every Width pixels, so no project changes; its hint on the panel says so: "one wave spans Width pixels, about twice AE's Width for the same look". (b) `shape` takes a third word, "circle": each half wave is half a circle, w = sqrt(1 - (2u - 1)^2) with u the place in the half wave, on the side the sine is on, its crest where the sine's is, After Effects' rounded bites. (c) A new setting `pinning`, one of "none" (the start), "all_edges", "left_edge", "top_edge", "right_edge", "bottom_edge", "horizontal_edges" (top and bottom) or "vertical_edges" (left and right). A pinned edge scales the push to nothing at that edge of the drawing, rising in a straight line to the whole push a quarter of the drawing's width (left, right) or height (top, bottom) in; two pinned edges multiply. The drawing is the layer's own, not a layer grown by an earlier effect. The word is exact, as `edges`' is. **What changes in a saved project.** `pinning` is written only when it is not "none" or was already in the file, so a file from before D-745 is saved again byte for byte. **How an old project looks afterwards:** exactly as before; it has no pinning and reads as pinning none, and sine and triangle are unchanged. A pinning or shape word that is not a choice in a file keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID (D-46), and in a command is refused with a sentence. **Fixtures.** `tools/wave_warp_reference.py` works the circle and the pins; FX-WAVE-001 to 024, files and expected values, are unchanged, byte for byte. New: FX-WAVE-025 and 026 (circle, two directions), 027 to 033 (each pinning), 034 (pinning none written: 003 exactly), 035 (moved, all edges: the grown columns stay empty), 036 (circle, all edges, travelling), and 037 and 038 (pinning "center" and "All Edges", refused). **Gaps.** After Effects' other wave types (Square, Triangle's own shape, Sawtooth, Semicircle, Uncircle, Noise, Smooth Noise) are not added; our triangle is kept as it is. After Effects' Pinning "Center" is not added: it is shown once (MS Motions 2:55, its top edge left uneven), too little to say what it holds. No tutorial shows Horizontal Edges or Vertical Edges; we read them as the edges that run that way (top and bottom, left and right). The quarter ramp is read off one tutorial's grid; the other three show the same flat edges but give no numbers. After Effects' Antialiasing setting is not added. **If refused:** circle and pinning are removed and FX-WAVE-025 to 038 with them; a project saved with either keeps the word as written (the save merges the file's own settings), and the earlier build refuses an unknown shape with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID and ignores pinning.

D-746 / Glow's strength and fall-off in After Effects units, fitted to After Effects' own frames / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-23** under the owner's instruction of that day: "Proceed, if an effect is more like a inspiration/modified version of a AE effect, only improve it. But it is to be a 1 to 1 match, then go for it. Proceed down all the waves." Glow is a 1:1 effect (D-322, D-331, D-337). Audit row 12 (https://claude.ai/artifact/A63KdY44N4HfUHzUnLQhTp); built as B-625. **Evidence.** Wave 1 rebuilt eighteen Glow settings from seven After Effects tutorials (Valeri Visuals, Motion Nations, School of Motion's footage and square, Ducky, Robin, and SFP) and measured the light each adds, as band means of luma by distance from what glows. In 8 bpc and 32 bpc (After Effects) D-337's rule, the colour times GI x (t + 16 (1 - t)), seven times the intensity at the default threshold 60, lit the first 5 pixels 1.5 to 10 times brighter than After Effects (Valeri's white disc 113 levels where After Effects shows 76; Motion Nations's 190 where it shows 19) and reached far too far at a big radius. Three findings fix the rule: Valeri's disc at radius 400, intensity 2, Composite Original None, falls off as a Gaussian of sigma 161 pixels, 0.4 times the radius, at height exactly 1, so the light is held at 1 before it is spread; School of Motion's blue square (57, 67, 179) on grey turns (56, 70, 255) in its middle, so only the channel past the threshold glows; and Motion Nations's intensities 0.2, 0.6 and 1 rise less than in proportion, as the hold at 1 gives. **Rule (display values, After Effects units).** With t = threshold / 100, c = t + 16 (1 - t) and s = intensity x c / 3: based on bright, each of red, green and blue glows on its own when its 8-bit value is at least the threshold's share of 255; a glowing channel's light is min(1, s x its display value) at the pixel's covering; chosen colours and the tint keep the whole-pixel test and are held the same way; the spread is a Gaussian at sigma 0.4 x radius; the blurred light is laid on at strength 1 with Add or Screen, the covering as blurred. Intensity 0 still changes nothing: the dark ring After Effects draws there is not proven and is not added. **Fit and check.** The divisor 3 and the sigma 0.4 were fitted on Valeri 1 and 2 and Motion Nations 2 and 4, and checked on Motion Nations 1 and 3, Robin 1 and School of Motion's square, which took no part in the fit. Mean distance from After Effects over the bands brighter than 4 levels, as a factor: fitted cases 6.30 before, 1.11 after; checked cases 10.66 before, 1.23 after. The ten footage cases (SFP 1 to 5, School of Motion footage 1 to 3, Ducky 1 and 2) are 4.02 before and 4.65 after: at radius 10 After Effects' light reaches 15 to 100 pixels out on them, which no Gaussian at Valeri's measured reach can, so their stand-ins' scale is not what was recorded (a footage layer's own scale is not in the stills); their first 5 pixels improve (Ducky 1: 188 before, 72 after, After Effects 74). **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing in its form. A Glow in After Effects units in a composition at 8 bpc or 32 bpc (After Effects) draws dimmer near its edge and softer: at the defaults the light is held at 2.33 times the colour and 1 where D-337 multiplied it by 7, and it reaches a third further (sigma 0.4 x radius for 0.3). Classic units, Float and Display (the linear depths, and the card) are unchanged, as are Soft Physical Glow (D-353), Bloom, Glow Wipe and Halation, which do not use this rule. **Fixtures.** `tools/glow_display_reference.py` rewrote FX-GLDISP-001, 002, 003, 005 and 006 (old → new in document 25: 001 (6, 1) 0.0516353 0.0259644 0.0061506 0.0411864 → 0.0104154 0.00599268 0.00176362 0.0832082; 002 (6, 1) 0.00354139 0.00259961 0.00134748 1 → 0.00250415 0.00191615 0.0010096 1; 003 (15, 8) 1.04568 0.0426395 0 0.0699973 → 0.0707992 0.00412458 0 0.0707992; 005 (3, 4) 1 1 0.659293 1 → 0.962597 0.74472 0.187821 1; 006 (6, 1) 0.129412 x 4 → 0.109804 0.0287962 0 0.109804; 160, 154, 160, 160 and 160 pixels moved, by at most 3.858, 3.858, 3.724, 12.49 and 0.8286). 004, 007 and 008 are unchanged. A new check in the reference holds the per-channel test: FX-GLDISP-006's halo has red and no blue. **Gaps.** The linear depths keep D-331's rule: Wave 1 measured only 8 bpc and 32 bpc (After Effects) frames. The divisor 3 is fitted at threshold 60 only; Valeri's threshold-0 case is held at 1 and does not pin it, so the threshold's share of the strength is Creative COW's, not measured. P-26's tutorial 2 glow (32 bpc (After Effects), threshold 0, intensity 0.1) is about seven times dimmer than D-337 drew it, still brighter than Float's (B-216's picture check, 8 7 3 against Float's 5 4 1); its replay should be looked at again. School of Motion's square, a separate layer over grey: After Effects adds blue just outside it and barely darkens red and green (1, 6, 15 and 30 pixels out: red 103, 110, 122, 128 on a grey of 122); ours, where only blue glows, carries the square's covering with the blue light and darkens them more (89, 96, 107, 117), so its first 5 pixels read -19.6 levels of luma where After Effects reads -1.2. Before D-746 the white light hid this. A glow's covering over transparency, and 8 bpc layers compositing in linear light (D-333), are not changed here; Valeri's disc on a transparent layer reads 1.6 times After Effects for the same reason. Glow's other controls are D-747. **If refused.** Reverting B-625 and this entry's commit brings back D-337's rule and its values exactly.

D-747 / Glow's further After Effects controls: Composite Original, Glow Dimensions, Glow Colors A & B and the other Glow Operations / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-23** under the owner's instruction of that day: "Proceed, if an effect is more like a inspiration/modified version of a AE effect, only improve it. But it is to be a 1 to 1 match, then go for it. Proceed down all the waves." Glow is a 1:1 effect. Audit row 17 (https://claude.ai/artifact/A63KdY44N4HfUHzUnLQhTp); built as B-626. **What it adds.** Nine settings After Effects' Glow has and ours lacked, each saved under its own key and read as After Effects' starting value when a file does not have it: `composite` (Composite Original: "on_top", "behind" (start) or "none"), `dimensions` (Glow Dimensions: "both" (start), "horizontal" or "vertical"), `glow_colors` ("original" (start) or "a_and_b"), `color_looping` ("sawtooth_ab", "sawtooth_ba", "triangle_aba" (start) or "triangle_bab"), `color_loops` (1 to 127, start 1), `color_phase` (degrees, -3600 to 3600, start 0), `midpoint` (A & B Midpoint, 0 to 100, start 50), `color_a` (start #ffffff) and `color_b` (start #000000). The three numbers can be keyed. `operation` now takes, beside "add" and "screen", every mode with a blend formula already in this program: "normal", "multiply", "overlay", "soft_light", "hard_light", "darken", "lighten", "difference", "hue", "saturation", "color" and "luminosity" (D-647's and D-730's formulas). After Effects' other modes (the dodges and burns, linear and vivid light, exclusion and the rest) are still refused with a warning, so a file naming one is kept as written and the Glow left out, as before. **Rule (our basis; After Effects publishes no formula).** Dimensions: the light is spread along one axis only. A & B: after the spread, v is the light's brightest channel held to 0..1; u = frac(loops x (1 - v) + phase / 360); f is u (Sawtooth A>B), 1 - u (B>A), 1 - |2u - 1| (Triangle A>B>A) or |2u - 1| (B>A>B), bent to f^(ln 0.5 / ln m) with m the midpoint held to 0.001..0.999; the light becomes A + (B - A) f times v, at its covering, the colours as written in the display depths and through the sRGB curve in the linear ones, as the tint. Composite Original None: the light alone, the drawing left out (Intensity 0, or nothing that glows, leaves nothing). Add and Screen lay the light on as before whether On Top or Behind, which is why After Effects' start, Behind, draws every older file as it was. Every other operation is the W3C's (1 - as) ad cd + (1 - ad) as cs + as ad B(cd, cs) on straight colours: On Top, the light is the source and the drawing the backdrop; Behind, the other way round, so Normal Behind on an opaque drawing hides the light. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing: every file from before reads with the starting values and draws the same; the keys are written only when they differ from the start or the file had them. The card draws Add or Screen with both axes and the light's own colours, as before; anything else is drawn on the processor. **Fixtures.** `tools/glow_display_reference.py` adds FX-GLDISP-009 to 016 (None, Horizontal, A & B Sawtooth red to blue, Normal On Top, Normal Behind, Lighten On Top, Overlay Behind, and Vertical with Multiply On Top at 8 bpc), with checks in the script that None is the full Glow less the drawing, that Horizontal leaves an empty row empty, that A & B's brightest light is red and faintest blue, that Normal Behind on an opaque drawing changes nothing and that Lighten never darkens; 001 to 008 are unchanged. `tools/glow_reference.py` rewrote FX-GLOW-032's word "multiply" (now taken) → "color_dodge" (still refused), in its project and its description; its expected frames are unchanged. **Gaps.** None of the new settings was measured against After Effects' frames: Wave 1's tutorials use the starting values only, so the formulas above are our basis and are marked so. Color Looping's direction (which end of the light is A) is After Effects' documented reading, A at the brightest. **If refused.** Reverting B-626 and this entry's commit takes the settings away; files saved with them would then report an unknown setting ignored, as any newer file.

D-755 / Wave Warp gains After Effects' remaining wave types (audit row 9, D-745's gap) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-23** under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-23: "Proceed, if an effect is more like a inspiration/modified version of a AE effect, only improve it. But it is to be a 1 to 1 match, then go for it. Proceed down all the waves." D-149 makes Wave Warp an inspired effect, so it is only improved: sine, triangle and circle and everything they draw are unchanged. Built as B-634. **Why.** D-745 left After Effects' other Wave Types as a gap. Row 9 of the effects audit of 2026-10-22 and Wave 1 (lane B, 2026-10-23) found Motion Academy showing each type on the same layer and settings at the composition's frame 0 (Height 100, Width 100, Direction 90, its wave about 200 pixels long), which places each shape against the sine. Read as the layer's top edge less its bottom edge over the height and fitted at every whole degree of phase, the stills give: Sine, our sine at 0 degrees (correlation 0.990); Circle, our circle at 359 (0.990); Square, a square on the sine's halves at 359 (0.981; the sine itself only 0.901); Sawtooth, a sawtooth rising through each wave and dropping where the sine rises through nothing, at 359 (0.968; falling 0.486); Semicircle, one arch a wave pushing the other way from its points, the points where the sine rises through nothing, at 0 (0.977; the arch turned over 0.746). Lane G's outline fits of the same stills agree (square 0.991 and 0.995 on the top and bottom edges, sawtooth 0.991 and 0.983, semicircle 0.999 and 0.991). **Accepted.** `shape` takes six more words, each the place in the whole wave u = a / 2 pi - floor(a / 2 pi): "square", 1 for u under a half and -1 from a half on; "sawtooth", 2u - 1; "semicircle", 1 - 2 sqrt(1 - (2u - 1)^2); "uncircle", the semicircle turned over, 2 sqrt(1 - (2u - 1)^2) - 1; "noise" and "smooth_noise", ours in spirit: a fixed level from -1 to 1 at each knot, sixteen knots a wave joined by straight lines (noise) or two a wave joined smoothly (smooth noise), the levels from Scribble's 32-bit mix, so the same settings draw the same picture at every frame and on every machine, travelling with Phase and Speed as the other shapes do (document 20: no clock, no random state). The panel lists the nine in After Effects' order (Sine, Square, Triangle, Sawtooth, Circle, Semicircle, Uncircle, Noise, Smooth Noise). The word is exact. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing: `shape` is already stored as a word, not a number, so every existing file keeps its meaning and is saved again byte for byte; a file can now name the six new words. A file from before D-755 naming one of them was refused (EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID) and now draws it. **How an old project looks afterwards:** exactly as before. A shape word that is not a choice in a file keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID (D-46), and in a command is refused with a sentence. **Fixtures.** `tools/wave_warp_reference.py` works the new shapes; FX-WAVE-001 to 038's frames are unchanged, value for value. One old fixture's file changes: FX-WAVE-023 tested a refused shape with the word "square", which is now a choice, so its word becomes "hexagon" (`fx_wave_023.json` "square" -> "hexagon", its sentence likewise); it is still refused with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID and its expected frames, the drawing unchanged, are the same. New: FX-WAVE-039 to 042 (square, sawtooth, semicircle, uncircle at height 2, width 8), 043 and 044 (noise, smooth noise), 045 (noise travelling, frame 2 phase 90 exactly), 046 (semicircle, direction 0, all edges pinned) and 047 ("Smooth Noise", the panel's name, refused). **Gaps.** After Effects' Noise is random and changes from frame to frame with fine spikes a few pixels apart (Motion Academy 2:12); ours is fixed and smoother, in spirit only. No tutorial shows Smooth Noise or Uncircle; our uncircle is read as the semicircle turned over. Our triangle stays a quarter wave from After Effects' (its still fits ours at 270 degrees), kept as D-745 kept it. After Effects' Antialiasing is not added. **If refused:** the six words are removed and FX-WAVE-039 to 047 with them, and FX-WAVE-023 goes back to "square"; a project saved with one of them keeps the word as written, and the earlier build refuses it with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID.

D-756 / Fractal Noise's base cell matches After Effects' size: Scale 100 is a 66.7-pixel cell (audit of 2026-10-22, row 16, the Wave 1 "grain size" finding) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-23** under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-23: "Proceed, if an effect is more like a inspiration/modified version of a AE effect, only improve it. But it is to be a 1 to 1 match, then go for it. Proceed down all the waves." Fractal Noise is a 1:1 effect (D-128 and D-299: modelled on After Effects' Fractal Noise), so it is brought to After Effects' size in full; this reopens D-128's "size is how many pixels one cloud cell spans". Built as B-635. Audit page: https://claude.ai/artifact/A63KdY44N4HfUHzUnLQhTp, row 16. **Why.** Wave 1 (lane A, 2026-10-23) found our basic noise cell about 1.5 times too big, even at Complexity 1, on 6 of 7 tutorials, one short of the 7 a stored-check change needs, so the row stayed Likely. Wave 2 (lane E, 2026-10-23) measured four more creators on Block noise, where the cell is a hard lattice that can be read exactly (the period of the edge profile's autocorrelation, the same crop and script on both sides, reading error about 5 per cent): Akshay Morey (Complexity 2 and 6, both axes) After Effects 66 against ours 99; School of Motion (Contrast 168, Complexity 6) 68 against 99, and its Scale Width 391.1 261 against 392; Ben Marriott (Complexity 6) 66 against 99; Mason Rippel (Turbulent Smooth, Block, Complexity 6, 3840 by 2160) 66 against 98 to 100. Every ratio is 1.46 to 1.50. With wave 1's Manuel does Motion (60 against 90), Creative COW (9.5 blocks across against 6.3), Jake In Motion, Justin Odisho, Mike Murphy and CGStirk (soft noise, 1.55 to 1.8), 10 of 11 sources from 10 creators agree, 91 per cent; the eleventh, Cinecom, used Rotation, Sub Settings and Scale that ours could not then set. After Effects' lattice also peaks at 333 = 5 x 66.7, across 4 creators. Lane E checked the Sub Settings (D-743) explain part of the soft-noise gap but none of the block lattice's, which is 100 pixels in ours and 66.7 in After Effects at Scale 100 for every Complexity and both Fractal Types tried. **Accepted.** Fractal Noise's noise is worked at two thirds of its size: pixel (X, Y) samples the point ((X + 0.5) / c, (Y + 0.5) / c, z) with c = size / 1.5, so Scale 100 draws a 66.7-pixel cell, After Effects' own. Scale Width and Scale Height (D-299) scale c as they scaled the size, so a stretch keeps its proportion. Every other part of the rule is unchanged: the octaves, contrast, brightness, evolution, the Sub Settings, Rotation, Offset, Overflow and the blend. On the CPU and the card alike: the factor is applied at Fractal Noise's own entry, and nothing else draws through it. **Turbulent Noise is not changed.** It is drawn by the same engine as Fractal Noise (D-445, D-647), and its size keeps its meaning, the cell; its size is checked separately against After Effects (wave 3, lane J), and its fixtures do not move. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing in the file: `size`, `scale_width` and `scale_height` are read and written as before, so a file is saved back byte for byte. **How an old project looks afterwards:** every Fractal Noise draws its clouds or blocks at two thirds of the size it drew before D-756: cells 2/3 as wide and as tall, so about 2.25 times as many on the same layer; the levels, the contrast and the character are the same.
