A project that was matched to After Effects by eye at a raised size now draws finer than it did. There is no option to keep the old size: to get the old look back, multiply Size (or Scale) by 1.5, up to its limit of 1000. Nothing is silently replaced: a size outside its range is refused as before (EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, D-46). **Fixtures.** `tools/fractal_noise_reference.py` works c = size / 1.5 (`fractal_point`; the shared `point` that Turbulent Displace and Roughen Edges use is unchanged), and `tools/float_depth_reference.py` follows it. The project files are unchanged; the expected frames below move and their first values are retired, kept in the repository's history at commit 39ad6f68 (pixels moved of 160, largest move): FX-FRACTAL-001 frames 0 and 4, 135 by 0.018; 002, 135 by 0.518; 003, 135 by 0.810; 004, 135 by 0.506; 006, 129 by 1.000; 007, 135 by 0.733; 009 frames 0, 2 and 4, 135 by 0.518, 0.408 and 0.558; 010, 135 by 0.558; 011 frames 0, 2 and 4, 135 by 0.518, 0.558 and 0.462; 012 and 013, 135 by 0.338; 014 and 015, 135 by 0.518; 016, 131 by 0.346; 017, 131 by 0.218; 018, 135 by 0.259; 019 frames 2 and 4, 135 by 0.518; 020 frames 0 and 3, 108 by 0.441; 029, 135 by 0.503; 030, 16 by 0.628; 034, 20 by 1.000; FX-FNOISE-HDR-001, 135 by 4.02; 002, 120 by 1.000; 003, 133 by 3.43 (a move of 1 is a pixel now held at the other end of the ramp). Unchanged: 005 (contrast 0), 008 (brightness -100), 019's frame 0, the invalid 021 to 028, 031 to 033, 035 to 038, the Add and Screen float cases, and every Turbulent Noise, Turbulent Displace and Roughen Edges fixture. Document 25 prints the new values and the counts; document 21's point now reads c = size / 1.5. **Gaps.** Turbulent Noise's size is not changed here and is checked separately (wave 3, lane J). Lane E also found the Dynamic type differs (2 creators, Likely), and Strings, Turbulent Smooth's levels and Terrain differ on one source each (Unconfirmed); none of them is addressed by D-756, which is the base cell only. The factor is fitted on Block noise's lattice; the soft-noise measures agree with it but are looser (1.5 to 1.8). **If refused:** c goes back to the size, the reference tools and the four expected files go back to their values at 39ad6f68, and every project draws as before; a file saved in the meantime holds nothing new, so it reads back unchanged.

D-753 / Directional Blur's streak tapers at its ends, as After Effects' does (audit row 11) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-23** under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-23: "Proceed, if an effect is more like a inspiration/modified version of a AE effect, only improve it. But it is to be a 1 to 1 match, then go for it. Proceed down all the waves." D-92 says Directional Blur is "modelled on After Effects' Directional Blur", so it is a 1:1 effect and is brought to After Effects as far as the tutorial evidence allows; built as B-632. It reopens D-92's kernel (its shape) and D-98's flat average, and keeps D-98's lines and running sums. **Why.** Row 11 of the effects audit of 2026-10-22 (https://claude.ai/artifact/A63KdY44N4HfUHzUnLQhTp) said After Effects' streak fades at its ends where ours stops in a hard step. Wave 1 (lane C, 2026-10-23) fitted kernels to registered sharp and blurred frames from tutorials (robust mean absolute error, the worst 3 per cent of pixels dropped, the length free): a tapered kernel beat a flat box in every usable source, WTFx (0 and 118 degrees) 0.0068 against 0.0083 and 0.0073 against 0.0086, Justin 0.0325 against 0.0357, aace 0.0375 against 0.0408, emaeditzs 0.0119 against 0.0129, twibytez 0.0062 against 0.0070, and Jake's widths at 80, 50 and 20 per cent (72, 141, 234 against ours 144, 237, 258) say the same; Mutuals was too close to call (0.0042 against 0.0045). Wave 2 (lane F) added two full-resolution sources with the viewer's scale known, Если просто (45 degrees, Length 66.25) 0.0073 against 0.0140 and Хнар фильм (262 degrees, Length 81.4) 0.0041 against 0.0074, a tapered kernel's error about half the box's; in both, After Effects' visible streak is about Length long in all, with soft ends (1.08 to 1.33 and 0.86 to 1.05 x Length), where a flat box must be cut to 0.59 to 0.73 x Length to come close and still fits worse. Eight creators agree, which meets G23's T8 bar for reopening D-92 and D-98 (seven at 80 per cent); T6 (a hidden viewer resolution) is cleared by the four full-resolution sources agreeing. **Accepted.** Along each of D-98's lines, the columns j from the pixel's own are weighed by a tent `length` long in all, `h = max(|u_x|, |u_y|) x length / 2` columns each way: w_j = the integral of tri(t) x tent(j - t) dt, tri(t) = max(0, h - |t|) / h^2 and tent the line drawn straight between its column samples, as before. Worked out, w_0 = (h - 1/3) / h^2 (1 - h/3 below h = 1), and for j not 0, with x = h - |j| and c(v) = max(0, v)^3, w_j = (c(x + 1) - 2 c(x) + c(x - 1)) / (6 h^2), which is exactly (h - |j|) / h^2 from |j| = 1 to h - 1: the straight part is the running-sum pair Bloom's streaks already use (two stacked boxes of Length / 2 make the same tent), so the blur keeps D-98's speed on the processor and the card, and only a few columns at each end and the pixel's own are worked one by one. The weights sum to 1 and are heaviest at the pixel. Length 0 is the drawing untouched; the bounds still grow by ceil(length / 2), and `edges` (D-109) and the 8 bpc and 32 bpc display-value averaging (D-330, D-333) are unchanged. Bloom's streaks are not touched: they had their own tent already (D-98), and FX-BLOOM-001 to 028 do not move. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing in its form: no setting is added, renamed or written differently, so every file saves byte for byte as before. **How an old project looks afterwards:** the same Direction and Length streak the same distance, but each streak is heaviest at the drawing and fades to nothing at its two ends instead of stopping in a hard step, so it looks shorter and lighter than before (half its weight lies within 0.15 x Length of the pixel either way, where the flat average's half lay within 0.25 x Length); a layer that relied on the old hard-ended look needs a longer Length to look as strong. Nothing is silently replaced: a setting the build does not know is still refused or diagnosed as before. **Fixtures.** `tools/directional_blur_reference.py` works the tapered weights; its checks now say row 4 of the block is 23/24 covered at length 4 (it was 3.875/5), length 1 covers the block's edge column 11/12 and the one outside 1/12 (it was three quarters and a quarter), and length 2.5 reaches 1/600 two columns out (it was 1/15). The project files are unchanged; D-98's expected values are retired, kept in the repository's history at commit 438fe5d0, and moved by (pixels, largest change in a working value): FX-DIRBLUR-001 (and 008, and 011's frame 0) 67 by 0.183, 002 (and 003, 010's frame 2, 011's frame 4) 63 by 0.217, 004 98 by 0.290, 006 43 by 0.333, 007 57 by 0.287, 009 frames 0 and 3 80 by 0.263, 010 frame 4 73 by 0.299, 011 frame 2 75 by 0.258; 005 and 012 to 015 do not move. Cases of other effects with a directional blur ahead move with it, regenerated by their own tools, which import this one: FX-BLOCKLOAD-017 152 by 0.133, FX-BURN-014 56 by 0.158, FX-CCVIG-018 160 by 0.158, FX-EDGES-004 160 by 0.042, 005 160 by 0.055, 006 62 by 0.280, 009 160 by 0.143, FX-HALFTONE-016 75 by 1.000 (a dot's threshold crossed), FX-MOSAIC-013 152 by 0.073, FX-RADIAL-012 143 by 0.137, FX-RWIPE-021 21 by 0.133, FX-SPINZOOM-014 111 by 0.148, FX-TWIRL-015 72 by 0.133, 025 154 by 0.194, FX-VIGNETTE-018 160 by 0.158. Document 25 lists every case; document 21's rule is rewritten. **Gaps.** The tent is the simplest taper that fits; a Gaussian or Hann bell fits Если просто about as well (0.0073) and the tent ties the Gaussian on Хнар фильм (0.0041), so the exact bell After Effects uses is not claimed. The full span is Length; the fits put it between 0.86 and 1.33 x Length, so a small scale error either way is possible. Mutuals cannot tell box from taper. After Effects' bit depth was not shown in any source. **If refused:** the flat average comes back, the fixtures named above go back to their values at 438fe5d0, and no project needs changing, since no setting was added.

D-754 / Mosaic gains After Effects' Horizontal and Vertical Blocks and Sharp Colors (audit row 13) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-23** under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-23: "Proceed, if an effect is more like a inspiration/modified version of a AE effect, only improve it. But it is to be a 1 to 1 match, then go for it. Proceed down all the waves." D-144 says Mosaic is inspired by After Effects' Mosaic, not a 1:1 match, so it is only improved: what it does today stays, and what After Effects has that ours lacks is added beside it; built as B-633. **Why.** The effects audit of 2026-10-22 (https://claude.ai/artifact/A63KdY44N4HfUHzUnLQhTp) said After Effects' Mosaic is set by block counts, not a block size, and has a Sharp Colors switch ours lacks. Wave 3 (lane H, 2026-10-23, its verdicts in lane H's mosaic/VERDICT.md with sheets mosaic_jake.png and mosaic_vlad.png) looked at six tutorials by six creators (Jake, KuroCutt, Gabianco, Vlad, Chris Johnsson, Only One Minute): all six show separate Horizontal and Vertical Blocks counts that split the layer's box evenly (Jake's 10 by 10 on a 1920 by 1080 frame gives blocks 192 by 108, where ours, square, leaves a 120-pixel strip; Chris Johnsson's 45 by 45 on 16:9 makes blocks that are not square), After Effects starts at 10 by 10 with Sharp Colors off, and Sharp Colors is a switch beside them. G23: no trigger on the counts (6 of 6 agree), T6 on Vlad's layer size only; counts and Sharp Colors are confirmed candidates. **Accepted.** Mosaic gains four settings. `mode` is `size` (D-144's square blocks `size` pixels across, unchanged) or `count`. In `count`, `horizontal` and `vertical` (each 1 to 1000, a whole number, taken to the nearest with halves up, held inside its range at each frame, keyed like any number) split the drawing's own box, `W` by `H` pixels, evenly: the pixel `p` columns from the drawing's corner is in column of blocks `floor(p x horizontal / W)`, worked in whole numbers, so 10 across 16 columns gives blocks 2, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 2, 1, 2 and 1 wide and no strip is left over; pixels that an earlier effect grew beyond the box carry on in blocks the same width outward. `sharp_colors` is `off` (each block the mean of its pixels, as now) or `on` (every pixel of a block takes the block's middle pixel, the one at column `(first + last + 1) // 2` and the row likewise, a block cut short at the buffer's edge using its own middle), in either mode. The block colour is not changed: lane H also found After Effects averages the written (display) values where ours averages linear light, 60 to 80 levels lighter on Vlad's mixed blocks, but that changes how every existing Mosaic looks, so it is left for its own decision, not taken here. A draft scales `size` as before; the counts are not scaled, since they already follow the drawing's box. The card draws both modes with Mosaic's existing `blocks` pass, given the counted block edges, and its middle pixel when Sharp Colors is on. **What changes in a saved project.** A Mosaic saved before D-754 names none of the four, and reads as `mode` `size` with Sharp Colors `off`, which is exactly D-144's Mosaic, and saves byte for byte as it was: the new keys are written only when one differs from that reading or the file already named it. A new Mosaic added in the app starts in count mode at 10 by 10 with Sharp Colors off, as After Effects' does, its `size` 10 kept for when it is switched to size mode; this is a change to the default, so a Mosaic added after B-633 looks unlike one added before even with nothing touched. A value outside the contract (a `mode` or `sharp_colors` word not listed, a count outside 1 to 1000) leaves the effect out of the frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID and is kept as written, never silently replaced (document 28). **How an old project looks afterwards:** exactly as before. **Fixtures.** `tools/mosaic_reference.py` adds the counts and the middle pixel and checks them; FX-MOSAIC-001 to 020 are unchanged in project and value, and FX-MOSAIC-021 to 037 are new: counts split evenly (021 10 by 10, 022 4 by 2, 023 3 by 3, 024 1 by 1 = 007, 025 16 by 10 the drawing untouched), Sharp Colors in both modes (026, 027), counted blocks moved with the drawing (028), after a directional blur's growth (029), keyed counts (030), counts taken to the nearest whole number (031), a file naming `size` and `off` equal to one naming neither (032), and five values outside the contract (033 to 037). Document 25 lists every case; document 21's rule gains the counts and Sharp Colors. **Gaps.** The block colour (display against linear average) is not changed, as said. Whether After Effects' even split rounds a block edge down, as ours does, or to the nearest pixel is not visible at the sources' resolution, so a block edge may sit one pixel off After Effects'. Which pixel After Effects' Sharp Colors takes when a block is an even number of pixels wide is not visible either; ours takes the one right of and below the middle. **If refused:** the four settings go, FX-MOSAIC-021 to 037 go, and no saved project has used them, since the owner has not yet run a build with them.

D-759 / A Stroke added from now on starts at After Effects' Brush Hardness 79 with Stroke Sequentially on (audit of 2026-10-22, Path Stroke; wave 3, lane J) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-23** under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-23: "Proceed, if an effect is more like a inspiration/modified version of a AE effect, only improve it. But it is to be a 1 to 1 match, then go for it. Proceed down all the waves." Path Stroke is a 1:1 effect (D-356, D-357 and D-737: after After Effects' Stroke, "as added, After Effects' Stroke"), so its starting values are brought to After Effects'. Built as B-638. Audit page: https://claude.ai/artifact/A63KdY44N4HfUHzUnLQhTp. **Why.** Wave 3's lane J (2026-10-23) read After Effects' Effect Controls panel just after a Stroke is added in five tutorials by five creators: SA1NT (After Effects 2024, 2:00, https://youtu.be/xl5w5jZIiyk), Skyona (2:15, https://youtu.be/jVo3PNI5EKk), Maxwell (After Effects 2023, 0:56, https://youtu.be/0nhhwf6cnuw), Vanessa (CC 2019, 3:47, https://youtu.be/6VSB5SWMfy4) and Axel (2023/24, 4:50, https://youtu.be/vrOLufysQQY). All five show Brush Hardness 79% and Stroke Sequentially ticked; ours started at 75 and off. Every other start (Path 1, All Masks off, white, Brush Size 2, Opacity 100%, Start 0%, End 100%, Spacing 15%, Paint Style On Original Image) already matched. 5 of 5 agree across CC 2019 to 2024; it is a starting value read from the panel, not a measure of the picture. **Accepted.** A Stroke added in the window (the Effects panel, the search, or the `effect.add` command, which all go through the one as-added list) starts at Brush Hardness 79 and Stroke Sequentially on. Stroke Sequentially only acts with All Masks on (D-356), so a Stroke as added draws on one mask exactly as before except for the slightly harder brush edge (79 against 75). Nothing else about the rule changes. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing in the file's shape: Stroke's file has always held `brush_hardness` and `stroke_sequentially` (both required since D-356; a file without one is refused, EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, as before), so a Stroke added from now on writes `"brush_hardness": 79, "stroke_sequentially": "on"` where it wrote 75 and `"off"`. **How an old project looks afterwards:** exactly as before. Every Stroke saved before D-759 holds its own 75 and off (or whatever was set), reads them, draws them and saves them back byte for byte; no fallback is involved, so `persist.rs` is not changed. **Fixtures:** none added or changed. FX-STROKE-001 to 069 are written by `tools/stroke_reference.py` and `tools/stroke_text_reference.py` with their settings stated in each file, not by the as-added list, so none moves. The as-added values are not a picture a reference script can work out; B-638's app test holds them instead, and loads FX-STROKE-001's file (75 and off) to check that it opens and saves unchanged. **Gaps.** (1) Width: After Effects' line is about 2 times Brush Size across (3 of 3 sources that show it, median 1.9 to 1.94, Vanessa, Mike Murphy, Jake in Motion), where ours is 1 times (D-356's "size pixels across"); Likely, short of the 7 agreeing sources a stored-check change needs (T8 unmet), not changed here. (2) How Hardness looks: no source let the edge be measured; not changed. (3) Start and End: keyed in two tutorials but not measured; not changed. (4) The audit page's row number for Stroke is not recorded here. **If refused:** the as-added list goes back to 75 and off; a Stroke added in the meantime keeps 79 and on in its file, which reads and draws as set, and the owner can type 75 and off back in the panel.

D-757 / Turbulent Displace gains After Effects' Offset and its other Displacement types (Cross, Bulge, Twist and the three Smoothers) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-23** under the owner's instruction of that day: "Proceed, if an effect is more like a inspiration/modified version of a AE effect, only improve it. But it is to be a 1 to 1 match, then go for it. Proceed down all the waves." D-127 says Turbulent Displace is "modelled on After Effects' Turbulent Displace in spirit and not claimed to match it", so it is an inspired effect and is only improved: every existing setting keeps its meaning and nothing it draws today changes. Audit of 2026-10-22 (https://claude.ai/artifact/A63KdY44N4HfUHzUnLQhTp), Thin areas, the Turbulent Displace row: "No Bulge, Twist, Smoother or Cross types; no Offset", seen in the video check. Built as B-636. **Evidence.** Wave 2 (lane E, 2026-10-23) read After Effects' panel in nine tutorials by seven creators: Offset (Turbulence) is in every one, and Manuel's tutorial (youtube.com/watch?v=501MUGcxYRk) opens the Displacement menu at 2:01 (Turbulent, Bulge, Twist, Turbulent Smoother, Bulge Smoother, Twist Smoother, Vertical, Horizontal and Cross Displacement) and draws Bulge (1:58), Cross (2:28 to 2:34, Size 50 and 5), Vertical (2:04), Horizontal (2:25) and an Offset moved 159 pixels right (0:50) on one gradient. Measured on those stills (`aniso.py`, the half-length of the high-passed picture's autocorrelation along x and along y, in comp pixels): Cross Size 50 is 18 across by 183 down (10.2 times longer one way), Cross Size 5 is 6 by 15, Bulge 24 by 21 (round), Turbulent at Complexity 1 45 by 42. **Accepted.** (a) A new setting `offset`, two numbers in pixels (x, then y), -100000 to 100000 each, keyable, absent [0, 0]: the turbulence slid by that much in the drawing's own space, as Fractal Noise's Offset slides its clouds; it adds to the drift (D-411), and a draft scales it as a distance. (b) `displacement` takes six more words: "cross", "bulge", "twist", "turbulent_smoother", "bulge_smoother" and "twist_smoother". The rule is this program's own (`tools/turbulent_types_reference.py`, document 21): Cross pushes sideways from a field stretched eight times across and up and down from one stretched eight times down, so straight streaks cross; Bulge pushes each pixel by the field's slope (read a quarter of a cell either side, each held to -1..1), so it reads from uphill and the hills swell like lenses; Twist is Bulge's push turned a quarter, so the pixels swirl round the hills; the Smoother words give each finer octave a quarter of the last's strength where the others give a half. Every push stays within the Amount, so the layer grows by the same ceil(Amount) as before, and Pinning (D-306) fades every word alike. The words are exact, as before. **What changes in a saved project.** `offset` is written only when it is not [0, 0], is keyed or was in the file already, so a file from before D-757 is saved again byte for byte. **How an old project looks afterwards:** exactly as before. It has no offset and reads it as [0, 0], and Turbulent, Horizontal and Vertical are unchanged. A word that is not a choice, or an offset outside the range at any frame, keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID (D-46), and in a command is refused with a sentence. On the card, an offset rides with the drift; the six new words are drawn on the processor, as D-306's Horizontal, Vertical and Pinning are: the effect is left off the card's plan and drawn by the processor, with no warning, since nothing is lost (B-636's table checks those frames against the processor's). **Fixtures.** No existing fixture changes: FX-TURB-001 to 026, FX-TURB-AE-001 to 012, FX-BOIL and FX-SHIMMER keep their files and values byte for byte. New, in `Fixtures/turbulent_types/`, worked by `tools/turbulent_types_reference.py`: FX-TURB-TY-001 to 003 (Offset, written at [0, 0] equal to FX-TURB-AE-007, keyed), 004 to 009 (each new word), 010 (Turbulent Smoother at Complexity 1 equal to Turbulent), 011 (Bulge with edges repeat), 012 (Cross moved), 013 (Twist with Offset, seed and speed, two frames), 014 (Bulge in classic units), and 015 to 018 refused ("Bulge", "cross_displacement", Offset 100001, Offset keyed to -200000). **Gaps (owner options, not built).** The texture scale is kept: Wave 2 found ours about twice as fine as After Effects' at the same Size (seven of seven creators, median ratio 0.5), but matching it would change every saved Turbulent Displace and its fixtures, which an inspired effect does not do; it is offered as its own decision. Our Horizontal and Vertical keep their round field, where After Effects' Vertical streaks run 16.8 times longer down than across (Manuel 2:04, 15 by 252 pixels) and Horizontal's run across; changing them would change saved projects, so it is offered too. After Effects' Offset is a point that starts at the layer's middle (Manuel's 960, 540 on a 1920 by 1080 layer); ours is the slide from there, starting at [0, 0], so a value read off After Effects' panel is entered less the layer's middle. Resize Layer is not added: our layer always grows by ceil(Amount) when the edges are transparent, which is After Effects' Resize Layer on, and edges repeat keeps the size, near enough its off. Antialiasing for Best Quality is not added (ours always reads bilinearly), nor Complexity above 8 or between whole numbers. Cross's stretch of 8 is read off one creator's stills (10.2 at Size 50, 2.5 at Size 5, where the drawing's size cuts the streaks off), and Bulge and Twist's shapes off one still each; none of the new words was fitted to After Effects' numbers. **If refused:** reverting B-636 and this entry's commit removes the settings; a project saved with a new word or an offset keeps them as written (the save merges the file's own settings), and the earlier build refuses an unknown word with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID and draws the effect without its offset.

D-758 / 4-Color Gradient gains After Effects' Jitter / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-23** under the owner's instruction of that day: "Proceed, if an effect is more like a inspiration/modified version of a AE effect, only improve it. But it is to be a 1 to 1 match, then go for it. Proceed down all the waves." D-208 calls 4-Color Gradient's mixing "this program's own" and left Jitter out, so it is an inspired effect and is only improved: every existing setting keeps its meaning and nothing it draws today changes. Audit of 2026-10-22 (https://claude.ai/artifact/A63KdY44N4HfUHzUnLQhTp), Thin areas, the 4-Color Gradient row: "No Jitter". Built as B-637. **Evidence.** Wave 2 (lane E, 2026-10-23) read After Effects' panel in twelve tutorials by twelve creators: Jitter is in every one, and its default 0 matches ours. Three creators set it, but none gives a frame that can be measured: Jake In Motion's 1:10 and 1:12 stills (Jitter 0 and 100, the viewer at 200%) differ by a standard deviation of 0.21 levels, below what 720p video shows; Dope Motions animates Point 4 between its two stills; TamilEffectsGuru types it without holding it. After Effects' grain therefore cannot be measured, and the strength here is this program's own, kept small. **Accepted.** A new setting `jitter`, a number in per cent, 0 to 100, keyable, absent 0. With j = jitter / 1000 and (X, Y) the pixel's whole place in the drawing's own space (the top-left pixel (0, 0)), each of D-208's weights w_k is multiplied by 1 + j u_k, u_k the seeded number in -1..1 that Noise uses (`grade::unit`, seed 0, frame 0, channel k). So a pixel's four weights are each nudged up or down by up to j of themselves, a tenth at Jitter 100. The grain is fixed to the drawing, the same on every frame, and moves with the layer. Where a pixel sits exactly on a point (some d_k is 0) the weights stay 1 and 0, so a point's own colour is still exact. Jitter 0 is D-208's rule exactly. Nothing grows, and a draft changes nothing (the grain is per pixel of the drawing, as Noise's is). **What changes in a saved project.** `jitter` is written only when it is not 0, is keyed or was in the file already, so a file from before D-758 is saved again byte for byte. **How an old project looks afterwards:** exactly as before. It has no jitter and reads it as 0. A jitter outside 0..100 at any frame keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID (D-46), and in a command is refused with a sentence. On the card, a 4-Color Gradient with jitter above 0 is left off the card's plan and drawn by the processor, with no warning, since nothing is lost (as D-757's new words are; B-637's table checks those frames against the processor's). Jitter 0 is drawn on the card as before. **Fixtures.** No existing fixture changes: FX-4CG-001 to 026 keep their files and values byte for byte. New, in `Fixtures/four_color_gradient/`, worked by `tools/four_color_gradient_reference.py`: FX-4CG-027 to 029 (Jitter 50, Jitter 0 written, equal to FX-4CG-001, and Jitter 100), 030 (keyed), 031 (moved, so the grain moves with the drawing), 032 (after a growing Motion Tile), 033 (a point on a pixel centre stays exact), 034 (one colour four times is unchanged) and 035 to 037 refused (101, -1, keyed to 150). **Gaps (owner options, not built).** The Blend look is kept. Wave 2 found that After Effects' Blend fits a weight of 1/(d² + s²), s about equal to Blend in composition pixels, where ours changes the fall-off power over the whole picture (hard cells at Blend 5, grey at 206). That rests on one creator, and changing it would change every saved 4-Color Gradient and its fixtures, which an inspired effect does not do, so it stays offered as its own decision. Jitter's strength and grain (one pixel, fixed) are this program's own: After Effects' could not be measured, so ours is not claimed to match it. **If refused:** reverting B-637 and this entry's commit removes the setting. A project saved with a jitter keeps it as written (the save merges the file's own settings), and the earlier build draws the effect without its jitter.

D-760 / Drop Shadow gains After Effects' Shadow Only checkbox (audit of 2026-10-22, claim 13, "no Shadow Only") / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-23** under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-23: "Proceed, if an effect is more like a inspiration/modified version of a AE effect, only improve it. But it is to be a 1 to 1 match, then go for it. Proceed down all the waves." Drop Shadow is a 1:1 effect (D-115: modelled on After Effects' Drop Shadow), so it gains After Effects' missing fifth control. Built as B-639. Audit page: https://claude.ai/artifact/A63KdY44N4HfUHzUnLQhTp, claim 13. **Why.** D-115 left Shadow Only out ("Not in this decision: After Effects' Shadow Only"). Wave 3 (lane L, 2026-10-23) read After Effects' Effect Controls panel for Drop Shadow on all four measurable creators, Jake In Motion (nzapxMlX74A), Graphician (VhfHCfAN0M8, After Effects 2024), Anthony Mediaz (XBTK-VFsllI, After Effects 2026) and Emment (pK4hSNqNnMI, After Effects 2020), and on 3 Collective (aBx7D9jnbvM, After Effects 2020): every panel has the same six rows, Shadow Color, Opacity, Direction, Distance, Softness and Shadow Only, a checkbox, off by default. Jake In Motion ticks it at 0:47 (Opacity 69, Direction 111, Distance 21, Softness 36) and the face's yellow strokes vanish, leaving the soft dark-green shadow alone on the green background; 3 Collective ticks it at 0:48 on a corner-pinned duplicate to make a cast shadow. Adobe's own Help page for Drop Shadow lists Shadow Only as the control that shows the shadow without the layer. Ours had the first five; claim 13 holds on 5 of 5 sources. **Accepted.** `core.drop_shadow` takes `shadow_only`, the word "off" or "on", kept exactly as written so a wrong word is reported, as Radial Shadow's (D-211). With "on" the drawing is left out of the output and the shadow alone is drawn: the rule's `I + shadow * (1 - I.a)` with I taken as transparent, so the shadow is exactly the one "off" draws, in the same colour, opacity, place and softness, and is now seen also where the drawing covered it. The layer grows exactly as before. Opacity, softness and how the shadow is mixed are not changed (the other Wave 3 differences are Likely only and wait for the owner). It is the fifth row of Drop Shadow's panel, Shadow Only, Off or On, as After Effects names it; a Drop Shadow added from now on starts at "off". On the CPU and the card alike: the card's `shadow` pass is given the word and leaves the drawing out the same way. The word cannot be keyed, as Radial Shadow's cannot. **What changes in a saved project.** `shadow_only` is written only when it is "on", or when the file already had the word, so a file from before D-760 is saved back byte for byte. **How an old project looks afterwards:** exactly as before: a file without the word reads it as "off", and "off" draws as D-115 did, pixel for pixel. A word other than "off" or "on" in a file keeps the effect as written and leaves it out of every frame with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID (D-46), and in a command is refused with a sentence; nothing is silently replaced. **Fixtures.** `tools/drop_shadow_reference.py` works Shadow Only; FX-SHADOW-001 to 023 are unchanged, their files byte for byte and their expected frames value for value (none retired). New: FX-SHADOW-024 ("on" at the defaults: the shadow alone, FX-SHADOW-001's shadow wherever the card was empty, and nothing of the card), 025 ("on", distance 0: half the card's covering in black at every pixel), 026 ("off" written: FX-SHADOW-001 exactly), 027 ("on", blue, opacity 100, direction 90, distance 2, softness 3), 028 ("on", opacity 0: an empty frame), and 029 and 030 ("On", the panel's name, and "yes": refused, EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID). Document 21's rule and document 25's rows say the same. **Gaps.** No tutorial frame with Shadow Only on can be matched pixel for pixel: Jake In Motion's still is a stand-in drawing at an unknown depth, and its look (strokes gone, shadow alone) is compared by eye on the proof sheet. After Effects' Shadow Only is also used to put the shadow on a separate layer; ours does the same, with the layer still grown by the shadow's reach. Lane L's other Drop Shadow findings (opacity, softness spread and how the shadow is mixed) are not in this decision. **If refused:** the word is removed with its panel row, FX-SHADOW-024 to 030 are removed and the reference tool goes back to its values at ee66d03b; a project saved with Shadow Only "on" keeps the word, and the earlier build ignores it without a warning and draws the drawing with its shadow (checked: `fx_shadow_024.json` opened in the build of fee505f4 draws with no note).

D-749 / Curl Noise's look after After Effects: large soft marbling carried along the flow, Flow Softness higher is crisper, and the speeds added up frame by frame (the 2026-10-22 audit's rows 8, 13 and 14; `docs/effects/EFFECTS.md` row 214) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-23 under the owner's instruction for the audit's waves ("Proceed, if an effect is more like a inspiration/modified version of a AE effect, only improve it. But it is to be a 1 to 1 match, then go for it. Proceed down all the waves."); Curl Noise is a 1:1 effect. Built as B-628. Reopens D-680, which it supersedes.** **Evidence (Wave 1).** Lane A read After Effects' own Curl Noise pictures in seven tutorials (Softoni, Jake In Motion, SternFX, fimje, AE Basics, Vijay Gupta, DeshCloud) and measured each against ours at the same settings: the spread of the greys and how far the pattern holds across and down (comp pixels). After Effects shows large, soft, high-contrast marbling (spread 53 to 98, 53 to 294 px across); ours showed a fine grey hatching (spread 11 to 30, 16 to 36 px across, 2 to 38 down). Row 8 (the texture follows Scale, swirls grow with Sample Radius), row 13 (After Effects' Flow Softness turned down goes "posterized", so higher is crisper, the other way from ours) and row 14 (a keyed Speed in After Effects moves the noise on from where it is; ours jumped, because the drift was speed times frame) were Confirmed. **Accepted:** the rule in document 21 ("Curl Noise, D-749") and `tools/curl_noise_reference.py`: a smooth value noise of four octaves carried backwards along the curl of a two-lattice noise (a flow that never gathers or spreads), Size setting both; Swirl the flow's speed (Swirl / 180); Sample Radius the time the trace runs (0.045 a unit) and Sample Count its parts; the result a mix of the last value read and the mean of them all, crisper as Flow Softness goes up ((Flow Softness / 100)^0.37 of the last); Edge Definition a contrast gain (2 at 50, doubling every 50); and the drift and the depth's travel the sums of Speed / 10 and Turbulence Speed / 10 over the frames before this one, times 24 over the frames a second, so the same distance each second at any frame rate, and a keyed Speed carries on from where the noise is. Source This Layer and Other Layer keep D-583's lightness picture: V = 2 L - 1, the flow along the picture's edges made at most 1 / 9 long, so the point moves at most Size / 9 pixels a unit, in steps of at most a pixel; Rotation, Scale and Perspective Offset do nothing with a picture (as Smoothness and the rest already did). Curl Generation and Input Noise show the new flow and noise. The card (`src/gpu.rs`) works the same rule; the Draft preview scales Size, Offset, Speed, Softness and the drift with its quarter-size pixels, but not Sample Radius. **Fit and check.** The numbers 0.045, 0.37, 1.6 and the gain were fitted on two cases, fimje at After Effects' defaults and DeshCloud at Sample Radius 0; the other seven pictures were only checked. Three-way sheets (After Effects / the build before / this build), spread and pattern size across x down: fimje defaults (fit) 59, 126 x 69 / 17, 30 x 3 / 67, 159 x 72, close; DeshCloud SR 0 (fit) 98, 294 x 140 / 30, 36 x 38 / 77, 275 x 154, close; DeshCloud SR 42 (check) 73, 255 x 104 / 22, 16 x 3 / 71, 220 x 113, matches; DeshCloud SR 80 (check) 62, 123 x 69 / 17, 31 x 3 / 67, 160 x 72, close; SternFX Scale 100 (check) 57, 125 x 65 / 18, 28 x 2 / 67, 158 x 72, close; SternFX Scale 40 (check) 53, 53 x 26 / 11, 21 x 5 / 60, 63 x 30, matches; Vijay Gupta (check) 59, 126 x 69 / 17, 30 x 3 / 67, 159 x 72, close; Jake In Motion frame 46 (check) 60, 182 x 77 / 16, 29 x 3 / 68, 166 x 73, matches; Softoni frame 27 (check) 54, 182 x 70 / 18, 27 x 2 / 68, 167 x 70, close. Every case was "differs" before and is "matches" or "close" after (each of the three numbers within 1.25 times After Effects' for matches, 1.5 for close). Our swirls are busier at their smallest scale than After Effects' (the sheets show it); the numbers do not catch that. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing in the file: no setting is added, renamed or removed, and every project saved before opens with its settings as they were. **Older projects look different**: a Curl Noise saved before this build drew the fine hatching and now draws the marbling, and a project tuned by eye on the old look (Flow Softness low for crisp lines, Edge Definition, Swirl) will look different and may want its settings changed. A keyed Speed or Turbulence Speed now carries on from where the noise is, and a composition at other than 24 frames a second drifts the same distance a second as at 24, where before it drifted Speed / 10 a frame. **Fixtures.** `tools/curl_noise_reference.py` and `tools/curl_transform_reference.py` rewrite `Fixtures/curl_noise/expected_curl_noise.json` and `expected_curl_transform.json`; no fixture project file changes. Every working case's pixels moved, old to new as document 25 records per case (for example FX-CURL-001 270 of 320 pixels by at most 0.806 of a channel, FX-CURL-024 at most 14.268 in HDR, FX-CURL-048 40 of 160 by at most 0.463): FX-CURL-001 to 033, 045 to 052, 054 to 056 and 061 to 073; 18 of them also say different words (002, 003, 005 to 010, 015, 018 to 021, 029, 033, 045, 049, 069). The refused cases 034 to 044, 053, 057 to 060 and 074 to 077 are unchanged. The first values (D-446, D-583, D-646, D-680) are retired as D-110 retired its own: kept in git history at fee505f4, no longer checked. New: FX-CURL-078, Speed keyed from 0 at frame 0 to 40 at frame 4: frame 4 is frame 0 moved 6 pixels (0 + 1 + 2 + 3), not the 16 that speed times frame would jump to; frames 0, 2 and 4. **Gaps.** After Effects' defaults differ from ours (Swirl 180, Sample Count 3, Sample Radius 80, Flow Softness 25, Speed 0, Turbulence Speed 10); they are not changed here, so a new Curl Noise is not yet After Effects' new one (a separate decision; it would change what a newly added effect looks like, not old projects). Scale Width, Scale Height and Uniform Scaling are D-750. Our finest swirls are busier than After Effects'. With a picture at Flow Softness 0 the flow can sit on a knife edge (a saddle) where the card and the processor may send a pixel either way, so the checks allow up to 1920 x 1080 / 200 = 10368 such pixels in a full frame and say so; the fixtures hold the processor's. The fit is to seven YouTube-compressed tutorial screenshots, not to After Effects itself. **Speed.** The trace reads four octaves of noise a point and a step, so the cost changed; B-628's playtest records what was measured. **If refused:** revert B-628 and this entry's fixtures; FX-CURL-001 to 077 are D-680's again and the audit's rows 8, 13 and 14 stay open.

D-750 / Curl Noise's Uniform Scaling, Scale Width and Scale Height, after After Effects' Curl Noise Transform (the 2026-10-22 audit's row 15; `docs/effects/EFFECTS.md` row 214) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-23 under the owner's instruction for the audit's waves ("Proceed, if an effect is more like a inspiration/modified version of a AE effect, only improve it. But it is to be a 1 to 1 match, then go for it. Proceed down all the waves."); Curl Noise is a 1:1 effect. Built as B-629.** **Evidence (Wave 1).** After Effects' Curl Noise Transform has Uniform Scaling (on when added) with Scale, and, with it off, Scale Width and Scale Height (100 each): fimje's tutorial shows Uniform Scaling off with Scale Width 7500% and Scale Height 5% at 4:40, Softoni's panel shows "Scale 100 uniform" at 0:48, and Jake In Motion's beta stream unlinks them for "squished and elongated" noise (35:43). Ours had Scale only. Row 15 was Confirmed. **Accepted:** three settings after D-646's Scale: `uniform_scaling` "on" (as added) or "off"; `scale_width` and `scale_height`, 1 to 10000 per cent, 100 as added, each can be keyed. With Uniform Scaling on, Scale sets both ways as before and the two are kept but not read; with it off, the noise is Scale Width per cent as wide and Scale Height per cent as tall round the drawing's middle (document 21: mx = 100 / scale_width, my = 100 / scale_height), and Scale is kept but not read. As with Rotation and Scale, a picture (Source This Layer or Other Layer) is not scaled. The panel shows Uniform Scaling as an on/off choice and the two numbers beside Scale. **What changes in a saved project.** A project saved before this build has none of the three and reads them as added, Uniform Scaling on: it is drawn by its Scale as before and looks the same as under D-749. They are written only when not as added (D-304), so such a project is saved as it was. **Fixtures.** `tools/curl_transform_reference.py` adds FX-CURL-079 (Width 200, Height 100), 080 (Width and Height 200, the same as FX-CURL-063's Scale 200), 081 (Uniform on with Width 300 and Height 50 written: Scale 100's frame) and 082 (Width 7500, Height 5, the tutorial's long streaks: the greys change down the card more than ten times as much as across it), and refuses 083 (Width 0.5), 084 (Uniform Scaling "yes") and 085 (Height keyed to 20000) with `EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID`. No earlier expected value changes (FX-CURL-001 to 078 are as D-749 left them). **Gaps.** None known for row 15. After Effects' own defaults for the rest of the effect are D-749's gap. **If refused:** revert B-629 and this entry's fixtures; Curl Noise has Scale only again and row 15 stays open.

D-761 / A Radio Waves added from now on starts at After Effects' Lifespan 10 seconds and Fade-out Time 5 seconds, in the composition's frames (audit of 2026-10-22, Radio Waves; wave 3, lane n) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-23** under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-23: "Proceed, if an effect is more like a inspiration/modified version of a AE effect, only improve it. But it is to be a 1 to 1 match, then go for it. Proceed down all the waves." Radio Waves is a 1:1 effect (D-200, after After Effects' Radio Waves), so its starting values are brought to After Effects'. Built as B-640. Audit page: https://claude.ai/artifact/A63KdY44N4HfUHzUnLQhTp. **Why.** Wave 3's lane n (2026-10-23) read After Effects' Effect Controls panel for a freshly added Radio Waves: Lifespan (sec) 10.000 in five tutorials by five creators (True Visuals, Edit in Minutes, MOBOX, Himel 356, and Sahar's panel) and Fade-out Time 5.000 in six. Ours started at 96 frames and 48 frames (4 and 2 seconds at 24 fps). After Effects states both in seconds; ours keeps them in frames (D-200), so the start is worked in the composition the effect is added to. **Accepted.** A Radio Waves added in the window (the Effects panel, the search, or the `effect.add` command) starts at Lifespan = 10 seconds and Fade-out Time = 5 seconds in that composition's frames, to the nearest frame (half away from zero, document 20's rounding) and held inside the setting's range of 1 to 1000: 240 and 120 at 24 fps, 250 and 125 at 25, 300 and 150 at 29.97 and 30. Nothing else about the rule changes. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing in the file's shape: Radio Waves' file has always held `lifespan` and `fade_out_time` (both required since D-200; a file without one is refused, EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, as before), so a Radio Waves added from now on writes, at 24 fps, `"lifespan": 240, "fade_out_time": 120` where it wrote 96 and 48. **How an old project looks afterwards:** exactly as before. Every Radio Waves saved before D-761 holds its own 96 and 48 (or whatever was set), reads them, draws them and saves them back byte for byte; no fallback is involved, so `persist.rs` is not changed. **Fixtures:** none added or changed. FX-RWAVE fixtures are written by `tools/radio_waves_reference.py` with their settings stated in each file, not by the as-added list, so none moves. The as-added values are not a picture a reference script can work out; B-640's app test holds them instead at 24, 25, 29.97 and 120 fps, and loads `Fixtures/radio_waves/fx_rwave_001.json` (96 and 48) to check that it opens and saves unchanged. **Gaps.** (1) Above 100 frames a second, 10 seconds is more than the setting's top of 1000 frames, so the Lifespan is held at 1000 (at 120 fps: 1000 and 600, 8.3 seconds of life); the range is not widened here. (2) Only the as-added values move; the waves' look was not measured against After Effects in this change. **If refused:** `effect.add` goes back to 96 and 48 frames; a Radio Waves added in the meantime keeps its 10 and 5 seconds in its file, which reads and draws as set, and the owner can type 96 and 48 back in the panel.

D-762 / Cell Pattern gains After Effects' Offset, Overflow, Evolution Options (Cycle Evolution, Cycle) and Tiling Options, and Contrast up to 10000 (audit of 2026-10-22, Cell Pattern; wave 3, lane n) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-23** under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-23: "Proceed, if an effect is more like a inspiration/modified version of a AE effect, only improve it. But it is to be a 1 to 1 match, then go for it. Proceed down all the waves." Cell Pattern is an inspired effect (D-209: After Effects' Cell Pattern in purpose, this program's own rule), so it is only improved: the controls After Effects shows are added, and the look of every pattern as it draws today, Bubbles included, is kept. Built as B-641. Audit page: https://claude.ai/artifact/A63KdY44N4HfUHzUnLQhTp. **Why.** Wave 3's lane n (2026-10-23) read After Effects' Cell Pattern panel in four tutorials: mayankwise (After Effects 2025, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jERjrh3lPcg), AfterEffectsRF (CS6, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q65uQ6rPF2o), Digitguy Education (CC2014, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LMkcs2Hj3Q4) and Jake In Motion (CC, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y6R1_9E0tPo). All four show Overflow (set to Clip), Offset (the layer's centre, 960,540 or 640,360, or moved, 184.8,720), Tiling Options and Evolution Options, none of which ours had (D-209's known limits: always clipped, no Offset, no Tiling, no Cycle Evolution). Motion Design Maker (2022, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yrURCmTKYlk) typed Contrast 10000.00, which ours refused (top 1000; the effect was kept and left out with a warning). **Accepted.** Seven new settings, each drawing exactly as before when a file leaves it out: **Offset** (`offset`, x then y in pixels, -100000 to 100000, keyable, absent 0, 0) slides the cells over the drawing, a distance a draft scales; **Overflow** (`overflow`, "clip", "soft_clamp" or "wrap_back", absent "clip") after the contrast, Fractal Noise's three (D-647): Clip holds the grey inside black and white as before, Soft Clamp eases it back inside by 0.5 + 0.5 tanh(2 (v - 0.5)), Wrap Back folds it back at black and white; **Cycle Evolution** (`cycle_evolution`, "off" or "on", absent "off") with **Cycle (in Revolutions)** (`cycle`, 1 to 1000, keyable, its whole part N counted, absent 1) makes the evolution loop every N turns: the evolution is taken modulo 360 N degrees and each cell's point turns K / N times as fast, K a whole number from 1 to N picked by the cell's own noise, so evolution 360 N is evolution 0 exactly and a keyed evolution from 0 to 360 N loops without a jump; **Tiling** (`tiling`, "off" or "on", absent "off") with **Tiles Horizontal** and **Tiles Vertical** (`tiles_horizontal`, `tiles_vertical`, 1 to 1000, keyable, whole parts counted, absent 10) gives cell (m, n) the noise of cell (m mod Th, n mod Tv), so the pattern repeats every Th cells across and Tv down; and Contrast's range widens from 0..1000 to 0..10000. The new settings are on the card as well as the processor (the card reads the same points; Soft Clamp uses single precision's tanh there, within a level, as Fractal Noise's does). Document 21 gives the rule. **What changes in a saved project.** A Cell Pattern writes each new setting only when it differs from the value a file without it means, or is keyed, or was already in the file; a project saved before D-762 has none of them, reads them as absent, draws bit for bit as before and saves back byte for byte (B-641's test loads FX-CELL-001 to 033's files and checks both). A file holding Contrast between 1000 and 10000, refused before (EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, the effect kept and left out), now draws. **Fixtures:** FX-CELL-001 to 033 and their expected frames are unchanged (the reference file's 001 to 033 entries are byte for byte as before; the new ones follow them). Added: FX-CELL-034 to 049 (Offset 2, 0; Offset 0, 0 written = 001; Offset -1.5, 2.5; Offset keyed 0, 0 to 4, 0; Overflow clip written at Contrast 300 = 006; Soft Clamp and Wrap Back at Contrast 300; Contrast 10000 clipped and wrapped; Cycle 1 at evolution 90 = 010; Cycle 2 with evolution keyed 0 to 720, whose frame 4 is frame 0 exactly; Cycle off ignores Cycle; Cycle 2.7 counts 2; Tiling 2 by 2; Tiling off ignores the tiles; every new setting at its absent value = 001) and the invalid FX-CELL-050 to 059 (Contrast 10001; Overflow "allow_hdr"; Cycle Evolution "yes"; Cycle 0 and 1001; Tiling "yes"; Tiles Horizontal 0; Tiles Vertical 1001; Offset 100001 and keyed to -100001), written by `tools/cell_pattern_reference.py`. **Gaps.** (1) After Effects shows Offset as a point, the layer's centre as it starts; ours is the slide from there, 0, 0 as it starts, so a number read off After Effects' panel is typed as its difference from the layer's centre. (2) How After Effects' Cycle moves the cells inside a cycle was not seen (only that the loop closes); the K / N turning is ours. (3) After Effects' starting tile counts were not seen in the sources; 10 by 10 is ours. (4) After Effects lists 12 patterns, ours 4 (Bubbles, Crystals, Plates, Static Plates); the other 8 are not added here. (5) After Effects' Bubbles are round soft blobs where ours are flat cells with dark seams (wave 3: the look differs in 3 of 3 readable comparisons, sizes match); under "only improve" the look is not changed. (6) After Effects shows Evolution as revolutions and degrees; ours is degrees, as before. **If refused:** the seven settings and the wider Contrast are taken out again; projects that never set them are unaffected (their files never held them), and a project saved in the meantime that uses one is not dropped silently: how it then reads is decided under document 28 at that time.

D-765 / Layer markers, as After Effects' tutorials use them, and a marker's length (audit of 2026-10-22, Decision 4; wave 4, lane q) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-23** under the owner's answer of 2026-10-23 to the four decisions on the audit page (https://claude.ai/artifact/A63KdY44N4HfUHzUnLQhTp, v3, section "Final update"): "go by all your recommendations". This carries out Decision 4 (new features), the recommendation to build layer markers. Built as B-645. **Why.** Wave 4's lane q (2026-10-23) read six marker sources: Adobe's Layer markers and composition markers page (comp and layer markers, markers with a duration, Shift snapping to markers, the * key); Dan Ebberts on Creative Cow (2006) and on motionscript.com ("Marker Sync"), both driving animation from a layer's markers; Workbench (Joe Clay, 2017, "Semi-Automatic Animation"), which retimes from split layer markers with a duration; and two Lesterbanks quick tips (Creative Dojo, 2021; Mikey Borup), which trigger animation from markers. Ours had composition markers only (W-24). A layer's `markers`, which After Effects' tutorials put on nearly every layer they time to, was kept in the file by ADR-008's record but never read, never shown and never said: lane q's `proj_laymark.json`, a layer with `"markers": [{"frame": 12, "name": "hit"}]`, opened with no note, a document 28 breach. Nor did any marker have a length, Shift snap to markers, or J and K stop at them. **Accepted.** (1) A layer carries markers: a frame, a name (After Effects' comment) and a length, `duration_frames`, 0 for a marker on one frame; kept in frame order. Read and saved as real data, in the field shape the file already had: `{"frame": 12, "name": "hit"}`, with `"duration_frames": 6` only on a marker with a length. A marker may sit outside the layer's frames, as After Effects allows. (2) Composition markers take the same length, read and saved the same way (before D-765 a composition marker's `duration_frames` in a file was dropped on save without a word). (3) The timeline draws a layer's markers on its bar, a pennant on the frame with its name beside it, and a marker with a length as a strip along the bar's top to its end; a composition marker with a length gets the same strip on the ruler. (4) `*` (Numpad * or Shift+8) with layers selected adds a marker on each selected layer at the playhead, one entry to undo, as After Effects' Numpad *; with none selected it adds a composition marker, as before. On the bar, a layer marker is dragged to move it, Alt+dragged to pull out its length (After Effects' Alt-drag), double-clicked to name it, and Ctrl+clicked to remove it; a press that does not move puts the playhead on it. Each is one entry to undo, by the command `layer.set_markers` (document 24's new row; the whole list each time, as W-24's `timeline.set_markers`, document 26's one entry per edit and one per drag). Doc 24 had no other use of `*`; the shortcut list shows it once, as "Add a marker". (5) Shift-dragging the playhead snaps to every composition and layer marker, as it snaps to keys and layer ends. (6) J and K stop at the composition's markers and at the markers of the selected layers (every layer's when none is selected), as well as at keys. (7) A layer slid along the timeline carries its markers by the same number of frames, as its keys (D-740). **What changes in a saved project.** A layer with markers writes `"markers"`, `frame` and `name` per marker and `duration_frames` only when not 0; a layer without any writes no `markers` key, so a project saved before D-765 with no markers opens with no word said, looks the same and saves byte for byte as before (B-645's test loads `Fixtures/projects/minimal_project.json` and FX-LMARK-003). A project that had layer markers in it (from After Effects' naming, or written by hand) now shows them, and saves them back in frame order. A layer `markers` value this build cannot read (not a list, or an entry without a whole-number `frame`, a text `name` and, if given, a whole-number `duration_frames` of 0 or more) gets a PROJECT_FEATURE_UNSUPPORTED warning when opened naming the layer and where in the file; the file still opens, the layer shows no markers, and saving writes the value back exactly as it was. `null` is read as no markers and an empty list is kept as written. Adding a marker to that layer replaces the unreadable value (the warning says so). A composition `markers` value that cannot be read still refuses the file, as W-24 had it. **Fixtures:** none changes. Added: FX-LMARK-001 to 009 (`Fixtures/layer_markers/`, written by `tools/layer_markers_reference.py`): an After Effects-style marker; two out of order, one with a length; an old file with no markers; markers as text; a marker with a text frame; composition markers with a length beside a layer marker; a layer slid 5 frames carrying a marker with a length from 12 to 17; `null`; an empty list. **Evidence:** `verification/B-645_layer_markers_table.md` (written by `tests/b645_layer_markers.rs`), the app test `b645_layer_markers_are_added_undone_and_shown`, and a timeline picture in `verification/B-645 pictures/`. Not a picture change: nothing a render draws is different. **Gaps.** (1) Marker expressions (`marker.key(n).time`, `marker.nearestKey(time)`, `marker.numKeys`, `marker.key("begin")`), which Ebberts' and Workbench's techniques need, are not built: **follow-up proposal**, the expression engine (D-345) reads `thisLayer.marker` and `thisComp.marker` as keys with `time`, `index`, `comment` and `duration`, with fixtures from a reference script; not decided here. (2) A layer's time stretch (D-216) does not move its markers; After Effects stretches them with the layer. (3) Markers carry no chapter, web link, cue point or label colour, and are not exported. (4) PROJECT_FEATURE_UNSUPPORTED is document 28's proposed identifier (as D-527 uses it), not yet in the catalogue. (5) A composition marker's length is drawn but not dragged on the ruler (the file and the request carry it). **If refused:** the layer markers' reading, drawing and commands are taken out again; a layer's `markers` goes back to being kept in the file unread, so no project saved in the meantime loses them, and the unreadable-markers warning is decided again under document 28. A composition marker's length would again be dropped on save.

D-764 / A Curl Noise added from now on starts at After Effects' Speed 0, Turbulence Speed 10, Swirl 180, Sample Count 3, Sample Radius 80 and Flow Softness 25 (audit of 2026-10-22, Curl Noise, Decision 4; `docs/effects/EFFECTS.md` row 214) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-23** under the owner's answer of 2026-10-23 to the four decisions on the audit page https://claude.ai/artifact/A63KdY44N4HfUHzUnLQhTp (v3, "Final update"): "go by all your recommendations". It carries out Decision 4's recommendation that a new Curl Noise start where After Effects starts one. The earlier rule holds: "if an effect is more like a inspiration/modified version of a AE effect, only improve it. But it is to be a 1 to 1 match, then go for it." Curl Noise is a 1:1 effect (D-446, after After Effects' Curl Noise, Noise & Grain, 26.3 beta), so its starting values are brought to After Effects'. Built as B-643. **Why.** Wave 1's lane A read After Effects' Effect Controls panel for a freshly added Curl Noise (Softoni, 0:48; `S/wave1/a/curl/SOURCES.md`): Speed 0, Turbulence Speed 10, Swirl 180, Sample Count 3, Sample Radius 80, Flow Softness 25. D-749 fitted Curl Noise's look at exactly these values (its "AE defaults" case, `spec_curl_w1.json`), and its Gaps already named the as-added values as left for later. Ours started at 10, 20, 45, 12, 30 and 20. **Mapping.** Since D-749 each of the six settings is After Effects' own setting under the same name and in the same unit (Speed and Turbulence Speed in After Effects' per-second units, Swirl in degrees, Sample Radius in pixels, Sample Count a count, Flow Softness 0 to 100), so each number is carried over as it is: 0, 10, 180, 3, 80, 25. **Accepted.** A Curl Noise added in the window (the Effects panel, the search, or the `effect.add` command) starts at those six values. Every other starting value is unchanged. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing in the file's shape: Curl Noise's file has always held all six (each is required by `persist.rs` and always written), so a Curl Noise added from now on writes `"speed": 0, "turbulence_speed": 10, "swirl": 180, "sample_count": 3, "sample_radius": 80, "flow_softness": 25` where it wrote 10, 20, 45, 12, 30 and 20. **How an old project looks afterwards:** exactly as before. Every Curl Noise saved before D-764 holds its own six values, reads them, draws them and saves them back byte for byte. No fallback is involved, so `persist.rs` is not changed (as D-759 and D-761). **Fixtures:** none added or changed. The FX-CURL fixtures state their settings in each file and are written by their reference script, not by the as-added list, so none moves. B-643's app test holds the as-added values instead, and loads `Fixtures/curl_noise/fx_curl_001.json` (10, 20, 45, 12, 30, 20) to check that it opens at its own values and saves to the same bytes. **Gaps.** (1) After Effects' panel also shows Smoothness 0 and Vertical Bias 0. Ours read these two differently (our Vertical Bias 50 is "even", not After Effects' 0), so they are not carried over and stay at 50 and 50; matching them needs their meaning measured first. (2) Only the as-added values move; the look at these values is D-749's. **If refused:** `effect.add` goes back to 10, 20, 45, 12, 30 and 20; a Curl Noise added in the meantime keeps its After Effects values in its file, which reads and draws as set, and the owner can type the old ones back in the panel.

D-763 / In 8 bpc (After Effects) colours mix in display values, as After Effects does in an 8-bit project (audit of 2026-10-22, Decision 1) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-23**: on 2026-10-23 the owner answered "go by all your recommendations" on the audit page (https://claude.ai/artifact/A63KdY44N4HfUHzUnLQhTp), whose Decision 1 recommended "match After Effects in 8-bit projects and keep linear for 16 and 32-bit". Built as B-642. It widens D-330: D-330 rounded effects to 8 bits and made the four blurs average display values, but every layer was still laid on the one beneath in linear light. **Why.** After Effects in an 8-bit project has no linear working space: a layer's opacity, its mask's feather, its matte and its blend mode all act on the display values, the 0 to 255 numbers a picture is saved with. Ours did all of them in linear light, so the same layers came out in different colours. Three-way sheets (After Effects' own frame, this build before, this build after; `verification/B-642 pictures/`) measured, in levels of 255: km1's Screen median 7 and p90 15 before, 3 and 9 after, the mean level 56.7 before and 63.2 after against After Effects' 62.9; km4's Add median 30 and p90 54 before, 4 and 15 after, mean 157.5 and 186.2 against 188.0; gds2's Multiply at 70% median 4 and p90 24 before, 2 and 5 after; jim's Drop Shadow 50% shadow strength 0.373 before, 0.5 after, After Effects' 0.5; vlad's Mosaic mean block error 18.3 before, 1.9 after (worst block 78.2 before, 10.9 after); bullo's Gaussian Blur edge over a background, the middle row's mean difference 37.7 before and 14.7 after, ours 23.4 levels too light before and 2.1 too dark after. **Accepted.** In a composition whose outermost composition is in 8 bpc (After Effects), and in every composition drawn inside it: (1) each layer's picture, once its own effects have run, is taken to display values, its straight colour held to 0..1 and put through the sRGB curve, premultiplied; (2) its opacity, mask coverage (feather included) and matte act on those values exactly as before, since they only scale a pixel; (3) it is laid on the frame in its blend mode on those values, Normal with part alpha included; the blend modes that already worked on encoded colours (D-301, D-748) work on them as they are; (4) the whole frame is taken back to linear light at the end, so the rest of the program sees what it always has. An adjustment layer takes the frame back to linear light, runs its effects as before, and returns it to display values. Drop Shadow, Fill and Mosaic join D-330's blurs and D-337's Glow and Solid Composite on display values: their colours are used as written, not converted, and Mosaic's block average is the mean of display values; the Linear Wipe and Radial Wipe feathers only scale alpha, so they act on display values with no change of code; Echo mixes its copies in display values. Exposure stays in linear light, as D-330 has it. This is done in one place, the step that lays layers together; no effect gains a setting. The graphics card takes no part in 8 bpc: a frame of an 8 bpc composition is drawn wholly on the CPU, and the viewer says so ("The CPU drew this frame: its composition works in 8 bpc (After Effects)."). Display, Float and 32 bpc (After Effects) are unchanged, bit for bit. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing: no setting is added, renamed or written differently, and `eight_bpc` is the field D-330 already saves. Every file saves byte for byte as before. **How an old 8 bpc project looks afterwards:** wherever two layers meet, or a layer is part see-through, it now looks as After Effects shows it, and so different from before. A black Drop Shadow at 50% over white was light grey (188) and is now mid grey (127, After Effects' 127 or 128): shadows, soft mask edges and faded layers look darker and stronger. A Screen or Add layer lightens more than before (FX-MIX8-001: 182,127,219 was, 194,150,232 is). A Normal layer at 50% lies nearer the darker of the two colours. A Mosaic block over two colours is the mean of their display values, darker than before (184,96,147 was, 125,90,105 is). A single layer over nothing, with no opacity below 100%, looks exactly as before. Display projects, the program's default, are not touched. **Fixtures.** Added: FX-MIX8-001 to 012 in `Fixtures/display_mix/`, written by `tools/display_mix_reference.py`, which works the rule on its own in double precision and never runs the build's code: Screen, Add, Normal at 50%, a black Drop Shadow at 50% over white, a mask feathered 2 pixels and a Mosaic of 2 by 2, each in 8 bpc (odd numbers) and the same scene in Display (even numbers), whose frame is the linear-light mix as before. B-642's test also sets each 8 bpc scene to Display and checks it draws the Display frame, and back. No expected value of any existing fixture changes. The old 8 bpc cases are each one layer over nothing, so they draw as before within the tolerance (2e-5): FX-8BPC-001 1.3e-8 to 7.8e-8, 002 2.5e-8 to 1.5e-7, 004 1.3e-8 to 7.8e-8, 003 and 005 unmoved at 1.4e-7 and 3.1e-8, and D-330's nested rows 1.3e-8 to 1.7e-7 (the extra trip to display values and back in single precision); FX-GLDISP-001 to 008, FX-AE32 and every other test named in B-642's report pass unchanged. **Evidence.** `verification/B-642_display_mix_table.md` (52 of 52 checks), the three-way sheets in `verification/B-642 pictures/`, `verification/D-330_eight_bpc_table.md` and `verification/B-44_gpu_window_table.md` regenerated (8 bpc frames now drawn on the CPU). **Gaps.** (1) Bevel Alpha is unchanged. (2) Motion blur's averaging of moments stays in linear light. (3) Light Wrap now works on display values, as it reads the frame below; it was not compared with After Effects. (4) An adjustment layer's effects run in linear light between the two conversions. (5) A composition inside another is taken back to linear light at its end and returned to display values by the outer one, which loses nothing an 8 bpc picture holds. (6) bullo's Gaussian Blur is about 13% wider than After Effects' in the same sheet; that is the blur's width, not the mix, and is not changed here. (7) jim's sheet uses a stand-in drawing where After Effects' differs, so only the shadow's strength is compared. (8) Open option, not built: After Effects' default 32 bpc without Linearize Working Space also mixes display values, but our 32 bpc (After Effects) stays in linear light, as the owner picked ("keep linear for 16 and 32-bit"); D-333 is unchanged. **If refused:** layers are laid together in linear light in 8 bpc again, Drop Shadow, Fill, Mosaic and Echo go back to linear light, the card draws 8 bpc frames again, FX-MIX8-001 to 012 are retired, and no project needs changing, since no setting was added.

D-766 / After Effects' Expression Controls, and `if`, comparisons and logic in expressions (audit of 2026-10-22, expressions; wave 6, lane w6expr) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-23** under the owner's answer "go by all your recommendations" (Decision 4, new features). Built as B-646. Audit page: https://claude.ai/artifact/A63KdY44N4HfUHzUnLQhTp. **Why.** Wave 4's lane q (2026-10-23) typed the expressions After Effects tutorials teach first: a Slider Control driving `wiggle`'s amount (School of Motion, Nol Honig, AEJuice, Adobe's community) and a Checkbox Control switching a layer on with `if (effect("Checkbox Control")("Checkbox") == 1) 100 else 0`. Ours refused both when the text was read (`EXPRESSION_SYNTAX`) and drew the keyed values; the only way to build the same rig was a stand-in layer's rotation read through `thisComp.layer(...)` and `clamp`, which no tutorial shows. **How this reopens D-59.** D-59 said "there is no `if`, no comparison and no loop in this first version" and left `if`, comparisons and loops, and expressions on effect parameters, "not decided here", adding that adding them later "is a specification change with fixtures, not a rewrite". D-291 already let an effect's number setting carry an expression; this entry decides the rest except loops: `if`/`else`, comparisons and `&&`, `||`, `!` join the language, and an expression may read an effect's setting. Loops stay out, so D-59's two counted walls (a long text, and properties reading one another) are still the only ways to run long; an `if` counts as one step. Everything else D-59 and document 09 say is unchanged, and FX-EXPR-001 to 016 hold to the last digit. **Accepted.** (1) Six effects, After Effects' Expression Controls, each with one setting and drawing nothing: **Slider Control** (`core.slider_control`, Slider, `slider`, -1000000 to 1000000, added at 0), **Checkbox Control** (`core.checkbox_control`, Checkbox, `checkbox`, 0 off or 1 on, added off), **Angle Control** (`core.angle_control`, Angle in degrees, `angle`, -1000000000 to 1000000000, added at 0), **Point Control** (`core.point_control`, Point, `point`, x then y in the layer's pixels, added at 0, 0), **Color Control** (`core.color_control`, Color, `color`, red, green and blue as the effect holds them, added red, 1, 0, 0) and **Layer Control** (`core.layer_control`, Layer, `layer`, a layer's ID or "" for None, added None). The first five settings can be keyed and can carry their own expression (D-291); Layer cannot be keyed. (2) `effect(name)` on this layer and `thisComp.layer(id).effect(name)` on another, `name` being the effect's After Effects name, "Slider Control 2" for the second of the same kind, its match name ("ADBE Slider Control") or a number counting every effect from 1; then `(setting)` by name ("Slider"), match name ("ADBE Slider Control-0001") or 1, with `.value` and `.valueAtTime(t)`. A Checkbox reads 1 or 0, a Color a list of four with alpha 1, a Point a list of two and a Layer Control the layer it names. (3) `if (c) a else b` with braces, `else if` and the else on a later line; `< <= > >= == != === !==`; `&&`, `||` and `!`; `true` and `false`. Document 09 gives every rule. (4) A missing effect, a missing setting, a Layer Control naming no layer or a deleted one is `EXPRESSION_REFERENCE_MISSING`; another effect's setting is `EXPRESSION_SYNTAX`; a cycle through settings is `EXPRESSION_CYCLE` (document 28's existing identifiers, the first widened). As before a failing expression draws its property's keyed value and says so (D-767). (5) **Names are After Effects' and cannot be changed**: this program has no effect renaming, so "Slider Control 2" is the only way to tell two sliders apart, and the Effect Controls panel shows the number on the second one so the name typed is the name seen. **What changes in a saved project.** Six new type IDs, each with its one setting written as other effects' settings are. A project saved before D-766 holds none of them and loads, draws and saves back byte for byte (B-646's test loads `expression_project.json` and checks). An expression saved before D-766 that used `if`, a comparison or `effect(` failed then and now runs; no other expression changes value. A project using a control opened in a build from before D-766 keeps the effect as an unknown one under document 28 (`EFFECT_UNSUPPORTED`), never dropped, and the expressions reading it fail visibly. **Fixtures:** FX-EXPR-001 to 016 and `Fixtures/projects/expression_project.json` are unchanged (the generator's output for them is byte for byte as before). Added: `Fixtures/projects/expression_controls_project.json` and FX-EXPR-017 to 020 in document 25: the controls read every way (017), `if` and the operators (018), what is refused (019), and lane q's two tutorial rigs with real controls, a Slider Control driving `wiggle` and a Checkbox Control switching opacity (020), all from `tools/expression_reference.py`, which gains the same rules. **Gaps.** (1) After Effects' Point Control starts at the layer's centre in recent versions; ours at 0, 0 (not confirmed from a source). (2) After Effects' Color Control holds the colour as the swatch shows it; ours holds this program's working numbers, so a colour read into a property is not converted. (3) No colour swatch, no point handle in the viewer and no layer picker beyond a list; the settings are typed. (4) Layer Control cannot be keyed, and After Effects' "Source"/"Masks"/"Effects" choice on it is not offered. (5) Still no loops, no `? :`, no functions, no `.param(...)` and no reading of other effects' settings. (6) The pick whip onto an effect's setting (D-83 extended) is a follow-up proposal, not built here. **If refused:** the six controls and the new words are taken out again; projects that never used them are unaffected (their files never held them), and a project saved in the meantime that uses one is not dropped silently: how it then reads is decided under document 28 at that time.

D-767 / A failed expression says so beside the frame and in the snapshot JSON (audit of 2026-10-22, expressions; wave 6, lane w6expr) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-23** under the owner's answer "go by all your recommendations" (Decision 4, new features). Built as B-647. Audit page: https://claude.ai/artifact/A63KdY44N4HfUHzUnLQhTp. **Why.** Document 09 says a property whose expression fails is drawn at its keyed value "and the diagnostic is shown on that property", and an export over such a frame is refused. The export already says so; the viewer did not. Lane q (wave 4, 2026-10-23) rendered After Effects tutorial expressions through `tools/app_snapshot.py`: `if (...)` and `effect(...)` failed with `EXPRESSION_SYNTAX`, the keyed values were drawn, and neither the page's notes nor the snapshot JSON held a word of it, so a wrong picture read as a right one. The window's frame notes passed on only `TEXT_FONT_MISSING` (D-263). **Accepted.** (1) Every document 28 `EXPRESSION_` diagnostic recorded while a frame is made (`EXPRESSION_SYNTAX`, `EXPRESSION_TYPE`, `EXPRESSION_REFERENCE_MISSING`, `EXPRESSION_CYCLE`, `EXPRESSION_TIMEOUT`) is said beside that frame as a missing font is: its sentence in the notes, its code and sentence in the error details, for as long as the frame is on screen. (2) `tools/app_snapshot.py` counts these five as failures, as it counts a missing font, so a shot drawn with a failed expression is marked failed. (3) Nothing else changes: the property is still drawn at its keyed value (D-59), the export is still refused, and no pixel of any frame changes. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing. **Fixtures:** none changed; no pixel and no saved byte moves. B-647's app check is the evidence (a broken expression's note, its pixel at the keyed value, a working expression with no note). **Gaps.** (1) The note gives the sentence (property and frame), not the reason the expression failed. **If refused:** the frame notes go back to fonts only; nothing saved depends on it.

D-768 / Echo's Composite In Back puts the present copy at the back and Composite In Front puts it in front, as After Effects does (wave 7, lane w7a, Echo) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-24**. On 2026-10-24 the owner wrote: "based off the artifact, work on the limited/unconfirmed/weak areas; also do a performance audit on all the effects that are heavy hitters, figure out gpu-acceleration (deep-research if you must to fully utilize it's power) or optimize on cpu if you must. follow more tutorials that utlize these effects or multiple effects to further confirm it's look, function, and relationship with others and the features of the app." Built as B-648. It reopens D-195's operator rule and changes two of its stored values, so it was held to seven agreeing sources. **Why.** Adobe's manual: "Composite In Back: the image from the current time appears in the back, with each echo successively farther forward"; Composite In Front puts the current image in front. D-195 had the two the other way round. Seven tutorials from seven creators show the same in After Effects, and none shows otherwise: Jake In Motion (N2qxF8V57FE, 0:36 to 0:56), Andy Ford (Xv8Ttz5-02s, 1:55 to 2:31), Angie Taylor (Ve8BsPW6Gr8, 3:58 to 4:35), ANIMOTION (Hkw55cblOCk, 1:36 and 1:48), COLOR CODE (txI5gmsyxbU, 1:40 and 1:44), Pro_Art (5n2H17JMdYo, 2:42 to 2:45) and Motion Inspire (ySYuuu4V5v4, 3:41 and 3:44): with In Front the moving thing is whole on top of its trail; with In Back the trail lies over it, the oldest echo on top. Five more (m33ch, Bryan Delimata, Online Learning Space, AYANA, HOOP) cannot tell the two apart in their frames. **Accepted.** `composite_in_back` is `Q_N over ... over Q_1 over Q_0`; `composite_in_front` is `Q_0 over Q_1 over ... over Q_N` (document 21). Nothing else in Echo changes, the other five operators included. **What changes in a saved project.** No setting is added, renamed or written differently; files save byte for byte as before. A project saved with Composite In Back now draws as it drew with In Front before, and the other way round: the trail's stacking flips. **Fixtures.** FX-ECHO-010 and 011, frame 4: the two exchanged their values, 18 pixels of each moved by at most 0.206 (`tools/echo_reference.py`); D-195's values are retired, kept in the repository's history at commit 440cecf0. Every other Echo case is unchanged. **Evidence.** The seven sources above and the manual; three-way sheets (After Effects' frame, this build before, this build after) in `verification/B-648 pictures/`; `verification/B-648_echo_stacking_table.md`. **Gaps, measured and not changed here.** (1) Blend: COLOR CODE's white-background Blend is as light as Add (255 of 255), ours about 91; three sources, and the formula is not known. (2) Minimum on part see-through layers: three sources show a darker trail than ours; it would change FX-ECHO-008, so it needs seven. (3) Echo Time is held to whole frames (D-195); one source suggests After Effects samples between frames. (4) A layer's own movement leaves no trail, as in After Effects; tutorials precompose (Inhouse Digital pGTPmz7cG6A 6:28, Gina Design tP7Owd6bkb0). **If refused:** the two operators swap back, FX-ECHO-010 and 011 return to D-195's values at 440cecf0, and no project needs changing.

D-786 / Fill on an adjustment layer fills the frame beneath it (wave 7, lane w7e, tutorial replay) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-24** under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-24: "based off the artifact, work on the limited/unconfirmed/weak areas; also do a performance audit on all the effects that are heavy hitters, figure out gpu-acceleration (deep-research if you must to fully utilize it's power) or optimize on cpu if you must. follow more tutorials that utlize these effects or multiple effects to further confirm it's look, function, and relationship with others and the features of the app." Built as B-666. **Why.** Lane w7e rebuilt Ben Marriott's "2D Smoke & Explosions" cloud rig (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w8mHmW6GgHM): an adjustment layer called Effects holding Extract, Turbulent Displace, Gaussian Blur, Levels (Alpha) and Fill (white). At 9:27 he says "you just add the effect fill" and by 9:45 the grey, noise-multiplied strokes beneath are pure white. Ours left them grey (135 to 178 of 255) and said nothing. A test of one adjustment layer over a grey solid of 200 showed why: Tint on the adjustment layer gave 0, 200, 0 as it should, Fill (red) left 200, 200, 200 with no note. The adjustment layer's stack is made again where it runs on the frame beneath (D-66, `compose.rs`), and that remaking skipped the step D-418 added that tells each Fill which masks it fills, so every Fill there had no paths and drew nothing. That is a silent fidelity fallback, which document 28 forbids. **How this sits with the bar.** Nothing accepted is reopened and no stored check value changes: D-418 already says Fill Mask 0 with All Masks off fills the whole layer, and D-65 already says an adjustment layer's effects run on everything beneath as one picture. This entry makes the build do what the two say together; the tutorial is the After Effects source for the result. **Accepted.** (1) On an adjustment layer, a Fill with Fill Mask 0 and All Masks off fills everything beneath it by D-418's rule (each pixel P becomes P (1 - k) + C P.a k, k = Opacity / 100, alpha kept; Invert leaves nothing to fill), and the result is mixed back by the adjustment layer's coverage and opacity as D-65 says.
