(2) On an adjustment layer, a Fill that names a mask (Fill Mask 1 or more, or All Masks on) fills nothing and says `EFFECT_PATH_MISSING` every frame, with the remedy "Set Fill Mask to 0 and All Masks off to fill the whole frame beneath, or put the Fill on the layer itself". The adjustment layer's own masks still shape where it applies (D-66). **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing in the file. A project saved before D-786 that has a Fill with Fill Mask 0 on an adjustment layer now draws the fill where it drew nothing; one naming a mask draws as before and now says so each frame. A Fill on any other layer draws to the last digit as before (FX-FILL-001 to 044 hold; B-666's test also opens D-418's `fx_fill_001.json`, a project from before D-786, and draws it as pinned, and three of its own files write their mask in the old single `mask` record). **Fixtures:** none changed. Added: `Fixtures/fill_adjustment/` and FX-FILLADJ-001 to 009 in document 25, from `tools/fill_adjustment_reference.py`: as added, red (001); Fill opacity 50 (002); white on half-covered green, coverage kept (003); a mask on the adjustment layer (004); the adjustment layer at opacity 50 (005); Invert (006); Fill Mask 1 and All Masks on, not drawn and said (007, 008); two Fills in a row (009). **Gaps.** (1) Fill Mask n on an adjustment layer is not drawn: the adjustment layer's masks are not carried to the frame beneath as paths, and doing so under a moved or scaled adjustment layer is its own decision. (2) Likely the same skipped preparation affects the other effects whose masks, sound or paths are prepared per layer when put on an adjustment layer: Stroke, Vegas, Energy Stroke, Audio Spectrum, Audio Waveform, Inner/Outer Key, Reshape, Liquify, Mask Smear, Scribble and Particle Playground. Not checked effect by effect; reported, not built. (3) After Effects' Preserve Underlying Transparency (the T switch the tutorial sets on its noise solid) is not in this program; the rebuild used an alpha matte instead. **If refused:** the adjustment layer's Fill goes back to drawing nothing; nothing saved depends on it, and the warning for a named mask goes with it.

D-777 / Radio Waves: Parameters Are Set At, and Sides up to 128 (wave 7, lane w7c; effects audit weak areas) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-24** under the owner's words "based off the artifact, work on the limited/unconfirmed/weak areas; also do a performance audit on all the effects that are heavy hitters, figure out gpu-acceleration (deep-research if you must to fully utilize it's power) or optimize on cpu if you must. follow more tutorials that utlize these effects or multiple effects to further confirm it's look, function, and relationship with others and the features of the app." Built as B-657. Radio Waves is a 1:1 effect (D-200, its card pass D-345). **Why.** The audit's weak-areas list (audit page https://claude.ai/artifact/A63KdY44N4HfUHzUnLQhTp, "Radio Waves: Parameters Are Set At Birth, Sides up to 128") rests on wave 3's lane n reading After Effects' own panel: True Visuals (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=offPhZy7-NY, still at 0:00:05:19) shows "Parameters are set at: Birth" with every other setting at its start; MOBOX (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uZlCVIRsKeA, panel "Parameters are set at Birth", the producer point moved by an expression round a circle 400 pixels out) shows each ring staying round the point where it was sent, a lattice of circles, where ours drew every ring round today's point; Jake In Motion (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wf8XFPvUptc, about 4:05) types Sides 128 and Edit in Minutes (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=otdpArskcJ0, 2;08) Sides 72, both refused by ours (3 to 64). Both are After Effects controls ours lacked, added with the old look unchanged where a file does not ask for them, so one clear After Effects source each meets the bar. **Accepted.** (1) Sides go from 3 to 128, the whole part counted as before; 129 or more is `EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID` as 65 was. (2) A new setting, Parameters Are Set At, `parameters_at`, "birth" or "each_frame"; anything else is `EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID`. "each_frame" is D-200's rule, word for word: every wave alive is drawn with the settings at the frame shown. "birth" is After Effects' own: each wave keeps the producer point, expansion, orientation, direction, velocity, spin, lifespan, opacity, fade-in and fade-out times and start and end widths it had at the frame it was born (k times the interval, the settings read at that frame's whole number), so a moving producer leaves its rings where it sent them and a keyed opacity fades only the waves born later. Birth frames still follow the interval at the frame shown, and sides, profile and colour are the ones at the frame shown. Waves born up to 1000 frames back, the longest lifespan, are looked at, each alive while its age is below its own lifespan. With nothing keyed the two give the same picture to the last digit. (3) A Radio Waves added from now on is set at Birth, After Effects' own; the Effect Controls panel offers Each Frame first, then Birth. **What changes in a saved project.** The word is written only when it is "birth" or the file already held it (D-320's rule), so a project saved before D-777 has no `parameters_at`, opens as Each Frame, draws as before to the last digit and saves back byte for byte (B-657 loads `fx_rwave_015.json`, a keyed producer, and checks). The birth settings of each wave are worked out while drawing and never saved. A project using Birth or more than 64 sides opened in a build from before D-777: more than 64 sides is refused there with `EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID` (the effect kept as written and left out); the word itself is passed over by that build, which then draws Each Frame without a warning (measured: B-657's MOBOX project opens in the build at 440cecf0 with every ring round today's point). That older build cannot be changed now; it is recorded here. **Fixtures:** FX-RWAVE-001 to 027 unchanged to the last digit (their files and expected values compare equal). Added FX-RWAVE-028 to 035 in document 25 and `Fixtures/radio_waves/`, all from `tools/radio_waves_reference.py`, which gains the same rule: 128 sides (028), Birth with the producer keyed (029), Each Frame written (030, FX-RWAVE-015 exactly), a keyed opacity at Birth (031), Birth with nothing keyed (032, FX-RWAVE-008 exactly), a keyed lifespan at Birth (033) and two refusals, 129 sides (034) and "death" (035). The old refusal checks "sides 64.5" and "keyed to 70" become "128.5" and "keyed to 129". **Gaps.** (1) After Effects' Render Quality, Wave Type (Image Contour, Mask), Star, Curve Size and Reflection are still missing. (2) Whether After Effects holds sides, profile and colour at birth too is not seen in any source; ours takes them at the frame shown. (3) MOBOX's orbit speed cannot be read from the still; the B-657 picture assumes a turn a second, so that comparison is "close", not measured. (4) Speed: Birth reads the settings once per wave alive, up to 1000 divided by the interval reads a frame (500 at an interval of 2); noted for lane w7d, not optimised here. **If refused:** the word and the 65 to 128 sides are refused again; a project saved meanwhile with either is not dropped silently: the effect is kept as written and left out with `EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID`, decided under document 28 at that time.

D-778 / Shape Repeater: each copy's opacity steps by i / copies, as After Effects' does (wave 7, lane w7c; effects audit weak areas; reopens D-738 (c)) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-24** under the owner's words "based off the artifact, work on the limited/unconfirmed/weak areas; also do a performance audit on all the effects that are heavy hitters, figure out gpu-acceleration (deep-research if you must to fully utilize it's power) or optimize on cpu if you must. follow more tutorials that utlize these effects or multiple effects to further confirm it's look, function, and relationship with others and the features of the app." Built as B-658. The Repeater is a 1:1 After Effects operator (D-738 (c)). **Why.** The audit's weak-areas list (audit page https://claude.ai/artifact/A63KdY44N4HfUHzUnLQhTp, "Shape Repeater: opacity steps by i/copies in After Effects, i/(copies-1) in ours") was measured in seven tutorials by six creators, each copy's opacity read from the pixels against a copy at full opacity (the method reads about 0.01 to 0.05 high on small dots), and every one agrees with i / copies, none with i / (copies - 1): SSB Otaru (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ebvf79jTQWA, about 0:16 to 0:31; 6 copies, Start 0, End 100: measured 0, .18, .34, .51, .66, .84 against i / 6's 0, .167, .333, .5, .667, .833 and i / 5's last copy 1; with Start 100, End 0 the last copy is .21, i / 5 would give 0); Shake my art (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DtHNjDQHi2g, about 1:18; 7 copies, Start 7, End 100: last copy .854 against .867 and 1.0); Evan Abrams, Repeater Grids (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0oJ1Ipa_cdM, about 8:05; two repeaters of 9, Start 86.2, End 2.8: the top row's last dot .128 against .104 and .024, the far corner .014 against .015 and .0008); Visual Motions (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dJAUUqDuCUM, about 5:43; 15 copies, Start 0, End 89: copy 11 .663 against .653 and .699); AITEE Media (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9m2bQ3OfWG8, about 24:08 and 24:12; 9 copies, Start 100, End 0: last square .109 against .111 and 0); Evan Abrams for PremiumBeat (wave 4's record; 12 copies, Start 0, End 100: levels 2, 21, ... 234 of 255, exactly 255 i / 12); Luisa Winters (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sjayul5h-So, about 40:33; 7 copies, Start 100, End 11: the last flower .26 to .27 of copy 1 against i / 7's .272 and i / 6's .129). Two more could not tell (7 Minute AE Tutorials GVrc-S12elY, dots too small; Octopus Effects CFmKfBM-au4, 60 copies, the two rules within 1/60). Seven tutorials from six creators meets the bar for reopening an accepted decision and changing its stored values. **Accepted.** Copy i, from 0, has opacity start_opacity + (end_opacity - start_opacity) i / copies, copies being the setting itself at the frame shown, so the first copy is at the start opacity and the last stops one step short of the end, as After Effects' does; with copies 0 nothing is drawn. A fraction of a copy still draws the last copy at that fraction of its opacity (D-738 (c)), and because the ramp divides by copies itself, a copies key moving through a whole number moves the opacities smoothly. Nothing else of the repeater changes: placement, order, composite, the fraction of an offset. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing in the file: the file holds the start and end opacity as before, so every project opens and saves back byte for byte. A project with a repeater whose start and end opacity differ draws its later copies differently: with Start 100 and End 0 the last copy is now 1 / copies, no longer invisible, and each copy between moves toward the start by up to one step. A project whose start and end opacity are the same draws exactly as before. **Fixtures:** FX-SHPR-001 to 004's opacities in `Fixtures/shape_repeaters/expected_shape_repeaters.json` and document 25 are new, written by `tools/shape_repeater_reference.py` with the new rule (frame 0: Row's four squares 1, 0.8125, 0.625, 0.4375, where they were 1, 0.75, 0.5, 0.25); their points, order and stroke widths, FX-SHPR-005 and the refusals FX-SHPR-020 to 026 are unchanged; `host.json` is unchanged. The first values are retired, kept in the repository's history at commit 440cecf0. **Gaps.** (1) Every measured tutorial used Composite Below with the original copy at the start opacity; Above is taken to ramp the same way, not seen. (2) How After Effects ramps when copies is not a whole number is not seen in any source; ours divides by the setting itself. **If refused:** `tools/shape_repeater_reference.py` and the fixtures go back to commit 440cecf0's and the ramp to i / (count - 1); nothing in any file changes.

D-776 / Hue/Saturation gains After Effects' Colorize (wave 7, lane w7c; effects audit weak areas; an added After Effects control, the old look unchanged when it is off) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-24** under the owner's words "based off the artifact, work on the limited/unconfirmed/weak areas; also do a performance audit on all the effects that are heavy hitters, figure out gpu-acceleration (deep-research if you must to fully utilize it's power) or optimize on cpu if you must. follow more tutorials that utlize these effects or multiple effects to further confirm it's look, function, and relationship with others and the features of the app." Built as B-656. Hue/Saturation is a 1:1 After Effects effect (D-113); D-113 left Colorize out ("Not in this decision: After Effects' colorize option"), and the audit's weak-areas list (audit page https://claude.ai/artifact/A63KdY44N4HfUHzUnLQhTp) names it missing. **Why.** Colorize is a control After Effects' Hue/Saturation has and ours lacks; with it off, ours draws exactly as before, so one clear After Effects source is the bar. The source: Jake In Motion (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=76LQhG-nl_0, 2:24 to 2:48), Colorize checked on a photograph at its defaults Hue 0, Saturation 25, Lightness 0 (2:24), then Hue 80 (2:30), then Hue 180, Saturation 70, Lightness -4 (2:42, 2:48), with Master and Channel Control greyed out while it is checked. Thirteen points of the photograph were read in the tutorial's frames at those four settings (wave 3's contact sheet of the video; the video itself was behind a bot check this time and was not fetched) and against five candidate rules worked from the same points of the unchanged frame: keeping each pixel's HSL lightness, (max + min) / 2 of its encoded colour, and painting it the one hue and saturation meets After Effects within 2.0 levels of 255 at the median of 52 readings (mean 3.4; the largest, 21.6, on edges the half-size frame does not line up); Rec. 601 luma as the lightness is 19.6 at the median, Rec. 709 27.1, the mean of the three 15.7, and HSV's value 35.8. Frame+ (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TQwVJSUShPk) also shows the control, not measured. **Accepted.** Hue/Saturation gains `colorize`, "off" or "on", the word kept as written so a wrong one is reported, and `colorize_hue` (0 to 360 degrees), `colorize_saturation` (0 to 100) and `colorize_lightness` (-100 to 100), keyable, After Effects' defaults off, 0, 25 and 0. With Colorize on, each shown pixel's straight colour through the sRGB curve keeps its HSL lightness l, moved by `colorize_lightness` as the master lightness moves it (toward white by that share above 0, toward black below), and takes hue `colorize_hue` and saturation `colorize_saturation` / 100; the master hue, saturation and lightness and the six colour ranges are not used, as After Effects greys them out; the covering is kept and a pixel that does not show stays as it is. With Colorize on even at saturation 0 the layer changes (it turns grey at its own lightness). Effect Controls shows Colorize as an Off / On choice with its three numbers. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing for a project without the words: it reads Colorize as off and draws and saves back byte for byte. Each word is written only when it differs from its default (off, 0, 25, 0), is keyed, or was in the file. **Fixtures:** FX-HUESAT-027 to 032 and the refusals FX-HUESAT-033 to 036 are new, written by `tools/hue_saturation_reference.py`; FX-HUESAT-001 to 026 are unchanged. **Gaps.** (1) At 2:36 the panel reads Lightness 18 but the picture is the same as at 0, the scrub still under way; the rule for a raised Colorize Lightness is taken to be the master's, not seen settled. (2) One creator; After Effects' 16-bit and 32-bit handling of Colorize is not seen. **If refused:** the new fixtures and the reference's Colorize go back to commit 386183fe's and the build drops the four settings; projects without the words are untouched.

D-790 / An expression on a colour, a point or a word setting opens, is kept as written and is said (wave 7, lane w7f, after lane w7e's tutorial replay) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-24** under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-24: "based off the artifact, work on the limited/unconfirmed/weak areas; also do a performance audit on all the effects that are heavy hitters, figure out gpu-acceleration (deep-research if you must to fully utilize it's power) or optimize on cpu if you must. follow more tutorials that utlize these effects or multiple effects to further confirm it's look, function, and relationship with others and the features of the app." Built as B-670. **Why.** Lane w7e rebuilt Smertimba's soft neon glow (T4), where seven Drop Shadows' Color read a Color Control by `effect("Color Control")("Color")`. Our build refused the whole project on open (PROJECT_SCHEMA_INVALID): D-291 allowed an expression only on a setting of one number, and refused a file with one on a colour (a linear triple such as Tint's), a point (such as Twirl's Center) or a word (such as Drop Shadow's `#ff00f0`). Refusing the whole project for one setting is worse than document 28 asks: unknown or unsupported data is to be kept and said, not to stop the file opening. **How this sits with the bar.** Nothing accepted is reopened and no stored check value changes. This adds no look; it keeps a file that was refused and says what is not run, which is document 28's own rule (ADR-008). The tutorial is the After Effects source that such files exist. **Accepted.** (1) A project with an expression on an effect's colour, point or word setting opens. (2) The expression's text and its on/off switch are kept, and saving writes the setting's record back with the expression as read (`{"base", "keyframes", "expression"}`); a setting that had no keys is saved with an empty key list, as it was read. (3) The setting is drawn at its keys or its constant, exactly as the same file without the expression. (4) While the expression is on, every frame says `EXPRESSION_TYPE` naming the effect and the setting ("The expression on art's Drop Shadow color does not work at frame 0", detail: this build runs an expression only on a setting of one number, the expression is kept as written). Switched off, it is kept and nothing is said. (5) An export of a composition with such an expression on is refused with `EXPRESSION_TYPE`, as any failing expression's is (document 28: ERROR). **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing in a file that opened before. A file that was refused now opens, draws as without the expression, and saves the expression back. Keys inside a setting's record are written in sorted order, as every record of this build is; saving again gives the same bytes. **Fixtures:** none changed, none added. B-670's checks compare each frame with the frame of the same file without the expression, drawn by code that existed before D-790, and open D-291's own bands file `Fixtures/effect_mix/fx_mix_001.json` (a project from before D-790) and save it holding what it held. **Gaps.** (1) The expression is not run: Smertimba's neon draws each Drop Shadow at its own typed colour, not the Color Control's. Running colour and point expressions is its own decision, because the units are open: a Color Control gives linear values (document 09) while After Effects' expressions give sRGB-encoded ones, a word colour has no number slot to write the result into, and points' units differ between settings. Proposed, not built. (2) The app has no control to switch such an expression off or to edit it; the file keeps it and the frame notes say it. (3) An export is refused while one is on, so a project like the neon rig needs the expression removed or switched off in the file before export. **If refused:** such a project is refused on open again, as before D-790; nothing saved depends on it.

D-791 / Effects prepared from their own layer, on an adjustment layer: Audio Spectrum and Audio Waveform draw on the frame beneath, the rest say why they do not (wave 7, lane w7f, D-786 gap 2) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-24** under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-24: "based off the artifact, work on the limited/unconfirmed/weak areas; also do a performance audit on all the effects that are heavy hitters, figure out gpu-acceleration (deep-research if you must to fully utilize it's power) or optimize on cpu if you must. follow more tutorials that utlize these effects or multiple effects to further confirm it's look, function, and relationship with others and the features of the app." Built as B-671. **Why.** D-786's gap 2: the adjustment layer's stack is made again where it runs on the frame beneath (D-66), and that remaking skipped the steps that tell each effect its masks, sound or paths. Checked effect by effect on the bands of `Fixtures/effect_mix` under an adjustment layer with two masks drawn as paths only: Path Stroke, Vegas, Energy Stroke along masks, Audio Spectrum, Audio Waveform (on no mask too), Inner/Outer Key, Reshape, Mask Smear and Scribble were left out of the frame; Liquify drew without its Freeze Area Mask, Particle Playground without its Wall Mask, and Energy Stroke with Alpha Mode drew its beam uncut. None said anything (a silent fidelity fallback, which document 28 forbids). Energy Stroke between its points and Particle Playground with no wall already drew as on the layer itself. **How this sits with the bar.** Nothing accepted is reopened and no stored check value changes. D-420 and D-421 already say how the two sound effects hear a layer, and D-65 already says an adjustment layer's effects run on everything beneath as one picture; this entry makes the build do what they say together, as D-786 did for Fill. The rest only gain the warning document 28's EFFECT_PATH_MISSING row already names ("an adjustment layer has no masks to draw along"). **Accepted.** (1) On an adjustment layer, an Audio Spectrum or Audio Waveform with Path 0 hears its Audio Layer (or silence, with none) by D-420's and D-421's rule and draws on the frame beneath, mixed back by the adjustment layer's coverage and opacity as D-65 says; a missing or soundless Audio Layer is said every frame as on any layer. (2) On an adjustment layer, each of these says `EFFECT_PATH_MISSING` every frame ("Adjustment layer adj's Path Stroke works from a mask, a shape or the text of its own layer, which an effect on an adjustment layer cannot use yet", remedy: put the effect on the layer itself, or precompose the layers beneath and put it on the composition layer) and draws as before D-791: Path Stroke, Vegas and Scribble always; Energy Stroke along masks, shapes or text; Energy Stroke with Alpha Mode not Off (drawn uncut); Audio Spectrum and Audio Waveform with Path 1 or more; Inner/Outer Key with Foreground 1 or more; Reshape and Mask Smear naming any mask; Liquify with Freeze Area Mask 1 or more (drawn with nothing frozen); Particle Playground with Wall Mask 1 or more (drawn with no wall). (3) One that names nothing (Inner/Outer Key Foreground 0, Reshape or Mask Smear with no masks) does nothing and says nothing, as on any layer. The adjustment layer's own masks still shape where it applies (D-66). **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing in the file. A project saved before D-791 with an Audio Spectrum or Waveform on no mask on an adjustment layer now draws it where it drew nothing; every other case draws as before and now says so each frame. These effects on any other layer draw to the last digit as before (each one's own named test passes unchanged; they are listed in `verification/B-671_playtest.md`). **Fixtures:** none changed, none added. B-671's checks compare each adjustment-layer frame with the same effect on the layer itself, or with the file without what was left out, all drawn by code that existed before D-791, and open three projects from before it (`fx_aspec_002.json`, `fx_awave_002.json`, `fx_filladj_001.json`) and save them holding what they held. **Gaps.** (1) As D-786's gap 1, an adjustment layer's masks are not carried to the frame beneath as paths, so none of the effects in (2) draws on an adjustment layer; doing so under a moved or scaled adjustment layer is its own decision. (2) The load-time notes D-420, D-421 and D-613 give when a project opens are unchanged and still speak of a missing mask on the adjustment layer as on any layer. **If refused:** the two sound effects on an adjustment layer go back to drawing nothing, and the warnings go; nothing saved depends on it.

D-780 / The matte kit's box sums (Key Cleaner, Matte Choker, Refine Hard and Soft Matte) share their work across the processor's threads, the pixels bit for bit as before (wave 7, lane w7d, performance audit) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-24** under the owner's request of 2026-10-24: "also do a performance audit on all the effects that are heavy hitters, figure out gpu-acceleration (deep-research if you must to fully utilize it's power) or optimize on cpu if you must." Built as B-660. **Why.** W7's audit (`verification/W7_effect_performance_audit.md`) timed every effect at 1920 by 1080; Key Cleaner (about 240 to 330 ms a frame at Full), Matte Choker on the processor (93 to 303 ms; an export and 8 bpc always take it) and Refine Hard and Soft Matte (225 to 465 ms) were among the twenty slowest. All four go through `matte_refine::box_sum`, which summed down the columns of the whole picture on one thread and made two new lists for every row. **Accepted.** (1) The running totals down the columns are taken in bands of 256 numbers across, one band to a thread, each band keeping only the rows it still needs; every total is the same additions in the same order as before. (2) Each thread keeps its row lists from one row to the next instead of making them afresh. (3) The pixel loops around the box sums (reading and writing the layer, the edge region, the guides, decontamination) run per pixel on all threads; each pixel's arithmetic is unchanged. (4) Nothing else: no setting, no default, no card pass. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing. **Fixtures:** none changed. Evidence: `perf_audit_unchanged` hashes every effect's frame 30 at Full, as added and heavy, on the processor (its floats), on the card (its bytes) and in 8 bpc (its bytes), against `verification/W7_pixel_hashes.txt` taken at 440cecf0: all 369 rows are the same bit for bit; `b232_matte_refine` and `b383_key_cleaner` pass. Timing (5 alternating rounds, RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, 24-thread AMD64 Family 26 Model 68, release build, other lanes building): Final Render at Full, Key Cleaner 242.5 to 232.9 ms as added and 328.2 to 256.1 ms at radius 40; Matte Choker 93.4 to 71.8 and 303.1 to 232.9 ms. **Gaps.** (1) Refine Hard and Soft Matte did not get measurably faster (243.1 to 236.8, 225.0 to 243.4, 342.9 to 350.9 and 463.6 to 459.2 ms, inside the 6% the untouched rows moved): their time is in the guided filter's 13-number box sums, which are now bound by memory, not by the one thread. (2) Matte Choker on the card is unchanged (its own pass, about 20 to 57 ms). **If refused:** `matte_refine.rs` goes back to 440cecf0's; nothing saved depends on it.

D-781 / Caustics' blur reads the picture a row at a time going down, the pixels bit for bit as before (wave 7, lane w7d, performance audit) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-24** under the same request as D-780. Built as B-661. **Why.** Caustics (processor only) took 109 ms a frame at Full as added and 372 ms with Bottom Blur 40 (`verification/W7_effect_performance_audit.md`). Its Gaussian went down the columns one pixel at a time, each pixel reading every tap from a different row, so most of each read was thrown away. **Accepted.** (1) The downward pass now takes a whole row at a time and adds tap after tap of whole rows into it: every pixel still adds the same taps, with the same weights, in the same order. (2) The pass across, the tap weights, the held edges and everything else are unchanged; no setting, default or card pass. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing. **Fixtures:** none changed. Evidence: the 369-row hash check of D-780 (both Caustics rows the same bit for bit) and `b511_caustics` passes. Timing as D-780's: Final Render at Full 108.8 to 97.4 ms as added, 371.5 to 322.6 ms at Bottom Blur 40; the viewer at Full (Caustics has no card pass) 394.8 to 332.1 ms at Bottom Blur 40. **Gaps.** (1) The blur still does every tap (about 577 a pass at a large blur); a running box or an FFT would be much faster but adds in another order and moves the last bits, so it is proposed in D-783, not built. **If refused:** the old pass comes back; nothing saved depends on it.

D-782 / The motion finder behind Pixel Motion Blur and Timewarp shares its per-pixel steps across the processor's threads, the pixels bit for bit as before (wave 7, lane w7d, performance audit) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-24** under the same request as D-780. Built as B-662. **Why.** Pixel Motion Blur and Timewarp (processor only) were the two slowest effects in the audit: 188 to 273 ms and 189 to 442 ms a frame at Full. Both find motion with `flow::estimate`, several of whose per-pixel steps (the grey picture, the brightness match, the gradient products, the smoothing) ran on one thread. **Accepted.** (1) Those steps run per pixel on all threads; each pixel's arithmetic is unchanged, and the one sum (the mean brightness) stays a single pass in its old order. (2) Nothing else: no setting, default or card pass. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing. **Fixtures:** none changed. Evidence: the 369-row hash check (every Pixel Motion Blur and Timewarp row the same bit for bit), `b530_pixel_motion_blur`, `b531_timewarp` and `b264_flow_motion_griddler_fisheye` pass. Timing as D-780's: Final Render at Full, Pixel Motion Blur 188.0 to 166.5 ms as added and 273.4 to 259.1 ms heavy; Timewarp 189.1 to 159.7 and 442.3 to 393.1 ms; the viewer at Full 190.0 to 159.1, 313.4 to 288.9, 225.3 to 170.2 and 436.5 to 410.9 ms. **Gaps.** (1) The pyramid's warping and the per-level solve are still the bulk and still on the processor; a card motion finder is proposed in D-783, not built. **If refused:** `flow.rs` goes back to 440cecf0's; nothing saved depends on it.

D-783 / Speed trades that would move pixels, from W7's performance audit (wave 7, lane w7d) / **PROPOSED on 2026-10-24**, nothing built. W7's audit (`verification/W7_effect_performance_audit.md`, every effect at 1920 by 1080 on an RTX 4070 Ti SUPER and a 24-thread AMD64 Family 26 Model 68 processor, release build, a shared and busy machine) found these, each faster only by changing the picture; under D-222, D-229 and the rule that past-1-level, export-bytes and Draft-pixel changes stay proposed, each waits for the owner. No pixel difference was measured, because measuring one means building the change; each figure below is the measured cost today and the size of change expected. (1) **Scatterize on the card in f32.** Its card pass works in f64 and uploads a 56 MB f64 list a frame, so the viewer at Full takes 189.8 ms against the processor's 84.8 ms (the card is slower than the processor). In f32 the pass should fall to well under the processor's time; positions would move by up to about 1e-7 of a pixel, normally no level at all in 8-bit bytes, but not proven bit for bit. (2) **Curl Noise in single precision** (B-644's follow-up): viewer Full 64 to 65 ms, processor Full 91 to 115 ms; the field in f32 would change the last bits of the warp and, where a stroke sits on a pixel edge, possibly a level. (3) **Caustics' blur by a running box or an FFT** instead of every tap: Bottom Blur 40 still takes 322.6 ms a frame after B-661; either is a few tens of ms but adds in another order (about 1e-12 in f64, below one level). (4) **8 bpc (After Effects) frames on the card**: the card refuses 8 bpc (D-763), so every card effect falls to the processor there: Cartoon heavy 17.5 ms on the card against 447.1 ms in 8 bpc, Bilateral Blur 14.0 against 431.6, Matte Choker 57.2 against 274.7, Find Edges 40.8 against 516.6. The card would need D-763's per-step 8-bit rounding in every pass; where its float differs from the processor's by under a level the bytes match, elsewhere a level would move. (5) **A card motion finder** for Pixel Motion Blur and Timewarp (166.5 to 393.1 ms after B-662): f32 on the card would move the found motion slightly and so the drawn pixels. **If refused:** nothing changes; the audit stands as the record.

D-804 / The motion finder behind Pixel Motion Blur, Timewarp, Warp Stabilizer and Rolling Shutter Repair works in single precision, its found motion within 1e-4 px of double precision (wave 8, lane w8b; D-783's trade 5) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-25** under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-25: "nice; how many more effects need a speed/optimization audit; explore outside of effects and maybe the app's underlying architecture if we need to optimizat/speed up, change it in favor of both speed and visual precision, etc; also yes, let's do all five speed-ups, defer if the pixel cost is noticeably too much to AE/nuke/davinci resolve standards of optimization/visual practices. explore deeply the found, not built section, proceed with your recommendation/discretion." Built as B-685. **Why.** D-783 (5) proposed a card motion finder for Pixel Motion Blur and Timewarp, its cost "f32 ... would move the found motion slightly". The finder (`flow::estimate`, the pyramidal Lucas-Kanade pinned in `tools/flow_reference.py`) is nearly all of these effects' time. Its single-precision version was built and measured first, on the processor, because it is the arithmetic a card finder would do and it can be measured exactly against the double-precision rule. **The pixel cost, measured** (wave 8's bar: at 8 bpc at most 1 level on at least 99.9 % of pixels and at most 2 anywhere; in float at most 1e-4 on solid areas; no motion moved more than 0.05 px). Every fixture of the four effects at every frame, Full and Draft, and the reference shot (1920 by 1080, frames 0 to 210 every 30th, Full) with Pixel Motion Blur as added and heavy, Timewarp at speed 50 and heavy, Warp Stabilizer as added and Rolling Shutter Repair by Warp and by Pixel Motion: 100 % of pixels within 1 level, the largest 1 level; float at most 1.0e-6 on solid areas and 1.4e-6 anywhere; the found motion moved at most 8.95e-5 px, no vector of about 300 million more than 0.05 px. Every expected fixture value still holds (b530, b531, b532, b533, b264, the finder's own test). **Accepted.** (1) The finder's planes, pyramid, box sums, warps, gradient products, solve and smoothing work in 32-bit floats; the brightness match's two means are still summed in double precision in one ordered pass. (2) The field it gives the gather, the tween and the stabiliser's fit is double precision as before, converted at the end. (3) Nothing else: no setting, default, card pass or file field. **Speed** (RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, 24-thread AMD64 Family 26 Model 68 processor, release build, a shared machine with other lanes running; 7 alternating rounds, median of each, the reference shot frames 0 to 210 every 30th at Full on the processor): the finder alone 88.8 to 76.8 ms a frame for Pixel Motion Blur as added (1.16 times) and 81.6 to 65.9 ms for Timewarp at speed 50 (1.24 times); the whole frame 184.2 to 170.7 ms (1.08 times) and 182.6 to 166.2 ms (1.10 times). W7's viewer timing (5 alternating rounds) is within its noise on this machine, and its `(none)` row and Draft are no slower (CPU Draft 4.8 to 3.7 ms, Full 25.6 to 22.2 ms). The gain is small: the finder is held back by its per-level passes more than by its arithmetic's width. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing in the file; a file is saved back byte for byte. **How an old project looks afterwards:** a frame with one of the four effects may differ by 1 level on a few pixels; nothing moves by a visible amount. **Fixtures:** none changed. W7's hash record (`verification/W7_pixel_hashes.txt`, taken at 440cecf0) no longer holds bit for bit for the seven rows of these four effects, by design; the cost above replaces it for them, and the record is left as taken. **Gaps.** (1) The card finder itself is not built: D-805. (2) CC Wide Time does not use the finder (it repeats whole frames), so it shares nothing with this change. **If refused:** `src/flow.rs` goes back to B-684's double precision; nothing saved depends on it.

D-805 / A card motion finder for Pixel Motion Blur, Timewarp, Warp Stabilizer and Rolling Shutter Repair (wave 8, lane w8b; D-783's trade 5, continued) / **PROPOSED on 2026-10-25**, nothing built. D-804 measured the finder's pixel cost in single precision and it is far under the bar (at most 1 level, 8.95e-5 px of motion), so precision does not stand in the way. It is not built because it is a large change of its own: the effects run in the processor's compose step, which has no card; their neighbouring frames would have to be drawn and sent to the card; the finder needs card passes for the pyramid, the warps, the box sums and the per-level solve, and then a card gather and tween or a field read back. On the card the order of the sums would differ again, so its pixels would need the same measurement as D-804's. Expected: the finder from about 70 to 80 ms a frame to a few ms. **If refused:** nothing changes; the effects stay on the processor with D-804's finder. **Built as D-878 (wave 9, 2026-10-25).**

D-772 / Turbulent Noise's cell and contrast match After Effects': Scale 100 is Fractal Noise's 66.7-pixel cell, and the greys spread 0.64 times as far (audit page, "Turbulent Noise: size 1.4x, contrast 0.6x"; wave 7, lane w7b) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-24** under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-24: "based off the artifact, work on the limited/unconfirmed/weak areas; also do a performance audit on all the effects that are heavy hitters, figure out gpu-acceleration (deep-research if you must to fully utilize it's power) or optimize on cpu if you must. follow more tutorials that utlize these effects or multiple effects to further confirm it's look, function, and relationship with others and the features of the app." Turbulent Noise is a 1:1 effect (D-445: after After Effects' Turbulent Noise), so it is brought to After Effects' size and contrast in full; this reopens D-445's "size is the cell" and D-756's "Turbulent Noise is not changed", and moves older fixture values, so the bar was 7 agreeing tutorials. Built as B-652. Audit page: https://claude.ai/artifact/A63KdY44N4HfUHzUnLQhTp. **Why.** Wave 3 (lane J) found our Turbulent Noise about 1.4 times too coarse and about 1.6 times too contrasty against 3 creators, short of the bar. Wave 7 measured four more creators the same way, all in 8 bpc (D-763) on our side: the texture's correlation length (the distance at which the luminance autocorrelation falls to 0.5) and the luminance standard deviation, on a crop of the After Effects frame and on our frame at the same settings, in comp pixels. Ours over After Effects in size, and After Effects over ours in contrast: Manuel does Motion, https://youtu.be/WyHxDK45wmo at 0:33 (as added), 1.37 and 0.66; Angie Taylor, https://youtu.be/IWbIiTE9UhE at 1:02 (as added, over footage for an old-film look), 1.48 and 0.56; Crish Design, https://youtu.be/MMr3fjGRZ2Y at 0:54 to 1:02 (spoken: "I need to double the contrast to about 200 to get a very similar starting point" beside Fractal Noise; a relative reading), 1.43 and 0.49; Jake In Motion, https://youtu.be/kdttSozSLG4 at 4:36 (as added), 1.36 and 0.68 (1.48 and 0.56 read against his Fractal Noise beside it); ECAbrams, https://youtu.be/3QOUmiHxA7c at 3:38 (as added), 1.51 and 0.64; Mike Murphy, https://youtu.be/zu4Kw1EwTbs at 1:40 (inverted, used as a matte), 1.40 and 0.69; Opal, https://youtu.be/qemjeZgadkE at 0:44 (as added) and 0:52 (Contrast 80, Brightness -9), 1.38 and 0.63 (0.65 at Contrast 80). Seven of seven sources from seven creators agree: size 1.36 to 1.51, median 1.43, inside the 1.5 of D-756 within the reading's error; contrast 0.49 to 0.69, median 0.64. A stand-in before the build (our Turbulent Noise at Size 66.7 and Contrast 64) matched After Effects: ECAbrams length 25.5 against 25.8 and spread 15.9 against 16.3; Opal 28.4 against 28.3 and 16.0 against 16.4; Opal at Contrast 80, Brightness -9 mean 106 against 103 and spread 12.9 against 13.2. **Accepted.** Turbulent Noise's cell is c = size / 1.5, Fractal Noise's own (D-756): pixel (X, Y) samples ((X + 0.5 - offset x) / (c scale_width / 100), (Y + 0.5 - offset y) / (c scale_height / 100), evolution / 360), so Size 100 at Scale 100 draws After Effects' 66.7-pixel cell. Its grey is v = 0.5 + 0.5 n 0.64 contrast / 100 + brightness / 100: Contrast 100 spreads the greys 0.64 times as far as before, and every other contrast in proportion. Every other part of the rule is unchanged: the octaves, the types, invert, brightness, evolution, the Transform and Sub Settings, Overflow, opacity and every blend. On the processor and the card alike: both apply at Turbulent Noise's own entry into Fractal Noise's engine, and Fractal Noise itself is not changed. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing in the file: `size`, `contrast` and every other setting are read and written as before, so a file is saved back byte for byte. **How an old project looks afterwards:** every Turbulent Noise draws its clouds at two thirds of the size it drew before D-772 (about 2.25 times as many cells on the same layer) and with flatter greys, closer to the middle grey; brightness and the character are the same. To get the old look back, multiply Size by 1.5 (up to its limit of 1000) and Contrast by 1.5625 (up to 1000). Nothing is silently replaced: a setting outside its range is refused as before (EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, D-46). **Fixtures.** `tools/turbulent_noise_reference.py` works c = size / CELL with CELL = 1.5 (Fractal Noise's) and CONTRAST = 0.64; `tools/turbulent_noise_types_reference.py`, `tools/turbulent_more_reference.py` and `tools/turbulent_blends_reference.py` follow it, and their checks now compare Turbulent Noise with Fractal Noise at Contrast 64 and the same size. The project files are unchanged; the expected frames below move and their first values are retired, kept in the repository's history at commit 440cecf0 (pixels moved of 160 a frame, summed over a case's frames): FX-TURBNOISE-001 270; 002 to 008 135 each; 009 132; 010 135; 012 135; 013 405; 014 to 017 135 each; 018 and 019 131; 020 135; 021 270; 022 216; 032 127; 033 132; 034 to 036 135 each; 037 405; 038 to 048 135 each; 049 127; 050 131; 051 92; 052 73; 053 135; 054 108; 055 135; 063 and 064 135; 065 and 066 160; 069 and 070 135; 072 270; FX-TURBTYPE-001 to 008 135 each; 009 92; 010 134; 011 to 018 135 each; 019 405; 020 112; 021 and 022 135; 023 216. The largest move is 1.0 (a pixel now held at the other end of the ramp) in FX-TURBNOISE-001 to 060, 0.509 in 061 to 074 and 0.973 in FX-TURBTYPE. Unchanged: FX-TURBNOISE-011 (brightness -100), the invalid 023 to 031 and 056 to 060, the blends 061, 062, 067, 068, 071, 073 and 074, and the invalid FX-TURBTYPE-024 and 025; no Fractal Noise, Turbulent Displace or Roughen Edges fixture moves. Document 25 gives the counts; document 21's Turbulent Noise rule now reads c = size / 1.5 and 0.64 contrast. **Gaps.** The 0.64 is measured against today's Fractal Noise engine, whose own contrast at Sub Influence 70 and Sub Scaling 56 reads about 0.82 of After Effects' (Likely, about 6 sources, not built); if that is fixed later, Turbulent Noise's factor would become about 0.53 so its look stays After Effects'. The measures are on as-added Basic and Smooth noise mostly; the types (D-567) follow by the same factors, not each one measured. Masks, track mattes and blending over footage (Angie Taylor, Mike Murphy) read the same as the plain layer; Max and Dynamic types read differently from After Effects (Likely, 2 to 3 creators) and are not addressed here. **If refused:** c goes back to the size and the contrast factor to 1, the four reference tools and the four expected files go back to their values at 440cecf0, and every project draws as before; a file saved in the meantime holds nothing new, so it reads back unchanged.

D-820 / An expression runs on an effect's colour and point, and reads any effect's setting by its name or number (wave 8, lane w8e; the holds D-790 left) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-25** under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-25: "nice; how many more effects need a speed/optimization audit; explore outside of effects and maybe the app's underlying architecture if we need to optimizat/speed up, change it in favor of both speed and visual precision, etc; also yes, let's do all five speed-ups, defer if the pixel cost is noticeably too much to AE/nuke/davinci resolve standards of optimization/visual practices. explore deeply the found, not built section, proceed with your recommendation/discretion." Built as B-700. **Why.** D-790 let a project with an expression on a colour, a point or a word open, but kept the expression unrun and said EXPRESSION_TYPE every frame, and D-766 let an expression read only the six Expression Controls; any other effect's setting was EXPRESSION_SYNTAX. Lane w7e's replay of Smertimba's soft neon glow drives seven Drop Shadows' Color from one Color Control, the ordinary After Effects rig, and drew none of it. After Effects' own source is Adobe's expression language reference (https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/using/expression-language-reference.html): `effect(name)(name or index)` reads any effect's property, a colour is an array of four, red, green, blue and alpha, and a point property is in the layer's own pixels. **How this sits with the bar.** Nothing accepted is reopened. One stored check value changes, the FX-EXPR-019 row that pinned the old refusal (below). Every expression on a number setting gives what it gave (FX-EXPR-001 to 020, B-176 and B-14b pass unchanged). **Accepted.** (1) A colour, the three linear numbers a setting named `color` holds (Tint, Color Control and the rest), reads and is written as four numbers, red, green, blue and alpha, in this build's linear numbers; the alpha written is not kept. Three numbers for a colour is EXPRESSION_TYPE, as After Effects' "must be of dimension 4" is. This is the one place this build differs from After Effects on purpose: After Effects' numbers are in the project's colour space (sRGB in an 8-bit project), but FX-EXPR-017 already pins the Color Control's colour as its linear numbers (`[2] + [3]` is 1.75), so every colour here is linear alike. Pure colours (`[1, 0, 0, 1]`) are the same either way; a mid grey typed as `[0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 1]` is sRGB 188 here and 128 in After Effects. (2) A colour word (`"#rrggbb"`, sRGB, as Fill, Drop Shadow and their kin hold it) reads as the linear numbers of its 8-bit codes by the sRGB transfer, alpha 1, and is written back as the nearest 8-bit codes, which is all the word holds. (3) A point the file holds as per cent of the layer's width and height (a two-number setting held in -1000 to 1000 or -400 to 500; all 144 such settings found in the fixtures say per cent on the page) reads and is written in the layer's pixels, per cent times the drawing's width or height over 100, the drawing being the layer's picture as its effects run (for an adjustment layer, the composition). Reading another layer's per-cent point is EXPRESSION_TYPE, because that layer's drawing is not known where the expression runs; a drawing of no size is EXPRESSION_TYPE too. (4) Every other setting of up to four numbers reads and is written as the numbers it holds (pixel offsets, Point Control, a noise's centre); a checkbox as 1 or 0. (5) A choice from a list stays held and said as D-790 has it (EXPRESSION_TYPE): this build's word lists are not After Effects' menus item for item, so After Effects' 1-based menu number cannot be mapped cleanly. (6) `effect(name or number)(name or number)` reads any effect's setting, on this layer or, through `thisComp.layer(...)`, another, with `.value` and `.valueAtTime(t)`: by its name in the file (`"sigma_px"`), that name as After Effects writes names (`"Sigma Px"`), four of After Effects' own names (Drop Shadow's Shadow Color, Glow's Glow Threshold, Glow Radius and Glow Intensity), or a number counting this build's settings from 1, in the order the page lists them, which can differ from After Effects' (Gaussian Blur's 1 is its sigma; After Effects' is Blurriness). The value read is after that setting's own expression, held in its range. A setting that reads itself through others is EXPRESSION_CYCLE, more than 16 deep EXPRESSION_TIMEOUT, and a name or number the effect does not have EXPRESSION_REFERENCE_MISSING. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing in the file. A project saved before D-820 with a switched-on expression on a colour, a point or a colour word now draws what the expression gives; one whose expression gives the wrong count of numbers draws as before and still says EXPRESSION_TYPE. **Fixtures:** FX-EXPR-019's row `effect("Gaussian Blur")(1)`, 0, EXPRESSION_SYNTAX, becomes two rows, `effect("Gaussian Blur")("Blurriness")` and `effect("Gaussian Blur")(2)`, each 0, EXPRESSION_REFERENCE_MISSING; FX-EXPR-017 gains `effect("Gaussian Blur")(1)` (2 at every frame), `effect("Gaussian Blur")("sigma_px") * 10` (20) and `effect("Gaussian Blur")("Sigma Px").valueAtTime(0)` (2). All from `tools/expression_reference.py`, whose project files are unchanged (`--check`). **Gaps.** (1) The Effect Controls readout beside a keyed per-cent point with an expression measures the point against the composition's size, as do the runs that only ask whether an expression fails (the export's check); a layer not the composition's size can show there a number other than the one it draws with. (2) Menus, as (5). (3) Gaussian Blur's After Effects name Blurriness is not taken as an alias, because this build's blur holds Blurriness only when its Units say so (D-321). (4) After Effects' colour numbers in the project's colour space, as (1). **If refused:** expressions on colours, points and words go back to D-790's hold, and `effect(...)` back to Expression Controls only; nothing saved depends on it.

D-821 / The notes beside the frame say an effect that cannot find its mask, shape or text (wave 8, lane w8e) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-25** under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-25 (quoted with D-820). Built as B-701. **Why.** D-767 put a failed expression's warning beside the frame (`x-frame-notes`), with D-263's missing font. D-786 and D-791 made an effect on an adjustment layer that cannot use the masks, shapes or text it names say EFFECT_PATH_MISSING every frame, but the window passed only the font and expression warnings beside the frame, so the owner saw a Fill filling nothing with no word beside it; the warning reached only the log. **How this sits with the bar.** Nothing accepted is reopened and no stored check value changes; document 28 already says a warning is shown where the work is. **Accepted.** The notes beside the frame also carry every EFFECT_PATH_MISSING the frame says, the warning D-786's and D-791's effects on an adjustment layer give and the one an effect on any layer gives when the mask it names is not there, its sentence then its code, as the others are. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing. **Fixtures:** none changed, none added; B-701's app test opens D-786's FX-FILLADJ-007, 008 and 001. **If refused:** the notes go back to fonts and expressions only.

D-800 / Caustics' wide blurs go through an FFT, the same taps summed in another order, the pixels bit for bit as before (D-783 (3); wave 8, lane w8a) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-25** under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-25: "nice; how many more effects need a speed/optimization audit; explore outside of effects and maybe the app's underlying architecture if we need to optimizat/speed up, change it in favor of both speed and visual precision, etc; also yes, let's do all five speed-ups, defer if the pixel cost is noticeably too much to AE/nuke/davinci resolve standards of optimization/visual practices. explore deeply the found, not built section, proceed with your recommendation/discretion." The bar set for the five trades: at 8 bits at most 1 level on at least 99.9 per cent of pixels and at most 2 levels anywhere, a float error at most 1e-4 on solid areas, and no shape, edge or motion shift over 0.05 px. Built as B-680. **Why.** After B-661, Caustics with Bottom Blur 40 still took about 320 ms a frame at Full, because its Gaussian adds every tap (463 at sigma 76.8, Bottom Blur 40 on a 1920-wide layer) for every pixel, across then down. **Accepted.** (1) When the blur's radius is over 48 pixels, each held-out line (the outer pixel repeated r times at both ends, as before) is convolved with the same normalised taps through a radix-2 FFT in double precision, two channels a transform, across then down (`layer_fx::caustics_gaussian`). The taps, the held edges, sigma = Bottom Blur x width / 1000, and the result's place are unchanged; only the order of the sums changes, which moves a sum by under 1e-12 (tested), far below the picture's single precision. (2) A radius of 48 or less keeps the direct taps, so Smoothing as added (sigma 9.6, radius 29) and every Draft blur under radius 48 are the old arithmetic exactly. (3) No setting, default or card pass. A running box was not taken: three boxes are not a Gaussian (a visible shape change) and the FFT needs no trade. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing. **Fixtures:** none changed. **Evidence** (B-680): `perf_audit_pixels` (frame 30 at Full, before c4b0696c against after) finds 0 pixels changed and a float error of 0.00 on the processor, the card's viewer and 8 bpc, as added and at Bottom Blur 40 (`verification/B-680_caustics_pixel_table.md`); `d800_fft_blur_is_the_tap_sum` (sigma 8.4 to 96, 4 channels and 1, odd sizes) under 1e-12; `b511_caustics` passes; the 369-row hash check of D-780, run on the before and the after build, has every row but Scatterize's card (D-801) the same bit for bit. Timing, 5 alternating rounds on a busy shared machine (RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, 24-thread AMD64 Family 26 Model 68, release build): Bottom Blur 40 at Full 467.2 to 202.8 ms a frame in the final render, 463.8 to 189.4 in the viewer, 645.4 to 323.9 in 8 bpc, the after build faster in every round (0.37 to 0.58 of before); as added the change is within the load's noise, as expected (the blur stays direct). **Gaps.** (1) Most of Bottom Blur 40's remaining time is the rest of Caustics (the surface's refraction and light), not the blur. (2) The FFT is on the processor only; Caustics still has no card pass. **If refused:** the FFT goes and every blur takes the direct taps again; nothing saved depends on it.

D-801 / Scatterize on the card works in single precision from a compact list, at most 1 level on a handful of pixels (D-783 (1); wave 8, lane w8a) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-25** under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-25 quoted in D-800, within the bar given there. Built as B-681. **Why.** Scatterize's card pass worked in f64, which the RTX 4070 Ti SUPER runs slowly, and read a 56 MB f64 list a frame, so the viewer at Full took about 190 to 250 ms against the processor's 85 to 130: the card was slower than the processor. **Accepted.** (1) The card's list is now three single-precision numbers an entry, one entry per dot per 16 by 16 tile it can cover, in each tile farthest first as before: the dot's centre from the tile's corner (small numbers, held to about 1e-6 of a pixel) and the source pixel's index as exact bits; the tile starts stay in the f64 parameter list. (2) The pass reads those, works the distance, the weight 1 - distance and the four transfer modes in single precision, which is how the card keeps the picture anyway. (3) The list is built on all the processor's threads. (4) The processor's Scatterize, which an export and Final Render draw, is unchanged, bit for bit. No setting or default changes. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing in the file. **How an old project looks afterwards:** in the viewer on the card, a pixel where a dot's weight falls on a rounding edge can round one level the other way: 2 of 2,073,600 pixels at frame 30 of the reference shot, each by 1 level; the export does not change at all. **Fixtures:** none changed. `verification/D-676_scatterize_table.md`, which `b555_scatterize` writes, is re-taken: the card against the processor is still at most 1 level, with about 70 more 1-level pixels a frame (for example 1304 to 1376 of 2,073,600). **Evidence** (B-681): `perf_audit_pixels`, frame 30 at Full, before c4b0696c against after: the card's viewer 2 pixels changed, largest 1 level, 100.0000 per cent within 1 level, 0 over 2; the processor and 8 bpc 0 changed, float error 0.00 (`verification/B-681_scatterize_pixel_table.md`). A move in single precision of about 1e-6 of a pixel is far under the 0.05 px bar. `b555_scatterize` passes. The 369-row hash check of D-780, run on the before and the after build, has 368 rows the same bit for bit, the one other being this row's card picture, so no effect sharing the card's code moved. Timing, the same 5 alternating rounds as D-800: the viewer on the card at Full 250.8 to 109.5 ms a frame (0.27 to 0.55 of before in every round), Draft 35.1 to 30.4 (within the noise); the card's own drawing stage 205 to 227 ms down to 28.6 ms over 4 calls. **Gaps.** (1) Building and sending the list is now most of the card's time and swings widely under load; building it on the card would remove it. (2) The viewer at Full is now about as fast as the processor's 115.8 ms, not much faster. **If refused:** the f64 pass and list come back; nothing saved depends on it.

D-802 / Curl Noise on the card in single precision, not built: no speed gained and a 2-level move (D-783 (2); wave 8, lane w8a) / **PROPOSED on 2026-10-25** under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-25 quoted in D-800: "defer if the pixel cost is noticeably too much". **Why proposed.** B-644's follow-up was to work Curl Noise's field on the card in f32 instead of f64. It was built and measured (the code kept outside the repository as a diff, `D-802_curl_f32_card.diff` in the lane's scratch folder) and fails both halves of the trade. **Speed:** 2 alternating rounds, viewer on the card at Full, 73.1 to 74.2 ms a frame as added and 70.1 to 61.9 at Softness 40 and Flow Softness 40; the card's drawing stage 121.9 to 107.9 ms over 4 calls, 0 to 12 per cent. The time is in the lattice hashing of the value noise (8 corners, 2 lattices, about 144 noise reads a pixel), which is already single precision; the f64 parts were not the cost. **Pixels:** the viewer moved by at most 1 level at frame 30, but `b326_curl_noise`'s card-against-processor check found 2 levels (one pixel row at size 20, swirl 120, frame 239, Full: 259 against 260 across the row), over its 1-level rule and at the bar's limit. **Proposed:** keep Curl Noise's card pass as it is. A real gain would need fewer noise reads a pixel (sharing the lattice between neighbours), which changes no arithmetic and could be a later speed change. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing. **Fixtures:** none. **If accepted as built anyway:** the diff applies to `src/gpu.rs`, and `b326_curl_noise`'s rule would have to accept 2 levels; not recommended. **If refused:** nothing changes.

D-812 / An export that blocks on a missing drawing draws each frame once (wave 8, lane w8d; the app's architecture beyond single effects) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-25** under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-25: "nice; how many more effects need a speed/optimization audit; explore outside of effects and maybe the app's underlying architecture if we need to optimizat/speed up, change it in favor of both speed and visual precision, etc; also yes, let's do all five speed-ups, defer if the pixel cost is noticeably too much to AE/nuke/davinci resolve standards of optimization/visual practices. explore deeply the found, not built section, proceed with your recommendation/discretion." A change of speed only: every file and every report an export writes is the old build's byte for byte, so the pixel bar is met at zero. Built as B-692. **Why.** Document 07's default for a final export is to block on a missing drawing and write nothing before that is known. Until now the export planned every frame of the range to look for missing drawings (which reads and decodes every drawing), threw the plans away, and then planned, drew and encoded every frame a second time to write it. Wave 8's measurement (`tests/w8_arch_audit.rs`, release build, RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, Ryzen 9 9900X) found a blocking export took 1.0 to 2.2 times what the same export took with the missing drawing written transparent (which does not look first), on every shot measured: the reference shot 820 against 577 ms for 8 frames, 25 layers 6355 against 3446, 4K 4895 against 2906, Noise into Polar Coordinates 3491 against 1946. Blocking is the default, so this is every final export a user makes. **Accepted.** The check plans the range in the same chunks as before (D-231, frames side by side). When every plan in a chunk is whole (no missing drawing, no failed plan) and the files kept so far are under 1 GiB, the chunk is drawn and encoded at once from those plans, as `compose::render_frame` draws it, and its files are kept in memory; the frame's records are replayed into the check's log and into the frame's own log exactly as they were before, so the report says the same. Once the range is known whole the kept files are written in order; a frame not kept (past 1 GiB, or in or after a chunk with a missing drawing) is planned and drawn again when written, as before. A blocked export therefore costs what it did (it plans only, and stops), and a kept PNG that must be encoded again with the job's fidelity mark (an earlier frame logged a bypassed effect against it) draws its frame again, since the kept frame holds its file and not its picture. Nothing in a project or on screen changes; the window's progress counter does not move during the check, which now holds most of the work, and then runs quickly through the kept frames. **Measured.** The reference shot's frames 0 to 13 as 8-bit PNG, blocking, median of 7 alternating rounds: 1312 ms before, 899 after (32 per cent less), against 1087 for the same export writing the missing transparent; frames 0 to 47, which block (frames 14, 15, 38 and 39 miss a drawing), 904 before and 946 after (the same within the machine's spread). **Checked.** B-692 exports the reference shot (8-bit PNG, 16-bit premultiplied PNG, EXR half, GIF, animated PNG) and every composition of every fixture project in `Fixtures/` (8678 exports, 83202 files and reports) on the old build and the new, and every SHA-256 is the same. **Fixtures.** None is added or changed. **If refused:** the check goes back to planning only and every frame is drawn when written; every file stays the same.

D-813 / Drop Shadow and Rim Light blur the covering's alpha alone (wave 8, lane w8d; effect chains, the 7 Drop Shadows shot) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-25** under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-25: "nice; how many more effects need a speed/optimization audit; explore outside of effects and maybe the app's underlying architecture if we need to optimizat/speed up, change it in favor of both speed and visual precision, etc; also yes, let's do all five speed-ups, defer if the pixel cost is noticeably too much to AE/nuke/davinci resolve standards of optimization/visual practices. explore deeply the found, not built section, proceed with your recommendation/discretion." A change of speed only: every result is the old build's to the bit, so the pixel bar is met at zero. Built as B-693. **Why.** Wave 8's measurement of effect chains found the tutorial shot with seven Drop Shadows the slowest frame on the processor (about 0.9 to 1.2 s at 32 bpc). Both Drop Shadow and Rim Light read only the alpha of their blurred covering, yet each copied the whole drawing, set its colour to nought and blurred all four channels: three quarters of the blur's sums were of zeros. **Accepted.** On the processor (`layer_fx::drop_shadow` and `layer_fx::rim_light`) the covering is the drawing's alpha, one number a pixel, blurred by the same separable Gaussian (`effects::convolve`, now written for any number of channels and used with one), in the same order of sums, then read with the same bilinear weights in the same order as `sample_bilinear` read it. The rule in document 21 (sigma softness / 5 for Drop Shadow, softness / 3 for Rim Light, the radius, the bilinear read, Opacity, Shadow Only, the blend) is unchanged, and so is the card's Drop Shadow and Rim Light. **Measured** (release, RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, Ryzen 9 9900X, other lanes building; alternating rounds against c4b0696c): one Drop Shadow (softness 40, distance 12) on a 1920 by 1080 drawing 25.2 ms before and 11.7 after, one Rim Light (width 4, softness 3) 17.1 and 7.6 (medians of 15); the seven Drop Shadows shot drawn whole (`compose::render_frame`) at 32 bpc 934 ms before and 305 after, at 8 bpc 304 and 212, and at Draft 32 bpc 1487 and 254 (medians of 5); the reference shot with no effect, 104 and 100 (7 rounds, the same). **Checked.** 504 results (three drawings under 96 Drop Shadows and 72 Rim Lights spanning every setting) hash the same on the old build and the new, and B-692's 8678 exports of every fixture composition are the same with this change in. **Fixtures.** None is added or changed. **If refused:** the covering goes back to a four-channel copy of the drawing with its colour set to nought; every picture stays the same.

D-822 / An expression's colours are After Effects' numbers: 0 to 1 sRGB, linear only where After Effects' Linearize Working Space would be on (wave 8, lane w8e) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-25** under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-25: "nice; how many more effects need a speed/optimization audit; explore outside of effects and maybe the app's underlying architecture if we need to optimizat/speed up, change it in favor of both speed and visual precision, etc; also yes, let's do all five speed-ups, defer if the pixel cost is noticeably too much to AE/nuke/davinci resolve standards of optimization/visual practices. explore deeply the found, not built section, proceed with your recommendation/discretion." The owner asked for colours in expressions to be 1 to 1 with After Effects, so a tutorial typing `[1, 0.5, 0, 1]` gives After Effects' orange. This reopens D-820's colour rule (linear numbers) and changes one stored check value. Built as B-702. **Why.** D-820 read and wrote an expression's colour in this build's stored linear numbers, so `[1, 0.5, 0, 1]` on a Fill gave #ffbc00 rather than After Effects' #ff8000 and a Color Control read 0.5 where After Effects reads about 0.735. After Effects gives colour values to an expression as four numbers 0 to 1 (Dan Ebberts, Creative COW, https://creativecow.net/forums/thread/random-change-to-specific-color/), and they are the working space's numbers: with Linearize Working Space off they are the picker's sRGB numbers, and with it on they are linear, so the same colour shows other numbers (https://creativecow.net/forums/thread/when-working-in-a-linear-32-bit-floating-point-wor/, https://community.adobe.com/questions-529/after-effects-colors-are-off-71477, and Adobe's colour management page https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/using/color-management.html). Adobe's own pages do not state the linearized case for expressions in so many words; it is read from those threads, so it is held as likely. **Accepted.** In Display, 8 bpc and AE 32 bpc (none of which is After Effects with Linearize Working Space on) a colour setting reads in an expression as sRGB's transfer of its stored linear numbers, unclamped, and a colour an expression gives is turned back by the inverse transfer; a colour word reads its 8-bit codes over 255 and is written by rounding each number to 8 bits after holding it to 0 to 1. In Float without AE 32 bpc (After Effects' Linearize Working Space) colours stay D-820's linear numbers. The depth is the composition the expression is in; a nested composition whose pixels follow an outer Float composition still reads its own depth's numbers, a gap recorded in the code. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing is rewritten: a colour typed in an expression keeps its text and now gives After Effects' colour; a Color Control linked into a Fill or Tint gives the same colour as before, as the transfer goes out and back. **Fixtures:** FX-EXPR-017's Color Control row moved from 1.75 to 1.8808250210902997 in each of its four frames; the first values are retired and kept in the history at commit d336cf47. No other value moved (`tools/expression_reference.py` printed every other row as before). **If refused:** colours go back to D-820's linear numbers.

D-828 / A layer's Preserve Underlying Transparency, After Effects' T switch (wave 8, lane w8f; wave 7's "Found, not built": the T switch; an added After Effects switch, the old look unchanged when it is off) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-25** under the owner's words. On 2026-10-25 the owner wrote: "nice; how many more effects need a speed/optimization audit; explore outside of effects and maybe the app's underlying architecture if we need to optimizat/speed up, change it in favor of both speed and visual precision, etc; also yes, let's do all five speed-ups, defer if the pixel cost is noticeably too much to AE/nuke/davinci resolve standards of optimization/visual practices. explore deeply the found, not built section, proceed with your recommendation/discretion." Built as B-708. **Why.** After Effects' timeline has a T switch on every layer that draws, Preserve Underlying Transparency; ours had none, so a tutorial that uses it could only be stood in for with a track matte (wave 7's Ben Marriott smoke rig, lane w7e). It is a missing After Effects switch and, off, everything draws exactly as before, so one clear After Effects source is the bar. The source: After Effects' help, "Track mattes and traveling mattes" (helpx.adobe.com, its section on Preserve Underlying Transparency; the page itself returned 403 to the fetch and was read through the search engine's copy, not bypassed): "the opaque areas of the layer appear only when positioned over opaque areas in underlying layers ... similar to the behavior of a clipping mask in Adobe Photoshop". The tutorial: Ben Marriott, "2D Smoke & Explosions" (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w8mHmW6GgHM), 7:42 "turn on preserve underlying transparency so now it is going to only cover up our explosion area", then Multiply at 7:47; the panel at 9:45 shows the Multiply noise solid with the switch on. ProVideoCoalition's "CMG Hidden Gems" chapter 12 (stencils and the T) says the same. **Accepted.** A layer gains `preserve_transparency`, true or false. With it on the layer is drawn "atop" what is beneath it: document 21's blend equation without the layer's own term over nothing, `(1-Ad) Cs`, and the alpha beneath kept, `Co = (1-As) Cd + As Ad B`, `Ao = Ad`; for Normal `Cs Ad + Cd (1-As)`. Every blend mode takes it, in every depth. The track matte cuts the layer first and the opacity scales it, as without the switch; a matte-only layer is not part of what is beneath. Stencil Alpha and Stencil Luma draw nothing of their own, so the switch changes nothing on them. A null or adjustment layer has no switch, as After Effects shows none: a file that sets it on one is refused with the reason (document 28, no silent fallback), and so is the command. The timeline gains a T column after Mode, one button per layer that draws, sending `layer.toggle_preserve_transparency` (document 24), undoable. The card draws it in the same blend pass (Normal, Multiply, Screen, Add), within 1 level; the other modes stay on the CPU as before. A clear layer changes nothing, so the tile and box limits still hold. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing for a project without the word: it reads the switch off on every layer, draws as before and saves back byte for byte. `preserve_transparency: true` is written only on a layer that has it on. An older build opening a file with the word keeps it as an unknown word and draws the layer without the switch. **Fixtures:** FX-PRESERVE-001 to 008 (drawn) and 020 and 021 (refused) are new, written by `tools/preserve_transparency_reference.py`; no old fixture changes. **Evidence of the build** (B-708): every fixture within 2e-5 (largest 6.9e-8); the card within 1 level; on w7e's rebuild of the smoke rig, 8 bpc frame 7, the switch on the noise solid matches the matte stand-in on all but 0.044% of pixels (the partly covered cloud edges, where the two rules differ by design), and against the old app on the same file, which drew noise across the whole frame (7.7% white, 290 white pieces), it keeps the noise to the clouds as After Effects' 9:45 does (After Effects 2.0% white; ours 1.7%). **Gaps.** (1) After Effects breaks the strokes into more pieces (24 against our 5): the rebuild's noise and cloud timing, not the switch, which the stand-in shares. (2) After Effects' help page was read through a search engine's copy. (3) After Effects also lets T sit on a layer with a stencil above it and on a 3D layer; ours follows the same rule there without a separate check. **If refused:** the build drops the switch, the column and the command, and the FX-PRESERVE fixtures and the reference go; a project saved with the word is refused by name rather than drawn differently.

D-829 / Drop Shadow's softness up to 2000, as After Effects' panel takes it (wave 8, lane w8f; wave 7's "Found, not built": softness above 500; a wider range for an After Effects control, the look of every value already taken unchanged) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-25** under the owner's words. On 2026-10-25 the owner wrote: "nice; how many more effects need a speed/optimization audit; explore outside of effects and maybe the app's underlying architecture if we need to optimizat/speed up, change it in favor of both speed and visual precision, etc; also yes, let's do all five speed-ups, defer if the pixel cost is noticeably too much to AE/nuke/davinci resolve standards of optimization/visual practices. explore deeply the found, not built section, proceed with your recommendation/discretion." Built as B-709. **Why.** Ours stopped Drop Shadow's Softness at 500 and refused more (EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID, the effect kept and left out of the frame); After Effects takes more. Wave 7's rebuild of Smertimba's neon glow (lane w7e) had to hold two of its seven shadows at 500, and the glow's far tail came out short. Values 0 to 500 draw exactly as before, so this is a missing reach of an After Effects control and one clear After Effects source is the bar. The source: Smertimba, "soft neon glow with drop shadows" (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gsihkt5sO2w): softness 1000 typed at 1:56 and 2000 at 2:03, and the Effect Controls panel at 2:16 reading Drop Shadow 6 Softness 1000.0 and Drop Shadow 7 Softness 2000.0. **Accepted.** `softness` runs 0 to 2000; the rule is unchanged, sigma softness / 5 (D-774), so 2000 is sigma 400. The Effect Controls hint reads "pixels, 0 to 2000" and the field takes it typed or dragged. The card draws it as before, within 1 level. The text layer's own shadow (the Character panel's) keeps its 0 to 500, a separate control not asked about. **What it costs** (B-709, this machine, release build, a 960 by 200 white title in a 1920 by 1080 frame, distance 20, median of 3): softness 100, CPU 11 / card 10 ms; 500, 31 / 28 ms; 1000, 49 / 58 ms; 2000, 106 / 139 ms. Twenty times the radius costs about ten times the time and stays near a tenth of a second at the top, so no lower-quality shortcut (a blur on a smaller copy, or on the alpha only) was needed; none was made. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing for a file with softness 0 to 500: it reads, draws and saves as before. A file with softness 501 to 2000 was read with a warning and the shadow left out; it now draws the shadow, which is what its author set in After Effects or typed by hand. Above 2000 is refused as before. **Fixtures:** FX-SHADOW-031 (softness 600), 032 (1000) and 033 (2000) are new, each Shadow Only "on" at distance 0 so the whole frame is the shadow's far tail; FX-SHADOW-020's first value, softness 501, is retired (kept in the repository's history at commit 89d06d0c) and it is now softness 2001, refused the same way. `tools/drop_shadow_reference.py` works the wide blurs only where the frame reads them, the same normalised sum, checked against the whole-layer sum at softness 25 within 1e-15; every other case's numbers are unchanged. **Evidence of the build** (B-709, 21 of 21; B-58 114 of 114, B-639 64 of 64, B-654 94 of 94): 031 to 033 within 3.7e-11 and within a thousandth of each pixel's own value; 020 refused with EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID; the card within 1 level at softness 100 to 2000. On the neon rebuild at 8 bpc the red channel going up from the centre at 200/320/450 px is After Effects 63/34/15, the old app 19/1/0 (the two wide shadows refused), and now 83/44/22: the tail's falloff, the values at 320 and 450 over the value at 200, is After Effects 0.54 and 0.24, ours 0.52 and 0.26. **Gaps.** (1) After Effects' own top for Softness is not known: its help page refused the fetch (403) and no tutorial goes past 2000; ours stops there. (2) The neon rebuild is brighter overall than After Effects', the Segoe UI Light stand-in having about 2.2 times the ink of the tutorial's Montserrat Thin (TEXT_FONT_MISSING), which the falloff ratios divide out. **If refused:** the top goes back to 500, FX-SHADOW-031 to 033 go and 020 returns to 501; a file at 501 to 2000 is again read with a warning and its shadow left out.

D-830 / Effects that work from a layer's masks draw along an adjustment layer's own masks on the frame beneath (wave 8, lane w8f; wave 7's "Found, not built": mask-based effects on adjustment layers; reopens the stop-gaps D-786 (2) and D-791 (2), every look already drawn unchanged) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-25** under the owner's words. On 2026-10-25 the owner wrote: "nice; how many more effects need a speed/optimization audit; explore outside of effects and maybe the app's underlying architecture if we need to optimizat/speed up, change it in favor of both speed and visual precision, etc; also yes, let's do all five speed-ups, defer if the pixel cost is noticeably too much to AE/nuke/davinci resolve standards of optimization/visual practices. explore deeply the found, not built section, proceed with your recommendation/discretion." Built as B-710. **Why.** Path Stroke, Vegas, Scribble, Energy Stroke along a path or with Alpha Mode, Audio Spectrum and Audio Waveform on a Path, Inner/Outer Key, Reshape, Mask Smear, Liquify's Freeze Area Mask, Particle Playground's Wall Mask and Fill naming a mask, put on an adjustment layer, drew nothing and said EFFECT_PATH_MISSING every frame: D-786 and D-791 called that a gap ("which an effect on an adjustment layer cannot use yet"), not a look. After Effects draws them along the adjustment layer's own masks: AE Juice, "How to Add a Stroke Mask in After Effects" (https://aejuice.com/blog/how-to-add-a-stroke-mask-in-after-effects/), a mask drawn on an adjustment layer and Stroke pointed at it; and an Adobe Community answer (https://community.adobe.com/t5/after-effects-discussions/adjustment-layers-how-to-get-a-border-outline-for-the-whole-layer/m-p/13710436), a mask on an adjustment layer, then Stroke using that mask.
