Some rounds were faster after (card Draft scale 20 to 39 ms against 51 to 55 ms) but not consistently, and not beyond the noise. **Why it is not built.** The bar is that the delay goes down and nothing gets worse beyond the noise; Mailbox did neither reliably, and it risked a stall. **What would reopen it.** A quiet machine, where the run-to-run noise is under the few milliseconds Mailbox could save.

D-885 / The mask and handle boxes come with the frame instead of a separate ask (wave 10, input lag, lane L2, fix 1) / **PROPOSED**, built switched off. The owner's instruction of 2026-10-25: "let's explore more avenues to speed up app functions, (including effects), and make a much smoother, less input lag experience. like scaling, dragging playhead/layer bar, masks, keyframe points, etc. because there tends to be a slight delay, smooth but delayed movement." Claude offered six fixes, the first this one, and the owner answered "all six" on 2026-10-26. Built as B-765. **Why.** After every still frame the page asked a second time, `/boxes`, for where the selected layers' boxes, mask points and handles are; during a drag that is one more request a frame, on the same thread that makes the frames. **What was built.** A frame asked with `b=1` carries the `/boxes` answer after its pixels (`x-boxes` gives its length), made from the same snapshot as the pixels, so the boxes are always the picture's own; the page then does not ask `/boxes`. A frame the graphics card painted straight into the window brings none and the page asks `/boxes` as before (see the measurements). Asked without `b=1` nothing changes. **Why it is not accepted.** The bar is that the measured delay (median and p95) or the work per step goes down and nothing else gets worse beyond the noise. Measured in the real program (release build; RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, Vulkan; AMD64 Family 26 Model 68, 24 threads; a machine shared with other lanes' builds; wave 8's reference shot with 4 layers (L4) and 25 layers (L25); the delay from the hand's move to the picture drawn, per gesture; 4 alternating before/after rounds per shot, medians of the rounds): the `/boxes` asks per drag went from 50 to 180 to 0 or 1, but the delay did not go down. On the processor (CPU), median ms before to after, L4 Draft: mask 82 to 82, move 28 to 32, number 32 to 29, scale 24 to 26, scrub 38 to 45; L4 Full: mask 96 to 90, move 24 to 29, number 35 to 31, scale 31 to 26, scrub 50 to 46; L25 Draft: mask 133 to 137, move 61 to 67, scale 99 to 101, scrub 40 to 44; L25 Full: mask 132 to 146, move 69 to 71, scale 96 to 113, scrub 43 to 43, frames a second lower in every L25 row (for example scale Full 28 to 22). On the graphics card (GPU), with the boxes then on every frame, L4 Full mask 75 to 110 (p95 120 to 171, 32 to 19 frames a second), scrub 26 to 44, Draft scrub 26 to 48. Reading the stages: the picture now waits for its boxes to be worked out before it is sent, where before it was sent first and drawn while `/boxes` was being answered, so one fewer request did not buy a sooner picture. Taking the card's on-screen frames out (built) puts the GPU back on the old path; the CPU rows alone are no gain. The key gesture and, on L25, the number gesture gave no delay figures (every input was overtaken by the next). **So:** the server's `b=1` and the test stay; the page's switch `BOXES_WITH_FRAME` is `false`, so the app asks and draws exactly as before. **Checked** (`app/src/tests/frame_boxes.rs`, `verification/B-765_frame_boxes_table.md`): opened, after an edit, mid-drag, at the drag's end, after an undo and in another composition, Draft and Full, frames 0 and 120, the pixels with the boxes are the plain frame's byte for byte and the boxes are `/boxes`'s value for value, 25 of 25; a frame asked without `b=1` carries none. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing. **Fixtures:** none changed, none added. **Gaps.** (1) Making the boxes on a second thread after the picture is sent, or sending them as a second part of the same answer once the picture is out, could keep the one request without the wait; not built. (2) The on-screen exclusion was not measured again on its own; with the switch off it does not run. **If accepted later:** set `BOXES_WITH_FRAME` to `true` after a new measurement shows a gain. **If refused:** remove `b=1`, `boxes_of`'s second caller and the test; nothing saved depends on it.

D-886 / Only the changed part of a processor-drawn frame is sent, the whole frame otherwise (wave 10, input lag, lane L2, fix 5) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-26**. The owner's instruction of 2026-10-25: "let's explore more avenues to speed up app functions, (including effects), and make a much smoother, less input lag experience. like scaling, dragging playhead/layer bar, masks, keyframe points, etc. because there tends to be a slight delay, smooth but delayed movement." Claude offered six fixes, this the fifth, and the owner answered "all six" on 2026-10-26. Built as B-766. **Why.** When the processor (CPU) draws the viewer, every frame of a drag crossed from the program to the page whole (about 8 MB at 1920x1080) and was painted whole, even when a small layer had moved and the rest of the picture was the same. **What was built.** The program keeps the last whole frame it sent, with a number. The page says which numbered frame it is showing (`have=`); when the new frame is the same size, the program sends only the smallest rectangle holding every changed pixel (`x-changed: x,y,w,h`, all 0 when nothing changed) and the page paints that rectangle onto the picture it has. In every other case (first frame, a new size, the card's on-screen frames, a zoomed part, a lost or out-of-order answer) the whole frame is sent as before. A changed part that answers an older picture than the one the page now shows is thrown away, never painted, so no patch of an old picture can be left behind. The page's switch is `SEND_CHANGED`, `true`. **Checked** (`app/src/tests/changed_part.rs`, `verification/B-766_changed_part_table.md`): a simulated page canvas, given the parts the program sends across opening, an edit, a drag and its end, frames 0, 1, 2, 60 and 120, a switch to Draft and back (a new size), an undo, the alpha view on and off, an answer the page threw away and another composition, ends byte for byte equal to the whole frame each time, 21 of 21, 17 of them sent as parts; in the real program 16 of 16 steps gave 0 differing bytes against the whole frame. **Measured** in the real program (release build; RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, Vulkan; AMD64 Family 26 Model 68, 24 threads; a machine shared with other lanes' builds; wave 8's reference shot with 4 layers (L4) and 25 layers (L25), viewer on the CPU; the delay from the hand's move to the picture drawn; 4 alternating before/after rounds per shot, pooled), median ms before to after (p95 in brackets): L25 Draft move 47 to 27 (48 to 44), scrub 33 to 29 (44 to 37), mask 108 to 103 (125 to 134); L25 Full move 60 to 21 (60 to 30), scrub 39 to 20 (39 to 37), mask 121 to 105 (128 to 132); L4 Draft move 23 to 21 (23 to 24), number 25 to 24 (25 to 24), scrub 23 to 26 (42 to 46), mask 51 to 57 (60 to 66); L4 Full move 21 to 24 (21 to 24), number 28 to 29 (29 to 29), scrub 27 to 25 (30 to 38), mask 57 to 51 (66 to 62). Frames a second the same or higher in every row (L25 Full scrub 53 to 57). The time to carry a frame across fell in every row but L4 Full scrub (4.2 to 4.4 ms) (L25 Draft move 9.1 to 1.4 ms, L4 Full move 3.0 to 0.9 ms). The L4 rows move within the spread between rounds (for example L4 Draft mask's round medians 20 to 82 before and 20 to 82 after); there the page's paint step took about 1 to 2 ms longer (L4 Full move 9.5 to 11.9 ms) while the carry got as much shorter. In the Full rows of this measurement most answers were "nothing changed" (the gesture's frames came out identical), so the Full gains show the cost of an unchanged frame; the Draft rows sent real changed parts (L25 Draft move 179 parts). A first run counted the "nothing changed" answers as dropped frames and was thrown away; the figures above are the rerun. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing. **Fixtures:** none changed, none added. **Gaps.** (1) The card's on-screen frames already skip the crossing and are untouched. (2) A zoomed part of the frame (B-158) is still sent whole. (3) Only one rectangle is sent; two small changes far apart send everything between them. **If refused:** set `SEND_CHANGED` to `false` and the page asks and draws exactly as before; remove `have=`, the kept frame and the test to take it out fully; nothing saved depends on it.

D-890 / The viewer's frames are answered on a thread of their own, not the window's (wave 10, input lag, lane L5, fix 2) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-26**. The owner's instruction of 2026-10-25: "let's explore more avenues to speed up app functions, (including effects), and make a much smoother, less input lag experience. like scaling, dragging playhead/layer bar, masks, keyframe points, etc. because there tends to be a slight delay, smooth but delayed movement." Claude offered six fixes, this the second ("async protocol handlers"), and the owner answered "all six" on 2026-10-26. Built as B-770. **Why.** Every request the page sends to the program (frames, outlines, the Sheet grid, the graph's curves, and every command) was answered on the window's own thread, one after another. While a heavy frame rendered there, the next command of a drag (a mask point, a scale, a number) waited behind it, and so did the window's own input. **What was built.** The `frame` requests are now answered on one thread of their own (`off_the_window_thread`), in the order they were asked, through Tauri's asynchronous request handler. Commands (the `project` requests) stay on the window's thread, as does `/place`, which attaches the graphics card's picture to the window. A command finishes before any read the page sends after it is even queued, so that read always shows it; a read queued before a command may show it too, which is newer, never older. The page's own one-frame-in-flight rule and B-766's `have=` / `x-changed` are unchanged. The switch is `FRAMES_OFF_THE_WINDOW_THREAD` in `app/src/main.rs`, `true`. **Checked** (`app/src/tests/async_frames.rs`, `verification/B-770_async_frames_table.md`): frames asked on the frame thread with `have=`, drawn as the page draws them, are byte for byte the whole frame after opening, an edit, three drag steps and the drag's end, frames 0 and 60, Draft and back to Full, an undo and another composition, 12 of 12, including a read queued while the frame thread was busy and answered after the alpha view was switched on (it brought the newer picture); 64 queued jobs ran in the order queued. In the real program (4 layers, CPU, Full and Draft) 18 of 18 steps across frames 0, 1, 30, 60 and 120, a layer moved twice and an undo gave 0 differing bytes against the whole frame. **Measured** in the real program (release build; RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, Vulkan; AMD64 Family 26 Model 68, 24 threads; a machine shared with other lanes' builds; wave 8's reference shot with 4 layers (L4) and 25 layers (L25), viewer on the CPU and on the graphics card, Draft and Full; the delay from the hand's move to the picture drawn; 5 alternating before/after rounds per shot, 10 runs a row), median ms before to after (p95 in brackets): L25 CPU Draft mask 112 to 82 (128 to 100), scale 77 to 62 (94 to 75), move 27 to 24 (48 to 40), scrub 26 to 30 (35 to 38); L25 CPU Full mask 113 to 76 (129 to 92), scale 73 to 59 (89 to 76), move 27 to 25 (36 to 41), scrub 26 to 30 (39 to 35); L25 GPU Draft mask 79 to 66 (94 to 83), scale 52 to 41 (55 to 41), move 39 to 38 (41 to 40), scrub 30 to 30; L25 GPU Full mask 82 to 67 (96 to 84), scale 54 to 39 (55 to 40), move 52 to 36 (53 to 36), scrub 35 to 37 (36 to 38); L4 CPU Draft mask 46 to 36 (56 to 51), scale 22 to 20, move 22 to 23, scrub 30 to 30 (33 to 39), number 24 to 23 (28 to 23); L4 CPU Full mask 51 to 35 (60 to 51), scale 24 to 21, move 24 to 22, scrub 30 to 31 (32 to 35), number 28 to 24; L4 GPU Draft mask 57 to 36 (60 to 51), scale 23 to 32, move 23 to 22, scrub 30 to 30, number 44 to 32 (45 to 35); L4 GPU Full mask 60 to 49 (63 to 53), scale 40 to 36, move 27 to 31, scrub 27 to 31, number 43 to 34. The time a drag's command took fell sharply because it no longer waits for a render (L25 mask 42 to 6 ms, L25 scale 25 to 4.4 ms, L4 mask 12 to 3 ms). The cost: carrying a frame across takes about 0.1 to 1.3 ms longer for the extra hop between threads (L4 scrub 3.7 to 5.0 ms), and scrub rows are 0 to 4 ms slower. The rows that rose (scrubs, L4 GPU Draft scale, L4 GPU Full move) are within the spread between rounds (L4 GPU Draft scale runs 18 to 54 before and 18 to 45 after; L25 CPU scrub 18 to 33 before and 20 to 47 after). Frames a second are the same or within 2 to 4 of before (L4 scrub 58 to 56, L25 GPU mask 37 to 35). **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing. **Fixtures:** none changed, none added. **Gaps.** (1) Commands still run on the window's thread; a slow command (an import, a save) still holds the window. (2) One frame thread: a frame and an outline asked together are answered one after the other, as before. (3) Scrubbing gained nothing and costs the small hop. **If refused:** set `FRAMES_OFF_THE_WINDOW_THREAD` to `false` and every `frame` request is answered on the window's thread exactly as before; remove `off_the_window_thread` and the test to take it out fully; nothing saved depends on it.

D-896 / The precision rule: single precision by default, double only where it is proven needed, never half for the maths (wave 11, pick 10, lane L10) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-26**. On 2026-10-26 the owner asked how After Effects, Nuke and other professional programs balance speed against exact pixels, then answered: "Do all of your picks at your recommended order. Defer or tackle until solved if consequential to your discretion." This was the tenth pick. Built as B-776. **The rule.** (1) An effect's maths is worked in single precision (f32) by default; the drawing's pixels already are. (2) Double precision (f64) is kept only where one of these is shown: long running totals or prefix sums; a difference of large, nearly equal numbers set against a small epsilon (a variance); positions in picture coordinates walked or accumulated step by step; a hard threshold or cut-off the reference decides exactly; a division by something that can be very small. (3) Half precision is never used for the maths (D-874). (4) A change from double to single on the processor is made only when every fixture of the effect still passes at its tolerance (2e-5), the processor's floats stay within 1e-4 of before, the processor's 8-bit picture of the reference shot is identical to before (`perf_audit::perf_audit_pixels`), and the effect is measurably quicker in alternating before/after rounds (`perf_audit::perf_audit_timing`). The processor stays the reference for exports and stored checks; nothing switches silently. This extends D-228 (the card's audit) to the processor. **Converted.** Bilateral Blur's weights (`src/median.rs`, `bilateral_blur`: the distance falloff and each tap's level falloff, an `exp` per tap and channel), and so Cartoon, whose smoothing it is. The colours and the running sums stay double. Every fixture passes (FX-BILAT and FX-CARTOON 1 to 32, largest difference 3.6e-7); the processor's frame 30 at Full is identical in 8 bits for Bilateral Blur as added and at Radius 40 and for Cartoon as added and heavy, largest float change 1.2e-7. **Measured** (release build; AMD64 Family 26 Model 68, 24 threads; RTX 4070 Ti SUPER; a machine shared with other lanes' builds; one 1920x1080 layer of the reference shot, median of frames 0 to 210 by 30, processor at Full, which is an export's time; five rounds alternating the base build ec3f3c04 and this one, two sittings), ms before to after: Bilateral Blur Radius 40 276.4 to 234.7 and 307.5 to 273.3; as added 41.3 to 37.8 and 53.8 to 48.6; Cartoon heavy (Detail Radius 40) 288.0 to 255.6 and 354.2 to 295.6; Cartoon as added 65.4 to 60.4 and 70.1 to 71.1; no effect 16.6 to 16.9 and 18.1 to 22.0. The viewer draws these effects on the card, which is untouched. **Tried and not built: Deband** (`src/grade.rs`). (a) Its blur's weights, values and sums in single precision (as its card blur since D-550): 112.7 to 71.2 ms as added and 136.0 to 96.7 ms at Blur 40, every fixture within 2.5e-7, but 3 and 4 of the 2,073,600 pixels came out 1 level of 255 apart, so the export would not be identical. (b) Only its weights in single precision: identical, but 88.7 to 85.2 and 142.9 to 126.5 ms, within the spread between rounds (no effect moved 20.3 to 17.6). Neither is built. (a) is the owner's call: accept a 1-level change on a few export pixels for about 30% off Deband's export time. **Kept in double, with the reason** (`verification/B-776_precision_table.md`): Refine Soft Matte, Refine Hard Matte and Key Cleaner (the guided filter's totals over whole rows, then a variance against an epsilon of 1e-4; 216 to 430 ms, the slowest effects); Matte Choker (totals then a division by a covering that can be very small); Contour Paint (positions walked up to 1920 px with a stop test at 1e-6); Caustics (the wave heights' slopes become positions; its bottom picture's blur is a candidate, not tried); Halation and Soft Glow (already single); Fast Zoom Blur, Radial Blur and Light Burst (samples at worked-out positions along rays; not tried). **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing. **Fixtures:** none changed, none added. **Gaps.** (1) Only the slowest effects at Full were examined (down to Radial Blur, 88 ms); Brush Strokes, Bloom and the rest are not audited. (2) The timings come from a shared machine; the second sitting was noisier (Cartoon as added showed no gain there). (3) The Caustics bottom blur and Deband (a) are left open. **If refused:** put `bilateral_blur`'s weights back to `f64` (seven lines) and remove `tests/b776_precision.rs`; the rule's text can stay as guidance or go; nothing saved depends on it.

D-894 / The card-against-processor checks do not grade the colour of a pixel nobody can see (wave 11, pick 4, lane L4, part A) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-26**. The owner's instruction of 2026-10-26: "Do all of your picks at your recommended order. Defer or tackle until solved if consequential to your discretion." This is the first half of pick 4, "stop grading pixels nobody can see". Built as B-774. **Why.** A pixel whose alpha is 0 shows only what is behind it, so no viewer can see its colour. Several card speed-ups failed their checks only on such pixels (D-222 FFT Lens Blur, D-240 Kaleidoscope). D-345 and D-617 already skipped them, but only in some tests. **The rule, exactly.** It applies only where the graphics card's picture is held against the processor's picture of the same frame: the ADR-006 / D-100 1-level bar and wave 8's bar (within 1 level of 255 on at least 99.9% of pixels and within 2 everywhere). (1) *Straight 8-bit pictures* (the viewer's sRGB bytes, `to_srgb8_straight` against `preview_frame_srgb8`): where the alpha byte is 0 on **both** sides, the pixel's difference is 0, whatever its red, green and blue. That is alpha below 0.5/255 after rounding, so the rule never reaches a pixel whose alpha byte is 1. If only one side has alpha byte 0, all four channels are compared as before, so a pixel the card makes appear or vanish is still graded. (2) *Straight 16-bit*: the same rule would read "alpha below 257 of 65535 on both sides". No check compares 16-bit card pictures today, so none was changed. (3) *Straight float*: alpha below 1/255 on both sides. Again no such check exists today. (4) *Premultiplied pictures* (B-754's float checks in premultiplied linear light): no rule is needed, because colour is already multiplied by alpha. A pixel nobody can see has colour near 0 on both sides and is graded as stored. B-754 and B-758 keep their existing "both alphas 0" skip. **Proof that nothing visible is hidden.** A viewer sees colour × alpha + background × (1 − alpha). With alpha 0 on both sides, both pictures show exactly the background over any background, so over black and over white they differ by 0. B-774 checks this pixel by pixel. **What was built.** `seen` (the graded difference), `hidden` (whether the rule excused a pixel) and `shown` (the difference composited over black and over white, rounded to 8 bits) in `tests/effect_table/mod.rs`; D-617's `distance` now uses `seen`. The walks that compared every channel now use `seen`: `tests/eight_walk/mod.rs` (B-749, B-750), `tests/b688_eight_card.rs` and `tests/b748_card_blend_modes.rs`. The app's `perf_audit_eight` (D-808) gets the same one-line guard. Each table row now states how many pixels the rule excused and their largest difference over black or white. Byte-for-byte checks stay byte for byte, including a frame the card refuses, which must still equal the processor's exactly in all four channels. **Not changed.** Fixture checks against the reference tool's numbers (doc 25's 2e-5), exports, stored values, and every other card test with its own `distance` compare all four channels as before; they are stricter, and they pass. **Fixtures:** no expected value changed, none added. No fixture comparison is made looser: the rule touches only card-against-processor comparisons, never a comparison with a fixture's expected values. **Which checks got looser** (each run before and after on this build, RTX 4070 Ti SUPER): B-688 (every fixture project in 8 bpc, Full and Draft) excused 0 pixels, and its table is the same before and after; B-749 and B-750 excused 0 pixels, tables the same; B-748's sweep of blend modes with Preserve Transparency on excused 1 to 3 pixels in 20 of its rows (of 262,144 each), and every one of those rows already passed with the same largest difference, the same "over 1" and the same verdict. Every excused pixel's largest difference over black or white was 0. So today the rule changes no verdict; what it changes is what a card speed-up has to meet (D-895). **Gaps.** The rule is written for straight pictures; a check of a premultiplied picture that unpremultiplies before comparing must use the float form (4). **If refused:** make `seen` compare all four channels again (one line) and remove the guard in `perf_audit.rs`; the extra table wording disappears, and nothing saved depends on it.

D-895 / Lens Blur by Fourier transform on the viewer's card from radius 100, reopened from D-222 under D-894's rule (wave 11, pick 4, lane L4, part B) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-26**. The owner's instruction of 2026-10-26: "Do all of your picks at your recommended order. Defer or tackle until solved if consequential to your discretion." This is the second half of pick 4, "stop grading pixels nobody can see". Built as B-775. **Why reopened.** D-222 measured a single-precision FFT Lens Blur within 1 level wherever the result has any alpha. It failed only in the haze at the blur's edge, where alpha is under 1 of 255 and the hidden colour can be anything. The owner kept Lens Blur exact on 2026-09-30, because grading only visible pixels would then have widened the tolerance just to pass. D-894 now makes that the rule for every card check, with a proof that nothing visible is excused. **The other candidate.** D-240 (Kaleidoscope on the card, which failed only on 1 to 4 invisible pixels on mirror lines) is unlocked too. Its code was kept outside the repository and its speed was never measured. D-240 kept it on the processor "until the viewer is slow on it", so it is not built here and stays as decided. Lens Blur has the larger measured cost (252 ms a frame at radius 200, D-222). **What was built.** When a layer's Lens Blur has transparent edges (not "repeat") and no blur map, and its radius in the drawing's pixels is at least `LENS_FFT_FROM` (100), the viewer's card works it by fast Fourier transform. The steps are: the grown layer and the iris go into a field whose sides are powers of two; red+green, blue+alpha and the iris are transformed as three complex numbers; the layer's transforms are multiplied by the iris's and transformed back; each pixel is read where the exact gather would have put it. Single precision throughout, with the transform's angles computed in double precision. A Draft frame's radius is already shrunk, so Draft frames at radius 200 or less stay on the gather. Repeat edges, blur maps, smaller radii and a field too big for the card's buffers all keep the exact gather. The card's memory check counts the field (two buffers of 24 bytes a point: 403 MB per layer at 4096 by 2048, freed after the layer). Export and every processor path are unchanged; the processor stays the exact reference. **Two approaches.** (1) Radix-2 steps (11 to 12 passes per axis): it met the bar, but it was slower than the gather except at radius 200 at Full (Full medians, gather against transform: 54.6/92.6, 72.7/97.0, 116.5/159.8 and 235.3/171.2 ms at radius 25, 50, 100 and 200). (2) Radix-8 steps (4 passes per axis), the one built: it meets the same bar with the same results. Double precision (planned as a third approach) was not needed. **Accuracy** (`tests/b775_fft_lens_blur.rs`, `verification/B-775_fft_lens_blur_table.md`, 83 of 83; the transform forced at every radius against the processor's exact frame, both as the page receives them). On the reference shot at frame 100, with D-222's Lens Blur (hexagon iris, roundness 20, rotation 15, aspect 1.3, gain 2, threshold 80) on three layers, at radius 25, 50, 100 and 200, Full and Draft: largest difference 1 level, 0 pixels over 1, 100% within 1 on 2,073,600 pixels (Full) and 129,600 (Draft). No pixels were excused, because the shot's background is opaque. On every Lens Blur fixture that opens (69), first and middle frames, Full and Draft: 78 Lens Blurs went through the transform, largest difference 1 on 11,845 visible pixels. 1,037 fully transparent pixels had different hidden colours; these are the D-222 haze, and they show 0 difference over black and over white. At the shipped switch, radius 50 at Full and radius 200 at Draft stay on the gather, and radius 100 and 200 at Full use the transform (4 more rows). **Speed** (`verification/B-775_timing_table.md`, the `b775_fft_lens_blur_timing` test; the reference shot frame 100 with the Lens Blur on three layers; 5 rounds, gather and transform alternating; each round the median of 11 drawings after the card drops what it kept; RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, Vulkan, Ryzen 9 9900X with 24 threads, release; other lanes were building and testing on the machine). Full medians, gather then transform: radius 25 57.5 / 77.4, 50 83.8 / 80.8, 100 125.6 / 118.6, **200 285.1 / 137.6** ms. An earlier run on the same code: 54.7 / 72.0, 72.1 / 70.2, 117.4 / 112.8, 243.7 / 139.2. The transform's cost depends on the field size, not the radius, so it overtakes the gather at about radius 50 to 100. The switch is at 100, the smallest measured radius where it was faster in both runs. Draft is unaffected at the switch (radius 200 at Draft is 50 in the drawing). **Fixtures:** no expected value changed, none added. **Checks rerun:** B-59, B-64, B-65, B-155, B-164, B-238, B-749 and B-750 pass. **Gaps.** The field is padded to powers of two, so a layer just past a power of two (for example 1920 wide plus the blur's growth) does almost twice the work. Radix-3 or radix-5 steps would trim this. The iris's transform is redone for each layer that shares it. A card whose buffers cannot hold the field keeps the gather. **If refused:** set `LENS_FFT_FROM` to infinity (one line). Every Lens Blur is then the exact gather again, and nothing saved depends on it.

D-893 / A viewer frame nobody will see stops being drawn as soon as newer input arrives (wave 11, lane L1, pick 1, stoppable frames) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-26**. On 2026-10-26 the owner asked how After Effects, Nuke and other professional programs balance speed against exact pixels, and what we should do to compete (research in `S/wave11/pros_research.html`); the owner answered: "Do all of your picks at your recommended order. Defer or tackle until solved if consequential to your discretion." This is the first pick, built as B-773. **Why.** Since D-890 the viewer's frames are answered on a thread of their own, but a frame once started ran to its end: on the 25-layer shot on the processor a Full picture takes 100 to 200 ms, and when the hand moved again, or an undo or a click came, the page waited for a picture it would then throw away (B-162) before the one wanted could start. **What was built.** (1) A process-wide stop count (`src/stop.rs`). A viewer frame remembers the count as its request arrives; the page's `/stop` (answered at once on the window's thread) raises it, and the frame then ends at the next point it looks: between the top composition's layers while planning, and before each tile while the finished plan is drawn (the B-159 picture below the edited layer included). A stopped frame is an error, `PREVIEW_FRAME_STOPPED` (INFO), never a picture: the answer is status 204 with `x-stopped: 1` and no body, nothing of it reaches the ram frame cache, the page's `x-sent` record (D-886) or B-159's kept picture below, which is put back as it was. Exports, stored checks and a composition layer's inner frame drawn while planning never look, so they are never stopped. (2) The page (`stopsInFlight`, inside the B-162/B-163 markers) asks for a stop only when the frame in flight would not be drawn anyway (a Full sharpen picture when the drag has started again, B-162) or when the hand is still (an undo, a click, a typed value, a frame or quality change); a drag's own frames are never stopped, since each is the nearest picture to the hand there is, and never two stops running, so a stopped frame is always followed by one that is drawn. Playback frames are never stopped, and a scrub's frames only when one is the Full sharpen picture B-162 would throw away. After a stopped answer the page asks for the newest request, or the same frame again when nothing newer waits. The switch is `STOP_FRAMES` in `app/ui/index.html`, `true`. "The dragged layer drawn first" was not built: B-159 already starts a drag's frame from the kept picture below the dragged layer and every unchanged layer comes from the caches, so there was nothing left to reorder that could be measured. **Checked** (`app/src/tests/stoppable_frames.rs`, `verification/B-773_stoppable_frames_table.md`): on the reference shot's viewer on the processor, each frame is stopped at its first point, asked again and stopped at its second, and so on through every point it looks (8 or 9 per frame: between layers, at the draw, after it) until it comes back whole; every stopped answer had no picture, sent nothing and left the page's picture as it was, and the whole answer that followed was made afresh and byte for byte the frame of a second viewer given the same changes and never stopped, 11 of 11: the first frame, after an edit, two drag steps, before and after an undo, a frame change, Draft, a Draft frame change, back to Full and another composition. A frame not watched is never stopped even straight after a stop. The page's rule run under Node, 7 of 7. In the real program (25 layers, processor, Full, frames 90 to 95), a `/stop` sent 3 ms after the request stopped 6 of 6 frames with no picture, and each frame asked again came back whole (8,294,400 bytes) and made afresh. **Measured** in the real program (release build; RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, Vulkan; AMD64 Family 26 Model 68, 24 threads; a machine shared with other lanes' builds and lag runs; wave 8's reference shot with 4 layers (L4) and 25 layers (L25), viewer on the processor and the graphics card, Draft and Full; the delay from the hand's move to the picture drawn; the pause gestures hold the hand still 0.28 s half way and also give the first picture after the hand moves on; 5 alternating before/after rounds, 10 runs a row), median ms before to after (p95 in brackets): L25 processor Full mask 105 to 86 (141 to 107), scale 74 to 59 (94 to 75), move 49 to 40 (69 to 48), scrub 42 to 37 (56 to 48), mask with a pause 84 to 79 (127 to 107) and the first picture after the pause 216 to 77, move with a pause 43 to 38 (61 to 51) and the first picture after the pause 167 to 53; frames stopped of stops sent across the 10 runs: mask with a pause 11 of 21, move with a pause 11 of 17, scrub 5 of 8, mask 3 of 12, scale 2 of 11, move 0 of 9 (a stop that arrives after the frame is finished stops nothing). L25 processor Draft mask 99 to 80 (141 to 93), scale 57 to 58 (72 to 74), move 39 to 38, scrub 39 to 45 (52 to 46), mask with a pause 70 to 65, move with a pause 57 to 43; no Draft frame was stopped (4 stops sent, each arrived after the frame was done), so these rows move by the spread between rounds alone. L25 graphics card Full mask 78 to 81 (111 to 117), scale 41 to 40, move 43 to 40, scrub 37 to 37, mask with a pause 63 to 61, move with a pause 45 to 44; 1 frame stopped of 18 stops sent (the card's own draw cannot be stopped). L25 graphics card Draft first read 70 to 82 (mask), 22 to 45 (scale), 30 to 47 (move), 31 to 39 (scrub) with no stop sent at all; the before build ran equally slowly in rounds 4 and 5 (scale 48 to 59 before, 36 to 52 after), so three more alternating rounds were run on a quieter machine: mask 52 to 51 (67 to 64), move 19 to 19, scale 18 to 18, scrub 18 to 18. L4: no frame was stopped or stop sent in any row and every row is within the spread between rounds (processor Full mask 44 to 45, scrub 42 to 33; processor Draft scrub 33 to 39, runs 22 to 41 before and 25 to 69 after; graphics card Draft scale 26 to 13). Two L4 rounds of both builds were dropped and run again because a pointer passed over the test window during them. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing. **Fixtures:** none changed, none added. **Gaps.** (1) The graphics card's draw (`gpu.draw`) and a single effect within one tile run to their end; only the points between layers and between tiles can stop. (2) A composition layer's inner frame, drawn while the outer frame is planned, is never cut short. (3) A drag's own frames are not stopped by design, so a steady drag gains only where B-162 already threw the frame away. (4) The release build measured lacked only the `STOP_FRAMES` constant (on); the page check ran on the final build. **If refused:** set `STOP_FRAMES` to `false` in `app/ui/index.html` and the page never sends `/stop`, so every frame is drawn to its end as before (the checks left in cost a counter read each); remove `src/stop.rs`, its checks in `compose.rs`, `render.rs` and `preview.rs`, the `/stop` path and `x-stopped` answer in `app/src/main.rs`, `PREVIEW_FRAME_STOPPED` and the test to take it out fully; nothing saved depends on it.

D-901 / The viewer's profiler: for the frame on screen, the time each layer and effect took, whether the card or the processor drew it, and whether it came from memory, after After Effects' Composition Profiler (wave 11, pick 11, lane L11) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-26**. On 2026-10-26 the owner asked how After Effects, Nuke and other professional programs balance speed against exact pixels, and what we should do to compete (research in `S/wave11/pros_research.html`); the owner answered: "Do all of your picks at your recommended order. Defer or tackle until solved if consequential to your discretion." This is pick 11, built as B-781. **Why.** When a shot is slow nobody can see which layer or effect is to blame; After Effects 2024 added a Composition Profiler for exactly that, and every speed question this project has had (P-24, P-25, waves 9 to 11) was answered by an agent's timing run, never by the owner looking. **What was built.** (1) A stopwatch button beside the region button in the viewer's row, and the command finder line "Profiler: where this frame's time went", open a small panel. While it is open each viewer frame is asked with `prof=1`; the answer carries an `x-profile` header and the panel shows a sentence (the frame, its total time, drawn on the graphics card or the processor, or shown from memory) and a table, slowest first and the slowest marked: Layer, Time, Drawn on (graphics card, processor, or card and processor), Effects (each with its time, or "kept from before" when its picture came from the P-11 effect memory), From cache. A line under the table names the frame's own work (putting the layers together, drawing on the card). (2) "Measure again" asks the same frame with `prof=2`, which draws it fresh past the ram frame memory (the effect memory is still used, so what it saves is shown). Closing the panel stops asking. (3) No second timing system: the P-01 stages in `src/perf.rs` (`time`, `untimed`, `record`) now also run when a profile is being taken on this thread, and add their time to the layer that is open (`open_layer` / `close_layer` around each top layer in `compose.rs` plan and `render.rs` adjust and card draws; `left_for_card` names effects handed to the card). With the panel closed the only added work is one relaxed atomic read per stage call; the P-01 counters are written only when timing is on, as before. **Checked.** `b781_profiler_reports_layers_and_where_they_were_drawn` (app), 12 of 12 rows: no profile is sent when not asked; on the processor 4 rows for the 4 layers, all drawn on the processor; the Gaussian Blur (sigma 24) on layer 2 is timed (11.6 ms) and layer 2 is the slowest (16.8 ms); blur at most its layer, the layers at most the frame (66.6 ms); the pixels with the profiler on are byte for byte those of a viewer never profiled; asked again it is shown from memory with no rows; measured again it is drawn with the blur kept from before; on the card layer 2 and the blur say graphics card with the same pixels; with Echo before the blur the layer says card and processor, Echo processor, blur card. The full app suite (`cargo test --release -p anime_compositor_app`, no filter): 129 passed, 0 failed, 12 ignored (the keyboard and command finder pins now list the three new controls and the 131st finder line). Seen in a private copy of the app on the 25-layer shot (`S/wave11/L11/profiler_try.png`, `profiler_cpu.png`, `profiler_gpu.png`). **Measured.** The panel closed costs nothing measurable: the lag harness on the 25-layer shot (L25), a clean build of main 47f215a0 against this one, alternating, 3 rounds of 2 (6 reps per row), median delay in ms, release build, RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, AMD64 Family 26 Model 68, 24 threads, shared with other lanes running builds and timings: processor Draft mask 108 to 84, move 53 to 50, scrub 61 to 38; processor Full mask 143 to 113, move 65 to 30, scrub 40 to 43 (before's reps 37 to 74); card Draft mask 107 to 59, move 52 to 30, scrub 41 to 32; card Full mask 99 to 73, move 45 to 34, scrub 40 to 39. Not slower in 11 of 12 rows and the twelfth within its spread; the gains are the machine's load, not this change. **Gaps.** (1) Card work is timed for the whole frame, not per layer (the card's passes are queued and timed together). (2) Putting the layers together is one frame line, not charged to layers. (3) Two effects of the same kind on one layer show as one, their times summed. (4) A frame shown from memory has no rows; "Measure again" draws it. (5) An effect whose picture was kept at the project's first drawing shows "kept from before" with no time. (6) Work done on helper threads (tiles drawn side by side, pre-drawing) is not charged to a layer. (7) The panel shows the viewer's frame only, not an export. **Fixtures.** None changed; no pixel changed. **If refused.** Remove the button, the panel and the finder line; the hooks in `perf.rs` do nothing while no profile is asked.

D-897 / Drawings kept in the viewer's memory as floats while they fit, dropped to their own 8 bits (a quarter of the size) instead of being let go when keeping their floats would push something out, and widened again when asked for (wave 11, pick 6, lane L6) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-26**. The owner's instruction of 2026-10-26: "Do all of your picks at your recommended order. Defer or tackle until solved if consequential to your discretion." This was the sixth pick. Built as B-777. **Why.** The viewer's drawing cache (`CelCache`, B-08b, D-105) held every decoded drawing as 32-bit floats, 33,177,600 bytes for a 1920x1080 drawing, four times the decoder's 8,294,400 bytes (ADR-015). A budget that holds 72 drawings as floats holds about 4.6 times as many at 8 bits. **What was built** (`src/cache.rs`). A drawing is stored as floats, as before, whenever its floats fit the budget. When the budget is full, the cache lets go in this order, least recently used first in each step: the spare buffer (below); floats widened again from bytes it still holds, first for drawings the frame in hand does not use; then, while every drawing held and the drawings lately let go whole would all fit at 8 bits, an 8-bit drawing's floats, kept as the bytes they came from (`narrow`, the exact inverse of the widening, checked to the bit, and the drawing let go whole if it ever were not); and otherwise the oldest drawing whole, as before. The drawings lately let go whole are remembered by their 8-bit size only, up to the budget's worth: when they would not fit at 8 bits either, holding bytes would save no decode, and the cache behaves as before D-897, floats only. A drawing asked for whose floats have gone is widened again (`widen`) by the same arithmetic a decode does after the decoder: the byte divided by 255, through the sRGB transfer function when the drawing is sRGB, times alpha when alpha is straight, the same f32 operations in the same order, so the floats are the same to the bit; widened, they are held beside the bytes while there is room. While a frame still holds a drawing's floats, the cache hands back those same floats instead of a second copy, and the card's name for the drawing (B-44b) is kept across widening. A fresh decode's bytes are let go on the thread that decoded, as before, unless the drawing's floats are larger than the whole budget (then it is held at 8 bits only). An EXR has no 8-bit bytes and is held as floats only, as before; 16-bit input is refused by `media.rs` and is not affected. The switch is `KEEP_8BIT_CELS` in `src/cache.rs`, `true`; `false` holds floats only, as before. Nothing in a saved project changes; no fixture or expected value changed; export does not use this cache and is unchanged. **Checked** (`tests/b777_compact_cels.rs`, `verification/B-777_compact_cels_table.md`, 18 of 18): every fixture image that decodes, read four ways (sRGB or linear, straight or premultiplied) twice, both answers the fresh decode bit for bit, 3620 of 3620, and 3316 of 3316 eight-bit second answers came from memory with room for 8 bits only; EXRs not kept at 8 bits, 0 of 304; every 8-bit fixture image held as floats, let down to 8 bits when the room shrank, and asked for again, from memory, 3316 of 3316, and every answer bit for bit, 3620 of 3620; all 65,536 colour and alpha byte pairs under each of the four ways, widened from memory and let down then widened, bit for bit a fresh decode; the reference shot's frames 0, 12, 14, 25, 100 and 101 at Full, twice round, from a cache with room for four 8-bit drawings and from one with room for some floats too, the uncached frame bit for bit, 12 of 12 each. `p03_byte_equality` passes (the 8-bit picture byte-equal); `b06_mask`, `b08b_cache`, `b153_card_kept_memory`, `b161_decode_cache`, `b170_held`, `b44_gpu_preview`, `b48_memory`, `b740_mask_cache`, `b744_export_read_ahead`, `p11_effect_cache`, `b12b_declared_fixture`, the library's cache test and the app's 127 tests pass. `verification/B-08b_cache_table.md`'s two-cel rows were moved (20480 bytes for two cels; a third cel now leaves the large at 8 bits and the small as floats, 20480 bytes, the middle let go whole, the same checks); its ten-loop row is unchanged at 497,664,000 bytes. **How it got here.** The first build (6917cade) held the bytes always and the floats beside them while there was room, which kept the gains at 4 GiB but was slower at 1 GiB (39.9 to 43.2 ms playing, 49.6 to 55.8 scattered) and playing at 8 GiB (10.0 to 18.1), because the bytes took the room the floats had. Not merged; reworked under the owner's "tackle until solved": (1) floats instead of bytes, a drawing dropped to bytes only when keeping its floats would push something out, was slower at 4 GiB (79 ms) because a drawing was dropped and widened again every frame; (2) keeping the bytes beside floats widened again and dropping first what the frame in hand does not use fixed that; (3) remembering what was let go whole, so bytes are kept only when they could save a decode, made 1 GiB hold what it held before; (4) a fresh decode's bytes had been carried to the main thread and let go there, about 10 ms a frame at 1 GiB in 9 of 10 paired rounds, and are now let go where they are decoded. The widening's own cost was cut twice in the first build and kept: the decode's three steps folded into one pass with two 256-entry tables, and floats the cache lets go of that nothing else holds kept as one spare buffer and widened into (most of the cost was the system clearing fresh pages). The spare is now inside the budget: counted in what is held, kept only when there is room, and the first thing let go. **Measured** (`verification/B-777_timing_table.md`; release build; AMD Ryzen 9 9900X, 24 threads, 64 GB, RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, Windows 11; a machine shared with other lanes' builds; document 08's ten-layer shot, 166 distinct 1920x1080 drawings, processor at Draft through `preview_frame_cached`, the third of three loops of frames 0 to 239 and then 240 frames in a scattered order; five rounds alternating base 9be18462 and this build, the same test source; the viewer's memory setting, of which the drawings get 9/16), medians before to after: at 1 GiB (the smallest) 18 held either way, 570 MiB, every drawing still decoded again each loop, loop 42.5 to 39.9 ms a frame, scattered 49.3 to 49.5, no change; at 4 GiB 72 drawings held to 166, decodes in a loop 1287 to 0, loop 41.5 to 20.6, scattered 50.8 to 29.1; at 8 GiB (a 32 GB machine's Automatic) 145 to 166 held, decodes 237 to 0, loop 10.9 to 10.8, scattered 39.1 to 13.2; at 16 GiB (about this machine's Automatic) all 166 fit as floats either way, 9.0 to 8.9 and 9.0 to 9.2, no change, holding 5252 MiB both. **Gaps.** At 4 GiB the loop is 20.6 ms against the first build's 19.2: drawings move between floats and bytes as the loop comes round. In the app the drawings share the setting with finished frames (B-154), which this did not measure, and the input-lag harness was not run; the measurement is the processor's own frame time. **If refused.** `KEEP_8BIT_CELS` to `false`: the cache holds floats only, as before D-897, with the same pixels.

D-898 / A third viewer quality, In motion, while the hand drags or scrubs (wave 11, lane L23, pick 2) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-26**. On 2026-10-26 the owner asked how After Effects, Nuke and other professional programs balance speed against exact pixels (research in `S/wave11/pros_research.html`) and answered: "Do all of your picks at your recommended order. Defer or tackle until solved if consequential to your discretion." This is pick 2, built as B-778 on B-162/B-163 and D-893. After Effects lowers the resolution while you drag (Adaptive Resolution, Fast Previews), and Nuke and Natron draw a proxy while a value is scrubbed; ours drew Draft (a quarter each way) at best. **Why.** On the 25-layer shot on the processor, a dragged feathered mask still took 80 ms or more to show at Draft. Masks are drawn at full size, and all 16 moments of the shutter are drawn whatever the quality. **What was built.** (1) `PreviewQuality::Motion`, labelled "In motion": an eighth of the composition each way (`MOTION_DIVISOR` 8 in `src/preview.rs`), masks drawn at that size, and at most four moments of any switched-on shutter (`MOTION_SAMPLES` 4, `fewer_samples`). This covers the composition's motion blur and a layer's Force Motion Blur, Pixel Motion Blur and Timewarp. A project is copied only when one of them asks for more than four, so a switched-off shutter's default of 16 copies nothing. (2) A drawing taken down an eighth for a frame in motion is held in the cel cache beside the whole drawing (`CelCache::smaller`). Its key is the drawing's own key with "#1/8" added to its path. It counts in the same memory budget and is dropped oldest first with the rest. The whole drawing's own lookup can never return it. (3) In the page, with Refine when idle ticked, every frame asked for while the hand moves is asked `?q=motion`, whatever quality is chosen (Full, Half or Draft; before this, only Full asked for Draft). 0.2 s after the hand stops, the frame is asked at the chosen quality and replaces it. The window never stores Motion as the chosen quality and never keeps an In motion frame in the frame memory. It labels the frame "In motion" with `x-differs` true. (4) On the graphics card, a frame asked in motion is drawn at Draft and labelled Draft. True In motion measured slower there: move 32 to 43 ms, scale 35 to 41, scrub 32 to 39 on L25 Draft. A second try, without first taking the eighth down, gave move 29 to 38, scale 30 to 42, scrub 28 to 34. The card's cost is in its draws, not its pixels. **What this reopens.** D-50 declined drawings at draft resolution because they would change what the preview shows. In motion is the same drawings at a smaller size, labelled, never kept, and always replaced by the chosen picture, which is the line D-50 drew. D-269's "Masks at Draft resolution" is built for In motion only. The rule that Draft pixels do not change still holds: Draft, Half, Full, final frames, stored checks and exports are byte for byte as before. **Checked** (`app/src/tests/in_motion.rs`, `verification/B-778_in_motion_table.md`): An In motion frame is labelled In motion, not final, 240 by 135. Asked again, it is made afresh, and the frame memory holds no more. The chosen quality stays Full. The Full picture afterwards is byte for byte Full asked for alone. After each of these, the picture once still is byte for byte that quality asked for alone, and the In motion frame is the one asked for alone: a feathered mask added, the mask dragged, an undo, a frame change, Half, Draft, and a switch of composition. On the card, the frame in motion is byte for byte the card's Draft and labelled Draft. The eighth of a drawing is counted in the cache's budget, given back when asked again, and never returned to a request that is not in motion. Another size gets its own entry. The shutter rows pass. The B-162/B-163 table (`verification/B-163_refine_on_stop_table.md`, 23 of 23) and the B-773 (stoppable frames) table pass with In motion in place of Draft. **Measured** in the real program: release build; RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, Vulkan; AMD64 Family 26 Model 68, 24 threads; a machine shared with other lanes' builds and lag runs; wave 8's reference shot with 25 layers (L25); viewer on the processor and on the graphics card, with Draft and Full chosen; the delay from the hand's move to the picture drawn; 5 alternating before/after rounds, 10 runs a row; "before" is main at 47f215a0. Results are median ms before to after, with p95 in brackets. Processor, Draft chosen: mask 81 to 50 (100 to 67), number 67 to 46 (88 to 64), scale 63 to 48 (82 to 64), scrub 46 to 41 (56 to 45), move 39 to 36 (51 to 50), bar 45 to 44 (69 to 50). Processor, Full chosen: mask 82 to 46 (99 to 63), number 64 to 47 (86 to 64), scale 61 to 51 (79 to 65), scrub 44 to 39 (48 to 46), move 37 to 36 (46 to 44), bar 43 to 46 (53 to 48). The bar row is within the spread: runs were 36 to 49 before and 35 to 50 after. Graphics card, Draft chosen: mask 62 to 66, move 37 to 38, scale 36 to 37, scrub 30 to 30, bar 32 to 33, number 37 to 36. The mask row is within the spread: runs were 55 to 81 before and 57 to 81 after. Graphics card, Full chosen: mask 67 to 62, move 38 to 28, scale 40 to 43, scrub 39 to 36, bar 35 to 30, number 42 to 40. The "key" gesture gave no rows in either build. Two earlier builds made the processor's move and scrub slower. In one, the project was copied every frame for a switched-off shutter. In the other, masked drawings were taken down afresh every frame (3 to 8 ms, against 1 at Draft). Both were fixed before this run. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing. **Fixtures:** none changed, none added. **Gaps.** (1) L4 was not measured on the final build. An earlier build showed L4 gains (processor Draft mask 71 to 32), but it had the copy fault above. (2) A frame the window sends from its memory reports itself drawn on the processor. (3) On the card with Draft chosen, the frame asked for once still is the same Draft picture, made a second time. (4) Half's sharpen check `pre == 0.5` never matches, because `pre` is the divisor 2. So Half is never mapped back from a held plan. This costs a re-plan, not a wrong picture. (5) The release build measured lacked only the test rows and the D-898 comments. **If refused:** in `app/ui/index.html`, make `askedAs` return the request as asked (Full asking for Draft, as before), and the window never asks for In motion. To take it out fully, remove `PreviewQuality::Motion`, `MOTION_DIVISOR`, `MOTION_SAMPLES`, `fewer_samples`, `CelCache::smaller`, the "motion" query in `app/src/main.rs` and `app/src/tests/in_motion.rs`. Nothing saved depends on it.

D-900 / The RAM preview made by several workers at once, and at rest once the hand is still (wave 11, pick 5, lane L5, After Effects' multi-frame rendering) / **PROPOSED on 2026-10-26, both parts switched off; the part that makes frames ahead give way to the hand is built and on.** On 2026-10-26 the owner asked how After Effects, Nuke and other professional programs balance speed against exact pixels, and what we should do to compete (research in `S/wave11/pros_research.html`); the owner answered: "Do all of your picks at your recommended order. Defer or tackle until solved if consequential to your discretion." This is the fifth pick, built as B-780. The bar set for it: a faster first playback on the 25-layer shot (L25) and on a heavy-effect shot (document 08's declared ten layers, blurred and graded), with drag and scrub no slower beyond the spread between rounds, frames byte for byte the frames of one worker, and no stale frame after an edit, an undo or a composition switch; if not met after two real approaches, switched off and left PROPOSED. **Not met, so both parts are off.** **What was built.** (1) The render-ahead (B-154) takes a worker count, `AHEAD_WORKERS` in `app/src/main.rs`, 1: several workers claim frames from one shared list for the current sight (project, composition, quality, card), so no frame is made twice, and the card keeps one worker. (2) Frames are made ahead at rest, `AHEAD_AT_REST`, `false`: once a frame has been asked by hand and the hand has been still for half a second (`AHEAD_IDLE`), the loop round the playhead is made as if playing; never during a drag or an export. (3) On in the program: every frame made ahead is drawn inside `anime_compositor::stop::behind` (`src/stop.rs`), so any frame asked for by hand (`by_hand`, at the top of every viewer frame) or a `/stop` (D-893) stops it at the next point it looks, between layers or tiles, and nothing of it is kept; such frames are drawn on their own threads (`stop::pool`, below normal priority) so a frame asked for by hand never queues behind them; a worker holds the card's lock only while it draws on the card, since every frame asked for by hand looks at that lock. A frame made for a sight that has changed since (an edit, an undo, another composition) is not kept. (4) Beside several workers, and at rest, a worker draws with cels of its own, a quarter of the memory setting split between them and taken from the viewer's cels (`AHEAD_CELS`), so the memory setting is never exceeded and the picture B-159 keeps below the last edit is not pushed out; the first approach to (2), drawing with the viewer's own cels, pushed it out, so the next edit was drawn from nothing. **Checked** (`app/src/tests/ram_workers.rs`, `verification/B-780_ram_workers_table.md`, 30 of 30): with 4 workers, every frame of the reference shot at Draft and Full and every fourth of the ten declared layers is byte for byte the frame made by hand; layer 1 hidden while the loop is made: 240 of 240 frames from memory are the edited frame; after undo 0 stale; another composition opened while the loop is made, and back: 0 frames of the other; at rest (switch on for the test), with 1 and 4 workers: nothing made in the first quarter second, only the frames asked while stepping, then the rest of the loop and every frame byte for byte the frame made by hand; a frame asked by hand while playing at Full: 0 frames made ahead in the 0.3 s after it; the B-159 picture below an edit is still used after a loop made at rest; with room for 50 Draft frames the workers stop at 50; the workers' own cels are given back. **Measured** (release builds; AMD Ryzen 9 9900X, 24 threads; RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, Vulkan; Windows 11; a machine shared with other lanes' builds and lag runs; base is main at 47f215a0). First play (`app/src/tests/ram_workers_time.rs`, ignored, run deliberately: press Play, play one 240-frame loop as the page does, with and without a 2 s rest on frame 0 first; medians of 5 alternating rounds; seconds until 24 frames are held, and frames dropped): **several workers** (4 against 1, at rest on): not faster on the processor: on L25 it dropped 7 to 28 fewer frames in three of four rows, but on the ten declared layers at Draft it dropped 107 against 32, and after a rest 90 against 0, and took 7.9 s against 4.4 to hold 120 frames; each worker's smaller cels and the contention between them cost more than the extra threads gave (the card keeps one worker either way; its rows moved by up to 50 dropped frames between these two runs of the same code, which is the spread here). **At rest** (1 worker, on against base): after a 2 s rest, 24 frames held at Play in 0.0 to 0.2 s against 0.7 to 2.0 s in seven of eight rows, and on L25 on the processor at Full in 4.6 s against 8.7; frames dropped fell on L25 on the processor at Draft (7 against 32) and not beyond the spread elsewhere; without a rest, no change beyond the spread. But the next drag on the processor at Full was slower (lag harness, the delay from the hand's move to the picture drawn, 5 alternating rounds, L4, median ms base to at rest): mask 32 to 93, mask with a pause 41 to 68, move 22 to 37, move with a pause 26 to 37, processor Draft move 23 to 31; the card's rows were unchanged (Full mask 50 to 51, move 24 to 22). Two rounds each of variants (no reserved cels, no disk cache, fewer threads, 4 or 2) did not find one cause; most likely a frame still in flight when the hand comes back competes for the processor and memory bandwidth for the moment it takes to stop. **The program as built (both off) against base**: first play within the spread between rounds (L25 on the processor at Draft, no rest: 24 frames in 1.8 s against 1.7, 54 frames dropped against 50; the ten declared layers on the card at Full: 24 dropped against 185, a row where the same base build read 37.5 in ten earlier rounds); drag and scrub (lag harness as D-893, the delay from the hand's move to the picture drawn, 3 alternating rounds of L4 and L25 on the processor and the card, Draft and Full, every gesture, then 4 more of the processor Full mask, mask with a pause and scrub rows, median ms base to built): within the spread, e.g. L25 processor Draft move 44 to 37, mask 79 to 78, L25 card Full mask 60 to 70, move 40 to 42, L4 card Draft scrub 23 to 35 (p95 50 to 81), L4 processor Full mask 32 to 34 and in the 4 more 41 to 35; L25 processor Full mask, where each run paints a single frame, read 217 to 373 in the 3 rounds with single runs from 41 to 811 ms in both builds, and 81 to 79 in the 4 more, mask with a pause 48 to 65 and scrub 43 to 52 in the 4 more. With both switches off nothing is made ahead during a drag or a scrub in either build (frames are made ahead only after Play), and the only code added on that path is one counter per frame, so these rows move by the spread between runs. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing. **Fixtures:** none changed, none added. **Proposed, for the owner:** (a) switch `AHEAD_AT_REST` on with the viewer on the card only, where the drag did not slow and the first second of play after a rest is ready about 1 s sooner, though no fewer frames are dropped; (b) leave several workers off until each can share one cel cache. **If refused:** remove `AHEAD_WORKERS`, `AHEAD_AT_REST`, `AHEAD_CELS` and the worker's own cels in `app/src/main.rs`, `stop::behind`, `by_hand` and `pool` in `src/stop.rs`, the `Win32_System_Threading` feature in `Cargo.toml` and the two tests; nothing saved depends on it.

D-902 / A PNG's own colour information is named when it is not read: `MEDIA_COLOR_METADATA_IGNORED` (wave 11, pick 7, lane L7C1, step C1 of the colour-management plan) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-26**. On 2026-10-26 the owner asked how After Effects, Nuke and other professional programs balance speed against exact pixels, and what we should do to compete (research in `S/wave11/pros_research.html`); the owner answered: "Do all of your picks at your recommended order. Defer or tackle until solved if consequential to your discretion." This is step C1 of pick 7's plan (`S/wave11/L7/PLAN.md`), built as B-782. **Why.** Document 21 reads every PNG as sRGB, and says embedded profiles and gamma "require decoder-specific tests before being claimed as supported". Until now a PNG's sRGB, gAMA, cHRM, iCCP and cICP chunks were never looked at, so a file saved with a linear gamma, Rec. 2020 primaries, an ICC profile or an HDR (PQ) code was drawn as sRGB without a word: the silent fidelity fallback document 28 and CLAUDE.md forbid. **The rule.** At import, each PNG's header is read for those five chunks. When any one of them says something other than sRGB, the new warning `MEDIA_COLOR_METADATA_IGNORED` names the file and every colour chunk it carries with its stored numbers, in the order sRGB, gAMA, cHRM, iCCP, cICP: `sRGB`; `gAMA <stored value>` (100000 is gamma 1.0); `cHRM white x y, red x y, green x y, blue x y` (the stored values, 100000 to 1); `iCCP <n> bytes` (the profile's size; the profile is not read); `cICP <primaries>/<transfer>/<matrix>/<full range>`. The picture is drawn exactly as before, as sRGB with its numbers unchanged: no pixel, cache key or saved byte changes. A sequence says it once, naming its pattern and the drawings (`1-3`), as document 28 asks of repeated warnings (D-25); a still chosen on its own says it once, at import. **Exactly sRGB is quiet** (a choice): an sRGB chunk (any rendering intent), a cHRM of the sRGB primaries and D65 white (31270 32900, 64000 33000, 30000 60000, 15000 6000) and a cICP of 1/13/0/1 (BT.709 primaries, the sRGB curve, full range) state exactly what the build already assumes, so a file whose colour chunks all say that is drawn with no warning; a gAMA of 45455 is quiet beside an sRGB chunk, which the PNG specification says takes its place. This is the combination the PNG specification asks sRGB writers to store (sRGB with gAMA 45455 and those cHRM values), so warning on it would put a note on ordinary files and teach people to ignore the list. A gAMA of 45455 with no sRGB chunk does warn: it asks for a plain 1/2.2 power curve, not the sRGB curve, and the two differ by up to 9 levels of 255 (at level 16, measured over all 256 levels), which is visible in shadows. An iCCP chunk always warns, even beside sRGB, because the profile is never read and could say anything. Once any chunk is not quiet, every colour chunk is listed, quiet ones too, because the combination is what a person checks. **EXR keeps `MEDIA_EXR_ADJUSTED`.** An EXR whose `chromaticities` are not Rec. 709 already says so by name: D-62's `MEDIA_EXR_ADJUSTED` with the reason `primaries` and all eight numbers, once at import, and `Fixtures/exr/expected_exr.json` holds that text. A second ID for the same fact would say it twice and change a stored expected value for nothing, so the EXR case is left as it is; document 28's new row points to it. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing; the warning is said at import and is not saved. **Fixtures.** New: `Fixtures/colour/metadata/`, eleven 2 by 2 PNGs and a three-drawing sequence, all written byte by byte by `tools/colour_metadata_reference.py` (Python's standard library, sharing nothing with the build's decoder), and `expected_colour_metadata.json` with each file's expected chunk list and the picture every file must decode to (FX-COLMETA-001 to 003 in document 25). No existing fixture changes. **Gaps.** (1) PNG only: JPEG, TIFF and WebP ICC profiles and EXIF colour tags are still not looked at (the `image` crate decodes them as sRGB); a later unit. (2) The mDCV and cLLI HDR chunks are not named; they only mean something with a cICP, which is. (3) A malformed iCCP chunk, which the PNG decoder drops, is not named. (4) Each PNG's header is read twice at import, once for its size and once for its colour chunks; a header read is small. **If refused.** Remove `colour_chunks`, `colour_metadata` and the two calls in `src/media.rs` and `app/src/main.rs`, and the ID; files draw as they did.

D-905 / Colour management: our own named spaces, OpenColorIO as the outside judge (ADR-023; wave 11, pick 7, lane CM1, step C0 of the colour-management plan) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-26**. On 2026-10-26 the owner asked how After Effects, Nuke and other professional programs balance speed against exact pixels, and what we should do to compete (research in `S/wave11/pros_research.html`); the owner answered: "Do all of your picks at your recommended order. Defer or tackle until solved if consequential to your discretion." Pick 7 is colour management; its plan (`S/wave11/L7/PLAN.md`) put nine questions, and the owner answered: "go with your recommended answers for colour management". This is step C0, a record only: no code, no fixture and no pixel changes. **Why.** The build has one fixed pipeline (sRGB in, linear Rec.709 inside, sRGB out) whose primaries are never named; After Effects (26.5: OpenColorIO 2.5.1 with the ACES 2.0 configs), Nuke, Resolve and Blender all name their working space, tag files and offer viewer transforms. **The decision (ADR-023, `docs/adr/0023-colour-management.md`).** The hybrid of the plan's three options: our own named spaces and curves in `src/color.rs`, from their published specifications, matrices from the chromaticities in double precision; OpenColorIO used offline only, as the judge that writes expected values, never linked; the ACES output transform, too large to port, baked once into a table by OpenColorIO. **The owner's nine answers, as recommended.** (1) The working space with colour management on is ACEScg by default; linear Rec.709 is also offered. (2) ACES 2.0 only. (3) The ACES view as a table baked by OpenColorIO, within 1 level of 255 on 99.9% of pixels against OpenColorIO's own maths, is acceptable. (4) With colour management on only the Display and Float depths; 8 bpc (AE) and 32 bpc (AE) are refused with a reason. (5) Stored colours keep their look when the working space changes. (6) Exports never take the viewer's look unless chosen in the export's own Output. (7) No studio `.ocio` configs now (step C8 waits). (8) Lanes may install PyOpenColorIO, pinned, from PyPI in a separate tools environment, never shipped; recorded as a tool dependency in `docs/DEPENDENCIES.md` (purpose, version 2.5.1, BSD-3-Clause, no distribution impact). (9) An sRGB monitor is assumed; no wide-gamut or HDR display. Reference images are synthetic (charts and ramps we write); the Academy's test images are not downloaded, and OpenColorIO's built-in ACES 2.0 config is read by its URI, so nothing is downloaded. **The hard rule for every step.** Colour management is off by default, and off means every pixel, file, cache key and stored value byte for byte as before this decision, proved by the existing suites. **What changes.** Document 18 gains ADR-023, and ADR-007 now says OpenColorIO is the offline reference, still not linked. Document 21 gains "Colour spaces" (the primaries, whites, Bradford adaptation, curves and conversion order, and how they are checked). Document 28 gains three reserved identifiers outside the Core IDs table, which only holds what the build raises: `COLOR_SPACE_UNKNOWN` (C3), `COLOR_DEPTH_REFUSED` (C4) and `COLOR_VIEW_UNAVAILABLE` (C5). **The steps.** C1 (D-902) and C2 (D-906) are built; C3 to C7 follow in that order, each a D and B pair, fixture before code; C8 waits for the owner. **What it reopens, only while colour management is on.** ADR-007 (here), D-07 (C3), D-17 (C2: kept as one curve of several), D-62 (C3: the user chooses, never guessed), D-74, D-182 and D-822 with document 21's display-value rules (C4), D-319, D-330, D-333 and D-763 (C4), document 08 and document 20 step 9 (C5), D-73 (C6). D-23, ADR-006 and D-100a are unchanged. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing. **Fixtures.** None. **If refused.** Remove ADR-023 and its record, document 21's "Colour spaces", document 28's reserved section and ADR-007's last sentence; D-906's library is unused by the app and can go with it.

D-906 / The named colour spaces and curves, checked against OpenColorIO, not yet used by the app (ADR-023; wave 11, pick 7, lane CM1, step C2 of the colour-management plan) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-26**. On 2026-10-26 the owner asked how After Effects, Nuke and other professional programs balance speed against exact pixels, and what we should do to compete (research in `S/wave11/pros_research.html`); the owner answered: "Do all of your picks at your recommended order. Defer or tackle until solved if consequential to your discretion." For pick 7's colour-management plan the owner answered: "go with your recommended answers for colour management". This is step C2, built as B-785. **Why.** Every later step (input tags, the working space, the viewer's view, export outputs) converts between named spaces; the conversions come first, each checked against an outside judge before anything uses them. **The rule** (document 21, "Colour spaces"). `src/color.rs` gains five primaries-and-white sets (Rec.709, ACES AP1, ACES AP0, Rec.2020, P3-D65), six curves (linear, sRGB, BT.1886 gamma 2.4, gamma 2.2, ACEScct, ACEScc) and ten named spaces built from them (linear Rec.709, sRGB, BT.1886 and gamma 2.2 encoded Rec.709, ACEScg, ACEScct, ACEScc, ACES2065-1, linear Rec.2020, linear P3-D65). A conversion decodes each channel, applies a 3 by 3 matrix worked out in double precision from the chromaticities, and encodes each channel; the colour is rounded to single precision once, at the end. **The white adaptation is Bradford, measured, not assumed.** Where the whites differ (the ACES white against D65), OpenColorIO's config gives its Rec.709-to-ACES2065-1 matrix as literal numbers; the Bradford matrix computed here equals them to 2.4e-15 (first entry 2.5216861867438833 against OpenColorIO's 2.52168618674388), CAT02's differs at the fourth decimal (2.52193), and by up to 5.2e-3 in an entry over the three D65 spaces against AP0 and AP1. **sRGB stays D-17's curve**, byte for byte, through the functions the build already uses. **Where OpenColorIO does not follow the published formula, the build follows the formula,** and says so: OpenColorIO's sRGB is a smooth power curve whose straight bottom piece ends at 0.0393 with slope 12.923, where the standard's ends at 0.04045 with 12.92 (between 0 and 1 at most 6.6e-7 apart in linear light and 6.3e-6 encoded, under a hundredth of a level of 255; below 0, where both carry the straight piece on, 2.5e-4 of the number); OpenColorIO's ACEScc is a 4096-step table clamped to -0.36..1.5 with negatives set to 0 (3e-6 off mid-range, 3e-4 when encoding), and its ACEScct encoding, worked in single precision, cancels at -0.01 to land 1.2e-6 of the answer off the formula. Neither ACES log curve is capped at 65504, as in OpenColorIO. Gamma 2.4 and 2.2 pass negative numbers unchanged, as OpenColorIO's. OpenColorIO's default optimisation (which allows an approximate power, off by 2.5e-5 on sRGB) is not used: the reference runs at `OPTIMIZATION_LOSSLESS`. **The bar**, set in the fixture before the code was run: |build - OpenColorIO| at most 1e-6 times the sample's size; for the rows where OpenColorIO leaves the formula, the same bar against the formula worked in double precision, which the fixture also carries. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing; nothing in the app calls the new functions, colour management stays off, and today's functions are not touched. **Fixtures.** New: `Fixtures/colour/expected_conversions.json` (FX-COLCONV-001 to 003 in document 25), written by `tools/ocio_reference.py` with PyOpenColorIO 2.5.1 from its built-in config `ocio://studio-config-v4.0.0_aces-v2.0_ocio-v2.5`, nothing downloaded: 30 conversions (the 20 pairs of the five linear spaces, each curve both ways) on 5,200 linear and 5,177 encoded samples, including numbers below 0 and up to 64, and OpenColorIO's five matrices to ACES2065-1. No existing fixture changes. **Evidence.** `tests/b785_colour_conversions.rs` writes `verification/B-785_conversion_table.md`; its playtest is `verification/B-785_playtest.md`. **Gaps.** (1) The app does not use any of this yet (C3). (2) Camera log curves (LogC, S-Log3, V-Log, Apple Log) are not in the list (C8). (3) No card copy yet; the card needs none until C5. (4) `convert` works the matrix out on every call; a caller converting pictures keeps `gamut_matrix` once. **If refused.** Remove the section after today's functions in `src/color.rs`, the test, the tool and the fixture; nothing else uses them.

D-909 / "Interpret as" per file, and colour management's working space in the project file, converted at decode; the switch itself not in the window until C4 and C5 (ADR-023; wave 11, pick 7, lane CM3, step C3 of the colour-management plan) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-26**. On 2026-10-26 the owner asked how After Effects, Nuke and other professional programs balance speed against exact pixels, and what we should do to compete (research in `S/wave11/pros_research.html`); the owner answered: "Do all of your picks at your recommended order. Defer or tackle until solved if consequential to your discretion." For pick 7's colour-management plan the owner answered: "go with your recommended answers for colour management" (answer 1: ACEScg the working space by default with colour management on, linear Rec.709 also offered). This is step C3, built as B-788. **Why.** Until now a drawing could only say "sRGB" or "linear" (D-62: an EXR is linear Rec.709), so an EXR rendered in ACES (ACES2065-1 or ACEScg, as 3D renderers and Nuke deliver them) was drawn with the wrong primaries: washed out, its reds orange. After Effects, Nuke and Resolve let the user say what a file is. **The rule (document 21, "Colour spaces", Interpret as).** An image asset's `interpretation.color_space` takes one of ten words: today's `srgb` and `linear-srgb`, and new `acescg`, `aces2065-1`, `acescct`, `acescc`, `linear-rec2020`, `linear-p3-d65`, `bt1886-rec709` (gamma 2.4) and `gamma22-rec709`, which are D-906's named spaces. At decode (document 21 step 1) each channel goes through the space's curve to linear light, then through D-906's 3 by 3 matrix from the space's primaries to the working space's, in double precision, rounded to single precision once; then, for straight alpha, the colour is multiplied by alpha, as before. The matrix is worked out once per picture, not per pixel. An 8-bit drawing takes the curve from the per-byte tables D-897 made (now one per curve), then the matrix. **A new word works with colour management off.** It converts into today's working space, linear Rec.709, which is what the drawing's numbers mean; today's two words are untouched, byte for byte, so every project saved before this draws exactly as it did. After Effects ignores a file's profile when its project has no working space; we do not, because the user chose the word, the conversion is exact, and drawing an ACES file as Rec.709 is the error the word exists to correct. Document 21's "while off, nothing changes" therefore reads "nothing changes for anything saved before D-909". **"Interpret as" in the window.** The Project panel's line for a selected still or sequence gains an "Interpret as" list of the ten names (sRGB; Linear Rec.709; ACEScg; ACES2065-1; ACEScct; ACEScc; Linear Rec.2020; Linear P3-D65; Gamma 2.4 Rec.709 (BT.1886); Gamma 2.2 Rec.709), sending the new command `asset.set_interpretation` (document 24), one step of history. A sound or a lookup file has no such list (D-71, D-182). **Colour management in the project file.** `color_settings` gains `color_management`, written only when on (`true`); `working_space` may then be `acescg` (the default when on) or `linear-srgb`. With it on and the working space ACEScg, every drawing converts into ACEScg at decode, today's words included (an sRGB drawing's colours go through the sRGB curve and the Rec.709-to-ACEScg matrix). With it on and the working space linear Rec.709, every picture is exactly as with it off. `working_space` `acescg` without `color_management` is refused at opening as `PROJECT_SCHEMA_INVALID` (a working space other than today's needs the switch that says so), and so is a working-space word this build does not have: every pixel of the project depends on it, so no picture could be drawn honestly, and nothing on disk is changed (as for a newer schema version). **The switch is not in the window yet, my call under the owner's "to your discretion".** With ACEScg working and nothing else done, three things would be wrong on screen: stored colours (a solid's, a text's, a shape's fill, every effect's colour setting) are still linear Rec.709 numbers and would be read as ACEScg, so they would shift (C4, the owner's answer 5); the viewer still encodes the working numbers as if they were Rec.709, so every picture would look too saturated (C5, the ACES view); and the 8 bpc (AE) and 32 bpc (AE) depths are not yet refused with it on (C4, answer 4). A switch that makes pictures wrong is worse than no switch, so until C4 and C5 land a project has colour management on only through its file, and the record says so here, in document 21 and in the playtest. Such a file opens, draws its drawings in ACEScg, keeps its key and saves back byte for byte. **A word this build does not know** (from a later build, or typed by hand) is `COLOR_SPACE_UNKNOWN` (document 28, moved from the reserved list to Core IDs): the stored word is kept and saved back byte for byte; the asset draws as missing (transparent), never as sRGB; the person opening the project is told once, naming the asset and the word; every frame that would have drawn it says so in the frame's log, which marks an export made meanwhile as incomplete; the window's list shows the word as "not known to this build". **Caches (document 27).** The decoded-drawing key already holds the interpretation; it now holds the word, and with colour management on the working space too. For today's two words with it off the key is unchanged (the same digest on disk, so no decoded drawing is thrown away).
