The finished-frame cache compares the whole project, the new setting included. **The graphics card** needs nothing: the conversion happens before a drawing reaches it. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing for any project saved before this; a new word appears only when the user picks one, and `color_management` only in a file that has it. Old projects open exactly as before (FX-COLINT-005). **Fixtures.** New, in `Fixtures/colour/interpret/`, written by `tools/interpret_reference.py` with PyOpenColorIO 2.5.1 (D-906's tool dependency; its built-in config `ocio://studio-config-v4.0.0_aces-v2.0_ocio-v2.5`, `OPTIMIZATION_LOSSLESS`, nothing downloaded; both pictures written with Python's standard library): `media/aces_chart.exr`, a 144 by 120 float chart stored in ACES2065-1 (the 24 ColorChecker patches from X-Rite's published sRGB values, converted by OpenColorIO, and a sixth row of ACEScg colours outside Rec.709 and greys up to 8); `media/ramp.png`, a 16 by 16 8-bit ramp with alphas from 0 to 255; ten projects tagging them; and `expected_interpretation.json`, OpenColorIO's numbers for every case and, for the 8-bit ramp, the published curve worked in double precision with OpenColorIO's matrix, the judge for the sRGB and ACEScc rows where OpenColorIO leaves the formula (D-906). FX-COLINT-001 to 007 in document 25. The bar, set before the code: |build - expected| at most 1e-6 times the colour's size (at least 1), every pixel; and the chart tagged ACES2065-1 in today's working space shows X-Rite's own bytes again through today's view, every ColorChecker patch exactly. `Schemas/project-v0.schema.json` gains the words, `color_management` and `acescg`. No existing fixture changes. **Evidence.** `tests/b788_interpret_as.rs` writes `verification/B-788_interpret_as_table.md` (every case against OpenColorIO, the chart's view bytes against X-Rite's, the unknown word kept, the refusals, the old projects); pictures of the chart tagged three ways through the real app in `verification/B-788 pictures/`; the playtest `verification/B-788_playtest.md`. **Gaps.** (1) C4: stored colours, display-value rules and the depth refusal are not done; with colour management on, a solid, text, shape or effect colour is read as an ACEScg number. (2) C5: the viewer has no ACES view; with ACEScg working the picture looks too saturated. (3) Hence no switch in the window (above). (4) The Project panel's thumbnails and the import preview still draw a file as sRGB or linear Rec.709 whatever its word, as before. (5) An EXR's own `chromaticities` are still only reported (`MEDIA_EXR_ADJUSTED` `primaries`, D-62), never used to choose a word; a PNG's colour chunks likewise (D-902). (6) Exports still write sRGB from the working numbers; with ACEScg working an export holds ACEScg numbers labelled sRGB (C6). (7) Camera log curves are not offered (C8). **If refused.** Remove the eight new words, `color_management`, `acescg` and `asset.set_interpretation`; a project that used them would then be refused at opening; today's projects are unaffected either way.
D-915 / The viewer's colour view with colour management on: Standard, Un-tone-mapped and ACES 2.0 SDR, the ACES view a table baked by OpenColorIO; the switch still not in the window until C4 lands (ADR-023; wave 11, pick 7, lane CM5, step C5 of the colour-management plan) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-26**. On 2026-10-26 the owner asked how After Effects, Nuke and other professional programs balance speed against exact pixels, and what we should do to compete (research in `S/wave11/pros_research.html`); the owner answered: "Do all of your picks at your recommended order. Defer or tackle until solved if consequential to your discretion." For pick 7's colour-management plan the owner answered: "go with your recommended answers for colour management" (answer 2: ACES 2.0 only; answer 3: the ACES view as a table baked by OpenColorIO, within 1 level of 255 on 99.9% of pixels against OpenColorIO's own maths, is acceptable; answer 6: exports never take the viewer's look unless chosen in the export's own Output; answer 9: an sRGB monitor). This is step C5, built as B-794. **Why.** With colour management on and ACEScg working (D-909), the viewer still put the working numbers through D-17's sRGB curve as if they were Rec.709, so every picture looked too saturated, and anything brighter than 1 clipped hard to flat white or a flat primary. After Effects 26.5 (OpenColorIO mode), Nuke, Resolve and Blender show the working space through a display's view, and their default is the ACES output transform, which rolls highlights off and keeps their hue. **The rule (document 21, "Colour spaces", The view).** With colour management on, the viewer shows the picture through one of three views, applied once, at the 8-bit encode, after the unpremultiply: **ACES 2.0 SDR** (the default when on; OpenColorIO's view "ACES 2.0 - SDR 100 nits (Rec.709)" of its "sRGB - Display"): the working colour to ACEScg by D-906's matrix (none when the working space is ACEScg), D-906's ACEScct curve, then a tetrahedral lookup in a table of 97 by 97 by 97 colours that OpenColorIO baked, which gives the sRGB display's values; **Un-tone-mapped** (OpenColorIO's "Un-tone-mapped"): the working colour to linear Rec.709 by D-906's matrix (none when the working space is linear Rec.709), then D-17's sRGB curve, clipped at 0 and 1 by the quantiser as today; **Standard**: today's encode, D-17's sRGB curve on the working numbers, byte for byte (with ACEScg working it shows the numbers as if they were Rec.709, for comparison). Alpha is quantised as before. With colour management off there is no view: the viewer is Standard, exactly today's. **Where the view is applied, and where not.** The viewer only: the processor's encode of a viewer frame, the graphics card's encode pass (the same table and the same steps in single precision), the frames made ahead while playing, and the soloed and onion-skin pictures the viewer shows. Never an export or a render to file (answer 6; step C6 adds the export's own Output choice), never a trace image (D-23), never the Project panel's thumbnails, and never D-907's card export, which reads the card's floats, not its bytes. A frame in 8 bpc (After Effects), whose card sum is in display values, is drawn by the processor while a view other than Standard is shown (`GPU_PREVIEW_ON_CPU`, INFO); step C4 refuses that depth with colour management on. **The table.** `assets/colour/aces2_sdr_srgb_97.f32`, written by `tools/view_reference.py` with OpenColorIO 2.5.1's Baker (its built-in config `ocio://studio-config-v4.0.0_aces-v2.0_ocio-v2.5`, input space ACEScct, 97 points a side), stored as the Baker's numbers in little-endian single precision (10.9 MB, built into the program; the same as a 25 MB .cube text). It lives in `assets/`, not `Fixtures/`, because the program ships it, as it ships its fonts; its expected values and its SHA-256, the recorded check, are in `Fixtures/colour/view/expected_view.json`. On the card it is sent once, when a view other than Standard is first shown. **How the table's size was chosen, measured before the code** (by the reference tool's own lookup in Python against OpenColorIO's analytic view, on the fixture's barred cases, 2,576 pixels: a white ramp and a fire gradient up to 64 times white, and the 24 ColorChecker patches from 4 stops under to 6 over, from both working spaces): 65 points with trilinear lookup, the plan's first size, 97.9% within 1 level on a 40,000-colour stress set; 65 with tetrahedral lookup, 99.767% on the barred cases (the chart 99.24%, the fire 99.80%): misses; other shapers (a plain log2 of 20 stops, a sixth-root power) were worse than ACEScct at 65 (96.7% and 93.3% on the stress set); 97 with trilinear, 99.922% (the chart 99.62%); 97 with tetrahedral, 100% of the barred cases, so 97 with tetrahedral is taken; 129 with tetrahedral is also 100% at 2.4 times the size. Where a table cannot follow ACES 2.0 is its gamut compression of very saturated colours at and above white: pure Rec.709 primaries ramped up to 64 times white and a stress set half outside Rec.709 stay below the bar at every size tried (the 40,000-colour stress set: 98.85% at 65, 99.80% at 97, 99.875% at 129, tetrahedral), and are reported beside the bar, not hidden. **In the project file.** `color_settings` may carry `view`: `aces-2.0-sdr`, `un-tone-mapped` or `standard`, read only with colour management on; absent means ACES 2.0 SDR. A file that has `view` gets it rewritten with the view in use; a file without it gets it only when the view chosen is not ACES 2.0 SDR, so every D-909 file saves back byte for byte. With colour management off `view` is not read and is saved back unchanged. A `view` that is not a word is `PROJECT_SCHEMA_INVALID` at `/color_settings/view`. **A word this build does not have** (from a later build, or typed by hand) is `COLOR_VIEW_UNAVAILABLE` (document 28, moved from the reserved list to Core IDs, its meaning widened from a table that fails its check to a view the build cannot show): the word is kept and saved back byte for byte, the viewer shows Standard, the person opening the project is told once, naming the word, and the View menu's list shows it as "not known to this build, Standard shown". The table is built into the program and its check is a test, so a table that fails cannot reach a person. **In the window.** The View menu gains a "Colour view" list (ACES 2.0 SDR, Un-tone-mapped, Standard), shown only while the project has colour management on, sending the new command `project.set_view` (document 24), one step of history; with colour management off it is refused and the list is not there. **The switch for colour management is still not in the window, my call under the owner's "to your discretion".** D-909's reasons stand while C4 is not on main: stored colours would still be read as ACEScg numbers and the 8 bpc (After Effects) and 32 bpc (After Effects) depths are not yet refused; so a project has colour management on only through its file, and the View menu's list appears only for such a file. When C4 lands, the switch can be offered with both steps done. **Caches (document 27).** The finished-frame cache compares the whole project, so the view is in its key; with colour management off the view is never read, so every key is as before. No other cache holds encoded bytes. **The graphics card.** The encode pass reads one more number, the view, in the slot that was always 0, and a fourth buffer, the table; with the number 0 it does exactly today's arithmetic, so every card picture with colour management off is the same bytes, proved by the existing card suites (B-754's float frames, B-222's colour effects and the card tables). **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing for any project saved before this; `view` appears only when the user picks a view other than ACES 2.0 SDR in a file that has colour management on. **Fixtures.** New, in `Fixtures/colour/view/`, written by `tools/view_reference.py` with PyOpenColorIO 2.5.1 (D-906's tool dependency; `OPTIMIZATION_LOSSLESS`; nothing downloaded; the picture written with Python's standard library): `media/hdr_scene.exr`, 512 by 256 float, linear Rec.709, eight bands of 32 rows (a white ramp from 1/256 to 64, a fire gradient from black through deep red, orange and yellow to 64, and pure red, green, blue, cyan, magenta and yellow ramps to 64); six projects showing it (ACES by default, Un-tone-mapped, Standard, an unknown view word, and colour management off with and without a `view`); and `expected_view.json`, OpenColorIO's analytic ACES 2.0 SDR and Un-tone-mapped views, as 8-bit levels, of every band, the chart and the stress set, from both working spaces, with the table's SHA-256. FX-COLVIEW-001 to 006 in document 25. The bar, set before the code: within 1 level of 255 on every channel on at least 99.9% of the barred cases' pixels, for each view and each working space; the reported rows are printed beside it; the card's encode within 1 level of the processor's on every pixel, Display and Float, frames past 1 included. `Schemas/project-v0.schema.json` gains `view`. No existing fixture changes. **Evidence.** `tests/b794_colour_view.rs` writes `verification/B-794_colour_view_table.md` (the table's check, every case against OpenColorIO, the card against the processor, the project files, off is today); Standard beside ACES of the HDR scene in `verification/B-794 pictures/`; the playtest `verification/B-794_playtest.md`. **Gaps.** (1) No colour-management switch in the window until C4 (above). (2) Very saturated colours at and above white miss the 1-level bar against OpenColorIO's analytic view by up to a few levels (reported rows); a bigger table does not cure it. (3) The Project panel's thumbnails, the import preview, the colour pickers and Info still show working numbers through Standard (C7). (4) Exports still write the working numbers through D-17's sRGB curve, whatever the view (answer 6; C6 adds the choice). (5) Only the sRGB display: no Rec.709 (BT.1886), P3 or HDR displays (answer 9, C8). **If refused.** Remove `view`, `project.set_view`, the View menu's list and the table; a project with colour management on shows Standard again; a saved `view` is then a key this build does not read, kept by the file's unknown-field rule; today's projects are unaffected either way.

D-910 / Colour management's stored colours, display-value rules and depths: the picture means the same in either working space (ADR-023; wave 11, pick 7, lane CM4, step C4 of the colour-management plan) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-26**. On 2026-10-26 the owner asked how After Effects, Nuke and other professional programs balance speed against exact pixels, and what we should do to compete (research in `S/wave11/pros_research.html`); the owner answered: "Do all of your picks at your recommended order. Defer or tackle until solved if consequential to your discretion." For pick 7's colour-management plan the owner answered: "go with your recommended answers for colour management" (answer 4: with colour management on only Display and Float are offered; answer 5: stored colours keep their meaning). This is step C4, built as B-789. **Why.** D-909 let a project work in ACEScg, but everything the user typed or picked is a linear Rec.709 number: a solid's colour (D-74), a text's or a shape's fill and stroke, a Gradient's or Fill's `#rrggbb`, a Tint's colours, an expression's colour (D-822). Read as ACEScg numbers those shift (an orange 0.8 0.3 0.05 shows redder and more saturated). And the rules that work on display values (Overlay and the other modes of D-301 and D-748, a luma matte, Levels, Curves, Hue/Saturation, Glow's threshold, Color Lookup, Gradient's mix) were written for Rec.709 numbers encoded by the sRGB curve; fed ACEScg numbers they give another picture. After Effects, with a working space set, reads a solid's colour and runs its display-referred effects in the working space, so a project changes look when its working space changes; we keep the look instead, which is the owner's answer 5. **The rule (document 21, "Colour spaces", Stored colours).** Only when colour management is on and the working space is ACEScg; with it off, or on with linear Rec.709, nothing below does anything, and every pixel, file, cache key and stored value is as today. (1) A stored colour is a linear Rec.709 number, always: a solid's colour, and a text layer's or shape layer's drawing (fills, strokes, gradients), are drawn as today, then go through D-906's Rec.709-to-ACEScg matrix, once. (2) A layer's effects run on linear Rec.709 numbers: the layer's picture goes through the ACEScg-to-Rec.709 matrix, its whole effect stack runs exactly as today (so every colour setting, every display-value rule and every expression colour means what it meant), and the result goes back through the Rec.709-to-ACEScg matrix. An adjustment layer's stack does the same with the picture beneath it. A picture an effect reads from another layer (a displacement map, a Set Matte source, Gradient Wipe's map) is given to it in Rec.709. (3) A blend mode other than Normal and Stencil Alpha mixes the two pictures as linear Rec.709 numbers (each through the matrix, mixed by today's rule, the result back): Multiply, Screen and Add included, because a product, or a sum held to 1, of two colours is not the same in two sets of primaries. Normal (over) and Stencil Alpha mix by alpha alone, which is the same in any primaries. (4) A luma or inverted luma matte reads its matte's luma from the matte's colour in Rec.709 (D-293's Rec.709 weights on Rec.709 numbers, through the sRGB curve). (5) Light Wrap reads both pictures in Rec.709. The matrices are D-906's, worked once in double precision; a picture is converted in single precision. Moves, scales, masks, feathers, opacity, motion blur, frame blending and over are sums of colours weighted by numbers that do not depend on the colour, so they give the same picture in either set of primaries and are not converted. **Depths (answer 4).** 8 bpc (AE) and 32 bpc (AE) copy After Effects' project without colour management (D-330, D-333); with colour management on they are refused with the new `COLOR_DEPTH_REFUSED` (document 28, moved from the reserved list to Core IDs). Choosing either in a composition's settings (`SET_COMPOSITION_SETTINGS`) is refused and the project left as it was, saying "With colour management on, a composition works in Display or Float: 8 bpc (AE) and 32 bpc (AE) copy After Effects without colour management."; a project file with colour management on and a composition in either depth is refused at opening with the same words, nothing on disk changed (no build writes one, and drawing it either way would be a guess). Display and Float are unchanged. **The graphics card** hands a frame of a project working in ACEScg to the processor, with `GPU_PREVIEW_ON_CPU` INFO "the project works in ACEScg, which the graphics card does not draw yet"; the card's copy of the conversions is left for later (gap 1), so the card never shows a different picture. With linear Rec.709 working the card draws as today. **Caches (document 27).** The finished-frame key gains the working space only when it is ACEScg; a layer's effect result is already keyed by its drawing's interpretation, which holds the working space (D-909). Keys with colour management off or working in linear Rec.709 are unchanged. **Gap 8 of B-788 closed.** An asset whose word this build does not know lost its word when saved by a project with no record of how it was opened (an asset brought back by undo after the project was saved without it): `COLOR_SPACE_UNKNOWN`'s word is now kept with the asset itself and always saved back. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing for any project saved before; a file with colour management on and an AE depth, which no build wrote, is now refused. **Fixtures (written before the code).** New, in `Fixtures/colour/c4/`, by `tools/c4_reference.py` with PyOpenColorIO 2.5.1 (D-906's tool dependency, its built-in config, `OPTIMIZATION_LOSSLESS`, nothing downloaded): four scenes, each a 16 by 4 composition saved twice with colour management on, once working in linear Rec.709 and once in ACEScg: an orange solid; a white solid under Gradient `#ff8000` to `#2040c0`, left to right; an Overlay of 0.6 0.1 0.4 over 0.2 0.5 0.05; and a red solid luma-matted by a hidden solid under Gradient `#000000` to `#40c0ff`, over black. Each scene's expected picture is worked from the published rules (D-74, D-114, D-301, D-293, the sRGB curve) in double precision, and its ACEScg numbers are OpenColorIO's conversion of it. Three more projects: colour management on with 8 bpc (AE), and with 32 bpc (AE), refused at opening; with Float, opened. FX-COLC4-001 to 005 in document 25. The bar, set before the code: every pixel within 1e-5 in linear light of the expected numbers in each working space, and the two working spaces' pictures the same bytes through today's view once the ACEScg picture is taken back to Rec.709 (the viewer's own ACES view is C5). Today's renderer already meets the linear Rec.709 half (worst 4.6e-8, measured before any code). No existing fixture changes. **Evidence.** `tests/b789_stored_colours.rs` writes `verification/B-789_stored_colours_table.md`; pictures of the four scenes in both working spaces in `verification/B-789 pictures/`; the playtest `verification/B-789_playtest.md`. **Gaps.** (1) The graphics card does not draw projects working in ACEScg (above); its copy of the conversions would be a separate step. (2) The viewer still shows working numbers as Rec.709 (C5), so the switch stays out of the window until C5, as D-909 said. (3) Effects run on Rec.709 numbers, so a colour from an ACES drawing outside Rec.709 (a negative Rec.709 number) is clipped by an effect that holds numbers to 0..1, as with colour management off; an effect that works per channel on linear numbers (Channel Mixer, Exposure) mixes Rec.709 channels, not ACEScg ones. (4) Display depth's hold of numbers to 0..1 applies to the working numbers; a Rec.709 colour from 0 to 1 stays from 0 to 1 in ACEScg, so only colours from outside Rec.709 meet it. (5) Exports still write the working numbers as sRGB (C6). **If refused.** Remove the conversions in `src/compose.rs` and `src/render.rs` and the depth refusals; a project working in ACEScg then reads its stored colours as ACEScg numbers, as after D-909.

D-917 / The export's Output with colour management on: sRGB, Rec.709 (BT.1886) or the ACES 2.0 SDR view for pictures, the working space, ACEScg or ACES2065-1 for EXR, each file labelled with what it holds (ADR-023; wave 11, pick 7, lane C6, step C6 of the colour-management plan) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-26**. For a picture format (PNG, animated PNG, GIF, MP4): `default`, **sRGB**: the working colour to linear Rec.709 by D-906's matrix (none when the working space is linear Rec.709), then D-17's sRGB curve, which is OpenColorIO's "Un-tone-mapped" view of "sRGB - Display" and D-915's Un-tone-mapped view; `rec709`, **Rec.709 (BT.1886)**: the same matrix, then D-906's BT.1886 curve (a pure power of 1/2.4, below 0 unchanged and so clipped to 0), OpenColorIO's "Un-tone-mapped" view of "Rec.1886 Rec.709 - Display"; `aces-view`, **ACES 2.0 SDR view**: D-915's view, its code and its table (`assets/colour/aces2_sdr_srgb_97.f32`) reused as they are, no second table: the working colour to ACEScg, D-906's ACEScct curve, the tetrahedral lookup. For EXR: `default`, **the working space**: the working buffer unchanged, as D-62 writes it; `acescg`, **ACEScg**: the working colour by D-906's matrix to ACEScg; `aces2065-1`, **ACES2065-1**: to ACES2065-1 (AP0). An EXR's matrix goes on the premultiplied numbers (a matrix and a multiplication by alpha commute), alpha untouched, and half samples are taken from the converted floats as before. **Where a picture output is applied.** Exactly where the sRGB curve is applied today: after the unpremultiply for straight alpha, on the premultiplied numbers for premultiplied alpha (as today's curve is), then quantised by D-17's rule at 8 or 16 bits; alpha as before. An MP4's background colour (D-311), a stored linear Rec.709 colour, goes through the same output from linear Rec.709 before it is laid under. A GIF's palette is made from the output's bytes. **What each file says (only with colour management on).** A PNG or animated PNG gets one colour chunk: `sRGB` (rendering intent 0, perceptual) for sRGB and the ACES view, whose values are sRGB display values, or `cICP` 1, 1, 0, 1 (BT.709 primaries, BT.709 transfer, RGB, full range) for Rec.709 (BT.1886), the code point H.273 gives both BT.709 and BT.1886 material; and its `ColorSpace` text tag names the output: "sRGB IEC 61966-2-1" as today, "Rec.709, BT.1886 (gamma 2.4)", or "sRGB IEC 61966-2-1, the ACES 2.0 SDR view", each followed by the depth as today. An MP4's colour labels follow the output: transfer 1 (BT.709) for Rec.709 (BT.1886), transfer 13 (IEC 61966-2-1, sRGB) for sRGB and the ACES view, primaries and matrix BT.709 and limited range as today. An EXR's `chromaticities` attribute names its numbers' primaries and white: Rec.709 and D65 for linear Rec.709, ACES AP1 (0.713 0.293, 0.165 0.830, 0.128 0.044) or AP0 (0.7347 0.2653, 0 1, 0.0001 -0.077) with the ACES white (0.32168 0.33767), so an EXR in the working space of an ACEScg project now says AP1. It is not the ACES container file (SMPTE ST 2065-4, which also asks for uncompressed or no compression and other attributes); the build does not claim it. GIF has no colour description and gets none. **Colour management off: every byte as before.** The word is then not read beyond its check: a non-default output with colour management off is refused before anything is written (`COMMAND_INVALID_VALUE`, "Colour management is off, so the export writes sRGB as it always has; turn colour management on to choose an Output"), and no PNG gets a chunk, no tag, MP4 label or EXR attribute changes. With colour management on and linear Rec.709 working, `default` writes today's pixels byte for byte; only the PNG's `sRGB` chunk and the MP4's transfer label are new. With colour management on and ACEScg working, `default` now converts to Rec.709 first (D-909's gap 6, closed by this step): the same picture the Un-tone-mapped view shows. An output that does not belong to the format (`acescg` for a PNG, `rec709` for an EXR) is refused the same way, naming the output and the format. **The card export (D-911).** The card's frames are read back as floats and encoded on the processor by the same code (D-907), so every output works with the tick and nothing is refused for it; an ACEScg project's frames are drawn by the processor already (D-910). **In the window.** Beside the export window's format list, an "Output" list shown only while the project has colour management on: for the picture formats "sRGB" (the default), "Rec.709 (BT.1886)" and "ACES 2.0 SDR view", for EXR "Working space" (the default), "ACEScg" and "ACES2065-1"; sent as `output=` with Export and with Add to Render queue, only when not the default (document 24). The status line and the queue's row name a chosen output. **What changes in a saved project:** nothing. Export choices are not saved in the project file (D-911); a render queue row keeps the job's choices for the sitting, and a row or a request without the word is `default`, today's export. **Fixtures.** New, in `Fixtures/colour/output/`, written by `tools/output_reference.py` with PyOpenColorIO 2.5.1 (D-906's tool dependency; its built-in config `ocio://studio-config-v4.0.0_aces-v2.0_ocio-v2.5`, `OPTIMIZATION_LOSSLESS`, nothing downloaded; the picture written with Python's standard library): `media/output_chart.exr`, 264 by 4 float, linear Rec.709, premultiplied (a white ramp from 1/256 to 64, a fire gradient to 64, the 24 ColorChecker patches from 4 stops under to 6 over, and an orange with alpha from 0 to 1); `chart_acescg.json`, `chart_rec709.json` (colour management on, each working space) and `chart_off.json`; and `expected_output.json`: OpenColorIO's sRGB, Rec.709 and analytic ACES 2.0 SDR display values of every pixel from both working spaces as levels (8 and 16 bits straight, 8 bits premultiplied), its ACEScg and ACES2065-1 numbers of every pixel, and the labels each file must carry. The bar, set before the code: sRGB and Rec.709 within 1 level on every channel of every pixel at 8 and 16 bits; the ACES view within 1 level of 255 on 99.9% of pixels (D-915's bar; at 16 bits 257 levels), the rest reported; EXR numbers within 1e-6 of the colour's size (its largest channel, at least 1), alpha exact; with colour management off 0 changed bytes in every existing export suite. No existing fixture changes. **Evidence.** `tests/b796_export_output.rs` writes `verification/B-796_export_output_table.md`; pictures of the chart exported each way in `verification/B-796 pictures/`; the playtest `verification/B-796_playtest.md`. **Gaps.** (1) The ACES view is offered for the sRGB display only: no ACES view for a Rec.709 (BT.1886), P3 or HDR display (answer 9, C8). (2) No ACES container file (ST 2065-4) and no log outputs (ACEScct) for EXR. (3) The H.264 stream on the non-Windows road (ffmpeg) is labelled by ffmpeg's own arguments, not checked on this machine. (4) The WAV beside, thumbnails and trace images are unchanged (D-23). **If refused.** Remove `output`, the window's list and the labels; an export with colour management on is then today's again (ACEScg numbers through the sRGB curve, called sRGB); projects are unaffected either way, since nothing is saved.

D-899 / Below 100% zoom the viewer draws at the size it is shown, with a Full pixels tick for today's way (wave 11, lane L23, pick 3) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-26**. On 2026-10-26 the owner asked how After Effects, Nuke and other professional programs balance speed against exact pixels (research in `S/wave11/pros_research.html`) and answered: "Do all of your picks at your recommended order. Defer or tackle until solved if consequential to your discretion." This is pick 3, built as B-779. **What this reopens.** D-229 built "only the part on screen" at 100% or more. Its other half, drawing below 100% at the size shown, was DECLINED by the owner on 2026-09-30, because a smaller picture changes the pixels on screen against Full. This pick, which the owner took on 2026-10-26, reopens that half, on the terms the 2026-09-29 rule asks for: the smaller picture is labelled, never final, and a viewer choice (Full pixels) keeps today's way. **How the professional programs do it.** After Effects' viewer Resolution menu has Auto, which draws at the resolution the zoom shows (Full at 100%, Half at 50%, and so on). Nuke's proxy mode and its viewer downrez draw fewer pixels than the format while you look. Natron's viewer has a proxy level and an automatic one. All three label the viewer and render final frames at full resolution. **What was built.** Page only; the window and the library are unchanged. (1) `sizedAs` in `app/ui/index.html`, inside the B-162/B-163 markers, picks the coarsest of Full, Half and Draft (divisors 1, 2, 4) that still has a picture pixel for every screen pixel. It never picks finer than the quality chosen. "Shown" is screen device pixels per composition pixel (`shownScale() * devicePixelRatio`), so a high-density screen keeps more. Only a frame asked for by number is sized; playback plays at the quality chosen. Only a picture the processor draws is sized (`shownNow` returns null while the last frame's `x-drawn-on` named the card), because the card drew Half at 25% no quicker than Full (below). The frame then goes through B-158's part on screen (`seenPart`, D-229) and D-898's In motion while the hand moves, unchanged. (2) A sized picture does not change the quality chosen (`if (!rough && !sized) quality = drawnAt;`). Its label reads "Half (size shown), not final". (3) `sizeStillRight` asks again after a zoom when the still picture is another size than the one now shown, and after each still picture is drawn. (4) A **Full pixels** tick in the quality menu, off unless ticked and remembered (`prefs.fullPixels`), keeps the quality chosen at any zoom. On this machine's screen (Windows scale 150%, device pixel ratio 1.5), sizing starts below 33%: fit (69%, 1.03 device pixels per composition pixel) and 50% (0.75) stay Full, and 25% (0.375) draws Half. **Checked** (`app/src/tests/shown_size.rs`, `verification/B-779_shown_size_table.md`): the page's own `sizedAs` under Node for 13 cases, among them 100%, 200%, 60%, 50%, 30%, 25% and 10% with Full chosen, Half and Draft chosen, Full pixels ticked, and the part (`/at/`) and playback (`/play/`) routes left alone. The window's Half frame is 960 by 540, a quarter of Full's bytes, and labelled not final; Full asked after it is byte for byte Full asked for alone; and the page lines are in place. In the real program (a private copy, reference shot with 25 layers, processor and card): fit, 100%, 50%, 25%, 50%, 100% at Full each drew Full, Full, Full, "Half (size shown), not final", Full, Full on the processor and Full throughout on the card, with the chosen quality left Full and no request asked again in the 0.6 s after each; 15 quick changes then a stop asked In motion stand-ins and one Full, nothing more, on both. The B-162/B-163 table passes with the marker line changed. **Measured** (RTX 4070 Ti SUPER on Vulkan, AMD64 Family 26 Model 68 with 24 threads, release build, screen at 150%, machine shared with other lanes; reference shot L25, 25 layers, Full chosen; lag harness, 5 rounds of 2 repeats each, before = B-778, before and after alternating; milliseconds, medians). The gain is the time from letting go to the final picture, since a drag already draws In motion. Processor at 25% (Full becomes Half): mask 411 to 292, scale 394 to 277, move 335 to 271, number 381 to 311, bar 323 to 283; a first run gave 422 to 346, 378 to 299, 349 to 295, 345 to 341 and 295 to 273. Drag delays at 25% stayed within noise (mask 39 to 50, scale 48 to 41, move 32 to 30, number 58 to 48, bar 42 to 48; the first run 49 to 49, 46 to 45, 38 to 39, 47 to 46, 45 to 42). At fit, where the code asks exactly what it did, the two builds differed by up to about 45 ms either way (processor from letting go: bar 258 to 286, mask 302 to 347, move 283 to 327, number 350 to 335, scale 344 to 322, scrub 396 to 407), which is this shared machine's noise. On the card at 25% Half was no quicker than Full (from letting go: bar 208 to 206, mask 252 to 273, move 234 to 257, number 227 to 227, scale 243 to 252), so the card is left out. The first build also sent one extra In motion request on the card before the sharp picture, because the card names In motion "Draft"; `drawnRough` fixed it, and the fetch log shows only the stand-ins and the one Full. Final and export pixels are unchanged: the window draws Half exactly as it always has, and exports never pass through the page. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing. The Full pixels tick is a page preference, not part of the project. **Fixtures:** none changed, none added. **Gaps.** On a 150% screen nothing changes at fit or 50%; a 100% screen sizes from 50%. The card is not sized; a card path that draws fewer pixels more cheaply would be a separate proposal. Playback is not sized. The harness's scrub at 25% gave no readings on the card. Whether Half at 25% looks the same as Full is judged by eye (playtest step 3), not by bytes. **If refused:** tick Full pixels, or make `shownNow` return `null` in `app/ui/index.html` so it is always ticked; to take it out fully, remove `sizedAs`, `shownNow`, `sizeStillRight`, `drawnRough`, `onCard`, the tick and `prefs.fullPixels`, and `app/src/tests/shown_size.rs`. Nothing saved depends on it.

D-903 / A Fast quality on Refine Hard Matte and Refine Soft Matte, chosen by the user, after Nuke's quality settings (wave 11, pick 9, lane L9, first step) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-26**. On 2026-10-26 the owner asked how After Effects, Nuke and other professional programs balance speed against exact pixels (`S/wave11/pros_research.html`), then answered: "Do all of your picks at your recommended order. Defer or tackle until solved if consequential to your discretion." Pick 9 was "Fast" quality settings on heavy effects that the user chooses, as Nuke has them (its Blur's quality, which works a large blur on a smaller picture), the defaults staying exact, taken a step at a time; this is the first step. Built as B-783. **Why these two.** The survey (`S/wave11/L9/SURVEY.md`) ranked the heavy effects by the time a fast way would save on each frame against how much the picture would change. Refine Soft Matte and Refine Hard Matte came first: they are among the slowest effects at Full on the processor (W7: Refine Soft Matte 351 ms as added and 459 ms heavy, Refine Hard Matte 237 and 243 ms), the card does not draw them, so the viewer waits as long as an export does, and their filter's own authors published the fast way (He and Sun, "Fast Guided Filter", 2015): work the filter's coefficients on a picture cut down by s, then read them back smoothly, so the edge still follows the full picture. After Effects' Refine effects have no such setting; Nuke's Blur quality is the same idea. **What it does.** A setting Quality, Exact or Fast, on both effects. Exact is the default and is document 21's rule as it always was, to the last digit. Fast works each guided filter on blocks s by s, s = min(4, floor(r / 4)) for its radius r, so below radius 8 nothing changes, and at radius 40 the filter works on a picture 4 times smaller each way. **The picture changes when Fast is chosen, by design.** It is the user's choice, so the processor draws Fast in every frame, exports and stored renders included, not only in the viewer; a file that says "fast" exports fast. Nothing switches to Fast on its own: no quality of the viewer, no Draft, no In motion chooses it. Card and processor agree trivially: neither quality is drawn on the card (the stack around it still is). **What changes in a saved project.** A new setting, `quality`, written only when it is "fast"; a file at the default never has it, so every older file opens as Exact and saves back byte for byte. A word other than "exact" or "fast" is kept as written and the effect left out with `EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID` (document 28). **Fixtures:** FX-MREF-036 to 041 in `Fixtures/matte_refine/`, worked by `tools/matte_refine_fast_reference.py` into `expected_matte_refine_fast.json`, which imports the D-352 reference and does not change it; FX-MREF-001 to 035 are unchanged. FX-MREF-038 is FX-MREF-013 at Fast (radius 2), the same frame. **Gaps.** (1) Key Cleaner (D-503) uses the same filter and stays exact; its own Quality is the next step. (2) The fill colour's and decontamination's box sums stay full size. (3) Fast's change from Exact is largest on a matte with detail smaller than a block (hair finer than s pixels). **Built (B-783) and measured.** `tests/b783_fast_refine.rs`, `verification/B-783_fast_refine_table.md` 48 of 48 checks: FX-MREF-036 to 041 within 2e-5, files open, save and refuse as above, the frame the same however it is tiled, and the card's frame within 1 level of the processor's. Exact is unchanged: the W7 hashes of all six Refine Soft, Refine Hard and Key Cleaner rows (processor floats, card bytes, 8 bpc bytes) are the same as at 9b57ca62, and B-232's and D-503's tables still pass. Time (AMD processor, 24 threads, release, reference shot 1920 by 1080, one layer after a Color Key and a moving Noise, processor at Full, median of 5 rounds taking Exact and Fast in turn, other lanes building on the machine): Refine Soft Matte as added 312.2 against 245.8 ms (0.79), at radius 40 431.9 against 266.9 (0.62); Refine Hard Matte at feather 16 236.1 against 152.6 (0.65), feather and decontamination radius 40 236.5 against 158.5 (0.67) (`verification/B-783_fast_refine_timing_table.md`). The pixels, frame 100 at Full: Fast differs from Exact on average by 0.16 levels of 255 (Soft as added), 0.39 (Soft at 40) and 0.26 (Hard at 40); at most 61, 62 and 225 levels, in the half-keyed noisy cloud, where detail is finer than a block and Hard's Contrast sharpens it; Hard as added (feather 2) is Exact to the byte (`verification/B-783 pictures/`). **If refused:** remove the setting, `tools/matte_refine_fast_reference.py`, FX-MREF-036 to 041 and `tests/b783_fast_refine.rs`; Exact is untouched either way. **Quiet re-measure (2026-10-27)**, nothing else building: Fast takes 0.58 to 0.81 of Exact's time (Soft as added 0.81, Soft heavy 0.58, Hard heavy 0.62, Hard feather 16 0.64); `verification/B-783_fast_refine_timing_table.md`.

Defer or tackle until solved if consequential to your discretion." Pick 8 on that page: "Export on the graphics card, as an option, off by default and never switched silently", gain "much faster exports (not yet measured)", pixels "within the viewer's 1-level bar, not byte-identical", my advice "Later; ask again after 1 to 6". For pick 8 the owner said "Measure first": build it switched off, measure the speed and the pixel difference on the reference shot, and the owner then decides whether to offer it. Built as B-786. **What ADR-006 says.** As D-100 amended it, ADR-006 allows the card for the viewer only: "A GPU export is not allowed, and would need a decision of its own." This is that decision, proposed; until it is accepted no export the app makes uses the card. **What it does.** A switch in the export code, `export::ON_CARD`, false, not in the export window, set only by its tests. Set, each frame is planned as the viewer's card plans it at Full (`compose::plan_frame_for_card`), so any effect the card does not draw is run on the processor first; then drawn by the viewer's own card drawing (`Gpu::draw_held`), read back as the processor's working floats (`Gpu::sum_back`, B-754) and encoded exactly as the processor's frame is (PNG, EXR, GIF, animated PNG, MP4, the same code). A frame the card refuses (an adjustment layer with a Glow, motion blur with no card effect, a Light Wrap blurred larger than the card allows, 8 bpc on a card without double precision, and the rest of `Gpu::refuse`) or fails to read back is drawn by the processor, whole, the same bytes as an export without the card, and its reason is in the report. The report ends with one line: how many of the frames the card drew, which frames, which frames the processor drew, and which effects the processor ran first on the card's frames (for example, a Gaussian Blur one way only, D-303). No card to be had is said too, and every frame is then the processor's. Nothing changes silently: off, an export is today's, byte for byte. **Tackled three ways.** (1) One connection to the card, the drawings decoded and sent to it afresh each frame: the reference shot exported in 0.86x and 0.81x the processor's time in two runs (slower), the 25-layer project 1.13x and 0.94x. (2) Three connections, three frames on the card at once: slower again, 0.60x and 0.82x. (3) Each connection keeps the drawings it planned with (a `CelCache` of 1 GiB), so a drawing held over several frames is decoded and sent to the card once, as in the viewer: kept, with one connection (`export::CARDS`, 1; three were again slower). **Measured (B-786)**, `verification/B-786_card_export_table.md`: RTX 4070 Ti SUPER on Vulkan, AMD processor of 24 threads (as recorded in D-899), release build, the whole export from the call to its report, 8-bit PNG at 1920 by 1080, the processor, the card with one connection and with three taking turns, 5 rounds, the first to go moving on each round, other lanes of wave 11 building on the machine. The reference shot, all 240 frames: processor 12,596 ms (52.5 ms a frame), card 13,378 ms (55.7), 0.94x, no gain: its four layers are few and its drawings change often, so the time is the PNG decode and encode both ways share, which the processor does several frames at once and the card path one connection at a time. The 25-layer project (the reference shot's four layers and 21 copies, moved, scaled, turned, faded and laid in overlay, lighten, screen, multiply and add, a Gaussian Blur of 6 on every fifth), frames 0 to 47: processor 15,540 ms (323.8 ms a frame), card 6,306 ms (131.4), 2.46x faster. The pixels: every pixel of every card frame within 1 level of 255 of the processor's (497,664,000 of 497,664,000 on the reference shot, 99,532,800 of 99,532,800 on the 25 layers), at most 1 level, and no frame the same bytes (0 of 240, 0 of 48): the card sums in another order, so even an invisible difference changes the file. EXR float, linear premultiplied as written: largest difference 0.00043 (reference shot, frames 0 to 47) and 0.00043 (25 layers, 0 to 23), mean 3.9e-5 and 2.3e-5, under a tenth of one 8-bit level. **Off is today's export.** The B-160 check, every export it makes (the reference shot as PNG, MP4, 16-bit PNG, EXR half and float, GIF and animated PNG, and every fixture project that opens), hashed file by file with its report, gives the same 167,631 lines before (068db4d6) and after but one, the MP4 as written, whose hash with its dates set aside is the same (Windows stamps the moment into it, B-160); and the export tests b160_faster_export (b160_frames_at_once_writes_the_same_bytes), b692_export_once, b22b_choices, b520_sound_export, b21b_formats, b16b_exr, b21d_mp4, b21c_films, b744_export_read_ahead, d48_export_threads, t08_export and h04_exported_file, with b786_card_export, and the app's suite, pass. **What changes in a saved project:** nothing; the switch is not saved anywhere, and no file has a new field. **Fixtures:** none; the processor stays the reference, and the card is held to the viewer's bar of 1 level (D-165). **Gaps.** (1) Not in the export window: offering it needs the owner's yes, then a tick "Draw on the graphics card (faster, not exact)" and its playtest. (2) A project of few layers whose drawings change each frame gains nothing; the gain grows with the layers and card effects per frame. (3) The card's frames are never the processor's bytes, so a stored render or check made with it could not be compared byte for byte; the processor stays the reference for those (wave 11's standing principle). (4) Planning with the connection's drawings runs one frame at a time on the processor; a second planning thread ahead of the card is the next step if it is offered. (5) Measured on one machine; a card without double precision draws 8 bpc frames on the processor, named in the report. **Recommendation:** offer it, labelled, for heavy projects, off by default: 2.46x on 25 layers within 1 level, and the same time on the light reference shot. **If refused:** remove `ON_CARD`, `CARDS`, the card branch of `export.rs` and `tests/b786_card_export.rs`; exports are unchanged either way. **Quiet re-measure (2026-10-27)**, nothing else building: reference shot card 1.07x (one connection) and 1.01x (three); 25 layers 3.36x and 2.59x; rounds within about 4%; pixels as before. `verification/B-786_card_export_table.md`.

D-911 / Export on the graphics card offered as a tick, "Faster on the graphics card (not byte-exact)", off by default, the processor staying the default (wave 11, pick 8, lane L8b; D-907's recommendation) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-27**. On 2026-10-26 the owner asked how After Effects, Nuke and other professional programs balance speed against exact pixels (`S/wave11/pros_research.html`), then answered: "Do all of your picks at your recommended order. Defer or tackle until solved if consequential to your discretion." For pick 8 the owner said "Measure first"; D-907 measured it (2.46x on a 25-layer project, 0.94x on the light reference shot, every pixel within 1 level, no frame the same bytes). On 2026-10-27, told the recommendation "offer it later as a ticked option for heavy projects, labelled not byte-exact, processor stays default", the owner answered: "do what you recommend for the decisions." **What ADR-006 says now.** Amended by this entry: the card may draw an export only when the user ticks it for that export. The processor stays the default and the only reference: every fixture, stored check and unticked export stays on the processor and byte-exact. **What it does.** The export window (the Composition menu, under Export..., below the format list) has a tick "Faster on the graphics card (not byte-exact)", not ticked when the window opens. Its hint: it draws the frames on the graphics card as the viewer does; it helps heavy projects (many layers, card effects) and may be slower on light ones; its pixels can differ from the processor's by one step in 255, so the files are not byte-exact; a frame the card cannot draw is drawn by the processor and the report says which. Ticked, the page sends `card=on` with Export and with Add to Render queue, read into `ExportChoices::on_card`, which replaces D-907's process-wide switch `export::ON_CARD` (removed): the choice belongs to that export, and to that row of the render queue. The status line says "on the graphics card (not byte-exact)" and the queue's row says "on the graphics card". The export then runs D-907's card path unchanged: its report ends "Exported on the graphics card (D-911): the card drew N of M frames", names the frames the card drew, the frames the processor drew, and the effects the processor ran first. A frame the card refuses now names its frame in the reason ("Frame 0: ..."). No card to be had is a warning in the report and the processor draws every frame. **What changes in a saved project:** nothing. Export choices are not saved in the project file (no format, quality, dither or WAV choice is either); like the other ticks the page keeps it for the sitting only (session storage), and a new sitting starts unticked. Every project opens and saves back byte for byte. **Unticked is today's export.** With the tick off the card is never opened. The B-160 check, every export it makes hashed file by file with its report, gives the same 167,631 lines at c7d34d67 and with B-790 but one, the MP4 as written, whose hash with its dates set aside is the same (Windows stamps the moment into it, B-160); the named export tests (b160_faster_export, b692_export_once, b22b_choices, b520_sound_export, b21b_formats, b16b_exr, b21d_mp4, b21c_films, b744_export_read_ahead, d48_export_threads, t08_export, h04_exported_file, b786_card_export) and the app's suite pass. **Fixtures:** none; the processor stays the reference, and the card is held to the viewer's bar of 1 level (D-165), as measured in `verification/B-786_card_export_table.md`. **Gaps.** (1) D-907's gaps (2) to (5) stand: a light project gains nothing; card files are never the processor's bytes; planning runs one frame at a time; measured on one machine. (2) The tick is offered for every format; an MP4 or GIF gains least, as their encode dominates. (3) The tick is not remembered between sittings, by design (off by default). **If refused:** remove the tick from `app/ui/index.html`, `on_card` from `ExportChoices` and the app's `card=` reading; D-907 stands as built, switched off.

D-908 / The RAM preview made at rest only while the graphics card draws the viewer (wave 11, pick 5 continued, lane L5a, D-900's at-rest half) / **PROPOSED on 2026-10-26, switched off; the fixes it brought are built and on.** On 2026-10-26 the owner answered D-900's question on the at-rest half: "(a) only, card viewer": make the loop round the playhead ahead at rest, once the hand has been still for half a second, only while the card draws the viewer, after measuring again that drags are not slowed there; the processor keeps it off and several workers stay off. The wave 11 answer applies too: "Do all of your picks at your recommended order. Defer or tackle until solved if consequential to your discretion." Built as B-787. **What it does when switched on.** Two switches in the program, one for the card (`AHEAD_AT_REST`) and one for the processor (`AHEAD_AT_REST_CPU`, D-900, off). With the card's on, a frame asked for by hand on the card starts the one worker once the hand is still; with the processor drawing (no card, or the card switched off) nothing is started after a frame asked by hand, as before B-780. Frames kept are byte for byte what the viewer draws and are never sent for another quality, composition, project or for the other drawer. **Why it is off.** Smoke rounds on a machine shared with other lanes (not results; L4 shot, card, alternating with the build before): switched on as first built, the next drag at Full was slower (move 11 to 23 ms, scale 11 to 21, number 14 to 21, mask 39 to 58). The cause: the frames kept from a loop made at rest count against the memory setting, and the viewer's cels were shrunk to make room, so the next drag's frames were made from cold. Two approaches followed. (1) Frames made at rest are kept only in the room the cels leave, older sights given up first. (2) As (1) with a quarter of the setting left free for the cels to grow into, and a frame asked by hand takes its room back from frames kept for other sights (`FrameCache::trim`). With (2) move, scale, number, the bar and mask came back to the build before's times at Full and Draft, but a mask drag that holds still halfway stayed about 3 times slower at Full (12 against 35 to 38 ms, four repeats). Its cause on the card is not found; a pause of 0.28 s is shorter than the half second of rest, so a likely cause is a loop begun in the rest before the drag still holding the card or its stored layers. Per the owner's bar this is recorded PROPOSED with the card's switch off. **Also fixed (on).** (a) B-780's test row "4 worker(s): frames made ahead in the 0.3 s after it" failed on a busy machine (got 1 or 2, expected 0), even run alone. Two causes, one a real race: a worker took the moment it chose a frame after choosing it, so a /stop between the two was not seen; the moment is now taken under the frame memory's lock, with the hand's stop marked under it too (`stop::hand`, `stop::behind(since, ..)`). The other was timing: the half second of rest was counted from when the hand's frame was asked, so a ten-layer Full frame slower than half a second on a busy machine was followed at once by frames made at rest; rest now counts from when the hand's frame is finished. A third showed once those were fixed, on a machine so busy the test took 517 s instead of about 150: a worker below normal priority that had drawn its frame before the hand asked could be kept waiting and store it after; a frame chosen before the hand's ask is now never kept after it (checked under the frame memory's lock) and is made again later. (b) The trim in (2) runs only when an at-rest switch is on, so with both off the memory behaves as before. **What changes in a saved project:** nothing. **Fixtures:** none. **Built (B-787) and checked.** `app/src/tests/ram_workers.rs`: `verification/B-787_card_at_rest_table.md` (the switches as built, then the card's switched on for its rows: loops made at rest on the card byte for byte the frames made by hand, none made with the processor, and no stale frame after an edit, undo, frame change, quality change or composition switch) and B-780's table, 30 of 30, run repeatedly. **Timings:** held for main's quiet slot (seven lanes on the machine); the drag delays, release to final and first-play gain go in `verification/B-787_card_at_rest_timing_table.md` when measured. **Gaps.** (1) The cause of the slower held mask drag on the card. (2) A longer quiet period before making frames at rest was not tried as a fix: one longer than the harness's rest between gestures (about 1.5 s) would only hide the slower drag from it, not remove it. **If accepted:** set `AHEAD_AT_REST` to true and the test's first row to "on". **If refused:** remove the switch, `FrameCache::trim` and `frames_room`; the race and rest fixes stay.

D-913 / A Fast quality on Bilateral Blur and Cartoon, chosen by the user, on a bilateral grid (wave 11, pick 9, lane L9c, third step) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-27, on the brief's condition (Exact unchanged to the bit, Fast clearly faster); the times are main's quiet-slot measurement, still to come**. On 2026-10-26 the owner answered the professional-programs survey: "Do all of your picks at your recommended order. Defer or tackle until solved if consequential to your discretion." Pick 9 is "Fast" quality settings on heavy effects that the user chooses, defaults exact, a step at a time (D-903 was the first step); on 2026-10-27 the owner said to "work on other lanes in parallel to work on what we have left... do what you recommend for the decisions". Built as B-792. **Why these two.** In W7 Bilateral Blur at radius 40 takes 385.8 ms a frame at Full on the processor and Cartoon at detail radius 40 422.9 ms, among the slowest; both weigh a whole disc of taps for every pixel (about 5,000 at radius 40). The bilateral grid is how the filter's own authors made it fast: Paris and Durand (2006) showed the bilateral filter is a linear blur in a space of position and value followed by a division, so it can be worked on a coarse grid; Chen, Paris and Durand (2007) named the grid and its three steps (splat, blur, slice). Written from the papers; no code ported, none copied. **What it does.** A setting Quality, Exact or Fast, on Bilateral Blur and on Cartoon (whose smoothing is Bilateral Blur). Exact is the default and document 21's rule as it always was. Fast: one grid per value worked, cells radius / 2.2 pixels across and 1.1 Threshold levels deep (spread chosen so the grid's blur matches the exact bells'), each pixel added into its 8 nearest cells, the grid blurred 1 2 1 along each axis, each pixel read back at its own place and level and divided. Below radius 4.4 (cells under 2 pixels), or where the grid would hold more than 4 cells for each pixel (a Threshold very small against the layer's spread of levels), Fast is the exact rule; document 21 states this, so it is the rule and not a silent fallback. **The picture changes when Fast is chosen, by design**; it is the user's choice, so every frame draws it, exports included. Nothing switches to Fast on its own. **The card.** The card draws Exact (14 to 17 ms at radius 40 at 1080p), so a card grid would save little, and a grid's adding-in on the card needs atomic sums whose order changes from run to run. So Fast is drawn by the processor: a layer whose Bilateral Blur or Cartoon is Fast goes to the processor, named by the card's own rule (`card_can`), and the card's frame is the processor's. Fast is for exports and for the processor's view; on a machine with a card the viewer is quicker at Exact. **What changes in a saved project.** A new setting, `quality`, written only when it is "fast"; every older file opens as Exact and saves back byte for byte. Another word is kept as written and the effect left out with `EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID` (document 28). **Fixtures:** FX-BILAT-018 to 023 in `Fixtures/bilateral_blur/expected_bilateral_blur_fast.json` and FX-CARTOON-033 and 034 in `Fixtures/cartoon/expected_cartoon_fast.json`, worked by `tools/bilateral_grid_reference.py`, which imports the D-358 and D-448 references and changes neither. FX-BILAT-020 (radius 4) and 021 (Threshold 1) are the exact frame. **Gaps.** (1) Fast is not drawn on the card (above). (2) The grid is coarse across: a speck smaller than a cell is smoothed a little more or less than Exact smooths it, and on a tiny layer (the 16 by 10 fixtures) at a large radius the grid is only a few cells, so Fast moves further from Exact there. (3) The rest of Cartoon (edges, line, fill) stays exact. **Built (B-792).** `tests/b792_fast_bilateral.rs`, `verification/B-792_fast_bilateral_table.md`, pictures in `verification/B-792 pictures/`; 66 of 66 checks pass. Exact unchanged to the bit: the W7 hashes (processor floats, card bytes, 8 bpc bytes) of Bilateral Blur as added and at radius 40 and of Cartoon as added and heavy are the same before and after. Fast against Exact at 1080p, frame 100, in 8-bit levels (mean / largest / pixels within 1 level): Bilateral as added 0.22 / 7 / 98.97%, radius 40 0.25 / 18 / 97.25%, Cartoon as added 0.24 / 17 / 95.72%, Cartoon heavy 0.33 / 37 / 89.69%; the pictures show no halos or banding, so the finer grid was not needed. Time: to be measured by main in a quiet slot (`b792_fast_bilateral_timing`). **If refused:** remove the setting, `tools/bilateral_grid_reference.py`, FX-BILAT-018 to 023, FX-CARTOON-033 and 034 and `tests/b792_fast_bilateral.rs`; Exact is untouched either way.
