D-914 / A Fast quality on the big blurs inside Glow, Bloom, Deband and Halation, chosen by the user, after Nuke's Blur quality (wave 11, pick 9, lane L9d, fourth step) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-26**. On 2026-10-26 the owner answered the professional-programs survey (`S/wave11/pros_research.html`): "Do all of your picks at your recommended order. Defer or tackle until solved if consequential to your discretion." Pick 9 is "Fast" quality settings on heavy effects that the user chooses, the defaults staying exact, a step at a time (D-903 the first); on 2026-10-27 the owner said to "work on other lanes in parallel to work on what we have left... do what you recommend for the decisions". This is the survey's candidate 3 (`S/wave11/L9/SURVEY.md`: the big blurs inside Halation, Glow, Bloom and Deband, 150 to 195 ms a frame on the processor, a small change at large radii). Built as B-793. **What it does.** A setting Quality, Exact or Fast, on Glow, Bloom, Deband and Halation, as D-903's. Exact is the default and is document 21's rule as it always was, to the last digit, on the processor and on the card. Fast works each big blur on a smaller picture, as Nuke's Blur does at a quality below full. **One rule for how small** (`blurs::cell`, which Soft Physical Glow and Halation have used at Exact since D-353): a blur at sigma works on cells d by d, d the smallest power of two with 8 d above sigma, so 4 to 8 cells a sigma; below sigma 8 d is 1 and Fast is Exact itself, to the bit. **The reduced blur** (`blurs::reduced`, Glow's and Bloom's): the picture averaged over the cells from its top left corner, blurred there by document 21's Gaussian at sigma_l = sqrt(sigma^2 - d^2 / 4) / d (the cells' average and the read back spread it by about d^2 / 4 between them), and read back bilinearly at every pixel; the picture grows by the full blur's reach, as at Exact. Glow: its light's blur, in both dimensions (Glow Dimensions horizontal or vertical stays Exact). Bloom: each of its four halo blurs at its own sigma, so at radius 100 they work on cells 8, 4, 2 and 1 wide; the streaks are not blurs and stay as they are. **Deband is different, and why.** Its blur stops at edges: each tap is weighed by the product of (1 - E) over the pixels between. The reduced blur was tried first and is refused: a cell holds both sides of an edge, so the dark block's colour bled up to 30 levels of 255 into the bands beside it (FX-DEBAND-027's drawing, cells 4 by 4). Fast Deband instead reads a tap every d pixels (the same cell d), tap m weighed by the Gaussian at sigma / d at m, through the product of (1 - E) over every pixel between, so an edge stops it where it stops Exact: at most 1 level of 255 from Exact on the same drawing. **Halation** already works its levels on cells at Exact (D-353); Fast takes each level one cell coarser, the cell of 2 sigma, 2 to 4 cells a sigma, from sigma 4 (radius 12, the default). **The picture changes when Fast is chosen, by design.** It is the user's choice, so the processor draws Fast in every frame, exports and stored renders included; nothing switches to Fast on its own: no viewer quality, no Draft, no In motion chooses it. **The card.** Halation at Fast stays on the card, which works the same coarser levels, its frame within the card's 1 level of the processor's. Glow, Bloom and Deband at Fast are drawn by the processor, named in `compose::card_can`: the card has no reduced blur of its own, and the processor's Fast picture is the one exports draw. So in the viewer, with the card on, Glow, Bloom or Deband at Fast can be slower than at Exact, which the card draws; Fast is for the processor's frames (exports, stored renders, no card). **What changes in a saved project.** A new setting, `quality`, on all four, written only when it is "fast"; a file at the default never has it, so every older file opens as Exact and saves back byte for byte. A word other than "exact" or "fast" is kept as written and the effect left out with `EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID` (document 28). **Fixtures:** FX-GLOW-034 to 037, FX-BLOOM-029 to 032, FX-DEBAND-025 to 028 and FX-HALO-019 to 022, worked by `tools/fast_blur_reference.py` into `expected_glow_fast.json`, `expected_bloom_fast.json`, `expected_deband_fast.json` and `expected_halation_fast.json` in each effect's folder; it imports the four effects' references and does not change them, and every earlier case is unchanged. FX-GLOW-034, FX-BLOOM-029, FX-DEBAND-025 and FX-HALO-019 are Fast below its threshold, the same frame as Exact. **Gaps.** (1) Glow in one dimension stays Exact at Fast. (2) Glow's, Bloom's and Deband's Fast are not drawn on the card. (3) Fast's change from Exact is largest round a light smaller than a cell (a single bright pixel), where the reduced blur spreads it a little wider. **If refused:** remove the setting, `tools/fast_blur_reference.py`, the sixteen fixtures and `tests/b793_fast_blur.rs`; Exact is untouched either way. **Correction before any code (b0d9a17f).** The reference first read the reduced blur back only inside the picture, which darkened a glow near the picture's edge by up to 0.01; the blurred cells reach past the edge, as Exact's blur does, so it reads them there too. The Glow and Bloom fixtures were worked again before any code existed; the rule is otherwise as above. **Built (B-793); the timings wait for a quiet slot.** `tests/b793_fast_blur.rs`, `verification/B-793_fast_blur_table.md` 118 of 118 checks: the sixteen fixtures within 2e-5, files open, save and refuse as above, the commands, the frame the same however it is tiled, and the card's frame within 1 level of the processor's (Glow, Bloom and Deband at Fast left off the card, Halation at Fast on it, the reference shot at radius 100 included). Exact is unchanged: the W7 hashes of the eight Glow, Bloom, Deband and Halation rows (processor floats, card bytes, 8 bpc bytes) are the same as at c7d34d67, and B-33's, B-40's, B-47's, B-51's, B-206's, B-216's, B-233's, B-336's, B-393's, B-422's, B-423's, B-424's, B-625's and B-626's tables still pass. The pixels, the reference shot's frame 100 at Full: Fast differs from Exact on average by 0.010 levels of 255 (Glow at radius 60), 0.009 (Bloom at radius 100), 0.076 (Deband at blur 60) and 0.030 (Halation at radius 100); at most 1, 1, 23 and 4 levels, Deband's largest along the soft edge of a cloud, where a tap every 4 pixels sees the edge a little differently; Glow at radius 21 and Deband at blur 16 are Exact to the byte (`verification/B-793 pictures/`). The one shared reduced blur is `blurs::reduced` with its cell rule `blurs::cell`; Halation's levels use the same cell rule.

D-918 / With colour management on, the colour pickers, an eyedropper and an Info row show two sets of numbers, the working space's and the view's, as After Effects does (ADR-023; wave 11, pick 7, lane C7, step C7 of the colour-management plan) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-26**. On 2026-10-26 the owner asked how After Effects, Nuke and other professional programs balance speed against exact pixels, and what we should do to compete (research in `S/wave11/pros_research.html`); the owner answered: "Do all of your picks at your recommended order. Defer or tackle until solved if consequential to your discretion." For pick 7's colour-management plan the owner answered: "go with your recommended answers for colour management". This is step C7, built as B-797. **Why.** With colour management on and ACEScg working (D-909), a colour has three different sets of numbers: the one the file stores (linear Rec.709, D-910), the working space's (ACEScg), and what the screen shows through the view (D-915). The picker's hex is only the first through the sRGB curve, so it no longer says what the picture holds or what the screen shows: `#ff8000` is stored as 1, 0.216, 0, is 0.686, 0.268, 0.044 in ACEScg, and shows through ACES 2.0 SDR as the levels 196, 103, 25 (OpenColorIO's numbers, from the fixture below). After Effects (26.5, OpenColorIO mode) shows the working and the display numbers in its Info panel and colour picker. **What there was.** The colour pickers are the system's own (D-74: 256 levels a channel through the sRGB curve; D-822: an expression's colour is linear Rec.709); this reopens D-74 and D-822 only to show more numbers, and both stand. The app had no eyedropper and no Info panel; the only matches for either word were the Eyedropper Fill effect and the picker itself. Adding both only for colour management, my call under the owner's "to your discretion", keeps every window with colour management off exactly as it is. **The rule.** One colour's readout is four things, worked by the code that already does each step and nothing new: **Stored**, linear Rec.709, straight (D-910); **Working**, the working space's numbers, straight: D-906's Rec.709-to-ACEScg matrix (`color::convert_rgba`) when the working space is ACEScg, the stored numbers themselves when it is linear Rec.709; **Display**, the three 8-bit levels the view on screen gives that colour, worked by the viewer's own encode (`view::encode8`, D-915), so they are exactly the viewer's bytes; and, for a pixel, **Alpha**. For a picker the stored colour is the picker's hex through the sRGB curve, as it is saved (D-74). For a pixel of the picture the working numbers are the pixel's, unpremultiplied, and the stored numbers come back through the ACEScg-to-Rec.709 matrix. **In the window, only with colour management on.** (1) An **Info** row under the picture, shown and hidden as the View menu's Colour view list is (D-915). Its first line is the pixel under the pointer: the composition on screen at the frame shown, drawn exactly at Full as an export draws it, read at the composition pixel under the pointer when the pointer rests; it reads "x, y  Working (ACEScg) r g b  Display (ACES 2.0 SDR) r g b  Alpha a". Its second line is the colour picker touched last (any of the window's colour pickers: a solid's colour, an effect's colour, a text's or a shape's fill), its hex, its working numbers and its display levels. (2) An **eyedropper**, a button "Pick from the picture" in the Info row: after pressing it, a click on the picture sets the colour picker touched last to that pixel's stored colour, as the picker's own hex, nearest of its 256 levels a channel (D-74), and sends it as if the user had picked it, one step of history as a pick is; pressing the button again, or Escape, puts it away. **Round trip.** The numbers shown are never written anywhere. A picked or typed colour is saved exactly as before; a hex read back through the readout gives the same hex; the eyedropper's colour is the picker's own value, so it reads back the same. **With colour management off** there is no Info row and no eyedropper, the pickers are as today, and the window's question (below) answers "off": every pixel, file, cache key and stored value is as today. **The window's question.** A new route, `colour-info`: `?rgb=r,g,b` (a stored colour) or `?frame=&x=&y=` (a pixel of the composition on screen) answers the readout as JSON, with the working space's and the view's names and the nearest picker hex; with colour management off it answers only that it is off. The last frame drawn for it is kept while the project, composition and frame stay the same, so a resting pointer does not redraw. Nothing is added to the project, the history or document 24's commands. **What changes in a saved project.** Nothing. **Fixtures (written before the code).** New, `Fixtures/colour/c7/expected_readout.json`, by `tools/c7_reference.py` with PyOpenColorIO 2.5.1 (D-906's tool dependency; its built-in config `ocio://studio-config-v4.0.0_aces-v2.0_ocio-v2.5`, `OPTIMIZATION_LOSSLESS`, nothing downloaded): the 24 ColorChecker swatches and nine plain ones (`#ff8000`, black, white, `#808080`, the three primaries, `#010101`, `#fefefe`) as a picker's hex, each with its stored number (the sRGB curve's published decode), its working numbers in both working spaces and its display levels through both views from both working spaces; and 64 points of D-915's HDR scene (`Fixtures/colour/view/media/hdr_scene.exr`, eight per band) with the same numbers from the picture's own 32-bit floats. FX-COLC7-001 to 004 in document 25. The bars, set before the code: working and stored within 1e-6 times max(1, |c|); a picker's hex back exactly; display within 1 level of OpenColorIO on the picker cases and the barred bands (the pure primary ramps reported, as in D-915) and exactly the viewer's own byte at that pixel; with colour management off, nothing new. **Correction, after the first run of the code and before it was committed:** two of those bars were wrong and are corrected in the fixture and here, nothing else changed. (a) Working and stored numbers are held to 1e-6 times the colour's size (its largest channel, at least 1), D-909's bar, not each channel's own: a pure green at 64 times white comes back from ACEScg with a red of -1.1e-6 where 0 is expected, a single-precision rounding of a colour of size 64 (1.8e-8 of its size). (b) The three pure primaries `#ff0000`, `#00ff00` and `#0000ff` are reported beside the display bar, not barred, as D-915 reports its pure primary ramps: they are where the 97-point table cannot follow ACES 2.0's gamut compression (`#ff0000` through ACES 2.0 SDR shows 196, 25, 12 where OpenColorIO gives 196, 23, 11). No existing fixture changes. **Evidence.** The app test `b797_colour_info_from_the_window` (`app/src/tests/editing.rs`) writes `verification/B-797_colour_info_table.md`; a check through a private copy of the app; the playtest `verification/B-797_playtest.md`. **Gaps.** (1) The pointer's numbers are of the exact Full frame: a viewer at Half or Draft, or drawn by the card (within 1 level, D-165), may show a level or so otherwise; solo, the onion skin and a turned or mirrored view (W-41b) are not reflected. (2) The picker line reads the picker's 8-bit hex, the picker's own precision, not a stored number typed or worked out more finely (an expression's colour, D-822). (3) The eyedropper picks the nearest of the picker's 256 levels; a pixel outside 0 to 1 in Rec.709 (an HDR highlight, an ACES colour outside Rec.709) is held to the nearest picker colour, while the Info row shows its full numbers. (4) After Effects shows Info with colour management off too; we do not, so nothing changes there. (5) The pointer's numbers wait for the pointer to rest; a heavy composition takes its drawing time once per frame. **If refused.** Remove the route, the Info row, the eyedropper and `view::Readout`; nothing saved depends on them.

D-646 / Curl Noise, Rotation, Scale and Perspective Offset, after After Effects' Curl Noise (Noise & Grain, 26.3) Transform controls (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, row 214) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-13 under the owner's /loop request (the coordinator's lane B queue); every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5 (largest 1.9e-7); every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; no existing Curl, Fractal or Turbulent Noise expected value changed; built B-525.** **What was built.** `core.curl_noise` takes `rotation` (-100000 to 100000 degrees, 0 when added), `scale` (1 to 10000 per cent, 100) and `perspective_offset` (`off` when added, or `on`); both numbers can be keyed; a file without them reads them as added, and they are written only when moved, keyed or already in the file (D-304). With c the drawing's middle, m = 100 / Scale and theta = Rotation, octave o of the made noise is read at c + m R(-theta) (p - w_o (Offset + drift x frame) - c), w_o = 0.5^o with Perspective Offset on, else 1; the slope worked there is brought back by m R(theta) before Swirl and Vertical Bias; the seed is read at octave 0's point. Rotation 0 with Scale 100 takes the old path exactly, so every file before D-646 draws as before (FX-CURL-001 to 060 hold, b326 and b461 unchanged). On the card the `curlfield` pass does the same. **App.** Rotation (a dial) and Scale on Curl Noise's card, Perspective Offset among its choices; a window from before sends neither and they read as added. **Gaps.** Adobe publishes no formula, so the turn, the scale and Perspective Offset's halving per octave are ours, after Fractal Noise's same controls; with Source This Layer or Other Layer Rotation and Scale move only the seed (the picture is read unturned and at its own size, as Size does not scale it) and Perspective Offset does nothing; the turn is round the drawing's middle (After Effects' own centre is not published); Rotation 360 equals Rotation 0 only within the tolerance (the cosine and sine are not exact). **Timing.** PROVISIONAL (a busy machine), `verification/B-525_curl_transform_timing_table.md`: on the reference shot with three layers, Curl Noise as added 76.2 ms a frame on the card (27.1 for the Noise alone) and with Rotation 45, Scale 150 and Perspective Offset 76.7; on the processor 394.5 and 316.7 (57.7 alone), the spread the busy machine's; the Transform adds nothing measurable. **Evidence.** Fixtures first (f0ffeb40, `tools/curl_transform_reference.py`, FX-CURL-061 to 077); code 7b7655a8; `tests/b525_curl_transform.rs`, `verification/D-646_curl_transform_table.md` 122 of 122 checks; pictures in `verification/D-646 pictures/`; playtest `verification/B-525_playtest.md`, awaiting the owner.

D-645 / Keyed level, pan, and sound through composition layers, S-7 of D-638 (D-638 decisions on level, pan and nested sound) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-13 under the owner's acceptance of D-638 ("for the sound plan, proceed with your recommendations, in case of music, dialogue use, etc that may overlap with the compositing", relayed by the coordinator); every sample within document 25's 2e-5 (largest 5.6e-17), every click on the reference's sample, every peak within 0.01 dB; no new tolerance; built B-524.** **What was built.** An audio layer's `gain_db` is a number (as every file before) or keys with a base (-96 to +12 dB, keys only, no expression); a new `pan` is absent (the centre), a number or keys (-100 all left to +100 all right). Both are read at the frame and the next and moved in a straight line across the frame's samples (the level in dB), after the layer's sound effects; the pan by the balance law, left times min(1, 1 - p/100), right times min(1, 1 + p/100), so the centre leaves the sound unchanged and an unkeyed layer's mix is the same bit for bit. A composition layer switched on is now heard: outer frame f plays the inner composition's frame g = floor(source time) from g's first sample, so a layer start, an offset, a stretch and a time remap all place it; nothing is heard outside the inner composition's frames; nested to any depth; a missing composition is silent (its `COMPOSITION_REFERENCE_MISSING` is said on opening), and a cycle cannot open and is silent if an edit makes one. An MP4 gets a sound track when the composition has sound here or inside. The level command on a keyed level sets its base and keeps the keys. Values are saved as written (a plain number stays plain). **App.** The sound panel shows the level's base, a Level keys line when the level is keyed, and a Pan line when a pan is set; the window asks for the mix when a composition layer is present. **Gaps.** A composition layer has no level or pan of its own (its inner layers' are heard); a composition layer at a different frame rate, a stretch other than 100% or a time remap is heard frame by frame (each outer frame plays its inner frame's samples onward), so it can repeat or skip short pieces rather than being resampled; a composition layer's one switch mutes both its picture and its sound; the panel shows level keys and pan but cannot key the level or set the pan (no command yet; the level number sets the keys' base); an Opus file inside a nested composition is not heard in the window (the window's left-out fallback covers outer layers only; an export has it); Audio Spectrum and Waveform still read the level's base, not its keyed value. Behaviour change by design: a project with sound inside a composition layer is now heard there, in the window and in an MP4. **Unchanged.** b20b_audio (D-71), b519, b520, b518, b521, b522, b523, b299_audio_spectrum and b300_audio_waveform (D-420), b12b (no new diagnostic), b07_effects, b21d_mp4, t08_export and b09_persistence pass unchanged; lib 24 of 24; app 93 of 95, the 2 known failures (gestures target, pick whip) and none new. **Timing (release build, this machine, recorded only).** Two seconds mixed: a plain level and pan 2.6 ms, a keyed level 1.9 ms, two compositions deep 1.2 ms. **Evidence.** Fixtures first (ac817d83, `tools/sound_layer_reference.py`, FX-SLAY-001 to 018, 101 to 105); code 1cd48809; `tests/b524_sound_layer.rs`, `verification/D-645_sound_layer_table.md` 126 of 126 checks, with the click, level, saved-again and has-sound tables; waveforms in `verification/D-645 pictures/`; playtest `verification/B-524_playtest.md`, awaiting the owner.

D-644 / Distortion, S-6 of D-638: the third sound effect (D-638 decisions 6 and 7; `docs/effects/EFFECTS.md` row 414) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-13 under the owner's acceptance of D-638 ("for the sound plan, proceed with your recommendations", relayed by the coordinator); every sample within document 25's 2e-5 (largest 2.2e-16), every peak and every 2nd and 3rd harmonic within 0.01 dB, Resolution and Downsample exact; no new tolerance; built B-523.** **What was built.** `core.distortion` with After Effects 26.0's controls and starting values (Type: Soft Clip, Hard Clip, Saturation 1, Saturation 2, Tube, Fuzz, Soft Clip; Drive 0 to 100%, 25; Gain 0 to 300, 25; Mix 0 to 100%, 100; Volume 0 to 100, 11; Resolution 1 to 24 bits, 24; Downsample 1 to 32, 1), by our own rule, now in document 21: each channel's sample times 10^(drive / 50) (Drive 0 to 100% is 0 to +40 dB) through the type's curve, one of ours each (Soft Clip tanh; Hard Clip held to -1..1; Saturation 1 u / (1 + |u|); Saturation 2 (2 / pi) atan(pi u / 2); Tube a tanh shifted by a quarter so it is lopsided and adds even harmonics; Fuzz a square root held to 1), then Resolution's 2^(bits - 1) steps and Downsample's hold, counted from the layer's first sample; that times gain / 25 is mixed with the clean sound by Mix, then times volume / 11. So the starting values (Gain 25, Volume 11, Resolution 24, Downsample 1) change only the curve. Every number can be keyed (Resolution and Downsample take the whole part); Type is a word, kept with `EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID` when it is not one of the six, like any setting out of range. Like Noise Gate and Compressor it goes on audio layers only, runs before the level and in order with the layer's other sound effects, and has no picture Mix or expression; its own Mix is saved as `wet` so it never meets the picture Mix. **Measured.** A 1 kHz sine at -6 dB at the starting values: Soft Clip 3rd harmonic -17.74 dB, Hard Clip -15.51, Saturation 1 -17.09, Saturation 2 -16.35, Fuzz -12.57, all with no 2nd; Tube 2nd -20.50 and 3rd -18.45. **App.** Audio: Distortion in the Effects list for a sound layer only; its card has Type and the six numbers, and no picture Mix row. **Gaps.** No oversampling: with a high Drive, harmonics above 24 kHz fold back down as aliasing (a logged ceiling; `ponytail:` note in `audio::distortion`, a 4x oversampled path if a playtest hears it). The curves are ours, so the sound differs from After Effects' at the same settings. **Unchanged.** b521 (Noise Gate), b522 (Compressor), b20b_audio (D-71), b299_audio_spectrum and b300_audio_waveform (D-420), b518, b519, b520, b12b (no new diagnostic), b07_effects, b21d_mp4 and t08_export pass unchanged; lib 24 of 24; app 93 of 95, the 2 known failures (gestures target, pick whip) and none new. **Timing (release build, this machine, recorded only).** Two seconds of fx_dist_001 mix in 0.9 ms without the distortion and 5.7 ms with it. **Evidence.** Fixtures first (db6f0a7d, `tools/distortion_reference.py`, FX-DIST-001 to 018, 101 to 103); code 48e2b6d0; `tests/b523_distortion.rs`, `verification/D-644_distortion_table.md` 240 of 240 checks, with the harmonic, curve and level tables; curves, sine close-ups and waveforms in `verification/D-644 pictures/`; playtest `verification/B-523_playtest.md`, awaiting the owner.

D-643 / Compressor, S-5 of D-638: the second sound effect (D-638 decisions 6 and 7; `docs/effects/EFFECTS.md` row 413) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-13 under the owner's acceptance of D-638 ("for the sound plan, proceed with your recommendations", relayed by the coordinator); every sample within document 25's 2e-5, every peak within 0.01 dB, the steady gain curve within 0.01 dB (largest 4.3e-8 dB), every 63% and 90% time on its exact sample; no new tolerance; built B-522.** **What was built.** `core.compressor` with After Effects 26.0's controls and starting values (Threshold -60 to 0 dB, -16; Ratio 0.4 to 30, 3; Knee 0 to 30 dB, 15; Attack 0 to 400 ms, 6; Release 1 to 4000 ms, 440; Auto Release, on; Makeup Gain -30 to 30 dB, 0; Output Limit -30 to 0 dB, 0), by our own rule, now in document 21: the louder channel's level, a soft knee centred on the threshold giving the wanted gain change, the change eased toward it sample by sample (Attack when it must fall, Release when it may rise), then Makeup Gain and an instant Output Limit on the louder channel that keeps the balance. **Auto Release** is our own two-speed release: a tenth of Release while the gain is more than 3 dB below where it is heading, then Release for the last 3 dB, so a deep cut comes back fast without pumping on the tail (with the starting values, 63% back in 44 ms and 90% in 464 ms, against 438 ms and 1,013 ms with it off). Every number can be keyed; Auto Release is a word, "on" or "off", kept with `EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID` when it is anything else, like any setting out of range. A Ratio below 1 expands above the threshold (louder gets louder), held by the Output Limit. Like Noise Gate (D-642) it goes on audio layers only, runs before the level and in order with the layer's other sound effects, and has no Mix or expression. **App.** Audio: Compressor in the Effects list for a sound layer only; its card has the seven numbers and Auto Release, and no Mix. **Gaps.** No side chain, look-ahead or RMS detection (the level is each sample's peak, so a low note's own waveform can ripple the gain at short attack and release times); the Output Limit is an instant clip-free scale, not a look-ahead limiter. The window-stretch cost of D-642 applies here too. **Unchanged.** b521 (Noise Gate), b20b_audio (D-71), b299_audio_spectrum and b300_audio_waveform (D-420), b518, b519, b520, b12b (no new diagnostic), b07_effects, b21d_mp4 and t08_export pass unchanged; lib 24 of 24; app 93 of 95, the 2 known failures (gestures target, pick whip) and none new. **Timing (release build, this machine, recorded only).** Four seconds of fx_comp_004 mix in 1.7 ms without the compressor and 10.7 ms with it. **Evidence.** Fixtures first (d49a28af, `tools/compressor_reference.py`, FX-COMP-001 to 016, 101 to 103); code 2ba495c2; `tests/b522_compressor.rs`, `verification/D-643_compressor_table.md` 131 of 131 checks, with the timing, curve and level tables; waveforms and gain-curve charts in `verification/D-643 pictures/`; playtest `verification/B-522_playtest.md`, awaiting the owner.

D-642 / Noise Gate, S-4 of D-638: the first sound effect, and sound effects allowed on audio layers only (D-638 decisions 3, 6 and 7; `docs/effects/EFFECTS.md` row 415) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-13 under the owner's acceptance of D-638 ("for the sound plan, proceed with your recommendations", relayed by the coordinator); every sample within document 25's 2e-5, every peak within 0.01 dB, every opening and closing on its exact sample; no new tolerance; built B-521.** **What was built.** `core.noise_gate` with After Effects 26.0's four controls and starting values (Threshold -60 to 0 dB, -60; Attack 0 to 1000 ms, 10; Hold 0 to 2500 ms, 40; Release 5 to 4000 ms, 220), by our own rule, now in document 21: the louder channel at or above the threshold opens the gate over Attack, it stays open for Hold after the sound falls below, then closes over Release, each a straight ramp counted in whole samples. Every setting can be keyed, and a keyed setting moves in a straight line across each frame's samples. The gate works on the layer's sound before its level, from the layer's first sample, so what came before is heard in a stretch mixed alone; gates run in order. **Decision 3's other half.** An audio layer may now hold an effects list of sound effects; a picture effect on an audio layer, a sound effect on a picture layer, a Mix on a sound effect or an expression on one is `PROJECT_SCHEMA_INVALID` on opening, and the same is refused by the commands. An unknown effect on an audio layer is kept and saved as written and bypassed with `EFFECT_UNSUPPORTED`; a gate setting outside its range is kept and bypassed with `EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID`, on opening and again when mixed (in an export's warnings once). An empty effects list on an audio layer stays refused (FX-AUD-031) and none is ever written, so a file without sound effects saves exactly as before. **Export.** An MP4's sound is now mixed once for the whole range and handed over frame by frame, since a gate needs what came before. **App.** The Effects list offers only Audio: Noise Gate for a sound layer and never for a picture layer; the effect card has no Mix; keyed gate settings show on the timeline under the sound layer. **Gaps.** No look-ahead, side chain or range; the gate closes fully. The window's stretches are mixed from the gated layer's first sample each time, so their cost grows with how far in playback starts (a ponytail note in `audio::mix`; a kept state per layer if it is ever felt). The app's control list test adds effects to a picture layer, so Noise Gate's settings are checked through the core's own test rather than there. **Unchanged.** b20b_audio (D-71), b299_audio_spectrum and b300_audio_waveform (D-420), b518, b519, b520 (every click still on its sample), b12b (no new diagnostic), b07_effects, b21d_mp4 and t08_export pass unchanged; lib 24 of 24; app 93 of 95, the 2 known failures (gestures target, pick whip) and none new. **Timing (release build, this machine, recorded only).** Two seconds of fx_gate_001 mix in 1.5 ms without the gate and 3.4 ms with it. **Evidence.** Fixtures first (0f89f0ca, `tools/noise_gate_reference.py`, FX-GATE-001 to 014, 101 to 104, 201); code 62894479; `tests/b521_noise_gate.rs`, `verification/D-642_noise_gate_table.md` 97 of 97 checks, with the level table and the timing of each gate; waveforms before and after in `verification/D-642 pictures/`; playtest `verification/B-521_playtest.md`, awaiting the owner.

D-641 / Exporting sound, S-3 of D-638: an MP4 carries the composition's sound, and a WAV can be written beside frames (D-638 decisions 2 and 5; ADR-018, D-639, D-640) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-13 under the owner's acceptance of D-638 ("for the sound plan, proceed with your recommendations", relayed by the coordinator); every click lands on its exact sample, every WAV value within document 25's 2e-5; no new tolerance; built B-520.** **What was built.** On Windows an MP4 of a composition with an audio layer switched on gets a sound track: Media Foundation's AAC encoder, 48,000 a second, two channels, 192 kilobits a second, fed each frame's mix (D-640) after its picture. The sound track keeps the encoder's own clock; the film's index gets its length in the film's clock and an edit list that plays it from its first sample for exactly the samples written, so the encoder's padding at the end is not heard. Measured: Windows' encoder hands its output already lined up with what it was given, so the start delay the edit list records is 0. A sound track that is reordered, or already holds an edit list, is refused rather than guessed at. A PNG or EXR sequence or an animated PNG can also write its sound as a 24-bit WAV beside it ("Sound as a WAV beside it" on the export bar), named after the frames (`shot_%04d.png` gives `shot.wav`); a GIF never carries sound. Sound past full level is written at full level with the new warning `EXPORT_SOUND_CLIPPED` (document 28), giving how many values and from which frame. A layer whose sound is not read is left out with its warning, once. **Checked by the click method.** Each test MP4 is decoded by ffmpeg 8.1 and by Windows' own decoder; the loudest sample near each click must be that frame's first sample exactly. AAC files are never compared byte for byte. **Gaps.** Off Windows an MP4 goes through ffmpeg with no sound, with a `MEDIA_AUDIO_PREVIEW_ONLY` warning saying so. ffmpeg ignores the edit list's end and decodes the encoder's padding (72,704 samples for 72,000; Windows' reader stops on the last). An export does not apply solo to sound, as it does not to pictures. The WAV's whole range is held in memory at once (about 0.8 MB a second). **Unchanged.** Projects are not touched; an MP4 of a composition with no sound layer is the picture-only film it always was. b20b_audio (D-71), b299_audio_spectrum and b300_audio_waveform (D-420), b518, b519, b21d_mp4, b21c_films, b22b_choices, t08_export and the other export tests pass unchanged. **Timing.** Not measured separately: the whole b520 run, ten exports of 6 to 72 frames and their decodes, takes about 5 s. **Evidence.** Fixtures first (d850d102, `tools/sound_export_reference.py`, FX-SOUND-EXP-001 to 011); code 330f2be9; `tests/b520_sound_export.rs`, `verification/D-641_sound_export_table.md` 65 of 65 checks, with the click table; the owner's film `verification/D-641 film/flash_and_click.mp4`; playtest `verification/B-520_playtest.md`, awaiting the owner.

D-640 / Hearing sound in step, S-2 of D-638: the core mixes a composition's sound and the window plays it (D-638 decisions 3 and 4; D-71, ADR-018, D-639) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-13 under the owner's acceptance of D-638 ("for the sound plan, proceed with your recommendations", relayed by the coordinator); every sample within document 25's 2e-5, every peak within 0.01 dB; no new tolerance; built B-519.** **What was built.** `audio::mix` mixes the composition's audio layers for a stretch of frames by the rule now in document 21: each sample at 48,000 a second belongs to its ADR-018 frame; an audio layer that is on and whose span holds that frame reads its working sound (D-639) from its local frame's first sample, so every frame starts on its own sample however the rate divides; times the layer's level; the layers are added and nothing is clipped. A layer whose sound is not read is left out with its warning and the others are heard: Opus (`MEDIA_AUDIO_PREVIEW_ONLY`) and a file that cannot be read (`MEDIA_AUDIO_UNREADABLE`). Each sound's working sound is worked out once and kept with it. The window asks the core for a second at a time on the frame scheme (`/mix`, solo applied as the picture is), plays each stretch on its audio clock where its first frame falls, and asks for the next half a second before the current one ends; a stretch that arrives late starts partway in, never late, so the sound stays on its frames. A scrub plays one frame's mix. A level changed while playing is heard from the next stretch. An Opus layer, which the core leaves out, is still played by the window from the file, as D-71 played every sound. **Decision 3's other half, sound effects only on audio layers, comes with the first sound effect (S-4, Noise Gate)**, since there is nothing to refuse until then. **Not yet.** Sound through composition layers, keyed level and pan are S-7; a layer's stretch and time remap are not applied to its sound, as D-71 never applied them. **Unchanged.** Projects are not touched: no field is added. b20b_audio (D-71), b299_audio_spectrum and b300_audio_waveform (D-420, D-421), b518 and b12b pass unchanged. **Timing.** Not measured separately: the whole b519 run, fourteen mixes of 4 to 36 frames, takes 0.08 s. **Evidence.** Fixtures first (0dbeacd5, `tools/sound_mix_reference.py`, FX-SOUND-MIX-001 to 014); code c2dd68e5; `tests/b519_sound_mix.rs`, `verification/D-640_sound_mix_table.md` 72 of 72 checks, with the level table (each channel's loudest sample, within 0.01 dB) and a picture of each mix in `verification/D-640 pictures/`; the app's sound test checks `/mix` against the core's samples (`verification/B-20c_panel_table.md` 22 of 22); playtest `verification/B-519_playtest.md` (the reference shot's clicks landing on their drawings), awaiting the owner.

D-639 / Reading sound, S-1 of D-638: FLAC, MP3, Ogg Vorbis and AAC read by the core, and the working sound (D-638 decisions 1 (a) and 2; P0-14; D-71, D-420) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-13 under the owner's acceptance of D-638 ("for the sound plan, proceed with your recommendations", relayed by the coordinator); every lossless sample within document 25's 2e-5; every lossy sample measured within 1e-6 of ffmpeg's decode, so 2e-5 is proposed and held for lossy files too; no new tolerance; built B-518.** **What was built.** `audio::read_file` picks the road by the file's name: WAV as D-71 reads it, by hand; FLAC, MP3 and Ogg Vorbis by `symphonia` 0.6.1 with its default features off and only those three formats on; `.m4a`, `.aac`, and the first sound track of `.mp4` and `.mov`, by Windows' Media Foundation source reader asked for 32-bit floats (on other systems an `ffmpeg` the user installed, D-30's second road, not run by any test here). Opus is not read: `MEDIA_AUDIO_PREVIEW_ONLY` (WARNING, new, document 28's sixty-sixth identifier) keeps the layer and its reference, the window still plays it, and exports and sound effects will leave it out. `Sound::working` gives any sound as 48,000 samples a second in two channels, 64-bit, by the downmix and windowed-sinc rule now in document 21; a 48,000 stereo file is its own working sound, sample for sample. Audio Spectrum, Audio Waveform and the app's import all read through `read_file`, so they take every format. Bringing in an `.mp4` or `.mov` makes an audio layer and says its picture is not brought in. **Measured.** Against ffmpeg 8.1's decode of the same files at 57 named places each (18 to 105 for the other rates), the largest differences were: MP3 2.98e-7, Ogg Vorbis 5.96e-8, AAC in M4A, MP4 and MOV 8.05e-7, raw AAC 9.83e-7; WAV and FLAC 0. The fixtures carried a pre-code bound of 0.02 for the lossy files; the table now holds them to 2e-5 as well. **Found while building.** Media Foundation does not honour an MP4's edit list, so it hands back the encoder's start delay (1,024 samples) and a padded end; the core reads the edit list itself (`edit_list`: the first sound track's `elst`, after any empty edits), and the clicks then land on their samples (4000 and 24000). A raw `.aac` file records no start delay at all, so it is read 1,024 samples late, as ffmpeg reads it: a gap of the format, not of the reader, recorded in the fixtures. The iTunes gapless note some encoders write instead of an edit list is not read (a ceiling, to add if such a file is met). An M4A's length is 72,000 by the edit list against ffmpeg's 72,704, which keeps the padding; the fixtures allow that range. **Timing** (PROVISIONAL, four other builds running): a three-minute 44,100 stereo file reads in 13 ms as WAV, 145 ms as FLAC, 207 ms as MP3 and 2.6 s as M4A (Windows' decoder), and its working sound takes a further 230 to 420 ms; `verification/B-518_sound_read_timing_table.md`. **Unchanged.** Every existing project opens, draws and saves as before: b20b_audio (D-71), b299_audio_spectrum and b300_audio_waveform (D-420, D-421) pass unchanged, and a WAV read by `read_file` is D-71's reader's answer sample for sample. **Evidence.** Fixtures first (83297d29, `tools/sound_read_reference.py`, FX-SOUND-READ-001 to 014); code 3d1fe2a9; `tests/b518_sound_read.rs`, `verification/D-639_sound_read_table.md` 77 of 77 checks; waveform pictures `verification/D-639 pictures/`; playtest `verification/B-518_playtest.md`, awaiting the owner. The dependency record names `symphonia` and its nine crates (MPL-2.0 now thirteen crates, all unmodified).

D-638 / Sound support: reading sound, hearing it in step, exporting it, and three sound effects after After Effects 26.0's Compressor, Distortion and Noise Gate (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Audio, rows 413 to 415; P0-14; reopens D-63, D-71's ceilings and D-172) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-13 by the owner, every recommended option (1 (a), 2, 3, 4 (a), 5, 6, 7 and 8), with S-7 moved into the build:** "for the sound plan, proceed with your recommendations, in case of music, dialogue use, etc that may overlap with the compositing." (relayed by the coordinator). Music and dialogue need keyed level (fades), pan and sound heard through composition layers, so S-7 follows S-6 rather than waiting to be asked. Built as S-1 to S-7, each with its own D and B number: S-1 D-639/B-518, S-2 D-640/B-519, S-3 D-641/B-520, S-4 D-642/B-521, S-5 D-643/B-522, S-6 D-644/B-523, S-7 D-645/B-524. Originally **PROPOSED on 2026-10-13.** The owner chose "Build sound support" for the three Audio rows on 2026-10-13, relayed by the coordinator: "That reopens D-63/D-172, so it needs a plan before any code." This entry is that plan. No sound code is written until the owner accepts it. **Where things stand.** An audio layer (D-71) has a level (`gain_db`, -96 to +12, not keyed) and an on/off switch, and nothing else. The core reads a WAV's header exactly and, since D-420, its samples, for Audio Spectrum and Audio Waveform. Every other format (FLAC, MP3, Ogg Vorbis, AAC, Opus) is decoded and played only by the window's web view, and D-172 measured that decoder as sample-exact. The window plays from the audio clock, so picture and sound cannot drift. No export carries sound. Video files are not brought in at all (D-274 is only proposed). Sound inside a composition layer is not heard through it. **Decisions for the owner, each with the agent's recommendation.** **1. What sound the core reads.** (a) *Recommended:* WAV as now; FLAC, MP3 and Ogg Vorbis through `symphonia` (pure Rust, MPL-2.0, the licence five crates under Tauri already carry; only those formats' features switched on); AAC, in `.m4a` and `.aac` files and as the sound track of `.mp4` and `.mov` files, through the decoder Windows carries (Media Foundation's source reader, already in the build for writing MP4). So the build ships no AAC decoder, and the AAC patent question stays with Windows, as H.264 does for D-30. On other systems, an `ffmpeg` the user installed, D-30's second road. Bringing in a video file gives an audio layer holding its first sound track; its picture is not brought in, and the import says so. Opus is not read by either road, so it still plays in the window but is left out of exports and sound effects, with a warning on the layer (a new diagnostic, not a silent gap). (b) `symphonia` for everything, AAC included: one road, but this build would then ship an AAC decoder. (c) WAV only, other files converted by the user first. **2. The core's working sound.** *Recommended:* every layer's sound is converted on reading to 48,000 samples a second, two channels, 64-bit floating point, by a windowed-sinc rule of this program's own, written in document 21 so the reference tool can repeat it. A mono file plays equally in both channels. No new crate for this. **3. On the timeline, first stage small.** *Recommended:* only what an audio layer has today: its level and its on/off switch (which mutes it), plus the three sound effects in its effects list. D-71 forbids effects on an audio layer; this would allow sound effects there and only there. A picture effect on an audio layer, or a sound effect on a picture layer, stays `PROJECT_SCHEMA_INVALID`. A file without them reads, draws, sounds and saves exactly as before. Keyed level (fades), pan, and sound heard through a composition layer come later as their own unit (S-7, in the build since the acceptance), not in the first stage. **4. Hearing it while previewing.** (a) *Recommended:* the core mixes the composition's sound (levels, switches, effects) for the stretch being played and hands the window the finished samples; the window plays them from its audio clock as today, and the picture keeps following that clock. What is heard is then exactly what is exported. A changed setting is heard from the next stretch the core mixes; how soon is measured on the owner's machine, not promised. Stepping one frame still plays that frame's samples. (b) Keep the window's decoder and imitate the effects with the browser's own sound nodes: quicker to build, but the browser's compressor and gate follow their own maths, so the preview would differ from the export, and nothing could check it. **5. Export.** *Recommended:* MP4 gains a sound track: AAC, 48,000 a second, two channels, 192 kilobits a second, from the encoder Windows carries, with the encoder's start delay recorded in the file so players skip it. Image sequences, EXR and animated PNG may write a 24-bit WAV beside them (a choice in the export dialog, off as now). GIF carries no sound, and the dialog says so. Sync is checked without ears: the test sound has a click on the first sample of frames 2 and 12 (B-112's method); the exported MP4 is decoded with ffmpeg 8.1, and each click must land on exactly sample floor(n x 48000 x denominator / numerator) of its frame. The WAV is compared value for value with its fixture. An AAC file is never compared byte for byte, because Windows' encoder is not ours. **6. The three effects, under our own names, with After Effects 26.0's controls and starting values (from Adobe's beta forum post for 26.0; Adobe publishes no maths, so every rule is ours, written in document 21).** *Compressor* (`core.compressor`): Threshold -60 to 0 dB (-16), Ratio 0.4 to 30 (3), Knee 0 to 30 dB (15), Attack 0 to 400 ms (6), Release 1 to 4000 ms (440), Auto Release (on), Makeup Gain -30 to +30 dB (0), Output Limit -30 to 0 dB (0). Our rule: the louder channel's peak level in decibels, a soft knee, the gain eased toward its target with the attack and release times; Auto Release our own two-speed release. *Distortion* (`core.distortion`): Type (Soft Clip, Hard Clip, Saturation 1, Saturation 2, Tube, Fuzz; Soft Clip), Drive 0 to 100% (25), Gain 0 to 300 (25), Mix 0 to 100% (100), Volume 0 to 100 (11), Resolution and Downsample. Adobe gives no range for the last two, so ours: Resolution 1 to 24 bits (24, which changes nothing) and Downsample 1 to 32 (1, which changes nothing). Each type is one curve of ours; no oversampling in the first unit, so strong drive can alias, logged as a ceiling. *Noise Gate* (`core.noise_gate`): Threshold -60 to 0 dB (-60), Attack 0 to 1000 ms (10), Hold 0 to 2500 ms (40), Release 5 to 4000 ms (220). Our rule: the louder channel's peak opens the gate; it opens over Attack, stays open Hold after the sound falls below Threshold, then closes over Release, each a straight ramp counted in whole samples. Every number keyable; a keyed number moves in a straight line across each frame's samples rather than jumping at frame edges (recommended, so no clicks). **7. How sound is checked without ears.** Each unit's fixtures are written first by a Python reference tool, as for pictures: decoding (each format's samples at named places against ffmpeg's decode of the same file, exact for WAV and FLAC; for MP3, Vorbis and AAC the tolerance is measured and proposed in that unit, not assumed); mixing (a 1 kHz sine at -6 dB through a level of -6 dB peaks at -12.00 dB; a switched-off layer is all zeros; two layers add); Noise Gate (a burst after silence: the sample where the gain starts to rise, where it reaches full, how long it holds, where it is shut); Compressor (the steady gain curve from -60 to 0 dB in 1 dB steps, and the time a step takes to reach 63% and 90% of its change); Distortion (each type's curve from input to output, and a sine's 2nd and 3rd harmonic levels; Resolution and Downsample exact). The owner judges each unit from pictures and tables: a waveform before and after, a gain-curve chart, a level table, and a playtest sheet that says what should be heard. **8. Build order, small units, each fixtures first, code, then records.** S-1 reading (decision 1 and 2): judge a table of each test file's length, rate, channels and click positions against the WAV, and a waveform picture for each format. S-2 mixing and hearing it (3 and 4): judge the level table, and a playtest where the reference shot's clicks land on their drawings. S-3 export (5): judge the click table from the decoded MP4 and WAV, and play the MP4 in Windows' own player. S-4 Noise Gate, S-5 Compressor, S-6 Distortion (6 and 7): judge each from its before-and-after waveform and its timing table or curve chart. S-7, after S-6 (the owner's acceptance moved it into the build): keyed level, pan, and sound through composition layers. **Libraries.** One new crate family: `symphonia` (MPL-2.0), only for decision 1 (a) or (b). Media Foundation is part of Windows and already used. No new crate for mixing, resampling, the effects or WAV writing. **What it changes in other decisions.** D-71's "no sound in any export" and "no effects on an audio layer" ceilings end, D-172's "no decoder in the core" ends for the formats in decision 1, and EFFECTS rows 413 to 415 stop being "not applicable". Every existing project opens, draws and saves as it does today. **For the owner:** accept the plan as recommended, or name the decisions to change (for example 1 (b), or 4 (b)).

D-637 / Color Grade, fourth unit: Lumetri Color's Creative Sharpen and a squarer vignette (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, Color Correction, row 121, Lumetri Color; D-397, D-571) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-13 under the owner's /loop request (the coordinator's queue for lane B); every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-517.** **What was built.** `core.color_grade` gains `sharpen`, -100 to 100 (0, keyable), the Sharpen effect's rule (D-147's unsharp mask) at a 1-pixel blur and no threshold, run after the faded film and before the vibrance; below 0 it softens toward the blur, -100 the blur itself. `vignette_roundness` now runs -100 to 100: 0 to 100 as before; below 0 the half-axes stay 0's (the layer's own shape) and the distance is measured by a squarer norm, p = 2 / (1 + roundness / 100), -100 the larger of the two distances, a rectangle. The Vignette effect (D-126) is unchanged. Saved by D-121's rule, so a D-571 file opens, draws and saves exactly as before. Under D-566 FX-GRADE-034, which pinned roundness -20 as refused while the squarer vignette was not built, now pins roundness -101 as refused (e21d5d97); no other existing case changed. **Our choices (deviations).** Adobe publishes no maths: the 1-pixel blur radius is ours, and a Draft preview does not halve it (the sharpen works on the pixels drawn); the squarer norm is ours. A grade with a sharpen is drawn by the processor (the sharpen reads the pixels round each, as D-571's refined key), the same picture, slower; the card draws the vignette's new shapes itself. **Not built**, by the owner's answers of 2026-10-13, relayed by the coordinator: (1) Vegas stays masks-only, D-444 stands, Image Contours and open masks remain gaps; (2) Contour Paint's Freehand Flow Adjustments stay a gap; (3) Lumetri's dragged curves and wheels and the key eyedropper stay gaps, so row 121 stays partial. Evidence: FX-GRADE4-001 to 016 (`tools/color_grade_4_reference.py`, fixtures e21d5d97), code df7b0888, `tests/b517_color_grade_4.rs`, `verification/D-637_color_grade_4_table.md` 115 of 115 checks, FX-GRADE, FX-GRADE2 and FX-GRADE3 unchanged; B-155 shows no fall-back; speed `verification/B-517_color_grade_4_timing_table.md` (PROVISIONAL, the machine not quiet (another lane's b155 and four cargo processes running): on the card the reference shot with a moving Noise took 34.2 ms a frame, 42.9 with a dark vignette at roundness -60, 269.2 with sharpen 50 (drawn by the processor); on the processor 124.5, 473.4 and 486.4).

D-673 / Hair, after CycoreFX's CC Hair (Simulation) (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, row 354) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-13 under the owner's /loop request (D-600), lane C's design D-670 approved by the coordinator; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-552.** **What was built.** `core.hair`, in Generate beside Drizzle: Length, Thickness, Weight, Constant Mass, Density, the Hair Color group (Hair Color, Color Inheritance, Opacity) and the Light and Shading groups (Light Intensity, Light Direction, Ambient, Diffuse, Specular, Roughness, Metal). Each strand has its own root, lean and length from Noise's hash; it grows only where the layer is opaque enough, leaves the layer towards the viewer, hangs down by its weight (up for a negative weight, more for a longer strand with Constant Mass on), narrows to a quarter at its tip and is drawn as eight straight pieces seen straight on. It takes the hair colour mixed towards the picture under its root and is lit brightest where it runs across the light. The strands are laid over the layer in order. Nothing moves by itself and nothing is carried from frame to frame (document 20). Draw code in `src/simulate.rs`; the strands are binned with `particles::tile_lists`, nothing in `src/particles.rs` changed. **Sources read:** the CycoreFX HD 1.8.1 manual's CC Hair page (the controls and what each is for: Weight pulling the hair down, below 0 up; Constant Mass; Density; the Hair Color group; the Light and Shading groups). **Gaps:** CycoreFX publishes no formula, so the rule, the units (Length 100 a tenth of the layer's height, Thickness 1 a 1080th of it, Weight 100 a hang of the strand's own length at its tip), the strand's shape, the lighting, the ranges and the settings when added are ours; the manual's Hairfall Map (a second layer steering the hair) is not offered; the strands are seen straight on, not through the composition camera; hair reaching past the layer's edge is cut there. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-HAIR-001 to 032 (`tools/hair_reference.py`, 7c960f80) in document 25; code 1ef3d81c; `verification/D-673_hair_table.md` 189 of 189. **On the card:** a new pass `hair`, in double precision, the strands built and binned into the card's 16 by 16 tiles on the processor; every fixture at Full and Draft and the reference shot at frames 0, 100 and 239, as added, as a long fur and with a keyed weight, within 1 level (50 of 50 comparisons). One new measured stage, `effect: hair`.

D-674 / Mercury, after CycoreFX's CC Mr. Mercury (Simulation) (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, row 355) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-13 under the owner's /loop request (D-600), lane C's design D-670 approved by the coordinator; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-553.** **What was built.** `core.mercury`, in Generate beside Hair: Radius X and Y, Producer, Direction, Velocity, Birth Rate, Longevity, Gravity, Resistance, Extra, Animation (Explosive, Direction, Twirl, Vortex, Fixed), Blob Influence, Influence Map (In and Out, In, Out, Constant), Blob Birth Size, Blob Death Size and Drizzle's Light and Shading groups. Drops are counted from the in point by the summed birth rate, as Drizzle's; each is born at a place in the producer's ellipse where the layer is opaque enough, takes the layer's colour there and follows a path in closed form (thrown, slowed by the resistance and pulled by the gravity; circling for Vortex; turning round the producer for Twirl; still for Fixed), every birth setting read at the frame it was born. The drops run together as metaballs, a lone drop a half sphere, and are lit by Blobbylize's rule (D-379). The layer becomes the drops alone. Nothing is carried from frame to frame (document 20): every frame sums the keyed birth rate from the in point (a `ponytail:` ceiling, O(frames) a frame when it is keyed, as Drizzle's). Draw code in `src/simulate.rs`; the drops' reach is binned with `particles::tile_lists`, nothing in `src/particles.rs` changed. **Sources read:** the CycoreFX HD 1.8.1 manual's CC Mr. Mercury page (the controls and what each is for: the producer's radii and place, Extra as more randomness, Animation as the way the drops move, Blob Influence as how much they run together, Influence Map as how they grow and shrink over their lives, the Light and Shading groups shared with CC Blobbylize). **Gaps:** CycoreFX publishes no formula, so the rule, the units (Velocity 100 a layer's height a second, Gravity 100 a height a second a second, Blob Birth Size 100 a radius of a twentieth of the height), the metaball shape, the ranges and the settings when added are ours; only five ways the drops move are offered (Explosive, Direction, Twirl, Vortex, Fixed), each path ours, and the manual's others are not; Longevity is read at the in point only; After Effects' lights are not offered; there is no seed, as CC Mr. Mercury has none. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-MERCURY-001 to 038 (`tools/mercury_reference.py`, ccd337a3) in document 25; code be08421f; `verification/D-674_mercury_table.md` 217 of 217. **On the card:** a new pass `mercury`, in double precision over the processor's tile lists of live drops, the field, slope and colour summed per pixel as on the processor; every fixture at Full and Draft and the reference shot at frames 0, 100 and 239, as added, as a vortex under an orange point light and with a keyed birth rate, within 1 level (56 of 56 comparisons). One new measured stage, `effect: mercury`. **Change from D-670:** the design had Mercury call `particles::alive` with a Particle Space value set; its paths are its own closed forms in `src/simulate.rs` instead, because the Animation words have no Particle Space twins, so `src/particles.rs` is not called for motion, only for binning.

D-675 / Polygon Shards, after CycoreFX's CC Pixel Polly (Simulation) (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, row 358) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-13 under the owner's /loop request (D-600), lane C's design D-670 approved by the coordinator; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-554.** **What was built.** `core.polygon_shards`, in Generate beside Mercury: Force, Gravity, Spinning, Force Center, Direction Randomness, Speed Randomness, Grid Spacing, Object (Polygon, Textured Polygon, Square, Textured Square), Enable Depth Sort and Start Time. The layer is cut along a grid of Grid Spacing pixels, each cell two triangles or one square; each shard is thrown away from the force centre and towards the viewer, slower further out, falls by the gravity and turns about its own random axis, its flight in closed form from the start time with every setting read at the frame drawn. The shards are drawn in 3D through the composition camera when the file has one (as Particle Space, D-610), else through an eye of the effect's own, far to near with Depth Sort on; a textured shard shows the picture it was cut from, a plain one its own average colour. The layer becomes the shards alone. Nothing is carried from frame to frame (document 20). Draw code in `src/simulate.rs`; the shards are binned with `particles::tile_lists`, nothing in `src/particles.rs` changed. Not a 3D layer: D-309 and D-355 stand, the 3D is inside the effect as D-600 asks. **Sources read:** the CycoreFX HD 1.8.1 manual's CC Pixel Polly page (the controls and what each is for: Force, Gravity, Spinning, Force Center, Direction and Speed Randomness, Grid Spacing, the four Objects, Enable Depth Sort, Start Time). **Gaps:** CycoreFX publishes no formula, so the rule, the units (Force 100 throws a shard at the force centre a quarter of the layer's height a second, Gravity 1 a height a second a second, Spinning in degrees a second), the throw's lean towards the viewer, a plain shard's colour (the average of its pixels), the effect's own eye (a 39.6 degree view), the ranges and the settings when added are ours; every setting is read at the frame drawn, so a keyed Force changes the whole flight, not only what follows the key; there is no seed, as CC Pixel Polly has none; shards thrown past the layer's edge are cut there. Rule in document 21; fixtures FX-POLYGON-SHARDS-001 to 036 (`tools/polygon_shards_reference.py`, 73a23aba) in document 25; code 52ffce8b; `verification/D-675_polygon_shards_table.md` 208 of 208. **On the card:** a new pass `shards`, in double precision, each shard's place, turn and colour worked and binned into the card's 16 by 16 tiles on the processor, the ray to each shard's plane worked per pixel on the card; every fixture at Full and Draft and the reference shot at frames 0, 100 and 239, as added, as small flat triangles from the top left and with a keyed force in grid order, within 1 level (54 of 54 comparisons). D-678 / Foam, after After Effects' Foam (Simulation) (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md`, row 363) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-13 under the owner's /loop request (D-600), lane C's design D-670 approved by the coordinator; every fixture pixel within document 25's 2e-5; every viewer picture within ADR-006's 1 level (D-100); no new tolerance; built B-557.** **What was built.** `core.foam`, in Generate beside Polygon Shards: View (Draft, Rendered); the Producer group (Producer Point, X and Y Size, Orientation, Zoom Producer Point, Production Rate); the Bubbles group (Size, Size Variance, Lifespan, Bubble Growth Speed, Strength); the Physics group (Initial Speed, Initial Direction, Wind Speed, Wind Direction, Turbulence, Wobble Amount, Repulsion, Pop Velocity, Viscosity, Stickiness); Zoom; Universe Size; the Rendering group (Blend Mode, Bubble Texture, Bubble Orientation, Reflection Strength, Reflection Convergence); Simulation Quality; Random Seed. D-679 / Advanced Lightning's Alpha Obstacle on a solid layer, explained in its tooltip / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-13 by the owner ("proceed with recommendations"), option (a) of `verification/diagnosis/silent_settings.md`; no engine, fixture or tolerance change.** The real-app effect check drew no bolt for Advanced Lightning at Alpha Obstacle 50 on an opaque layer. D-680 / Curl Noise's walk slows where the flow is weak, and reads every pixel it crosses / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-14 by the owner ("go with fixes 1 and 2") after `verification/diagnosis/curl_seams.md`; a specification change, FX-CURL-001 to 060 and the Transform's frames regenerated.** The real-app check showed straight-edged wedges (seams) and a comb of streaks in Final Render. The diagnosis found the flow was made one long everywhere, so a walk ran its full length through the flow's crossing points into another stream, and the brightening, worked from the step weights alone, made those wedges solid; and with fewer steps than pixels the seed was read several pixels apart, the comb. Fix 2: the flow is divided by the larger of its length and 1 / s (s the noise size), so it is shorter where the slope is weaker than one per noise size, each step moves the step length times that flow, and the brightening grows with the distance walked over twice the radius. Fix 1: each step is read at ceil(step length) evenly spaced points, so no pixel is skipped; only whole steps count in the brightening. Curl Generation still shows the direction one long. In the diagnosis' own copy the seam pixels fell from 6.35% to 1.09% at the check's settings and from 2.64% to 0% at Swirl 0, 24 samples, radius 20. Document 21's steps 3 and 6 say the rule; the card's `curlfield` and `curlflow` work it the same way. **Gaps:** the swirl's size (fix 3): on 2026-10-22 the owner took the recommendation, no change; a larger Size, about 280, gives the broad swirls; the walk now takes up to ceil(radius / steps) times as many reads, so Final Render is slower; B-326, B-461 and B-525's timings are measured again. **Superseded on 2026-10-23 by D-749**, which replaces this walk with one fitted to After Effects' pictures; FX-CURL-001 to 077 hold D-749's rule.

D-713 / Particle Playground's further mapper properties (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md` row 364; P0-6, D-614) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-13 under the owner's /loop request, as lane K's fourth unit closing the particle rows' buildable gaps; built B-583.** **What was built.** The Persistent and Ephemeral Property Mappers' channels take, after what After Effects' property mappers can set, seven more words after D-614's thirteen: `x_scale`, `y_scale`, `angular_velocity` (degrees a second), `torque` (degrees a second a second), `lifespan` (seconds), `kinetic_friction` and `static_friction` (pixels a second a second). A particle is born with X and Y Scale 1, no spin, an endless lifespan and no friction; a child takes its parent's. In every step of h seconds the angle grows by w h + T h^2 / 2 and w by T h. Kinetic friction K cuts a moving particle's speed by K h before the move, never below 0. Static friction S keeps a still particle where it is, the Wall not asked, while the pull on it (gravity and its forces) is S or less. A particle dies at the first step point, after the Persistent mapper's puts, at which its age is its lifespan or more. The Ephemeral mapper's angular velocity, torque and frictions last one step (the angular velocity it changed is taken back, as D-614's speed); its X and Y Scale and lifespan are for the drawing only (an endless lifespan stays endless under every operator). Drawing: a dot's radii are R S_x and R S_y, each below 0.7 drawn at 0.7 with the colour times r / 0.7; equal radii draw D-613's disc, others an oval turned with the particle covering clamp(min(r) (1 - |(l_x / r_x, l_y / r_y)|) + 1/2); a piece and a Layer Map copy are stretched along their own axes. The card's sprites carry the two radii and turn, a piece's number (its origin worked out from it) and both scales, and draw the same, within 1 level. Draft scales a friction's Min and Max as it does a place's. A file written before D-713 is the effect it was. **Still gaps:** Mass (FX-PMAP-039 still refuses it, untouched), Gradient Velocity (no source says what it does), Character and Font Size (no text particles), Repel (the owner's choice of approach is pending). **Sources:** our own rules, stated in `tools/particle_mapper_physics_reference.py` (Adobe publishes no formula); no text or code copied, no open-source code used. **Checks:** fixtures first (aa119565): FX-PMPH-001..028, 25 drawn cases and 3 refused files (Gradient Velocity, Character, Font Size); seven cases also list every particle. `verification/D-713_particle_mapper_physics_table.md` 133 of 133: every case within 2e-5, every listed particle within 1e-7, all 25 drawn files at Full and Draft on the card within 1 level. Code 933d40c0; b493, b494 (D-614's table: FX-PMAP-039's refusal sentence now lists the new words), b155_gpu_chain and lib pass; app tests 93 passed, the 2 known failures.

D-703 / Smear's pivot: the mask turned and scaled about the outline's mean (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md` Distort, row 164) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-13 by the owner, asked directly by the coordinator and answered in session.** `core.mask_smear` (D-607, B-486) keeps turning and scaling the source outline about the mean of its 64 resampled points. This is this program's own rule (document 21), recorded as a deviation, not a match: After Effects does not publish the point its Smear turns and scales about. Nothing changes in code or fixtures; FX-SMEAR-003 to 005 (`tools/mask_smear_reference.py`, b486) already pin the mean as the pivot. Row 164 is now done, and with it every row of P0-18 (Bezier Warp, Mesh Warp, Warp, Liquify, Reshape, Smear), so P0-18 is done. Remaining gaps on the row: masks chosen by number; L-05. **For the owner:** nothing further to decide; B-486's playtest awaits.

Code 648521af. `verification/D-714_particle_plane_square_table.md` 98 of 98: every case within 2e-5, all 18 files at Full and Draft on the card within 1 level (largest 0), 2 reference-shot setups within 1 level. D-715 / Particle Playground's Mass (`docs/effects/EFFECTS.md` row 364; P0-6, D-613, D-614, D-713) / **ACCEPTED on 2026-10-13: an owner specification decision, asked directly by the coordinator and answered in session; built B-585.** **The decision.** FX-PMAP-039 may be regenerated so that the property mappers can drive Mass, keeping it an invalid case with a word that is still refused: it now writes Persistent Map Red To "repel" (it was "mass"). The same day the owner kept Repel as a gap. Regenerated alone, naming this decision, in 98d84560; no other expected value changed. **What was built.** The mappers' property list takes "mass", last: 1 when born; in every step the particle's force (its own X and Y Force and the Ephemeral mapper's, D-614) is divided by its mass before it joins Gravity's pull; Gravity pulls every mass alike; at a mass of 0 or below the force does nothing (a particle with no mass is not pushed, rather than pushed without limit); D-713's Static Friction weighs the pull after the division; the Ephemeral mapper's mass is the operator for one step; the Particle Exploder's children are born with their parent's mass. Draft does not scale a mapper's Mass range, as it has no unit. A file written before D-715 is the effect it was. **Sources:** our own rule, stated in `tools/particle_mapper_mass_reference.py` (Adobe's page says only that Mass works with Force to set acceleration); no text or code copied. **Checks:** new fixtures 14f30c38: FX-PMASS-001..014 drawn, 015 and 016 refused ("Mass", "weight"), 5 particle listings. ## Assumptions and change log

A-01: solo development is permanent for planning purposes. A-02: artistic acceptance requires the owner using the tool on a real shot, and cannot be replaced by fixtures. A-03: owner verification is genuine and unhurried; the protocol in document 12 fails if artifacts go unread.

Version 0.3 supersedes 0.2. It closes D-01, D-03, D-05, D-06 and D-13 through D-16, and adds D-12. Further changes are recorded in git history and in `docs/adr/`.

Version 0.6 adds D-21, from B-05: document 28's catalog names no identifier for a command rejected at validation, and document 26 requires that rejection be reported without changing the document. The model half of T-03 is no longer NOT RUN; its results are in `verification/B-05_model_table.md`. The render half of T-03, the four FX-XF transform fixtures, remains NOT RUN and belongs to B-05a. B-04 raised no new decision: `verification/B-04_exposure_table.md` records T-02 passing under the rules documents 20 and 25 already state.

Version 0.7 adds D-22, from B-05a: document 21 and document 19 disagree about whether a stored scale is a percentage or a unit factor, and a renderer cannot be written without picking one. T-03 is now fully RUN and PASSING; the render half's results are in `verification/B-05a_transform_table.md`, with ADR-011's two further artifacts in `verification/B-05a_tiling_proof.md` and `verification/B-05a_scaling_table.md`.

Version 0.8 adds D-23, from B-05b: ADR-012 asks for trace images in the working space and for images the owner can look at, and linear light cannot be both. Trace mode itself raises no new test; it is the diagnostic facility document 12's protocol leans on, and its results are in `verification/B-05b_trace_table.md`.

Version 0.25 adds D-44, D-45 and D-46, all from B-07, and ADR-017. D-44 is the one that changes a requirement: the effect stack turns out never to be tiled, because it runs over the whole layer buffer before the frame plan exists, so the tiled-versus-full-frame comparison R-05 asked for has no region-of-interest optimisation to be about, and tile-size invariance at six sizes is what B-07 proves instead. D-45 registers a fourth effect command, changing an existing effect's settings, which document 24 does not list and without which an effect cannot be used. D-46 gives `EFFECT_PARAMETER_INVALID` the two severities D-43 gave `MASK_INVALID_OUTLINE`, so that a project holding a bad number is neither refused nor silently repaired. B-07's results are in `verification/B-07_effects_table.md`, 60 checks.

Version 0.24 adds D-42 and D-43, both from B-06, and ADR-016. D-42 replaces this build's first reading of document 21 step 5 - that a matte layer is hidden by being switched off - with an explicit `matte_only` flag, because overloading one field with two meanings is a trap for an owner who verifies by reading files and pictures. D-43 gives a mask outline this build refuses to draw its own identifier in document 28 rather than borrowing two that no longer fit, and closed a silent fidelity fallback found while doing it: an undrawable mask was skipped at render time with nothing recorded. ADR-016 records the rasterization rule and reference tool document 25 line 51 told B-06 to select - a 4x4 ordered sample grid, even-odd, checked against a second implementation written from document 19 by a different method - which closes that line's OPEN.

Version 0.23 adds D-39, from B-11's offline check: read off the build, R-11 holds; watched while running, the operating system's web view contacts the network on its own account and six switches did not stop it. It is OPEN because all three answers — accept and document, block at the firewall per machine, or stop using the system web view — are the owner's and not an agent's.

Version 0.22 closes D-34 and D-37. The owner delegated both to the agent's recommendation on 2026-09-05, which is why each entry records the reasoning at length rather than a name and a yes: a delegated decision that does not say why it went the way it did is indistinguishable from a guess. D-34 keeps the copyright line as it stands and explains why an agent should not be the one to put a legal name in a public file. D-37 unparks the bounded preview cache as B-08b, scoped to decoded cels, with a memory ceiling, outside the export path, and with masks and effects left parked; ADR-015 is its architecture record and document 23's parked table loses a row.

Version 0.21 adds D-38, from the shell's dependency intake: the graph went from 28 crates to 264 and `Cargo.lock` stopped being the same question as "what is in this build". It is PROVISIONAL because it is a reading of document 10 rather than a measurement, and because a second supported platform would ask it again.

Version 0.20 adds D-37, from B-08's latency measurement: document 23 parked the bounded preview cache behind a trigger worded as a measurement rather than an opinion, and that measurement has now been taken. It is OPEN rather than PROVISIONAL because unparking a feature is the owner's decision and not an agent's reading.

Version 0.19 adds D-36, from B-08's window: SP-05 measured two transports, found them within four percent of each other, and explicitly declined to pick one. A viewer cannot decline. It is PROVISIONAL because the reasoning is about shape rather than measurement, and reversing it costs one function.

Version 0.18 adds D-35, from B-08's playback clock: which frame a viewer shows when it is not playing is a question no requirement answers and every viewer has to answer. It is PROVISIONAL rather than CLOSED because it is an agent's reading, not the owner's decision, and it is cheap to reverse.

Version 0.17 closes D-31 with the owner's answer - MIT OR Apache-2.0 - and adds D-32, D-33 and D-34, all from the same session: the two behaviours B-08 could not be started without, and the one thing the licence decision left open. D-32 and D-33 are owner decisions rather than agent readings, so they are CLOSED rather than PROVISIONAL; D-34 is OPEN because a copyright holder's name cannot be derived from anything in this repository.

Version 0.16 adds D-31, from B-11's dependency and licence record: this project has never chosen a licence for its own code, which nothing has needed until now and which only the owner can answer. The record itself, `docs/DEPENDENCIES.md`, raises no other decision — it is a bill of materials generated from `Cargo.lock` with every dependency's licence text archived under `Licenses/`, and it deliberately reaches no legal conclusion, because document 10 reserves those for a reviewer and none is engaged. Three entries are flagged for a reviewer rather than decided: `unicode-ident`'s Unicode-3.0 term, which is an `AND` rather than an `OR`; `zlib-rs`, which offers no alternative to the Zlib licence; and `memchr`'s public-domain option, which is avoidable by taking its MIT half.

Version 0.15 adds D-28, D-29 and D-30, all from T-08, the first code that writes files meant to leave the application. D-28 registers a conflict rather than resolving it: document 07 blocks an export that has a frame with no drawing, document 28 writes that frame transparent with a warning, and export cannot have two defaults. D-29 settles how a composition that starts before frame zero names its files, which no document covers. D-30 records that video export is a codec and a licence decision and leaves it to the owner. T-08's results are in `verification/T-08_export_table.md`, beside six exported frames of the reference shot, one of which is deliberately empty.

Version 0.14 adds D-26 and D-27, both from B-08a, the first code that assembles a render from a saved project rather than from test scaffolding. D-26: document 28 names no identifier for a render request naming a frame the composition does not contain, so one had to be chosen. D-27 registers a numbering conflict rather than resolving it - documents 11 and 15 disagree about whether export is B-06 or B-10, and the reading that lost would have sent a fresh session to build the parked mask feature. B-08a's results are in `verification/B-08a_compose_table.md`, beside four frames of the reference shot rendered from a saved project file. It installs `FrameLog` in production for the first time and fixes this build's default tile size at 128 pixels, which is a measurement from `verification/B-05a_scaling_table.md` and not a decision.

Version 0.13 records the second hardening pass, which covered the four units the first did not reach: 52 further deliberate single-change defects across B-05, B-05a, B-05b and B-09, all now caught, twelve of them only after those units' fixtures were strengthened. Every merged unit's fixture has now been shown capable of failing. No decision was needed and no D-number was added; the report is `verification/HARDENING_mutation_report.md`, and the four tables grew to 66, 30, 33 and 92 checks.

Version 0.12 records the hardening pass: 55 deliberate single-change defects across B-02, B-03, B-04, B-04b and B-05c, all now caught, six of them only after T-01's fixture was strengthened. No decision was needed and no D-number was added; the report is `verification/HARDENING_mutation_report.md`.

Version 0.11 adds D-25, from B-04b: document 28 requires repeated frame-level warnings to be rate-limited while retaining counts and ranges, and specifies no limit and no shape, so the implementation had to choose both. The rate-limiting itself is now RUN and PASSING against the reference shot's twenty-frame sequence gap, evidence in `verification/B-04b_frame_log_table.md`.
